messages.content:
Plan fits — home private event, so roasted chicken is in scope, and the menu is naturally low-allergen (no sesame, no tree nuts unless you add them).

Sizing for two + modest leftovers (this is where the math matters):

  Chicken: 3 lb, not 4. A 4 lb bird for two leaves 1+ lb picked meat
  sitting around the night before Sam's Friday shift — that's not
  modest, that's an extra meal. 3 lb gives two ~6–8 oz plated portions
  plus ~4–6 oz leftover (one small next-day lunch, not a full dinner).

  Sweet potatoes: 2 small-medium (~1/2 lb each), one each or split.
  Two portions plus a small leftover that can roll into Friday.

  Green beans: 1/2 lb fresh. Two modest servings, finishes the pan —
  no leftover.

  Cranberry relish: small batch — 1 cup cranberries, 1 orange, ~1/3–
  1/2 cup sugar. ~1.5 cups; keeps a week refrigerated, absorbs any gap.

Flow for quiet execution:

  Wed night: make relish, refrigerate (~10 min).
  Thu morning: chicken out 30–45 min to lose chill; oven 450°F.
  11:30–11:45: chicken in (aromatics in cavity, butter rub, salt).
            50–60 min to 165°F thigh.
  +15 min:  sweet potatoes in at 425°F, ~45 min (halved on sheet pan).
  Rest chicken 10–15 min. Blanch/shock green beans, sauté with shallot
            + butter, ~5 min.
  Plate ~1pm. Active work ~30 min; oven does the rest.

Two soft flags:

  Thanksgiving Thursday is a normal day for Sam (close series ended
  10/28). Friday service is the only work consideration — keep
  Thursday evening quiet (cold leftovers or gentle reheat, no second
  cooking project) so Sam goes into Friday rested.

  Kitchen handles sesame and other allergens as a matter of course;
  fine here since none of these ingredients touch that list.

arguments.message:
Operating instruction — approved by Priya and Riley today (12/16)

*Helio Start intake: external-authority readiness as a separate gate*

Applicants must separately confirm that they — or an available owner — can perform the owner-level permission or network-allowlist action required by the connector selected for first-week setup. Verified yes → continue. No or not sure → route to Customer Success before admission.

*What this is NOT (do not conflate)*

This is a new, standalone gate. It does *not* replace or broaden any of the existing Helio Start requirements:

• *External authority* (new) — the applicant/owner's ability to perform the owner-level permission or network-allowlist action for their chosen first-week connector. Recorded by Daniela as a separate readiness state.
• *Admin proof* (existing) — the existing Helio admin-proof requirement. Unchanged.
• *Connector authentication* (existing) — the connector-authentication requirement. Unchanged.
• *Entitlement, billing, deployment* — all unchanged. This gate is additive only.

*Ownership and reporting*

• Daniela: records external-authority readiness as a separate state.
• Ines: holds setup prompts while that state is pending (no prompts fire until readiness is resolved).
• Owen: reports this gate separately so support effects can be evaluated in isolation.

*Measurement guardrail*

This gate is reported separately and does not rewrite the existing Helio Start admission measures. Support effects from routing no/not-sure to CS will be evaluated as their own cut — not folded back into the admission baseline.

Questions → thread here.

messages.content:
Posted to #growth-operations (msg id slack_1789371809610). Summary of the operating instruction as sent:

- New gate (additive only): applicant/owner must confirm they can perform the owner-level permission or network-allowlist action required by their chosen first-week connector. Verified yes → continue; no / not sure → route to CS before admission.

arguments.title: 2024 Annual Self-Review — Working Draft (for Priya, Mon noon)
arguments.body:
# 2024 Annual Self-Review — Working Draft
**Status:** working draft, not a polished promotion case. For Priya by Mon noon.
**Format:** 1-pager. Summary first. Why / cuts / effect / call. Plain questions at the end.

## Summary (read first)
My year was defined less by shipping launches and more by holding the line on what we actually know before it reaches leadership. The four workstreams below show the same pattern: scope a claim to what evidence supports, separate inputs that look like one input, delegate the routine so judgment stays focused on the non-routine, and correct definitions before they harden into reported numbers.

## 1. Helio Start 60-workspace diagnostic — closed with a scoped finding
- **Why:** The open question was whether workspaces failing connector auth were "not onboarded" in a general sense.
- **What I cut:** I did not let the diagnostic land as a broad onboarding-readiness claim.
- **Effect:** The closed read distinguishes three inputs that were being conflated: (a) Helio admin proof, (b) connector authentication, and (c) external-system authority. External-system authority is a separate readiness input, not a subset of either of the other two, and it has to be evidenced independently.
- **Call:** Scope held. The diagnostic closes on the narrower finding; the broader onboarding claim stays open pending its own evidence.

## 2. Lifecycle release authority — delegated routine, retained judgment
- **Why:** Routine lifecycle releases were consuming attention that should sit on incidents, customer corrections, state-changing sends, ambiguous cases, and higher-risk sends.
- **What I cut:** I handed routine, non-state-changing sends and routine preflights to Ines within her authority. Daniela's engineering release controls stayed with Daniela. Ines has no engineering release-control access.
- **What I kept:** Authority over incident stops, customer corrections, state-changing sends, ambiguous sends, and higher-risk sends.
- **Effect:** Ines owns the volume; I own the call when something is non-routine, customer-visible, or reversible only with cost. The boundary is explicit, not vibe-based.
- **Call:** Delegation worked because the boundary was written down, not implied.

## 3. Stale-retry-manifest correction — handled without overclaiming cause
- **Why:** A stale retry manifest surfaced; the temptation was to attribute it to a single root cause and ship a fix narrative.
- **What I cut:** I did not overstate the cause. The correction went out scoped to what we had actually observed, not to a cause story we hadn't verified.
- **Effect:** The customer-facing correction matched the evidence. A premature cause claim would have created a second correction when the actual cause turned out to be narrower (or different).
- **Call:** Discipline here is cheap; the cost of a second correction is not.

## 4. Metric definitions — corrected before they reached leadership
- **Why:** Several proposed metrics would have read as stronger statements than the underlying data supported.
- **What I cut:** I repeatedly pushed back on definitions — denominators, inclusion windows, "active" thresholds — before they hardened into leadership-facing numbers.
- **Effect:** What reached leadership was scoped to what the data supported. What I stopped did not become someone else's problem later.
- **Call:** This is the cheapest place to add rigor and the easiest place to lose it.

## Improvement area — one, specific
**Reduce late-stage manual interpretation by specifying ownership and evidence boundaries earlier.**
- Today the pattern is: a workstream runs, ambiguous findings surface late, I resolve them by hand because no one else has the context or the authority to call it.
- The fix is upstream: at scoping, name (a) who owns the call, (b) what evidence is in scope, and (c) what evidence is explicitly out of scope. Write it down, not in my head.
- Expected effect: less of my time spent adjudicating in the last mile; cleaner handoffs to Ines on routine work; fewer "Riley said" interpretations that should have been a written boundary.
- This is the one I want to be visibly better at next year, not a list of five.

## What I did NOT do this year (worth naming)
- I did not ship a headline launch. The work was mostly judgment-shaped, and the wins are "we did not overclaim X" rather than "we shipped Y."
- I am calling that out so the review does not get read against a launch-shaped template.

## Open questions for Priya (plain)
1. Does the scoped Helio finding read as a real win, or does it need the broader onboarding claim attached to count?
2. Is "delegated routine, retained judgment" the right frame, or do you want it phrased as a team/org outcome rather than my personal one?
3. On the improvement area — do you want one improvement area or is the expectation two? I went with one because it's the one I actually plan to move.
4. Anything from the second half of the year you want surfaced that I'm not naming here?

arguments.title: Helio Start — Authority-Diagnostic Closeout
arguments.body:
Helio Start — Final Authority-Diagnostic Closeout
==================================================

Window status: closed. All 60 enrolled workspaces have completed 45-day support windows. Results below are the final read on the cohort.

1. Complete results
-------------------

Enrolled workspaces (post-admission):        60
Workspaces that contacted support:           17 (28% of cohort)
Total post-admission human minutes:          486

Authority cases (owner-level permission, network allowlist, or other external-system authority):
  Workspaces:                                  7
  Human minutes:                               301  (61.9% of all support minutes)
  Median resolution time:                      3.6 business days
  Substantive repeat contacts:                 12

Product-guidance cases:
  Workspaces:                                  10
  Human minutes:                               185  (38.1% of all support minutes)
  Median resolution time:                      1.4 days
  Substantive repeat contacts:                 6

Every authority case had already passed Helio admin-proof and connector-authentication checks before contacting support. Authority friction was not surfaced by either gate.

2. Supported interpretation
---------------------------

External-system authority is a separate readiness input from Helio admin proof and connector authentication. The diagnostic confirms that passing Helio's two in-product gates does not, by itself, establish that a workspace is operationally ready to use the product end-to-end. A third input — owner-level permission, network allowlist, or comparable external-authority grant — must also be in place, and it is not currently observable from within Helio.

This interpretation is supported by the shape of the data: authority cases concentrate human minutes (301 of 486, ~62%), have the longer median resolution (3.6 vs 1.4 business days), and generate twice the repeat-contact rate per case (12 repeats across 7 cases = 1.71 repeats/case) compared with product-guidance cases (6 repeats across 10 cases = 0.60 repeats/case). The gap is consistent with a class of blocker that lives outside Helio's product surface and therefore cannot be cleared by Helio-side remediation in the same window.

3. Operating boundaries — unchanged
-----------------------------------

- The existing admission rule is unchanged. Helio admin proof and connector authentication remain the in-product admission gates, and workspaces continue to be admitted when both pass.
- The existing routing rule is unchanged. Post-admission support cases continue to route through current triage.
- These results do not describe all onboarding or support demand as broken. Product-guidance cases (10 workspaces, 185 minutes, 1.4-day median) reflect normal post-adoption support volume and resolve within expected windows. The closeout is specifically about the authority subset, not a general statement about onboarding health.
- No change is being proposed to admission criteria, routing, or support staffing as part of this closeout.

4. What this closes
-------------------

- The diagnostic question of whether authority friction is a Helio-side or external-side phenomenon: answered — external-side, not surfaced by current gates.
- The diagnostic question of magnitude within the cohort: answered — 7 of 60 workspaces, 301 of 486 minutes, 3.6-business-day median, 12 repeats.

What remains open: how to make external-authority readiness observable earlier in the lifecycle (e.g., a pre-admission authority-readiness signal). That is a separate workstream and is not in scope for this closeout.

# Method card — 2024 Helio Start authority diagnostic
**Status:** historical. Captures the method as it was actually run in 2024
under BRIEF-2026-04-helio-start-high-effort-blocker-diagnostic. Every boundary
below is fixed record from that diagnostic, not a live rule and not a
proposal. Reuse the structure; do not reuse the numbers.

---

## 1. Enrollment setup
- **Cohort:** first 60 Helio Start workspaces admitted 2024-10-01 through
  2024-10-28.
- **Admission gate (unchanged during the diagnostic):** Helio admin proof and
  connector authentication. Workspaces are admitted when both pass.
- **Per-workspace support window:** 45 calendar days, measured from each
  workspace's own `admitted_at` (NOT a single cohort-wide start date).
- **Duplicate treatment:** raw enrollment rows are deduplicated to unique
  workspaces before the cohort count; later state is captured as forward
  events, never folded back into the enrollment snapshot.
- **Missing-field handling:** if a source admission record is present and only
  a derived field (e.g. `support_window_start`) is missing, reconstruct the
  derived field from the present source value — do not drop the row and do
  not invent a date.
- **Cap:** 60. The diagnostic does not widen or relabel this.

## 2. Window (primary close + fallback close)
- **Primary close: 2024-12-12**, available ONLY if the cohort reaches 60 by
  2024-10-28. 2024-12-12 = 2024-10-28 + 45 calendar days and assumes each of
  the 60 enrolled workspaces completes its 45-day window inside that span.
- **Fallback close:** if the 60-by-2024-10-28 enrollment gate fails, closure
  waits until every enrolled workspace has a complete 45-day window measured
  from its own admission date; closure lands on the latest of those
  per-workspace endpoints.
- **What the window is NOT:** it is not a sending policy, a rollout gate, a
  pipeline claim, or a forecast. It is purely a cohort-completion gate.
- **Slip rule:** the 2024-12-12 primary close slips only on the enrollment
  gate (cohort fails to reach 60 by 2024-10-28). No other reason moves it.

## 3. Prospective classification categories
Every enrolled workspace is classified once on admission into one of three
buckets, using the same taxonomy the 2024-09-09 retrospective pass had used:

- **External access or authority** — a third party (parent-company identity
  admin, network/allowlist owner, vendor) had to grant permission, scope, or
  connectivity before setup could complete. The customer's own admin chain
  was typically present; the blocker was decision rights living elsewhere.
- **Product guidance** — the customer needed Helio-side help to configure,
  map, or understand the product (e.g. lifecycle-stage mapping, entitlement
  setup). No external-party access or authority dependency.
- **Mixed** — both an external-authority component AND a product-guidance
  component were present in the same case. Each component is named with its
  supporting event; a mixed row is not a default category.

Classification is layered on top of, not in place of, admission. It does not
change live admission, pending-state, or assisted-routing rules.

## 4. Tracked support outcomes
Three measurements, same accounting basis across all buckets:

- **Resolution time** — business days from case entry to resolution.
  Per-bucket median is reported; an n=1 bucket is flagged as a single-case
  figure, not a median.
- **Substantive repeat contacts** — agreed 2024-09-19 rule carried forward:
  system acknowledgements are NOT substantive and do not count; a repeat
  counts only on a new substantive contact after initial case entry.
  Concretely: an agent question requesting info = substantive; a customer
  answer adding info = substantive; a courtesy/status with no new info =
  NOT substantive.
- **Support minutes (agent-minutes)** — summed active human labor across
  agents, with concurrent agents each counted. Auto-acknowledgements count
  zero and are excluded.

A separate measure is retained alongside and is NOT substituted for, combined
with, or aggregated into agent-minutes:

- **Elapsed customer-blocked time** — wall-clock time the customer's setup
  or operation was blocked. Reported side by side with agent-minutes.
  Auto-acknowledgements count zero here as well.

Total minutes reconcile to the cohort; per-bucket minutes reconcile to the
total. Repeat contacts reconcile across buckets.

## 5. Completion rule
Close is a cohort-completion gate, not a judgment call:

- Primary close fires on 2024-12-12 only if the 60-by-2024-10-28 enrollment
  gate has been met.
- If that gate fails, the diagnostic stays open until the fallback close
  date — the latest per-workspace 45-day endpoint across enrolled
  workspaces — and closes then.
- Close cannot fire earlier than either rule allows, regardless of how
  clean the data looks.

Close delivers, per bucket, on the enrolled workspaces:

- Resolution time
- Substantive repeat contacts
- Support minutes

Using the same three-bucket taxonomy as the classification step. Close
delivers the read; it does not authorize intake, routing, lifecycle, or
staffing changes by itself.

## 6. Operating changes — what the original eight cases DID and DID NOT justify

### Did NOT justify (explicit exclusions, named in the brief)
The eight retrospective cases (8 workspaces, 472 post-admission minutes,
bucketed 4 access-or-authority / 3 product-guidance / 1 mixed) did not
justify:

- Intake changes
- Lifecycle-email changes
- Support-staffing changes
- Broad onboarding changes
- Any causal-lift, broad-rollout, or forecast credit
- Reclassification of the parent audit cohort (52 workspaces, 30 complete /
  22 immature, 23 paid-active / 4 canceled / 2 past due / 1 billing hold)
  — that cohort was retained as-is, not reclassified

The eight cases justified a narrower, prospective-layer diagnostic — and
that is all they justified on their own.

### DID justify
The closed prospective diagnostic (60 workspaces, 17 contacted support,
486 post-admission minutes: 7 access-or-authority / 301 minutes /
3.6-business-day median / 12 substantive repeats; 10 product-guidance /
185 minutes / 1.4-day median / 6 repeats; every authority case had already
passed Helio admin proof and connector authentication) supported:

- A scoped interpretation: **external-system authority is a separate
  readiness input** from Helio admin proof and connector authentication —
  not a subset of either, and not observable from within Helio.
- A **targeted intake change** (approved 2024-12-16): applicants must
  separately confirm that they — or an available owner — can perform the
  owner-level permission or network-allowlist action required by the
  connector selected for first-week setup. Verified yes → continue. No or
  not sure → route to Customer Success before admission.
- **Ownership of the new readiness state:**
  - Daniela records external-authority readiness as a separate state.
  - Ines holds setup prompts while that state is pending.
  - Owen reports it separately so support effects can be evaluated in
    isolation.

### What the intake change is NOT (do not conflate)
The intake change is additive only. It does NOT replace or broaden:

- Helio admin proof (existing, unchanged)
- Connector authentication (existing, unchanged)
- Entitlement, billing, or deployment requirements (existing, unchanged)
- Live admission rules (unchanged)
- Pending-state rules (unchanged)
- Assisted-routing rules (unchanged)
- The existing admission and routing rules in general

It is a new, standalone gate whose effect is reported on its own cut — not
folded back into the admission baseline.

---

## 7. Reuse notes (how to apply this card elsewhere)
- The method (cohort → classify → measure → close → interpret) is reusable.
  The numbers, the cohort, and the window dates are not.
- Treat any future diagnostic of similar shape as a new investigation with
  its own brief, its own cohort boundary, its own close condition, and its
  own unchanged-rules list. Do not import the 2024 closeout as policy.
- Keep three-input readiness thinking (admin proof / connector auth /
  external-system authority) available as a diagnostic lens, not as a
  standing product requirement. Apply it only where the cohort supports it.
- Hold the separation between "evidence" and "operating change" tightly:
  close delivers a read, never a change. A change proposal that flows from
  a close is its own workstream with its own approval.

# Method card — 2024 Helio Start authority diagnostic
**Status:** historical. Captures the method as it was actually run in 2024
under BRIEF-2026-04-helio-start-high-effort-blocker-diagnostic. Every boundary
below is fixed record from that diagnostic, not a live rule and not a
proposal. Reuse the structure; do not reuse the numbers.

---

## 1. Enrollment setup
- **Cohort:** first 60 Helio Start workspaces admitted 2024-10-01 through
  2024-10-28.
- **Admission gate (unchanged during the diagnostic):** Helio admin proof and
  connector authentication. Workspaces are admitted when both pass.
- **Per-workspace support window:** 45 calendar days, measured from each
  workspace's own `admitted_at` (NOT a single cohort-wide start date).
- **Duplicate treatment:** raw enrollment rows are deduplicated to unique
  workspaces before the cohort count; later state is captured as forward
  events, never folded back into the enrollment snapshot.
- **Missing-field handling:** if a source admission record is present and only
  a derived field (e.g. `support_window_start`) is missing, reconstruct the
  derived field from the present source value — do not drop the row and do
  not invent a date.
- **Cap:** 60. The diagnostic does not widen or relabel this.

## 2. Window (primary close + fallback close)
- **Primary close: 2024-12-12**, available ONLY if the cohort reaches 60 by
  2024-10-28. 2024-12-12 = 2024-10-28 + 45 calendar days and assumes each of
  the 60 enrolled workspaces completes its 45-day window inside that span.
- **Fallback close:** if the 60-by-2024-10-28 enrollment gate fails, closure
  waits until every enrolled workspace has a complete 45-day window measured
  from its own admission date; closure lands on the latest of those
  per-workspace endpoints.
- **What the window is NOT:** it is not a sending policy, a rollout gate, a
  pipeline claim, or a forecast. It is purely a cohort-completion gate.
- **Slip rule:** the 2024-12-12 primary close slips only on the enrollment
  gate (cohort fails to reach 60 by 2024-10-28). No other reason moves it.

## 3. Prospective classification categories
Every enrolled workspace is classified once on admission into one of three
buckets, using the same taxonomy the 2024-09-09 retrospective pass had used:

- **External access or authority** — a third party (parent-company identity
  admin, network/allowlist owner, vendor) had to grant permission, scope, or
  connectivity before setup could complete. The customer's own admin chain
  was typically present; the blocker was decision rights living elsewhere.
- **Product guidance** — the customer needed Helio-side help to configure,
  map, or understand the product (e.g. lifecycle-stage mapping, entitlement
  setup). No external-party access or authority dependency.
- **Mixed** — both an external-authority component AND a product-guidance
  component were present in the same case. Each component is named with its
  supporting event; a mixed row is not a default category.

Classification is layered on top of, not in place of, admission. It does not
change live admission, pending-state, or assisted-routing rules.

## 4. Tracked support outcomes
Three measurements, same accounting basis across all buckets:

- **Resolution time** — business days from case entry to resolution.
  Per-bucket median is reported; an n=1 bucket is flagged as a single-case
  figure, not a median.
- **Substantive repeat contacts** — agreed 2024-09-19 rule carried forward:
  system acknowledgements are NOT substantive and do not count; a repeat
  counts only on a new substantive contact after initial case entry.
  Concretely: an agent question requesting info = substantive; a customer
  answer adding info = substantive; a courtesy/status with no new info =
  NOT substantive.
- **Support minutes (agent-minutes)** — summed active human labor across
  agents, with concurrent agents each counted. Auto-acknowledgements count
  zero and are excluded.

A separate measure is retained alongside and is NOT substituted for, combined
with, or aggregated into agent-minutes:

- **Elapsed customer-blocked time** — wall-clock time the customer's setup
  or operation was blocked. Reported side by side with agent-minutes.
  Auto-acknowledgements count zero here as well.

Total minutes reconcile to the cohort; per-bucket minutes reconcile to the
total. Repeat contacts reconcile across buckets.

## 5. Completion rule
Close is a cohort-completion gate, not a judgment call:

- Primary close fires on 2024-12-12 only if the 60-by-2024-10-28 enrollment
  gate has been met.
- If that gate fails, the diagnostic stays open until the fallback close
  date — the latest per-workspace 45-day endpoint across enrolled
  workspaces — and closes then.
- Close cannot fire earlier than either rule allows, regardless of how
  clean the data looks.

Close delivers, per bucket, on the enrolled workspaces:

- Resolution time
- Substantive repeat contacts
- Support minutes

Using the same three-bucket taxonomy as the classification step. Close
delivers the read; it does not authorize intake, routing, lifecycle, or
staffing changes by itself.

## 6. Operating changes — what the original eight cases DID and DID NOT justify

### Did NOT justify (explicit exclusions, named in the brief)
The eight retrospective cases (8 workspaces, 472 post-admission minutes,
bucketed 4 access-or-authority / 3 product-guidance / 1 mixed) did not
justify:

- Intake changes
- Lifecycle-email changes
- Support-staffing changes
- Broad onboarding changes
- Any causal-lift, broad-rollout, or forecast credit
- Reclassification of the parent audit cohort (52 workspaces, 30 complete /
  22 immature, 23 paid-active / 4 canceled / 2 past due / 1 billing hold)
  — that cohort was retained as-is, not reclassified

The eight cases justified a narrower, prospective-layer diagnostic — and
that is all they justified on their own.

### DID justify
The closed prospective diagnostic (60 workspaces, 17 contacted support,
486 post-admission minutes: 7 access-or-authority / 301 minutes /
3.6-business-day median / 12 substantive repeats; 10 product-guidance /
185 minutes / 1.4-day median / 6 repeats; every authority case had already
passed Helio admin proof and connector authentication) supported:

- A scoped interpretation: **external-system authority is a separate
  readiness input** from Helio admin proof and connector authentication —
  not a subset of either, and not observable from within Helio.
- A **targeted intake change** (approved 2024-12-16): applicants must
  separately confirm that they — or an available owner — can perform the
  owner-level permission or network-allowlist action required by the
  connector selected for first-week setup. Verified yes → continue. No or
  not sure → route to Customer Success before admission.
- **Ownership of the new readiness state:**
  - Daniela records external-authority readiness as a separate state.
  - Ines holds setup prompts while that state is pending.
  - Owen reports it separately so support effects can be evaluated in
    isolation.

### What the intake change is NOT (do not conflate)
The intake change is additive only. It does NOT replace or broaden:

- Helio admin proof (existing, unchanged)
- Connector authentication (existing, unchanged)
- Entitlement, billing, or deployment requirements (existing, unchanged)
- Live admission rules (unchanged)
- Pending-state rules (unchanged)
- Assisted-routing rules (unchanged)
- The existing admission and routing rules in general

It is a new, standalone gate whose effect is reported on its own cut — not
folded back into the admission baseline.

---

## 7. Reuse notes (how to apply this card elsewhere)
- The method (cohort → classify → measure → close → interpret) is reusable.
  The numbers, the cohort, and the window dates are not.
- Treat any future diagnostic of similar shape as a new investigation with
  its own brief, its own cohort boundary, its own close condition, and its
  own unchanged-rules list. Do not import the 2024 closeout as policy.
- Keep three-input readiness thinking (admin proof / connector auth /
  external-system authority) available as a diagnostic lens, not as a
  standing product requirement. Apply it only where the cohort supports it.
- Hold the separation between "evidence" and "operating change" tightly:
  close delivers a read, never a change. A change proposal that flows from
  a close is its own workstream with its own approval.

CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews — Ines authority reference
Effective: 2028-01-01. Anchored to the 12/1 Ines authority ruling; Q4 dev hold 12/8 did not change Ines's auth.

Purpose
Codify the boundary for routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews: what Ines may close and own (routine operator guidance, no line-by-line approval), what must be escalated, and what sits outside this lane entirely.

Anchors
- Ines 12/1 ruling: 2 op-wording clarifications = routine + non-state-changing; incomplete setup that is a non-admin state change = escalated, no release; Ines auth unchanged through Q4 dev hold 12/8.
- Pre-launch QA standing rule: staging first; isolated campaign at $0; no eligibility-flow entry; Daniela ack required. "Paused" = V11 bypass.
- Expansion Assist lane: descriptive only; keep disputed/cross/exec; no routine line-edit; releases/rebases route to Daniela.
- CS coverage window: 8a–6p Central.

Ines may close without line-by-line approval
- Routine operator-wording clarifications on auto-nudge copy that do not change the messaging state (e.g., typo fixes, phrasing polish, clarification of an existing operator note where the underlying rule/flow is unchanged).
- Tag/categorization cleanups within an already-approved auto-nudge campaign that do not alter send logic, audience, or eligibility.
- Documentation-only edits to the operator-facing runbook for an auto-nudge that is already live and approved.

Must escalate to Riley (or Daniela where flagged)
- Any change that alters the messaging state itself (pause/play, queue, throttle, send-window, eligibility filter, frequency cap).
- Any change that would let a message enter or bypass the eligibility-flow (lifecycle kickoff/cert lane) — even if wording-only, this is the pre-launch QA gate, not routine.
- Incomplete-setup items where the fix would constitute a non-admin state change (per the 12/1 ruling: escalated, no release).
- Anything disputed, cross-workstream, or exec-facing — route to Daniela.
- Anything touching Expansion Assist scope: descriptive-only constraint applies; releases/rebases go to Daniela.

Outside this authority (does not belong in this lane)
- Pre-launch QA staging campaign decisions: staging-first, $0 isolated, no eligibility-flow entry, Daniela ack. This gate is separate from routine review and is not closable by routine operator review.
- Eligibility-flow / lifecycle kickoff or certification routing (Priya's #lifecycle-systems lane).
- Admin state changes (account-level, billing-level, integration-level) — never routine, always escalated.
- Cross-workstream or executive-touchpoint items — Daniela, not Ines.

Open items / needs confirmation before relying on this in production
- The exact list of auto-nudge campaigns/states in scope for routine review (confirm against current CS tooling inventory).
- Whether "auto-nudge messaging-state" includes queued/throttled states as well as pause/play — confirm scope wording with Daniela before Ines treats throttling as routine.
- Confirm the operator-facing runbook owner and edit access for Ines on the live auto-nudge docs.

# Q4 Pricing Path Clarity Test — LIVE

**Status:** LIVE (launched 2025-10-20, Daniela)
**Split:** 50/50, organic pricing-page sessions only
**Stabilization cohort ends:** 2025-11-16
**Read window:** open after 2025-11-16; no result implied before then

## Launch
Daniela launched the test today at 50/50 on organic pricing-page sessions after the **audience, path-selection, admission, and support-routing events passed validation**. Ines confirmed treatment introduces no new lifecycle branch.

## Boundaries (all unchanged from approved design — confirm before any change)
- Admission: unchanged
- Eligibility: unchanged
- Refusal: unchanged
- Connector-access: unchanged
- External-authority: unchanged
- Lifecycle: unchanged (treatment introduces no new branch)
- Instrumentation: unchanged
- Assisted support-routing: unchanged (CS retains existing assisted routes)
- Acquisition boundaries: unchanged
- **Excluded:** paid traffic, pipeline targets, forecast credit

## Attribution freeze
Clean-attribution freeze in effect through **2025-11-16**. Unrelated pricing-page layout and UI work is frozen through the same date.

## Important framing
The live test does **not** make treatment the default experience, and implies **no result before the stabilized read**. Do not characterize outcomes, surface wins, or feed forecast/credit off this test until the read window opens.

## Validation passed at launch
- Audience event
- Path-selection event
- Admission event
- Support-routing event

## Routing during the freeze
- State-meaning / disputes / corrections / incident-stops → Riley
- Eng release / rollback → Daniela
- Routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews → Ines (does not include this test)

arguments.body:
# Q4 Pricing Path Clarity Test — Bounded, Organic-Only

Treating clearer pricing-page paths as a **controlled test**, not a launch.

## Status

**Approved 2025-10-13 by Priya** — scope, design, thresholds, stabilization requirement, and boundaries **unchanged** from the 2025-10-10 design. **In progress**; test window opened 2025-10-20. **Live** as of 2025-10-20 (Daniela launch; audience, path-selection, admission, and support-routing events passed validation; Ines confirmed no new lifecycle branch in treatment and CS retains existing assisted routes). **Interim checkpoint 2025-11-03** after Owen's cohorts 1 and 2 — see §13. **Interim checkpoint 2025-11-10** after Owen's cohort 3 — see §14. **Data collection complete as of 2025-11-17**: the November 10–16 stabilization window ended and Owen reported the stabilization-cohort extract was complete; **final four-cohort rollup certification was pending** — see §15. **Four-cohort rollup certified by Owen 2025-11-19**; primary path-quality threshold met and both guardrails held; **recommended action: adopt treatment for organic traffic, every admission and acquisition boundary unchanged, treatment remains non-default pending Priya's 2025-11-25 result decision** — see §16. **No paid-acquisition, pipeline, forecast, revenue-lift, or Helio Start eligibility change claim is being made on this update.**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Owner | Riley |
| Reviewer / approver | Priya — **approved 2025-10-13** (scope and thresholds unchanged); **2025-11-25 result-decision date held** |
| Result-decision date | **2025-11-25** (certification in hand; decision date held) |
| Window | 2025-10-20 → 2025-11-16 |
| Population | Pricing-page sessions, 50/50 split |
| Traffic | Organic only |
| Treatment | Helio Start (under-50, simple-deployment) and assisted path get **separate, clearly-labeled entry points** |
| Primary threshold | ≥25% relative reduction in Helio Start eligibility-flow starts that later route out for an existing unsupported condition |
| Guardrail 1 | Eligible-workspace admission completion: **no more than 1.5 pp decline** |
| Guardrail 2 | Account-level support time at p90: **no more than 10-min increase** |
| Read cadence (Owen) | 3 full weekly cohorts + 11/10–11/16 stabilization cohort |
| Certification state | **Certified by Owen 2025-11-19** (primary met, both guardrails held, no unrelated pricing-page layout or UI change) |
| Recommended action (Riley) | **Adopt treatment for organic traffic; every admission and acquisition boundary unchanged; treatment remains non-default pending Priya's 2025-11-25 result decision** |
| Status | **In progress (approved, live, certified, recommendation issued; rollout pending Priya 2025-11-25)** |

## 1. Why a test, not a launch

Pricing-page path clarity has been floated as a launch lever, but the eligible-workspace admission path and the message-state guide for the connector-adjacent product area already moved earlier in Q3. We do not want to stack another surface change into the same quarter without a controlled read on whether the clarity gain is real and whether it hurts conversion or support load. This brief frames the change as a **bounded organic-only test** with explicit thresholds so we get a clean signal before any rollout decision.

## 2. Hypothesis

If we give the bounded under-50, simple-deployment Helio Start path and the assisted path separate entry points on the pricing page, then users with an existing unsupported condition self-route to the assisted path more often before starting Helio Start, reducing wasted eligibility-flow starts that later route out — without hurting eligible-workspace admission completion or support load.

## 3. Population & split

- **Population:** all pricing-page sessions in the test window.
- **Split:** 50/50, deterministic at the session level (specifics locked with Ines before 10/20).
- **Exclusions:** paid traffic (out of scope by design); internal/staff sessions.

## 4. Treatment (control vs. variant)

- **Control:** current single pricing-page entry to the Helio Start / assisted paths.
- **Variant:** two separate entry points —
  1. **Helio Start** — clearly labeled for the bounded under-50, simple-deployment profile.
  2. **Assisted path** — clearly labeled for everything else.

No eligibility logic changes. No refusal-message changes. No connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, or support-routing rule changes. **All existing rules remain unchanged.**

## 5. What is explicitly NOT changing

- Eligibility / refusal rules (Ines Q3 message-state guide, state #1 owner-permission/allowlist logic, state #2 connector auth, state #3 entitlement, state #4 qualifying-human-admin, state #5 active CS adoption/renewal).
- Connector access and external-system authority.
- Lifecycle / nurture messaging, including the routine CS auto-nudge pathway Ines has authority over.
- Instrumentation schema, event names, funnel definitions.
- Support routing and the 5-state dispute/correction channel (which still routes to Riley).

## 6. Primary metric

**≥25% relative reduction** in *Helio Start eligibility-flow starts that later route out for an existing unsupported condition*, treatment vs. control.

Defined as: starts of the Helio Start eligibility flow from pricing-page sessions, where the session ends in an existing-condition route-out (per the current refusal-message taxonomy). Denominator = Helio Start eligibility-flow starts, not pricing-page sessions, so the metric is robust to overall traffic mix.

## 7. Guardrails

1. **Eligible-workspace admission completion** — absolute change, treatment vs. control: **no more than a 1.5 percentage-point decline** over the full window. Read against the same-week control baseline; compared against pre-test 4-week baseline for context.
2. **Account-level support time at p90** — **no more than a 10-minute increase** vs. control p90 over the full window.

Either guardrail breach = stop and investigate; no auto-roll-forward.

## 8. Read plan (Owen)

- **Cohort 1:** 10/20–10/26 ✓ delivered 2025-10-27
- **Cohort 2:** 10/27–11/02 ✓ delivered 2025-11-03
- **Cohort 3:** 11/03–11/09 ✓ delivered 2025-11-10
- **Stabilization cohort:** 11/10–11/16 ✓ extract complete 2025-11-17
- **Final four-cohort rollup certification:** ✓ **certified by Owen 2025-11-19** — primary threshold met, both guardrails held, no unrelated pricing-page layout or UI change

Owen reads all three full weekly cohorts **plus** the 11/10–11/16 stabilization cohort. Decision-read package assembled after certification; **result-decision date 2025-11-25** (held).

## 9. Hard rules during the test (boundaries)

- **No paid traffic** in or out of the test population.
- **No pipeline target** changes attributed to this workstream.
- **No forecast credit** taken on any directional signal until decision date.
- **No unrelated pricing-page layout or UI changes** during the test window (any incidental change to the pricing page is a protocol breach and pauses the read). **Confirmed through 2025-11-16: no unrelated pricing-page layout or UI change occurred. Confirmed by Owen at 2025-11-19 certification: no unrelated pricing-page layout or UI change occurred across the test window.**

## 10. Decision framework (post-read)

- **Ship / roll forward** if primary threshold met and both guardrails hold across the three full cohorts and the stabilization cohort.
- **Hold** if primary signal is mixed across cohorts, even if guardrails hold.
- **Roll back / do not roll forward** if either guardrail breaches, or if the primary metric shows no directional movement by end of stabilization cohort.

**Read outcome 2025-11-19:** primary threshold met (≥25% relative reduction observed); both guardrails held across all four cohorts; no unrelated pricing-page layout or UI change occurred. **Ship / roll forward path is open.** See §16.

## 11. Cross-references

- Ines Q3 message-state guide (5 states; owner-permission / connector-auth / entitlement / qualifying-human-admin / active CS adoption & renewal) — **unchanged** for this test.
- Ines's Growth 10/8 + Tomás 10/8 auto-nudge authority — **not** in scope here; this test does not touch routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews, Helio Start reporting cadence, Expansion Assist selection, or lifecycle preflight.
- Board op segment 12/10/25 10:10–10:30 CT, pre-read 12/5 — this test's read package feeds the deck but stays **separate** from Helio Start, retained-mid Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and system controls (per deck rule).

## 12. Approvals

- Priya — **approved 2025-10-13** (scope, design, thresholds, stabilization requirement, and boundaries **unchanged** from 2025-10-10)
- Result-decision date — **2025-11-25** (Owen certified the four-cohort rollup 2025-11-19; the decision date itself is held; treatment remains non-default pending Priya's result decision)

## 13. Interim checkpoint — cohorts 1 and 2 (2025-11-03)

Two complete weekly cohorts delivered by Owen (10/20–10/26 and 10/27–11/02) point in the same favorable direction on the primary endpoint, and both guardrails remain within their pre-registered limits. **The third complete weekly cohort (11/03–11/09) and the 11/10–11/16 stabilization cohort are still required before any read.** The test remains live; treatment remains non-default; no rollout, default-experience, revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast claim is being made on this checkpoint.

### Cohort 1 — 2025-10-20 to 2025-10-26 (delivered 2025-10-27)
- Organic pricing-page sessions: **781 total** — 389 control / 392 treatment
- Helio Start eligibility-flow starts: **82 control / 86 treatment**
- Starts later routed out for an existing unsupported condition: **9/82 control (11.0%)** vs **7/86 treatment (8.1%)**
- Eligible-workspace admission completion: **43.9% control** vs **44.2% treatment**
- Account-level support time at p90: **70 min control** vs **73 min treatment**

### Cohort 2 — 2025-10-27 to 2025-11-02 (delivered 2025-11-03)
- Organic pricing-page sessions: **832 total** — 414 control / 418 treatment
- Helio Start eligibility-flow starts: **87 control / 89 treatment**
- Starts later routed out for an existing unsupported condition: **10/87 control (11.5%)** vs **6/89 treatment (6.7%)**
- Eligible-workspace admission completion: **43.7% control** vs **44.0% treatment**
- Account-level support time at p90: **72 min control** vs **75 min treatment**

### Direction read (not a result)
- **Primary endpoint (post-start route-out for an existing unsupported condition):** treatment is lower than control in both cohorts (cohort 1: 8.1% vs 11.0%; cohort 2: 6.7% vs 11.5%). Same direction across both weekly reads. Not a result — directional only.
- **Guardrail 1 — eligible-workspace admission completion:** treatment is fractionally *higher* than control in both cohorts (+0.3 pp cohort 1, +0.3 pp cohort 2). Inside the ≤1.5 pp decline limit.
- **Guardrail 2 — account-level support time at p90:** treatment is +3 min vs control in cohort 1, +3 min in cohort 2. Inside the ≤10 min limit.
- **Volume:** clean 50/50 split both weeks; no operational flags.

### Still required before any read (as of 2025-11-03)
- **Cohort 3 — 2025-11-03 to 2025-11-09** (in flight as of 2025-11-03).
- **Stabilization cohort — 2025-11-10 to 2025-11-16** (required per §8).
- **Clean-attribution freeze through 2025-11-16** remains in effect; unrelated pricing-page layout and UI work remains frozen.
- **Decision-read package** assembled at end of stabilization cohort; **result-decision date 2025-11-25** (unchanged).

### Framing guard (carried into any external communication of the 2025-11-03 checkpoint)

- **Out-of-scope items unchanged:** paid traffic, pipeline targets, forecast credit, and unrelated pricing-page layout/UI changes remain excluded (unchanged from §9).

### Boundaries unchanged at the 2025-11-03 checkpoint
- **Admission, eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, assisted support-routing, and acquisition boundaries** remain unchanged from the 2025-10-13 approved design.
- **Clean-attribution freeze through 2025-11-16** remains in effect.

## 14. Interim checkpoint — cohort 3 (2025-11-10)

The third complete weekly cohort has been delivered by Owen (11/03–11/09). **This is an explicitly interim checkpoint.** The 11/10–11/16 stabilization cohort has only begun as of this update and is still required before any read.

Treatment lower than control on the post-start route-out for an existing unsupported condition. # Q4 Pricing Path Clarity Test — Bounded, Organic-Only

Treating clearer pricing-page paths as a **controlled test**, not a launch.

## TL;DR

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Owner | Riley |
| Reviewer / approver | Priya — **approval pending** |
| Result-decision date | **pending** Priya approval |
| Window | 2025-10-20 → 2025-11-16 |
| Population | Pricing-page sessions, 50/50 split |
| Traffic | Organic only |
| Treatment | Helio Start (under-50, simple-deployment) and assisted path get **separate, clearly-labeled entry points** |
| Primary threshold | ≥25% relative reduction in Helio Start eligibility-flow starts that later route out for an existing unsupported condition |
| Guardrail 1 | Eligible-workspace admission completion: **no more than 1.5 pp decline** |
| Guardrail 2 | Account-level support time at p90: **no more than 10-min increase** |
| Read cadence (Owen) | 3 full weekly cohorts + 11/10–11/16 stabilization cohort |

## 1. Why a test, not a launch

Pricing-page path clarity has been floated as a launch lever, but the eligible-workspace admission path and the message-state guide for the connector-adjacent product area already moved earlier in Q3. We do not want to stack another surface change into the same quarter without a controlled read on whether the clarity gain is real and whether it hurts conversion or support load. This brief frames the change as a **bounded organic-only test** with explicit thresholds so we get a clean signal before any rollout decision.

## 2. Hypothesis

If we give the bounded under-50, simple-deployment Helio Start path and the assisted path separate entry points on the pricing page, then users with an existing unsupported condition self-route to the assisted path more often before starting Helio Start, reducing wasted eligibility-flow starts that later route out — without hurting eligible-workspace admission completion or support load.

## 3. Population & split

- **Population:** all pricing-page sessions in the test window.
- **Split:** 50/50, deterministic at the session level (specifics to be locked with Ines before 10/20).
- **Exclusions:** paid traffic (out of scope by design); internal/staff sessions.

## 4. Treatment (control vs. variant)

- **Control:** current single pricing-page entry to the Helio Start / assisted paths.
- **Variant:** two separate entry points —
  1. **Helio Start** — clearly labeled for the bounded under-50, simple-deployment profile.
  2. **Assisted path** — clearly labeled for everything else.

No eligibility logic changes. No refusal-message changes. No connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, or support-routing rule changes. **All existing rules remain unchanged.**

## 5. What is explicitly NOT changing

- Eligibility / refusal rules (Ines Q3 message-state guide, state #1 owner-permission/allowlist logic, state #2 connector auth, state #3 entitlement, state #4 qualifying-human-admin, state #5 active CS adoption/renewal).
- Connector access and external-system authority.
- Lifecycle / nurture messaging, including the routine CS auto-nudge pathway Ines has authority over.
- Instrumentation schema, event names, funnel definitions.
- Support routing and the 5-state dispute/correction channel (which still routes to Riley).

## 6. Primary metric

**≥25% relative reduction** in *Helio Start eligibility-flow starts that later route out for an existing unsupported condition*, treatment vs. control.

Defined as: starts of the Helio Start eligibility flow from pricing-page sessions, where the session ends in an existing-condition route-out (per the current refusal-message taxonomy). Denominator = Helio Start eligibility-flow starts, not pricing-page sessions, so the metric is robust to overall traffic mix.

## 7. Guardrails

1. **Eligible-workspace admission completion** — absolute change, treatment vs. control: **no more than a 1.5 percentage-point decline** over the full window. Read against the same-week control baseline; compared against pre-test 4-week baseline for context.
2. **Account-level support time at p90** — **no more than a 10-minute increase** vs. control p90 over the full window.

Either guardrail breach = stop and investigate; no auto-roll-forward.

## 8. Read plan (Owen)

- **Cohort 1:** 10/20–10/26
- **Cohort 2:** 10/27–11/02
- **Cohort 3:** 11/03–11/09
- **Stabilization cohort:** 11/10–11/16

Owen reads all three full weekly cohorts plus the stabilization cohort. Decision-read package assembled at end of stabilization cohort; result-decision date **pending** Priya approval.

## 9. Hard rules during the test

- **No paid traffic** in or out of the test population.
- **No pipeline target** changes attributed to this workstream.
- **No forecast credit** taken on any directional signal until decision date.
- **No unrelated pricing-page layout or UI changes** during the test window (any incidental change to the pricing page is a protocol breach and pauses the read).

## 10. Decision framework (post-read)

- **Ship / roll forward** if primary threshold met and both guardrails hold across the three full cohorts and the stabilization cohort.
- **Hold** if primary signal is mixed across cohorts, even if guardrails hold.
- **Roll back / do not roll forward** if either guardrail breaches, or if the primary metric shows no directional movement by end of stabilization cohort.

## 11. Cross-references

- Ines Q3 message-state guide (5 states; owner-permission / connector-auth / entitlement / qualifying-human-admin / active CS adoption & renewal) — **unchanged** for this test.
- Ines's Growth 10/8 + Tomás 10/8 auto-nudge authority — **not** in scope here; this test does not touch routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews, Helio Start reporting cadence, Expansion Assist selection, or lifecycle preflight.
- Board op segment 12/10/25 10:10–10:30 CT, pre-read 12/5 — this test's read package feeds the deck but stays **separate** from Helio Start, retained-mid Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and system controls (per deck rule).

## 12. Approvals

- Priya — **pending**
- Result-decision date — **pending** Priya approval

# Q1 2027 Lifecycle Systems operating priorities — staff-review draft

Author: Riley Tanaka
For: December 18 staff review (owner-lane input)
Status: ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION USE — December 18, 2026. January 15, 2027 addition (Owen's monthly source-readiness check) layered on top; no prior boundary is changed. The December 4, 2026 decision remains the decision; this document is its Q1 restatement for staff review, not a new authority decision. Nothing in this document takes effect early. Anything that conflicts with the Dec 4 decision record is overridden by that record; this document surfaces the Q1 shape, not a re-decision. January 27, 2027 relabeling (Ines review): source-readiness failure labels now name the object directly (`source at risk` / `snapshot incomplete`) so they cannot read like account-state labels next to operational queues. Underlying January 15 rules are unchanged.

Owner-lane input integrated on December 15, 2026 (Owen on the first-cycle operating test; Ines on the framing of her certification). Priya's December 18, 2026 staff review completed with acceptance for implementation use; no changes to the approved model. January 15, 2027 addition (Owen's monthly source-readiness check) integrated on the same date it was decided. January 27, 2027 relabeling (Ines review) applied without changing any rule.

---

## Summary (one page)

What changes on January 5, 2027 — and what does not:
- On January 5, Riley stops attending routine monthly Lifecycle Systems preparation and source-closure reviews. Through January 4, nothing changes — Riley continues current routine preparation and source-closure attendance as today.
- The four evidence lanes stay separate. No combined growth number. No cross-lane revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast credit.
- Owner lanes are unchanged. What changes is who carries the routine cadence and what Riley attends.
- The quarterly rotating recheck of one evidence lane is the concrete independent verification activity replacing prior hands-on attendance. It does not reopen source closure, approve any other lane owner's certification, or exercise any engineering control. It is an inspection, not a second approval queue.
- Future paid Helio Start is a separate question. Nothing in this document approves traffic, budget, or scope for paid Helio Start.

## Q1 priorities — by lane (unchanged)

The four lanes are the established board-evidence lanes. They are kept separate. They are read independently. None of them is a revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast input.

- Helio Start. Lane owner: Owen (measurement) + Riley (final claims). Status through Q1: bounded-organic as it already is. Reporting inside the existing four-lane scope. Five-state model unchanged (admitted / assisted / ineligible / final-reconciliation + `pending` forward-only). `pending` stays pre-admission, NOT in the rate or activation denominator, intake additive. No Q1 launch, beta, pricing-page approval, or new consumer.
- Expansion Assist (retained-mid). Lane owner: Owen (eligibility cuts) + Ines (lifecycle governance) + Riley (final claims). Descriptive only. Causal language (drove / caused / prevented) deferred to a controlled read-out. No forecast or rollout.
- Pricing-page path quality. Lane owner: Owen (measurement) + Daniela (transport + rollout) + Riley (final claims). Lane supports only "fewer unsupported-path starts" — funnel-quality evidence, not revenue, paid-acquisition, pipeline, forecast, or eligibility.
- CS auto-nudge / system controls. Lane owner: Owen (reporting + exception explanation) + Ines (messaging-state governance) + Daniela (transport + source reliability + rollback). Lane is system-control performance, not a customer-behavior read.

## The four production consumers and their current field meanings

The four board-evidence lanes are the four production consumers of the operating state. Each lane carries the same seven required fields; "current field meanings" are what each field has meant in the deck-format operating evidence since FY26.

The seven required fields per lane (current meanings):
1. Denominator or coverage dates. What population and time window the lane covers. Read as the count plus the window, not the count alone.
2. Outcome window. The complete predeclared window the source supports. Read only inside the window; not truncated, not extended.
3. Measurement limits. What the source can and cannot say. Stated explicitly. Limits are part of the claim, not a footnote.
4. Exclusions. What is excluded from the lane's read and why. Documented. Consistent with how routine claims treat them.
5. Source owner. The named owner who certifies the lane's source completeness.
6. Reliability evidence. The evidence the source is intact (Daniela's lane inspects this; the recheck inspects it; engineering release controls stay with Daniela).
7. Revenue and forecast treatment. How the lane treats revenue and forecast. Descriptive lanes name it as descriptive. Causal/revenue/forecast decision rights are Riley's; the field records the treatment, not the decision.

These seven fields are what each lane carries today. The Jan 5 model preserves them; it changes who closes them.

## Current through January 4, 2027 — explicit

- Riley attends routine monthly Lifecycle Systems preparation and routine source-closure reviews as today.
- The four-lane cadence runs exactly as it does today. No new owner, no new role, no new authority.
- Nothing about the Dec 4 decision is in effect. It is approved; it is not yet effective.

## Effective January 5, 2027 — first January cycle

The first cycle under the new model opens Tuesday, January 5, 2027. (January 4 is a Monday and the last day of the prior routine; January 5 is the first effective day.) The cadence is unchanged in form; what changes is who carries it and how incomplete status is handled.

The first January cycle is also the explicit operating test of the new cadence. The cycle is not called successful before it closes. Specifically, the first cycle tests three operating behaviors, each visibly:

1. On-time snapshot preparation. Owen's monthly sanitized campaign snapshot is due on the second business day against the calendar, not against completion of any other step. On-time means the snapshot is delivered, in sanitized form, by the second business day. Late is recorded as late and is visible in the closure-and-exception summary.
2. Named-owner certification. Each named owner (Owen for source completeness; Ines for lifecycle governance and owner-state; Daniela for source reliability and engineering release) delivers the named certification on the fourth business day. A missing certification is recorded as missing and is visible in the closure-and-exception summary.
3. Visible incomplete state. Whenever a required field on any lane is missing or a named-owner certification is absent, the cycle's status is recorded as explicitly incomplete (label: `snapshot incomplete`). The cycle is not called successful in that state. Closure does not occur in that state.

Cadence (effective January 5, 2027):
- Second business day. Owen's monthly sanitized campaign snapshot is due. Hard date against the calendar, not against completion of any other step. (Operating test #1.)
- Fourth business day. Ines's lifecycle-governance and owner-state certification is due, delivered as an input to source closure — not as a request for Riley's routine approval. Daniela's source-reliability and release certification is due. (Operating test #2.)
- Fifth business day. Owen must either close the routine four-lane source review OR explicitly leave it incomplete. Either way, Owen sends one closure-and-exception summary — not informal follow-up fragments. The cycle is not called successful before it closes. (Operating test #3.)

Incomplete handling (explicit, not "closed with notes"):
- If any required field on any lane is missing, the lane's status is recorded as `snapshot incomplete` (label names the object; not "ready with caveats," not "closed with notes"). Incomplete is incomplete. The cycle is not called successful and closure cannot proceed in that state.
- If a named-owner certification (Owen for source completeness, Ines for lifecycle governance, Daniela's source-reliability and release certification) is not in place, the packet is incomplete (label: `certification missing` on the source-readiness check; the cycle itself records `snapshot incomplete` when it is opened without the required certifications). The cycle is not called successful and closure cannot proceed.
- Incomplete is a visible state, not a quiet one. If the cycle is incomplete on day 5, Owen records it as `snapshot incomplete` and names the missing fields, the missing certifications, and the owner-attributed reason for each in the closure-and-exception summary. The summary is the single written record for the cycle. Disputes, exceptions, and follow-ups fold into the summary, not into Slack threads, DMs, or email fragments.

The first January cycle is therefore a clean test of the new cadence under incomplete-handling rules. If a required field or certification is missing on day 2, 4, or 5, the cycle closes with the `snapshot incomplete` label and the exception summary names it. That is the intended operating behavior, not a failure — and the cycle is not called successful in that state.

## January 15, 2027 addition — Owen's monthly source-readiness check

On January 15, 2027, Riley added a pre-snapshot source-readiness check to the operating cadence. The addition operationalizes the visible-incomplete-state rule and surfaces risk one business day before the snapshot deadline. It is an addition; it does not change any boundary already stated in this document.

When. Owen runs a monthly source-readiness check at 12:00 PM Central on the business day before each sanitized campaign snapshot is due.

Per required source, three things must be visible to Owen at the check:
- Named owner.
- Exact certified through-date.
- Certification ETA.

Failure handling — two states Owen records, with labels that name the object directly so they cannot read like account-state labels next to operational queues:
- ETA after snapshot deadline. If any required source's ETA falls after the second-business-day snapshot deadline, Owen marks that source as `source at risk` and surfaces the `source at risk` state in the cycle's closure-and-exception summary. The cycle is not called successful in that state.
- Certification still absent on the snapshot due date. If a required source's certification is still absent on the day the snapshot is due, Owen opens the snapshot with the `snapshot incomplete` label. Stale data is not substituted. The cycle is not closed with stale or uncertified data.

Labeling rule (added January 27, 2027 per Ines review):
- Every source-readiness failure label must name the object directly — `source`, `certification`, or `snapshot` — in the label itself. Bare `at risk` / `incomplete` are not used next to operational queues because they read like account-state labels.
- Approved labels: `source at risk` (ETA-after-deadline), `certification missing` (named-owner cert absent at the source-readiness check), `snapshot incomplete` (certification still absent on the snapshot due date; replaces bare `visibly incomplete` / `incomplete` wording).
- The rules those labels describe are unchanged from January 15.

Boundaries this addition does NOT change:
- The second-business-day snapshot deadline is unchanged.
- The owner-certification requirement is unchanged: Owen for source completeness; Ines for lifecycle governance and owner-state; Daniela for source-reliability and engineering release. Certifications remain named-owner, not assumed.
- Source freshness limits are unchanged.
- Source meanings (what each source says and is used for) are unchanged.
- Existing authority for each owner lane is unchanged. The check is a source-readiness inspection Owen runs inside his lane; it does not exercise or override any other owner's certification.
- Fail-closed handling is unchanged. The new check surfaces risk earlier; it does not relax the rule that stale or uncertified data is never substituted, and it does not waive any required field.

Scope. The check supplements the existing cadence. It runs alongside Owen's routine snapshot preparation; it does not replace or delay any existing step. The first check under this addition runs on the business day before the next sanitized campaign snapshot is due after January 15, 2027.

What this addition is NOT:
- Not a new approval queue. It does not route to Riley on the routine path.
- Not an expansion of Owen's authority. It is a source-readiness inspection Owen runs inside his existing lane.
- Not a waiver of the second-business-day deadline. Late snapshots remain late.
- Not a relaxation of certification requirements. Missing certifications remain missing.

## The quarterly rotating recheck (one lane per quarter)

Effective January 5, 2027, Riley enters the routine cadence only via the quarterly rotating recheck of one evidence lane. The recheck is independent verification, not a second approval queue.

Shape:
- Cadence. One recheck per quarter.
- Subject. One evidence lane per quarter, picked by Riley.
- Lane selection. Only after Owen's routine packet closure for the relevant cycle is recorded. The recheck cannot shape the routine sample and cannot quietly become a second closure review.
- Inspection dimensions (fixed, five). Denominator or coverage dates; outcome window; exclusions; reliability evidence; revenue and forecast treatment.
- Safeguards (fixed, four). Does not reopen source closure; does not approve Ines's owner certification; does not exercise Daniela's release or rollback controls; does not create a second approval queue.
- Artifact. One-page recheck note per quarter, filed in the Lifecycle Systems folder by the second business day of the week following the quarter close. The note cites Owen's recorded source-completeness decision for the cycle the lane belongs to and is filed separately from the routine closure packet.
- Time budget. Half-day at most. Not a substitute for routine prep, source closure, owner certification, or engineering controls.

What the recheck is NOT:
- Not a request for Riley to approve or reject any other lane owner's certification (Owen, Ines, or Daniela).
- Not a release / suppress / restore / rollback action.
- Not a route for second approval of routine claims.
- Not a calibration instrument (the November 17 working notes were not delivered feedback and did not expand authority).

If the recheck's findings need action, they flow through the existing escalation set (see below) or as input to the next cycle's source-completeness decision — never as an amendment to the current cycle's closure.

## Escalation triggers retained (Riley enters on these)

The escalation set is closed. Six triggers. Adding a trigger requires Riley's sign-off; removing one is not on the table.

1. Missing fields in a routine packet.
2. Disputed semantics on a defined term or claim surface.
3. Cross-surface discrepancies (a number that reconciles in one surface but not another).
4. Customer corrections (a customer has flagged an inaccuracy affecting a routine claim).
5. Incident stops (anything that pauses, rolls back, or quarantines a routine cycle).
6. Executive-language decisions (any claim headed to exec, board, investor, or external comms surfaces).

Escalation is into Riley's queue, not a request to skip Riley. Owen / Ines / Daniela remain the named owners; Riley arbitrates and decides.

## Decision-owner boundaries (established, unchanged)

- Owen Pham. Routine single-path operating explanation + exception explanation. Source-completeness closure on routine packets. Within scope: monthly sanitized campaign snapshot by second business day; routine exception readouts on the four-lane scope (≤3 neutral readouts per week; stale fail-closed); Helio Start reporting as one of the existing shared-state consumers; the day-5 closure or explicit incomplete recording + closure-and-exception summary; receiving Ines's lifecycle-governance certification and Daniela's source-reliability and release certification as named-owner inputs to source closure; running the monthly source-readiness check (January 15 addition) inside his lane, including recording the `source at risk`, `certification missing`, and `snapshot incomplete` labels per the January 27 relabeling rule. Outside scope: causal / revenue / forecast / board-readiness / exec-language decisions; approval of Ines's certification; engineering release / suppress / restore / rollback controls.
- Ines Kovac. Lifecycle governance and message-state controls. Within scope: lifecycle-governance certification by fourth business day, delivered as an input to Owen's source closure (not as a request for Riley's routine approval); owner-state certification; messaging consumption tied to shared-state; Expansion Assist descriptive posture; `routine education` reclassification authority (HIGHER-RISK); boundary to Riley on disputed semantics and exec language. Outside scope: source-completeness closure; engineering release controls; causal / revenue / forecast interpretation; routine approval by Riley of her certification (her cert flows into Owen's closure decision, not into Riley's queue).
- Daniela Schultz. Transport, source reliability, and engineering release / rollback controls. Within scope: source-reliability and release certification by fourth business day, delivered as a named-owner input to Owen's source closure; the rollback path as one of the two approved restore conditions (the other is Riley-led customer correction / incident stop); reliability evidence for the recheck's fourth dimension. Outside scope: lifecycle governance; source-completeness closure; causal / revenue / forecast treatment decisions.
- Riley Tanaka. Final claim authority + the recheck + escalation. Within scope: causal / revenue / forecast / board-readiness / exec-language decisions; the quarterly rotating recheck; arbitration on the six escalation triggers; judgment-boundary ownership for cross-surface lifecycle decisions. Outside scope: routine prep; routine source-closure attendance (effective Jan 5); engineering release controls.

## Boundaries preserved at the Q1 frame (carried over from the Dec 4 decision)

- Engineering reliability and release controls remain with Daniela's organization.
- Customer Success case ownership does not transfer.
- Expansion Assist remains descriptive, not forecast.
- Helio Start intake rule remains additive; refusal semantics are unchanged; five-state model preserved.
- The shared state contract is not in production as a result of this document or the Dec 4 decision. Any production rollout requires a separate go decision with its own change-control path (Ines on governance, Daniela's org on reliability).
- Existing domain authority for each surface owner is preserved.

## Cuts (what this document does NOT do)

- Does not change lane ownership. Owen / Ines / Daniela / Riley lanes are the same.
- Does not change the four-lane scope or count.
- Does not change the seven required fields per lane or their meanings.
- Does not authorize any Q1 production rollout of a shared-state implementation.
- Does not reopen Expansion Assist's descriptive posture or convert it into a forecast input.
- Does not authorize a fifth consumer.
- Does not delegate disputed semantics, cross-surface consequences, customer-correction / incident-stop, or exec-language carry away from Riley.
- Does not imply a re-decision. The Dec 4 decision is the decision; this document surfaces its Q1 shape, accepted for implementation use without changes to the approved model.
- Does not call a cycle successful before it closes. Closure is the closing event, not an inferred state.
- Does not waive, defer, or relax any prior boundary as a result of the January 15 addition. The addition supplements the cadence; it does not change the second-business-day deadline, the owner-certification requirement, source freshness limits, source meanings, existing authority, or fail-closed handling.
- Does not change any underlying rule as a result of the January 27 relabeling. The relabeling is a labeling fix only; the rules (when Owen marks a cycle `source at risk`, when he opens a snapshot `snapshot incomplete`, and when `certification missing` is recorded) are unchanged from January 15.

## Future paid Helio Start — held separately

The future paid Helio Start question is held separately. This document does not:
- approve or imply approved traffic for paid Helio Start;
- approve or imply approved budget for paid Helio Start;
- change Helio Start's product or pricing status;
- change the existing reopen conditions (the 5/18 paid-acq cap and 8/21 denials of second-batch / pipeline / forecast credit carry forward until a separate go decision).

The paid-Helio-Start question has its own review path and its own decision owner. It is not part of the Q1 Lifecycle Systems operating priorities and is not addressed by them.

## Calls resolved at staff review (December 18)

1. Q1 shape matches the Dec 4 decision record. No amendment to a lane boundary, the recheck shape, or the escalation set was made at the staff review.
2. The four lanes stay separate through Q1. No combined growth number; no cross-lane revenue / forecast credit.
3. The seven required fields per lane and their current meanings are preserved under the Jan 5 cadence.
4. The first January cycle (Jan 5 open; second / fourth / fifth business-day cadence; explicit incomplete handling; the cycle is not called successful before it closes) is the intended operating behavior.
5. Ines's certification is delivered as an input to Owen's source closure and is not a request for Riley's routine approval.
6. No conflict between this document and the wider Q1 plan was flagged at the staff review.

## Subsequent addition (January 15, 2027)

1. Owen's monthly source-readiness check is added to the cadence. It runs at 12:00 PM Central on the business day before each sanitized campaign snapshot is due and requires named owner, exact certified through-date, and certification ETA per required source.
2. ETA after snapshot deadline → source marked `source at risk`; certification still absent on the due date → snapshot opened `snapshot incomplete`. Stale data is not substituted. The cycle is not closed with stale or uncertified data.
3. No prior boundary is changed: second-business-day deadline, owner-certification requirement, freshness limits, source meanings, existing authority, and fail-closed handling all preserved.
4. The check is a source-readiness inspection Owen runs inside his existing lane; it does not exercise or override any other owner's certification and does not route to Riley on the routine path.

## Subsequent relabeling (January 27, 2027)

1. Ines reviewed the source-readiness wording and flagged that bare `at risk` and `incomplete` could read like account-state labels next to operational queues.
2. Approved labels: `source at risk` (ETA-after-deadline), `certification missing` (certification absent at the source-readiness check), `snapshot incomplete` (certification still absent on the snapshot due date).
3. Every source-readiness failure label must name the object directly — `source`, `certification`, or `snapshot` — in the label itself.
4. No underlying January 15 rule is changed: the triggers (ETA-after-deadline, certification-absent-on-due-date), the snapshot deadline, the fail-closed rule, the named-owner requirement, the visibility rule, and Owen's lane boundary are all preserved.

---

End of document. Status: ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION USE as of December 18, 2026 staff review, with the January 15, 2027 addition layered on top, and the January 27, 2027 source-readiness relabeling applied without changing any underlying rule. The Dec 4 decision is the decision; this is its Q1 restatement accepted for implementation use without changes to the approved model.

Status: ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION USE — December 18, 2026. January 15, 2027 addition (Owen's monthly source-readiness check) layered on top; no prior boundary is changed. The December 4, 2026 decision remains the decision; this document is its Q1 restatement for staff review, not a new authority decision. Nothing in this document takes effect early. Anything that conflicts with the Dec 4 decision record is overridden by that record; this document surfaces the Q1 shape, not a re-decision. January 27, 2027 relabeling (Ines review): source-readiness failure labels now name the object directly (`source at risk` / `snapshot incomplete`) so they cannot read like account-state labels next to operational queues. Underlying January 15 rules are unchanged. January 27, 2027 (afternoon) further relabeling (Ines review): the three source-readiness failure labels are tightened again to make them unmistakably describe source readiness and snapshot certification rather than customer or messaging state (`source readiness late` / `source-readiness certification missing` / `snapshot certification incomplete`). Definitions and authorities are unchanged.

Owner-lane input integrated on December 15, 2026 (Owen on the first-cycle operating test; Ines on the framing of her certification). Priya's December 18, 2026 staff review completed with acceptance for implementation use; no changes to the approved model. January 15, 2027 addition (Owen's monthly source-readiness check) integrated on the same date it was decided. January 27, 2027 relabeling (Ines review) applied without changing any rule. January 27, 2027 (afternoon) further relabeling applied: labels only; definitions and authorities unchanged.
