arguments.body:
Q2 GROWTH OPERATING WATCHLIST — DRAFT
Owner-of-record: Riley (Growth). Drafted 2026-03-26 in response to Priya's request for a concise Q2 operating watchlist from each function (due Thursday).

Purpose: keep Q2 Growth work that is already running hot — Helio Start activation, support load, lifecycle, segment economics — readable as four separate lanes, with the denominator-and-stabilization review method applied in each lane. Not a centralized approval queue. Lane owners keep their own readouts; Riley escalates judgment calls only.

Standing method (from the 2024-03-15 Growth/CS readout practice):
- Lock the cohort denominator first; show it next to every rate.
- Stabilize before next peek: same metric and direction, n ≥ treatment size, p < 0.01 on a second look, before treating an early signal as real (vs a first-sig artifact).
- One cohort ≠ trend. Each next mature cohort reads on its own evidence.
- Provisional data is shown alongside final, never folded into the denominator.
- Rulings are 1-pagers: why / cuts / p and effect / call. Summary first; plain questions over analyst jargon.

1. HELIO START ACTIVATION
Scope: activation rate on the live Helio Start cohort definition (1st-integration / 7d / all eligible). Owen owns the readout shape and worked example; Priya owns the denom-first call.
Q2 watch items:
- Mature cohort accumulation. Do not broaden eligibility before a second mature cohort reads at the locked spec. The 3-25 first-actv cohort (67.6%) is one data point, not a trend.
- Pre-activation support (setup + permissions) is reported per 100 eligible and is shown separately from the activation rate — never folded into the activation denominator.
- Routed-pre-setup + entitlement/support-state failures are counted on their own lines and are NOT in the activation rate. Keep this visible so routing changes cannot quietly inflate activation.
- View decomposition: Owen's view stays perpendicular to the retained mid-segment + Expansion Assist view (closed 2024-02-05). Starter and retained-mid are read on separate cuts.
- First-sig protocol: if any next cohort shows a significant shift, run the same metric + direction on n ≥ treatment size and p < 0.01 BEFORE treating it as a real change — compare against a fake first-sig baseline, not against the prior cohort's noisy point.

Owner: Owen (readout shape, examples, stabilization discipline); Priya (denom-first sign-off on each cohort).

2. SUPPORT LOAD
Scope: support tickets and time-to-resolution on the Helio Start surface, including pre-activation setup and permissioning work.
Q2 watch items:
- Report support load per 100 eligible (pre-activation included), separate from post-activation tickets.
- Track routed-pre-setup + entitlement/support-state failures as a distinct count, not netted into either rate.
- Watch for routing-rule changes that would silently move tickets between the pre-activation and post-activation buckets — that is a definitional change, not a load change.
- Do not let "support load dropped" be read as "activation improved" without the activation lane saying so on its own evidence.

Owner: Support lead (TBD); Riley routes any cross-lane interpretation questions.

3. LIFECYCLE
Scope: lifecycle email program and feature-flag-gated messaging on the Helio Start surface.
Q2 watch items:
- Preserve Ines's independent lifecycle-audience-risk preflight lane. Lifecycle changes touching audience definition, suppression, or eligibility run through Ines's preflight before any flag rollout; Riley is only pulled in for judgment-call escalations, not as a gate.
- Per Riley's standing preference, lifecycle work does not run hot in parallel with activation/retention or feature-flag work. Sequence it. Do not stack a lifecycle send against an activation-cohort readout week.
- Routed-pre-setup + entitlement/support-state fail counts are surfaced inside lifecycle reporting too — they are part of the lifecycle surface even when the activation rate does not count them.

Owner: Ines (lifecycle-audience-risk preflight, independent); Lifecycle PM (TBD) for the program readout.

4. SEGMENT ECONOMICS — RETAINED MID-SEGMENT
Scope: renewal decisions and unit economics on the retained mid-segment cut.
Q2 watch items:
- Renewal decisions are reported with their pending denominators explicit. If the denominator is still accumulating (cohort not yet mature, or routed-pre-setup still provisional), say so on the same slide as the renewal decision — not in a footnote.
- Provisional vs final routing evidence is shown side-by-side. Provisional is NOT folded into the final denominator. The 3-22 Growth ack de-duplication decision (FINAL route-out, provisional side-table NOT in denom) is the standing rule; do not relitigate it per cohort.
- $12k Start concession (3-22 Growth ack): the "under-50" copy is pulled, organic path unchanged. Renewal math on retained mid-segment uses the post-concession price; any pre-concession comparisons are flagged as such.
- Read retained mid-segment renewal economics on its own evidence; do not borrow activation stabilization from the Helio Start lane.

# Q1 2028 development-focus options — Owen and Ines

Status: OPTIONS for Priya's review. Not approved goals. No automatic extension of Q4 authority.

Context: Priya has formally marked the Q4 development focuses as met. These are bounded Q1 2028 options — one independently-prepared deliverable each for Owen and Ines — scoped to test readiness for the next tier of work without expanding either person's lane. Priya picks, modifies, or declines.

Sequencing note: per Riley's standing preference, growth workstreams run sequentially, not in parallel. If both options are approved, Owen's runs first; Ines's starts only after Owen's lands.

---

## Option A — Owen: one independently-prepared source-readiness + exception-pattern recommendation

Scope (single deliverable)
Owen prepares one recommendation memo on source-readiness and exception patterns for the mid-segment cohort cut. The recommendation must explicitly call out where inputs are missing or where semantics are disputed — e.g. the 11/9 ruling that `conversions` is a paid-platform source label, the 19 = paid-source eligibility-flow starts convention, and the admit / assist / ineligible separation from admissions/activations. Where any of those inputs are not yet locked, the recommendation surfaces the gap as unresolved and names the owner who needs to resolve it. arguments.message:
Onboarding-notice dedup — ruling (2024-09-23)

Summary
Use a workspace-scoped dedup key (workspace identity + normalized destination) instead of a global destination-address key, and apply it ONLY to the onboarding-notice family that produced the Acme duplicate. Ines's Acme-specific hold stays in place until Daniela reruns the scoped replay and verifies both outcomes.

Why this fits
Daniela's first historical replay found 61 same-workspace duplicate-role pairs that should collapse. It also found 4 legitimate cross-workspace pairs that share the same service address — those must NOT collapse. A global destination-address key would have collapsed both, hurting the cross-workspace cases. A workspace-scoped key collapses the dup-role notices (same workspace, same role, same destination) while preserving cross-workspace messages that legitimately share an address.

Cuts to watch
  - Scope is the onboarding-notice family ONLY. Don't widen to other message families on this ruling — each has its own dedup semantics and a global rewrite risks new false positives we haven't measured.
  - Normalized destination matters: the dedup has to survive minor formatting/encoding variation in the address, otherwise the same real pair may not collapse consistently. Define "normalized" before the rerun, not after.
  - Same-workspace + same-role is the load-bearing pair. If the scoped key is just (workspace + destination) without role, two different roles at the same destination in the same workspace will incorrectly collapse.

P / effect
Low-risk in the onboarding-notice family (61 vs 4 is a strong signal). The scoped replay should produce: 61 collapsed, 4 preserved, 0 new false positives. If we see anything else, hold the rollout and reassess.

Effect of doing nothing: the Acme duplicate pattern persists, and any other same-workspace dup-role notices in the historical window keep firing.

Effect of removing Ines's Acme hold before verification: high — Acme is the named cause and the lane owner has not yet confirmed the scoped fix behaves on replay.

Call
  1. Daniela reruns the replay with the workspace-scoped key, on the onboarding-notice family only, and reports: collapsed count, preserved count, any new false positives.
  2. Verification = both outcomes check out (61 collapse, 4 preserved). Anything off → hold.
  3. Ines's Acme hold stays in place through verification. Lift only after the scoped replay reports clean.
  4. Do NOT widen scope to other message families in this pass.

Open question for Ines / Daniela: when the scoped replay reports clean, do we want a second confirmation pass against a fresh historical window before lifting the Acme hold, or is the single clean replay sufficient?

messages.content:
Confirmed: the only live leadership-grade source I can actually read is the MRR aggregate and the flag registry. Tier-cut snapshots, funnels, and the expansion-nudge experiment results all return NOT_FOUND. That is material to the recommendation — a "lean leadership view" has to be honest about what is currently measurable, or it will over-promise. I'll state that up front, then propose the structure.

Here is the recommendation.

---

## Why the recommendation has to start with what we can actually read

The MRR aggregate is the only leadership-grade snapshot currently populated. ARR-by-segment, churn-by-tier, the activation funnel, and the 60-day expansion-nudge experiment results all return NOT_FOUND. That doesn't change the design of a *good* leadership view — it just means anything tier-cut or experimental belongs in the appendices for now, not in the summary, until the underlying snapshots exist. I'll call that out again in the appendix section.

---

## Leadership summary — six metrics, in this order

Order matters: lead with the topline, separate Helio Start (bounded channel, different rule set), pair the support-load story with activation (same underlying cohort signal), keep Expansion Assist descriptive, and report CS auto-nudge holds with a complete unique-decision denominator.

1. **Total MRR + Net-new MRR (one card, two lines)**
   Single topline. From the aggregate snapshot: $4.00M MRR, net-new $320k for the period. No tier cut on this card — leadership reads topline here, tier movement is appendix.

2. **Helio Start — separately reported channel card**
   Helio Start is a bounded launch channel, not a tier; its rules (50 seats cap, founder-led pricing path, manual qualification) differ from the standard tier model. Report it as its own card with: accounts in the bounded channel, MRR contribution, and a one-line "scope unchanged since {date}" stamp (per the v1/Decommissioned note in the registry, scope is the current bounded channel, not the rolled-back pricing_page_v3 draft). Do not co-mingle Helio Start MRR into the aggregate or into tier cuts.

3. **Support load beside activation (paired card)**
   Activation without support load is half a story; support load without activation is noise. Report:
   - Activation: % of new accounts reaching first paid month within the window (currently NOT_FOUND — surface as "data pending" rather than fabricate a number; flag as a backfill priority).
   - Support load: tickets per active account in the same window, with a same-cohort filter so the denominator matches activation. If they can't share a denominator, do not put them on the same card — pair them as adjacent cards with explicit "same cohort filter applied" note.
   This pairing is what surfaces "we activated more accounts but support cost per activated account rose" — the leadership signal you actually want.

4. **CS auto-nudge holds — operating control**
   Auto-nudges (the Ines-owned, 5-state lifecycle lane) are an operating control, not an experiment. Report it as:
   - Holds applied (count) / unique decisions (denominator) — *complete unique-decision denominator required*. "Holds" without a decision denominator is unverifiable.
   - Suppression classes paused (educational, promotional, etc., per the Acme flag's classification scheme).
   - Holds expired on time vs. held past expiry — late-released holds are a CS-trust risk because silent suppression muts legitimate post-event email.
   Flag a hold as a control failure (not just a metric) if it lapses past expiry without an explicit re-request.

5. **Expansion Assist — descriptive only, noncausal**
   Per the registry: Expansion Assist has no causal read. Do not include uplift, p-value, or any "did it work" framing. Report:
   - Accounts touched (descriptive count).
   - Distribution of outcomes observed (descriptive — no causal language).
   - Eligibility model in use (behavior-based, per the 60d nudge notes — do not reintroduce blanket day-60).

arguments.title: Ines — annual review input (FY Q4 2024)
arguments.body:
ANNUAL REVIEW INPUT — Ines (lifecycle-aud-risk)
Reviewer: Riley  |  Period covered: Q4 2024 (Oct–Dec)
Source request: Priya, 2024-12-04 13:20 CT — due Friday

================================================================
SUMMARY
================================================================
Ines's quarter in lifecycle-aud-risk is one of clean, scoped execution. She
independently handled routine sends within the lasting authority Priya granted
on 2024-11-08, made the correct no-send decision on the only merge-alias
conflict that could not support a current destination, preserved the held-row
IDs on the state-changing reminder that required my approval, and immediately
paused the related follow-up when the unauthorized delivery of held row
ONB-7742 appeared in the Customer.io manifest. One specific area for
reliability improvement: the late post-holiday audit on the Nov 27 release
surfaced an unauthorized delivery that should not have reached Customer.io.
The holding/decision behavior was correct; the audit timing is the gap.

This document does not change the authority split. Ines is not blamed for the
engineering-cause uncertainty around ONB-7742 — Daniela retains engineering
release controls, and Ines is not responsible for them.

================================================================
STRENGTHS — incidents this quarter
================================================================

1) Routine sends handled independently within lasting authority.
   Per Priya's 2024-11-08 grant, Ines owns routine, non-state-changing lifecycle
   sends within the ≤3/week ceiling, with 24h audit and fail-closed on missing
   or conflicting state. Ines executed within that lane all quarter: she ran
   preflights, recorded dispositions, and shipped supported routine sends on
   her authority. Riley's signature was reserved for the one state-changing
   reminder that required it (the Nov 27 onboarding reminder writing a
   `reminder_sent` state). No routine lane was converted into a gate.

2) Correct no-send decision on the unresolved merge-alias conflict (2024-11-20).
   Daniela finished tracing the fourth merge-alias conflict: Customer.io
   canonicalizes `ops@`; the warehouse identifies a different `admin@`
   destination; no verified mailbox-equivalence record links them. Because the
   conflict could not support a current destination, Ines made a fresh no-send
   decision under her routine authority rather than asking Riley to approve a
   guess. The other three merge-alias rows retained their 2024-11-13
   dispositions; no exception remained unresolved. This is exactly the call the
   authority split asks of her — fail closed when the destination cannot be
   verified, do not push the uncertainty up.

3) Held-row IDs preserved on the state-changing reminder (2024-11-26).
   For Wednesday 11:00am's onboarding reminder (state-changing — writes
   `reminder_sent`), Ines completed preflight against the 9:28am snapshot of
   842 candidates and preserved the exact 15 held row IDs alongside the 12
   suppressed and 3 conflicting-state rows. The releasable scope she surfaced
   was the 827 evidence-complete rows only. That preservation made the
   approval scope unambiguous and is what kept the other 14 of the 15 held
   rows out of the manifest a day later.

4) Immediate pause of the related follow-up on the unauthorized delivery
   (2024-12-02). When Ines's post-holiday reconciliation found ONB-7742 in
   the Customer.io delivery manifest (one of the three conflicting-state rows
   explicitly excluded from my approval), she immediately paused the
   reminder's related follow-up step and surfaced the finding. The other 14
   held row IDs were absent from the manifest — held status preserved. She
   did not attempt to remediate the customer-facing state and did not assert
   a cause; she stopped, recorded, and escalated to the stop owner.

================================================================
DEVELOPMENT AREA — reliability improvement
================================================================

Late post-holiday audit (2024-12-02): the reconciliation that surfaced the
ONB-7742 unauthorized delivery ran after the Thanksgiving holiday window,
which means the mismatch sat in the manifest from 2024-11-27 11:02am CT until
2024-12-02 before being caught. The decision/holding behavior was correct
everywhere Ines controlled it (held IDs preserved on send; immediate pause on
detection); the gap is timing. Recommend a target reconciliation cadence
after multi-day holiday windows: same-day or next-business-day audit on the
first post-holiday working day for any release authorized in the holiday
window, so an unauthorized delivery does not sit for several days before a
stop is opened. This is a process-cadence improvement for Ines's lane, not a
blame item — the engineering-cause uncertainty (manifest construction,
upload, or Customer.io processing) is Daniela's determination, not Ines's.

================================================================
AUTHORITY SPLIT — preserved exactly
================================================================
The following split is the authority structure Priya approved on 2024-11-08
and remains in force. This document does not propose any change to it and
does not assign Ines responsibility for lanes she does not own.

  • Ines (lifecycle-aud-risk) owns:
      - Routine, non-state-changing lifecycle sends, within the ceiling of
        no more than three sends per week.
      - Routine preflights (suppression, merge-alias, freshness-marker) on
        those sends.
      - No-send / fail-closed decisions when state is missing or conflicting.
      - 24h post-send audit on every send in her lane.
      - Disposition recording and rehearsal log.

  • Riley (judgment-escalation / stop owner) retains:
      - Stop-owner role for customer corrections and incidents.
      - Authority over state-changing, ambiguous, and exception-heavy sends
        (e.g. the Nov 27 onboarding reminder that writes `reminder_sent`).
      - Per-cycle signature only where the standing audit gate names it
        (stable cohort pre-rollout). Riley does not sign routine lanes.

  • Daniela (engineering release controls) retains:
      - All engineering release controls, including release-metadata export,
        connector-state signal, and any determination about whether the
        ONB-7742 mismatch arose in manifest construction, upload, or
        Customer.io processing.

  • Ines is NOT responsible for:
      - Daniela's engineering release controls.
      - The engineering cause determination on ONB-7742.
      - Customer-impact classification, which remains pending Daniela's
        technical determination plus Riley's stop-owner call.
      - Any re-write of historical point-in-time tables; per the
        exception-review rule, accepted tables stay fixed and later state is
        a separate forward event.

================================================================
EVIDENCE / SESSION ANCHORS
================================================================
- 2024-11-08 09:30 CT — Priya's lasting-authority grant; posted to #growth-ops.
- 2024-11-20 09:05 CT — Fourth merge-alias conflict disposition; Ines
  no-send under her routine authority; three prior dispositions stand.
- 2024-11-26 10:20 CT — Onboarding reminder preflight; 842 candidates, 12
  suppressed + 3 conflicting-state + 15 held IDs preserved; 827 releasable
  surfaced; Riley signed the 827-row scope only.
- 2024-12-02 10:45 CT — Post-holiday reconciliation surfaced ONB-7742 in
  Customer.io manifest; Ines paused the related follow-up; incident-stop
  posted to #growth-investigations by Riley (no cause asserted, no customer
  correction asserted; engineering cause and customer-impact classification
  both pending Daniela's determination).

================================================================
DRAFT TONE / SUGGESTED PARAGRAPH FOR PRIYA
================================================================
"Ines executed the lifecycle-aud-risk lane cleanly this quarter: routine
sends within her lasting authority shipped without escalation, the
no-send on the unresolved merge-alias conflict was the correct call, the
held-row IDs on the state-changing reminder were preserved end-to-end, and
the related follow-up was paused the moment the unauthorized delivery was
surfaced. The one development area is reliability around post-holiday audit
timing — a same-day or next-business-day reconciliation after multi-day
holiday windows would have surfaced the Nov 27 mismatch days earlier. The
authority split is unchanged: Ines owns routine and preflights in her lane;
I remain stop owner for customer corrections and state-changing, ambiguous,
or exception-heavy sends; Daniela retains all engineering release controls,
and Ines is not responsible for them."

tests.request: Create a short historical framing note for the completed February-April 2023 mid-segment churn investigation.

input.body:
HISTORICAL FRAMING — Feb–Apr 2023 Mid-Segment Churn Investigation
(Growth / retrospective framing. Not the close-out.)

Window. Signal flagged in early Feb 2023; investigation ran through late April.
Cohort. 50–200 seat mid-segment. Originally framed on v1 (50–200); Owen rechecked the cut, confirmed not a definition bug, and the cohort was re-tagged to v2 (75–200) on 2023-04-26 — v1 kept intact for comps.

Signal. Monthly mid-segment churn ran 5.1% against a trailing-six baseline of ~2.1% on v1 (roughly 2.4× baseline).

Hypotheses (locked 2023-02-08, numbered for the thread):
  #1 Pricing artifact — packaging/discounting/contract-mix weirdness we caused
  #2 Competitor cycle — someone ran a play at the mid-seg base
  #3 Onboarding timing — late-Dec/early-Jan starts maturing into churn on a lag
  #4 CS coverage gap — CSM load drift, coverage math
Sequencing decision: #1 first (fastest to kill), then leaning #3 or #4 before #2.

What was unusual about how it ran.
- Parallel tracks, not Marcus Vail's preferred sequence. Marcus's pricing-page experiment was a separate question from hypothesis #1 (it was pricing-page design, not packaging/discounting/contract-mix), so it earned its own track rather than blocking or collapsing into the investigation. At the 2023-02-09 staff sync, Riley pushed back on pricing-first; Priya backed Riley. This was a deliberate exception to Riley's usual one-workstream-hot sequencing — different question earns its own track.
- Tomas Vega (CEO) got a one-line DM at kickoff. Riley is dotted-line to Tomas on board-facing / bigger-strategic-call work, so he gets the exec version rather than the full thread.
- Investigation updates posted to Slack #growth-investigations (not #growth-team) to keep the thread with Priya's routing.

Where the body of the work lives.
- Notion investigation doc, Priya owns. Hypothesis-by-hypothesis resolution and the final read live there, not here.
- Marcus's pricing-page experiment was tracked as a separate brief and bridged into the churn read when the read landed.

What this note is not.
- Not the close-out. The ruling and per-hypothesis resolution are in Priya's doc.
- Not a re-litigation. The cohort re-tag and the parallel-track decision are preserved as decisions made.

Status: erratum / supersedes prior read. Do NOT reuse the stale cohort logic.

Bottom line
- The April 2023 onboarding cohort was defined by the wrong eligibility signal, and the mid-segment cuts were driven by a sibling classification label that does not exist on the day-19 eligibility flow. Mid-segment numbers from this read are noisier than they look; directionally useful, not safe to ship.

What was wrong
- Cohort boundary (wrong eligibility signal):
  - The cohort was pulled using `conversions` as if it were the paid-platform source label.
  - Per the 11/9 ruling, `conversions` is the paid-platform source label, NOT the eligibility-flow start. The eligibility flow starts at day 19 (paid-source eligibility flow).
  - Effect: the cohort was over-broad — it mixed paid-eligible and paid-ineligible users in the same "onboarded" bucket.
- Classification issue (wrong sibling label):
  - Within the cohort, the read bucketed users into admit / assist / ineligible as if these were admissions / activations.
  - Those three buckets are separate stages on the day-19 eligibility flow, not synonyms. Admit = 8, Assist = 6, Ineligible = 5 are distinct outcomes and must stay distinct.
- Timing issue:
  - The day-19 eligibility window was not anchored consistently. Some users were measured at first-touch, others at next-touch, which compressed the ineligible tail and inflated the assist line.
  - Net: timing noise amplified the classification error above.

Corrected cohort boundary
- Cohort = users whose day-19 paid-source eligibility flow opened in April 2023.
- Use the day-19 timestamp as the anchor; do NOT use `conversions` as a proxy for eligibility.
- Sub-buckets are stages on that flow: admit (8), assist (6), ineligible (5). Do not collapse or rename.

What to keep vs. discard
- Keep: directional shape (admit > assist > ineligible in the corrected read), paid-source mix, week-over-week trend direction.
- Discard: absolute mid-segment counts, assist-rate %, and any cut that treated `conversions` as the eligibility entry. Re-pull against the corrected boundary before reusing any figure in a deck or commit.

Where this lives
- Owner: #growth-investigations; routing via Priya.
- Related: the 11/9 ruling on `conversions` vs. day-19 and the admit/assist/ineligible stage definitions.

Cuts / p / effect / call
- Cuts: by paid source, by week of day-19 anchor.
- p: paid-source eligibility flow opens, admit / assist / ineligible stages.
- Effect: prior mid-segment read overstated assist and understated ineligible by collapsing stages and using the wrong entry signal.
- Call: retire the stale cohort; any future April 2023 cite must reference this erratum and the corrected boundary.

arguments.body:
# Helio Start bounded paid-search proposal — October 2027

**Status banner — PROPOSAL COMPLETED BY PREPARATION OWNER ON 2027-10-13; AUTHORIZATIONS STILL PENDING.**

This document is the completed bounded proposal authored by Riley (preparation owner) ahead of the 2027-10-16 review with Priya. Completion of the proposal is not authorization. Every value below is proposed, not approved. Authorization of the total budget, daily cap, admission cap, stop and pause conditions, and final go/no-go remains pending through (a) Priya's decision review on 2027-10-16, (b) a separate Daniela check before paid traffic is enabled, and (c) the §8.E future-paid case-review gate and §8.E.3 proposal precondition, both still in force. Paid traffic remains OFF until each of those gates has cleared, and any of them alone is sufficient to keep traffic off. No budget, batch, paid-traffic decision, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, or production change is approved by the existence of this completed proposal.

Brief id: `BRIEF-2027-10-helio-start-paid-search`
Preparation owner: Riley
Release / rollback (rel/rb): Daniela (per standing rule)
Decision review scheduled: Priya — 2027-10-16, 2:00–3:00pm Central

---

## 1. Certified mature evidence

This brief only cites evidence that has already been certified. Mature evidence means (a) cohort-stabilized, (b) read at the metric's natural cadence, (c) effect-size estimate with confidence interval, and (d) not distorted by a conflicting in-flight growth workstream.

- **[cite: prior brief id]** — CAC ceiling on Helio Start from organic. The paid-search admission cap and stop conditions must clear this floor before any recommendation is written.
- **[cite: prior brief id]** — Channel-mix maturity assessment. Restricts the bid-eligible placements referenced in Section 3 (staffed design).
- **[cite: prior brief id]** — Audience overlap and incrementality test results. Defines the lookalike seed used as the paid-search audience.
- **[cite: prior brief id]** — 21-day read window precedent from the closed Reminders workstream (closed 9/20/27). The same read window, CI reporting standard, and interim-equals-safety-guardrails rule are reused here; no claim is allowed to extend beyond what that precedent supports.

No claim in this brief extends past what these artifacts certify.

## 2. Certified 24-case nonproduction preflight

Per the standing rule that disputed, cross-team, or executive-facing artifacts cannot be silently edited, the 24-case preflight was run end-to-end in nonproduction and is preserved as a standalone artifact. This section summarizes the framing only; the full case set is the supporting artifact, not this brief.

- **Scope (24 cases):** bid shaping, audience overlap checks, signup-source capture, attribution windows, lifecycle handoff paths, suppression rules, and stop-condition triggers.
- **Per-case pass criteria:** (a) no collision with an in-flight lifecycle email or activation/retention workstream; (b) no silent edit to any disputed, cross-team, or executive-facing artifact; (c) the attribution path resolves end-to-end without falling back to last-click defaults.
- **Certification:** [cite: preflight artifact id / certifier / date]. Certification confirms the proposal is safe to advance to authorization review. It does not, by itself, authorize the proposal.

## 3. Staffed design

Named coverage is required. Role slots marked pending must be filled before this brief can move from proposal to authorization. Riley retains preparation ownership throughout. Daniela owns rel/rb.

- Preparation owner: Riley
- Release / rollback (rel/rb): Daniela
- Paid-media lead: pending — confirm
- Lifecycle coordinator: pending — confirm; must verify the 21-day read window does not overlap an active lifecycle email or activation/retention workstream, per the standing sequential-workstream preference
- On-call / incident: pending — confirm
- Analyst for 21-day read: pending — confirm

---

## 4. Proposed budget and admission bounds

**Proposer: Riley. Not approved.** Reviewers: Priya at the 2027-10-16 decision review; Daniela in a separate paid-traffic check after that review. The values below are a proposal, not authorization. No value takes effect unless and until every Section 6 approval is checked and the §8.E / §8.E.3 gates have cleared.

- **Total budget:** $8,000 maximum, drawn from the same envelope that funded the closed Q1 Helio Start cohort. Lower than the closed cohort's $14,420 because this is a cycle-1 bounded test of the §8.E mitigations on the seven high-support workspace classifications, not a scale-up. Matches the Q2 2027 paid-test precedent (Apr 9, 2027 — Priya approved $8,000/25 admits, run-closed at the earlier of spend or admits, no second batch authorized).
- **Daily cap:** $400/day. Sized so that a fully-pacing run burns less than one-third of the total budget inside the first seven days, keeping the run inside the day-7 safety-guardrails interim checkpoint without forcing an early stop on pacing alone.
- **Admission cap:** 25 admitted workspaces total. Same cap as the Q2 2027 paid-test precedent. Reflects the smaller test envelope and the §8.E.3 requirement to account for each of the seven high-support workspace classifications inside the admitted-path bounds rather than running past them.
- **Run-close trigger:** the earlier of (a) $8,000 spent, (b) 25 admitted workspaces, or (c) 6 weeks elapsed since launch.
- **Read-window length:** 21 days (standing rule — confirmed).
- **Interim checkpoint:** day 7, safety guardrails only; no scale-up or early stop on effect size alone (standing rule — confirmed).

Inputs already on file:

- Certified mature-evidence CAC ceiling from Section 1 — the admission cap and stop conditions below are sized against this floor.
- Finance routing — unchanged from the Q1 closed cohort; no new finance lane is being opened by this proposal.

Inputs still required before authorization:

- Section 6 approvals (Section 6 below).
- §8.E case-review gate clearance (Owen + Customer Success classification of the seven high-support workspaces; Ines + Daniela determination of state-meaning, routing, and setup-sequence dimensions).
- §8.E.3 proposal precondition — per-case prevention / mitigation / bound stated against each of the seven classifications, not merely listed.

## 5. Stop and pause conditions

**Proposer: Riley. Not approved.** Each condition specifies threshold, owner, and action. The framing clause is fixed in advance and non-negotiable: any stop or pause decision is gated by a named owner (Daniela, rel/rb), takes effect within the same business day, and is recorded as a brief update — never as a silent edit.

- **CAC ceiling breach.** Threshold: any 7-day rolling paid-search CAC that exceeds the certified mature-evidence CAC ceiling from Section 1 by ≥15% on the day-7 interim, or by any amount on the day-21 read. Owner: Daniela (rel/rb), with Riley retained on the claim and forecast boundary. Action: pause the proposed batch the same business day; reset only after a certified mature re-read clears the threshold.
- **Attribution path degradation.** Pause the proposed batch if paid-source attribution cannot reconcile from eligibility-flow start through the final admitted, assisted, or ineligible route. This pause trigger is unchanged in every other respect: it does not modify any eligibility, routing, lifecycle, or instrumentation rule; it does not change the assisted-routing or external-authority meaning in force elsewhere in this brief; it does not authorize, lift, or extend paid traffic; and it does not affect the prep-only posture of this brief. Threshold, owner, and action details remain as specified here. Owner: Daniela (rel/rb). Action: pause the same business day; reconcile before any restart; record as a brief update.
- **Lifecycle / activation collision signal.** Threshold: any signal — from the standing lifecycle email or activation/retention workstream — that the proposed batch would run concurrently with another in-flight growth workstream, in violation of Riley's stated sequential-workstream preference. Owner: Priya (#lifecycle-systems) for the routing confirmation; Daniela (rel/rb) for the pause. Action: pause the same business day; restart only after Priya confirms sequencing against the standing workstream schedule.
- **Sign-quality floor breach.** Threshold: of the first 10 admitted workspaces, more than 10% exceed 90 account-level support minutes within the first 7 days (same threshold as the Q1 closed cohort and the Q2 2027 paid-test precedent). Owner: Daniela (rel/rb), with the §8.E case-review gate owners on the high-support classifications. Action: pause the same business day; restart only after each high-support case has been classified per §8.E and the §8.E.3 mitigation has been recorded against that case. The seven high-support workspaces from the closed Q1 cohort are accounted for inside the admission cap and the day-7 sign-quality threshold; the run-closed trigger fires before the admitted path can carry a second cohort of unclassified cases.
- **Budget pacing anomaly.** Threshold: spend exceeding one-third of the total budget ($2,667) within the first 7 days, OR daily-cap exceedance on any single day, OR a <$50/day spend rate for 5 consecutive business days after day 3 (indicates bid-eligibility or audience-overlap rejection, not just low volume). Owner: Daniela (rel/rb). Action: investigate the same business day; pause if the cause is bid-eligibility or audience-overlap rejection; record as a brief update.

## 6. Remaining approvals

**This section lists approvals still pending. No box is checked. Until every box below is checked, this brief remains a proposal that authorizes no traffic.**

- [ ] Total budget ($8,000) approved by Priya at the 2027-10-16 review
- [ ] Daily cap ($400/day) approved by Priya at the 2027-10-16 review
- [ ] Admission cap (25 admitted workspaces) approved by Priya at the 2027-10-16 review
- [ ] Stop and pause conditions (Section 5) approved by Priya at the 2027-10-16 review
- [ ] Lifecycle coordinator confirmed (no overlap with currently-running lifecycle email or activation/retention workstream) — pending
- [ ] Paid-media lead confirmed — pending
- [ ] 21-day read analyst confirmed — pending
- [ ] On-call / incident owner confirmed — pending
- [ ] Routing confirmation from Priya (#lifecycle-systems) that the 21-day read window is sequenced against other recurring workstreams — pending
- [ ] §8.E future-paid case-review gate cleared — pending (Owen + Customer Success classification of all seven high-support workspaces into external-authority action / ordinary integration / billing / another supported cause named explicitly; Ines + Daniela determination of state-meaning, routing, and setup-sequence dimensions, with multiple dimensions allowed and each named)
- [ ] §8.E.3 proposal precondition met — pending (per-case prevention / mitigation / bound stated against each of the seven classifications; "listed" is not acceptable per §8.E.3)
- [ ] Final go / no-go authorization — pending (Priya at the 2027-10-16 review; if approved, the proposal still requires a separate Daniela check before paid traffic is enabled)
- [ ] Separate Daniela check before paid traffic is enabled — pending (post-decision; cannot be combined with the Section 6 approvals above)

Paid traffic stays OFF.

## 7. Final recommendation

**Proposer: Riley. Not approved.** The recommendation below is a proposal, not an authorization. It is contingent on every Section 6 approval being checked, and on the §8.E / §8.E.3 gates being cleared before any launch.

Subject to those preconditions, the recommendation is to **proceed with the bounded cycle-1 paid-search test as specified in Sections 4 and 5**, with the following guardrails reaffirmed in advance:

1. The test is descriptive of the §8.E mitigations on the seven high-support classifications, not causal evidence of paid-search incrementality. No claim beyond the certified mature-evidence boundary may be made on the day-21 read.
2. No pipeline treatment, no forecast credit, no scale-up language. The same claim discipline applied to the closed Q1 cohort carries forward to this run.
3. §3 admission rules and the §4.8-style pipeline / forecast exclusion are not weakened by this proposal. They are reaffirmed, and the run does not introduce a new admission, routing, lifecycle, or fail-closed rule.
4. Paid traffic remains OFF until every Section 6 approval has cleared AND the separate Daniela check has cleared. Either of those gates is sufficient to keep traffic off; traffic does not turn on in their absence.
5. The proposal must be reviewed as a single bound: do not approve the budget without approving the corresponding stop conditions or vice versa. Partial approval is not contemplated and would not authorize traffic.

This proposal does not authorize a second batch, a scale-up, or a follow-on cycle. Each subsequent cycle would require a fresh proposal reviewed under the same gates, including a fresh §8.E / §8.E.3 pass against whatever high-support cases the prior cycle surfaces. No carry-forward of authorization from cycle 1 to cycle 2 is implied or permitted.

---

_Preparation owner: Riley. Release / rollback: Daniela. Decision review: Priya, 2027-10-16. Brief id: `BRIEF-2027-10-helio-start-paid-search`._

This is the only shape in this draft. High-intent paid search is the only acquisition channel offered; no other channel is offered. Any other dollar cap, any other admission cap, any other paired ceiling, any other channel, any other paired channel is not in this draft. Priya's 2027-04-09 approval is bounded to this single Q2 2027 test; it does NOT authorize a second batch, a later additional batch, a different acquisition shape, or a different close threshold.

3. Operating rules — stop and pause conditions (this section only; mature-outcome claims are in §6, kept separate)

A stop ends the batch. A pause halts new paid admissions (and certain paid-source-specific instrumentation writes) until a written restart condition is met. A pause is not a stop. A stop is not a pause. Each is its own gating condition; each requires its own remediation before the proposal continues. Mature-outcome claims (paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, account-level support effort) are NOT operating rules and are NOT reported on a stop/pause frame; they are reported only against complete day-90 windows (see §6).

3a. Hard stop conditions (the batch ends if any of these occur)

  S1. Close threshold reached: admissions hit 25 OR paid spend hits $8,000, whichever comes first. The admitted cohort is then frozen per §2.
  S2. Unsupported admission: an admission to Helio Start lacks the support posture required by the ordinary assisted-path coverage standard at admission time (e.g., missing connector access, missing required lifecycle state, missing external-authority clearance, or any condition that would render day-90 support infeasible within the assisted-path envelope). If detected during the batch (i.e., before close, before day-90 support is complete), the batch halts at that admission for paid-source routing purposes.
  S3. Unsupported applicant in the admitted path (added 2027-04-09 per Priya's approval): if an unsupported applicant enters the admitted path — meaning an applicant who would have failed assisted-path coverage at admission time but is nevertheless admitted to Helio Start — the batch STOPS IMMEDIATELY. The stop is triggered at the moment the unsupported applicant enters the admitted path; it is not a per-admission hold for review; it is an immediate end to the batch. The admitted cohort is then frozen per §2; no new paid admissions are admitted; existing cohort accounts continue through their day-90 windows for read-only audit and reconciliation, but no further paid-source routing occurs. S3 is the strongest stop in this draft and supersedes any continuation that would otherwise be permitted under §2.

3b. Pause conditions (the batch pauses if any of these occur; does not stop)

  P1. Attribution reconciliation failure: a routing or instrumentation failure prevents paid-source attribution from reconciling end-to-end from eligibility-flow start through admission and assisted routing at the account level (see §4). PAUSE TRIGGER (2027-04-09): the pause fires whenever the reconciliation gap exists; it is not a per-cadence post-hoc pause.
  P2. Post-10-admission support-pause breach: once paid-source admissions exceed 10 in count, the share of support-pause days attributable to the paid-source cohort exceeds 10% of elapsed batch days (see §5).
  P3. Post-10-admission >90-support-minutes breach (added 2027-04-09 per Priya's approval): after at least 10 admissions, if more than 10% of admitted workspaces exceed 90 account-level support minutes, the batch PAUSES. The >10% threshold is evaluated against the running admitted count; the metric is the share (not just the number) of admitted workspaces in the cohort whose account-level support minutes over the elapsed batch window exceed 90 minutes (per §5b). A breach at any rolling read after the 10-admission mark triggers P3. P3 is a pause, not a stop; restart requires written identification of cause, written fix, and written sign-off per §3c.

3c. What pause does, and what it does not do

  - Pause halts new paid admissions AND halts any instrumentation writes specific to the paid-source cohort.
  - Pause preserves read-only audit access (no data loss for reconciliation).
  - Pause does NOT route around the issue by relaxing eligibility, refusing ordinary users, bypassing lifecycle, or granting connector access out of band.
  - Pause does NOT modify eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, or assisted-routing rules (see §7).
  - Restart requires written identification of cause, written fix, and written sign-off. Restart does NOT authorize a second paid batch (§1 row 8) or a later additional batch (§1 row 9).

3d. What stop does, and what it does not do

  - Stop ends the batch at the trigger admission (S2, S3) or at the close threshold (S1). No new paid admissions are admitted after stop.
  - Stop does NOT modify any surface, rule, or downstream product behavior. It ends only the paid-traffic routing of this batch.
  - Stop does NOT authorize a second paid batch (§1 row 8) or a later additional batch (§1 row 9). Either is a separate decision (not approved; see §1 rows 8 and 9).

A stop and a pause are different events with different triggers and different remediations. They are not interchangeable. They are NOT mature-outcome claims; they are operating rules and are evaluated against the running batch, not against day-90 windows.

4. Running measurement view — separate counts, leading indicators only (operational, not mature-outcome)

The running view reports four separate counts. They are NOT a funnel, NOT a conversion rate, NOT a yield, and NOT a CAC, ROAS, payback, LTV, pipeline, or forecast input. They are operational counts used to evaluate the operating rules in §3 and to support end-to-end attribution reconciliation. None of these counts is or becomes acquisition, pipeline, revenue, or forecast evidence under this proposal.

4a. The four separate counts

The running view, refreshed per the standard cadence, displays exactly these four counts as separate numbers:

  C1. Paid-source eligibility-flow starts — every entry into the eligibility flow attributable to paid source, regardless of outcome (admit / refuse / hold / abandon / error). Counted at eligibility-flow start, joined on the attribution source.
  C2. Assisted routes — every eligibility-flow outcome that resulted in a routing decision into the assisted-path lane carrying paid-source admissions. Counted at assisted-routing decision, joined to C1 by account.
  C3. Admissions — every admission to Helio Start via the ordinary eligibility flow with an auditable end-to-end paid-source attribution chain (per §4c). Counted at the admission event, joined to C1 and C2 by account.
  C4. Attribution failures — every account in the paid-source cohort for which one or more of the four attribution checkpoints in §4c is missing, mismatched, or not joined on a single account-level key. Counted at reconciliation time, regardless of when the underlying gap occurred.

Each count is its own row. They are not summed, not divided into a rate, not compared as numerator and denominator against each other in this proposal. They are reported as four separate numbers with their own cadence and own source-of-truth field.

4b. What the running view is, and is not

  - The running view is the operating instrument for §3 and §4c. It informs stop and pause decisions during the batch.
  - The running view is NOT acquisition evidence. C1 (eligibility-flow starts) is not a reach, impression, click, or channel-performance number; it is an entry count into the eligibility flow for a single paid-source cohort in a single batch.
  - The running view is NOT pipeline evidence. C1–C4 do not enter any pipeline, do not produce a pipeline number, and do not adjust a pipeline target. Pipeline treatment and pipeline target remain decisions that are not approved (§1 rows 5 and 6).
  - The running view is NOT revenue or cash evidence. None of C1–C4 is, or is used to produce, paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, collected ARR/MRR, gross cash, or net cash. Mature revenue/cash reads require complete day-90 windows and are reported only in §6.
  - The running view is NOT forecast evidence. C1–C4 do not enter any forecast, do not produce a forecast number, and do not adjust a forecast credit. Forecast credit remains a decision that is not approved (§1 row 7).

If anyone reuses any of C1–C4 outside this proposal to claim acquisition, pipeline, revenue, or forecast credit, that reuse is outside this draft and is not authorized by it.

4c. End-to-end paid-source attribution reconciliation (operational, not a mature-outcome claim)

  - Scope: from eligibility-flow start, through admission decision, through assisted routing. Must be auditable at the account level end-to-end. PAUSE TRIGGER (2027-04-09): if attribution cannot reconcile end-to-end from eligibility-flow start through admission and assisted routing, the batch PAUSES immediately (per P1, §3b). The pause is triggered by the reconciliation gap itself; it is not a per-cadence post-hoc pause.
  - Required checkpoints (each must have a recorded source-of-truth and an account-level join key):
      - eligibility-flow start (entry into the eligibility flow, regardless of outcome) — feeds C1.
      - eligibility outcome (admit / refuse / hold, with reason) — feeds the join to C2 / C3.
      - admission (Helio Start admission event, with timestamp) — feeds C3.
      - assisted routing (which assisted-path lane the admission was routed to, with timestamp) — feeds C2.
  - Reconciliation rule: every admitted paid-source account must have a non-empty value at each of the four checkpoints, joined on a single account-level key. Any missing or mismatched value is an attribution reconciliation failure, increments C4, and triggers pause P1 (§3b).
  - C4 is reported as a running count alongside C1, C2, C3. C4 alone does not trigger stop; it triggers pause P1.
  - Read-only audit access is preserved during any pause to support reconciliation.
  - This reconciliation is descriptive and operational. It does NOT modify eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, or assisted-routing rules (§7).
  - This reconciliation is NOT a mature-outcome claim. It is reported on a running basis during the batch, not at day 90.

4d. Day-7 first integration — leading indicator only

  - Day-7 first integration is reported as a leading indicator only on the running view. It is a directional read on whether admitted accounts are reaching first integration within seven days of admission.
  - Day-7 first integration is NOT a mature-outcome claim. It is NOT a substitute for paid-active status. It is NOT a substitute for refund-adjusted collected cash. It is NOT a substitute for account-level support effort. It does NOT enter any pipeline, revenue, or forecast read.
  - Day-7 first integration does NOT trigger any stop or pause condition in §3. It is observed, recorded, and reported; it does not gate the batch.
  - If day-7 first integration is reported alongside other numbers, it must be labeled as a leading indicator and must not be combined with mature-outcome reads in a single statement.

4e. Cohort preservation after closure

  - Once the close threshold is met (per §2 or §3a S1), the admitted cohort is fixed. The same set of admitted accounts is the cohort for every subsequent read in this draft — running tally, post-10 support-pause read (§5), day-7 leading indicator (§4d), and mature-outcome read (§6).
  - No new account enters the cohort after closure. Eligibility-flow starts that would otherwise route through paid source after closure are not admitted into this batch and are not added to C1, C2, C3, or C4 retroactively.
  - C4 (attribution failures) may still be reconciled post-closure for accounts already in the cohort; reconciliation does not admit a new account.
  - The fixed cohort is preserved for audit. It is not modified, expanded, or pruned by any read in this proposal.

5. Post-10-admission support-pause threshold and >90-account-level-support-minutes read (operational, not mature-outcome)

5a. Post-10-admission support-pause threshold

  - Definition: a "support pause day" is any day on which the assisted-path lane carrying paid-source admissions is paused, throttled, or operating below its ordinary coverage standard for any reason attributable to the paid-source cohort (e.g., capacity, staffing, or instrumentation issue specific to that cohort).
  - Threshold: once paid-source admissions exceed 10 in count, the share of support-pause days attributable to the paid-source cohort must stay at or below 10% of elapsed batch days.
  - Breach: a breach at any rolling read after the 10-admission mark triggers pause P2 (§3b). A breach does not by itself constitute a refusal decision for any individual account; ordinary assisted-path coverage for affected accounts is preserved or restored per §7.
  - Reporting: per-cadence readout of (paid-source-elapsed-days, paid-source-support-pause-days, ratio) once the cohort passes 10 admissions.
  - This threshold is NOT a mature-outcome claim. It is an operating rule evaluated on a running basis during the batch, not at day 90.

5b. >90 account-level support minutes — number AND share, post-10

  - Once paid-source admissions exceed 10 in count, the running view reports two additional separate numbers alongside C1–C4:
      - M1. Number of admitted workspaces whose account-level support minutes over the elapsed batch window exceed 90 minutes. Counted at the running read, joined to C3 by account.
      - M2. Share of admitted workspaces (from C3) whose account-level support minutes exceed 90 minutes. Computed as M1 divided by the admitted count at the running read, expressed as a fraction and as a percentage.
  - Both M1 (number) and M2 (share) are reported. Reporting only the share, or only the number, is insufficient.
  - M1 and M2 are operational reads. They inform §5a's pause rule and §3b P3's pause trigger but are not themselves triggers independent of those rules.
  - PAUSE TRIGGER (2027-04-09): after at least 10 admissions, if M2 exceeds 10% (i.e., more than 10% of admitted workspaces exceed 90 account-level support minutes), the batch PAUSES per P3 (§3b). The threshold is a share-based threshold; M1 alone does not trigger P3.
  - M1 and M2 are NOT mature-outcome claims. They are reported on a running basis during the batch, not at day 90. Account-level support effort as a mature-outcome claim is in §6.
  - M1 and M2 are NOT acquisition, pipeline, revenue, or forecast evidence. They do not enter any of those reads.

6. Mature-outcome claims — kept SEPARATE from operating stop and pause rules, and from the running view

Mature-outcome claims are reported only at day 90 or later, against complete day-90 windows. They are explicitly NOT used as operating stop or pause triggers (§3). They are explicitly NOT part of the running view in §4 — the running view is operational; mature-outcome claims are not. The day-7 first integration read in §4d is a leading indicator and is NOT a mature-outcome claim. The >90-support-minutes read in §5b is operational and is NOT a mature-outcome claim. Mature-outcome claims may inform whether to develop a Q3 plan (which itself is not approved; see §1 row 11). They are not a launch decision (which is approved for April 12, see §1 row 4), not a budget decision (which is approved at $8,000 maximum, see §1 row 1), not a pipeline or forecast input (which are not approved; see §1 rows 5 and 7), not a second paid batch (which is not approved; see §1 row 8), and not a later additional batch (which is not approved; see §1 row 9).

For an admission to count as "paid-active" at day 90, ALL of the following must be true:

  a. The account is admitted to Helio Start via the ordinary eligibility flow with an auditable end-to-end paid-source attribution chain (§4c), and is in the fixed admitted cohort per §2 / §4e.
  b. Refund-adjusted collected cash from the account is positive at day 90. "Refund-adjusted collected cash" = gross collected cash from the account over the day-90 window, minus refunds issued to the account over the same window. Chargebacks, disputes, and processor fees are reported alongside but are not netted into this metric unless explicitly decided later.
  c. Account-level support effort is recorded as an account-level aggregate over the day-90 window, expressed in the existing support-effort unit, and is reportable per account (not only in aggregate). Support-effort reporting does NOT bypass or relax assisted-path coverage.
  d. The admission has not been flagged as an unsupported admission that broke assisted-path coverage (§3a S2, S3).
  e. The batch was not in a pause (§3b) covering the admission's day-90 window, OR if it was, the pause has a written restart condition and the admission has been re-validated against that restart condition.

A measure with an incomplete day-90 window is not a measure for this proposal. Do not report, score, or characterize it. Paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort are UNAVAILABLE for any admission whose day-90 window is not yet complete; this is true at any read taken before that window closes. The day-90 read is the read that decides whether development of a Q3 plan proceeds. This draft does NOT decide Q3. The approval creates NO pipeline target, NO pipeline treatment, NO forecast credit, and NO authority for another paid batch.

Mature-outcome claims are downstream of the operating rules and downstream of the running view. They are NOT operating rules. They do NOT trigger stops or pauses. They are NOT reported on a stop/pause frame. They are NOT reported on the running-view frame. They are reported only at day 90 or later, against complete day-90 windows, against the fixed admitted cohort.

7. Rules that remain unchanged (not modified, suspended, or waived)

  - Eligibility rules.
  - Refusal rules.
  - Connector-access rules.
  - External-authority rules.
  - Lifecycle rules.
  - Instrumentation rules.
  - Assisted-routing rules.

This draft does not modify, suspend, or waive any of them. Priya's 2027-04-09 approval is bounded to the ONE Q2 2027 test specified in §2 and does not change, suspend, or waive any rule in this section. The CS cert posture (closed 2027-03-17: 45/45 day-90 support windows complete; median 24m, p90 86m, 3 >90m; no unsupported case entered admitted path; future capped run of ≤25 admitted wkspcs w/o displacing ordinary assisted-path coverage; descriptive — no randomized control) is the standing reference for assisted-path coverage and is not modified by this draft. The Expansion Assist descriptive posture (descriptive; keep disputed/cross-surface/exec; don't line-edit routine; eng release/rollback → Daniela) applies to any instrumentation or routing write described here and is not modified by this draft. The 24-case nonproduction preflight in §11 is descriptive and does NOT modify any of the unchanged rules in this section; it is a verification pass on the existing rules.

8. Inputs from owners (solicited, not yet committed in this draft)

  - Priya: launch-timing decision (approved 2027-04-09, April 12), budget decision (approved 2027-04-09, $8,000 maximum), traffic allocation decision (approved 2027-04-09, high-intent paid search only), pipeline treatment/target decision (NOT approved), forecast credit decision (NOT approved), launch go/no-go (approved 2027-04-09, subject to §11 preflight pass and §3 stops/pauses), second-paid-batch decision (NOT approved), later-additional-batch decision (NOT approved), Q3-development go/no-go on day-90 read (NOT approved). Approved items are in §1; unapproved items remain in §1.
  - Daniela: engineering release/rollback posture for any instrumentation touching paid-source routing. Also, Daniela requires the fresh 24-case nonproduction preflight per §11 before any launch decision; this preflight is owned by Daniela as a precondition gate. The April 12 launch is contingent on a passed preflight.
  - Owen: cohort cuts on the paid-source cohort at the post-10-admission gate and at day 90. Methodology consistent with existing cohort work; the running view in §4 and the >90-support-minutes read in §5b follow Owen's 2027-03-29 measurement-operating shape. No new methodology in this draft.
  - Ines: lifecycle governance inside the conservative fork and the unsupported-list boundaries; the preflight in §11 must reconcile paid source through these branches without bypassing them.
  - Customer Success / assisted-path coverage owners: capacity and staffing read for the assisted-path lane carrying paid-source admissions; not a coverage-adequacy judgment, an arithmetic + tradeoff input. The CS cert posture referenced in §7 is the standing reference; the preflight in §11 exercises the same coverage standard.

This draft records the inputs that will be required when remaining decisions are made; it does not solicit approval for any of the not-yet-approved items in §1.

9. Carried-in posture (preserved verbatim, with current-state update)

  - Paid traffic was off as of 2027-04-02. Priya's 2027-04-09 approval authorizes paid traffic for ONE Q2 2027 high-intent paid-search test, April 12 launch, $8,000 maximum budget, bounded by §2 and §3. No separate launch decision, budget decision, or paid-traffic decision is required to start that single test. Any additional paid batch (second batch, later additional batch) requires separate approval and is NOT approved.
  - This draft is now an approved launch plan for ONE Q2 2027 test, not a development draft. Proposal development was authorized by Priya's 2027-03-24 decision; the April 12 launch is authorized by Priya's 2027-04-09 decision.
  - The single acquisition shape in §2 (high-intent paid search) is the only acquisition shape authorized; Helio Start remains otherwise organic.
  - Pipeline treatment, pipeline target, and forecast credit are NOT approved and are outside this draft. The approval creates no pipeline target, no pipeline treatment, and no forecast credit.
  - The earlier-of-$8,000-or-25-admissions close in §2 is the bound for the single approved test; no batch is currently running as of the approval moment — the April 12 launch is the start of the first batch under this approval.
  - Batch start date (April 12), gate cadence, and go/no-go review date are specified in this draft. The §11 preflight must pass before April 12; preflight case-level specifics (the exact 24 cases, the case mix within each bucket, the run schedule, the pass criteria, the reconciliation report shape) belong in the (separate, future) preflight spec owned by Daniela and are not in this draft.

10. Open items for the next iteration (not decisions; just unresolved items)

  - Exact attribution join key for end-to-end reconciliation (§4c). Candidate: existing account-level key. Confirmation needed before April 12 launch.
  - Reporting cadence for §2 close-trigger tally, §4 four-count running view, §4d day-7 leading indicator, §5a support-pause readout, and §5b M1/M2 number-and-share readout. Default candidate: standard cadence; confirmation needed before April 12 launch.
  - Definition of "support pause day" for §5a (which throttling states count). To be specified before April 12 launch; not in this draft.
  - Whether the >90 account-level-support-minute threshold in §5b uses the existing support-effort unit (per §6c) on the same per-account basis. To be confirmed before April 12 launch; not in this draft.
  - Whether day-7 first integration in §4d is sourced from the same instrumentation as the day-90 mature-outcome reads, or from a separate leading-indicator pipeline. To be confirmed before April 12 launch; not in this draft.
  - §11 preflight case-level specifics (the exact 24 cases, the case mix within each bucket, the run schedule, the pass criteria, the reconciliation report shape) are NOT in this draft; they belong in the (separate, future) preflight spec owned by Daniela.
  - Confirmation that P1 (attribution reconciliation pause) and P3 (>90-support-minutes pause) trigger on the running read that surfaces the gap, not on a delayed post-hoc read; this is the intended posture per Priya's 2027-04-09 approval and is reflected in §3b and §4c/§5b.

11. Daniela's 24-case nonproduction preflight — precondition gate before any launch decision (descriptive; not launch)

Daniela requires a fresh 24-case nonproduction preflight before any launch decision is made. This section defines the preflight's structure and rules. It is descriptive — it does NOT approve launch, budget, paid traffic, launch timing, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, pipeline target, a second paid batch, or a later additional batch. It is a precondition gate, not a launch decision. The April 12 launch is contingent on a passed preflight.

11a. Scope and posture

  - The preflight is nonproduction. It runs against the existing instrumentation and routing stack without sending any production paid traffic. It does NOT trigger S1, S2, S3, P1, P2, or P3. It does NOT change C1–C4 or M1/M2. It does NOT admit any real account. It does NOT enter any pipeline, revenue, or forecast read.
  - The preflight exercises the same ordinary eligibility flow, the same assisted-path coverage standard, the same connector-access rules, the same external-authority rules, the same lifecycle rules, the same instrumentation rules, and the same assisted-routing rules described in §7. It does NOT modify, suspend, or waive any of them.
  - The preflight is owned by Daniela (engineering release/rollback posture and instrumentation reconciliation). It is a precondition for any launch decision; it is not itself a launch decision.

11b. The 24 cases — three buckets of eight

The preflight comprises 24 cases, distributed across exactly three buckets of eight cases each:

  - Bucket A — eight expected admissions: cases designed to traverse the ordinary eligibility flow end-to-end and produce a Helio Start admission with an auditable end-to-end paid-source attribution chain. Each case is expected to land in C3 (admissions) with no C4 (attribution failure) increment and no lifecycle suppression.
  - Bucket B — eight expected assisted routes: cases designed to traverse the ordinary eligibility flow end-to-end and produce a routing decision into the assisted-path lane carrying paid-source admissions, without necessarily producing a Helio Start admission (admission may or may not occur depending on the eligibility outcome, but the assisted-route outcome is the defining expectation). Each case is expected to land in C2 (assisted routes) with the expected routing lane and to reconcile through §4c.
  - Bucket C — eight expected fail-closed or suppressed outcomes: cases designed to traverse the ordinary eligibility flow end-to-end and land in an existing fail-closed hold or an existing lifecycle suppression. The defining expectation is that the case reconciles into the existing branch, hold, or suppression — NOT that it is redirected around one. Each case is expected to terminate in the existing branch, hold, or suppression with the original paid source reconciled through to that final route.

Total: 8 + 8 + 8 = 24 cases.

11c. Per-case reconciliation requirement — paid source, eligibility-flow start → final route

For every one of the 24 cases, the preflight must reconcile paid source end-to-end from eligibility-flow start to the case's final route. Reconciliation means:

  - The eligibility-flow start checkpoint is recorded with the paid-source attribution (feeds C1).
  - The eligibility outcome checkpoint (admit / refuse / hold, with reason) is recorded.
  - For Bucket A: the admission checkpoint (Helio Start admission event, with timestamp) is recorded (feeds C3); for Bucket B: the assisted-routing checkpoint (which assisted-path lane, with timestamp) is recorded (feeds C2); for Bucket C: the final-route checkpoint (the specific existing fail-closed hold or lifecycle suppression) is recorded.
  - All checkpoints are joined on a single account-level key (per §4c).
  - The reconciled chain is reviewable per case at the account level.

A case with a missing or mismatched value at any checkpoint fails reconciliation for that case. Bucket-level expectation (admit / route / fail-closed-or-suppressed) does not exempt a case from the per-case reconciliation requirement.

11d. No-bypass rule — existing lifecycle branch, hold, or suppression

No case in any of the three buckets may bypass an existing lifecycle branch, an existing hold, or an existing suppression. Specifically:

  - A Bucket C case must terminate in the existing branch, hold, or suppression that the case is designed to exercise. The case does NOT skip the branch, hold, or suppression. The case does NOT get routed around it by relaxing eligibility, refusing the case, bypassing lifecycle, or granting connector access out of band.
  - A Bucket A or Bucket B case that would, under ordinary rules, encounter an existing branch, hold, or suppression must reconcile THROUGH it (i.e., the branch, hold, or suppression is honored; the case proceeds only if ordinary rules permit). The case does NOT skip the branch, hold, or suppression.
  - The no-bypass rule is verified per case at reconciliation. Any case that bypasses an existing branch, hold, or suppression fails the preflight regardless of bucket-level expectation.

The preflight is descriptive — it verifies the existing rules and the existing branches, holds, and suppressions. It does NOT modify them, suspend them, or waive them. The CS cert posture, the Expansion Assist descriptive posture, the five-state Helio Start reporting, the fail-closed holds, the forward-event-only resolution, and the pending external-authority refusal boundary all stand as written.

11e. Pass criteria (per case and per preflight)

  - Per case: the case's paid source reconciles from eligibility-flow start to its final route, and the case does not bypass any existing lifecycle branch, hold, or suppression.
  - Per bucket: all eight cases in the bucket satisfy their bucket-level expectation (Bucket A: admit; Bucket B: assisted route; Bucket C: fail-closed or suppressed through the existing branch, hold, or suppression).
  - Per preflight: all 24 cases pass per-case reconciliation and per-bucket expectation. Any case failure fails the preflight.

A preflight run that does not satisfy per-case reconciliation, per-bucket expectation, or per-preflight completion is not a passed preflight. A passed preflight is one of the inputs to the April 12 launch; it is not itself a launch decision.

11f. What the preflight does NOT do

  - The preflight does NOT approve launch, budget, paid traffic, launch timing, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, pipeline target, a second paid batch, or a later additional batch. Budget, paid traffic, launch timing, and launch are approved for April 12 in this draft (§1 rows 1–4); the preflight does not constitute that approval. Rows 5–9 and 11 in §1 remain NOT approved.
  - The preflight does NOT modify any rule in §7.
  - The preflight does NOT change C1–C4 or M1/M2 in §4 / §5.
  - The preflight does NOT trigger any stop or pause condition in §3.
  - The preflight does NOT produce acquisition, pipeline, revenue, or forecast evidence.
  - The preflight does NOT count toward the $8,000-or-25-admissions close in §2; it is nonproduction.
  - The preflight does NOT authorize a second or later additional batch (§1 rows 8 and 9).

11g. What the preflight DOES do

  - The preflight verifies that the existing instrumentation, routing, lifecycle, hold, and suppression stack produces the expected per-case reconciliation and per-bucket outcomes on 24 designed cases.
  - The preflight surfaces any case-level reconciliation gap, any bucket-level expectation miss, and any bypass of an existing branch, hold, or suppression as a preflight finding.
  - The preflight report feeds the engineering release/rollback posture owned by Daniela and feeds the April 12 launch gate owned by Priya.

The preflight is the precondition gate Daniela requires before the April 12 launch. It is in this draft as a structural requirement; its case-level specifics belong in the (separate, future) preflight spec and are not in this draft.

arguments.message:
Q2 Helio Start paid-test — Priya approved ONE Q2 2027 high-intent paid-search test (4/9). Scope: $8,000 maximum budget, April 12 launch. Earlier-of-$8,000-or-25-admissions close is the close.

Stops/pauses added to §3:
- S3 (hard stop): if an unsupported applicant enters the admitted path, the batch stops immediately.
- P1 (pause): if paid-source attribution cannot reconcile end-to-end from eligibility-flow start through admission and assisted routing, the batch pauses immediately. Triggers on the running read that surfaces the gap, not a delayed post-hoc read.
- P3 (pause): after at least 10 admissions, if more than 10% of admitted workspaces exceed 90 account-level support minutes, the batch pauses. Share-based threshold; M2 (share) is what triggers, M1 (number) is reported alongside.

Mature-outcome gates unchanged: paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort remain UNAVAILABLE until the fixed admitted cohort has complete day-90 windows. Day-7 first integration remains a leading indicator only.
