arguments.title: Helio Start pre-discovery readout — measurement spine
arguments.body:
Pre-read for Monday. Builds on the baseline summary Priya already read. Goal of this doc: lock the measurement spine before we go further on naming, lifecycle, or pricing mechanics.

Sections:
1. Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
2. Measurement method
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
5. Open questions (lifecycle, instrumentation, support, eng sizing)

—
1. Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
—

"Helio Start" is the working name for the sub-50-seat tier we are pre-discovering. It is internal shorthand only.

Priya's gate (2023-06-14): the name implies nothing customer-facing until all of the following are ready — eligibility rules, refusal rules, instrumentation, lifecycle paths, and support boundaries. Nothing in this doc, in the baseline summary, or in any Slack thread should be read as a launch commitment, a launch date, or a marketing promise.

If this tier ships, the working name may change. Anything written here should hold under that.

—
2. Measurement method
—

Cohort definitions (locked):
- Mid-seg v2 = 75–200 seats (default since 2023-04-26). 50–75 = starter band. v1 (50–200) stays in the warehouse for back-compat comps only — we do not roll v1 forward.
- Under-50 / sub-50 = the band this tier work is actually about. We report it separately from mid-seg v2 in every cut going forward.

Activation (locked):
- Activation definition v3: `+ ≥1 in-product event in 14d` (locked 2023-03-16). Target: 60% for mid-seg+ in 14d; the conditional 65% target is tied to sub-50 tier ship in Q3 and is not in scope of this doc.
- Activation KPI is owned by me.

What we measure for the sub-50 work (per the 2023-06-01 small-biz tier scoping):
- Activation deltas (vs. control, vs. mid-seg v2 baseline)
- Support load (tickets / contact rate per activated account, by seat band)
- Gross retention by seat band (we are NOT using ACV as a metric for this tier)

What we explicitly do NOT do in this readout:
- We do not pool 50–75 into mid-seg v2. The 50–75 band is reported on its own line.
- We do not mix sub-50 cuts with the mid-seg v2 cohort for significance. They are separate populations with different effect-size expectations.
- We do not use first-significance-only as evidence. Standing rule from 2023-03-26: first sig on a growth exp does not ship — wait one stab cohort. Pre-registered stab def (same metric, same direction, n ≥ treatment) plus p<0.01 on the second-look cohort must clear before the next peek.

Cuts (per Owen's cadence, locked 2023-02-13): every ruling — in or out — gets a 1-pager with why, cuts, p-value, effect-size, and call. Summary up top, raw attached.

—
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
—

Headline: simple under-50 deployments where the customer lands a first integration inside week 1 are already behaving near the target range. The gap is not in the happy path — the gap is in the friction modes around it.

Specifically:
- Near target: first-week first integration on simple under-50 deployments. Activation v3 sits in the band we would expect a healthy sub-50 segment to reach if the deployment stayed simple.
- Lagging by more than 15 points: permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity. Each of these on its own pulls activation v3 down by ≥15 points relative to the simple-deployment baseline.

Read: the activation ceiling for sub-50 is not gated by acquisition quality or by the product's ability to deliver value on a clean install. It is gated by the four friction modes above. Any tier design that does not address those four modes will not move the activation KPI regardless of pricing, naming, or lifecycle cadence.

Implication for scoping: the four friction modes are the spine of what "Helio Start" needs to actually solve. Anything we add on top (lifecycle nudges, expansion plays, pricing-page mechanics) is downstream of these four.

We are NOT yet calling this finding "shippable." It is a baseline read, not a treatment effect. It needs the second-look cohort before we promote it.

—
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
—

Pending decisions — to be locked before any customer-facing naming:

Eligibility (open):
- Which seat bands qualify. Band 20–75 is pending as the working envelope; we need a clean ruling on whether 20–50, 50–75, or 20–75 is the in-scope band for the tier.
- Self-serve vs. sales-assisted boundary for sub-50. Affects refusal-rule design.
- Trial vs. freemium vs. paid-only entry. Affects refusal rules and instrumentation scope.

Refusal rules (open):
- When do we say "this customer is not a Helio Start fit" — at signup, at first-integration miss, at billing-failure, or at migration-complexity flag?
- What is the escalation path for refused accounts (sales handoff, hold queue, manual review)? Affects support load metric.
- How refusal interacts with the four friction modes: if a customer hits permissions or migration friction, do we refuse, route, or sequence?

Implication of the baseline: refusal rules need to be at least as good at catching the four friction modes as they are at catching fit-mismatches. A tier that refuses on fit but admits on permissions complexity will still miss the activation target.

Naming implication: until eligibility and refusal rules are locked, "Helio Start" stays internal. We will not surface the name in lifecycle copy, pricing, or sales conversations.

—
5. Open questions
—

Lifecycle:
- What is the in-product nudge cadence for the four friction modes? Standing rule (2023-03-26) applies — first sig does not ship, wait one stab cohort.
- Email vs. in-product vs. PostHog-flagged-only routing for sub-50 expansion plays — must stay disambiguated from email-lift attribution per the expansion_nudge_60d_v1 precedent (launched 2023-05-23, mid-seg v2 only).
- How does the lifecycle path branch when a customer hits a refusal rule?

Instrumentation:
- Are permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity each individually evented in PostHog with sufficient coverage to support the activation v3 cut? Need an audit before we can run the 1-pagers.
- Seat-band tagging at signup — do we have a reliable band-at-signup field, or do we reconstruct it post-hoc? Affects whether eligibility can be measured cleanly.
- Refusal-rule eventing — what fires when a refusal rule trips, and where does it land in the warehouse?

Support:
- Support load model for the four friction modes — what is the expected ticket volume per activated sub-50 account under each mode? Marcus Vail (CRO) alignment requires this to be explicit before any instrumentation commitments land.
- Support boundary: what does Helio support cover for the tier vs. what falls to self-serve docs / community?
- How refusal escalations hit support load — do they count against the support-load metric for this tier?

Engineering sizing:
- Daniela (eng) capacity is the binding constraint. Need a clean read on the eng ask for the four friction-mode fixes before we can promise anything to Marcus Vail on a ship window.
- Which of the four friction modes are quick wins vs. multi-quarter work? Determines whether we scope to a v0 of the tier or wait for a fuller build.
- Instrumentation work above — eng sizing depends on what the audit surfaces.

—
End of pre-read. Next step: walk this with Priya Monday, then lock the band decision and start the instrumentation audit.

arguments.body:
Pre-read for Monday. Builds on the baseline summary Priya already read. Goal of this doc: lock the measurement spine before we go further on naming, lifecycle, or pricing mechanics.

How to read this doc: the refusal rules, eligibility checks, and tier design we are pre-discovering exist to protect customers from a self-serve setup that won't deliver value for them. If a setup will fail for an account — whether because of permissions, import, billing, or migration complexity, or because the account's needs exceed what self-serve carries — the right move is to route that account to a path where they can succeed, not to push them through a plan they will churn out of. Every refusal rule below should be readable as a customer safeguard first.

Sections:
1. Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
2. Measurement method
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
5. Open questions (lifecycle, instrumentation, support, eng sizing)

—
1. Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
—

"Helio Start" is the working name for the sub-50-seat tier we are pre-discovering. It is internal shorthand only.

Priya's gate (2023-06-14): the name implies nothing customer-facing until all of the following are ready — eligibility rules, refusal rules, instrumentation, lifecycle paths, and support boundaries. Nothing in this doc, in the baseline summary, or in any Slack thread should be read as a launch commitment, a launch date, or a marketing promise.

The framing is protective, not exclusionary: we are pre-discovering whether the tier can be designed so that customers who enter it have a realistic path to activation, and so that customers the tier won't serve are routed to a path that does. If the design can't meet that bar, the right answer is to not ship the tier, not to ship it with weaker rules.

If this tier ships, the working name may change. Anything written here should hold under that.

—
2. Measurement method
—

Cohort definitions (locked):
- Mid-seg v2 = 75–200 seats (default since 2023-04-26). 50–75 = starter band. v1 (50–200) stays in the warehouse for back-compat comps only — we do not roll v1 forward.
- Under-50 / sub-50 = the band this tier work is actually about. We report it separately from mid-seg v2 in every cut going forward.

Activation (locked):
- Activation definition v3: `+ ≥1 in-product event in 14d` (locked 2023-03-16). Target: 60% for mid-seg+ in 14d; the conditional 65% target is tied to sub-50 tier ship in Q3 and is not in scope of this doc.
- Activation KPI is owned by me.

What we measure for the sub-50 work (per the 2023-06-01 small-biz tier scoping):
- Activation deltas (vs. control, vs. mid-seg v2 baseline)
- Support load (tickets / contact rate per activated account, by seat band)
- Gross retention by seat band (we are NOT using ACV as a metric for this tier)

What we explicitly do NOT do in this readout:
- We do not pool 50–75 into mid-seg v2. The 50–75 band is reported on its own line.
- We do not mix sub-50 cuts with the mid-seg v2 cohort for significance. They are separate populations with different effect-size expectations.
- We do not use first-significance-only as evidence. Standing rule from 2023-03-26: first sig on a growth exp does not ship — wait one stab cohort. Pre-registered stab def (same metric, same direction, n ≥ treatment) plus p<0.01 on the second-look cohort must clear before the next peek.

Cuts (per Owen's cadence, locked 2023-02-13): every ruling — in or out — gets a 1-pager with why, cuts, p-value, effect-size, and call. Summary up top, raw attached.

—
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
—

Caveat on what this section shows (Owen, 2023-06-17): the baseline below is descriptive, not causal. It describes what we observe in the data, not what produces activation. In particular, first-week first integration is observed alongside activation in simple deployments — it is not, by itself, established as the cause of activation. We will not promote any framing that treats first-week integration as the lever that "creates" activation until we have a treatment effect in a controlled cut.

Headline: simple under-50 deployments where the customer lands a first integration inside week 1 are already behaving near the target range. The gap is not in the happy path — the gap is in the friction modes around it.

Specifically:
- Near target: first-week first integration on simple under-50 deployments. Activation v3 sits in the band we would expect a healthy sub-50 segment to reach if the deployment stayed simple.
- Lagging by more than 15 points: permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity. Each of these on its own pulls activation v3 down by ≥15 points relative to the simple-deployment baseline.

Read (descriptive): across the sub-50 population we have today, activation v3 is high in the simple-deployment, first-week-first-integration subset and lower in the four friction modes. The descriptive pattern is consistent with — but does not prove — those friction modes being the binding constraint on the segment's activation ceiling. A treatment-effect read (does fixing each mode move activation in a controlled cut?) is the next step.

Implication for scoping: if a future controlled cut confirms the friction-mode pattern as causal, the activation ceiling for sub-50 is gated by those four modes, not by acquisition quality or by the product's ability to deliver value on a clean install. Anything we add on top (lifecycle nudges, expansion plays, pricing-page mechanics) would be downstream of these four. Until that controlled cut lands, we treat the friction modes as the leading candidate spine for what "Helio Start" would need to actually solve — not as a confirmed one.

We are NOT yet calling this finding "shippable." It is a baseline read, not a treatment effect. It needs the second-look cohort and a controlled cut before we promote it.

—
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
—

Framing (Priya, 2023-06-17): the labels below are written so the tier reads as protective for the customer, not as a screen that sorts accounts into a lower tier. We don't say "this account isn't a fit for us." We say "this self-serve setup won't carry this account" — and route them to a path where the setup does carry them. The same framing applies to entry-mechanic choices: trial vs. freemium vs. paid-only entry is about making sure the customer has enough runway and context to succeed, not about offering a cheaper plan.

Pending decisions — to be locked before any customer-facing naming:

Eligibility (open):
- Which seat bands qualify. Band 20–75 is pending as the working envelope; we need a clean ruling on whether 20–50, 50–75, or 20–75 is the in-scope band for the tier. Bands describe what the self-serve setup can carry, not what tier of customer we're willing to take.
- Self-serve vs. sales-assisted boundary for sub-50. Affects refusal-rule design — the question is at what point an account needs a human to succeed, not at what point we choose not to sell to them.
- Trial vs. freemium vs. paid-only entry. The choice is governed by what gives the customer a fair chance to land a first integration and learn whether the product carries their use case — not by offering a lower-priced path.

Refusal rules (open):
- When do we route an account off the self-serve path — at signup, at first-integration miss, at billing-failure, or at migration-complexity flag? Each trigger is a moment where the self-serve setup has stopped carrying the account, and the right response is to move them to a path that does.
- What is the escalation path for routed accounts (sales handoff, hold queue, manual review)? Affects support load metric. The path should make the account feel handed-off, not refused.
- How refusal interacts with the four friction modes: if a customer hits permissions or migration friction, do we route, hold, or sequence? The principle is the same — the self-serve path has stopped carrying the account, so we don't keep them on it.

Implication of the baseline: refusal rules need to be at least as good at catching the four friction modes as they are at catching setup failures generally. A tier that routes on complexity but admits on permissions friction will still miss the activation target, and more importantly will leave customers stuck in a setup that won't deliver for them. The refusal rules protect the customer from that outcome; they are not a filter that protects us from the customer.

Naming implication: until eligibility and refusal rules are locked, "Helio Start" stays internal. We will not surface the name in lifecycle copy, pricing, or sales conversations.

—
5. Open questions
—

Lifecycle:
- What is the in-product nudge cadence for the four friction modes? Standing rule (2023-03-26) applies — first sig does not ship, wait one stab cohort.
- Email vs. in-product vs. PostHog-flagged-only routing for sub-50 expansion plays — must stay disambiguated from email-lift attribution per the expansion_nudge_60d_v1 precedent (launched 2023-05-23, mid-seg v2 only).
- How does the lifecycle path branch when a customer hits a refusal rule? The branch should be a hand-off to a setup that will carry them, not a stop sign.

Instrumentation:
- Are permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity each individually evented in PostHog with sufficient coverage to support the activation v3 cut? Need an audit before we can run the 1-pagers.
- Seat-band tagging at signup — do we have a reliable band-at-signup field, or do we reconstruct it post-hoc? Affects whether eligibility can be measured cleanly.
- Refusal-rule eventing — what fires when a refusal rule trips, and where does it land in the warehouse? Need the same eventing for the routing hand-off, not just the refusal moment.

Support:
- Support load model for the four friction modes — what is the expected ticket volume per activated sub-50 account under each mode? Marcus Vail (CRO) alignment requires this to be explicit before any instrumentation commitments land.
- Support boundary: what does Helio support cover for the tier vs. what falls to self-serve docs / community? The boundary should make it clear to the customer where the hand-off is.
- How refusal escalations hit support load — do they count against the support-load metric for this tier? Need this pinned before we read the load number.

Engineering sizing:
- Daniela (eng) capacity is the binding constraint. Need a clean read on the eng ask for the four friction-mode fixes before we can promise anything to Marcus Vail on a ship window.
- Which of the four friction modes are quick wins vs. multi-quarter work? Determines whether we scope to a v0 of the tier or wait for a fuller build.
- Instrumentation work above — eng sizing depends on what the audit surfaces.

—
End of pre-read. Next step: walk this with Priya Monday, then lock the band decision and start the instrumentation audit.

arguments.title: Helio Start pre-discovery readout — measurement spine
arguments.body:
Pre-read for Monday. Builds on the baseline summary Priya already read. Goal of this doc: lock the measurement spine before we go further on naming, lifecycle, or pricing mechanics.

Sections:
1. Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
2. Measurement method
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
5. Open questions (lifecycle, instrumentation, support, eng sizing)

—
1. Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
—

"Helio Start" is the working name for the sub-50-seat tier we are pre-discovering. It is internal shorthand only.

Priya's gate (2023-06-14): the name implies nothing customer-facing until all of the following are ready — eligibility rules, refusal rules, instrumentation, lifecycle paths, and support boundaries. Nothing in this doc, in the baseline summary, or in any Slack thread should be read as a launch commitment, a launch date, or a marketing promise.

If this tier ships, the working name may change. Anything written here should hold under that.

—
2. Measurement method
—

Cohort definitions (locked):
- Mid-seg v2 = 75–200 seats (default since 2023-04-26). 50–75 = starter band. v1 (50–200) stays in the warehouse for back-compat comps only — we do not roll v1 forward.
- Under-50 / sub-50 = the band this tier work is actually about. We report it separately from mid-seg v2 in every cut going forward.

Activation (locked):
- Activation definition v3: `+ ≥1 in-product event in 14d` (locked 2023-03-16). Target: 60% for mid-seg+ in 14d; the conditional 65% target is tied to sub-50 tier ship in Q3 and is not in scope of this doc.
- Activation KPI is owned by me.

What we measure for the sub-50 work (per the 2023-06-01 small-biz tier scoping):
- Activation deltas (vs. control, vs. mid-seg v2 baseline)
- Support load (tickets / contact rate per activated account, by seat band)
- Gross retention by seat band (we are NOT using ACV as a metric for this tier)

What we explicitly do NOT do in this readout:
- We do not pool 50–75 into mid-seg v2. The 50–75 band is reported on its own line.
- We do not mix sub-50 cuts with the mid-seg v2 cohort for significance. They are separate populations with different effect-size expectations.
- We do not use first-significance-only as evidence. Standing rule from 2023-03-26: first sig on a growth exp does not ship — wait one stab cohort. Pre-registered stab def (same metric, same direction, n ≥ treatment) plus p<0.01 on the second-look cohort must clear before the next peek.

Cuts (per Owen's cadence, locked 2023-02-13): every ruling — in or out — gets a 1-pager with why, cuts, p-value, effect-size, and call. Summary up top, raw attached.

—
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
—

Headline: simple under-50 deployments where the customer lands a first integration inside week 1 are already behaving near the target range. The gap is not in the happy path — the gap is in the friction modes around it.

Specifically:
- Near target: first-week first integration on simple under-50 deployments. Activation v3 sits in the band we would expect a healthy sub-50 segment to reach if the deployment stayed simple.
- Lagging by more than 15 points: permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity. Each of these on its own pulls activation v3 down by ≥15 points relative to the simple-deployment baseline.

Read: the activation ceiling for sub-50 is not gated by acquisition quality or by the product's ability to deliver value on a clean install. It is gated by the four friction modes above. Any tier design that does not address those four modes will not move the activation KPI regardless of pricing, naming, or lifecycle cadence.

Implication for scoping: the four friction modes are the spine of what "Helio Start" needs to actually solve. Anything we add on top (lifecycle nudges, expansion plays, pricing-page mechanics) is downstream of these four.

We are NOT yet calling this finding "shippable." It is a baseline read, not a treatment effect. It needs the second-look cohort before we promote it.

—
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
—

Pending decisions — to be locked before any customer-facing naming:

Eligibility (open):
- Which seat bands qualify. Band 20–75 is pending as the working envelope; we need a clean ruling on whether 20–50, 50–75, or 20–75 is the in-scope band for the tier.
- Self-serve vs. sales-assisted boundary for sub-50. Affects refusal-rule design.
- Trial vs. freemium vs. paid-only entry. Affects refusal rules and instrumentation scope.

Refusal rules (open):
- When do we say "this customer is not a Helio Start fit" — at signup, at first-integration miss, at billing-failure, or at migration-complexity flag?
- What is the escalation path for refused accounts (sales handoff, hold queue, manual review)? Affects support load metric.
- How refusal interacts with the four friction modes: if a customer hits permissions or migration friction, do we refuse, route, or sequence?

Implication of the baseline: refusal rules need to be at least as good at catching the four friction modes as they are at catching fit-mismatches. A tier that refuses on fit but admits on permissions complexity will still miss the activation target.

Naming implication: until eligibility and refusal rules are locked, "Helio Start" stays internal. We will not surface the name in lifecycle copy, pricing, or sales conversations.

—
5. Open questions
—

Lifecycle:
- What is the in-product nudge cadence for the four friction modes? Standing rule (2023-03-26) applies — first sig does not ship, wait one stab cohort.
- Email vs. in-product vs. PostHog-flagged-only routing for sub-50 expansion plays — must stay disambiguated from email-lift attribution per the expansion_nudge_60d_v1 precedent (launched 2023-05-23, mid-seg v2 only).
- How does the lifecycle path branch when a customer hits a refusal rule?

Instrumentation:
- Are permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity each individually evented in PostHog with sufficient coverage to support the activation v3 cut? Need an audit before we can run the 1-pagers.
- Seat-band tagging at signup — do we have a reliable band-at-signup field, or do we reconstruct it post-hoc? Affects whether eligibility can be measured cleanly.
- Refusal-rule eventing — what fires when a refusal rule trips, and where does it land in the warehouse?

Support:
- Support load model for the four friction modes — what is the expected ticket volume per activated sub-50 account under each mode? Marcus Vail (CRO) alignment requires this to be explicit before any instrumentation commitments land.
- Support boundary: what does Helio support cover for the tier vs. what falls to self-serve docs / community?
- How refusal escalations hit support load — do they count against the support-load metric for this tier?

Engineering sizing:
- Daniela (eng) capacity is the binding constraint. Need a clean read on the eng ask for the four friction-mode fixes before we can promise anything to Marcus Vail on a ship window.
- Which of the four friction modes are quick wins vs. multi-quarter work? Determines whether we scope to a v0 of the tier or wait for a fuller build.
- Instrumentation work above — eng sizing depends on what the audit surfaces.

—
End of pre-read. Next step: walk this with Priya Monday, then lock the band decision and start the instrumentation audit.

Pre-read for Monday. Builds on the baseline summary Priya already read. Goal of this doc: lock the measurement spine before we go further on naming, lifecycle, or pricing mechanics.

How to read this doc: the refusal rules, eligibility checks, and tier design we are pre-discovering exist to protect customers from a self-serve setup that won't deliver value for them. If a setup will fail for an account — whether because of permissions, import, billing, or migration complexity, or because the account's needs exceed what self-serve carries — the right move is to route that account to a path where they can succeed, not to push them through a plan they will churn out of. Every refusal rule below should be readable as a customer safeguard first.

Sections:
1. Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
2. Measurement method
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
5. Open questions (lifecycle, instrumentation, support, eng sizing)

—
1. Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
—

"Helio Start" is the working name for the sub-50-seat tier we are pre-discovering. It is internal shorthand only.

Priya's gate (2023-06-14): the name implies nothing customer-facing until all of the following are ready — eligibility rules, refusal rules, instrumentation, lifecycle paths, and support boundaries. Nothing in this doc, in the baseline summary, or in any Slack thread should be read as a launch commitment, a launch date, or a marketing promise.

The framing is protective, not exclusionary: we are pre-discovering whether the tier can be designed so that customers who enter it have a realistic path to activation, and so that customers the tier won't serve are routed to a path that does. If the design can't meet that bar, the right answer is to not ship the tier, not to ship it with weaker rules.

If this tier ships, the working name may change. Anything written here should hold under that.

—
2. Measurement method
—

Cohort definitions (locked):
- Mid-seg v2 = 75–200 seats (default since 2023-04-26). 50–75 = starter band. v1 (50–200) stays in the warehouse for back-compat comps only — we do not roll v1 forward.
- Under-50 / sub-50 = the band this tier work is actually about. We report it separately from mid-seg v2 in every cut going forward.

Activation (locked):
- Activation definition v3: `+ ≥1 in-product event in 14d` (locked 2023-03-16). Target: 60% for mid-seg+ in 14d; the conditional 65% target is tied to sub-50 tier ship in Q3 and is not in scope of this doc.
- Activation KPI is owned by me.

What we measure for the sub-50 work (per the 2023-06-01 small-biz tier scoping):
- Activation deltas (vs. control, vs. mid-seg v2 baseline)
- Support load (tickets / contact rate per activated account, by seat band)
- Gross retention by seat band (we are NOT using ACV as a metric for this tier)

What we explicitly do NOT do in this readout:
- We do not pool 50–75 into mid-seg v2. The 50–75 band is reported on its own line.
- We do not mix sub-50 cuts with the mid-seg v2 cohort for significance. They are separate populations with different effect-size expectations.
- We do not use first-significance-only as evidence. Standing rule from 2023-03-26: first sig on a growth exp does not ship — wait one stab cohort. Pre-registered stab def (same metric, same direction, n ≥ treatment) plus p<0.01 on the second-look cohort must clear before the next peek.

Cuts (per Owen's cadence, locked 2023-02-13): every ruling — in or out — gets a 1-pager with why, cuts, p-value, effect-size, and call. Summary up top, raw attached.

—
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
—

Caveat on what this section shows (Owen, 2023-06-17): the baseline below is descriptive, not causal. It describes what we observe in the data, not what produces activation. In particular, first-week first integration is observed alongside activation in simple deployments — it is not, by itself, established as the cause of activation. We will not promote any framing that treats first-week integration as the lever that "creates" activation until we have a treatment effect in a controlled cut.

Headline: simple under-50 deployments where the customer lands a first integration inside week 1 are already behaving near the target range. The gap is not in the happy path — the gap is in the friction modes around it.

Specifically:
- Near target: first-week first integration on simple under-50 deployments. Activation v3 sits in the band we would expect a healthy sub-50 segment to reach if the deployment stayed simple.
- Lagging by more than 15 points: permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity. Each of these on its own pulls activation v3 down by ≥15 points relative to the simple-deployment baseline.

Read (descriptive): across the sub-50 population we have today, activation v3 is high in the simple-deployment, first-week-first-integration subset and lower in the four friction modes. The descriptive pattern is consistent with — but does not prove — those friction modes being the binding constraint on the segment's activation ceiling. A treatment-effect read (does fixing each mode move activation in a controlled cut?) is the next step.

Implication for scoping: if a future controlled cut confirms the friction-mode pattern as causal, the activation ceiling for sub-50 is gated by those four modes, not by acquisition quality or by the product's ability to deliver value on a clean install. Anything we add on top (lifecycle nudges, expansion plays, pricing-page mechanics) would be downstream of these four. Until that controlled cut lands, we treat the friction modes as the leading candidate spine for what "Helio Start" would need to actually solve — not as a confirmed one.

We are NOT yet calling this finding "shippable." It is a baseline read, not a treatment effect. It needs the second-look cohort and a controlled cut before we promote it.

—
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
—

Framing (Priya, 2023-06-17): the labels below are written so the tier reads as protective for the customer, not as a screen that sorts accounts into a lower tier. We don't say "this account isn't a fit for us." We say "this self-serve setup won't carry this account" — and route them to a path where the setup does carry them. The same framing applies to entry-mechanic choices: trial vs. freemium vs. paid-only entry is about making sure the customer has enough runway and context to succeed, not about offering a cheaper plan.

Pending decisions — to be locked before any customer-facing naming:

Eligibility (open):
- Which seat bands qualify. Band 20–75 is pending as the working envelope; we need a clean ruling on whether 20–50, 50–75, or 20–75 is the in-scope band for the tier. Bands describe what the self-serve setup can carry, not what tier of customer we're willing to take.
- Self-serve vs. sales-assisted boundary for sub-50. Affects refusal-rule design — the question is at what point an account needs a human to succeed, not at what point we choose not to sell to them.
- Trial vs. freemium vs. paid-only entry. The choice is governed by what gives the customer a fair chance to land a first integration and learn whether the product carries their use case — not by offering a lower-priced path.

Refusal rules (open):
- When do we route an account off the self-serve path — at signup, at first-integration miss, at billing-failure, or at migration-complexity flag? Each trigger is a moment where the self-serve setup has stopped carrying the account, and the right response is to move them to a path that does.
- What is the escalation path for routed accounts (sales handoff, hold queue, manual review)? Affects support load metric. The path should make the account feel handed-off, not refused.
- How refusal interacts with the four friction modes: if a customer hits permissions or migration friction, do we route, hold, or sequence? The principle is the same — the self-serve path has stopped carrying the account, so we don't keep them on it.

Implication of the baseline: refusal rules need to be at least as good at catching the four friction modes as they are at catching setup failures generally. A tier that routes on complexity but admits on permissions friction will still miss the activation target, and more importantly will leave customers stuck in a setup that won't deliver for them. The refusal rules protect the customer from that outcome; they are not a filter that protects us from the customer.

Naming implication: until eligibility and refusal rules are locked, "Helio Start" stays internal. We will not surface the name in lifecycle copy, pricing, or sales conversations.

—
5. Open questions
—

Lifecycle:
- What is the in-product nudge cadence for the four friction modes? Standing rule (2023-03-26) applies — first sig does not ship, wait one stab cohort.
- Email vs. in-product vs. PostHog-flagged-only routing for sub-50 expansion plays — must stay disambiguated from email-lift attribution per the expansion_nudge_60d_v1 precedent (launched 2023-05-23, mid-seg v2 only).
- How does the lifecycle path branch when a customer hits a refusal rule? The branch should be a hand-off to a setup that will carry them, not a stop sign.

Instrumentation:
- Are permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity each individually evented in PostHog with sufficient coverage to support the activation v3 cut? Need an audit before we can run the 1-pagers.
- Seat-band tagging at signup — do we have a reliable band-at-signup field, or do we reconstruct it post-hoc? Affects whether eligibility can be measured cleanly.
- Refusal-rule eventing — what fires when a refusal rule trips, and where does it land in the warehouse? Need the same eventing for the routing hand-off, not just the refusal moment.

Support:
- Support load model for the four friction modes — what is the expected ticket volume per activated sub-50 account under each mode? Marcus Vail (CRO) alignment requires this to be explicit before any instrumentation commitments land.
- Support boundary: what does Helio support cover for the tier vs. what falls to self-serve docs / community? The boundary should make it clear to the customer where the hand-off is.
- How refusal escalations hit support load — do they count against the support-load metric for this tier? Need this pinned before we read the load number.

Engineering sizing:
- Daniela (eng) capacity is the binding constraint. Need a clean read on the eng ask for the four friction-mode fixes before we can promise anything to Marcus Vail on a ship window.
- Which of the four friction modes are quick wins vs. multi-quarter work? Determines whether we scope to a v0 of the tier or wait for a fuller build.
- Instrumentation work above — eng sizing depends on what the audit surfaces.

—
End of pre-read. Next step: walk this with Priya Monday, then lock the band decision and start the instrumentation audit.

arguments.title: Helio Start first beta read — Aug 22
arguments.body:
# Helio Start first beta read — Aug 22

Working agenda. Goal: a decision read, not a dashboard tour.

## Activation shape
- Cohort definition + window (per activation KPI v3: ≥1 in-product event in 14d).
- Mid-segment (75–200, v2) curve vs. prior baselines (T6M v1 ≈ 2.1% on 50–200).
- Time-to-first-event distribution; where do beta wsps land on the curve.
- Open: are we reading activation lift, or just confirmation that nothing regressed?

## Support-load mix
- Ticket volume + category mix from the controlled-beta path only (learning coverage — non-public).
- Top failure modes (onboarding, entitlement mismatch, in-product confusion).
- Ines QA tier notes: state-changing = heavy review, mapping/education = light.
- Compare mix against a pre-beta baseline so we don't read absolute volume as a signal.

## Lifecycle education / copy risks
- Email + in-product education surfaces touching beta wsps.
- Copy that could be misread as a launch, pricing move, or paid-acquisition prompt — flag and hold.
- 'Helio Start' framing (2023-07-26): education + manual review only. Anything beyond that needs naming before it ships.

## Instrumentation confidence
- PostHog coverage on the events we'd cite (state-changing vs. mapping/education).
- Entitlement_state capture timing — per Daniela, captured at ws creation, updated on support handoff / billing change. No plan_name inference. Verify this held for the beta cohort.
- Gaps that would block a clean read (e.g. missing billing_account_mode on early-trial wsps — still open from 2023-08-01 review).

## Decision boundary
The only question on the table:

**Keep capped vs. widen later.**

Out of scope for this read:
- Launch framing (we are not launching).
- Pricing-page motion (Marcus's workstream, separate).
- Paid acquisition (not in scope for this cohort).
- Expansion / revenue credit (controlled-beta invites = learning coverage only — no pipeline, forecast, or pricing-page credit; 2023-08-15 Marcus hold still applies).

A widen-later call requires:
- Stab check on the same metric / direction, n ≥ treatment, p < 0.01 second look, before the next peek (standing rule 2023-03-26).
- Documentation of any instrumentation gaps closed, not deferred.

A keep-capped call is the default if activation shape, support load, or instrumentation confidence don't clear.

- Activation definition v3: `+ ≥1 in-product event in 14d` (locked 2023-03-16). Target: 60% for mid-seg+ in 14d; the conditional 65% target is tied to sub-50 tier ship in Q3 and is not in scope of this doc.
- Activation KPI is owned by me.

What we measure for the sub-50 work (per the 2023-06-01 small-biz tier scoping):
- Activation deltas (vs. control, vs. mid-seg v2 baseline)
- Support load (tickets / contact rate per activated account, by seat band)
- Gross retention by seat band (we are NOT using ACV as a metric for this tier)

What we explicitly do NOT do in this readout:
- We do not pool 50–75 into mid-seg v2. The 50–75 band is reported on its own line.
- We do not mix sub-50 cuts with the mid-seg v2 cohort for significance. They are separate populations with different effect-size expectations.
- We do not use first-significance-only as evidence. Standing rule from 2023-03-26: first sig on a growth exp does not ship — wait one stab cohort. Pre-registered stab def (same metric, same direction, n ≥ treatment) plus p<0.01 on the second-look cohort must clear before the next peek.

Cuts (per Owen's cadence, locked 2023-02-13): every ruling — in or out — gets a 1-pager with why, cuts, p-value, effect-size, and call. Summary up top, raw attached.

—
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
—

Headline: simple under-50 deployments where the customer lands a first integration inside week 1 are already behaving near the target range. The gap is not in the happy path — the gap is in the friction modes around it.

Specifically:
- Near target: first-week first integration on simple under-50 deployments. Activation v3 sits in the band we would expect a healthy sub-50 segment to reach if the deployment stayed simple.
- Lagging by more than 15 points: permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity. Each of these on its own pulls activation v3 down by ≥15 points relative to the simple-deployment baseline.

Read: the activation ceiling for sub-50 is not gated by acquisition quality or by the product's ability to deliver value on a clean install. It is gated by the four friction modes above. Any tier design that does not address those four modes will not move the activation KPI regardless of pricing, naming, or lifecycle cadence.

Implication for scoping: the four friction modes are the spine of what "Helio Start" needs to actually solve. Anything we add on top (lifecycle nudges, expansion plays, pricing-page mechanics) is downstream of these four.

We are NOT yet calling this finding "shippable." It is a baseline read, not a treatment effect. It needs the second-look cohort before we promote it.

—
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
—

Pending decisions — to be locked before any customer-facing naming:

Eligibility (open):
- Which seat bands qualify. Band 20–75 is pending as the working envelope; we need a clean ruling on whether 20–50, 50–75, or 20–75 is the in-scope band for the tier.
- Self-serve vs. sales-assisted boundary for sub-50. Affects refusal-rule design.
- Trial vs. freemium vs. paid-only entry. Affects refusal rules and instrumentation scope.

Refusal rules (open):
- When do we say "this customer is not a Helio Start fit" — at signup, at first-integration miss, at billing-failure, or at migration-complexity flag?
- What is the escalation path for refused accounts (sales handoff, hold queue, manual review)? Affects support load metric.
- How refusal interacts with the four friction modes: if a customer hits permissions or migration friction, do we refuse, route, or sequence?

Implication of the baseline: refusal rules need to be at least as good at catching the four friction modes as they are at catching fit-mismatches. A tier that refuses on fit but admits on permissions complexity will still miss the activation target.

Naming implication: until eligibility and refusal rules are locked, "Helio Start" stays internal. We will not surface the name in lifecycle copy, pricing, or sales conversations.

—
5. Open questions
—

Lifecycle:
- What is the in-product nudge cadence for the four friction modes? Standing rule (2023-03-26) applies — first sig does not ship, wait one stab cohort.
- Email vs. in-product vs. PostHog-flagged-only routing for sub-50 expansion plays — must stay disambiguated from email-lift attribution per the expansion_nudge_60d_v1 precedent (launched 2023-05-23, mid-seg v2 only).
- How does the lifecycle path branch when a customer hits a refusal rule?

Instrumentation:
- Are permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity each individually evented in PostHog with sufficient coverage to support the activation v3 cut? Need an audit before we can run the 1-pagers.
- Seat-band tagging at signup — do we have a reliable band-at-signup field, or do we reconstruct it post-hoc? Affects whether eligibility can be measured cleanly.
- Refusal-rule eventing — what fires when a refusal rule trips, and where does it land in the warehouse?

Support:
- Support load model for the four friction modes — what is the expected ticket volume per activated sub-50 account under each mode? Marcus Vail (CRO) alignment requires this to be explicit before any instrumentation commitments land.
- Support boundary: what does Helio support cover for the tier vs. what falls to self-serve docs / community?
- How refusal escalations hit support load — do they count against the support-load metric for this tier?

Engineering sizing:
- Daniela (eng) capacity is the binding constraint. Need a clean read on the eng ask for the four friction-mode fixes before we can promise anything to Marcus Vail on a ship window.
- Which of the four friction modes are quick wins vs. multi-quarter work? Determines whether we scope to a v0 of the tier or wait for a fuller build.
- Instrumentation work above — eng sizing depends on what the audit surfaces.

—
End of pre-read. Next step: walk this with Priya Monday, then lock the band decision and start the instrumentation audit.

arguments.body:
Pre-read for Monday. Builds on the baseline summary Priya already read. Goal of this doc: lock the measurement spine before we go further on naming, lifecycle, or pricing mechanics.

How to read this doc: the refusal rules, eligibility checks, and tier design we are pre-discovering exist to protect customers from a self-serve setup that won't deliver value for them. If a setup will fail for an account — whether because of permissions, import, billing, or migration complexity, or because the account's needs exceed what self-serve carries — the right move is to route that account to a path where they can succeed, not to push them through a plan they will churn out of. Every refusal rule below should be readable as a customer safeguard first.

Sections:
1. Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
2. Measurement method
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
5. Open questions (lifecycle, instrumentation, support, eng sizing)

—
1. Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
—

"Helio Start" is the working name for the sub-50-seat tier we are pre-discovering. It is internal shorthand only.

Priya's gate (2023-06-14): the name implies nothing customer-facing until all of the following are ready — eligibility rules, refusal rules, instrumentation, lifecycle paths, and support boundaries. Nothing in this doc, in the baseline summary, or in any Slack thread should be read as a launch commitment, a launch date, or a marketing promise.

The framing is protective, not exclusionary: we are pre-discovering whether the tier can be designed so that customers who enter it have a realistic path to activation, and so that customers the tier won't serve are routed to a path that does. If the design can't meet that bar, the right answer is to not ship the tier, not to ship it with weaker rules.

If this tier ships, the working name may change. Anything written here should hold under that.

—
2. Measurement method
—

Cohort definitions (locked):
- Mid-seg v2 = 75–200 seats (default since 2023-04-26). 50–75 = starter band. v1 (50–200) stays in the warehouse for back-compat comps only — we do not roll v1 forward.
- Under-50 / sub-50 = the band this tier work is actually about. We report it separately from mid-seg v2 in every cut going forward.

Activation (locked):
- Activation definition v3: `+ ≥1 in-product event in 14d` (locked 2023-03-16). Target: 60% for mid-seg+ in 14d; the conditional 65% target is tied to sub-50 tier ship in Q3 and is not in scope of this doc.
- Activation KPI is owned by me.

What we measure for the sub-50 work (per the 2023-06-01 small-biz tier scoping):
- Activation deltas (vs. control, vs. mid-seg v2 baseline)
- Support load (tickets / contact rate per activated account, by seat band)
- Gross retention by seat band (we are NOT using ACV as a metric for this tier)

What we explicitly do NOT do in this readout:
- We do not pool 50–75 into mid-seg v2. The 50–75 band is reported on its own line.
- We do not mix sub-50 cuts with the mid-seg v2 cohort for significance. They are separate populations with different effect-size expectations.
- We do not use first-significance-only as evidence. Standing rule from 2023-03-26: first sig on a growth exp does not ship — wait one stab cohort. Pre-registered stab def (same metric, same direction, n ≥ treatment) plus p<0.01 on the second-look cohort must clear before the next peek.

Cuts (per Owen's cadence, locked 2023-02-13): every ruling — in or out — gets a 1-pager with why, cuts, p-value, effect-size, and call. Summary up top, raw attached.

—
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
—

Caveat on what this section shows (Owen, 2023-06-17): the baseline below is descriptive, not causal. It describes what we observe in the data, not what produces activation. In particular, first-week first integration is observed alongside activation in simple deployments — it is not, by itself, established as the cause of activation. We will not promote any framing that treats first-week integration as the lever that "creates" activation until we have a treatment effect in a controlled cut.

Headline: simple under-50 deployments where the customer lands a first integration inside week 1 are already behaving near the target range. The gap is not in the happy path — the gap is in the friction modes around it.

Specifically:
- Near target: first-week first integration on simple under-50 deployments. Activation v3 sits in the band we would expect a healthy sub-50 segment to reach if the deployment stayed simple.
- Lagging by more than 15 points: permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity. Each of these on its own pulls activation v3 down by ≥15 points relative to the simple-deployment baseline.

Read (descriptive): across the sub-50 population we have today, activation v3 is high in the simple-deployment, first-week-first-integration subset and lower in the four friction modes. The descriptive pattern is consistent with — but does not prove — those friction modes being the binding constraint on the segment's activation ceiling. A treatment-effect read (does fixing each mode move activation in a controlled cut?) is the next step.

Implication for scoping: if a future controlled cut confirms the friction-mode pattern as causal, the activation ceiling for sub-50 is gated by those four modes, not by acquisition quality or by the product's ability to deliver value on a clean install. Anything we add on top (lifecycle nudges, expansion plays, pricing-page mechanics) would be downstream of these four. Until that controlled cut lands, we treat the friction modes as the leading candidate spine for what "Helio Start" would need to actually solve — not as a confirmed one.

We are NOT yet calling this finding "shippable." It is a baseline read, not a treatment effect. It needs the second-look cohort and a controlled cut before we promote it.

—
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
—

Framing (Priya, 2023-06-17): the labels below are written so the tier reads as protective for the customer, not as a screen that sorts accounts into a lower tier. We don't say "this account isn't a fit for us." We say "this self-serve setup won't carry this account" — and route them to a path where the setup does carry them. The same framing applies to entry-mechanic choices: trial vs. freemium vs. paid-only entry is about making sure the customer has enough runway and context to succeed, not about offering a cheaper plan.

Pending decisions — to be locked before any customer-facing naming:

Eligibility (open):
- Which seat bands qualify. Band 20–75 is pending as the working envelope; we need a clean ruling on whether 20–50, 50–75, or 20–75 is the in-scope band for the tier. Bands describe what the self-serve setup can carry, not what tier of customer we're willing to take.
- Self-serve vs. sales-assisted boundary for sub-50. Affects refusal-rule design — the question is at what point an account needs a human to succeed, not at what point we choose not to sell to them.
- Trial vs. freemium vs. paid-only entry. The choice is governed by what gives the customer a fair chance to land a first integration and learn whether the product carries their use case — not by offering a lower-priced path.

Refusal rules (open):
- When do we route an account off the self-serve path — at signup, at first-integration miss, at billing-failure, or at migration-complexity flag? Each trigger is a moment where the self-serve setup has stopped carrying the account, and the right response is to move them to a path that does.
- What is the escalation path for routed accounts (sales handoff, hold queue, manual review)? Affects support load metric. The path should make the account feel handed-off, not refused.
- How refusal interacts with the four friction modes: if a customer hits permissions or migration friction, do we route, hold, or sequence? The principle is the same — the self-serve path has stopped carrying the account, so we don't keep them on it.

Implication of the baseline: refusal rules need to be at least as good at catching the four friction modes as they are at catching setup failures generally. A tier that routes on complexity but admits on permissions friction will still miss the activation target, and more importantly will leave customers stuck in a setup that won't deliver for them. The refusal rules protect the customer from that outcome; they are not a filter that protects us from the customer.

Naming implication: until eligibility and refusal rules are locked, "Helio Start" stays internal. We will not surface the name in lifecycle copy, pricing, or sales conversations.

—
5. Open questions
—

Lifecycle:
- What is the in-product nudge cadence for the four friction modes? Standing rule (2023-03-26) applies — first sig does not ship, wait one stab cohort.
- Email vs. in-product vs. PostHog-flagged-only routing for sub-50 expansion plays — must stay disambiguated from email-lift attribution per the expansion_nudge_60d_v1 precedent (launched 2023-05-23, mid-seg v2 only).
- How does the lifecycle path branch when a customer hits a refusal rule? The branch should be a hand-off to a setup that will carry them, not a stop sign.

Instrumentation:
- Are permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity each individually evented in PostHog with sufficient coverage to support the activation v3 cut? Need an audit before we can run the 1-pagers.
- Seat-band tagging at signup — do we have a reliable band-at-signup field, or do we reconstruct it post-hoc? Affects whether eligibility can be measured cleanly.
- Refusal-rule eventing — what fires when a refusal rule trips, and where does it land in the warehouse? Need the same eventing for the routing hand-off, not just the refusal moment.

Support:
- Support load model for the four friction modes — what is the expected ticket volume per activated sub-50 account under each mode? Marcus Vail (CRO) alignment requires this to be explicit before any instrumentation commitments land.
- Support boundary: what does Helio support cover for the tier vs. what falls to self-serve docs / community? The boundary should make it clear to the customer where the hand-off is.
- How refusal escalations hit support load — do they count against the support-load metric for this tier? Need this pinned before we read the load number.

Engineering sizing:
- Daniela (eng) capacity is the binding constraint. Need a clean read on the eng ask for the four friction-mode fixes before we can promise anything to Marcus Vail on a ship window.
- Which of the four friction modes are quick wins vs. multi-quarter work? Determines whether we scope to a v0 of the tier or wait for a fuller build.
- Instrumentation work above — eng sizing depends on what the audit surfaces.

—
End of pre-read. Next step: walk this with Priya Monday, then lock the band decision and start the instrumentation audit.

arguments.title: Helio Start Q4 controlled beta — operating shape
arguments.body:
Helio Start — Q4 operating shape (controlled beta)
Owner: Riley · Audience: staff leads · Source of truth: 09-28 closeout (Tomás accepted frame)
Status: Q4 controlled beta ONLY. Not a GA plan. Not a pricing-page plan. Not a new team charter.

This doc exists because shorthand drifted after the 09-28 closeout. If you are writing about Helio Start in Q4, this is the version you read first. If something here disagrees with a Slack thread, an earlier doc, or a deck — this doc wins until the next closeout updates it.

────────────────────────
1. Eligible accounts
────────────────────────
A workspace is eligible for the Q4 Helio Start controlled beta only if ALL of the following are true at invite:

- Workspace size: under 50 workspaces. (Mid-seg v2 default is 75–200; 50–75 is starter. Helio Start beta is a different cohort window and is gated separately — it is not mid-seg.)
- Integration pattern: first-week integration (the workspace reaches its first successful integration within week 1 of invite).
- Admin ownership: clean admin ownership — a single, identifiable admin who can attest to admin proof at invite.
- No manual billing need: the workspace does not require manual billing intervention to operate in the beta.
- No import or migration need: the workspace does not require import, data migration, or migration-help support to operate in the beta.

Eligibility is checked at invite, not at signup. An account that becomes eligible later does not retroactively enter. Eligibility fields must be complete before invite is sent.

────────────────────────
2. Explicit unsupported list
────────────────────────
The following are NOT supported in the Q4 controlled beta. Staff leads must not promise, imply, or design toward any of these:

- Manual billing setup, billing-expectation remediation, or hand-holding through billing flows. (These routed 7 of 34 support questions in the 09-26 rollup and are a known load driver.)
- Import, data migration, or migration-help work. (4 of 34 support questions in the 09-26 rollup.)
- Inherited-integration workspaces where the attestor at invite is an admin who did not set up the original integration. (Admin-proof attestation cannot reliably catch this — known false-negative edge, not a defect. Watch, do not counter.)
- Shared-admin-alias workspaces. (Same class of edge as inherited-integration.)
- Pricing-page exposure of Helio Start as a self-serve path. (Directly contradicts the 09-28 not-approved list. See also the website footer FAQ cleanup note still open.)
- Paid acquisition funnels into Helio Start.
- GA planning, GA timelines, or any forecastable launch language.

────────────────────────
3. Measurement and dashboard shape
────────────────────────
Owen owns the Helio Start beta dashboard and readout. Shape of the readout:

- Activation is reported separately from retained mid-seg (v2: 75–200 default, 50–75 starter) and separately from Expansion Assist. These are three different measurements — do not collapse them into one number.
- Beta dashboard reads use the existing 09-26 rollup format: live accounts, de-duped first-integration attempts, invite acceptances since the admin-proof patch, admin_proof_attested count, unsure-routed-to-CS count, and a support-question breakdown by category (permissions/admin-ownership, billing-expectation, import/migration, API-key/setup docs-first).
- Success metric for the beta: activation under defs v3 (+ ≥1 in-product event in 14d). Do not substitute a revenue, expansion, or retention metric for the activation read.
- Inherited-integration and shared-admin-alias cases are tracked as known edges, not as defects to be removed from the read.

────────────────────────
4. Lifecycle boundaries
────────────────────────
Ines owns lifecycle copy for the Q4 controlled beta. The fork stays narrow:

- Only the conservative, non-state-changing lifecycle fork runs in Q4. No state-changing sends go out to the Helio Start beta cohort.
- The fork boundary from sub-50 to mid-seg is a documented state: same event, same threshold, same QA tier per send. Support and CS must read the boundary the same way.
- Lifecycle copy must not promise anything in the explicit unsupported list (section 2). If a send would imply manual billing help, import help, inherited-integration handling, shared-admin-alias handling, pricing-page exposure, paid acquisition, or GA/launch language, it does not ship.
- The lifecycle fork is allowed to run in Q4 only as long as the unsupported list stays explicit. If the unsupported list needs to widen, that is a closeout-level decision, not a copy-level decision.

────────────────────────
5. Instrumentation responsibilities
────────────────────────
- Daniela owns entitlement and support-state instrumentation in the measurement plan.
  - Entitlement_state is captured at workspace creation and updated on support handoff and billing change. There is no plan_name inference. Legacy null rows are annotated with the awaiting_backfill sentinel, not imputed from plan name.
  - Support-state updates flow through the CS-owned support-handoff taxonomy (YELLOW per Daniela's 6/26 readout — CS-owned). The taxonomy is what makes a support-state change a measurement event rather than a free-text note.
- Owen owns readout wiring against entitlement and support-state events. The beta dashboard reads entitlement_state and support_state as first-class fields; the readout does not infer them.
- Inherited-integration and shared-admin-alias edges are tagged in the readout, not silently dropped.

────────────────────────
6. Language that is not allowed
────────────────────────
The following language is not allowed in Q4 Helio Start docs, decks, Slack posts, or customer-facing copy without the explicit beta-validated-not-committed tag and a separate approval:

- "Launch" or "launching" applied to Helio Start in Q4.
- "GA," "generally available," or any GA-timing language.
- "Pipeline" applied to Helio Start revenue or accounts in Q4, unless explicitly tagged beta-validated-not-committed.
- "Pricing page" exposure of Helio Start as a self-serve path.
- "Paid acquisition" or any acquisition-funnel framing of Helio Start.
- "Forecast" applied to Helio Start Q4 numbers. Marcus Vail explicitly accepted at the 09-28 closeout that there is no Q4 launch forecast to claim.
- "Self-serve" applied to Helio Start in any Q4 customer-facing surface.
- Any framing that implies Helio Start in Q4 is a Growth process output, a new formal team, or a public launch commitment. Riley's Q4 role is cross-functional operating model only.

If a draft contains any of the above language, it is rewritten before review — not annotated, not caveated. The bar is the word does not appear.

────────────────────────
What this doc is not
────────────────────────
- It is not a GA plan. There is no Q4 GA plan.
- It is not a pricing-page plan. Pricing-page exposure is explicitly out of scope for Q4.
- It is not a new team charter. The Q4 operating model is the same cross-functional shape that ran in Q3, with the same role split (Owen / Daniela / Ines / Riley), minus anything that would imply a formal team or public commitment.

────────────────────────
Pointers
────────────────────────
- 09-28 closeout ruling: Tomás accepted the controlled-beta frame, gates, and not-approved list as written above.
- 09-26 rollup: live dashboard numbers and the support-question breakdown cited above.
- 09-14 admin-proof patch resolution: admin_proof_attested logs at invite; unsure routes to CS pre-setup.
- 09-20 inherited-integration edge: known false-negative class, watch not counter.
- 09-25 plan_name→entitlement fallback PR: rejected; use awaiting_backfill, not inference.
- Open (not in this doc): website footer FAQ still implies a Helio Start self-serve path. Revisit before any site copy refresh in Q4.

arguments.title: Helio Start pre-discovery readout — measurement spine
arguments.body:
Pre-read for Monday. Builds on the baseline summary Priya already read. Goal of this doc: lock the measurement spine before we go further on naming, lifecycle, or pricing mechanics.

Sections:
1. Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
2. Measurement method
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
5. Open questions (lifecycle, instrumentation, support, eng sizing)

—
1. Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
—

"Helio Start" is the working name for the sub-50-seat tier we are pre-discovering. It is internal shorthand only.

Priya's gate (2023-06-14): the name implies nothing customer-facing until all of the following are ready — eligibility rules, refusal rules, instrumentation, lifecycle paths, and support boundaries. Nothing in this doc, in the baseline summary, or in any Slack thread should be read as a launch commitment, a launch date, or a marketing promise.

If this tier ships, the working name may change. Anything written here should hold under that.

—
2. Measurement method
—

Cohort definitions (locked):
- Mid-seg v2 = 75–200 seats (default since 2023-04-26). 50–75 = starter band. v1 (50–200) stays in the warehouse for back-compat comps only — we do not roll v1 forward.
- Under-50 / sub-50 = the band this tier work is actually about. We report it separately from mid-seg v2 in every cut going forward.

Activation (locked):
- Activation definition v3: `+ ≥1 in-product event in 14d` (locked 2023-03-16). Target: 60% for mid-seg+ in 14d; the conditional 65% target is tied to sub-50 tier ship in Q3 and is not in scope of this doc.
- Activation KPI is owned by me.

What we measure for the sub-50 work (per the 2023-06-01 small-biz tier scoping):
- Activation deltas (vs. control, vs. mid-seg v2 baseline)
- Support load (tickets / contact rate per activated account, by seat band)
- Gross retention by seat band (we are NOT using ACV as a metric for this tier)

What we explicitly do NOT do in this readout:
- We do not pool 50–75 into mid-seg v2. The 50–75 band is reported on its own line.
- We do not mix sub-50 cuts with the mid-seg v2 cohort for significance. They are separate populations with different effect-size expectations.
- We do not use first-significance-only as evidence. Standing rule from 2023-03-26: first sig on a growth exp does not ship — wait one stab cohort. Pre-registered stab def (same metric, same direction, n ≥ treatment) plus p<0.01 on the second-look cohort must clear before the next peek.

Cuts (per Owen's cadence, locked 2023-02-13): every ruling — in or out — gets a 1-pager with why, cuts, p-value, effect-size, and call. Summary up top, raw attached.

—
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
—

Headline: simple under-50 deployments where the customer lands a first integration inside week 1 are already behaving near the target range. The gap is not in the happy path — the gap is in the friction modes around it.

Specifically:
- Near target: first-week first integration on simple under-50 deployments. Activation v3 sits in the band we would expect a healthy sub-50 segment to reach if the deployment stayed simple.
- Lagging by more than 15 points: permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity. Each of these on its own pulls activation v3 down by ≥15 points relative to the simple-deployment baseline.

Read: the activation ceiling for sub-50 is not gated by acquisition quality or by the product's ability to deliver value on a clean install. It is gated by the four friction modes above. Any tier design that does not address those four modes will not move the activation KPI regardless of pricing, naming, or lifecycle cadence.

Implication for scoping: the four friction modes are the spine of what "Helio Start" needs to actually solve. Anything we add on top (lifecycle nudges, expansion plays, pricing-page mechanics) is downstream of these four.

We are NOT yet calling this finding "shippable." It is a baseline read, not a treatment effect. It needs the second-look cohort before we promote it.

—
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
—

Pending decisions — to be locked before any customer-facing naming:

Eligibility (open):
- Which seat bands qualify. Band 20–75 is pending as the working envelope; we need a clean ruling on whether 20–50, 50–75, or 20–75 is the in-scope band for the tier.
- Self-serve vs. sales-assisted boundary for sub-50. Affects refusal-rule design.
- Trial vs. freemium vs. paid-only entry. Affects refusal rules and instrumentation scope.

Refusal rules (open):
- When do we say "this customer is not a Helio Start fit" — at signup, at first-integration miss, at billing-failure, or at migration-complexity flag?
- What is the escalation path for refused accounts (sales handoff, hold queue, manual review)? Affects support load metric.
- How refusal interacts with the four friction modes: if a customer hits permissions or migration friction, do we refuse, route, or sequence?

Implication of the baseline: refusal rules need to be at least as good at catching the four friction modes as they are at catching fit-mismatches. A tier that refuses on fit but admits on permissions complexity will still miss the activation target.

Naming implication: until eligibility and refusal rules are locked, "Helio Start" stays internal. We will not surface the name in lifecycle copy, pricing, or sales conversations.

—
5. Open questions
—

Lifecycle:
- What is the in-product nudge cadence for the four friction modes? Standing rule (2023-03-26) applies — first sig does not ship, wait one stab cohort.
- Email vs. in-product vs. PostHog-flagged-only routing for sub-50 expansion plays — must stay disambiguated from email-lift attribution per the expansion_nudge_60d_v1 precedent (launched 2023-05-23, mid-seg v2 only).
- How does the lifecycle path branch when a customer hits a refusal rule?

Instrumentation:
- Are permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity each individually evented in PostHog with sufficient coverage to support the activation v3 cut? Need an audit before we can run the 1-pagers.
- Seat-band tagging at signup — do we have a reliable band-at-signup field, or do we reconstruct it post-hoc? Affects whether eligibility can be measured cleanly.
- Refusal-rule eventing — what fires when a refusal rule trips, and where does it land in the warehouse?

Support:
- Support load model for the four friction modes — what is the expected ticket volume per activated sub-50 account under each mode? Marcus Vail (CRO) alignment requires this to be explicit before any instrumentation commitments land.
- Support boundary: what does Helio support cover for the tier vs. what falls to self-serve docs / community?
- How refusal escalations hit support load — do they count against the support-load metric for this tier?

Engineering sizing:
- Daniela (eng) capacity is the binding constraint. Need a clean read on the eng ask for the four friction-mode fixes before we can promise anything to Marcus Vail on a ship window.
- Which of the four friction modes are quick wins vs. multi-quarter work? Determines whether we scope to a v0 of the tier or wait for a fuller build.
- Instrumentation work above — eng sizing depends on what the audit surfaces.

—
End of pre-read. Next step: walk this with Priya Monday, then lock the band decision and start the instrumentation audit.
