arguments.body:
## 1. Purpose

Priya approved the $36,000 half-time Lifecycle Systems operations-contractor option on Aug 26, 2025. This brief is the implementation plan. No individual contractor has been selected; candidate evaluation and selection remain open and are scoped here, not pre-decided.

**Update 2025-08-28 (Finance):** Finance will not advance the contractor requisition further until 30-day and 60-day *pre-requisition* outcomes are observable. The first 30 days establish a complete campaign inventory, a recurring audit calendar, and an owner-approved handoff map for the assigned scope. The first 60 days test whether repeatable preparation hours fall, while separately tracking review burden, rework, cycle time, and boundary integrity. These observation windows run on the standing lanes only — no contractor is on payroll, no prep is delegated, and no scope is shifted to the contractor yet. The standing 30/60/90 *post-start* review cadence in §9 only becomes meaningful once a contractor starts, which itself only happens after this pre-requisition observation closes favorably.

**Update 2025-09-08 (Priya review of first-round candidate assessment):** Priya reviewed the first-round assessment and agreed that **Candidates A and C should advance** to the next round and **Candidate B should not**. The reasoning Priya endorsed: B's repeated push for eventual contractor review signoff conflicts with the role's categorical authority boundaries — i.e., B's boundary-discipline gap is dispositive against the eleven binding exclusions in §6 and against the 2025-08-05 midyear reaffirmation on the higher-risk `routine education` lane. Final contractor has **not been selected**; final interviews, references, selection, and onboarding remain pending. Two probes from the first-round screen are still owed and now carry forward to the final-interview cycle:

- **A's remaining probe — tooling-adaptation (forward to interview cycle).** Walk through your first 30 days on a Lifecycle Systems tool you don't yet know — what do you build first, and what do you not build? Tests whether A's lifecycle-tooling gap turns into improvisation in the tooling (a drift vector against the evidence-led-not-systems-led posture in §7) or into a scoped ramp that stays in prep and reconciliation. Failure mode is A drifting into systems-led work; success mode is A naming the tool boundary and asking the standing lane owner to set the read/write scope. This is the one probe most likely to surface drift before it reaches audit-risk territory, and it pairs with the week-6 lane check (E5) as the second gate.
- **C's remaining probe — denominator and rework on a quantitative inconsistency (forward to interview cycle).** You're doing repeatable evidence packaging and you spot a quantitative inconsistency in the source data — a denominator that doesn't tie out, or a rework pattern you can't yet explain. Walk me through your next 60 minutes. Tests whether C names the boundary correctly (route to Owen's analytical-conclusion lane, not fix the number) and whether C recognizes that a denominator question is a reporting-semantics question, which is Owen's lane per §2. Failure mode is C defaulting to "polish the narrative" or rewriting the number; success mode is C halting evidence packaging on that row and handing the inconsistency to Owen with the source intact. This is the probe most likely to surface whether C's documentation strength crosses into exec-language drafting (exclusion #11) or stays in prep.

Both probes carry forward unchanged; no replacement probes are introduced by the disposition. A and C advance to the interview stations listed in §8; B does not advance and is closed out at the first-round screen. The selection gate remains Priya's, with Riley drafting the recommendation. No pre-decision.

**Update 2025-09-10 (Q4 Lifecycle Systems planning check — readiness assignments):** The Sept 10 planning check (Priya, Riley, Owen, Ines, Daniela) confirmed the readiness-inputs split for the §3 30-day baseline artifacts. The first-round candidate screen closed with A and C as the **only finalists**; selection remains open. Final contractor is not selected; final interviews, references, selection, and onboarding remain pending. Per the planning check, the §3a/§3b/§3c baseline artifacts are now assigned to named owners with dated hand-offs so the 30-day baseline can be assembled on the standing lanes without depending on a contractor being on payroll:

- **§3a — Complete campaign inventory (Owen, by 2025-09-17).** Owen owns the current campaign-inventory inputs and will deliver the §3a artifact by Sept 17. The §3a completion sign-off remains Owen (reporting shape) plus Ines (state-meaning classification); Owen's Sept 17 input is the upstream pull, not the dual sign-off.
- **§3b — Recurring audit calendar (Ines, by 2025-09-18).** Ines owns the recurring-audit-calendar inputs and will deliver the §3b artifact by Sept 18. Calendar sign-off remains the four lane owners per §3b; Ines's Sept 18 input is the upstream draft.
- **§3c — Owner-approved handoff map (Ines, by 2025-09-18; engineering/no-production-access scope — Daniela, documented).** Ines owns the handoff-map inputs and will deliver the §3c artifact by Sept 18. Separately, Daniela documents the contractor's **no-production-access setup** — i.e., the engineering-side confirmation that whatever onboarding the contractor eventually receives is read-only/non-production and does not include release, deploy, or rollback authority (Daniela's lane is unchanged; this is the §3c engineering row made explicit). Handoff-map sign-off remains each named lane owner on their rows per §3c.

**Approval gate ahead of any contractor onboarding:** Onboarding materials (runbook tour draft, supervised-shadow plan, read-only access scope memo, evaluation rubric) **may be prepared** during the pre-requisition observation window — preparing materials is not the same as granting access or assigning work. **No individual contractor access, authority, or October work assignment is approved before a contractor is selected and hired.** Specifically:

- No contractor account is created on Lifecycle Systems surfaces.
- No contractor is added to the recurring audit calendar, the campaign inventory, or the handoff map as a row-owner.
- No October work (the start slot in §8) is assigned to a contractor. The start slot remains contingent on §3 and §4 closing favorably AND a final selection by Priya.
- No reference checks, background checks, or contract-vehicle work creates an expectation of hire; those workstreams remain neutral until selection.
- The week-6 lane check (E5), the post-start 30/60/90 cadence (§9), and the read-only access scope memo all become meaningful only after a contractor starts — none of them authorize a contractor in advance.

The pre-requisition observation in §3 and §4 continues to run on the standing lanes only. Lane protection (§2) is unchanged: Owen = reporting semantics + analytical conclusions; Ines = message-state governance with `routine education` HIGHER-RISK, boundary = Riley; Riley = exception + disputed semantics + cross-surface + exec language; Daniela = engineering release + rollback. The contractor — if and when hired — sits below these lanes, never above or alongside them. Selection remains open; A and C are the finalists advancing into the interview stations in §8; B does not advance.

**Update 2025-09-12 (Finalist interview evidence + reference-check priority):** Sept 12 interview cycle closed for both finalists (A and C). Finalist evidence from the Sept 12 stations (Lifecycle Systems runbook walk-through, Ines state-meaning scenario, Owen reporting-semantics scenario, disputed-edge scenario to Riley, Daniela scope-of-release scenario) plus the carried-forward probes (A's tooling-adaptation, C's denominator-and-rework) is in. Reference-check priority is set on an evidence basis — A first, C second — because A's gating probe cleared on self-description (not observed behavior) and A's boundary-discipline claim needs validation against prior owner-lane / approval-gate structures; C's gating probe cleared on directly observable behavior so reference value-add on the gating surface is lower. Both finalists still clear the 2-approved-references standard; the ranking is sequencing, not preference. Selection still open; no final contractor selected.

**Update 2025-09-18 (Priya's preferred-candidate selection — Candidate A; Candidate C remains alternate):** Priya reviewed the complete finalist evidence on Sept 18 — Sept 12 interview transcripts, Sept 13–Sept 17 reference-check returns on Candidate A (run first per the 2025-09-12 evidence-based sequencing), and the reference-check returns on Candidate C — and selected Candidate A as Helio's preferred Lifecycle Systems operations-contractor candidate for the $36,000 half-time engagement originally targeting Oct 1, 2025. Candidate C remains the alternate. Selection rationale rests on three pillars: (1) audit traceability — A's evidence-packaging background plus the sample-export work in the Sept 12 interview (duplicate inventory row caught before narrative built; evidence kept separate from owner approval on the spot) maps 1:1 onto the §5 eligible-work list and the §4c rework-tracking metric, and references validated the posture across prior engagements; (2) demonstrated tooling-learning ability — the tooling-adaptation probe cleared in self-description at the Sept 12 interview, and references validated the description against prior ramp history (prior Customer.io-style ramps stayed in prep/reconciliation, supervised/unsupervised split clean, no drift vector against the §7 evidence-led-not-systems-led posture); (3) consistent respect for the preparation-only authority boundary — across first-round, the Sept 12 interview stations, and the reference-check returns, A deferred on every state-meaning call, every analytical conclusion, every disputed-edge call, and every release/rollback reference. The 2025-08-05 midyear reaffirmation on the higher-risk `routine education` lane was the explicit boundary A was tested against; A's posture stayed inside that line without exception. C was a credible runner-up on documentation and on the directly-observable denominator-and-rework probe, but C's tooling-fluency gap and the smaller reference-check validation surface on C's gating probe kept C as the alternate rather than the preferred candidate.

**Status as of the close of the 2025-09-18 review — six gates that remain open between preferred-candidate status and a contractor touching Lifecycle Systems work, each NOT-satisfied today:**

1. **Acceptance.** Candidate A has NOT accepted. No offer has been extended. A has not been informed of the selection and has not responded to anything.
2. **Remaining checks.** Candidate A has NOT passed all remaining checks. Reference-check returns are in hand and read, but the §3 30-day baseline (campaign inventory, recurring audit calendar, owner-approved handoff map) and the §4 60-day trend are still being assembled on the standing lanes and have not been read by Finance; Daniela's no-production-access setup documentation has been delivered alongside §3c but has not been signed off by all named lane owners; the read-only access scope memo (Daniela + Ines) is not finalized; background-check and contract-vehicle workstreams remain open.
3. **Hire.** Candidate A has NOT been hired. No offer letter has been issued. No contract vehicle (1099 vs. PEO vs. agency-of-record) has been selected. No cost-center or accrual coding has been assigned to the $36,000.
4. **Access.** Candidate A has NOT received access. No contractor account exists on Lifecycle Systems surfaces or any adjacent surface (audit log, runbook repo, ticket queue, message-send tooling). No read-only role has been provisioned. No credential has been issued.
5. **Onboarding.** Candidate A has NOT begun onboarding. No runbook tour, no supervised-shadow slot, no onboarding prep activated for A specifically.
6. **October work.** Candidate A has NOT received October work. No work item, campaign, audit log, runbook section, ticket-queue lane, message-send template, or cohort has been assigned to A. The Oct start slot remains contingent on §3 and §4 closing favorably AND a final selection by Priya AND A's acceptance AND the remaining checks clearing AND the contract vehicle settling AND access being provisioned.

Lane protection (§2) and the categorical exclusions (§6) are explicitly unchanged by the Sept 18 selection.

**Update 2025-09-23 (Target start date shift — Oct 1 → Oct 6):** Procurement relayed on Sept 23 that Candidate A remains interested in the half-time Lifecycle Systems operations-contractor role, but **Oct 6, 2025 is the earliest possible start date rather than Oct 1, 2025** — a five-business-day shift inside the role's onboarding window. The revised date is acceptable from the Helio side and is workable because this role adds **preparation capacity** to the standing lanes, not production coverage: the eligible work in §5 (campaign inventory, recurring audit calendar upkeep, audit-log reconciliation diffs, runbook hygiene, ticket-queue triage, pre-flight checks) is preparation and evidence work, not live-operations coverage. A five-day shift therefore does not compress any standing-lane deliverable, does not shorten any sign-off window, and does not require any lane owner to re-cut the §3a/§3b/§3c 30-day baseline artifacts (Owen's Sept 17 §3a, Ines's Sept 18 §3b/§3c, Daniela's no-production-access setup documentation) or the §4 60-day trend observation. The shift leaves the §3 and §4 Finance pre-requisition observation windows unchanged — the 30-day baseline still runs on the standing lanes only, with no contractor on payroll — and leaves the post-start 30/60/90 review cadence anchored to contractor start (now Oct 6 rather than Oct 1). The Sept 23–Sept 30 onboarding prep window in §8 shifts to Sept 30–Oct 5; read-only access provisioning (if and when the gates in §1 clear) shifts into that window with the same sequencing (Daniela + Ines read-only access scope memo first; supervised-shadow slot at the end; no live operations authority until start day). Readiness-inputs owners and dates (Owen §3a by Sept 17; Ines §3b/§3c by Sept 18; Daniela no-production-access setup documentation) are unchanged. The post-start review dates in §9 shift to Nov 6 (30-day), Dec 6 (60-day), and Jan 6 (90-day).

**Status as of 2025-09-23 — the six gates from the 2025-09-18 update are all still open and are explicitly re-stated here against the revised start date so they don't quietly close:**

1. **Acceptance.** Candidate A has NOT accepted. The revised Oct 6 start date is acceptable on the Helio side; Procurement owns the contact-with-candidate step from here. Riley will not contact Candidate A directly.
2. **Remaining checks.** Candidate A has NOT passed all remaining checks. Same gate list as Sept 18 — reference-check returns in hand and read; §3 30-day baseline and §4 60-day trend still being assembled on the standing lanes; read-only access scope memo not finalized; background-check and contract-vehicle workstreams remain open.
3. **Hire.** Candidate A has NOT been hired. No offer letter has been issued on either Oct 1 or Oct 6 timing. No contract vehicle selected. No cost-center or accrual coding assigned.
4. **Access.** Candidate A has NOT received access. No contractor account on Lifecycle Systems surfaces or any adjacent surface. No read-only role provisioned. No credential issued. The Oct 6 start date does not authorize access in advance; access provisioning remains gated on hire.
5. **Onboarding.** Candidate A has NOT begun onboarding. No runbook tour, no supervised-shadow slot, no onboarding prep activated for A specifically.
6. **October work.** Candidate A has NOT received October work. No work item, campaign, audit log, runbook section, ticket-queue lane, message-send template, or cohort has been assigned to A. The Oct 6 start slot remains contingent on all of the above clearing. The five-day shift does not authorize October work in advance.

Lane protection (§2), the §3/§4 Finance pre-requisition observation framework, the §5 eligible-work list, the §6 eleven categorical exclusions, and the §7 evidence limits are all unchanged by the date shift. The selection gate (Priya's final say, with Riley drafting the recommendation) is unchanged. The candidate remains the preferred candidate, not the hired contractor.

## 2. Scope guardrails (protected lanes — do not cross)

Lane ownership is preserved exactly as the standing audit (Priya 2025-03-24, reaffirmed 2025-08-05) sets it. The contractor sits BELOW these lanes; the lanes do not move. The pre-requisition observation in §3 and §4 is run by the lane owners themselves, not by any external party.

- Owen — Lifecycle Systems reporting semantics + analytical conclusions + exception readouts + Helio Start report.
- Ines — message-state governance (the 5-state guide, Q3 #2, OK'd 2025-07-25, holds); `routine education` remains HIGHER-RISK with Riley as boundary.
- Riley — exception escalation + disputed semantics + cross-surface calls + exec language.
- Daniela — engineering release control + rollback authority. Unchanged.

The pre-requisition observation does NOT shift any of these to anyone else, contractor or otherwise. After observation closes, the contractor absorbs the eligible repeatable operations work in §5; semantic decisions, governance calls, exception calls, and engineering controls stay where they are.

## 3. First 30 days — establish the baseline (Finance gate 1)

The first 30 days run on the standing lanes only, with the lane owners themselves doing the work. The goal is to produce a complete, observable starting state. Three artifacts are required at the end of 30 days:

- **3a. Complete campaign inventory.** Every active Lifecycle Systems campaign across every surface, with: surface, owner, state-meaning implications (yes/no per the 5-state guide), cadence, current volume, and the lane owner responsible for review. The inventory is complete when Owen signs off on reporting shape and Ines signs off on state-meaning classification. **Per the 2025-09-10 planning check, Owen owns the campaign-inventory inputs and delivers the §3a upstream pull by 2025-09-17; the §3a completion sign-off (Owen + Ines) follows from that input.**
- **3b. Recurring audit calendar.** A published calendar that shows when each recurring audit/review cycle runs, who attends, and what evidence each cycle is supposed to produce. The calendar is in place when the four lane owners (Owen, Ines, Riley, Daniela) have each signed their own lane and the calendar is durable enough to repeat without ad-hoc rescheduling. **Per the 2025-09-10 planning check, Ines owns the recurring-audit-calendar inputs and delivers the §3b upstream draft by 2025-09-18; the four-lane sign-off follows from that draft.**
- **3c. Owner-approved handoff map.** For each task class assigned to the contractor in §5, a one-line map showing (i) which standing lane owns the task today, (ii) which lane reviews the contractor's output, and (iii) what triggers an immediate hand-back to the lane owner. The map is approved when each named lane owner signs the row(s) that touch their lane. **Per the 2025-09-10 planning check, Ines owns the handoff-map inputs and delivers the §3c upstream draft by 2025-09-18; the per-lane sign-off follows. Separately, Daniela documents the contractor's no-production-access setup (the §3c engineering row — onboarding is read-only/non-production; release, deploy, and rollback authority stay with Daniela); engineering release control is unchanged.**

This 30-day window is a baseline, not a pilot. No contractor is hired. No work is delegated. **Onboarding materials (runbook tour draft, supervised-shadow plan, read-only access scope memo, evaluation rubric) may be prepared during this window — preparing materials is permitted and does not authorize any contractor. No individual contractor access, authority, or October work assignment is approved before a contractor is selected and hired.** The artifact is the observable starting state against which any future contractor contribution is measured.

## 4. First 60 days — test the trend (Finance gate 2)

The first 60 days continue to run on the standing lanes only, and add four tracked metrics to the 30-day baseline. No efficiency target is set in advance (see §7 — evidence limits).

- **4a. Repeatable preparation hours (test).** Are the hours the lane owners spend on the eligible repeatable operations work in §5 falling, holding, or rising? Direction is observed, not prescribed. A fall is a signal, not a success criterion by itself.
- **4b. Review burden (track).** Are the hours lane owners spend reviewing their own outputs, peer outputs, and exception readouts stable, rising, or shifting? Reviewed as separate from preparation hours, not bundled.
- **4c. Rework (track).** How often is a Lifecycle Systems output re-opened or corrected, and on what trigger? Tracked per surface.
- **4d. Cycle time (track).** End-to-end time from campaign event to evidence-packaged readout, by surface. Tracked, not optimized in the window.
- **4e. Boundary integrity (track).** Are the protected lanes in §2 staying clean? Specifically: any state-meaning change attempted outside Ines? Any disputed-semantics call attempted outside Riley? Any analytical conclusion issued outside Owen? Any release/rollback attempted outside Daniela? Any substitution of the standing lane owners by anyone else? Each "yes" is a boundary incident and is logged, regardless of intent.

The 60-day trend is read alongside the 30-day baseline. No single metric decides the requisition; the read is whether the baseline held and the trend in 4a–4e is interpretable.

## 5. Eligible repeatable operations work (post-hire scope; not active yet)

These are the task classes the contractor will absorb IF the requisition advances after §3 and §4 close. Until then, the lane owners do this work themselves and the standing cadence is the only cadence.

Contractor-owned (subject to Ines/Riley sign-off per item type):

- Routine cohort ingestion hygiene — pulling, deduplicating, and staging cohort data for Owen's readouts.
- Drafting neutral message copy templates for non-state-meaning surfaces (transactional notifications, renewal reminders) — Ines retains approval on state-meaning copy.
- Pre-flight checks on outbound message sends (template ID, cohort lock, suppression list sanity) — does NOT include approval to release.
- Documentation upkeep for the Lifecycle Systems runbook (non-semantic sections).
- Audit log reconciliation — pulling daily diffs and flagging anomalies to Owen for analytical interpretation.
- Routine backlog hygiene on the Lifecycle Systems ticket queue — triage, label, route. Routing decisions stay with the relevant lane owner.

## 6. Categorical exclusions (contractor does NOT do)

- Message-state governance, including the 5 states (ext-sys authority, connector auth, entitlement, qualifying-human-admin, active CS adoption/renewal) — Ines only.
- Disputed semantics — Riley only.
- Exception escalation calls — Riley only.
- Any statement that reads as analytical conclusion or changes reporting semantics — Owen only.
- Any release, deploy, or rollback on Lifecycle Systems surfaces — Daniela only.
- `routine education` content decisions (HIGHER-RISK; boundary = Riley).
- Engineering change requests or scope-of-work determinations for Lifecycle Systems.
- Final say on anything customer-facing that is non-transactional.

## 7. Evidence limits — what this brief does and does not promise

This is explicit so Finance, Priya, and the lane owners read the same thing.

- **No specific efficiency result is promised before anyone is hired.** §4 tracks whether repeatable preparation hours fall, but does not commit to a number, a percent, or a target. A fall is observed, not bought.
- **No promise that review burden will fall.** Review burden is tracked, not assumed to fall. If review burden rises while preparation hours fall, that is a real signal and the brief does not pre-decide whether it is acceptable.
- **No promise that rework will fall.** Rework is tracked. The 60-day read may show rework flat or rising; that is information, not failure.
- **No promise that cycle time will compress.** Cycle time is observed. The brief does not set a cycle-time target before observation closes.
- **No shifting of semantics, governance, exception decisions, or engineering controls to the contractor.** The pre-requisition observation in §3 and §4 runs entirely on the standing lanes. The contractor — if hired — sits below the four named lanes (§2). The contractor does not own state-meaning, disputed semantics, exception calls, analytical conclusions, releases, or rollbacks at any point.
- **No addition of a fifth consumer.** The contractor is not the fifth consumer of Lifecycle Systems. The lane owners and the four standing lanes remain the system.
- **No contractor access, authority, or October work assignment is approved before a contractor is selected and hired.** Per the 2025-09-10 planning check (see §1), onboarding materials may be prepared during the pre-requisition observation window, but no individual contractor account, role, calendar slot, or work assignment is approved in advance of selection. The Oct start slot in §8 remains contingent on §3 and §4 closing favorably AND a final selection by Priya. **Per the 2025-09-23 update, the start slot is Oct 6, 2025; the five-day shift does not authorize any contractor in advance of the remaining gates closing.**
- **Selection remains open.** No individual contractor is selected. Per the 2025-09-08 disposition in §1, A and C advance from the first-round screen and B does not; final interviews, references, selection, and onboarding remain pending. Per the 2025-09-10 planning check, A and C are the only finalists and selection remains open. Per the 2025-09-12 evidence read and reference-check priority, A and C remain the finalists. Per the 2025-09-18 preferred-candidate selection, A is the preferred candidate and C remains the alternate; preferred-candidate status does not waive any remaining check, does not authorize access, does not begin onboarding, does not assign October work, and does not create an expectation of hire. The Sept 5–Sept 22 sourcing and interview window in §8 is contingent on §3 and §4 closing favorably; it does not run on a fixed clock ahead of the observation. The Oct 6 start slot does not waive any of the six §1 gates.
- **Pre-requisition observation ≠ post-start review.** The 30-day and 60-day windows in §3 and §4 are pre-requisition, no-contractor observations. The 30/60/90 *post-start* cadence in §9 only becomes meaningful after a contractor actually starts.

## 8. September readiness sequence (contingent on §3 and §4 closing)

- Sept 1 — Brief published; lane owners confirm boundary read-back. Priya signs off.
- Sept 3 — Candidate evaluation rubric drafted by Riley; circulated to Owen + Ines for input on boundary tests (does this task cross their lane?). 2 approved references standard preserved.
- Sept 5–Sept 12 — Candidate sourcing window open. Review-closure authority unchanged from standing practice. (Only opens if Finance has cleared §3.)
- Sept 10 — Q4 Lifecycle Systems planning check held (Priya, Riley, Owen, Ines, Daniela). Readiness-inputs split confirmed: Owen (campaign inventory) by Sept 17; Ines (recurring audit calendar + handoff map) by Sept 18; Daniela (no-production-access setup documentation). Finalists reduced to A and C; selection remains open; onboarding materials may be prepared but no individual contractor access, authority, or October work assignment is approved before a contractor is selected and hired.
- Sept 12–Sept 22 — Interview cycle. Required stations: (a) Lifecycle Systems runbook walk-through, (b) Ines state-meaning scenario (must defer on state-meaning calls), (c) Owen reporting-semantics scenario (must defer on analytical conclusions), (d) disputed-edge scenario handed to Riley, (e) Daniela scope-of-release scenario (must defer on any release/rollback call). **Per the 2025-09-08 disposition, A's tooling-adaptation probe and C's denominator-and-rework probe (both carried forward from the first-round screen, see §1) are added into these interview stations as the gating probes for those two candidates.** B is not interviewed.
- Sept 17 — Owen delivers §3a campaign-inventory inputs (readiness gate per Sept 10 planning check).
- Sept 18 — Ines delivers §3b recurring-audit-calendar inputs and §3c handoff-map inputs (readiness gate per Sept 10 planning check). Daniela's no-production-access setup documentation is in place alongside the §3c engineering row.
- Sept 22 — Selection decision: Riley proposes, Priya confirms. Final say sits with Priya. (Only runs if Finance has cleared §4 and a contractor has been selected from the A/C finalist set.)
- **Sept 30–Oct 5 — Onboarding prep window (only if a contractor has been selected and hired):** read-only access to Lifecycle Systems surfaces, runbook tour, supervised shadow on one routine cycle. No live operations authority until Oct 6. Per §1 and §7, none of this onboarding prep is approved in advance of selection; the prep work itself may be drafted during the pre-requisition window, but no contractor account is created and no live authority transfers until after selection and hire. **Per the 2025-09-23 update, the start slot shifts from Oct 1 to Oct 6, and this prep window shifts from Sept 23–Sept 30 to Sept 30–Oct 5 accordingly. The five-day shift does not authorize any contractor in advance.**
- **Oct 6, 2025 — Contractor start; first post-start 30-day review calendared. (Only if selection cleared and contract vehicle is settled.) Per the 2025-09-23 update, the target start date is Oct 6 rather than Oct 1; the five-day shift is workable because this role adds preparation capacity rather than production coverage. The shift does not waive any of the six §1 gates: acceptance, remaining checks, hire, access, onboarding, October work.**

## 9. Procurement + interview milestones

Pre-requisition observation:
- 30-day gate (§3): complete campaign inventory + recurring audit calendar + owner-approved handoff map. Finance reads and clears.
- 60-day gate (§4): trend in 4a–4e, evidence read against §7. Finance reads and clears.

Post-hire cadence (only after a contractor starts):

- Sept 8 — Priya review of first-round candidate assessment: A and C advance, B does not. Final contractor still unselected; final interviews, references, selection, and onboarding remain pending. A's tooling-adaptation probe and C's denominator-and-rework probe carried forward into the §8 interview cycle.
- **Sept 10 — Q4 Lifecycle Systems planning check (Priya, Riley, Owen, Ines, Daniela). A and C confirmed as the only finalists; selection remains open. Readiness-inputs assignments logged: Owen (campaign inventory) by Sept 17; Ines (recurring audit calendar + handoff map) by Sept 18; Daniela (no-production-access setup documentation). Onboarding materials may be prepared during the pre-requisition observation window; no individual contractor access, authority, or October work assignment is approved before a contractor is selected and hired.**
- **Sept 17 — Owen delivers §3a campaign-inventory inputs.**
- **Sept 18 — Ines delivers §3b recurring-audit-calendar inputs and §3c handoff-map inputs; Daniela's no-production-access setup documentation is in place.**
- Sept 12 — Interview cycle closes for finalists A and C; finalist evidence in. Reference-check priority set on an evidence basis — A first, C second. Selection still open.
- Sept 13–Sept 22 — Reference-check window. A's references run first per the 2025-09-12 evidence-based sequencing; C's references run second. Selection still open.
- Sept 18 — Priya's preferred-candidate selection: Candidate A preferred, Candidate C alternate. Six §1 gates (acceptance, remaining checks, hire, access, onboarding, October work) all still open. Hand-off to Procurement for the offer process opens.
- **Sept 23 — Procurement relays that Candidate A's earliest possible start is Oct 6 rather than Oct 1. Helio-side revised date accepted; workable because the role adds preparation capacity, not production coverage. The six §1 gates are re-stated against the revised date; all six still open.**
- Sept 1 — Brief finalized; lane-owner read-back complete.
- Sept 5 — Candidate sourcing opens (contingent).
- Sept 12 — Sourcing closes; longlist set (contingent).

## 10. Open items

Default: Owen (campaign inventory, reporting shape), Ines (state-meaning classification), with Riley on the handoff map and Daniela on read-only access scope. **Per the 2025-09-10 planning check: Owen delivers the §3a campaign-inventory inputs by 2025-09-17; Ines delivers the §3b recurring-audit-calendar inputs and the §3c handoff-map inputs by 2025-09-18; Daniela documents the contractor's no-production-access setup as the §3c engineering row. - Contract vehicle (1099 vs. PEO vs. agency-of-record) — Priya to confirm by Sept 5; affects onboarding prep timeline. (Does not move forward until §3 and §4 close and a contractor is selected.) **Per the 2025-09-23 date shift, the contract vehicle still does not need to settle until selection; the five-day shift does not change that gate.**
- Background-check + reference-check vendor selection — Priya. **No reference or background check creates an expectation of hire; checks remain neutral until selection.** Reference-check returns for A (run first per 2025-09-12 sequencing) and C are in hand as of the 2025-09-18 preferred-candidate selection; further checks (e.g., background-check completion) remain open.
- Read-only access scope on Lifecycle Systems — Daniela + Ines to confirm by Sept 8; engineering release control not affected. **Per the 2025-09-10 planning check, Daniela's no-production-access setup documentation is the engineering-side confirmation of the read-only scope and is delivered alongside §3c. Per the 2025-09-23 date shift, the read-only access scope memo still gates access provisioning — the five-day shift does not authorize provisioning in advance of selection.**
- Cost-center + accrual coding for $36,000 — Finance; needed before Oct 6 invoice (per the 2025-09-23 date shift; previously Oct 1).
- Q3 meeting-cadence interaction — contractor is silent on disputed/cross-surface items; standing-lane ≤3 neutral/wk stays as-is.

- Evidence-read attendees at the §3 and §4 gates — Riley to confirm with Priya who joins the read (suggested: Finance + Priya + Riley; Owen and Ines on call for lane-specific questions).

Per the 2025-09-08 disposition (§1) and the 2025-09-10 planning check (§1), A and C are the finalists advancing out of the first-round screen; final interviews, reference checks, selection, and onboarding remain to be run. Per the 2025-09-23 date shift, the target start shifts from Oct 1 to Oct 6; the six §1 gates are re-stated against the revised date and remain open. Riley drafts the recommendation, Priya confirms. No pre-decision.**

No individual contractor account, access scope, calendar slot, or October work assignment is approved before a contractor is selected and hired. Per the 2025-09-23 date shift, the prep window shifts from Sept 23–Sept 30 to Sept 30–Oct 5; the same authorization gate applies — drafts OK, account creation and authority transfer not.**

Lane protection (§2), the §3/§4 Finance pre-requisition observation framework, the §5 eligible-work list, the §6 eleven categorical exclusions, and the §7 evidence limits are unchanged by the shift. The post-start 30/60/90 review dates shift to Nov 6 / Dec 6 / Jan 6. Readiness-inputs owners and dates (Owen §3a by Sept 17; Ines §3b/§3c by Sept 18; Daniela no-production-access setup documentation) are unchanged.**

## 11. Summary (1-liner)

$36k half-time Lifecycle Systems operations contractor, **Oct 6, 2025 start** (per the 2025-09-23 update; previously Oct 1); pre-requisition Finance observation (30-day baseline + 60-day trend) runs on standing lanes only with no contractor on payroll; eligible repeatable ops work absorbed post-hire only; protected lanes unchanged; selection opens only if §3 and §4 clear; no specific efficiency result promised before anyone is hired. **As of 2025-09-08: first-round candidate screen closed with A and C advancing and B held; final contractor unselected, final interviews/references/selection/onboarding pending; tooling-adaptation probe (A) and denominator-and-rework probe (C) carried forward into the interview cycle. As of 2025-09-23: target start shifts from Oct 1 to Oct 6 per Procurement's relay on Candidate A's earliest availability; five-day shift is workable because the role adds preparation capacity rather than production coverage; the six §1 gates are re-stated against the revised date and remain open; lane protection, eligible work, categorical exclusions, evidence limits, and the §3a/§3b/§3c readiness dates are unchanged; the post-start 30/60/90 review dates shift to Nov 6 / Dec 6 / Jan 6; preferred-candidate status does not waive any remaining check, does not authorize access, does not begin onboarding, does not assign October work, and does not create an expectation of hire.**

arguments.body:

input.body:
Historical decision rule: how evidence about onboarding timing (#3) would affect the priority of the Customer Success coverage hypothesis (#4)

Source: churn-investigation Notion doc, hypothesis section. Set 2023-02-08; reaffirmed after Priya 1:1 on 2023-02-10 ("cuts clean"); locked as written into the Notion doc on 2023-02-12 to stop re-litigating the sequencing.

The four-bucket hypothesis list (set 2023-02-08):
  #1 pricing artifact — packaging / discounting / contract-mix weirdness; we created the spike
  #2 competitor cycle — someone ran a play at the mid-seg base
  #3 onboarding timing — late-Dec / early-Jan starts maturing into churn on a lag
  #4 CS coverage gap — CSM load drift, pure coverage math

Original sequencing (2023-02-08): #1 first because it is the fastest to kill; then lean #3 or #4 before #2. Marcus Vail's pricing-page experiment is explicitly held out of this thread as a separate question — it is not #1 even though both are pricing-adjacent, to keep the read clean.

Decision rule (2023-02-10, after Priya 1:1; carried verbatim into the Feb 12 Notion lock):
  "#4 CS coverage gap — drops if #3 confirms."

Plain reading:
  - #3 and #4 are framed as a conditional pair. If evidence on #3 confirms the onboarding-timing mechanism, the #4 CS-coverage hypothesis is dropped from the active read.
  - The direction is asymmetric: confirmation of #3 retires #4. The reverse — confirmation of #4 — does not, on the face of the recorded rule, retire #3; #3's lag-window observation runs independently until ~Feb 28 when the baseline settles.
  - #2 competitor cycle is sequenced after both #3 and #4 for the same reason — neither pricing-adjacent nor coverage-mechanic, so it stays at the back until the front-bucket pair is resolved.

Operational definition of "confirms" — NOT documented in the recorded rule. The Feb 10 entry is one line ("drops if #3 confirms") and the Feb 12 lock preserved that wording. The rule as written does not specify:
  - what evidence threshold counts as confirmation (effect size, cohort scope, time window)
  - whether partial confirmation down-weights #4 vs. retiring it
  - what the read at the ~Feb 28 baseline-settles milestone is supposed to look like to trigger the drop
  - whether a non-confirming #3 read would *strengthen* #4 by default or just leave it open
  This is an open definition, not a missing decision. Anyone applying the rule should treat "confirms" as needing an operational definition before the Feb 28 read, and should not assume the Feb 10 wording implies one.

Scope guardrails preserved across the Feb 8 / Feb 10 / Feb 12 record:
  - Marcus Vail's pricing-page experiment stays siloed (separate question from #1, not packaging / discounting / contract-mix weirdness); bridged as a separate brief when the churn read is ready. Pricing-page contamination risk is flagged in the readout if the test ships inside the Feb 15 → Feb 28 hypothesis window.
  - Owen rechecked the cohort cut on Feb 9 — confirmed not a definition bug.
  - Churn read targets the 50–200 seat mid-seg cut; headline number is 5.1% monthly vs. 2.1% trailing six.
  - Riley refers to the four buckets by number; sequencing is locked; re-litigating the order is not the use of this rule.

Status as of the Feb 12 Notion lock: rule is in force. The Feb 28 baseline-settles milestone has not yet been recorded as closed in this set of session history.

input.body:
HISTORICAL SETUP — describes the test plan as designed before the ruling. Not a current conclusion; do not cite as evidence.

Scope
- Channel: #growth-investigations
- Workstream: churn / cohort
- Owner of pre-ruling design: Riley; cohort cuts w/ Owen (mid-segment, read locks first)
- Sequencing note: held off running while activation/retention + lifecycle email were live, per sum-first sequencing rule

Hypothesis (H2)
- Among users entering the paid-source eligibility flow (entry = step 19), downstream churn is driven primarily by the post-flow outcome (admit vs. assist vs. ineligible), not by the paid-source `conversions` label itself.
- Null: outcome mix is independent of paid-source label; admit/assist/ineligible rates ~ equal across `conversions` cohorts.
- Source label rule (locked 11/9): `conversions` = paid-platform source label; 19 = paid-source eligibility-flow start. Admit 8 / assist 6 / ineligible 5 tracked as separate outcome states, NOT collapsed into admissions or activations.

Cohort & cuts
- Population: paid-source entrants, eligibility-flow step 19 reached in the analysis window
- Primary cut: outcome state (admit / assist / ineligible)
- Secondary cut: paid-source label (`conversions`)
- Exclusions: organic-source users; users who exited the flow before step 19

Metric
- Primary: 30-day churn rate by outcome state, stratified by `conversions` label
- Secondary: time-to-churn from step 19; outcome-mix shift between source labels

Guardrails
- Min cell size per source-label × outcome cell before reporting
- Do not re-classify any admit/assist/ineligible as admission or activation
- Read locks held until cohort cuts signed off (Owen, mid-segment)

Design
- Descriptive + stratified comparison; no causal claim pre-ruling
- Pre-registered reads: outcome-state distribution by `conversions`; 30-day churn by cell
- Decision rule (pre-ruling): if outcome-state mix differs materially across `conversions` labels, H2 supported and follow-up causal design queued; if not, H2 rejected and label treated as neutral.

Status
- Superseded by the 11/9 ruling on `conversions` / 19 / admit-assist-ineligible definitions
- Filed for archive only — do not use as the basis for any current call.

HISTORICAL SETUP — describes the test plan as designed before the ruling. Not a current conclusion; do not cite as evidence.

Scope
- Channel: #growth-investigations
- Workstream: churn / cohort
- Owner of pre-ruling design: Riley; cohort cuts w/ Owen (mid-segment, read locks first)
- Sequencing note: held off running while activation/retention + lifecycle email were live, per sum-first sequencing rule

Hypothesis (H2)
- Among users entering the paid-source eligibility flow (entry = step 19), downstream churn is driven primarily by the post-flow outcome (admit vs. assist vs. ineligible), not by the paid-source `conversions` label itself.
- Null: outcome mix is independent of paid-source label; admit/assist/ineligible rates ~ equal across `conversions` cohorts.
- Source label rule (locked 11/9): `conversions` = paid-platform source label; 19 = paid-source eligibility-flow start. Admit 8 / assist 6 / ineligible 5 tracked as separate outcome states, NOT collapsed into admissions or activations.

Cohort & cuts
- Population: paid-source entrants, eligibility-flow step 19 reached in the analysis window
- Primary cut: outcome state (admit / assist / ineligible)
- Secondary cut: paid-source label (`conversions`)
- Exclusions: organic-source users; users who exited the flow before step 19

Metric
- Primary: 30-day churn rate by outcome state, stratified by `conversions` label
- Secondary: time-to-churn from step 19; outcome-mix shift between source labels

Guardrails
- Min cell size per source-label × outcome cell before reporting
- Do not re-classify any admit/assist/ineligible as admission or activation
- Read locks held until cohort cuts signed off (Owen, mid-segment)

Design
- Descriptive + stratified comparison; no causal claim pre-ruling
- Pre-registered reads: outcome-state distribution by `conversions`; 30-day churn by cell
- Decision rule (pre-ruling): if outcome-state mix differs materially across `conversions` labels, H2 supported and follow-up causal design queued; if not, H2 rejected and label treated as neutral.

Status
- Superseded by the 11/9 ruling on `conversions` / 19 / admit-assist-ineligible definitions
- Filed for archive only — do not use as the basis for any current call.

operations.content: Within-arm observation ≠ arm. For EXP-2023-05-expansion-nudge / `expansion_nudge_60d_v1`, depth split (high vs low active-admin) is a within-treatment observation on a 25% rollout, not a pre-stratified arm — so 'active-admin moved' could be selection, not treatment. Treating it as a renewal signal inverts the 2023-06-22 ruling. Minimum before CS acts: (1) pre-reg depth stratum definition + cutpoint, (2) stratified effect-size + p + CI per stratum, (3) treatment/control balance check on depth, (4) regression with depth×treatment interaction, (5) standing p<0.01 2nd-look bar (2023-03-26 rule). If interaction not significant or balance broken, do not promote to CS.

arguments.body:
# Q1 2027 Lifecycle Systems operating priorities — staff-review draft

Author: Riley Tanaka
For: December 18 staff review (owner-lane input)
Status: DRAFT. Restates the December 4, 2026 decision already approved by Priya (Lifecycle Systems operating model, effective January 5, 2027). It is a Q1 restatement for staff review, not a new authority decision. Nothing in this draft takes effect early. Anything that conflicts with the Dec 4 decision record is overridden by that record; this draft surfaces the Q1 shape, not a re-decision.

---

## Summary (one page)

What changes on January 5, 2027 — and what does not:
- On January 5, Riley stops attending routine monthly Lifecycle Systems preparation and source-closure reviews. Through January 4, nothing changes — Riley continues current routine preparation and source-closure attendance as today.
- The four evidence lanes stay separate. No combined growth number. No cross-lane revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast credit.
- Owner lanes are unchanged. What changes is who carries the routine cadence and what Riley attends.
- The quarterly rotating recheck of one evidence lane is the concrete independent verification activity replacing prior hands-on attendance. It does not reopen source closure, approve any other lane owner's certification, or exercise any engineering control. It is an inspection, not a second approval queue.
- Future paid Helio Start is a separate question. Nothing in this draft approves traffic, budget, or scope for paid Helio Start.

## Q1 priorities — by lane (unchanged)

The four lanes are the established board-evidence lanes. They are kept separate. They are read independently. None of them is a revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast input.

- Helio Start. Lane owner: Owen (measurement) + Riley (final claims). Status through Q1: bounded-organic as it already is. Reporting inside the existing four-lane scope. Five-state model unchanged (admitted / assisted / ineligible / final-reconciliation + `pending` forward-only). `pending` stays pre-admission, NOT in the rate or activation denominator, intake additive. No Q1 launch, beta, pricing-page approval, or new consumer.
- Expansion Assist (retained-mid). Lane owner: Owen (eligibility cuts) + Ines (lifecycle governance) + Riley (final claims). Descriptive only. Causal language (drove / caused / prevented) deferred to a controlled read-out. No forecast or rollout.
- Pricing-page path quality. Lane owner: Owen (measurement) + Daniela (transport + rollout) + Riley (final claims). Lane supports only "fewer unsupported-path starts" — funnel-quality evidence, not revenue, paid-acquisition, pipeline, forecast, or eligibility.
- CS auto-nudge / system controls. Lane owner: Owen (reporting + exception explanation) + Ines (messaging-state governance) + Daniela (transport + source reliability + rollback). Lane is system-control performance, not a customer-behavior read.

## The four production consumers and their current field meanings

The four board-evidence lanes are the four production consumers of the operating state. Each lane carries the same seven required fields; "current field meanings" are what each field has meant in the deck-format operating evidence since FY26.

The seven required fields per lane (current meanings):
1. Denominator or coverage dates. What population and time window the lane covers. Read as the count plus the window, not the count alone.
2. Outcome window. The complete predeclared window the source supports. Read only inside the window; not truncated, not extended.
3. Measurement limits. What the source can and cannot say. Stated explicitly. Limits are part of the claim, not a footnote.
4. Exclusions. What is excluded from the lane's read and why. Documented. Consistent with how routine claims treat them.
5. Source owner. The named owner who certifies the lane's source completeness.
6. Reliability evidence. The evidence the source is intact (Daniela's lane inspects this; the recheck inspects it; engineering release controls stay with Daniela).
7. Revenue and forecast treatment. How the lane treats revenue and forecast. Descriptive lanes name it as descriptive. Causal/revenue/forecast decision rights are Riley's; the field records the treatment, not the decision.

These seven fields are what each lane carries today. The Jan 5 model preserves them; it changes who closes them.

## Current through January 4, 2027 — explicit

- Riley attends routine monthly Lifecycle Systems preparation and routine source-closure reviews as today.
- The four-lane cadence runs exactly as it does today. No new owner, no new role, no new authority.
- Nothing about the Dec 4 decision is in effect. It is approved; it is not yet effective.

## Effective January 5, 2027 — first January cycle

The first cycle under the new model opens Tuesday, January 5, 2027. (January 4 is a Monday and the last day of the prior routine; January 5 is the first effective day.) The cadence is unchanged in form; what changes is who carries it and how incomplete status is handled.

Cadence (effective January 5, 2027):
- Second business day. Owen's monthly sanitized campaign snapshot is due. Hard date against the calendar, not against completion of any other step.
- Fourth business day. Ines's lifecycle-governance and owner-state certification is due. Daniela's source-reliability and release certification is due.
- Fifth business day. Owen must either close the routine four-lane source review OR explicitly leave it incomplete. Either way, Owen sends one closure-and-exception summary — not informal follow-up fragments.

Incomplete handling (explicit, not "closed with notes"):
- If any required field on any lane is missing, the lane's status is recorded as explicitly incomplete. Not "ready with caveats." Not "closed with notes." Incomplete is incomplete. The closure cannot proceed in that state.
- If a named-owner certification (Owen for source completeness, Ines for lifecycle governance, Daniela's source-reliability and release certification) is not in place, the packet is incomplete. Closure cannot proceed.
- If Owen closes the packet incomplete, the closure-and-exception summary names the missing fields, the missing certifications, and the owner-attributed reason for each. The summary is the single written record for the cycle. Disputes, exceptions, and follow-ups fold into the summary, not into Slack threads, DMs, or email fragments.

The first January cycle is therefore a clean test of the new cadence under incomplete-handling rules. If a required field is missing on day 2, 4, or 5, the cycle closes incomplete and the exception summary names it. That is the intended operating behavior, not a failure.

## The quarterly rotating recheck (one lane per quarter)

Effective January 5, 2027, Riley enters the routine cadence only via the quarterly rotating recheck of one evidence lane. The recheck is independent verification, not a second approval queue.

Shape:
- Cadence. One recheck per quarter.
- Subject. One evidence lane per quarter, picked by Riley.
- Lane selection. Only after Owen's routine packet closure for the relevant cycle is recorded. The recheck cannot shape the routine sample and cannot quietly become a second closure review.
- Inspection dimensions (fixed, five). Denominator or coverage dates; outcome window; exclusions; reliability evidence; revenue and forecast treatment.
- Safeguards (fixed, four). Does not reopen source closure; does not approve Ines's owner certification; does not exercise Daniela's release or rollback controls; does not create a second approval queue.
- Artifact. One-page recheck note per quarter, filed in the Lifecycle Systems folder by the second business day of the week following the quarter close. The note cites Owen's recorded source-completeness decision for the cycle the lane belongs to and is filed separately from the routine closure packet.
- Time budget. Half-day at most. Not a substitute for routine prep, source closure, owner certification, or engineering controls.

What the recheck is NOT:
- Not a request for Riley to approve or reject any other lane owner's certification.
- Not a release / suppress / restore / rollback action.
- Not a route for second approval of routine claims.
- Not a calibration instrument (the November 17 working notes were not delivered feedback and did not expand authority).

If the recheck's findings need action, they flow through the existing escalation set (see below) or as input to the next cycle's source-completeness decision — never as an amendment to the current cycle's closure.

## Escalation triggers retained (Riley enters on these)

The escalation set is closed. Six triggers. Adding a trigger requires Riley's sign-off; removing one is not on the table.

1. Missing fields in a routine packet.
2. Disputed semantics on a defined term or claim surface.
3. Cross-surface discrepancies (a number that reconciles in one surface but not another).
4. Customer corrections (a customer has flagged an inaccuracy affecting a routine claim).
5. Incident stops (anything that pauses, rolls back, or quarantines a routine cycle).
6. Executive-language decisions (any claim headed to exec, board, investor, or external comms surfaces).

Escalation is into Riley's queue, not a request to skip Riley. Owen / Ines remain the named owners; Riley arbitrates and decides.

## Decision-owner boundaries (established, unchanged)

- Owen Pham. Routine single-path operating explanation + exception explanation. Source-completeness closure on routine packets. Within scope: monthly sanitized campaign snapshot by second business day; routine exception readouts on the four-lane scope (≤3 neutral readouts per week; stale fail-closed); Helio Start reporting as one of the existing shared-state consumers; the day-5 closure or explicit incomplete recording + closure-and-exception summary. Outside scope: causal / revenue / forecast / board-readiness / exec-language decisions; approval of Ines's certification; engineering release / suppress / restore / rollback controls.
- Ines Kovac. Lifecycle governance and message-state controls. Within scope: lifecycle-governance certification by fourth business day; owner-state certification; messaging consumption tied to shared-state; Expansion Assist descriptive posture; `routine education` reclassification authority (HIGHER-RISK); boundary to Riley on disputed semantics and exec language. Outside scope: source-completeness closure; engineering release controls; causal / revenue / forecast interpretation.
- Daniela Schultz. Transport, source reliability, and engineering release / rollback controls. Within scope: source-reliability and release certification by fourth business day; the rollback path as one of the two approved restore conditions (the other is Riley-led customer correction / incident stop); reliability evidence for the recheck's fourth dimension. Outside scope: lifecycle governance; source-completeness closure; causal / revenue / forecast treatment decisions.
- Riley Tanaka. Final claim authority + the recheck + escalation. Within scope: causal / revenue / forecast / board-readiness / exec-language decisions; the quarterly rotating recheck; arbitration on the six escalation triggers; judgment-boundary ownership for cross-surface lifecycle decisions. Outside scope: routine prep; routine source-closure attendance (effective Jan 5); engineering release controls.

## Boundaries preserved at the Q1 frame (carried over from the Dec 4 decision)

- Engineering reliability and release controls remain with Daniela's organization.
- Customer Success case ownership does not transfer.
- Expansion Assist remains descriptive, not forecast.
- Helio Start intake rule remains additive; refusal semantics are unchanged; five-state model preserved.
- The shared state contract is not in production as a result of this draft or the Dec 4 decision. Any production rollout requires a separate go decision with its own change-control path (Ines on governance, Daniela's org on reliability).
- Existing domain authority for each surface owner is preserved.

## Cuts (what this draft does NOT do)

- Does not change lane ownership. Owen / Ines / Daniela / Riley lanes are the same.
- Does not change the four-lane scope or count.
- Does not change the seven required fields per lane or their meanings.
- Does not authorize any Q1 production rollout of a shared-state implementation.
- Does not reopen Expansion Assist's descriptive posture or convert it into a forecast input.
- Does not authorize a fifth consumer.
- Does not delegate disputed semantics, cross-surface consequences, customer-correction / incident-stop, or exec-language carry away from Riley.
- Does not imply a re-decision. The Dec 4 decision is the decision; this draft surfaces its Q1 shape for staff review.

## Future paid Helio Start — held separately

The future paid Helio Start question is held separately. This draft does not:
- approve or imply approved traffic for paid Helio Start;
- approve or imply approved budget for paid Helio Start;
- change Helio Start's product or pricing status;
- change the existing reopen conditions (the 5/18 paid-acq cap and 8/21 denials of second-batch / pipeline / forecast credit carry forward until a separate go decision).

The paid-Helio-Start question has its own review path and its own decision owner. It is not part of the Q1 Lifecycle Systems operating priorities and is not addressed by them.

## Calls for staff review (December 18)

1. Confirm the Q1 shape matches the Dec 4 decision record. Any amendment to a lane boundary, the recheck shape, or the escalation set is a re-decision, not a staff-review edit.
2. Confirm the four lanes stay separate through Q1. No combined growth number; no cross-lane revenue / forecast credit.
3. Confirm the seven required fields per lane and their current meanings are preserved under the Jan 5 cadence.
4. Confirm the first January cycle (Jan 5 open; second / fourth / fifth business-day cadence; explicit incomplete handling) is the intended operating behavior.
5. Flag any conflict between this draft and the wider Q1 plan so we reconcile before Q1 starts.

---

End of draft. Status: DRAFT for December 18 staff review. Owner-lane input invited. The Dec 4 decision is the decision; this is its Q1 restatement.

Each named owner (Owen for source completeness; Ines for lifecycle governance and owner-state; Daniela for source reliability and engineering release) delivers the named certification on the fourth business day. A missing certification is recorded as missing and is visible in the closure-and-exception summary.
3. Visible incomplete state. Whenever a required field on any lane is missing or a named-owner certification is absent, the cycle's status is recorded as explicitly incomplete. The cycle is not called successful in that state. Closure does not occur in that state.

Cadence (effective January 5, 2027):
- Second business day. Owen's monthly sanitized campaign snapshot is due. Hard date against the calendar, not against completion of any other step. (Operating test #1.)
- Fourth business day. Ines's lifecycle-governance and owner-state certification is due, delivered as an input to source closure — not as a request for Riley's routine approval. Daniela's source-reliability and release certification is due. (Operating test #2.)
- Fifth business day. Owen must either close the routine four-lane source review OR explicitly leave it incomplete. Either way, Owen sends one closure-and-exception summary — not informal follow-up fragments. The cycle is not called successful before it closes. (Operating test #3.)

Incomplete handling (explicit, not "closed with notes"):
- If any required field on any lane is missing, the lane's status is recorded as explicitly incomplete. Not "ready with caveats." Not "closed with notes." Incomplete is incomplete. The cycle is not called successful and closure cannot proceed in that state.
- If a named-owner certification (Owen for source completeness, Ines for lifecycle governance, Daniela's source-reliability and release certification) is not in place, the packet is incomplete. The cycle is not called successful and closure cannot proceed.
- Incomplete is a visible state, not a quiet one. If the cycle is incomplete on day 5, Owen records it as incomplete and names the missing fields, the missing certifications, and the owner-attributed reason for each in the closure-and-exception summary. The summary is the single written record for the cycle. Disputes, exceptions, and follow-ups fold into the summary, not into Slack threads, DMs, or email fragments.

The first January cycle is therefore a clean test of the new cadence under incomplete-handling rules. If a required field or certification is missing on day 2, 4, or 5, the cycle closes incomplete and the exception summary names it. That is the intended operating behavior, not a failure — and the cycle is not called successful in that state.

## The quarterly rotating recheck (one lane per quarter)

Effective January 5, 2027, Riley enters the routine cadence only via the quarterly rotating recheck of one evidence lane. The recheck is independent verification, not a second approval queue.

Shape:
- Cadence. One recheck per quarter.
- Subject. One evidence lane per quarter, picked by Riley.
- Lane selection. Only after Owen's routine packet closure for the relevant cycle is recorded. The recheck cannot shape the routine sample and cannot quietly become a second closure review.
- Inspection dimensions (fixed, five). Denominator or coverage dates; outcome window; exclusions; reliability evidence; revenue and forecast treatment.
- Safeguards (fixed, four). Does not reopen source closure; does not approve Ines's owner certification; does not exercise Daniela's release or rollback controls; does not create a second approval queue.
- Artifact. One-page recheck note per quarter, filed in the Lifecycle Systems folder by the second business day of the week following the quarter close. The note cites Owen's recorded source-completeness decision for the cycle the lane belongs to and is filed separately from the routine closure packet.
- Time budget. Half-day at most. Not a substitute for routine prep, source closure, owner certification, or engineering controls.

What the recheck is NOT:
- Not a request for Riley to approve or reject any other lane owner's certification (Owen, Ines, or Daniela).
- Not a release / suppress / restore / rollback action.
- Not a route for second approval of routine claims.
- Not a calibration instrument (the November 17 working notes were not delivered feedback and did not expand authority).

If the recheck's findings need action, they flow through the existing escalation set (see below) or as input to the next cycle's source-completeness decision — never as an amendment to the current cycle's closure.

## Escalation triggers retained (Riley enters on these)

The escalation set is closed. Six triggers. Adding a trigger requires Riley's sign-off; removing one is not on the table.

1. Missing fields in a routine packet.
2. Disputed semantics on a defined term or claim surface.
3. Cross-surface discrepancies (a number that reconciles in one surface but not another).
4. Customer corrections (a customer has flagged an inaccuracy affecting a routine claim).
5. Incident stops (anything that pauses, rolls back, or quarantines a routine cycle).
6. Executive-language decisions (any claim headed to exec, board, investor, or external comms surfaces).

Escalation is into Riley's queue, not a request to skip Riley. Owen / Ines / Daniela remain the named owners; Riley arbitrates and decides.

## Decision-owner boundaries (established, unchanged)

- Owen Pham. Routine single-path operating explanation + exception explanation. Source-completeness closure on routine packets. Within scope: monthly sanitized campaign snapshot by second business day; routine exception readouts on the four-lane scope (≤3 neutral readouts per week; stale fail-closed); Helio Start reporting as one of the existing shared-state consumers; the day-5 closure or explicit incomplete recording + closure-and-exception summary; receiving Ines's lifecycle-governance certification and Daniela's source-reliability and release certification as named-owner inputs to source closure. Outside scope: causal / revenue / forecast / board-readiness / exec-language decisions; approval of Ines's certification; engineering release / suppress / restore / rollback controls.
- Ines Kovac. Lifecycle governance and message-state controls. Within scope: lifecycle-governance certification by fourth business day, delivered as an input to Owen's source closure (not as a request for Riley's routine approval); owner-state certification; messaging consumption tied to shared-state; Expansion Assist descriptive posture; `routine education` reclassification authority (HIGHER-RISK); boundary to Riley on disputed semantics and exec language. Outside scope: source-completeness closure; engineering release controls; causal / revenue / forecast interpretation; routine approval by Riley of her certification (her cert flows into Owen's closure decision, not into Riley's queue).
- Daniela Schultz. Transport, source reliability, and engineering release / rollback controls. Within scope: source-reliability and release certification by fourth business day, delivered as a named-owner input to Owen's source closure; the rollback path as one of the two approved restore conditions (the other is Riley-led customer correction / incident stop); reliability evidence for the recheck's fourth dimension. Outside scope: lifecycle governance; source-completeness closure; causal / revenue / forecast treatment decisions.
- Riley Tanaka. Final claim authority + the recheck + escalation. Within scope: causal / revenue / forecast / board-readiness / exec-language decisions; the quarterly rotating recheck; arbitration on the six escalation triggers; judgment-boundary ownership for cross-surface lifecycle decisions. Outside scope: routine prep; routine source-closure attendance (effective Jan 5); engineering release controls.

## Boundaries preserved at the Q1 frame (carried over from the Dec 4 decision)

- Engineering reliability and release controls remain with Daniela's organization.
- Customer Success case ownership does not transfer.
- Expansion Assist remains descriptive, not forecast.
- Helio Start intake rule remains additive; refusal semantics are unchanged; five-state model preserved.
- The shared state contract is not in production as a result of this draft or the Dec 4 decision. Any production rollout requires a separate go decision with its own change-control path (Ines on governance, Daniela's org on reliability).
- Existing domain authority for each surface owner is preserved.

## Cuts (what this draft does NOT do)

- Does not change lane ownership. Owen / Ines / Daniela / Riley lanes are the same.
- Does not change the four-lane scope or count.
- Does not change the seven required fields per lane or their meanings.
- Does not authorize any Q1 production rollout of a shared-state implementation.
- Does not reopen Expansion Assist's descriptive posture or convert it into a forecast input.
- Does not authorize a fifth consumer.
- Does not delegate disputed semantics, cross-surface consequences, customer-correction / incident-stop, or exec-language carry away from Riley.
- Does not imply a re-decision. The Dec 4 decision is the decision; this draft surfaces its Q1 shape for staff review.
- Does not call a cycle successful before it closes. Closure is the closing event, not an inferred state.

## Future paid Helio Start — held separately

The future paid Helio Start question is held separately. This draft does not:
- approve or imply approved traffic for paid Helio Start;
- approve or imply approved budget for paid Helio Start;
- change Helio Start's product or pricing status;
- change the existing reopen conditions (the 5/18 paid-acq cap and 8/21 denials of second-batch / pipeline / forecast credit carry forward until a separate go decision).

The paid-Helio-Start question has its own review path and its own decision owner. It is not part of the Q1 Lifecycle Systems operating priorities and is not addressed by them.

## Calls for staff review (December 18)

1. Confirm the Q1 shape matches the Dec 4 decision record. Any amendment to a lane boundary, the recheck shape, or the escalation set is a re-decision, not a staff-review edit.
2. Confirm the four lanes stay separate through Q1. No combined growth number; no cross-lane revenue / forecast credit.
3. Confirm the seven required fields per lane and their current meanings are preserved under the Jan 5 cadence.
4. Confirm the first January cycle (Jan 5 open; second / fourth / fifth business-day cadence; explicit incomplete handling; the cycle is not called successful before it closes) is the intended operating behavior.
5. Confirm that Ines's certification is delivered as an input to Owen's source closure and is not a request for Riley's routine approval.
6. Flag any conflict between this draft and the wider Q1 plan so we reconcile before Q1 starts.

---

End of draft. Status: DRAFT for December 18 staff review. Owner-lane input invited. The Dec 4 decision is the decision; this is its Q1 restatement.

# July owner lanes — historical interpretation guardrail

Purpose: help teams using the current investigation framework readouts understand what the July 2023 owner-lane arrangement did and did not establish. This is a historical governance guardrail. It is not a current process guide, not a re-decision of any later lane boundary, and not a source of operating authority today.

## What the July 2023 arrangement was

On 2023-07-04, Priya allocated informal owner-lanes for one month of investigation-framework work. The allocation was scoped to July 2023 only.

- Owen — Helio Start baseline + expansion eligibility cuts.
- Ines — lifecycle fork risk + copy boundaries (Helio Start and expansion-nudge).
- Riley — decision rules, executive tradeoffs, cross-functional guardrails.

Three things to keep in mind when you read this allocation today:

1. It was a July 2023 working allocation. It was not a permanent org-chart change and not a delegation of decision rights.
2. The investigation framework itself was informal in July 2023. It was not yet a formalized company process.
3. The allocation did not survive as written. Each later boundary decision stands on its own record and supersedes the July 2023 working allocation where they overlap.

## What it DID establish

- Named working owners for the three threads active in July 2023 (Helio Start baseline + expansion cuts, lifecycle-fork risk + copy boundaries, decision rules + exec + cross-fn).
- A clear "not permanent" framing, so readers do not import the allocation into later quarters.
- An "informal framework" framing, so readers do not treat July 2023 readouts as if they were produced under a later formalized cadence.

## What it DID NOT establish

- Lane ownership for any later period. The four current board-evidence lanes (Helio Start, Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, CS auto-nudge controls) have their own later owner assignments.
- Decision rights. It allocated working attention for the month, not authority over causal claims, revenue treatment, forecast credit, or executive language. Those rights have lived elsewhere in every later quarter.
- Source-completeness closure authority. Routine four-lane source-completeness closure is a later (2025-07-01) decision record, with subsequent bounded updates (2025-09-24 Ines routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state closure delegation; 2026-09-24 Owen routine source-completeness closure across the four board-evidence lanes). None of these are part of the July 2023 arrangement.
- A re-decision or amendment of any later lane boundary. If a current readout reads back to "what the lanes were in July 2023," the answer is the working allocation above — and only that, for that month.

## How to use this when reading current readouts

When a current readout cites the investigation framework and a reader reaches back to July 2023:

- Treat the July 2023 allocation as a working arrangement for one month, not as standing governance.
- Treat the investigation framework in July 2023 as informal, not as the formalized cadence used in later quarters.
- Anchor any operating authority on the later decision record, not on the July 2023 allocation. The July 2023 allocation names who was doing the work in July 2023; it does not name who carries the authority today.
- Do not infer causal, revenue, forecast, executive-language, source-completeness closure, lifecycle-governance, engineering release, or forecast-credit decisions from the July 2023 allocation. Those rights have a different record.
- If the July 2023 allocation appears to conflict with a later decision record, the later record governs.

## Cuts (what this guardrail is NOT)

- Not a current process guide. The current operating cadence, the four board-evidence lanes, the seven required fields, the recheck, and the escalation set are documented in later decisions and are out of scope here.
- Not a re-decision. This guardrail restates the historical scope of the July 2023 allocation; it does not amend, extend, or replace any later decision record.
- Not an expansion of any lane owner's authority. Owen's, Ines's, and Daniela's current authorities stand on later decision records; this guardrail neither adds to nor subtracts from them.
- Not a fifth consumer or a fifth lane. The four board-evidence lanes remain the four.
- Not a forecast, revenue, causal, or board-readiness input. The July 2023 allocation carried no such rights.

---
