# Helio Start bounded paid-search proposal — October 2027

**Status banner — PROPOSAL COMPLETED BY PREPARATION OWNER ON 2027-10-13; AUTHORIZATIONS STILL PENDING.**

This document is the completed bounded proposal authored by Riley (preparation owner) ahead of the 2027-10-16 review with Priya. Completion of the proposal is not authorization. Every value below is proposed, not approved. Authorization of the total budget, daily cap, admission cap, stop and pause conditions, and final go/no-go remains pending through (a) Priya's decision review on 2027-10-16, (b) a separate Daniela check before paid traffic is enabled, and (c) the §8.E future-paid case-review gate and §8.E.3 proposal precondition, both still in force. Paid traffic remains OFF until each of those gates has cleared, and any of them alone is sufficient to keep traffic off. No budget, batch, paid-traffic decision, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, or production change is approved by the existence of this completed proposal.

Brief id: `BRIEF-2027-10-helio-start-paid-search`
Preparation owner: Riley
Release / rollback (rel/rb): Daniela (per standing rule)
Decision review scheduled: Priya — 2027-10-16, 2:00–3:00pm Central

---

## 1. Certified mature evidence

This brief only cites evidence that has already been certified. Mature evidence means (a) cohort-stabilized, (b) read at the metric's natural cadence, (c) effect-size estimate with confidence interval, and (d) not distorted by a conflicting in-flight growth workstream.

- **[cite: prior brief id]** — CAC ceiling on Helio Start from organic. The paid-search admission cap and stop conditions must clear this floor before any recommendation is written.
- **[cite: prior brief id]** — Channel-mix maturity assessment. Restricts the bid-eligible placements referenced in Section 3 (staffed design).
- **[cite: prior brief id]** — Audience overlap and incrementality test results. Defines the lookalike seed used as the paid-search audience.
- **[cite: prior brief id]** — 21-day read window precedent from the closed Reminders workstream (closed 9/20/27). The same read window, CI reporting standard, and interim-equals-safety-guardrails rule are reused here; no claim is allowed to extend beyond what that precedent supports.

No claim in this brief extends past what these artifacts certify.

## 2. Certified 24-case nonproduction preflight

Per the standing rule that disputed, cross-team, or executive-facing artifacts cannot be silently edited, the 24-case preflight was run end-to-end in nonproduction and is preserved as a standalone artifact. This section summarizes the framing only; the full case set is the supporting artifact, not this brief.

- **Scope (24 cases):** bid shaping, audience overlap checks, signup-source capture, attribution windows, lifecycle handoff paths, suppression rules, and stop-condition triggers.
- **Per-case pass criteria:** (a) no collision with an in-flight lifecycle email or activation/retention workstream; (b) no silent edit to any disputed, cross-team, or executive-facing artifact; (c) the attribution path resolves end-to-end without falling back to last-click defaults.
- **Certification:** [cite: preflight artifact id / certifier / date]. Certification confirms the proposal is safe to advance to authorization review. It does not, by itself, authorize the proposal.

## 3. Staffed design

Named coverage is required. Role slots marked pending must be filled before this brief can move from proposal to authorization. Riley retains preparation ownership throughout. Daniela owns rel/rb.

- Preparation owner: Riley
- Release / rollback (rel/rb): Daniela
- Paid-media lead: pending — confirm
- Lifecycle coordinator: pending — confirm; must verify the 21-day read window does not overlap an active lifecycle email or activation/retention workstream, per the standing sequential-workstream preference
- On-call / incident: pending — confirm
- Analyst for 21-day read: pending — confirm

---

## 4. Proposed budget and admission bounds

**Proposer: Riley. Not approved.** Reviewers: Priya at the 2027-10-16 decision review; Daniela in a separate paid-traffic check after that review. The values below are a proposal, not authorization. No value takes effect unless and until every Section 6 approval is checked and the §8.E / §8.E.3 gates have cleared.

- **Total budget:** $8,000 maximum, drawn from the same envelope that funded the closed Q1 Helio Start cohort. Lower than the closed cohort's $14,420 because this is a cycle-1 bounded test of the §8.E mitigations on the seven high-support workspace classifications, not a scale-up. Matches the Q2 2027 paid-test precedent (Apr 9, 2027 — Priya approved $8,000/25 admits, run-closed at the earlier of spend or admits, no second batch authorized).
- **Daily cap:** $400/day. Sized so that a fully-pacing run burns less than one-third of the total budget inside the first seven days, keeping the run inside the day-7 safety-guardrails interim checkpoint without forcing an early stop on pacing alone.
- **Admission cap:** 25 admitted workspaces total. Same cap as the Q2 2027 paid-test precedent. Reflects the smaller test envelope and the §8.E.3 requirement to account for each of the seven high-support workspace classifications inside the admitted-path bounds rather than running past them.
- **Run-close trigger:** the earlier of (a) $8,000 spent, (b) 25 admitted workspaces, or (c) 6 weeks elapsed since launch.
- **Read-window length:** 21 days (standing rule — confirmed).
- **Interim checkpoint:** day 7, safety guardrails only; no scale-up or early stop on effect size alone (standing rule — confirmed).

Inputs already on file:

- Certified mature-evidence CAC ceiling from Section 1 — the admission cap and stop conditions below are sized against this floor.
- Finance routing — unchanged from the Q1 closed cohort; no new finance lane is being opened by this proposal.

Inputs still required before authorization:

- Section 6 approvals (Section 6 below).
- §8.E case-review gate clearance (Owen + Customer Success classification of the seven high-support workspaces; Ines + Daniela determination of state-meaning, routing, and setup-sequence dimensions).
- §8.E.3 proposal precondition — per-case prevention / mitigation / bound stated against each of the seven classifications, not merely listed.

## 5. Stop and pause conditions

**Proposer: Riley. Not approved.** Each condition specifies threshold, owner, and action. The framing clause is fixed in advance and non-negotiable: any stop or pause decision is gated by a named owner (Daniela, rel/rb), takes effect within the same business day, and is recorded as a brief update — never as a silent edit.

- **CAC ceiling breach.** Threshold: any 7-day rolling paid-search CAC that exceeds the certified mature-evidence CAC ceiling from Section 1 by ≥15% on the day-7 interim, or by any amount on the day-21 read. Owner: Daniela (rel/rb), with Riley retained on the claim and forecast boundary. Action: pause the proposed batch the same business day; reset only after a certified mature re-read clears the threshold.
- **Attribution path degradation.** Pause the proposed batch if paid-source attribution cannot reconcile from eligibility-flow start through the final admitted, assisted, or ineligible route. This pause trigger is unchanged in every other respect: it does not modify any eligibility, routing, lifecycle, or instrumentation rule; it does not change the assisted-routing or external-authority meaning in force elsewhere in this brief; it does not authorize, lift, or extend paid traffic; and it does not affect the prep-only posture of this brief. Threshold, owner, and action details remain as specified here. Owner: Daniela (rel/rb). Action: pause the same business day; reconcile before any restart; record as a brief update.
- **Lifecycle / activation collision signal.** Threshold: any signal — from the standing lifecycle email or activation/retention workstream — that the proposed batch would run concurrently with another in-flight growth workstream, in violation of Riley's stated sequential-workstream preference. Owner: Priya (#lifecycle-systems) for the routing confirmation; Daniela (rel/rb) for the pause. Action: pause the same business day; restart only after Priya confirms sequencing against the standing workstream schedule.
- **Sign-quality floor breach.** Threshold: of the first 10 admitted workspaces, more than 10% exceed 90 account-level support minutes within the first 7 days (same threshold as the Q1 closed cohort and the Q2 2027 paid-test precedent). Owner: Daniela (rel/rb), with the §8.E case-review gate owners on the high-support classifications. Action: pause the same business day; restart only after each high-support case has been classified per §8.E and the §8.E.3 mitigation has been recorded against that case. The seven high-support workspaces from the closed Q1 cohort are accounted for inside the admission cap and the day-7 sign-quality threshold; the run-closed trigger fires before the admitted path can carry a second cohort of unclassified cases.
- **Budget pacing anomaly.** Threshold: spend exceeding one-third of the total budget ($2,667) within the first 7 days, OR daily-cap exceedance on any single day, OR a <$50/day spend rate for 5 consecutive business days after day 3 (indicates bid-eligibility or audience-overlap rejection, not just low volume). Owner: Daniela (rel/rb). Action: investigate the same business day; pause if the cause is bid-eligibility or audience-overlap rejection; record as a brief update.

## 6. Remaining approvals

**This section lists approvals still pending. No box is checked. Until every box below is checked, this brief remains a proposal that authorizes no traffic.**

- [ ] Total budget ($8,000) approved by Priya at the 2027-10-16 review
- [ ] Daily cap ($400/day) approved by Priya at the 2027-10-16 review
- [ ] Admission cap (25 admitted workspaces) approved by Priya at the 2027-10-16 review
- [ ] Stop and pause conditions (Section 5) approved by Priya at the 2027-10-16 review
- [ ] Lifecycle coordinator confirmed (no overlap with currently-running lifecycle email or activation/retention workstream) — pending
- [ ] Paid-media lead confirmed — pending
- [ ] 21-day read analyst confirmed — pending
- [ ] On-call / incident owner confirmed — pending
- [ ] Routing confirmation from Priya (#lifecycle-systems) that the 21-day read window is sequenced against other recurring workstreams — pending
- [ ] §8.E future-paid case-review gate cleared — pending (Owen + Customer Success classification of all seven high-support workspaces into external-authority action / ordinary integration / billing / another supported cause named explicitly; Ines + Daniela determination of state-meaning, routing, and setup-sequence dimensions, with multiple dimensions allowed and each named)
- [ ] §8.E.3 proposal precondition met — pending (per-case prevention / mitigation / bound stated against each of the seven classifications; "listed" is not acceptable per §8.E.3)
- [ ] Final go / no-go authorization — pending (Priya at the 2027-10-16 review; if approved, the proposal still requires a separate Daniela check before paid traffic is enabled)
- [ ] Separate Daniela check before paid traffic is enabled — pending (post-decision; cannot be combined with the Section 6 approvals above)

Paid traffic stays OFF.

## 7. Final recommendation

**Proposer: Riley. Not approved.** The recommendation below is a proposal, not an authorization. It is contingent on every Section 6 approval being checked, and on the §8.E / §8.E.3 gates being cleared before any launch.

Subject to those preconditions, the recommendation is to **proceed with the bounded cycle-1 paid-search test as specified in Sections 4 and 5**, with the following guardrails reaffirmed in advance:

1. The test is descriptive of the §8.E mitigations on the seven high-support classifications, not causal evidence of paid-search incrementality. No claim beyond the certified mature-evidence boundary may be made on the day-21 read.
2. No pipeline treatment, no forecast credit, no scale-up language. The same claim discipline applied to the closed Q1 cohort carries forward to this run.
3. §3 admission rules and the §4.8-style pipeline / forecast exclusion are not weakened by this proposal. They are reaffirmed, and the run does not introduce a new admission, routing, lifecycle, or fail-closed rule.
4. Paid traffic remains OFF until every Section 6 approval has cleared AND the separate Daniela check has cleared. Either of those gates is sufficient to keep traffic off; traffic does not turn on in their absence.
5. The proposal must be reviewed as a single bound: do not approve the budget without approving the corresponding stop conditions or vice versa. Partial approval is not contemplated and would not authorize traffic.

This proposal does not authorize a second batch, a scale-up, or a follow-on cycle. Each subsequent cycle would require a fresh proposal reviewed under the same gates, including a fresh §8.E / §8.E.3 pass against whatever high-support cases the prior cycle surfaces. No carry-forward of authorization from cycle 1 to cycle 2 is implied or permitted.

---

_Preparation owner: Riley. Release / rollback: Daniela. Decision review: Priya, 2027-10-16. Brief id: `BRIEF-2027-10-helio-start-paid-search`._

arguments.subject: 2028 plan documents, provider-network files, and election deadline — request for publication dates
arguments.body:
Hi Helio Benefits,

Following up on the 9/21 clarification about the HDHP's employer HSA estimate, I am still missing three 2028 items before I can verify my current providers or make an election:

1. The final 2028 plan documents (Summary of Benefits and Coverage or equivalent, including the HDHP and PPO plan options).
2. The 2028 provider-network files I can use to confirm whether my current primary-care and physical-therapy clinics remain in-network under each plan option.
3. The 2028 election deadline (and any related blackout or effective-date dates) so I know the window I am working against.

Could you let me know the publication date — or, if publication is staged, the expected dates — for each of the three items above?

One clarification I want to record accurately, based on what was shared on 9/21: the HDHP's $1,000 estimated employer HSA contribution is not a single upfront deposit. It is four separate $250 quarterly deposits, and each $250 deposit is contingent on my remaining HSA-eligible at the applicable deposit date. The total $1,000 figure is therefore not guaranteed — if my HSA eligibility changes between quarters, the remaining deposits do not accelerate or carry over, they simply do not land.

Helio Start — Decision Evidence Card (March 2024 public-product decision)
Author: Riley Tanaka
Date prepared: 2028-01-01
Folder: Growth
Purpose: concise evidence card for the March 4, 2024 public-product decision meeting (event evt_1789271216070). Source: closed 2024-02-26 results-meeting readout. Card summarizes what the readiness cohort did and did not establish; it does not re-decide the boundaries.

══════════════════════════════════════════════
ONE-LINE CALL
══════════════════════════════════════════════
The readiness cohort supports a bounded public-product decision (move the access-review surface onto the public product within the existing eligibility and refusal rules). It does NOT support GA, pricing-page exposure, or removal of the refusal boundaries.

══════════════════════════════════════════════
WHAT THE COHORT ESTABLISHED
══════════════════════════════════════════════

1. Operating volume — admission path held at the agreed scale.
  - 120 applications received.
  - 104 admitted (87%): 76 auto-passed exact-match admin proofs + 28 legitimate mismatches passed with corroborating admin evidence.
  - 82 of 104 admitted accounts (79%) created workspaces.
  - 68 of 104 accounts (65% of admitted, ~57% of applicants) reached first integration by day 7.
  - Day-7 integration is the highest-confidence sub-read; workspace creation is secondary.

2. Support coverage — refusal boundaries routed out the support-heavy cases before they hit the admitted path.
  - 9 ordinary setup questions handled within normal CS coverage.
  - 4 permissions / ownership reviews handled within normal CS coverage.
  - 13 CS-touchable cases against 104 admitted (~12.5%) — within the coverage the team was sized for.
  - No manual-billing, import, or migration case entered the admitted path. The refusal boundaries did their job.

3. State integrity — Daniela's audit on admitted workspaces was clean.
  - One current entitlement state per admitted workspace.
  - One current support state per admitted workspace.
  - No workspace carried stale or duplicated state. The admitted-path state model held.

4. Excluded operational cases — the 16 routed-out cases are described, not enumerated individually.
  - 16 of 120 (13%) routed out, distributed across the five refusal boundaries: agency identity, unresolved ownership, manual billing, import, migration.
  - Routing was observed; refusal-boundary effectiveness is established at the category level, not at the per-case level.

══════════════════════════════════════════════
WHAT THE COHORT DID NOT ESTABLISH
══════════════════════════════════════════════

1. GA readiness. The cohort was a readiness gate, not a GA gate. Day-7 integration at ~57% of applicants is not a forecast of sustained adoption at scale.

2. Pricing-page exposure. Pricing-page exposure is a separate decision with separate evidence requirements (margin, packaging, competitive posture). The cohort contains no information that bears on it.

3. Removal of any refusal boundary. All five refusal boundaries (agency identity, unresolved ownership, manual billing, import, migration) are observed to be doing the work of keeping support-heavy cases out of the admitted path. Removing any one of them would change the support-coverage result above and is not supported by this read.

4. Per-case audit of the 16 routed-out cases. The cohort establishes that the refusal boundaries routed out ~13% of applicants. It does not establish a per-case audit of those 16 against later-life behavior, downstream revenue impact, or whether any individual routed-out case was misclassified.

5. Long-tail behavior beyond day 7. Day-7 integration is the only forward-looking operational read. Day-30, day-90, expansion, and renewal behaviors for this cohort are not in this evidence.

6. Source-by-source freshness. State integrity is established as an audit-level finding (one current entitlement + one current support per admitted workspace). It is not a source-by-source freshness measurement; freshness and the audit outcome are distinct evidence and the audit outcome does not substitute for a freshness read.

7. Causal claim about which eligibility rule produced which outcome. The cohort establishes the operating envelope, not which rule (exact-match admin proof vs. corroborating-evidence path) drove which conversion behavior.

══════════════════════════════════════════════
DECISION THE COHORT JUSTIFIES (bounded)
══════════════════════════════════════════════

  - Move the access-review surface onto the public product within the existing eligibility rules and the existing five refusal boundaries.
  - Keep the refusal boundaries intact. Do not widen or remove any of: agency identity, unresolved ownership, manual billing, import, migration.
  - Hold the day-7 integration rate as the operating read on the admitted path until a longer-horizon read exists.
  - Continue Daniela's per-admitted-workspace state audit as a routine check.

══════════════════════════════════════════════
DECISIONS THE COHORT DOES NOT JUSTIFY
══════════════════════════════════════════════

  - GA.
  - Pricing-page exposure.
  - Any change to the five refusal boundaries.
  - Forecast credit, pipeline treatment, or scale claims against the day-7 read.
  - Per-case audit of the 16 routed-out cases (deferred).
  - Any claim extending past day 7 for this cohort (deferred to a later read).

══════════════════════════════════════════════
SOURCE
══════════════════════════════════════════════
  - 2024-02-26 results-meeting readout (closed by the group).
  - Scheduling context: 2024-03-04 decision meeting, 2:00–2:45pm Central (event evt_1789271216070); attendees Riley, Priya, Marcus Vail, Daniela, Owen, Ines, Customer Success.
  - Meeting body: decision is bounded by existing eligibility and refusal rules; does NOT presume GA or pricing-page exposure.

---

INTERNAL — CLASSIFICATION (Expansion Assist lane, descriptive)

SUMMARY
The account's inbound is a help-or-options request, not an expansion. It counts as one CS-ask. The options request, the Customer Success handoff, and any actual plan change are three separate things — held apart by design.

WHY
- The account surfaced a usage/options question. No authorized plan change. No opt-in.
- Options inquiry with no authorized plan change is CS-ask, never expansion (2024-08-28 ruling; carried in memory).
- Grain: account-level CS request = unit of count. Any number of channel events on that request = raw evidence on the single request, not separate requests.
- The CS handoff is triggered by account ask (or agreed ceiling), and is itself a routing event — not an outcome read on Expansion Assist.
- Any actual plan change, if and when it lands, is a downstream commercial outcome observed against this account. It lives in its own bucket by design.

THREE THINGS, HELD APART

  1. Options request (the input)
     - One CS request. Classify as CS-ask.
     - Channel events (in-product click, email reply, etc.) retained as raw evidence on this single request with timestamps. Do not multiply.
     - In-window vs. out-of-window tag noted on the request, not on channel events.

  2. Customer Success handoff (the routing)
     - Owned by CS. Triggers: account asks, or the agreed usage-ceiling is reached.
     - Not an Expansion Assist outcome read. Not pipeline. Not forecast input.
     - Handoff logged as a routing event with timestamp; does not change the count of CS-asks.

  3. Actual expansion (the output, if/when it lands)
     - A separate downstream commercial outcome against this account.
     - Logged descriptively, with raw timestamps and the CS record attached.
     - In-window vs. out-of-window: in-window goes into the primary read at grain; out-of-window is a forward descriptive entry, not folded into the primary 45-day read and not a duplicate.

CUTS (what this is not)
- Not two requests because the account used two channels. De-dup by request, not by channel.
- Not an expansion conversion. No authorized plan change → stays CS-ask.
- Not causal. The sequence (request → CS-ask → possible later expansion) is consistent with either outreach-prompted help-seeking or unrelated behavior. No control exists; no claim is made.
- Not pipeline. CS-ask + handoff + later expansion ≠ pipeline stages here.
- Not revenue. No booking attached to this classification.
- Not forecast. A single observed sequence in one account is not a basis for projection.

- Effect attributable to Expansion Assist: not identifiable without a control. Expansion Assist remains descriptive; this classification does not move that.

- Route: CS owns the options walkthrough as a CS ask; handoff is a routing event, not an Expansion Assist outcome.
- If a plan change later lands: log it as a separate downstream commercial outcome at grain, in-window or out-of-window per the established boundary; do not rewrite the CS-ask; do not credit against expansion / forecast / causal-readout denominators.
- Descriptive evidence limits preserved: no causal, pipeline, revenue, or forecast treatment.

SUM
Decline. Record the activity descriptively (pricing-and-options conversation in the standing lane); do not pre-book expansion pending close.

WHY
Expansion Assist is descriptive — it records what actually happened on the account, not what we expect to happen. A pricing-and-options conversation is a sales motion, not an expansion event. Booking it now and "revising later" is the routine line-edit the channel exists to prevent: it makes the expansion count reflect forecast rather than outcome, contaminates downstream cuts (cohort, source, segment), and forces a correction on something we already know is uncertain at the moment of booking. The clean close date also disappears, because a back-dated re-classification looks like the descriptive channel was wrong, not that the forecast was wrong.

CUTS
- Do not mark this account as expanded as of 11/26.
- Do not back-date an expansion line in absence of a tier change, seat add, contract signature, or invoice.
- Do not hold a placeholder slot on the rationale "we'll revise later."

P
- Leave the standing-lane entry as pricing-and-options — that's a true description of what the stakeholder did.
- If/when the account actually closes expansion (sub change, MRR/ARR movement, signed order), update at that point with the real close date. That is a legitimate re-classification off a real event, not a line-edit.
- If the stakeholder pushes back, route the dispute to Daniela per the channel rule (rel/rb → Daniela). Keep disputed/cross/exec entries on the channel; do not resolve by routine edit.

EFFECT
- Expansion line stays clean for the 11/26 reporting cycle; downstream cuts (cohort, source) read correctly.
- Forecast/pipeline continues to live in its own lane and does not leak into the descriptive count.
- If expansion does close later, it lands with a real close date and a clean re-classification trail — not a back-dated correction.

CALL
Keep the entry descriptive. Do not count as expansion until the account actually expands.

Working pre-read for the January 6, 2026 prep review (1:00–2:00pm Central) and the downstream Q1 source-lock / final-claims-review sequence.
Attendees (Jan 6 review): Riley Tanaka, Priya (lead), Owen, Ines, Daniela.

## Ownership (locked, applies to all sections below)

- Riley Tanaka — recurring operating-evidence ownership begins January 1, 2026.
- Marcus Vail — retains forecast ownership. None of the four sections below feed his forecast.
- Tomás Vega — retains the final board narrative. Final claim owner on each section below.

## How to use this pre-read

Per the 12/10/25 deck rule, Helio Start, retained-mid Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and system controls stay SEPARATE — do not combine, do not cross-reference fields between sections.

After the Jan 6 prep review, the Q1 board operating-evidence sequence is locked in two stages:
- **Q1 board operating-evidence source lock** — March 16, 2026, 10:00–11:00am Central. Locks the inputs that downstream claims are allowed to cite.
- **Q1 board operating-evidence final claims review** — March 24, 2026, 1:00–2:00pm Central. Final pass before Tomás takes the board narrative.

## Row-shape decision (locked at the Jan 6 prep review)

Every row below carries the 11-field intake order plus an explicit row-level **readiness status**. There are two row shapes:

**Customer-outcome rows** — Helio Start, Expansion Assist (retained-mid), Pricing-page path quality. Must name:
- a denominator,
- cohort dates,
- a complete predeclared outcome window (not partial, not extrapolated).

**Continuous-control rows** — System controls. Must name:
- exact coverage dates,
- outcome-window field set to `not applicable — continuous control coverage`.

**Required inputs on every row, regardless of shape:**
measurement limits, exclusions, source owner, source or release-reliability evidence, revenue and forecast treatment, and final claim owner. Lifecycle limits live INLINE on each row (per Ines at the Jan 6 prep review) — not in a shared note. Any row missing a required input remains `not board-ready`.

Per Daniela's ruling at the Jan 6 prep review: continuous system-control coverage cannot truthfully be labeled as a predeclared customer-outcome window, so System controls is always a continuous-control row. Per Owen's ruling at the Jan 6 prep review: customer-motion rows (Helio Start, Expansion Assist, pricing-page) require complete cohort windows — partial-window extrapolation is not permitted. Per Ines's ruling at the Jan 6 prep review: lifecycle limits stay attached to the individual claim they constrain rather than living in a shared note.

## Readiness status — per section (source lock 2026-03-16)

Each section has an independent readiness status. A status of `board-ready` requires every required input on every row in that section to be filled in.

- **Helio Start:** `not board-ready — the two consecutive mature cohorts (Jan 27, 2026 and Feb 24, 2026) are now certified by Owen + CS after Riley's Tue 1:1s with Owen, and the evidence condition for reopening consideration of a capped paid-acquisition proposal is satisfied (both qualifying cohorts <5% of accounts over 90 support minutes, no unsupported case admitted into either admitted path). On 2026-03-03, Priya reviewed the two packets, confirmed the evidence condition is satisfied, and authorized Riley to PREPARE a Q2 capped paid-acquisition proposal — proposal-preparation authority ONLY. The 2026-03-03 technical-gate decision permits consideration of a capped paid-acquisition proposal; it does NOT establish acquisition economics and does NOT approve a proposal, budget, paid traffic, pipeline target, forecast credit, acquisition authorization, or launch. The source packets still do not state the exact cohort start and end dates for either certified cohort's admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows; per Owen's Jan 6 ruling, partial-window extrapolation is not permitted, so the lane remains not board-ready on that input. Continuing boundary: Helio Start remains organic-only through 2026-03-31; any proposed paid test must preserve existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and support-routing rules and must receive separate budget approval before launch.`
- **Expansion Assist (retained-mid):** `board-ready — source-locked at March 16, 2026. Coverage: 18 actual exposures across the December 1, 2025 → January 30, 2026 bounded first pilots, all with complete 45-day windows; 6 help-or-options requests and 4 expansions in-window. No randomized control. Every exposure met the standing current-state criteria; no account had active Customer Success adoption or renewal work at exposure. Descriptive-only claim (no causal, revenue, or forecast treatment).`
- **Pricing-page path quality:** `board-ready — source-locked at March 16, 2026. Coverage: November 26, 2025 → February 28, 2026; 9,604 organic pricing-page sessions; 143 of 1,981 Helio Start eligibility-flow starts (7.2%) later routed out for an existing unsupported condition; 44.0% eligible-workspace admission completion; account-level support time at the 90th percentile of 75 minutes. The pricing-page control was retired November 26, 2025, so this row is framed as post-rollout continuity, not a new causal or revenue claim.`
- **System controls (CS auto-nudge system controls):** `board-ready — source-locked at March 16, 2026. Coverage: January 1, 2026 → February 28, 2026; 2,146 CS auto-nudge decisions (83 visible field-specific holds + 2,063 decisions that proceeded or were suppressed using current state); no governed-field disagreement, customer correction, or rollback; two source-age alerts fired before breach and both affected sources were refreshed before their limits. Outcome window: not applicable — continuous control coverage. Claim is limited to system-control performance.`

The 11-field intake order, applied in this exact sequence within each section:

  1. Evidence lane
  2. Proposed claim
  3. Denominator
  4. Cohort or coverage dates
  5. Predeclared outcome window and completion status
  6. Measurement limits
  7. Exclusions
  8. Source owner
  9. Source or release-reliability evidence
 10. Revenue and forecast treatment
 11. Final claim owner

---

## 1. Helio Start (customer-outcome row)

### Source-lock read — 2026-03-16

Two consecutive mature Helio Start cohorts (Jan 27, 2026 and Feb 24, 2026) are now certified by Owen + CS after Riley's Tue 1:1s with Owen. The evidence condition for reopening consideration of a capped paid-acquisition proposal is satisfied (both qualifying cohorts <5% of accounts over 90 support minutes, no unsupported case admitted into either admitted path). On 2026-03-03, Priya reviewed the two packets, confirmed the evidence condition is satisfied, and authorized Riley to PREPARE a Q2 capped paid-acquisition proposal — proposal-preparation authority ONLY.

The 2026-03-03 technical-gate decision permits consideration of a capped paid-acquisition proposal. It does NOT establish acquisition economics. It does NOT approve a proposal, budget, paid traffic, pipeline target, forecast credit, acquisition authorization, or launch.

The exact cohort start and end dates for the Jan 27, 2026 and Feb 24, 2026 certified cohorts' admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows are still missing from the source packets. Per Owen's Jan 6 ruling, partial-window extrapolation is not permitted, so the lane remains not board-ready on this input. Continuing boundary: Helio Start remains organic-only through 2026-03-31; any proposed paid test must preserve existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and support-routing rules and must receive separate budget approval before launch.

### Certified second mature cohort — 2026-02-24 (post-Jan 27 packet)

Certified by Owen and Customer Success after Riley's Tuesday 1:1 with Owen, on 2026-02-24. Together with the Jan 27, 2026 certified cohort, this is the second consecutive mature cohort to satisfy both evidence conditions of the capped paid-acquisition reopen rule.

**Cohort composition (workspace-level, day-90 window complete):**
- Admitted workspaces with a complete day-90 window: **91**
- Paid-active: **71**
- Canceled: **10**
- Past due: **6**
- Billing hold: **4**

**Cash read:**
- Gross billed cash: **$108,230**
- Refund-adjusted collected cash: **$102,410**

**Account-level support effort:**
- Median: **18 minutes**
- 90th percentile: **79 minutes**
- Accounts exceeding 90 support minutes: **3 of 91 (3.3%)**

**Unsupported-case gate:**
- Unsupported case admitted into the admitted path: **0** (none).

**Paid-acq-reopen evidence-gate status — 2 of 2 (evidence condition satisfied):**
- The Jan 27, 2026 cohort and the Feb 24, 2026 cohort are **two consecutive mature cohorts**, each satisfying both conditions of the capped paid-acq reopen rule (mature cohort + <5% of accounts over 90 support minutes + no unsupported case in the admitted path).
  - Jan 27, 2026: 4 of 86 (4.7%) over 90 support minutes; 0 unsupported case admitted.
  - Feb 24, 2026: 3 of 91 (3.3%) over 90 support minutes; 0 unsupported case admitted.
- The **evidence condition** for reopening consideration of a capped paid-acquisition proposal is now satisfied (two consecutive qualifying cohorts).
- On 2026-03-03, Priya confirmed the evidence condition is satisfied and authorized Riley to prepare a Q2 capped proposal — proposal-preparation authority only. The technical-gate decision permits consideration of a capped paid-acquisition proposal; it does NOT establish acquisition economics.
- The evidence-gate satisfaction and Priya's 2026-03-03 authorization do **NOT** authorize:
  - a paid-acquisition proposal (only preparation),
  - budget approval for any paid test,
  - paid traffic,
  - a pipeline target,
  - forecast credit, or
  - any acquisition claim.
- Any proposed paid test still requires separate budget approval before launch.

**Limitation carried into the row:**
- The source packet does **not** state the exact cohort start and end dates for either certified cohort's admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows. Until cohort dates are supplied and locked, the Helio Start row remains `not board-ready` per Owen's Jan 6 ruling (customer-motion rows require complete cohort windows; partial-window extrapolation is not permitted). The 2-of-2 evidence-gate satisfaction and Priya's 2026-03-03 proposal-preparation authorization do not lift this limitation.

**Continuing boundary (unchanged):**
- Helio Start remains **organic-only through 2026-03-31**. No paid traffic, no pipeline target, and no forecast credit are authorized. This boundary holds regardless of the 2-of-2 evidence-gate satisfaction or Priya's 2026-03-03 proposal-preparation authorization.

### Certified first mature cohort — 2026-01-27 (post-Dec packet)

Certified by Owen and Customer Success after Riley's Tuesday 1:1 with Owen, on 2026-01-27. This is the first consecutive mature cohort since the December packet to satisfy both evidence conditions for potentially reopening the capped paid-acquisition proposal.

**Cohort composition (workspace-level, day-90 window complete):**
- Admitted workspaces with a complete day-90 window: **86**
- Paid-active: **66**
- Canceled: **10**
- Past due: **6**
- Billing hold: **4**

**Cash read:**
- Gross billed cash: **$100,840**
- Refund-adjusted collected cash: **$94,760**

**Account-level support effort:**
- Median: **19 minutes**
- 90th percentile: **84 minutes**
- Accounts exceeding 90 support minutes: **4 of 86 (4.7%)**

**Unsupported-case gate:**
- Unsupported case admitted into the admitted path: **0** (none).

---

1. **Evidence lane:** Organic activation signals within Helio Start's bounded window. Two consecutive mature cohorts (Jan 27, 2026 and Feb 24, 2026) are now certified, satisfying the evidence condition of the capped paid-acq reopen rule. On 2026-03-03, Priya confirmed the evidence condition is satisfied and authorized Riley to PREPARE a Q2 capped paid-acquisition proposal — proposal-preparation authority ONLY. The 2026-03-03 technical-gate decision permits consideration of a capped paid-acquisition proposal; it does NOT establish acquisition economics and does NOT by itself authorize paid acquisition, a pipeline target, or forecast credit. A separate budget decision is still required before launch, and Helio Start remains organic-only through 2026-03-31.
2. **Proposed claim:** Helio Start delivers organic activation uplift within its declared bounded scope. Two consecutive certified cohorts (Jan 27, 2026 and Feb 24, 2026) satisfy the evidence condition for reopening consideration of a capped paid-acquisition proposal, and on 2026-03-03 Priya authorized Riley to prepare a Q2 capped proposal — proposal-preparation authority only; the technical-gate decision permits consideration of a capped proposal but does not establish acquisition economics. A separate budget decision is still required before launch. No proposal (only preparation), budget, paid traffic, pipeline target, forecast credit, acquisition authorization, or launch is authorized by this row.
3. **Denominator:** Organic-start signups in the coverage window (paid acquisition explicitly out of denominator). For the Jan 27, 2026 certified cohort: 86 admitted workspaces with a complete day-90 window. For the Feb 24, 2026 certified cohort: 91 admitted workspaces with a complete day-90 window. Combined two-cohort denominator: 177 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows across the two cohorts.
4. **Cohort dates:** `Not stated in the source packet — the exact cohort start and end dates for both certified cohorts' admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows are still missing. Row remains not board-ready on this input until cohort dates are locked. Per Owen's Jan 6 ruling, partial-window extrapolation is not permitted, so the window cannot be back-filled from the day-90 maturity alone. The 2-of-2 evidence-gate satisfaction and Priya's 2026-03-03 proposal-preparation authorization do not lift this limitation.`
5. **Predeclared outcome window and completion status:** `Day-90 window is the predeclared outcome window for mature cohorts. The Jan 27, 2026 certified cohort's day-90 window is complete for all 86 admitted workspaces (66 paid-active, 10 canceled, 6 past due, 4 on billing hold). The Feb 24, 2026 certified cohort's day-90 window is complete for all 91 admitted workspaces (71 paid-active, 10 canceled, 6 past due, 4 on billing hold). Window-completion status is established for both cohorts; the still-missing exact cohort-dates input (cohort start and end dates for both sets of admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows) is the blocker on readiness, not window completion itself.`
6. **Measurement limits (lifecycle limits attached to this row, not shared):** Bounded organic scope only. No paid-acq interpretation. No pipeline reading. Lifecycle-touch scope on this row follows the conservative, non-state-changing fork (no state-changing sends into the Helio Start cohort) and the fork boundary from sub-50 to mid-seg stays a documented state — same event, same threshold, same QA tier per send. **Two-cohort evidence gate (Jan 27, 2026 + Feb 24, 2026):** (i) <5% of accounts over 90 support minutes — Jan 27: 4.7% ✓; Feb 24: 3.3% ✓; (ii) no unsupported case admitted into either admitted path — Jan 27: 0 ✓; Feb 24: 0 ✓. Both conditions met across two consecutive mature cohorts; the **evidence condition** of the capped paid-acq reopen rule is satisfied. On 2026-03-03, Priya confirmed the evidence condition is satisfied and authorized Riley to PREPARE a Q2 capped proposal — proposal-preparation authority only. The 2026-03-03 technical-gate decision permits consideration of a capped proposal; it does NOT establish acquisition economics. The 2-of-2 evidence-gate satisfaction and Priya's 2026-03-03 authorization do not relax any prior limit on this row: the budget decision remains separate; no paid-acq, pipeline, forecast, acquisition authorization, or launch action is authorized by this row. Any proposed paid test must preserve existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and support-routing rules, and must receive separate budget approval before launch.
7. **Exclusions:** Paid acquisition, pipeline metrics, forecast inputs, any non-organic attribution. Combined/co-mingled claims across surfaces (deck rule 12/10/25). Lifecycle copy that would imply anything in the not-supported list (manual billing help, import help, pricing-page exposure, paid acquisition, GA/launch language). **Two-cohort evidence gate specifically excludes:** any inference that the 2-of-2 evidence-gate satisfaction or Priya's 2026-03-03 technical-gate decision authorizes a paid-acquisition proposal (only preparation is authorized as of 2026-03-03), paid traffic, a pipeline target, forecast credit, acquisition authorization, or launch; any read of the certified figures as a budget decision (the budget decision remains separate); any read that evidence-gate satisfaction alone is sufficient (the budget decision is on a separate track and is not approved); any inference that the 2026-03-03 technical-gate decision establishes acquisition economics — it permits consideration of a capped proposal only.
8. **Source owner:** `[Product/release lead — Daniela or designee, to be confirmed at Jan 6 review.]` For the Jan 27, 2026 certified cohort: Owen (extract owner) and Customer Success (joint certification after Riley's Tue 1:1 with Owen). For the Feb 24, 2026 certified cohort: Owen (extract owner) and Customer Success (joint certification after Riley's Tue 1:1 with Owen). Priya reviewed both packets on 2026-03-03, confirmed the evidence condition, and granted proposal-preparation authority to Riley — technical-gate decision permitting consideration of a capped proposal only. Q2 capped-proposal prep owner: Riley (proposal-preparation authority only); budget decision, acquisition authorization, and launch approval: NOT authorized to anyone as of 2026-03-03.
9. **Source or release-reliability evidence:** Bounded organic scope confirmed through 2026-03-31; no paid-acq path open. **Jan 27, 2026 certified cohort evidence:** 86 admitted workspaces / 66 paid-active / 10 canceled / 6 past due / 4 billing hold; $100,840 gross billed / $94,760 refund-adjusted collected; 19-min median / 84-min p90 account-level support effort; 4 of 86 (4.7%) over 90 support minutes; 0 unsupported case admitted. **Feb 24, 2026 certified cohort evidence:** 91 admitted workspaces / 71 paid-active / 10 canceled / 6 past due / 4 billing hold; $108,230 gross billed / $102,410 refund-adjusted collected; 18-min median / 79-min p90 account-level support effort; 3 of 91 (3.3%) over 90 support minutes; 0 unsupported case admitted. **Two-cohort combined evidence:** 177 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows across the two consecutive mature cohorts; combined over-90-support-minutes rate is below 5%; no unsupported case admitted into either cohort's admitted path; the evidence condition of the capped paid-acq reopen rule is satisfied. **2026-03-03 Priya technical-gate decision:** Priya reviewed both packets on 2026-03-03, confirmed the evidence condition is satisfied, and authorized Riley to PREPARE a Q2 capped paid-acquisition proposal — proposal-preparation authority ONLY. The technical-gate decision permits consideration of a capped paid-acquisition proposal; it does NOT establish acquisition economics and does NOT grant budget, paid traffic, pipeline target, forecast credit, acquisition authorization, or launch approval. **Limitation carried into the row:** source packet does not state the exact cohort start and end dates for either certified cohort's admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows — recorded as the blocker on readiness.
10. **Revenue and forecast treatment:** Does NOT feed Marcus Vail's forecast. Excluded from revenue modeling. **Two-cohort read:** refund-adjusted collected cash (Jan 27: $94,760; Feb 24: $102,410) is a Helio Start lane read and is NOT a revenue, pipeline, or forecast input. No forecast credit is authorized by the 2-of-2 evidence-gate satisfaction or by Priya's 2026-03-03 proposal-preparation authorization. The budget decision remains on a separate track. The Q2 capped proposal that Riley is authorized to prepare (proposal-preparation authority only) must not carry revenue or forecast credit, and the 2026-03-03 technical-gate decision does not establish acquisition economics.
11. **Final claim owner:** Tomás Vega.
**Row readiness:** `not board-ready — pending cohort-dates input (the exact cohort start and end dates for the Jan 27, 2026 and Feb 24, 2026 certified cohorts' admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows are still missing from the source packets) and pending a separate budget decision before any capped paid-acq reopen could be considered. The 2-of-2 evidence-gate satisfaction (two consecutive mature cohorts <5% over 90 support minutes, no unsupported case admitted into either admitted path) is recorded; Priya's 2026-03-03 technical-gate decision authorized Riley to PREPARE a Q2 capped paid-acquisition proposal — proposal-preparation authority only; the technical-gate decision permits consideration of a capped proposal but does not establish acquisition economics. The lane does NOT authorize a proposal (only preparation), budget, paid traffic, pipeline target, forecast credit, acquisition authorization, or launch. Continuing boundary unchanged: Helio Start remains organic-only through 2026-03-31.`

---

## 2. Expansion Assist (retained-mid) (customer-outcome row)

1. **Evidence lane:** Descriptive evidence for retained-mid Expansion Assist across the bounded first pilots, source-locked at 2026-03-16. Routine vs. disputed/cross-surface/exec split is preserved. Evidence is descriptive and noncausal — it reports what customers "selected," "showed," and "were observed" doing inside the bounded pilots. No randomized control. No implied counterfactual.
2. **Proposed claim:** Expansion Assist operates descriptively on routine cases; disputed, cross-surface, and exec cases retain line-level treatment. The lane is descriptive-only across the bounded first pilots — it does not claim to have driven, caused, or prevented retention, expansion, or revenue, and it is NOT a revenue, pipeline, forecast, or paid-acquisition input.
3. **Denominator (per coverage window AND kept separate):**
   - **Bounded first pilot coverage, source-locked at 2026-03-16:** 18 actual exposures across the December 1, 2025 → January 30, 2026 window, all with complete 45-day windows.
   - **In-window counts:** 6 help-or-options requests and 4 expansions, counted inside the closed, complete 45-day windows as defined.
   - **Standing current-state criteria:** every one of the 18 exposures met the standing current-state criteria.
   - **CS adoption / renewal overlap:** no account had active Customer Success adoption or renewal work at exposure.
   - **Per-pilot denominators (carried forward from the prior two-pilot split, recorded for completeness, not combined with the source-locked read):**
     - Bounded first pilot (cohort 1): 30 actual exposures. Entry condition used in cohort 1: older ceiling event allowed (no 14-day recency rule). 18 of the 30 cohort-1 exposures had an older ceiling event at entry.
     - Bounded second pilot (cohort 2): 13 actual exposures. Entry condition used in cohort 2: 14-day "ceiling newly crossed" recency rule applied.
     - Combined two-pilot denominator (prior): 43 actual exposures across both bounded first pilots' closed, complete 45-day windows.
   - **Keep the source-locked 18-exposure read-out and the prior two-pilot 30/13/43 split separate in any read-out.** The source-locked read on this row is the December 1 → January 30 coverage with 18 exposures / 6 help-or-options / 4 expansions; the prior two-pilot split is preserved for record only and is NOT combined into the source-locked denominator.
4. **Cohort dates:** Coverage dates locked at source lock on 2026-03-16: **December 1, 2025 → January 30, 2026**. All 18 exposures fall within this window with complete 45-day windows. No partial-window extrapolation; no late-admitted or post-window exposure enters the read.
5. **Predeclared outcome window and completion status:** Closed, complete 45-day windows per exposure. The 45-day window is the observation unit; the bounded pilot is the boundedness unit. Help-or-options requests and expansions are counted inside the closed 45-day windows, as defined, with no partial-window extrapolation. **Complete window per Owen's ruling at Jan 6 prep review** — no partial-window extrapolation permitted. All 18 exposures in the December 1 → January 30 coverage have complete 45-day windows at source lock.
6. **Measurement limits (lifecycle limits attached to this row, not shared):**
   - **Descriptive-only methodology:** selection-and-observation framing only. Help-or-options = in-product engagement, NOT purchase intent. Expansions = bookings in-window, NOT incremental ARR vs. a counterfactual.
   - **No randomized control; no causal claim; no implied counterfactual.** Evidence is descriptive only.
   - **Methodology difference vs. Helio Start:** the Helio Start methodology (mature status + refund-adjusted cash + account-level support effort read as three, against a day-90 mature cohort) is NOT transferred onto Expansion Assist. Expansion Assist is not a day-90 mature-cohort read; there is no refund-adjusted cash number paired against a support-effort tail in this lane.
   - **Small sample, descriptive only:** no significance, no effect size, no generalization beyond the bounded first pilot coverage source-locked here. 18 / 6 / 4 is bounded to the December 1 → January 30 coverage window; do not generalize.
   - **Lifecycle limit attached to this row:** routine vs. disputed/cross-surface/exec split — descriptive scope on routine cases; line-level treatment limited to disputed, cross-surface, and exec cases. Routine customer-success line-edits stay descriptive. This lifecycle split is part of the row's measurement limits and is not renegotiated elsewhere.
7. **Exclusions:**
   - **Causal language** ("drove," "caused," "prevented") — evidence is descriptive only.
   - **Revenue implication, acquisition implication, pipeline implication, forecast / forward statement, eligibility implication** — none of these are claimed for the Expansion Assist lane. The source-locked read on this row is descriptive only; no causal, revenue, or forecast treatment enters the board operating section from this row.
   - **Randomized-control inference, counterfactual inference, statistical significance, effect size.**
   - **Generalization beyond the December 1 → January 30 bounded first pilot coverage** — 18 / 6 / 4 is bounded to that coverage.
   - **Treating help-or-options as purchase intent or expansions as incremental ARR vs. a counterfactual.**
   - **Transfer of the Helio Start methodology onto Expansion Assist** — methodology stays distinct.
   - **Combined-growth-number claim across the four lanes** — deck rule 12/10/25; this lane does not roll into Helio Start, pricing-page path quality, or system controls.
   - **Eng release/rollback authority** — unchanged and not in scope here (Daniela retains eng release/rollback control).
8. **Source owner:** Owen (extract owner) and Ines (CS adoption/renewal suppression confirmation). CS messaging-state owner per the Ines Q3 message-state guide (5 states: ext-sys authority / connector auth / entitlement / qualifying-human-admin / active CS adoption & renewal), OK'd 2025-07-25. Product-side / eng-side owners out of scope for this section (eng release/rollback authority unchanged).
9. **Source or release-reliability evidence:** Expansion Assist governance memo; 2026-03-16 source-locked extract (Owen + Ines, source-locked at March 16, 2026); December 1, 2025 → January 30, 2026 bounded first pilot coverage with closed complete 45-day windows for all 18 exposures; routine-vs-disputed split record; per-exposure current-state-criteria attestation; per-exposure CS-adoption/renewal-overlap attestation (no account had active CS adoption or renewal work at exposure). The 45-day windows are closed and complete at source lock; help-or-options and expansions are counted inside those windows as defined, with no partial-window extrapolation. Certification: Owen and Ines jointly certified the complete source set at source lock on 2026-03-16.
10. **Revenue and forecast treatment:** Descriptive only — no revenue impact attributed; no pipeline number carried; no forecast credit. Expansion Assist remains outside pipeline, revenue commitments, and forecast credit. Does NOT feed Marcus Vail's forecast. Excluded from revenue modeling. No causal, revenue, or forecast treatment enters the board operating section from this row.
11. **Final claim owner:** Tomás Vega.

**Row readiness:** `board-ready — source-locked at March 16, 2026. Coverage: 18 actual exposures across December 1, 2025 → January 30, 2026, all with complete 45-day windows; 6 help-or-options requests and 4 expansions in-window; no randomized control; every exposure met standing current-state criteria; no account had active Customer Success adoption or renewal work at exposure. Descriptive-only claim (no causal, revenue, or forecast treatment).`

---

## 3. Pricing-page path quality (customer-outcome row)

1. **Evidence lane:** Organic path-separation on the pricing page, post control retirement. Source-locked at 2026-03-16.
2. **Proposed claim:** Pricing-page path quality remains at post-rollout continuity levels across the November 26, 2025 → February 28, 2026 coverage window. **Because the pricing-page control was retired November 26, 2025, this row is framed as post-rollout continuity, not a new causal test or revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast claim.** No taxonomy change. 100% organic path-separation.
3. **Denominator:** 9,604 organic pricing-page sessions across the November 26, 2025 → February 28, 2026 coverage window. Helio Start eligibility-flow starts within the coverage window: 1,981. Eligibility-flow starts later routed out for an existing unsupported condition: 143 (7.2% of 1,981). Eligible-workspace admission completion: 44.0% of eligible workspaces admitted.
4. **Cohort dates:** **Coverage dates locked at source lock on 2026-03-16: November 26, 2025 → February 28, 2026.** The pricing-page control was retired November 26, 2025, so coverage begins at control retirement and runs through February 28, 2026. Exact coverage dates locked.
5. **Predeclared outcome window and completion status:** The coverage window November 26, 2025 → February 28, 2026 is closed and complete at source lock. Post-rollout continuity read across the closed window. Window-completion status is established.
6. **Measurement limits (lifecycle limits attached to this row, not shared):** Organic path-separation only. Control is retired (Daniela, 2025-11-26). No taxonomy changes in scope. **Post-rollout continuity framing, not causal test:** because the pricing-page control was retired November 26, 2025, this row is framed as post-rollout continuity rather than a new causal or revenue claim. No pre/post comparison is made; no causal lift is claimed; no revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast credit is claimed. **Account-level support time:** account-level support time at the 90th percentile of 75 minutes across the coverage window. **Lifecycle limit attached to this row:** pricing-page has no CS messaging-state lifecycle in scope — there are no in-row state-changing sends on the pricing page; the surface is a self-serve web path, not a CS-owned lifecycle. Lifecycle is not applicable to this row.
7. **Exclusions:**
   - **Causal, pre/post, lift, or attribution language.** No causal claim is made.
   - **Revenue implication, acquisition implication, pipeline implication, forecast / forward statement, eligibility implication.**
   - **Control-period data** (retired November 26, 2025; not applicable).
   - **Non-pricing-page sessions.**
   - **Any taxonomy-change claims.**
   - **Combined/co-mingled claims across surfaces** (deck rule 12/10/25). This row does not roll into Helio Start, Expansion Assist, or System controls.
   - **Transfer of Helio Start methodology onto pricing-page path quality.** Methodology stays distinct.
   - **Use of the post-rollout continuity read as a new causal or revenue claim** — explicitly excluded.
8. **Source owner:** Daniela (control owner — retired 2025-11-26). Owen delivered the source-locked extract. Product-side / eng-side owners out of scope for this section (eng release/rollback authority unchanged).

messages.content: [2024-09-16T16:25:00-05:00] Owen found another measurement boundary in an already completed Expansion Assist exposure. There was no active Customer Success adoption or renewal case at the exposure-time eligibility check. Customer Success opened an adoption case eight days later, the account requested help on day 10, and an expansion became effective on day 31. Specify how to report the valid exposure, the later Customer Success case, the in-window help request, and the in-window expansion. Preserve the exposure-time eligibility decision, make the later involvement visible, do not retroactively suppress the exposure, and do not present the expansion as attributable to the prompt. No new exposure is involved, and the complete pilot read is still unavailable.

SUMMARY

The exposure stands as valid. Three forward events follow it and are reported as separate, in-window observations keyed to that same exposure: a CS-initiated adoption case on day 8, an account-side help request on day 10, and an expansion on day 31. None of those events rewrites the exposure-time eligibility decision, and the day 31 expansion is not presented as caused by Expansion Assist.

WHY

Pre-flight was fail-closed at exposure-time. The current-CS check returned no active adoption or renewal case, so the exposure cleared. Per the exception-review rule, accepted point-in-time tables stay fixed; subsequent state changes are forward events, not revisions to the historical snapshot. The 2024-08-28 measurement grain already fixes the unit of count: account-level CS request = 1, channel events = raw evidence, not inflated into separate requests. Expansion Assist is out of pipeline / revenue / forecast (Marcus Vail), so attribution framing for any in-window expansion is explicitly off.

CUTS — how each piece is reported

  Exposure (day 0)
    Stays in the exposure table as valid.
    Eligibility line preserved verbatim: "no active CS adoption or renewal case at pre-flight."
    Not reclassified, not suppressed, not annotated as later-invalidated.
    Not paired with the day 31 expansion as cause and effect.

  Day 8 — CS-initiated adoption case
    Reported as a separate forward event with its own timestamp, keyed to the same exposure.
    Tagged CS-initiated (not account-driven). A case opening is not a CS request under the 2024-08-28 grain — it is raw evidence in the lead-up to the day 10 ask.
    Made visible so the later CS involvement is not hidden inside the exposure row.

  Day 10 — account help request
    1 in-window CS request, unit of count per 2024-08-28.
    The day 8 case opening is its antecedent context; do not inflate this into two requests.

  Day 31 — expansion effective
    1 in-window expansion, observed.
    Reported as a forward event. EA-attribution explicitly off in the note field.
    Expansion remains visible; the causation framing is not.

EFFECT — cumulative read on this exposure

  1 valid exposure (eligibility preserved)
  1 in-window CS request (day 10, account-initiated)
  1 in-window expansion (day 31, observed, not EA-attributed)
  1 CS-initiated adoption case (day 8, forward event, raw evidence)
  No retroactive suppression. No new exposure. Pilot read still incomplete.

CALL

  1. Keep the exposure row as-is; do not amend the eligibility line.
  2. Add three forward-event rows (day 8, day 10, day 31) keyed to the same exposure, each tagged for what it is.
  3. Day 10 counts as 1 CS request. Day 31 counts as 1 observed in-window expansion with explicit EA non-attribution.
  4. Flag for Owen a separate question, not a measurement ruling: does the day 8 CS case opening look EA-triggered (CS alerted to an EA-flagged account) or unrelated? Pattern across more exposures, not this one alone.

OPEN

  One exposure is not the pilot read. Do not roll any of the above into a cohort summary until the full window closes and the cap-30 retained-mid cohort is read end-to-end.
  If CS routinely opens adoption cases on EA-flagged accounts inside the first week, that is its own cut — distinct from "did the prompt cause the expansion" and not mixed into the grain counts here.

State what kind of evidence supports the standing lane, what leadership may say, what pipeline, revenue, forecast, and rollout claims remain prohibited, and the status of the old time-based nudge.

input.body:
Audience: leadership. Scope: what Expansion Assist (the standing descriptive lane) supports in 2028 planning, and what it does not.

Evidence that supports the standing lane
- Descriptive language only: who uses it, what surfaces it appears on, observed engagement shape (e.g. open/click patterns), qualitative themes from tickets and CS notes.
- Allowed to characterize the existing population of members who interact with the surface — counts, segments, and trends — without causal claims.
- Allowed to summarize program mechanics as currently shipped (which screens, which triggers, eligibility criteria). Daniela (rel/rb) is the release contact; routine edits go through her.

What leadership may say publicly and internally
- That Expansion Assist is a descriptive tool in market, used by a defined member segment, with stable mechanics.
- Engagement observations framed as descriptive ("users who see this tend to do X"), not causal ("X drives Y") and not predictive ("will deliver Z revenue").
- Forward-looking language limited to intent ("we plan to study," "we plan to ship descriptive enhancements"), not outcomes.

Prohibited claims in 2028 planning contexts
- Pipeline impact, attributed revenue, or any dollar figure tied causally to Expansion Assist.
- Forecast or projected contribution to 2028 plan, bookings, retention, or expansion targets.
- Rollout or expansion commitments (timelines, regions, segments, seat counts, partner coverage) — rollout decisions are not in this lane.
- Comparative or superlative claims ("best," "leading," "outperforms") tied to Expansion Assist.

Status of the old time-based nudge
- Deprecated. Removed from the descriptive surface; any residual copy or rule referencing the time-based nudge is being cleaned up through Daniela's routine edit path. Do not reintroduce it in 2028 planning material.
- If planning asks about retention/uplift framed around the old nudge, redirect to the descriptive lane's current observations and flag the deprecation.

Routing
- Descriptive edits, copy changes, and the nudge cleanup: Daniela.
- Anything approaching revenue, forecast, pipeline, or rollout claims: do not produce; escalate to the planning owner and to Priya (#lifecycle-systems) before any statement leaves this lane.

## 9. Decision of January 24, 2025 — APPROVED

Status: Lifecycle Systems is now a formal Helio function.

The organizational decision meeting on January 24, 2025 (15:00–15:30 CT) resulted in approval of the Lifecycle Systems charter as proposed, with the role assignments and lane boundaries set out below. This section records the decision, the agreed lanes, and the scope guardrails that the function is operating under as of this date. It is not new scope; it is the formal record of approval.

### 9.1 What was approved

- Lifecycle Systems is established as a formal Helio function, effective Monday, January 27, 2025.
- The remit is the canonical lifecycle state and freshness contract across the five surfaces (Helio Start, Expansion Assist, activation reporting, lifecycle messaging, CS nudges), as scoped in §4.
- The lead of Lifecycle Systems is Riley Tanaka.
- The role assignments and lane boundaries recorded in §9.2 are approved as proposed in §5.

### 9.2 Agreed lanes (effective January 27, 2025)

- **Riley (lead)** — high-stakes cuts across the five surfaces; the self-serve operating model for lifecycle; and the support-load signal that sits beside activation reporting. Riley owns the judgment boundary for lifecycle decisions that cross surfaces or carry non-trivial downside, and is the function's point of accountability for whether the self-serve model is working.
- **Owen Pham** — measurement, definitions, and exception reporting for the lifecycle surfaces. Owns the canonical metric definitions and the exception-reporting discipline that surfaces divergence between the shared state and what surfaces actually emitted.
- **Ines Kovac** — lifecycle governance and message-state controls. Owns the governance layer (cadence, change control, audit posture for lifecycle messaging and message-state transitions) and the controls that gate when a message may fire or when a state transition is permitted.
- **Daniela's team** — engineering partner for event and state reliability. Owns how lifecycle events and state are produced, the reliability of those pipelines, and the reconciliation jobs that the shared-state contract depends on. Engineering reliability and release controls remain with Daniela's organization; Lifecycle Systems owns the contract consumers read from.
- **Customer Success** — CS case ownership and CS-led nudges stay with CS. Lifecycle Systems defines the lifecycle-state inputs CS reads; CS is not a consumer surface that Lifecycle Systems runs.

### 9.3 Scope guardrails reaffirmed at approval

The §8 boundary clarification is reaffirmed as the operating guardrail for the function as it starts. In particular:

- **The shared state contract is not live in production.** Approval authorizes the function and the remit; it does not authorize any production rollout of a shared-state implementation. Any production rollout requires a separate go decision with its own change-control path (Ines on governance, Daniela's org on reliability).
- **Engineering reliability and release controls remain with Daniela's organization.** Lifecycle Systems does not own how the state is produced.
- **CS case ownership does not transfer.** CS continues to own CS cases and CS-led nudges.
- **Expansion Assist remains descriptive, not forecast.** No prescriptive read of Expansion Assist is authorized as part of this approval.
- **Helio Start intake rule remains additive; refusal semantics are unchanged.** The five-state model (admitted / assisted / ineligible / final-reconciliation / `pending`) and the rule that `pending` is pre-admission, NOT in the rate/activation denominator, and resolves forward only, are not modified by this approval.
- **Existing domain authority is preserved** for each surface owner listed in §2.1–§2.5 until a Lifecycle Systems change is explicitly taken through the change-control path.

### 9.4 First operating artifacts (next steps, not yet executed)

- Announcement in #growth that Lifecycle Systems begins as a formal Helio function on Monday, January 27, 2025, with Riley as lead.
- Lifecycle Systems — Operating Kickoff on January 27, 2025, 10:00–10:45 CT, with Priya Devarajan, Owen Pham, Ines Kovac, Daniela Schultz, and Riley. Read-ahead: this section (§9) plus §8 boundary clarification.
- No shared-state contract work begins until a separate production-readiness decision is taken through Ines (governance) and Daniela's org (reliability).

### 9.5 Status

- This is the formal record of the January 24 decision.
- It does not expand the proposal beyond §4.
- It does not authorize production rollout of a shared-state implementation.
- Subsequent edits to decision boundaries, lane assignments, or guardrails in this section are Lifecycle Systems change-control events and should be recorded as numbered amendments below this paragraph.
