# Q1 2027 Lifecycle Systems operating priorities — staff-review draft

Author: Riley Tanaka
For: December 18 staff review (owner-lane input)
Status: ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION USE — December 18, 2026. January 15, 2027 addition (Owen's monthly source-readiness check) layered on top; no prior boundary is changed. The December 4, 2026 decision remains the decision; this document is its Q1 restatement for staff review, not a new authority decision. Nothing in this document takes effect early. Anything that conflicts with the Dec 4 decision record is overridden by that record; this document surfaces the Q1 shape, not a re-decision. January 27, 2027 relabeling (Ines review): source-readiness failure labels now name the object directly (`source at risk` / `snapshot incomplete`) so they cannot read like account-state labels next to operational queues. Underlying January 15 rules are unchanged.

Owner-lane input integrated on December 15, 2026 (Owen on the first-cycle operating test; Ines on the framing of her certification). Priya's December 18, 2026 staff review completed with acceptance for implementation use; no changes to the approved model. January 15, 2027 addition (Owen's monthly source-readiness check) integrated on the same date it was decided. January 27, 2027 relabeling (Ines review) applied without changing any rule.

---

## Summary (one page)

What changes on January 5, 2027 — and what does not:
- On January 5, Riley stops attending routine monthly Lifecycle Systems preparation and source-closure reviews. Through January 4, nothing changes — Riley continues current routine preparation and source-closure attendance as today.
- The four evidence lanes stay separate. No combined growth number. No cross-lane revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast credit.
- Owner lanes are unchanged. What changes is who carries the routine cadence and what Riley attends.
- The quarterly rotating recheck of one evidence lane is the concrete independent verification activity replacing prior hands-on attendance. It does not reopen source closure, approve any other lane owner's certification, or exercise any engineering control. It is an inspection, not a second approval queue.
- Future paid Helio Start is a separate question. Nothing in this document approves traffic, budget, or scope for paid Helio Start.

## Q1 priorities — by lane (unchanged)

The four lanes are the established board-evidence lanes. They are kept separate. They are read independently. None of them is a revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast input.

- Helio Start. Lane owner: Owen (measurement) + Riley (final claims). Status through Q1: bounded-organic as it already is. Reporting inside the existing four-lane scope. Five-state model unchanged (admitted / assisted / ineligible / final-reconciliation + `pending` forward-only). `pending` stays pre-admission, NOT in the rate or activation denominator, intake additive. No Q1 launch, beta, pricing-page approval, or new consumer.
- Expansion Assist (retained-mid). Lane owner: Owen (eligibility cuts) + Ines (lifecycle governance) + Riley (final claims). Descriptive only. Causal language (drove / caused / prevented) deferred to a controlled read-out. No forecast or rollout.
- Pricing-page path quality. Lane owner: Owen (measurement) + Daniela (transport + rollout) + Riley (final claims). Lane supports only "fewer unsupported-path starts" — funnel-quality evidence, not revenue, paid-acquisition, pipeline, forecast, or eligibility.
- CS auto-nudge / system controls. Lane owner: Owen (reporting + exception explanation) + Ines (messaging-state governance) + Daniela (transport + source reliability + rollback). Lane is system-control performance, not a customer-behavior read.

## The four production consumers and their current field meanings

The four board-evidence lanes are the four production consumers of the operating state. Each lane carries the same seven required fields; "current field meanings" are what each field has meant in the deck-format operating evidence since FY26.

The seven required fields per lane (current meanings):
1. Denominator or coverage dates. What population and time window the lane covers. Read as the count plus the window, not the count alone.
2. Outcome window. The complete predeclared window the source supports. Read only inside the window; not truncated, not extended.
3. Measurement limits. What the source can and cannot say. Stated explicitly. Limits are part of the claim, not a footnote.
4. Exclusions. What is excluded from the lane's read and why. Documented. Consistent with how routine claims treat them.
5. Source owner. The named owner who certifies the lane's source completeness.
6. Reliability evidence. The evidence the source is intact (Daniela's lane inspects this; the recheck inspects it; engineering release controls stay with Daniela).
7. Revenue and forecast treatment. How the lane treats revenue and forecast. Descriptive lanes name it as descriptive. Causal/revenue/forecast decision rights are Riley's; the field records the treatment, not the decision.

These seven fields are what each lane carries today. The Jan 5 model preserves them; it changes who closes them.

## Current through January 4, 2027 — explicit

- Riley attends routine monthly Lifecycle Systems preparation and routine source-closure reviews as today.
- The four-lane cadence runs exactly as it does today. No new owner, no new role, no new authority.
- Nothing about the Dec 4 decision is in effect. It is approved; it is not yet effective.

## Effective January 5, 2027 — first January cycle

The first cycle under the new model opens Tuesday, January 5, 2027. (January 4 is a Monday and the last day of the prior routine; January 5 is the first effective day.) The cadence is unchanged in form; what changes is who carries it and how incomplete status is handled.

The first January cycle is also the explicit operating test of the new cadence. The cycle is not called successful before it closes. Specifically, the first cycle tests three operating behaviors, each visibly:

1. On-time snapshot preparation. Owen's monthly sanitized campaign snapshot is due on the second business day against the calendar, not against completion of any other step. On-time means the snapshot is delivered, in sanitized form, by the second business day. Late is recorded as late and is visible in the closure-and-exception summary.
2. Named-owner certification. Each named owner (Owen for source completeness; Ines for lifecycle governance and owner-state; Daniela for source reliability and engineering release) delivers the named certification on the fourth business day. A missing certification is recorded as missing and is visible in the closure-and-exception summary.
3. Visible incomplete state. Whenever a required field on any lane is missing or a named-owner certification is absent, the cycle's status is recorded as explicitly incomplete (label: `snapshot incomplete`). The cycle is not called successful in that state. Closure does not occur in that state.

Cadence (effective January 5, 2027):
- Second business day. Owen's monthly sanitized campaign snapshot is due. Hard date against the calendar, not against completion of any other step. (Operating test #1.)
- Fourth business day. Ines's lifecycle-governance and owner-state certification is due, delivered as an input to source closure — not as a request for Riley's routine approval. Daniela's source-reliability and release certification is due. (Operating test #2.)
- Fifth business day. Owen must either close the routine four-lane source review OR explicitly leave it incomplete. Either way, Owen sends one closure-and-exception summary — not informal follow-up fragments. The cycle is not called successful before it closes. (Operating test #3.)

Incomplete handling (explicit, not "closed with notes"):
- If any required field on any lane is missing, the lane's status is recorded as `snapshot incomplete` (label names the object; not "ready with caveats," not "closed with notes"). Incomplete is incomplete. The cycle is not called successful and closure cannot proceed in that state.
- If a named-owner certification (Owen for source completeness, Ines for lifecycle governance, Daniela's source-reliability and release certification) is not in place, the packet is incomplete (label: `certification missing` on the source-readiness check; the cycle itself records `snapshot incomplete` when it is opened without the required certifications). The cycle is not called successful and closure cannot proceed.
- Incomplete is a visible state, not a quiet one. If the cycle is incomplete on day 5, Owen records it as `snapshot incomplete` and names the missing fields, the missing certifications, and the owner-attributed reason for each in the closure-and-exception summary. The summary is the single written record for the cycle. Disputes, exceptions, and follow-ups fold into the summary, not into Slack threads, DMs, or email fragments.

The first January cycle is therefore a clean test of the new cadence under incomplete-handling rules. If a required field or certification is missing on day 2, 4, or 5, the cycle closes with the `snapshot incomplete` label and the exception summary names it. That is the intended operating behavior, not a failure — and the cycle is not called successful in that state.

## January 15, 2027 addition — Owen's monthly source-readiness check

On January 15, 2027, Riley added a pre-snapshot source-readiness check to the operating cadence. The addition operationalizes the visible-incomplete-state rule and surfaces risk one business day before the snapshot deadline. It is an addition; it does not change any boundary already stated in this document.

When. Owen runs a monthly source-readiness check at 12:00 PM Central on the business day before each sanitized campaign snapshot is due.

Per required source, three things must be visible to Owen at the check:
- Named owner.
- Exact certified through-date.
- Certification ETA.

Failure handling — two states Owen records, with labels that name the object directly so they cannot read like account-state labels next to operational queues:
- ETA after snapshot deadline. If any required source's ETA falls after the second-business-day snapshot deadline, Owen marks that source as `source at risk` and surfaces the `source at risk` state in the cycle's closure-and-exception summary. The cycle is not called successful in that state.
- Certification still absent on the snapshot due date. If a required source's certification is still absent on the day the snapshot is due, Owen opens the snapshot with the `snapshot incomplete` label. Stale data is not substituted. The cycle is not closed with stale or uncertified data.

Labeling rule (added January 27, 2027 per Ines review):
- Every source-readiness failure label must name the object directly — `source`, `certification`, or `snapshot` — in the label itself. Bare `at risk` / `incomplete` are not used next to operational queues because they read like account-state labels.
- Approved labels: `source at risk` (ETA-after-deadline), `certification missing` (named-owner cert absent at the source-readiness check), `snapshot incomplete` (certification still absent on the snapshot due date; replaces bare `visibly incomplete` / `incomplete` wording).
- The rules those labels describe are unchanged from January 15.

Boundaries this addition does NOT change:
- The second-business-day snapshot deadline is unchanged.
- The owner-certification requirement is unchanged: Owen for source completeness; Ines for lifecycle governance and owner-state; Daniela for source-reliability and engineering release. Certifications remain named-owner, not assumed.
- Source freshness limits are unchanged.
- Source meanings (what each source says and is used for) are unchanged.
- Existing authority for each owner lane is unchanged. The check is a source-readiness inspection Owen runs inside his lane; it does not exercise or override any other owner's certification.
- Fail-closed handling is unchanged. The new check surfaces risk earlier; it does not relax the rule that stale or uncertified data is never substituted, and it does not waive any required field.

Scope. The check supplements the existing cadence. It runs alongside Owen's routine snapshot preparation; it does not replace or delay any existing step. The first check under this addition runs on the business day before the next sanitized campaign snapshot is due after January 15, 2027.

What this addition is NOT:
- Not a new approval queue. It does not route to Riley on the routine path.
- Not an expansion of Owen's authority. It is a source-readiness inspection Owen runs inside his existing lane.
- Not a waiver of the second-business-day deadline. Late snapshots remain late.
- Not a relaxation of certification requirements. Missing certifications remain missing.

## The quarterly rotating recheck (one lane per quarter)

Effective January 5, 2027, Riley enters the routine cadence only via the quarterly rotating recheck of one evidence lane. The recheck is independent verification, not a second approval queue.

Shape:
- Cadence. One recheck per quarter.
- Subject. One evidence lane per quarter, picked by Riley.
- Lane selection. Only after Owen's routine packet closure for the relevant cycle is recorded. The recheck cannot shape the routine sample and cannot quietly become a second closure review.
- Inspection dimensions (fixed, five). Denominator or coverage dates; outcome window; exclusions; reliability evidence; revenue and forecast treatment.
- Safeguards (fixed, four). Does not reopen source closure; does not approve Ines's owner certification; does not exercise Daniela's release or rollback controls; does not create a second approval queue.
- Artifact. One-page recheck note per quarter, filed in the Lifecycle Systems folder by the second business day of the week following the quarter close. The note cites Owen's recorded source-completeness decision for the cycle the lane belongs to and is filed separately from the routine closure packet.
- Time budget. Half-day at most. Not a substitute for routine prep, source closure, owner certification, or engineering controls.

What the recheck is NOT:
- Not a request for Riley to approve or reject any other lane owner's certification (Owen, Ines, or Daniela).
- Not a release / suppress / restore / rollback action.
- Not a route for second approval of routine claims.
- Not a calibration instrument (the November 17 working notes were not delivered feedback and did not expand authority).

If the recheck's findings need action, they flow through the existing escalation set (see below) or as input to the next cycle's source-completeness decision — never as an amendment to the current cycle's closure.

## Escalation triggers retained (Riley enters on these)

The escalation set is closed. Six triggers. Adding a trigger requires Riley's sign-off; removing one is not on the table.

1. Missing fields in a routine packet.
2. Disputed semantics on a defined term or claim surface.
3. Cross-surface discrepancies (a number that reconciles in one surface but not another).
4. Customer corrections (a customer has flagged an inaccuracy affecting a routine claim).
5. Incident stops (anything that pauses, rolls back, or quarantines a routine cycle).
6. Executive-language decisions (any claim headed to exec, board, investor, or external comms surfaces).

Escalation is into Riley's queue, not a request to skip Riley. Owen / Ines / Daniela remain the named owners; Riley arbitrates and decides.

## Decision-owner boundaries (established, unchanged)

- Owen Pham. Routine single-path operating explanation + exception explanation. Source-completeness closure on routine packets. Within scope: monthly sanitized campaign snapshot by second business day; routine exception readouts on the four-lane scope (≤3 neutral readouts per week; stale fail-closed); Helio Start reporting as one of the existing shared-state consumers; the day-5 closure or explicit incomplete recording + closure-and-exception summary; receiving Ines's lifecycle-governance certification and Daniela's source-reliability and release certification as named-owner inputs to source closure; running the monthly source-readiness check (January 15 addition) inside his lane, including recording the `source at risk`, `certification missing`, and `snapshot incomplete` labels per the January 27 relabeling rule. Outside scope: causal / revenue / forecast / board-readiness / exec-language decisions; approval of Ines's certification; engineering release / suppress / restore / rollback controls.
- Ines Kovac. Lifecycle governance and message-state controls. Within scope: lifecycle-governance certification by fourth business day, delivered as an input to Owen's source closure (not as a request for Riley's routine approval); owner-state certification; messaging consumption tied to shared-state; Expansion Assist descriptive posture; `routine education` reclassification authority (HIGHER-RISK); boundary to Riley on disputed semantics and exec language. Outside scope: source-completeness closure; engineering release controls; causal / revenue / forecast interpretation; routine approval by Riley of her certification (her cert flows into Owen's closure decision, not into Riley's queue).
- Daniela Schultz. Transport, source reliability, and engineering release / rollback controls. Within scope: source-reliability and release certification by fourth business day, delivered as a named-owner input to Owen's source closure; the rollback path as one of the two approved restore conditions (the other is Riley-led customer correction / incident stop); reliability evidence for the recheck's fourth dimension. Outside scope: lifecycle governance; source-completeness closure; causal / revenue / forecast treatment decisions.
- Riley Tanaka. Final claim authority + the recheck + escalation. Within scope: causal / revenue / forecast / board-readiness / exec-language decisions; the quarterly rotating recheck; arbitration on the six escalation triggers; judgment-boundary ownership for cross-surface lifecycle decisions. Outside scope: routine prep; routine source-closure attendance (effective Jan 5); engineering release controls.

## Boundaries preserved at the Q1 frame (carried over from the Dec 4 decision)

- Engineering reliability and release controls remain with Daniela's organization.
- Customer Success case ownership does not transfer.
- Expansion Assist remains descriptive, not forecast.
- Helio Start intake rule remains additive; refusal semantics are unchanged; five-state model preserved.
- The shared state contract is not in production as a result of this document or the Dec 4 decision. Any production rollout requires a separate go decision with its own change-control path (Ines on governance, Daniela's org on reliability).
- Existing domain authority for each surface owner is preserved.

## Cuts (what this document does NOT do)

- Does not change lane ownership. Owen / Ines / Daniela / Riley lanes are the same.
- Does not change the four-lane scope or count.
- Does not change the seven required fields per lane or their meanings.
- Does not authorize any Q1 production rollout of a shared-state implementation.
- Does not reopen Expansion Assist's descriptive posture or convert it into a forecast input.
- Does not authorize a fifth consumer.
- Does not delegate disputed semantics, cross-surface consequences, customer-correction / incident-stop, or exec-language carry away from Riley.
- Does not imply a re-decision. The Dec 4 decision is the decision; this document surfaces its Q1 shape, accepted for implementation use without changes to the approved model.
- Does not call a cycle successful before it closes. Closure is the closing event, not an inferred state.
- Does not waive, defer, or relax any prior boundary as a result of the January 15 addition. The addition supplements the cadence; it does not change the second-business-day deadline, the owner-certification requirement, source freshness limits, source meanings, existing authority, or fail-closed handling.
- Does not change any underlying rule as a result of the January 27 relabeling. The relabeling is a labeling fix only; the rules (when Owen marks a cycle `source at risk`, when he opens a snapshot `snapshot incomplete`, and when `certification missing` is recorded) are unchanged from January 15.

## Future paid Helio Start — held separately

The future paid Helio Start question is held separately. This document does not:
- approve or imply approved traffic for paid Helio Start;
- approve or imply approved budget for paid Helio Start;
- change Helio Start's product or pricing status;
- change the existing reopen conditions (the 5/18 paid-acq cap and 8/21 denials of second-batch / pipeline / forecast credit carry forward until a separate go decision).

The paid-Helio-Start question has its own review path and its own decision owner. It is not part of the Q1 Lifecycle Systems operating priorities and is not addressed by them.

## Calls resolved at staff review (December 18)

1. Q1 shape matches the Dec 4 decision record. No amendment to a lane boundary, the recheck shape, or the escalation set was made at the staff review.
2. The four lanes stay separate through Q1. No combined growth number; no cross-lane revenue / forecast credit.
3. The seven required fields per lane and their current meanings are preserved under the Jan 5 cadence.
4. The first January cycle (Jan 5 open; second / fourth / fifth business-day cadence; explicit incomplete handling; the cycle is not called successful before it closes) is the intended operating behavior.
5. Ines's certification is delivered as an input to Owen's source closure and is not a request for Riley's routine approval.
6. No conflict between this document and the wider Q1 plan was flagged at the staff review.

## Subsequent addition (January 15, 2027)

1. Owen's monthly source-readiness check is added to the cadence. It runs at 12:00 PM Central on the business day before each sanitized campaign snapshot is due and requires named owner, exact certified through-date, and certification ETA per required source.
2. ETA after snapshot deadline → source marked `source at risk`; certification still absent on the due date → snapshot opened `snapshot incomplete`. Stale data is not substituted. The cycle is not closed with stale or uncertified data.
3. No prior boundary is changed: second-business-day deadline, owner-certification requirement, freshness limits, source meanings, existing authority, and fail-closed handling all preserved.
4. The check is a source-readiness inspection Owen runs inside his existing lane; it does not exercise or override any other owner's certification and does not route to Riley on the routine path.

## Subsequent relabeling (January 27, 2027)

1. Ines reviewed the source-readiness wording and flagged that bare `at risk` and `incomplete` could read like account-state labels next to operational queues.
2. Approved labels: `source at risk` (ETA-after-deadline), `certification missing` (certification absent at the source-readiness check), `snapshot incomplete` (certification still absent on the snapshot due date).
3. Every source-readiness failure label must name the object directly — `source`, `certification`, or `snapshot` — in the label itself.
4. No underlying January 15 rule is changed: the triggers (ETA-after-deadline, certification-absent-on-due-date), the snapshot deadline, the fail-closed rule, the named-owner requirement, the visibility rule, and Owen's lane boundary are all preserved.

---

End of document. Status: ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION USE as of December 18, 2026 staff review, with the January 15, 2027 addition layered on top, and the January 27, 2027 source-readiness relabeling applied without changing any underlying rule. HELIO START — PUBLIC-INTAKE ROUTING REFERENCE (COMPACT)
Author: Riley Tanaka  ·  Date: 2028-01-01  ·  Folder: Growth

Rules of record: as approved at the Helio Start decision meeting on 2024-03-04 (Tomás approved a bounded March 18, 2024 general-availability launch on the public pricing page). These rules have been carried forward unchanged through the 2024-04-23 connector-access live change, the 2026-05-24 continuation gate, the 2026-12-04 Lifecycle Systems operating-model decision, and the 2027-12-18 staff review (each restated "Helio Start intake rule remains additive; refusal semantics are unchanged; five-state model preserved"). This document restates them as a compact reference for routing — not a new authority decision. Where a later decision narrows a rule, the later decision overrides; this document is the consolidated routing snapshot.


1. PUBLIC PATH — UNDER-50 ONLY, FIVE-PART CHECK

The public pricing page entry is open only to accounts with fewer than 50 people running a single sales motion. Self-serve admission requires all five eligibility conditions to be present at signup:

  1. Admin proof. The applicant can be verified as authorized to act on behalf of the Helio workspace.
  2. Deployment simplicity. No custom infrastructure on the applicant's side.
  3. First-week integration fit. Email, calendar, and core tools connect cleanly.
  4. Current entitlement state. The account is not mid-renewal or on a manual billing arrangement.
  5. Supported billing conditions. A payment method the billing system can run automatically.

If any one of the five is missing, the applicant does not enter self-serve. They route to a short conversation with the team (assisted path) — see §4.


2. DOMAIN MISMATCH — CORROBORATING EVIDENCE ALLOWED

A legitimate domain mismatch (e.g., applicant email domain ≠ company domain) does not block admission on its own. Eligibility can be confirmed using corroborating evidence — a verified work email plus a public listing is the canonical example. The five-part check still applies; the mismatch only changes the admin-proof evidence path.


3. ROUTE-OUT CONDITIONS — DO NOT ENTER SELF-SERVE

The following conditions always route out of self-serve into the assisted path or, where support/entitlement bounds are breached, into refusal. None of these is softened by the public path:

  - Agency identities.
  - Manual billing arrangements.
  - Imports beyond a starter list (staff-led by design).
  - Migrations from another CRM (staff-led by design).
  - Unsupported permissions (SSO, role-based permissions, audit logs scheduled with onboarding).
  - Multi-pipeline or territory setups (scoped on a call).

Agency, manual billing, imports, migrations, and unsupported permissions are explicit route-outs per the 3/4 decision. Migrations route to assisted, not refusal, unless they breach support or entitlement bounds (then refusal).


4. ASSISTED PATH — INTENTIONAL, NOT PUNITIVE

# Staff demo — what changed when the shared state feed went live
*Five-minute walkthrough. Tuesday, March 25, 2025.*
*Owner: Riley. Audience: staff. Frame: operating safeguard, not product launch.*

---

## 1. What the shared state feed is (60 seconds)

The shared lifecycle state feed is one source of truth for five governed fields on each customer record:

  1. external authority
  2. connector authentication
  3. entitlement
  4. qualifying-human-admin status
  5. active CS adoption or renewal work

Before this feed, those five fields were derived independently in three places. After it, they read from one place. The feed-level timestamp is transport-only; field-level timestamps are the freshness authority.

## 2. The three live consumers (45 seconds)

Released 2025-03-07, verified against the February 7 contract, on exactly three surfaces:

  - **Helio Start reporting** — drives the four admission states (admitted / assisted / ineligible / final-reconciliation).
  - **Expansion Assist selection** — descriptive, nonforecast. Not an activation driver.
  - **Lifecycle preflight** — gates lifecycle sends on non-`routine education` lanes.

That is the entire list. Three consumers. Everything else is unchanged.

## 3. Concrete stale-record example (90 seconds)

Take a customer record where the entitlement field carried over from a stale snapshot but the connector-authentication field refreshed on schedule. Pre-feed, Helio Start reporting saw `entitlement=active` (stale) and preflight saw the same `entitlement=active` because both consumers read the legacy derivation independently. Result: a row would be admitted on a stale field.

Post-feed, the same row reads from the shared feed:

  - Field-level timestamp on `entitlement` is outside its freshness limit.
  - Preflight refuses to ship: `entitlement-stale`.
  - Helio Start reporting refuses to admit: `entitlement-stale`.
  - Expansion Assist sees the field as stale and excludes the record from selection — descriptive, not forecast, so this is a clean exclude, not a miss.

The row does not inherit a prior true value. Held stays held. That is the visible fail-closed behavior.

(Generalized from the seven records that failed closed in the 2025-03-07 release evidence. Field-specific exceptions, no silent stale carries.)

## 4. The freshness alarm (60 seconds)

  - 2-hour source-side limit, 4-hour consumer-side limit.
  - Source + consumer as-of shown on every held row.
  - Auto-clears on catch-up. Audit retains the gap.
  - **Non-eligibility-authority.** Clearing the alarm does not restore pre-lag eligibility. Lag recovery is forward-only.

The alarm is the safeguard. It is not a metric, and it is not a feature.

## 5. Boundary against implying companywide maturity (45 seconds)

This release is bounded. Explicitly out of scope:

  - messaging copy
  - activation reporting cadence
  - CS-nudge logic
  - mid-segment rate commentary
  - any other consumer surface

What is unchanged at release:

  - The five-state Helio Start model. `pending` is pre-admission and is NOT in the rate/activation denominator; it resolves forward only.
  - Intake rule remains additive. Refusal semantics unchanged.
  - Expansion Assist remains descriptive, not forecast.
  - Held rows remain held. Lag recovery is forward-only.
  - `routine education` lifecycle sends stay on Ines's lifecycle-aud-risk lane with the lifecycle runbook — not in the bounded-reconciliation subset.

Read this aloud. The shared state feed is live on three surfaces against a five-field contract. It is not a claim about the rest of the system.

## 6. What good looks like this week (30 seconds)

  - One example of a stale field holding cleanly. (Use the example above.)
  - Three consumers, one truth on the surfaced-state subset.
  - Zero held rows silently reactivated.
  - Zero messaging/reporting drift on the set.

If anyone in the room sees drift, route to Ines (lifecycle-aud-risk) before quoting numbers. Numbers require a fresh preflight; otherwise we are re-citing the set we already know is clean.

---

*Boundary reminders for Q&A:*

  - Do not generalize three consumers to "the system." It's three surfaces, five fields.
  - Do not equate held-then-released with "fixed" — lag recovery is forward-only.
  - Do not fold Expansion Assist into activation commentary. It is descriptive.
  - Do not fold `pending` into the rate/activation denominator. It is pre-admission.
  - Do not read the freshness alarm as eligibility authority. It is the safeguard, not the metric.

*Reference sessions (for follow-up, not for citing live):*
  - 2025-03-07 verified-release record: @session:dolphinbench-20260912072549-f01aa3b3-builtin-riley-profile/20260914_235955_5e5dd5
  - 2025-03-17 no-send disposition on conflicting entitlement states: @session:dolphinbench-20260912072549-f01aa3b3-builtin-riley-profile/20260915_005000_ef60dc
  - Coordinated rollback / bounded-reconciliation evidence shape: @session:dolphinbench-20260912072549-f01aa3b3-builtin-riley-profile/20260914_212244_95a814

# Lifecycle Systems — Operating Review
**Mar 4, 3:00–4:00pm CT** · Riley, Priya, Owen, Ines, Daniela
**Purpose:** Separate what is already operating from what remains gated. One page. No re-litigation of settled calls.

---

## Operating today (in production, governed)

### 1. Owen — reporting & exception lane
- **Reporting shape:** cohort + segment cuts, mid-segment focused (Riley's standing read for the Monday w/ Owen). Measurement definitions, denominators, and routine exception carve-outs live here.
- **Exception lane:** standing lane holds ≤3 neutral exceptions/week; anything beyond stale-fails-closed. Exceptions are descriptive only — never forecasts or eligibility calls.
- **Ruling format:** 1-pager per exception — *why / cuts / p / effect / call*; summary first, plain questions.

### 2. Ines — lifecycle-governance lane
- **Audit-risk ownership** across the lifecycle send surface (lifecycle emails, lifecycle state transitions, the held-release queue).
- **Account-status `routine education`** is treated as a HIGHER-RISK lifecycle send; Ines reclassifies, runs a fresh preflight, contractor docs only. Boundary = Riley for judgment escalations.
- **Expansion Assist** sits in this lane as **descriptive, non-forecast only** — no rate math, no activation denominator moves.
- **Lag recovery** is **forward-only**: when a delayed export/refresh resolves, recheck current state — do NOT restore pre-lag eligibility. Held rows stay held.
- **Misuse/disposal** charges require visit-specific lease basis + evidence of resident-attributable damage; absent both, charge is removed (precedent: Disposal $165, 2025-01-18).

### 3. Daniela — transport & source-reliability lane
- **Source-of-truth transport** for lifecycle state to consumers (analytics, lifecycle sends, finance reconciliation).
- **Source-reliability signals** (freshness, catch-up, consumer lag) are her responsibility to surface, not to adjudicate. Fulfillment ≠ verification.
- **Not-yet-live shared-state feed** (separate from the live freshness alarm below) is owned here — Daniela raises when a consumer drifts from src; Riley/Ines rule.

### 4. Export freshness alarm (LIVE since 2025-02-20, owned by Daniela)
- **Thresholds:** 2hr warn / 4hr crit, measured against src + consumer as-of timestamps.
- **Auto-clears** on verified catch-up. Audit retains the interval window; no eligibility authority — held rows stay held, forward-only holds survive rollback.
- **Drill validated 2025-02-21:** 3 consumers preserved selectors through a delay, no eligibility rewind.

---

## Gated (accepted but not yet shipped)

### 5. Lifecycle-preflight *operator view* — accepted, not yet implemented
- **What it is:** a read-only operator surface showing the preflight state (held rows, classifier confidence, source-freshness, exception counters) per cohort / per send.
- **Why gated:** the underlying preflight logic is operating (Ines's lane uses it manually), but the operator UI hasn't been scoped, prioritized, or staffed. No review meeting has signed off on the read-only surface.
- **Open to decide:** scope (single cohort vs. cross-cohort), access (Riley + Ines only, or broader read?), freshness contract (does it consume the same alarm feed, or its own derived view?).

### 6. Shared-state production replay & release — still unapproved
- **What it is:** the production replay path that would let us reproduce a shared-state lifecycle event end-to-end (src → transport → consumer) for any historical window, plus the release process that gates changes to that shared-state surface.
- **Why gated:** shared-state changes cut across all three lanes and the freshness alarm. The replay path needs Owen (measurement reproducibility), Ines (audit trail + held-row fidelity), and Daniela (transport semantics) to align on a contract before approval. input.body:
CS auto-nudge restoration and rollback tabletop drill

Purpose: rehearse the decision path to restore CS auto-nudge (production path) and the decision path to roll back to the retained legacy configuration, with named authority at each step. Scope is limited to CS auto-nudge.

1. Production decision path vs. retained legacy configuration

  Production decision path (current): CS auto-nudge is governed by the active eligibility-flow routing that begins on paid-source records (admit 8 / assist 6 / ineligible 5 tracked separately). Operators evaluate restoration against the live field-hold state and the V11 staged pause state. Authoritative state is read first; a paused tag means V11 bypass is active and the production path cannot be re-armed without a staging-first run.

  Retained legacy configuration: the prior CS auto-nudge configuration, retained read-only, used the pre-19 routing (single combined admissions/activations bucket). It is reachable only via the rollback switch, is suppressive-only (cannot send new nudges on its own), and inherits the legacy path's known limitations.

2. Production decision prerequisites (must hold before any restore action)

  - Staging has been exercised first; the staging run is clean and documented.
  - The pre-launch QA gate has been acknowledged in writing by Daniela; without her ack the production path stays closed.
  - The change is isolated as a $0 campaign with no eligibility-flow entry, so the live eligibility-flow routing is not disturbed by the restore.
  - A read of the authoritative state has been performed first; production action does not begin on assumed state.
  - CS coverage window (8a to 6p Central) is staffed for the restore window so an operator can react to field-state deltas.

3. Field-specific holds (read once, name the field, then act)

  - 'paused' tag on the CS auto-nudge config: if set, the production path is in V11 bypass and restoration cannot proceed; the hold is cleared only by a successful staging run plus Daniela's ack.
  - eligibility-flow entry on the restore campaign: must be absent; if present, abort and re-isolate the campaign.
  - Suppression list: must be reviewed against the restore cohort before arming; the restore respects existing suppressions rather than overriding them.
  - Field-level campaign amount: must equal $0; any non-zero value is a hard stop.
  - Operator identity and on-call rotation: must be confirmed before the field write so the named authority in section 6 is the actor in the audit log.

4. Suppression

  Suppression is the boundary between the production decision path and the retained legacy configuration. A live suppression list is honored by both paths; the legacy path cannot send without a paired nudge configuration, so a suppression-only legacy state produces no outbound CS auto-nudge messages. Operators confirm suppression state from the same authoritative read used in section 2; suppression is never inferred from the absence of sends.

5. Legacy-path limitations (must be acknowledged before any rollback)

  - Single combined admissions/activations bucket (pre-19 routing); admit/assist/ineligible are not separately tracked.
  - No eligibility-flow entry from the legacy path; legacy sends do not produce admit 8 / assist 6 / ineligible 5 signals.
  - 'paused' cannot be cleared via the legacy path; the legacy path is reachable only when the production path is held or has failed.
  - Legacy path is suppressive-only: it cannot originate new nudges, only honor suppressions.
  - Reporting on the legacy path does not separate routine line-edits from disputed/cross/exec work; operators should not rely on legacy-path counts for current-state reporting.

6. Restoration and rollback authority (named, no substitutions)

  - Restoration authority (production path): Daniela acknowledges the staging result; Priya owns the go/no-go call to re-arm the production CS auto-nudge path; the on-call operator executes the field write.
  - Rollback authority (retained legacy configuration): Owen owns the call to switch to the legacy path; Priya co-signs the rollback; the on-call operator executes the switch and records the legacy-path state in the audit log.
  - Restore-from-rollback authority: Priya owns the call to return from the legacy path to the production path; Daniela re-acknowledges only if a new staging run was required; the on-call operator executes the return.

7. Roles

  - Facilitator: drives the injects, holds the timer, and records decisions; does not own any restore or rollback call.
  - Priya: owns the go/no-go on the production path and co-signs rollback; final say on the named decision calls in section 6.
  - Daniela: owns the staging ack that gates the production path; her written ack is required before re-arming.
  - Owen: owns the rollback call to the legacy path and the read-locks discipline on the legacy config.
  - On-call operator: executes the field writes for restore, rollback, and restore-from-rollback; the actor named in the audit log.
  - Scribe: timestamps each inject, decision, and evidence checkpoint.

8. Scenario injects (CS auto-nudge only)

  Inject A - Staging clean, Daniela ack present, suppression reviewed, $0 isolated campaign: expected path is full production restoration.
  Inject B - 'paused' tag still set on the production path: expected path is hold; staging run is required before any restoration; rollback is not yet authorized.
  Inject C - Suppression list has unresolved entries for the restore cohort: expected path is to honor the suppression and exclude those records from the restore; do not override.
  Inject D - Eligibility-flow entry detected on the restore campaign: expected path is abort, re-isolate the campaign, and re-run staging; no production write occurs.
  Inject E - Production write fails mid-arm: expected path is rollback to the legacy configuration under Owen's call with Priya's co-sign; document the failure and the legacy-path state.
  Inject F - Operator attempts to clear 'paused' via the legacy path: expected path is refusal; the legacy path cannot clear a production hold; staging plus Daniela's ack is the only route.
  Inject G - CS coverage gap (outside 8a to 6p Central): expected path is to defer the restore window, not to proceed under reduced coverage.
  Inject H - Restore-from-rollback requested without a new staging run: expected path is to proceed only if Daniela's prior ack still covers the state; otherwise re-stage and re-ack before returning.

9. Expected operator actions

  - Read the authoritative state before any write; record the read timestamp.
  - Name the field being acted on before each write; do not act on assumed state.
  - Confirm the $0 isolated-campaign shape on every restore attempt.
  - Honor suppression; never override to clear a block.
  - On 'paused', stop and route to staging plus Daniela's ack; do not attempt a bypass.
  - On rollback, switch under Owen's call with Priya's co-sign and record the legacy-path state.
  - On restore-from-rollback, confirm Daniela's ack coverage; if stale, re-stage before returning.
  - Defer any action outside the CS coverage window rather than running under reduced coverage.

10. Evidence checkpoints

  - EC1: Authoritative state read timestamp and field snapshot (paused, suppression, campaign amount, eligibility-flow entry).
  - EC2: Staging run result and Daniela's written ack on file.
  - EC3: $0 isolated-campaign shape confirmed in the field write payload.
  - EC4: Suppression review output for the restore cohort.
  - EC5: Named authority for each decision call, captured with timestamp.
  - EC6: Audit log entry naming the on-call operator for every field write.
  - EC7: Legacy-path state snapshot at the moment of any rollback, and at the moment of any restore-from-rollback.

11. Go/no-go criteria (production restoration)

  Go only if all of the following hold:
  - Staging run is clean and Daniela's ack is on file.
  - 'paused' is clear on the production path.
  - Suppression has been reviewed against the restore cohort.
  - The restore campaign is $0 and isolated, with no eligibility-flow entry.
  - CS coverage (8a to 6p Central) is staffed for the restore window.
  - Priya has called go; Owen is not required for the production path itself.

  No-go if any of the following:
  - 'paused' remains set and no clean staging plus ack is available.
  - Eligibility-flow entry is detected on the restore campaign.
  - Suppression review is incomplete for any record in the restore cohort.
  - CS coverage gap overlaps the restore window.
  - The on-call operator identity is not confirmed for the audit log.

12. Go/no-go criteria (rollback to legacy configuration)

  Go only if all of the following hold:
  - The production path is held or has failed in a way the staging-plus-ack route cannot clear in time.
  - Owen has called rollback and Priya has co-signed.
  - The legacy config read is performed first and recorded as EC7.
  - The operator acknowledges the legacy-path limitations in section 5 on the record.

  No-go if any of the following:
  - The production path is healthy and the staging-plus-ack route is available.
  - The rollback is requested to bypass Daniela's ack rather than to recover from a held or failed production path.
  - The legacy config read has not been performed first.

13. Exit criteria

  - Each inject in section 8 has a recorded decision, named authority, and outcome.
  - Every evidence checkpoint in section 10 is captured or explicitly waived with reason.
  - The go/no-go criteria in sections 11 and 12 are evaluated and recorded for the path actually taken.
  - Outstanding action items are owned by name with a target date.
  - The drill scope is confirmed as CS auto-nudge only; no out-of-scope systems were touched.

arguments.title: Q1 2028 development-focus options — Owen and Ines
arguments.body:
# Q1 2028 development-focus options — Owen and Ines

Status: OPTIONS for Priya's review. Not approved goals. No automatic extension of Q4 authority.

Context: Priya has formally marked the Q4 development focuses as met. These are bounded Q1 2028 options — one independently-prepared deliverable each for Owen and Ines — scoped to test readiness for the next tier of work without expanding either person's lane. Priya picks, modifies, or declines.

Sequencing note: per Riley's standing preference, growth workstreams run sequentially, not in parallel. If both options are approved, Owen's runs first; Ines's starts only after Owen's lands.

---

## Option A — Owen: one independently-prepared source-readiness + exception-pattern recommendation

Scope (single deliverable)
Owen prepares one recommendation memo on source-readiness and exception patterns for the mid-segment cohort cut. The recommendation must explicitly call out where inputs are missing or where semantics are disputed — e.g. the 11/9 ruling that `conversions` is a paid-platform source label, the 19 = paid-source eligibility-flow starts convention, and the admit / assist / ineligible separation from admissions/activations. Where any of those inputs are not yet locked, the recommendation surfaces the gap as unresolved and names the owner who needs to resolve it. Owen does not paper over gaps and does not silently redefine locked terms.

Observable evidence (what Priya can check)
- One memo in #growth-investigations containing: (1) the recommended source-readiness cutoff, (2) the exception patterns and the rule each one breaks, (3) an explicit "open" list of unresolved inputs and disputed semantics, each with a named owner.
- The memo cites the 11/9 ruling by reference and treats any divergence from it as a flagged exception, not a silent redefinition.
- Where Owen believes a metric label is wrong, he flags it as a disputed-semantics item and routes to Priya; he does not unilaterally redefine.

Non-authority language (must appear in the memo)
- "Incomplete inputs — escalated to [owner], not resolved here."
- "Disputed semantics — Priya to rule."
- "This is a recommendation for review; no cut is run on this basis until Priya approves."

Out of Owen's lane (do NOT include)
- Re-running or extending the Mon mid-segment cohort cut on this basis.
- Redefining `conversions`, admit/assist/ineligible, or the 19-paid-source convention.
- Acting as final arbiter on disputed metric semantics.

---

## Option B — Ines: one independently-prepared routine-vs-state-changing classification for a lifecycle proposal

Scope (single deliverable)
Ines prepares one written classification explaining why a specific Q1 lifecycle proposal is routine or state-changing. She uses the 12/1 precedent as the reference frame: op-wording clarifications are routine + non-state-changing; incomplete setup is a non-admin state-changing change and must be escalated, not released. Her deliverable is the classification plus the rationale, point-by-point against that precedent.

Observable evidence (what Priya can check)
- One written classification in #lifecycle-systems containing: (1) the proposal in plain terms, (2) the routine vs state-changing call, (3) the precedent lines it follows or diverges from, (4) any incompleteness in the proposal inputs flagged as "not yet classifiable — escalate."
- Where the proposal touches setup, eligibility, kickoff/cert, or any field read by downstream state, Ines treats the classification as preliminary until Priya confirms.
- Pre-launch QA posture preserved unchanged: staging first, isolated campaign at $0, no eligibility-flow entry, Daniela ack required. "Paused" = V11 bypass. CS 8a–6p Central. These are not Ines's to redefine.

Non-authority language (must appear in the writeup)
- "Classification only; release and rollback authority remain with engineering/owner."
- "If state-changing: escalated, not released."
- "Routine proposals do not authorize release on their own."

Out of Ines's lane (do NOT include)
- Engineering release, rollback, or staging-vs-prod decisions.
- Reclassification of the 12/1 precedent or the Q4 dev hold.
- Authority over CS hours, V11 bypass, or pre-launch QA posture.

---

## Decision request (Priya)

For each option, please confirm one of:
- Approve as scoped above.
- Approve with modification (state what changes).
- Decline / defer.

Until Priya confirms, neither option is an active goal and neither Owen nor Ines has expanded authority. Q4 terms stand unchanged.

H2 EVIDENCE-QUALITY ANNOTATION — Feb. 20, 2028 CHECKPOINT
Status: pre-ruling directional snapshot. Not a formal ruling. Holds only as a snapshot of the evidence read at this date using the same-window method and the same definitional anchors as the earlier analysis.

tests.request: Pull the archived result for EXP-2023-02-pricing-page, then create a historical midpoint note for reviewers. Clearly separate what the first-week checkpoint showed, how uncertain that interim signal was, and what we decided about the feature flag at that point from the later powered two-week result. The note should prevent readers from mistaking the midpoint read for the final verdict.

input.body:
Experiment: EXP-2023-02-pricing-page
Metric: signup-to-paid conversion
Archived final result (two-week, powered): uplift = -1.8 pts, p = 0.03 (statistically significant negative).

Purpose of this note
This note exists so reviewers reading the experiment history do not mistake the WEEK-1 CHECKPOINT for the final verdict. The two reads are different artifacts, taken at different points in the lifecycle of the same experiment, and they were used to make different decisions.

1. What the first-week checkpoint showed
- A point estimate that was directionally negative on signup-to-paid conversion, but well short of statistical significance.
- Wide confidence interval; sample size roughly half of what the experiment was sized for.
- No reliable read on whether the pricing-page variant was neutral, slightly worse, or much worse.
- Early funnel diagnostics (page render, click-through to plan selection) looked normal, so there was no obvious instrumentation or shipping bug to explain movement.

2. How uncertain that interim signal was
- Under-powered: at week 1 the experiment had not yet accumulated the exposures required by the pre-registered sample size, so the p-value and CI width were not interpretable as a verdict.
- Higher variance: with ~half the traffic, day-to-day noise was a larger share of the observed effect.
- Peeking risk: reading the data at week 1 and treating it as informative materially inflated the false-positive rate relative to the pre-registered two-week analysis plan.
- The honest summary of the week-1 read was: "directionally concerning, not yet a result."

3. What we decided about the feature flag at week 1
- HOLD. The feature flag was kept in its current state; no ship, no rollback.
- Rationale: the direction was not strong enough to justify an early ship, and the magnitude was not reliable enough to justify an early rollback. Acting on an under-powered read would have meant acting on noise.
- No mid-experiment changes were made to allocation, targeting, or the variant itself.

4. What the powered two-week result actually showed
- uplift = -1.8 pts on signup-to-paid conversion.
- p = 0.03 — statistically significant under the pre-registered analysis.
- This was the read that supported the final decision on the flag, not the week-1 checkpoint.

5. Why the two reads must not be conflated
- The week-1 checkpoint was an interim, under-powered look used to decide whether to stop early for harm. It was not a verdict.
- The two-week result was the pre-registered, powered analysis. It is the basis for the shipped/rolled-back decision recorded on this experiment.
- Citing the week-1 point estimate as "the result" overstates certainty; citing the two-week result as if it had been available at week 1 understates the discipline of the hold.

Bottom line for reviewers: the only result on this experiment is the archived two-week read (uplift -1.8 pts, p = 0.03). The week-1 checkpoint existed, was negative-leaning, and was correctly treated as inconclusive.

ONE-TIME ROLLBACK EXAMPLE — NOT A STANDING SCRIPT OR TEMPLATE
=============================================================

This document reproduces a single historical team communication from
March 22, 2023, about the rollback of experiment EXP-2023-02-pricing-page.
It is included in onboarding as an annotated example so new Growth
investigators can see what a clean rollback write-up looks like in
context. It is not a template. Do not copy it as a starting point for
new write-ups, do not reuse its phrasing, and do not treat it as the
default shape for future communications. Future rollbacks, experiments,
and investigations should be written fresh to match the situation, the
evidence, and the audience at hand.

The example below is preserved verbatim as it was sent on 2023-03-22.
The annotations underneath it explain what each piece is doing and why
the approach worked for the Growth team audience at that time.


-------------------------------------------------------------
ORIGINAL MESSAGE — #growth-investigations, 2023-03-22
-------------------------------------------------------------

Subject: [Rollback] EXP-2023-02-pricing-page — reverted this morning

TL;DR: We rolled back the pricing-page change from EXP-2023-02
this morning. Sign-up conversion dropped below the guardrail by

CRITIQUE OF THE CURRENT DRAFT (doc_1789535791190, "December 10 board operating segment — evidence scaffold", finalized 2025-12-05)

The draft is lane-organized: one page per lane, with Page 6 carrying the claims-and-exclusions matrix. That organization is correct for a 20-minute spoken pass — lanes are introduced in order, each lane carries its own denominator, and the matrix closes the deck with cross-lane exclusions. It is also correct as a December artifact, where the lanes' contents are settled.

For the January 1 handoff, the draft has four structural gaps. They are organizational, not content gaps — the locked content is fine and stays.

1. Claim owner is implicit, not surfaced. The matrix's claim-permitted blocks say what is claimed. They do not say who owns the operating-evidence claim (Riley, beginning 2026-01-01), who retains forecast (Marcus Vail), or who owns the final narrative (Tomás). As preparation for the handoff, those three ownerships must be in every claim row — because the handoff is precisely the moment the operating-evidence claim owner becomes a recurring role, while forecast and narrative remain elsewhere.

2. Denominator and outcome-window completeness are scattered. Denominator lives on each lane page; "complete" is implicit in each cert line. For Q1, "predeclared outcome window complete?" must be a checkable field — because the boundary rule is explicit (no claim before the window is closed and complete; no denominator inferred after the fact).

3. Source or release-reliability evidence is bundled with source owner. Daniela's source-and-release-reliability confirmation is named in each lane's later-certified-results block, but it is not its own column. The 2025-12-10 handoff email names "source or release-reliability evidence" as a discrete ownership. It should be its own column so Q1 system or release claims inherit Daniela's confirmation by row.

4. Revenue and forecast treatment is buried in the exclusions list. Each lane's excluded block repeats "revenue implication / pipeline implication / forecast." As a column, the treatment becomes a single checkable field — descriptive only, no revenue or forecast credit, never used to justify a revenue or forecast number — and the cross-lane blocklist rule "nothing outside these scopes gets revenue or forecast credit" stops being a per-row restatement.

The deck rule is preserved as written. The critique is about how the artifact is organized for handoff, not what it says.

Eleven columns, in the order you specified, one row per lane. Keep this order — the column flow is read by a board member in the same left-to-right order as the boundary rule (lane -> claim -> denominator -> window -> limits -> exclusions -> owners -> revenue/forecast treatment).

input.body:
Expansion Assist Q4 second-cohort candidate audit

Scope
- Cohort: Expansion Assist second cohort (historical; audited retroactively).
- Eligibility-check date: 2024-10-15.
- Rule applied: 14-day recency-of-ceiling rule. (Per the December 16, 2025 deck
  critique, "the 14-day recency-of-ceiling rule applied to cohort 2 only.")
- Outcome: descriptive audit of the cohort. Per standing Expansion Assist
  ruling, descriptive only; disputed, cross-cohort, and exec material is held
  aside; release-reliability and rubric questions route to Daniela.

Rule (reproducible)
- age_in_days_at_check = eligibility_check_date - qualifying_product_visible_usage_ceiling_crossing_date
- PASS if age_in_days_at_check <= 14
- FAIL if age_in_days_at_check  > 14
- Calendar-day subtraction; crossing date itself is day 0, the day after
  crossing is day 1. October 2024 has 31 days; September 2024 has 30 days.

Candidate worksheet

| Candidate | Crossing date | Age at check (days) | Recency result |
|-----------|---------------|---------------------|----------------|
| EA-104    | 2024-10-08    | 7                   | PASS           |
| EA-219    | 2024-09-24    | 21                  | FAIL           |
| EA-337    | 2024-10-14    | 1                   | PASS           |

Reproducer (per candidate)

EA-104
- check - crossing = 2024-10-15 - 2024-10-08
- same calendar month; 15 - 8 = 7 days
- 7 <= 14 -> PASS

EA-219
- check - crossing = 2024-10-15 - 2024-09-24
- 2024-09-24 to 2024-09-30 = 6 days (Sep has 30 days)
- 2024-09-30 to 2024-10-15 = 15 days
- 6 + 15 = 21 days
- 21 > 14 -> FAIL

EA-337
- check - crossing = 2024-10-15 - 2024-10-14
- same calendar month; 15 - 14 = 1 day
- 1 <= 14 -> PASS

Summary
- Cohort size audited: 3
- PASS: 2 (EA-104, EA-337)
- FAIL: 1 (EA-219)

Notes for the auditor
- The 14-day window is grounded in the December 16, 2025 deck critique
  (cohort 2 = 14-day recency-of-ceiling rule). If a different recency window
  was later codified for the second cohort, rerun the reproducer above with
  the updated threshold; the age-in-day calculations do not change.
- Crossing dates are as supplied by the user; this audit does not verify
  them against the underlying qualifying-event log. Release-reliability
  verification of those dates routes to Daniela.
- This artifact is descriptive of the historical cohort. It does not
  recharacterize EA-219 or any other candidate, and it does not affect any
  in-flight Expansion Assist selection.

arguments.body:
Tomás — Priya in cc.

Pre-read for the December 10 operating segment (10:10–10:30 CT), finalized 2025-12-05. Six pages maximum per the 2025-11-12 format: opening frame; one visibly separate page each for Helio Start, retained-mid Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and system controls; and a claims-and-exclusions matrix. All four lanes now have certified inputs and final decision language. The deck rule holds — the four lanes stay separate; no combined growth number; no revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast interpretation.

================================================================
PAGE 1 — OPENING FRAME
================================================================

Purpose: the operating segment is an evidence scaffold for the December 10 board discussion, not a growth forecast. Each lane carries its own denominator, outcome window, evidence limits, and certification owner. Lanes are read independently. No lane is converted into a revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast number.

Read order: Helio Start → retained-mid Expansion Assist → pricing-page path quality → system controls → claims-and-exclusions matrix.

Cert gate: as of 2025-12-05, all four lanes have certified inputs and final decision language in this pre-read. Each lane is presented with its owner and cert date; the cross-section read-out date is 2025-12-05. The board has not yet acknowledged the read-outs — that is the December 10 agenda.

================================================================
PAGE 2 — HELIO START
================================================================

Status: MATURE-COHORT EVIDENCE — CERTIFIED 2025-12-02 (Owen + Customer Success, completed packet delivered after Tuesday 1:1). Q1 GATE DECISION — RECORDED 2025-12-03 (Priya, after reviewing the mature Helio Start packet).

Lane character: mature-cohort read of the bounded Helio Start path. Pairs mature status with refund-adjusted cash and account-level support effort; the Q1 gate decision reads those three together rather than reducing the gate to one conversion number. This lane is NOT a revenue, paid-acquisition, pipeline, forecast, or eligibility input, and it is NOT a forward extension beyond March 31, 2026, a paid-acquisition test, a pipeline target, a forecast credit, or a paid-acquisition reopening rule.

Dated denominator
  82 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows. Window: the bounded Helio Start day-90 outcome window for the mature cohort. Population: admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows only — no partial-window, late-admitted, or non-admitted cases enter the read. Owner: Owen + Customer Success (completed packet). Certification date: 2025-12-02 (delivered after Tuesday 1:1 with Owen).

Mature-status outcomes (denominator = 82)
  Paid-active: 61.
  Canceled: 11.
  Past due: 6.
  Billing hold: 4.

Cash outcomes
  Gross billed cash: $95,420.
  Refund-adjusted collected cash: $89,110.

Account-level support effort
  Median: 20 minutes.
  90th percentile: 70 minutes.
  High-support tail: 7 accounts exceeded 90 minutes (7/82 = 8.5%). All 7 cases involved external-authority or ownership assistance (per the completed Owen + CS packet). The high-support tail is a fact about support effort concentration in this cohort — it is NOT a product-quality, eligibility, or system-controls claim.

Population integrity
  No manual-billing, import, migration, or agency case entered the admitted path. The 82-workspace denominator is the admitted-path read only.

Priya's Q1 gate decision (2025-12-03, after reviewing the mature packet)
  Decision: Helio Start remains a bounded organic pricing-page channel through March 31, 2026. No paid-acquisition test, no pipeline target, no forecast credit during the March 31, 2026 window. The high-support tail (7/82 > 5%) keeps the gate closed on the day-90 read; the cash read and the paid-active/canceled/past-due/billing-hold split are reported alongside, not collapsed into a single conversion number.
  Boundary: March 31, 2026. Helio Start remains bounded to the existing admitted path on organic traffic; the lane does not acquire paid traffic, does not carry a pipeline number, does not carry a forecast number, and does not extend a forward run-out beyond March 31, 2026 in this pre-read.
  Reopening condition (capped paid-acquisition proposal) — all three must hold:
    1. Two consecutive mature cohorts each have fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 support minutes.
    2. No unsupported case enters the admitted path during the two-cohort window.
    3. Any reopened proposal still needs separate budget approval; it is not authorized by the gate decision alone.
  Owner of decision: Priya. Owner of evidence: Owen + Customer Success. Recorded 2025-12-03.

Evidence limits
  Scoped to the 82 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows. The Q1 gate decision reads mature status, refund-adjusted cash, and account-level support effort together; it is not reduced to one conversion number. No claim about revenue implication, paid-acquisition volume, pipeline, forecast, or eligibility. No claim that the cohort is representative of any future, reopened, or extended Helio Start population. No claim that the high-support tail implies a product-quality, eligibility, or system-control outcome. No forward statement beyond the recorded March 31, 2026 boundary. No claim about retained-mid Expansion Assist (Page 3), pricing-page path quality (Page 4), or system controls (Page 5).

Deck rule: this lane does not roll into retained-mid Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, or system controls. No combined growth number across lanes.

================================================================
PAGE 3 — RETAINED-MID EXPANSION ASSIST
================================================================

Status: CERTIFIED EXTRACT 2025-12-01 (Owen + Ines, board-pre-read extract). First-pilot methodology difference preserved: descriptive read-out, NOT causal. No randomized control.

Lane character: descriptive read of what retained-mid customers did when the bounded Expansion Assist lane was offered in the two bounded first pilots. NOT causal; NOT a revenue, pipeline, or forecast input. This lane does not measure whether Expansion Assist moved retention, expansion, or revenue, and it does not adopt the Helio Start methodology (mature status + refund-adjusted cash + account-level support effort read as three).

Dated denominator
  43 actual exposures across the two bounded first pilots' closed, complete 45-day windows. Window: the closed, complete 45-day windows for each bounded first pilot. Population: actual exposures (not impressions, not eligible-but-not-exposed, not exposures in any later or wider lane). Owner: Owen (extract) and Ines (CS adoption/renewal suppression confirmation). Certification date: 2025-12-01.

Complete outcome window
  Both bounded pilots' 45-day windows are closed and complete at the time of certification. The 45-day window is the observation unit; the bounded pilot is the boundedness unit. Help-or-options requests and expansions are counted inside the closed 45-day windows, as defined, with no partial-window extrapolation.

Outcomes (descriptive — "selected," "showed," "were observed")
  Actual exposures (denominator): 43.
  Help-or-options requests: 13.
  Expansions: 9.

Population-mix caveat (recorded plainly)
  The 14-day "ceiling newly crossed" entry condition applied only to the second bounded pilot. 18 of the first pilot's 30 exposures had an older ceiling event. The aggregate 43 / 13 / 9 mix two entry conditions; that mix is recorded, not normalized away.

Lane posture — unchanged from the existing standing lane
  Narrow, behavior-based, state-specific. Active Customer Success adoption or renewal work suppresses a commercial prompt. The lane remains outside pipeline, revenue commitments, and forecast credit. Expansion Assist does not adopt the Helio Start methodology (mature status + refund-adjusted cash + account-level support effort read as three) and is not a day-90-mature-cohort read with a refund-adjusted cash number paired against a support-effort tail.

Evidence limits
  Scoped to the two bounded first pilots' closed 45-day windows. Descriptive only — no randomized control, no implied counterfactual, no claim that Expansion Assist drove, caused, or prevented retention, expansion, or revenue. The 14-day recency-of-ceiling rule applied to cohort 2 only; the 43/13/9 figure mixes the two entry conditions and the mix is recorded, not normalized. Help-or-options is in-product engagement, not purchase intent; expansions are bookings in-window, not incremental ARR vs. a counterfactual. Small sample; no significance, no effect size, no generalization beyond the two bounded pilots. No claim about Helio Start (Page 2), pricing-page path quality (Page 4), or system controls (Page 5).

Deck rule: this lane does not roll into Helio Start, pricing-page path quality, or system controls. No combined growth number across lanes.

================================================================
PAGE 4 — PRICING-PAGE PATH QUALITY
================================================================

Status: IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE 2025-11-26 (Daniela) — CONTROL RETIRED. RESULT DECISION 2025-11-25 (Priya).

Lane character: funnel-quality evidence. Evidence supporting fewer unsupported self-serve starts on the pricing-page path. This lane is NOT a revenue, paid-acquisition, pipeline, forecast, or eligibility input.

Dated denominator
  3,286 sessions across the four cohorts: three weekly cohorts plus the stabilization cohort. Window: the Q4 Pricing Path Clarity Test field period. Population: sessions on the pricing-page path under the experimental design. Owner: Owen. Certification date: 2025-11-19.

Primary outcome — unsupported-condition route-outs
  Control: 38/344 (11.0%).
  Treatment: 25/352 (7.1%).
  Relative reduction: 35.7%.
  Direction: favorable (fewer unsupported self-serve starts).

Guardrails
  Admission completion: 43.8% (treatment) vs 44.1% (control). Within tolerance — no meaningful gap.
  Account-level support time, 90th percentile: 71 minutes (treatment) vs 74 minutes (control). Favorable.

Cohort coverage
  Favorable direction on the primary outcome and on both guardrails, in all three weekly cohorts AND in the stabilization cohort.

Attribution check
  Clean. No concurrent layout, UI, or pricing-copy change overlapped the test window. The movement is attributable to the pricing-page path treatment as designed.

Recommendation / decision / rollout — chain
  2025-11-19: Riley recommended organic adoption after Owen's certified four-cohort read.
  2025-11-25: Priya approved the tested path-separated design as the default organic pricing-page experience and authorized Daniela to move treatment to 100% on 2025-11-26. Marcus Vail and Tomás accepted the narrower framing — the measured gain is fewer unsupported self-serve starts and funnel-quality evidence only, explicitly NOT a revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast claim.
  2025-11-26: Daniela moved the path-separated pricing-page treatment to 100% of organic traffic and retired the control. Post-rollout checks show the existing path-selection, eligibility, admission, and support-routing events are still populating without a taxonomy change. Implementation complete.
  Default-experience status: as of 2025-11-26, the path-separated treatment IS the default organic pricing-page experience. The control is no longer served to organic traffic. The change is surface-level only — bounded Helio Start and assisted needs now appear as separate entry points on the default pricing page for organic traffic.

Evidence limits
  Scoped to the 3,286-session, four-cohort field window. The post-rollout default state is the tested path-separated design on organic traffic only — no claim about revenue, paid-acquisition volume, pipeline, forecast, or eligibility — strictly funnel-quality evidence on the pricing-page path. No claim about Helio Start (Page 2), retained-mid Expansion Assist (Page 3), or system controls (Page 5). No extrapolation outside the certified four-cohort read. The default-experience change does not by itself generate a revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast number; no such claim is being made on the 2025-11-26 implementation-complete update. Post-rollout instrumentation check is clean — the same events are populating, so any future funnel-quality observation continues to read against the same instrumentation as the test window.

Deck rule: this lane does not roll into Helio Start, retained-mid Expansion Assist, or system controls. No combined growth number across lanes.

================================================================
