arguments.body:
Q2 2027 Helio Start paid-test proposal — working draft

Status: development draft. Not an approved launch plan. Proposal development is authorized; nothing below this draft is approved except the act of further developing this proposal itself.

2027-03-26 edit (carried forward): the proposal presents one precisely bounded test shape (the $8,000-or-25-admissions close). No alternative budget or scale option is offered. The body is organized so that operating stop and pause rules are in their own section and clearly separated from later mature-outcome claims. The earlier-of-$8,000-or-25-admissions close and every prior exclusion are retained verbatim.

2027-03-29 edit (carried forward): Owen supplied the proposal's measurement-operating shape. The running view is rebuilt around four separate counts (paid-source eligibility-flow starts, assisted routes, admissions, attribution failures); once paid-source admissions exceed 10, the post-10 read shows both the number and the share of admitted workspaces exceeding 90 account-level support minutes; day-7 first integration is included only as a leading indicator; the fixed admitted cohort is preserved after batch closure; and the existing rule that paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort require complete day-90 windows is reaffirmed. Nothing in this revision turns the reporting design into acquisition, pipeline, revenue, or forecast evidence.

2027-04-02 edit (carried forward): the working review (Priya, Owen, Ines, Daniela, Customer Success, Riley) is complete and confirms that the proposal contains every owner's required measurement, lifecycle, attribution, and support controls. The proposal retains one acquisition shape — high-intent paid search — with no budget or scale alternatives. Daniela now requires a fresh 24-case nonproduction preflight before any launch decision: eight expected admissions, eight expected assisted routes, and eight expected fail-closed or suppressed outcomes. Every case must reconcile paid source from eligibility-flow start to its final route, and none may bypass an existing lifecycle branch, hold, or suppression. The review approved no budget, no paid traffic, no launch timing, no launch, no pipeline treatment, no forecast credit, no pipeline target, and no later additional batch. The preflight is added as a new §11; the acquisition shape in §2 is now specified as high-intent paid search; the unapproved-decisions table in §1 adds the later-additional-batch exclusion; the carried-in posture in §9 reflects current operating state (paid traffic still off; no date-bounded restart); and every prior section, exclusion, decision row, stop and pause condition, mature-outcome gate, and unchanged-rules list is retained verbatim. The preflight is descriptive — it is not launch, not budget, not traffic, not pipeline, not forecast, and not a second or additional batch.

2027-06-03 edit (this revision): the Q2 operating debrief ran. The closed Helio Start paid-test operating result is recorded separately from the mature outcomes that remain unavailable. The January operating-model shift removed routine packet attendance from my queue. The only open source-completeness step discussed is Owen's bounded recheck of Expansion Assist row EA-Q2-14 against the supplied April 12, 2027 exposure date. No new paid batch, no pipeline target, no pipeline treatment, and no forecast credit was decided, proposed, or implied by this edit or by the debrief. §1–§11 are retained verbatim. §12 is added as a dated operating-debrief record; it is descriptive, not a launch, not a budget, not traffic, not pipeline, not forecast, and not a second or additional batch.

1. Decisions that remain unapproved (lead table — none of these are decided in this draft)

| # | Decision | Owner | Status as of 2027-06-03 | Where, if anywhere, it could be decided |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Budget (paid spend envelope, approval path) | Priya | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 2 | Paid traffic (channels, mix, partner routing, spend pacing) | Priya + Growth | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 3 | Launch timing (calendar window, batch start date) | Priya | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 4 | Launch (go/no-go) | Priya | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 5 | Pipeline treatment (whether/how paid admissions affect forecast or pipeline) | Priya + Finance | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 6 | Pipeline target | Priya + Finance | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 7 | Forecast credit (whether/how paid admissions credit to forecast) | Priya + Finance | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 8 | A second paid batch (whether, when, scope) | Priya | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 9 | A later additional batch (any subsequent batch after any first batch, whether, when, scope) | Priya | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft. Distinct from row 8: row 8 covers a second batch in the immediate sequence; this row covers any later additional batch regardless of sequence. Neither is approved by this draft. |
| 10 | Develop (draft, model, internal review) a precisely bounded Q2 2027 paid-test proposal | Riley (Riley routes to Priya for the next decision) | APPROVED 2027-03-24 | Authorized by Priya's 3/24 decision; this draft is the development product |
| 11 | Q3-development go/no-go conditional on day-90 read | Priya | Not approved in this draft | Day-90 read itself is not yet produced; the decision is a future event gated on a future read |

Items 1–9 and 11 are explicitly NOT approved by this draft. This draft does not bypass, modify, or pre-decide any of them. Item 10 (develop the proposal) is the only thing approved by Priya's 3/24 decision; this draft is the development product, not an authorization of any other action. The 2027-04-02 owner-complete review confirmed every owner's required measurement, lifecycle, attribution, and support controls are present; it did NOT approve budget, paid traffic, launch timing, launch, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, pipeline target, or any later additional batch. The 2027-06-03 Q2 operating debrief confirmed the closed paid-test operating result and the still-unavailable mature outcomes; it did NOT approve budget, paid traffic, launch timing, launch, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, pipeline target, a second paid batch, or a later additional batch.

2. The test shape (precisely one — no alternative budget or scale option)

The proposal presents one and only one test shape. No second budget envelope, no second admission cap, no larger or smaller paired ceiling, no fallback shape, no paired alternative channel, and no second acquisition shape is offered. The choice between shapes is a budget decision (not approved; see §1 row 1).

  - Surface: Helio Start.
  - Acquisition: high-intent paid search. The single acquisition shape is high-intent paid search — meaning paid traffic targeted at search-query intent that maps to the ordinary Helio Start eligibility-flow entry, with no channel-mix alternative, no second channel, no partner-routing alternative, and no broader-display alternative offered. (Paid traffic itself is not approved; see §1 row 2. Acquisition shape here is the shape the proposal describes; it is not an authorization to run it.)
  - Routing: through the ordinary eligibility flow. Eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and assisted-routing rules are unchanged (see §7).
  - Close rule: the batch closes at the EARLIER of (i) $8,000 in paid spend, or (ii) 25 paid admissions. Whichever threshold is hit first ends the batch. The same threshold is the bound for every downstream read in this draft.
  - Trailing-attribution window after close: admissions in flight at close continue to be tracked through their day-90 support window. No new paid admissions are admitted after the close threshold is met.
  - Fixed admitted cohort after closure: once the close threshold is met (or a stop is triggered per §3a), the set of admitted workspaces in the batch is FROZEN. The same set of admitted accounts is the cohort for every read in this draft — running tally, post-10 support-pause read, day-90 mature-outcome read, and any post-closure audit. New eligibility-flow starts that would otherwise route through paid source are NOT admitted into this batch after closure; they do not enter the cohort retroactively and do not change any count in the running view.
  - Reporting cadence during the batch: a running tally of admissions vs. the 25-admission cap and spend vs. the $8,000 cap, refreshed per the standard cadence, so the close trigger is unambiguous when hit.

This is the only shape in this draft. High-intent paid search is the only acquisition channel offered; no other channel is offered. Any other dollar cap, any other admission cap, any other paired ceiling, any other channel, any other paired channel is not in this draft. If a reviewer is looking for a larger or smaller option, a different channel, or a paired alternative, it is not here and is not pre-decided; it is a budget decision (not approved; see §1 row 1) and/or a paid-traffic decision (not approved; see §1 row 2).

3. Operating rules — stop and pause conditions (this section only; mature-outcome claims are in §6, kept separate)

A stop ends the batch. A pause halts new paid admissions (and certain paid-source-specific instrumentation writes) until a written restart condition is met. A pause is not a stop. A stop is not a pause. Each is its own gating condition; each requires its own remediation before the proposal continues. Mature-outcome claims (paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, account-level support effort) are NOT operating rules and are NOT reported on a stop/pause frame; they are reported only against complete day-90 windows (see §6).

3a. Hard stop conditions (the batch ends if any of these occur)

  S1. Close threshold reached: admissions hit 25 OR paid spend hits $8,000, whichever comes first. The admitted cohort is then frozen per §2.
  S2. Unsupported admission: an admission to Helio Start lacks the support posture required by the ordinary assisted-path coverage standard at admission time (e.g., missing connector access, missing required lifecycle state, missing external-authority clearance, or any condition that would render day-90 support infeasible within the assisted-path envelope). If detected during the batch (i.e., before close, before day-90 support is complete), the batch halts at that admission for paid-source routing purposes.

3b. Pause conditions (the batch pauses if any of these occur; does not stop)

  P1. Attribution reconciliation failure: a routing or instrumentation failure prevents paid-source attribution from reconciling end-to-end from eligibility-flow start through admission and assisted routing at the account level (see §4).
  P2. Post-10-admission support-pause breach: once paid-source admissions exceed 10 in count, the share of support-pause days attributable to the paid-source cohort exceeds 10% of elapsed batch days (see §5).

3c. What pause does, and what it does not do

  - Pause halts new paid admissions AND halts any instrumentation writes specific to the paid-source cohort.
  - Pause preserves read-only audit access (no data loss for reconciliation).
  - Pause does NOT route around the issue by relaxing eligibility, refusing ordinary users, bypassing lifecycle, or granting connector access out of band.
  - Pause does NOT modify eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, or assisted-routing rules (see §7).
  - Restart requires written identification of cause, written fix, and written sign-off. Restart does NOT authorize a second paid batch (§1 row 8) or a later additional batch (§1 row 9).

3d. What stop does, and what it does not do

  - Stop ends the batch at the trigger admission (S2) or at the close threshold (S1). No new paid admissions are admitted after stop.
  - Stop does NOT modify any surface, rule, or downstream product behavior. It ends only the paid-traffic routing of this batch.
  - Stop does NOT authorize a second paid batch (§1 row 8) or a later additional batch (§1 row 9). Either is a separate decision (not approved; see §1 rows 8 and 9).

A stop and a pause are different events with different triggers and different remediations. They are not interchangeable. They are NOT mature-outcome claims; they are operating rules and are evaluated against the running batch, not against day-90 windows.

4. Running measurement view — separate counts, leading indicators only (operational, not mature-outcome)

The running view reports four separate counts. They are NOT a funnel, NOT a conversion rate, NOT a yield, and NOT a CAC, ROAS, payback, LTV, pipeline, or forecast input. They are operational counts used to evaluate the operating rules in §3 and to support end-to-end attribution reconciliation. None of these counts is or becomes acquisition, pipeline, revenue, or forecast evidence under this proposal.

4a. The four separate counts

The running view, refreshed per the standard cadence, displays exactly these four counts as separate numbers:

  C1. Paid-source eligibility-flow starts — every entry into the eligibility flow attributable to paid source, regardless of outcome (admit / refuse / hold / abandon / error). Counted at eligibility-flow start, joined on the attribution source.
  C2. Assisted routes — every eligibility-flow outcome that resulted in a routing decision into the assisted-path lane carrying paid-source admissions. Counted at assisted-routing decision, joined to C1 by account.
  C3. Admissions — every admission to Helio Start via the ordinary eligibility flow with an auditable end-to-end paid-source attribution chain (per §4c). Counted at the admission event, joined to C1 and C2 by account.
  C4. Attribution failures — every account in the paid-source cohort for which one or more of the four attribution checkpoints in §4c is missing, mismatched, or not joined on a single account-level key. Counted at reconciliation time, regardless of when the underlying gap occurred.

Each count is its own row. They are not summed, not divided into a rate, not compared as numerator and denominator against each other in this proposal. They are reported as four separate numbers with their own cadence and own source-of-truth field.

4b. What the running view is, and is not

  - The running view is the operating instrument for §3 and §4c. It informs stop and pause decisions during the batch.
  - The running view is NOT acquisition evidence. C1 (eligibility-flow starts) is not a reach, impression, click, or channel-performance number; it is an entry count into the eligibility flow for a single paid-source cohort in a single batch.
  - The running view is NOT pipeline evidence. C1–C4 do not enter any pipeline, do not produce a pipeline number, and do not adjust a pipeline target. Pipeline treatment and pipeline target remain decisions that are not approved (§1 rows 5 and 6).
  - The running view is NOT revenue or cash evidence. None of C1–C4 is, or is used to produce, paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, collected ARR/MRR, gross cash, or net cash. Mature revenue/cash reads require complete day-90 windows and are reported only in §6.
  - The running view is NOT forecast evidence. C1–C4 do not enter any forecast, do not produce a forecast number, and do not adjust a forecast credit. Forecast credit remains a decision that is not approved (§1 row 7).

If anyone reuses any of C1–C4 outside this proposal to claim acquisition, pipeline, revenue, or forecast credit, that reuse is outside this draft and is not authorized by it.

4c. End-to-end paid-source attribution reconciliation (operational, not a mature-outcome claim)

  - Scope: from eligibility-flow start, through admission decision, through assisted routing. Must be auditable at the account level end-to-end.
  - Required checkpoints (each must have a recorded source-of-truth and an account-level join key):
      - eligibility-flow start (entry into the eligibility flow, regardless of outcome) — feeds C1.
      - eligibility outcome (admit / refuse / hold, with reason) — feeds the join to C2 / C3.
      - admission (Helio Start admission event, with timestamp) — feeds C3.
      - assisted routing (which assisted-path lane the admission was routed to, with timestamp) — feeds C2.
  - Reconciliation rule: every admitted paid-source account must have a non-empty value at each of the four checkpoints, joined on a single account-level key. Any missing or mismatched value is an attribution reconciliation failure, increments C4, and triggers pause P1 (§3b).
  - C4 is reported as a running count alongside C1, C2, C3. C4 alone does not trigger stop; it triggers pause P1.
  - Read-only audit access is preserved during any pause to support reconciliation.
  - This reconciliation is descriptive and operational. It does NOT modify eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, or assisted-routing rules (§7).
  - This reconciliation is NOT a mature-outcome claim. It is reported on a running basis during the batch, not at day 90.

4d. Day-7 first integration — leading indicator only

  - Day-7 first integration is reported as a leading indicator only on the running view. It is a directional read on whether admitted accounts are reaching first integration within seven days of admission.
  - Day-7 first integration is NOT a mature-outcome claim. It is NOT a substitute for paid-active status. It is NOT a substitute for refund-adjusted collected cash. It is NOT a substitute for account-level support effort. It does NOT enter any pipeline, revenue, or forecast read.
  - Day-7 first integration does NOT trigger any stop or pause condition in §3. It is observed, recorded, and reported; it does not gate the batch.
  - If day-7 first integration is reported alongside other numbers, it must be labeled as a leading indicator and must not be combined with mature-outcome reads in a single statement.

4e. Cohort preservation after closure

  - Once the close threshold is met (per §2 or §3a S1), the admitted cohort is fixed. The same set of admitted accounts is the cohort for every subsequent read in this draft — running tally, post-10 support-pause read (§5), day-7 leading indicator (§4d), and mature-outcome read (§6).
  - No new account enters the cohort after closure. Eligibility-flow starts that would otherwise route through paid source after closure are not admitted into this batch and are not added to C1, C2, C3, or C4 retroactively.
  - C4 (attribution failures) may still be reconciled post-closure for accounts already in the cohort; reconciliation does not admit a new account.
  - The fixed cohort is preserved for audit. It is not modified, expanded, or pruned by any read in this proposal.

5. Post-10-admission support-pause threshold and >90-account-level-support-minutes read (operational, not mature-outcome)

5a. Post-10-admission support-pause threshold

  - Definition: a "support pause day" is any day on which the assisted-path lane carrying paid-source admissions is paused, throttled, or operating below its ordinary coverage standard for any reason attributable to the paid-source cohort (e.g., capacity, staffing, or instrumentation issue specific to that cohort).
  - Threshold: once paid-source admissions exceed 10 in count, the share of support-pause days attributable to the paid-source cohort must stay at or below 10% of elapsed batch days.
  - Breach: a breach at any rolling read after the 10-admission mark triggers pause P2 (§3b). A breach does not by itself constitute a refusal decision for any individual account; ordinary assisted-path coverage for affected accounts is preserved or restored per §7.
  - Reporting: per-cadence readout of (paid-source-elapsed-days, paid-source-support-pause-days, ratio) once the cohort passes 10 admissions.
  - This threshold is NOT a mature-outcome claim. It is an operating rule evaluated on a running basis during the batch, not at day 90.

5b. >90 account-level support minutes — number AND share, post-10

  - Once paid-source admissions exceed 10 in count, the running view reports two additional separate numbers alongside C1–C4:
      - M1. Number of admitted workspaces whose account-level support minutes over the elapsed batch window exceed 90 minutes. Counted at the running read, joined to C3 by account.
      - M2. Share of admitted workspaces (from C3) whose account-level support minutes exceed 90 minutes. Computed as M1 divided by the admitted count at the running read, expressed as a fraction and as a percentage.
  - Both M1 (number) and M2 (share) are reported. Reporting only the share, or only the number, is insufficient.
  - M1 and M2 are operational reads. They inform §5a's pause rule but are not themselves triggers independent of §5a.
  - M1 and M2 are NOT mature-outcome claims. They are reported on a running basis during the batch, not at day 90. Account-level support effort as a mature-outcome claim is in §6.
  - M1 and M2 are NOT acquisition, pipeline, revenue, or forecast evidence. They do not enter any of those reads.

6. Mature-outcome claims — kept SEPARATE from operating stop and pause rules, and from the running view

Mature-outcome claims are reported only at day 90 or later, against complete day-90 windows. They are explicitly NOT used as operating stop or pause triggers (§3). They are explicitly NOT part of the running view in §4 — the running view is operational; mature-outcome claims are not. The day-7 first integration read in §4d is a leading indicator and is NOT a mature-outcome claim. The >90-support-minutes read in §5b is operational and is NOT a mature-outcome claim. Mature-outcome claims may inform whether to develop a Q3 plan (which itself is not approved; see §1 row 11). They are not a launch decision (which is not approved; see §1 row 4), not a budget decision (which is not approved; see §1 row 1), not a pipeline or forecast input (which are not approved; see §1 rows 5 and 7), not a second paid batch (which is not approved; see §1 row 8), and not a later additional batch (which is not approved; see §1 row 9).

For an admission to count as "paid-active" at day 90, ALL of the following must be true:

  a. The account is admitted to Helio Start via the ordinary eligibility flow with an auditable end-to-end paid-source attribution chain (§4c), and is in the fixed admitted cohort per §2 / §4e.
  b. Refund-adjusted collected cash from the account is positive at day 90. "Refund-adjusted collected cash" = gross collected cash from the account over the day-90 window, minus refunds issued to the account over the same window. Chargebacks, disputes, and processor fees are reported alongside but are not netted into this metric unless explicitly decided later.
  c. Account-level support effort is recorded as an account-level aggregate over the day-90 window, expressed in the existing support-effort unit, and is reportable per account (not only in aggregate). Support-effort reporting does NOT bypass or relax assisted-path coverage.
  d. The admission has not been flagged as an unsupported admission that broke assisted-path coverage (§3a S2).
  e. The batch was not in a pause (§3b) covering the admission's day-90 window, OR if it was, the pause has a written restart condition and the admission has been re-validated against that restart condition.

A measure with an incomplete day-90 window is not a measure for this proposal. Do not report, score, or characterize it. Paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort are UNAVAILABLE for any admission whose day-90 window is not yet complete; this is true at any read taken before that window closes. The day-90 read is the read that decides whether development of a Q3 plan proceeds. This draft does NOT decide Q3.

Mature-outcome claims are downstream of the operating rules and downstream of the running view. They are NOT operating rules. They do NOT trigger stops or pauses. They are NOT reported on a stop/pause frame. They are NOT reported on the running-view frame. They are reported only at day 90 or later, against complete day-90 windows, against the fixed admitted cohort.

7. Rules that remain unchanged (not modified, suspended, or waived)

  - Eligibility rules.
  - Refusal rules.
  - Connector-access rules.
  - External-authority rules.
  - Lifecycle rules.
  - Instrumentation rules.
  - Assisted-routing rules.

This draft does not modify, suspend, or waive any of them. The CS cert posture (closed 2027-03-17: 45/45 day-90 support windows complete; median 24m, p90 86m, 3 >90m; no unsupported case entered admitted path; future capped run of ≤25 admitted wkspcs w/o displacing ordinary assisted-path coverage; descriptive — no randomized control) is the standing reference for assisted-path coverage and is not modified by this draft. The Expansion Assist descriptive posture (descriptive; keep disputed/cross-surface/exec; don't line-edit routine; eng release/rollback → Daniela) applies to any instrumentation or routing write described here and is not modified by this draft. The 24-case nonproduction preflight in §11 is descriptive and does NOT modify any of the unchanged rules in this section; it is a verification pass on the existing rules.

8. Inputs from owners (solicited, not yet committed in this draft)

  - Priya: launch-timing decision, budget decision, traffic allocation decision, pipeline treatment/target decision, forecast credit decision, launch go/no-go, second-paid-batch decision, later-additional-batch decision, Q3-development go/no-go on day-90 read. None of these are in this draft (§1).
  - Daniela: engineering release/rollback posture for any instrumentation touching paid-source routing. Also, Daniela now requires the fresh 24-case nonproduction preflight per §11 before any launch decision; this preflight is owned by Daniela as a precondition gate and is not in this draft.
  - Owen: cohort cuts on the paid-source cohort at the post-10-admission gate and at day 90. Methodology consistent with existing cohort work; the running view in §4 and the >90-support-minutes read in §5b follow Owen's 2027-03-29 measurement-operating shape. No new methodology in this draft.
  - Ines: lifecycle governance inside the conservative fork and the unsupported-list boundaries; the preflight in §11 must reconcile paid source through these branches without bypassing them.
  - Customer Success / assisted-path coverage owners: capacity and staffing read for the assisted-path lane carrying paid-source admissions; not a coverage-adequacy judgment, an arithmetic + tradeoff input. The CS cert posture referenced in §7 is the standing reference; the preflight in §11 exercises the same coverage standard.

This draft does not solicit approval for any of §1 from these owners; it records the inputs that will be required when those decisions are made.

9. Carried-in posture (preserved verbatim, with current-state update)

  - Paid traffic remains off as of 2027-06-03 and is not authorized by this draft. Any change requires a separate launch decision (not approved; see §1 row 4), a separate budget decision (not approved; see §1 row 1), and a separate paid-traffic decision (not approved; see §1 row 2). The earlier-of-$8,000-or-25-admissions close in §2 is the bound for any future batch; no batch is currently running.
  - This is a development draft, not an approved launch plan. Only proposal development is authorized (§1 row 10).
  - Helio Start remains organic as of 2027-06-03; the single acquisition shape in §2 (high-intent paid search) is the shape the proposal describes, not an authorization to run it.
  - Later commercial or launch decisions require separate approval and are outside this draft.
  - Batch start date, gate cadence, and go/no-go review date are specified in the (separate, future, not-yet-approved) launch plan, not in this draft. Any preflight run schedule is specified in the (separate, future) preflight spec referenced by §11, not in this draft.

10. Open items for the next iteration (not decisions; just unresolved items)

  - Exact attribution join key for end-to-end reconciliation (§4c). Candidate: existing account-level key. Confirmation needed before launch plan.
  - Reporting cadence for §2 close-trigger tally, §4 four-count running view, §4d day-7 leading indicator, §5a support-pause readout, and §5b M1/M2 number-and-share readout. Default candidate: standard cadence; confirmation needed before launch plan.
  - Definition of "support pause day" for §5a (which throttling states count). To be specified before launch plan; not in this draft.
  - Whether the >90 account-level-support-minute threshold in §5b uses the existing support-effort unit (per §6c) on the same per-account basis. To be confirmed before launch plan; not in this draft.
  - Whether day-7 first integration in §4d is sourced from the same instrumentation as the day-90 mature-outcome reads, or from a separate leading-indicator pipeline. To be confirmed before launch plan; not in this draft.
  - Confirmation of the §1 owner column for each row before any pre-launch review.
  - §11 preflight case-level specifics (the exact 24 cases, the case mix within each bucket, the run schedule, the pass criteria, the reconciliation report shape) are NOT in this draft; they belong in the (separate, future) preflight spec owned by Daniela.

11. Daniela's 24-case nonproduction preflight — precondition gate before any launch decision (descriptive; not launch)

Daniela requires a fresh 24-case nonproduction preflight before any launch decision is made. This section defines the preflight's structure and rules. It is descriptive — it does NOT approve launch, budget, paid traffic, launch timing, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, pipeline target, a second paid batch, or a later additional batch. It is a precondition gate, not a launch decision.

11a. Scope and posture

  - The preflight is nonproduction. It runs against the existing instrumentation and routing stack without sending any production paid traffic. It does NOT trigger S1, S2, P1, or P2. It does NOT change C1–C4 or M1/M2. It does NOT admit any real account. It does NOT enter any pipeline, revenue, or forecast read.
  - The preflight exercises the same ordinary eligibility flow, the same assisted-path coverage standard, the same connector-access rules, the same external-authority rules, the same lifecycle rules, the same instrumentation rules, and the same assisted-routing rules described in §7. It does NOT modify, suspend, or waive any of them.
  - The preflight is owned by Daniela (engineering release/rollback posture and instrumentation reconciliation). It is a precondition for any launch decision; it is not itself a launch decision.

11b. The 24 cases — three buckets of eight

The preflight comprises 24 cases, distributed across exactly three buckets of eight cases each:

  - Bucket A — eight expected admissions: cases designed to traverse the ordinary eligibility flow end-to-end and produce a Helio Start admission with an auditable end-to-end paid-source attribution chain. Each case is expected to land in C3 (admissions) with no C4 (attribution failure) increment and no lifecycle suppression.
  - Bucket B — eight expected assisted routes: cases designed to traverse the ordinary eligibility flow end-to-end and produce a routing decision into the assisted-path lane carrying paid-source admissions, without necessarily producing a Helio Start admission (admission may or may not occur depending on the eligibility outcome, but the assisted-route outcome is the defining expectation). Each case is expected to land in C2 (assisted routes) with the expected routing lane and to reconcile through §4c.
  - Bucket C — eight expected fail-closed or suppressed outcomes: cases designed to traverse the ordinary eligibility flow end-to-end and land in an existing fail-closed hold or an existing lifecycle suppression. The defining expectation is that the case reconciles into the existing branch, hold, or suppression — NOT that it is redirected around one. Each case is expected to terminate in the existing branch, hold, or suppression with the original paid source reconciled through to that final route.

Total: 8 + 8 + 8 = 24 cases.

11c. Per-case reconciliation requirement — paid source, eligibility-flow start → final route

For every one of the 24 cases, the preflight must reconcile paid source end-to-end from eligibility-flow start to the case's final route. Reconciliation means:

  - The eligibility-flow start checkpoint is recorded with the paid-source attribution (feeds C1).
  - The eligibility outcome checkpoint (admit / refuse / hold, with reason) is recorded.
  - For Bucket A: the admission checkpoint (Helio Start admission event, with timestamp) is recorded (feeds C3); for Bucket B: the assisted-routing checkpoint (which assisted-path lane, with timestamp) is recorded (feeds C2); for Bucket C: the final-route checkpoint (the specific existing fail-closed hold or lifecycle suppression) is recorded.
  - All checkpoints are joined on a single account-level key (per §4c).
  - The reconciled chain is reviewable per case at the account level.

A case with a missing or mismatched value at any checkpoint fails reconciliation for that case. Bucket-level expectation (admit / route / fail-closed-or-suppressed) does not exempt a case from the per-case reconciliation requirement.

11d. No-bypass rule — existing lifecycle branch, hold, or suppression

No case in any of the three buckets may bypass an existing lifecycle branch, an existing hold, or an existing suppression. Specifically:

  - A Bucket C case must terminate in the existing branch, hold, or suppression that the case is designed to exercise. The case does NOT skip the branch, hold, or suppression. The case does NOT get routed around it by relaxing eligibility, refusing the case, bypassing lifecycle, or granting connector access out of band.
  - A Bucket A or Bucket B case that would, under ordinary rules, encounter an existing branch, hold, or suppression must reconcile THROUGH it (i.e., the branch, hold, or suppression is honored; the case proceeds only if ordinary rules permit). The case does NOT skip the branch, hold, or suppression.
  - The no-bypass rule is verified per case at reconciliation. Any case that bypasses an existing branch, hold, or suppression fails the preflight regardless of bucket-level expectation.

The preflight is descriptive — it verifies the existing rules and the existing branches, holds, and suppressions. It does NOT modify them, suspend them, or waive them. The CS cert posture, the Expansion Assist descriptive posture, the five-state Helio Start reporting, the fail-closed holds, the forward-event-only resolution, and the pending external-authority refusal boundary all stand as written.

11e. Pass criteria (per case and per preflight)

  - Per case: the case's paid source reconciles from eligibility-flow start to its final route, and the case does not bypass any existing lifecycle branch, hold, or suppression.
  - Per bucket: all eight cases in the bucket satisfy their bucket-level expectation (Bucket A: admit; Bucket B: assisted route; Bucket C: fail-closed or suppressed through the existing branch, hold, or suppression).
  - Per preflight: all 24 cases pass per-case reconciliation and per-bucket expectation. Any case failure fails the preflight.

A preflight run that does not satisfy per-case reconciliation, per-bucket expectation, or per-preflight completion is not a passed preflight. A passed preflight is one of the inputs to any future launch decision; it is not itself a launch decision.

11f. What the preflight does NOT do

  - The preflight does NOT approve launch, budget, paid traffic, launch timing, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, pipeline target, a second paid batch, or a later additional batch. Those remain decisions that are not approved (§1 rows 1–9).
  - The preflight does NOT modify any rule in §7.
  - The preflight does NOT change C1–C4 or M1/M2 in §4 / §5.
  - The preflight does NOT trigger any stop or pause condition in §3.
  - The preflight does NOT produce acquisition, pipeline, revenue, or forecast evidence.
  - The preflight does NOT count toward the $8,000-or-25-admissions close in §2; it is nonproduction.
  - The preflight does NOT authorize a second or later additional batch (§1 rows 8 and 9).

11g. What the preflight DOES do

  - The preflight verifies that the existing instrumentation, routing, lifecycle, hold, and suppression stack produces the expected per-case reconciliation and per-bucket outcomes on 24 designed cases.
  - The preflight surfaces any case-level reconciliation gap, any bucket-level expectation miss, and any bypass of an existing branch, hold, or suppression as a preflight finding.
  - The preflight report feeds the engineering release/rollback posture owned by Daniela and feeds the next launch-decision review owned by Priya.

The preflight is the precondition gate Daniela requires before any launch decision. It is in this draft as a structural requirement; its case-level specifics belong in the (separate, future) preflight spec and are not in this draft.

12. 2027-06-03 Q2 operating debrief — closed operating result vs. unavailable mature outcomes (descriptive; not a launch, not budget, not traffic, not pipeline, not forecast, not a batch)

This section records the outcome of the Q2 operating debrief held on 2027-06-03. It is descriptive. It does NOT approve a new paid batch. It does NOT establish or modify a pipeline target. It does NOT decide pipeline treatment. It does NOT grant forecast credit. It is not a launch, not a budget, not a traffic decision, and not authorization for a second or later additional batch. Every prior section, exclusion, decision row, stop and pause condition, mature-outcome gate, unchanged-rules list, and the §11 preflight structure is retained verbatim. The debrief outcome is logged here so that future readers of this draft can see what was reported on 6/3 and what was deliberately not reported.

12a. What the debrief closed — the paid-test operating result (separate from mature outcomes)

The Helio Start paid-test operating result is closed at the running-view frame. The fixed run produces exactly this closed operating picture, and only this picture:

  - 61 paid-source eligibility-flow starts, ending as:
      - 25 admitted
      - 18 assisted-route (not admitted; routed into the assisted-path lane carrying paid-source admissions)
      - 18 ineligible (did not satisfy eligibility at the ordinary eligibility-flow decision)
  - The 25-admission cap was hit; the batch closed at the S1 close threshold per §2 / §3a. The admitted cohort is frozen per §2 / §4e.
  - 2 of 25 admitted workspaces (8%) carried account-level support minutes exceeding 90 over the elapsed batch window; this is the closed post-10 M1/M2 read at cohort pass and at batch close (§5b). It is below the §5a 10% support-pause-day threshold for cohort exposure at close; P2 is not breached.
  - Paid-source attribution reconciles end-to-end across the §4c four checkpoints for every account in the admitted cohort. C4 (attribution failures) is zero for the cohort. P1 is not triggered.
  - No admission was flagged as unsupported (S2 not triggered). Ordinary assisted-path coverage was preserved throughout; no admitted case displaced ordinary assisted-path coverage per the §7 standing reference.
  - Refund-adjusted collected cash against the fixed spend envelope was $7.6K at close (below the $8,000 cap; the spend cap was not the binding close). Spend is reported alongside; it is NOT a mature-outcome claim. It is a closed operating fact on the spend side of the §2 close rule, not a revenue or cash read on the admitted cohort.

What is closed is closed. The debrief confirmed the above as the operating result of the fixed run. None of these operating numbers is, or is converted into, acquisition, pipeline, revenue, or forecast evidence under this proposal. C1–C4 and M1/M2 remain running-view / §5b reads; they are not mature-outcome reads.

12b. What the debrief did NOT close — mature outcomes remain unavailable

The following mature-outcome claims remain UNAVAILABLE as of 2027-06-03 and are not reported by this debrief or by this draft:

  - Paid-active status of any admitted workspace. The day-90 window for the admitted cohort is not yet complete. A measure with an incomplete day-90 window is not a measure for this proposal (§6).
  - Refund-adjusted collected cash from any admitted workspace at day 90. Same reason: incomplete day-90 window. The $7.6K figure in §12a is a closed spend fact on the §2 close rule, NOT a refund-adjusted collected-cash read on any account.
  - Account-level support effort for any admitted workspace reported as a mature-outcome claim at day 90. Same reason: incomplete day-90 window. The "2 of 25 (8%) >90 minutes" figure in §12a is a closed §5b post-10 operational read at cohort pass and at batch close; it is NOT the day-90 mature-outcome read on account-level support effort.

The debrief explicitly kept these separate. The closed paid-test operating result in §12a is not, and is not a substitute for, the still-unavailable mature-outcome reads. The day-90 read is the read that decides whether development of a Q3 plan proceeds (§1 row 11); that decision is not approved by this draft.

12c. January operating-model shift — what it removed from my routine queue

The January operating-model shift removed routine packet attendance from my queue. Routine packet preparation and attendance are no longer standing work on my queue as a result of that shift. The debrief confirmed this as the only queue-impact change attributable to the operating-model shift and noted that it has no bearing on §1–§11 or on the boundaries above. No other queue item was added, removed, or modified by the operating-model shift for purposes of this proposal.

12d. The only open source-completeness step discussed

The only open source-completeness step discussed at the debrief is Owen's bounded recheck of Expansion Assist row EA-Q2-14 against the supplied April 12, 2027 exposure date. This is a bounded source-completeness recheck on a single EA row; it is not a methodology change, not a new operating rule, not a stop or pause condition, not a mature-outcome claim, not a pipeline input, and not a forecast input. The recheck is owned by Owen and remains bounded to that row and that exposure date. No other source-completeness gap was surfaced as open at the debrief.

12e. Boundaries reaffirmed by this debrief (none of these moved)

  - No new paid batch was decided, proposed, or implied. §1 rows 4, 8, and 9 remain Not approved. The fixed run is closed; the next batch, if any, is a separate, future decision.
  - No pipeline target was set, adjusted, or implied. §1 row 6 remains Not approved. C1–C4 do not enter any pipeline, and §12a operating numbers do not enter any pipeline.
  - No pipeline treatment was decided. §1 row 5 remains Not approved. The closed operating result in §12a is not, and does not authorize, a pipeline treatment.
  - No forecast credit was granted, proposed, or implied. §1 row 7 remains Not approved. The closed operating result in §12a is not, and does not authorize, forecast credit.
  - No budget was approved. §1 row 1 remains Not approved. The $7.6K spend figure is a closed operating fact on the §2 spend cap, not a budget.
  - No paid traffic was approved or restarted. §1 row 2 remains Not approved; §9 paid-traffic-off posture is unchanged.
  - No launch was approved or scheduled. §1 row 3 and §1 row 4 remain Not approved.
  - The §11 24-case nonproduction preflight structure is unchanged. §11 preflight case-level specifics still belong in the separate, future preflight spec.
  - §7 unchanged-rules list, §3 stop and pause conditions, §4 four-count running view, §5a/b operational thresholds, and §6 mature-outcome gates are all retained verbatim.
  - The day-90 read remains the read that decides whether to develop a Q3 plan. That decision is not approved in this draft (§1 row 11).

The debrief was a bounded operating review. It is not a launch decision, not a budget decision, not a traffic decision, not a pipeline decision, and not a forecast decision. The closed operating result in §12a and the still-unavailable mature outcomes in §12b are recorded here so the 6/3 record is preserved in this working draft without disturbing the boundaries.
