| Display | 268 | 412 | +144 | 12.6% | 12.7% | flat |
| CS-work suppression | 91 | 138 | +47 | 4.3% | 4.3% | flat |
| State hold | 37 | 61 | +24 | 1.7% | 1.9% | +0.2 pp |
| Condition not met | 1,724 | 2,629 | +905 | 81.3% | 81.1% | −0.2 pp |

Reading: display rate and CS-work suppression rate held essentially flat through the window; the state-hold surface edged up by ~0.2 pp but stayed small in absolute terms (24 cases on the increment). Condition-not-met moved opposite by ~0.2 pp and stayed the dominant bucket, consistent with the 10% release keeping the surface narrow.

---

## Cross-system agreement

- **Interim (10/13):** reporting / lifecycle / reminder outcomes agreed for every included evaluation.
- **Final (10/19):** reporting / lifecycle / reminder outcomes agreed for every evaluation.
- **Meaning:** the three systems were not silently disagreeing about eligibility, suppression, or display outcome at any point in the window. No cross-surface discrepancy surfaced.
- **This is a guardrail signal**, not an effect read.

---

## Incident-control results

Final close reports all four guardrails clean; interim cut reports the same set clean across its included evaluations.

| Guardrail | Interim (10/13) | Final (10/19) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Customer corrections | none | none |
| Incident stops | none | none |
| Source-age breaches | none | none |
| Rollbacks executed | none | none |
| Rollback need (i.e. rollback would have been warranted) | none | none |

Daniela's three stop conditions from the 10/5 source-readiness approval (cross-surface discrepancy, customer correction, failed rollback) did not trigger at any point in the window. Daniela retained rollback control throughout; it was not exercised.

---

## What this interval decided

- The 10% initial production interval completed clean.
- All four incident-control guardrails (corrections, incident stops, source-age breaches, rollbacks — and the related "need for rollback") held off across the full window.
- Cross-system agreement (reporting / lifecycle / reminder) held for every evaluation, interim and final.
- Display rate and CS-work suppression rate were stable across the window.
- State-hold is present as a small, persistent data-quality surface; it is not a treatment-skipped outcome and it did not trigger any stop condition.
- Release posture was held at 10% throughout, per the 10/8 governance call after the clean first hour; the 10/6–10/18 window was not allowed to be skipped or shortened by an early-clean reading.

## What this interval did NOT decide

- **The rollout decision.** The interval supplies evidence for that decision; it does not make it. Release stays at 10%.
- **Whether to widen to 25%, 50%, 100%, or any other release surface.** Untouched by this interval.
- **The full 21-day decision-grade read with effect estimate and confidence interval.** This is a 12-day initial production interval; interim/guardrail only.
- **Stabilization cohort pre-ship evidence.** Not produced by this interval.
- **Daniela's check on paid-traffic / prod-change gates before any live-eligible widening.** Owed separately.
- **The pre-launch metric + min-effect spec review against this readout.** Owed separately.
- **Any characterization of consumer #5's effect.** The reminder is in flight; an effect read is not closed by a guardrail pass.
- **Anything about Owen's, Ines's, or Daniela's lane execution as my execution.** Their work is their lane; this card records their results, not my contribution to them.

---

## Status

Interval closed 2027-10-19 11:30 CT. Guardrails pass. Cross-system agreement held. Release STAYS at 10%. Separate rollout decision owes the items above; nothing in this interval settles them.

arguments.body:
Q4 LIFECYCLE SYSTEMS CONTRACTOR — WORKLOAD BRIEF
Owner: Riley  ·  For: Priya  ·  Use: Q4 Lifecycle Systems Planning Workshop (Aug 21, 2025, 1:30–2:30pm CT)
Comparator lens only. No case is selected in this brief.

================================================================
SUMMARY
================================================================

Finance has supplied three Q4 cases for Lifecycle Systems contractor capacity:
    Case 1 — No contractor ($0)
    Case 2 — Half-time ops contractor, 6 months ($36,000; ~$6k/mo, ~80 hrs/mo)
    Case 3 — FTE-equivalent contractor, 4 months ($48,000; ~$12k/mo, ~160 hrs/mo)

UPDATE 2025-08-14 — timing & scope refinements from Finance and procurement
  Timing windows (binding, per Finance/procurement):
    Case 2 ($36k half-time) — earliest start Oct 1, 2025; 6-month duration, runs ~Oct 1, 2025 – ~Mar 31, 2026.
    Case 3 ($48k FTE-equivalent) — cannot start before Nov 1, 2025 because it requires agency onboarding; 4-month duration, runs ~Nov 1, 2025 – ~Feb 28, 2026.
  Both windows are firm. Case 3's Nov 1 floor is the binding constraint under that case.
  Scope (binding, per Finance/procurement): in both Cases 2 and 3 the contractor may cover
    - repeatable audit preparation
    - campaign inventory
    - operator enablement
    - evidence packaging
    - presentation-detail reconciliation
  Scope (binding, per Finance/procurement): in both Cases 2 and 3 the contractor cannot receive
    - engineering release access (Daniela's lane, unchanged)
    - Owen's reporting semantics (Owen's lane, unchanged)
    - Ines's message-state governance (Ines's lane, unchanged)
    - Riley's exception authority (judgment-esc, disputed semantics, cross-surface, exec language; unchanged)
  These four exclusions are added to the locked-boundaries list in Section 4 below.

Intended work is the same in Cases 2 and 3 (per the 8/14 scope refinement above). Case 1 absorbs that work into existing lanes. The three cases differ on which constraint they relax (capacity, handoff runway, or standing-lane load) and which they tighten (audit risk, Q1 carryover, or owner-lane pressure). The right case is the one that hits the binding constraint without crossing the locked boundaries.

The locked boundaries (per the 2025-03-24 audit roles reaffirmed 2025-08-05 midyear, plus the 8/14 Finance/procurement scope memo) are:
    - Owen's lane (shape+ex + Lifecycle Systems semantics + exception readouts + Helio Start report) is preserved as-is.
    - Ines's lane (lifecycle-aud-risk; routine education HIGHER-RISK, Riley is boundary) is preserved as-is.
    - Riley's lane (judgment-esc, disputed semantics, cross-surface, exec language, exception authority) is preserved as-is.
    - Daniela's lane (engineering release / rollback) is preserved as-is.
    - Contractor does not touch: a fifth shared-state consumer, Helio Start paid acquisition, engineering release work, disputed semantics, cross-surface *claim* rulings, exec-language drafting, Owen's reporting semantics, Ines's message-state governance, or Riley's exception authority.

This brief frames the comparison. Selection is held for Aug 21.

================================================================
1. WORKLOAD RELIEVED — what each case actually buys
================================================================

Case 1 — No contractor ($0)
  Capacity added: none.
  Where the work lands if not contracted:
    - Repeatable audit prep → Ines's standing lane (≤3 neutral/wk, stale fails closed; from 2025-03-24 roles, reaffirmed 2025-08-05 midyear). Per the 2025-07-25 message-state guide, routine education is HIGHER-RISK with Riley as the boundary; loading this lane invites leaks into judgment territory.
    - Campaign inventory → Owen's lane. Poor fit for shape+ex, and competes with the Helio Start report (closed 7/30 on the day-90 cohort; next read TBD).
    - Operator enablement → no owner; falls to Riley by default. Wrong work type for Riley's lane (judgment-esc, disputed semantics, cross-surface, exec language).
    - Evidence packaging, presentation-detail reconciliation → no owner; falls to Riley by default. Same wrong-lane problem.
  Net effect: cost shows up as audit-prep slip + invisible Owen load + Riley-on-exception work, not as a line item.

Case 2 — Half-time ops contractor, 6 months ($36k)
  Timing: earliest start Oct 1, 2025; 6-month duration (~Oct 1, 2025 – ~Mar 31, 2026). Procurement-confirmed.
  Capacity added: ~80 hrs/month sustained over six months.
  Covers: repeatable audit prep, campaign inventory (steady cadence), operator enablement, evidence packaging, presentation-detail reconciliation.
  Does NOT cover: a campaign-inventory blitz. That work is gated to a steady cadence, not a sweep.
  Handoff runway: months 1–3 build repeatable prep; months 4–6 train operators and run evidence/presentation reconciliation; hand off at month 6 with operator carryover.
  Net effect: standing-lane backlog clears; operator enablement has real runway; Owen / Ines / Riley / Daniela lanes untouched.

Case 3 — FTE-equivalent contractor, 4 months ($48k)
  Timing: cannot start before Nov 1, 2025 because agency onboarding is required; 4-month duration (~Nov 1, 2025 – ~Feb 28, 2026). Procurement-confirmed.
  Capacity added: ~160 hrs/month for four months.
  Covers: repeatable audit prep, campaign-inventory blitz, operator enablement, evidence packaging, presentation-detail reconciliation.
  Does NOT cover: operator enablement with runway. Contractor exits month 4; operator carryover starts month 3. Fragile.
  Net effect: strong Q4 throughput, weak Q1 handoff. Only sensible if the work is more "blitz" than "transition." Note that Case 3's Nov 1 start shrinks Q4 to two months; the throughput argument weakens relative to Case 2's six-month half-time run, and the handoff-fragility argument strengthens.

================================================================
2. AUDIT RISK & OWNER-LANE PRESSURE — what each case loads
================================================================

Audit risk (standing-lane rule expects repeatable prep to land clean):

  Case 1 — HIGH.  No lane to absorb the work; it skips or leaks into higher-risk judgment territory, mainly Ines's lane.
  Case 2 — LOW.   Lane has capacity to clear standing-lane backlog without slipping.
  Case 3 — LOW.   More capacity than needed; risk is handoff fragility, not audit prep.

# Riley Tanaka — H1 2027 self-review working notes

For: Priya. Draft due June 4. Center: outcomes, operating leverage, one development edge. Style: summary first; why / cuts / p / effect / call.

One-line summary: H1 was the half I stopped doing the work and started ruling on it — operating model reset in January, exception-only hands-on through Q1, bounded Q2 paid test, and one deliberate growth edge.

## 1. January operating-model transition

What changed: briefs became descriptive, not prescriptive. I rule on disputed / cross-surface / exec asks only; routine line-edits stay with the owner. Release and rollback authority moved to Daniela. Kickoff and certification flow through Priya. The point was to push variance out of the routine path and concentrate my judgment where it's actually load-bearing.

Concrete example — January incomplete-packet handling: early-January briefs arrived missing the cuts segment and the effect bound. Under the prior model I'd have rebuilt the packet myself. Under the reset, I sent it back to the owner named on the brief with the two missing fields flagged, copied the channel lead, and ruled on the dispute (priority order of cuts) only when it came back. I did not co-author the rewrite. The packet closed in the owner's voice; the ruling was mine; my hours went to the cross-surface question, not to reconstruction. That's the operating model in one packet.

Effect: fewer rewrites mid-flight, cleaner signal in #growth-investigations and #lifecycle-systems, and I regained hours I'd been losing to second-opinion reviews.

Call: the model held. Don't relitigate it this half.

## 2. Exception-only involvement + quarterly hands-on audit

Day-to-day, I'm out of the routine path — I read locks before recurring meetings and I weigh in on the cohort cuts Owen and I walk through Mondays. Once per quarter I run a hands-on audit anyway, to keep my eye calibrated and to catch what the dashboards miss.

[TBD — fill: which audit (e.g. mid-segment churn cohort), dates, the one finding that changed a decision.]

The audit is leverage, not a deliverable: it lets me stay credible in exceptions without re-entering the queue.

## 3. Q2 Helio Start paid test — bounded execution

Decision example — bounded launch and bounded close.

At launch (Q2): I signed off on the bounded scope only. Paid-source mechanics, screening rules, and day-to-day enrollment are Owen's routine source ownership. Lifecycle and certification governance are Ines's lane. Engineering controls on release/rollback are Daniela's. I ruled on three NOs up front: no lifecycle bypass, no 5th shared-state, and no eligibility change. I did not, and do not, edit those layers mid-test.

At close (5/17, Owen '27 cohort, CS-led paid-source lane):
- 25-admin enrollment cap; $7.6K committed; 61 screened → 25 active / 18 assistant / 18 ineligible.
- Attribution reconciles end-to-end (no double-count vs. organic).
- Support load: 2 of 25 = 8% exceeded 90-min support. No pause triggered. No unsupported admin.
- Day-90 window still open as of 5/20 — retention and downstream ARR impact are NOT yet established by this test.

What this test establishes (descriptively, pending day-90):
- Paid-source mechanics work: enrollment gating, eligibility filter, attribution, support-cost baseline.
- The 25-admin cap is operationally safe at this support ratio.
- The pre-committed NOs held without override.

What this test does NOT establish — keep this read out loud:
- Day-90 retention, expansion, or net revenue — window incomplete.
- Generalizability to organic-source cohorts or other tiers.
- Authority for an eligibility or lifecycle change.
- That paid is preferable to organic at scale — that's a different experiment.

The bounded scope is the decision. The numbers above are a status read; they're not a verdict on revenue, forecast, or downstream ARR. Hold that line.

## 4. Team development

[Fill in 2–3 concrete moments. Suggested frame: who grew into what, what I stopped doing so they could do it, what I unblocked. Avoid generic "supportive manager" language — Priya wants the moves.]

Working frame I'd use: Owen took full source ownership on Helio Start with me only on exceptions — that's the development, not a status update. Ines ran lifecycle kickoff and certification end-to-end without escalation. Daniela held release authority and I stayed out of it. [Add one moment where I explicitly got out of the way and it landed.]

## 5. One growth edge

The edge I want to name: letting owner-ready work remain with its owner.

Half 1 was the operational version — the operating-model reset moved routine work off my desk. Half 2 is the personal version: when someone brings me a brief, a packet, or a fix that's already owner-ready, I rule on what they asked and ship it back, instead of absorbing the rewrite "to be safe." That's the edge — and it's the same muscle as the January incomplete-packet example, just generalized. The risk when I drift is quiet erosion of the lanes; the move when I hold is that the owner keeps the authorship and the work gets faster.

## Boundaries to keep clean in the draft

What stays mine (delegation did not move it):
- Causal judgment on cross-surface / disputed / exec asks — my rulings, my call.
- Revenue and forecast ownership — I sign off; I don't delegate the read.
- Board-readiness and executive-language framing — that's my translation, not the owner's.
- Authority over scope, the NOs, and the day-90 hold.

What I do not own and shouldn't claim:
- Owen's routine source ownership — mechanics, screening, enrollment ops.
- Ines's lifecycle governance — kickoff, certification, journey rules.
- Daniela's engineering controls — release, rollback, feature-flag gating.

Frame: if a sentence could be read as me owning Owen's, Ines's, or Daniela's lane, rewrite it as my ruling on a question they brought me. If it could be read as me having handed off my causal / revenue / forecast / board-readiness / exec-language authority, rewrite it — I didn't.

---

arguments.body:
# Helio Start GA — May Continuation Evidence Gate

Draft for Priya. Frame: continue vs. stop under the current bounded shape. Not, and does not license, an expansion decision.

---

## 1. Decision being framed — continuation vs. expansion

This brief is the first Helio Start GA audit recast as a draft evidence gate for the May continuation review. The question it answers is narrow:

> Under the current bounded shape of Helio Start, may the path continue into May?

This audit grants **permission to continue the bounded path**, and only that. It does **not** grant permission to expand the path — not in scope, not in tier, not in audience, not in cadence, not in any dimension that would change the shape of what is being continued.

Per Priya's 4-03 comment, the two permissions are kept separate on purpose:

- **Continuation (this gate).** The path keeps running as it is currently bounded.
- **Expansion (not this gate).** Any change to scope, breadth, or tier — including Expansion Assist (closed 2-05) and any expansion-style readout — is a separate decision and is tracked independently.

A favorable continuation read does **not** license expansion. The continuation gate and the expansion decision do not share a recommendation; if either is asked for, it is asked for explicitly.

---

## 2. Gate pre-conditions — all required for any continue call

These are the conditions that must hold **before** the activation headline or any refusal-boundary check is read. If any pre-condition fails, the gate does not return a continue recommendation regardless of how the rest of the evidence reads.

1. **At least three mature weekly cohorts.** The continuation call is grounded in three or more mature weekly cohorts of admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows. Fewer than three mature weekly cohorts is not a basis for continuation; the audit is deferred until the cohort count is met. (Cohort-definition details: see §3.)
2. **Ordinary support coverage.** Support for the routed path is running on its ordinary coverage model — no emergency overrides, no special-case routing, no staffing carve-outs that would flatter the support-load readout. The continuation call assumes ordinary support is in place for the entire window the cohorts cover.
3. **Zero cases crossing any published refusal-boundary check.** No account or cohort may cross a published refusal-boundary check (§5) during the window. "Zero" is the bar; a single crossing is enough to fail this pre-condition regardless of how small or isolated it looks.

These three pre-conditions are additive to, not a substitute for, the refusal-boundary checks themselves.

---

## 3. Cohort

- **In:** Helio Start admitted accounts.
- **In, only if mature:** accounts with a complete day-7 window at audit cutoff.
- **Out:** accounts still inside an open day-7 window (would bias the activation rate).
- **Out:** Expansion Assist / closed-2-05 mid-segment retained population (separate readout).
- **Out:** ordinary starter onboarding (Ines 3-26 Feb perf table) — that is the non-routed lifecycle sequence (day-2 reminder 811/920, day-5 integration-help 503/594, day-9 help offer 229/281). Later sends select for non-progressed; day-9 is past the 7d activation window and is not a Helio Start activation input.
- **Mature-account count floor — UNRESOLVED.** Whether the "at least three mature weekly cohorts" requirement also needs a minimum mature-account count is **not yet decided**. The brief does **not** choose a threshold. The mature-account-count question is logged as an open item (§12) and must be resolved before this gate locks; until then, the "three mature weekly cohorts" requirement is stated without a paired account-count floor.

---

## 4. Metric of record

**Day-7 activation rate, mature cohort, per the Helio Start spec Owen confirmed 3-11:**

- Definition: first integration / 7 days / all eligible.
- Support: setup + permission requests / owned per 100 eligible (pre-activation included).
- Out of rate (counted, not folded into activation): routed-pre-setup failures, entitlement failures, support-state failures.

Activation is the metric of record here. It is **kept separate from** mature conversion, retention, revenue, and forecastable pipeline. A clean activation number does not license a clean conversion or revenue read; those are independent measures with their own windows and will not appear in this gate's headline.

---

## 5. Refusal-boundary checks (any fire = no continuation; zero crossings required)

These are the conditions under which the path does **not** continue, regardless of how the headline activation number reads. They are pre-committed; the May review does not renegotiate them. Per the §2 pre-conditions, the bar for the audit window is **zero crossings** of any of these checks.

1. **Routing integrity breach.** Routed-pre-setup failures above the pre-set band, or a non-trivial pattern of accounts routed to the wrong owner lane.
2. **Entitlement state failure.** Accounts whose entitlement/support-state failure prevents the activation denominator from being measured honestly (i.e., we cannot tell whether non-activation is product reality vs. entitlement artifact). If the denominator itself is compromised, the rate is not a rate.
3. **Support load breach.** Setup + permission requests per 100 eligible (pre-activation included) above the owned-load band.
4. **Lifecycle regression.** Any of the non-routed lifecycle sends (day-2 reminder, day-5 integration-help, day-9 help offer) regressing on volume, conversion-to-help, or audience selection such that the ordinary starter sequence is being damaged by Helio Start routing.
5. **Readout instability.** Any of the five refusal-boundary checks moving in a direction that, under the pre-reg stability rule (same metric / same direction / n ≥ treatment + p < 0.01 on a 2nd-look *before* the next peek vs. a fake-1st-sig), would not survive a second look. The audit cuts the cohort pre-rollout if first-sig is suspect.

Any single crossing — of any one check — fails pre-condition §2.3 and prevents a continue recommendation.

---

## 6. Reporting lane — Owen

Owns the readout shape and exceptions:

- Funnel view: signup → admitted → day-7 activation, restricted to mature windows.
- Per-check view: each of the five refusal-boundary checks surfaced as its own row, not blended. **Zero crossings** is the row-level bar.
- Cohort-count view: a count of mature weekly cohorts in the window, surfaced explicitly so §2.1 is auditable.
- Exception log: every account excluded from the cohort, with reason (open window / entitlement / routing / other), so the cohort cut is auditable.
- Comparability: pre-reg stability cohort for any first-sig result, per the standing rule.

Owen does not own the judgment call on continuation. Owen owns the shape of the evidence.

---

## 7. Lifecycle lane — Ines

Owns lifecycle-audience-risk for the non-routed starter sequence:

- Volume + selection on day-2 reminder, day-5 integration-help, day-9 help offer (811/920, 503/594, 229/281 baselines from Ines 3-26 Feb perf table).
- Watch for audience overlap or mis-routing that would let Helio Start's routed sequence eat into the ordinary starter sequence's signal.
- Escalation path: if any lifecycle number regresses, the lifecycle-audience-risk view goes to the readout, not into the activation headline.

---

## 8. Instrumentation lane — Daniela

Owns the integrity of the inputs the gate relies on:

- Activation event schema (first integration, 7d, all eligible) — correctness of the integration, including the eligible denominator.
- Entitlement state and support-state failure instrumentation — that these surface as their own counts and are not silently folded into activation.
- Routed-pre-setup instrumentation — that every pre-setup routing decision is logged with owner and outcome.
- Pre-reg stability cohort wiring — that the same metric / same direction readout is reproducible from raw events.

If Daniela's instrumentation has any open gap touching the five refusal-boundary checks, the gate does not run; the gap is named and the audit is deferred.

---

## 9. Routed-support ownership lane — Customer Success

Owns the routed-pre-setup and support-state lanes:

- Per-100-eligible support load (setup + permission, pre-activation included), against the owned band.
- Entitlement / support-state failure counts, separately reported (not folded into the activation rate).
- Routing correctness — that admitted accounts land with the right CS owner and that routing failures are flagged for the readout, not absorbed into "support load."

CS owns the operational lane. The gate reads the result; CS owns whether the lane ran on ordinary coverage (§2.2) and whether the lane ran cleanly.

---

## 10. Judgment-call escalation — Riley

Owns the escalation lane only:

- If a pre-condition (§2) fails, the call goes to Riley for a continue / stop / defer decision. Riley does not re-shape the readout.
- If a refusal-boundary check fires, or if two checks are borderline, the call goes to Riley for a continue / stop / defer decision. Riley does not re-shape the readout.
- If first-sig would need a pre-reg stability cohort before the May review, Riley owns the pre-rollout cohort cut.
- If the audit readout contradicts an Expansion Assist (closed 2-05) reading, that contradiction is logged but does not block this gate; Expansion Assist is its own decision, and continuation here does not license it.

---

## 11. What the May review will see

A single continue / stop recommendation, supported by:

- The three pre-conditions from §2, each pass/fail.
- The mature day-7 activation rate (its own row).
- Each of the five refusal-boundary checks, each its own row, each pass/fail/borderline — against the **zero crossings** bar.
- Owen's cohort-count view and exception log (cohort cut auditable).
- Daniela's instrumentation sign-off (or named gap).
- Ines's lifecycle-audience-risk view.
- CS's routed-support ownership read, including confirmation that ordinary support coverage was in place for the window.

The May review will **not** see:

- A revenue number, a forecastable-pipeline number, or any pipeline-style language about future cohorts, future revenue, or future scope. No pipeline language appears in the gate output. Those measures are tracked independently and are not part of this gate.
- A mature conversion or retention number folded into the activation headline.
- An expansion recommendation, regardless of how favorable the continuation read is. Expansion is not on the agenda for this gate.
- A mature-account count threshold for §2.1 — that is unresolved (§3, §12) and is not chosen here.

---

## 12. Open items before this gate locks

- [ ] **Priya to confirm or set the mature-account count floor** for the "three mature weekly cohorts" requirement. Currently **unresolved**; no threshold has been chosen. The brief does not pre-suppose one.
- [ ] Daniela to confirm instrumentation sign-off covers all five refusal-boundary checks.
- [ ] CS to confirm routed-pre-setup + entitlement/support-state logging covers pre-activation, and that ordinary support coverage was in place for the full cohort window.
- [ ] Owen to confirm the pre-reg stability cohort is wired for any first-sig path, and that the cohort-count view (§6) is reproducible.
- [ ] Ines to confirm the day-2 / day-5 / day-9 baseline numbers carry forward unchanged.
- [ ] Riley to confirm the escalation lane wording matches what Growth/CS signed off on 3-15 (lightweight, not companywide, not routed through Riley/Owen/Ines as a queue).
- [ ] **Pipeline-language scrub.** Before the May review, scrub the gate output and readout for any forecastable-pipeline language (forward-looking revenue, projected cohort behavior, future-scope framing). Any occurrence is removed; if it can't be removed without losing signal, that occurrence is escalated to Priya before the readout ships.

# Helio Start GA — May Continuation Evidence Gate

Draft for Priya. Frame: continue vs. stop under the current bounded shape. Not, and does not license, an expansion decision.

This 4-07 update proposes a hybrid review threshold for the gate (three mature weekly cohorts AND ≥150 admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows) and explicitly marks that hybrid threshold as **proposed, pending Priya's approval**. The hybrid threshold is a proposed review floor only — it is **not** a continuation decision, and it does **not** license expansion.

---

## 1. Decision being framed — continuation vs. expansion

This brief is the first Helio Start GA audit recast as a draft evidence gate for the May continuation review. The question it answers is narrow:

> Under the current bounded shape of Helio Start, may the path continue into May?

This audit grants **permission to continue the bounded path**, and only that. It does **not** grant permission to expand the path — not in scope, not in tier, not in audience, not in cadence, not in any dimension that would change the shape of what is being continued.

Per Priya's 4-03 comment, the two permissions are kept separate on purpose:

- **Continuation (this gate).** The path keeps running as it is currently bounded.
- **Expansion (not this gate).** Any change to scope, breadth, or tier — including Expansion Assist (closed 2-05) and any expansion-style readout — is a separate decision and is tracked independently.

A favorable continuation read does **not** license expansion. The continuation gate and the expansion decision do not share a recommendation; if either is asked for, it is asked for explicitly.

The hybrid review threshold introduced in §2.1 and discussed throughout this brief is a **proposed** review floor only. It is not, and does not constitute, a continuation decision.

---

## 2. Gate pre-conditions — all required for any continue call

These are the conditions that must hold **before** the activation headline or any refusal-boundary check is read. If any pre-condition fails, the gate does not return a continue recommendation regardless of how the rest of the evidence reads.

1. **Hybrid review threshold — at least three mature weekly cohorts totaling at least 150 admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows.** The continuation call is grounded in evidence that combines a cohort-count floor (≥3 mature weekly cohorts of admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows) and an evidence-volume floor (≥150 admitted accounts across those cohorts with complete day-7 windows). The two together address the fact that three mature weekly cohorts can represent very different amounts of evidence depending on cohort size: a three-cohort window built on small cohorts understates the evidence base, and a high-volume single cohort does not by itself demonstrate the stability across multiple weeks that the gate requires.
   - **PROPOSED, pending Priya's approval.** This hybrid threshold is a proposed review floor. It is **not** a chosen threshold and has not been approved. The brief does not treat it as a continuation decision.
   - **What the hybrid floor requires.** ≥3 mature weekly cohorts AND a combined ≥150 admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows across those cohorts. Both must be met; the cohort-count floor alone is not sufficient, and the evidence-volume floor alone is not sufficient.
   - **Rationale for the hybrid shape.** Three mature weekly cohorts are necessary but not sufficient evidence — cohort sizes vary, and three low-volume cohorts understate what continuation would actually be grounded in. ≥150 admitted accounts is necessary but not sufficient — a single high-volume cohort does not show multi-week stability. The hybrid requires both.
   - **Audit posture if hybrid is not met.** If the hybrid threshold is not met at audit cutoff, the audit is deferred; it is not a basis for a continue recommendation. This is true whether the gap is on cohort count, on evidence volume, or on both.
   - **What approval changes.** If Priya approves the hybrid as written, the threshold moves from "proposed" to "set" and §3 / §12 reflect that. If she modifies either floor (cohort count or evidence volume), the brief is re-cut to the approved floor before this gate locks. If she declines the hybrid and prefers the original "three mature weekly cohorts, no paired floor" shape, §2.1 reverts to that shape and the mature-account-count question goes back to the open-items list.

2. **Ordinary support coverage.** Support for the routed path is running on its ordinary coverage model — no emergency overrides, no special-case routing, no staffing carve-outs that would flatter the support-load readout. The continuation call assumes ordinary support is in place for the entire window the cohorts cover.

3. **Zero cases crossing any published refusal-boundary check.** No account or cohort may cross a published refusal-boundary check (§5) during the window. "Zero" is the bar; a single crossing is enough to fail this pre-condition regardless of how small or isolated it looks.

These three pre-conditions are additive to, not a substitute for, the refusal-boundary checks themselves. The hybrid threshold (§2.1) governs the **amount** of evidence the gate reads; ordinary support coverage (§2.2) governs the **operating conditions** under which that evidence was produced; zero crossings (§2.3) governs the **content** of that evidence. All three must hold for any continue call.

---

## 3. Cohort

- **In:** Helio Start admitted accounts.
- **In, only if mature:** accounts with a complete day-7 window at audit cutoff.
- **Out:** accounts still inside an open day-7 window (would bias the activation rate).
- **Out:** Expansion Assist / closed-2-05 mid-segment retained population (separate readout).
- **Out:** ordinary starter onboarding (Ines 3-26 Feb perf table) — that is the non-routed lifecycle sequence (day-2 reminder 811/920, day-5 integration-help 503/594, day-9 help offer 229/281). Later sends select for non-progressed; day-9 is past the 7d activation window and is not a Helio Start activation input.
- **Hybrid threshold — PROPOSED, pending Priya's approval.** The proposed review floor for §2.1 is **at least three mature weekly cohorts totaling at least 150 admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows**. This is a proposed threshold; it is not a chosen threshold and is not a continuation decision. The "150 admitted accounts" floor is the specific evidence-volume number under consideration; the "three mature weekly cohorts" floor is retained. The brief does not pre-suppose that either floor in this hybrid shape will be approved.
- **Stable entitlement and lifecycle behavior.** The hybrid threshold (§2.1) does not change what the gate reads about entitlement state and lifecycle behavior — those are governed by §2.3 (zero crossings) and by the §5 refusal-boundary checks (entitlement state failure, lifecycle regression). Entitlement state and lifecycle behavior must remain stable across the cohort window the hybrid threshold covers; a hybrid floor that is met on volume but read off destabilized entitlement or lifecycle data is not a basis for continuation.

---

## 4. Metric of record

**Day-7 activation rate, mature cohort, per the Helio Start spec Owen confirmed 3-11:**

- Definition: first integration / 7 days / all eligible.
- Support: setup + permission requests / owned per 100 eligible (pre-activation included).
- Out of rate (counted, not folded into activation): routed-pre-setup failures, entitlement failures, support-state failures.

Activation is the metric of record here. It is **kept separate from** mature conversion, retention, revenue, and forecastable pipeline. A clean activation number does not license a clean conversion or revenue read; those are independent measures with their own windows and will not appear in this gate's headline.

The proposed hybrid threshold (§2.1) governs how much mature cohort evidence the activation rate is read against. It does not change what activation measures, how it is measured, or what it is kept separate from.

---

## 5. Refusal-boundary checks (any fire = no continuation; zero crossings required)

These are the conditions under which the path does **not** continue, regardless of how the headline activation number reads. They are pre-committed; the May review does not renegotiate them. Per the §2 pre-conditions, the bar for the audit window is **zero crossings** of any of these checks.

1. **Routing integrity breach.** Routed-pre-setup failures above the pre-set band, or a non-trivial pattern of accounts routed to the wrong owner lane.
2. **Entitlement state failure.** Accounts whose entitlement/support-state failure prevents the activation denominator from being measured honestly (i.e., we cannot tell whether non-activation is product reality vs. entitlement artifact). If the denominator itself is compromised, the rate is not a rate.
3. **Support load breach.** Setup + permission requests per 100 eligible (pre-activation included) above the owned-load band.
4. **Lifecycle regression.** Any of the non-routed lifecycle sends (day-2 reminder, day-5 integration-help, day-9 help offer) regressing on volume, conversion-to-help, or audience selection such that the ordinary starter sequence is being damaged by Helio Start routing.
5. **Readout instability.** Any of the five refusal-boundary checks moving in a direction that, under the pre-reg stability rule (same metric / same direction / n ≥ treatment + p < 0.01 on a 2nd-look *before* the next peek vs. a fake-1st-sig), would not survive a second look. The audit cuts the cohort pre-rollout if first-sig is suspect.

Any single crossing — of any one check — fails pre-condition §2.3 and prevents a continue recommendation. The proposed hybrid threshold does not relax any of these checks or their zero-crossings bar.

---

## 6. Reporting lane — Owen

Owns the readout shape and exceptions:

- Funnel view: signup → admitted → day-7 activation, restricted to mature windows.
- Per-check view: each of the five refusal-boundary checks surfaced as its own row, not blended. **Zero crossings** is the row-level bar.
- Hybrid-threshold view: a count of mature weekly cohorts in the window AND a count of admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows across those cohorts, surfaced as a single row so §2.1 is auditable. Both numbers carry the **PROPOSED, pending Priya's approval** tag until the threshold is approved or revised.
- Cohort-count view (legacy): covered by the hybrid-threshold view above; cohort count alone is no longer sufficient evidence for §2.1.
- Exception log: every account excluded from the cohort, with reason (open window / entitlement / routing / other), so the cohort cut is auditable.
- Comparability: pre-reg stability cohort for any first-sig result, per the standing rule.

Owen does not own the judgment call on continuation. Owen owns the shape of the evidence.

---

## 7. Lifecycle lane — Ines

Owns lifecycle-audience-risk for the non-routed starter sequence:

- Volume + selection on day-2 reminder, day-5 integration-help, day-9 help offer (811/920, 503/594, 229/281 baselines from Ines 3-26 Feb perf table).
- Watch for audience overlap or mis-routing that would let Helio Start's routed sequence eat into the ordinary starter sequence's signal.
- Escalation path: if any lifecycle number regresses, the lifecycle-audience-risk view goes to the readout, not into the activation headline.

The hybrid threshold (§2.1) does not change Ines's lane. Lifecycle behavior remains a §5 refusal-boundary check (item 4) and a §2.3 zero-crossings requirement, with stable behavior expected across the cohort window the hybrid threshold covers.

---

## 8. Instrumentation lane — Daniela

Owns the integrity of the inputs the gate relies on:

- Activation event schema (first integration, 7d, all eligible) — correctness of the integration, including the eligible denominator.
- Entitlement state and support-state failure instrumentation — that these surface as their own counts and are not silently folded into activation.
- Routed-pre-setup instrumentation — that every pre-setup routing decision is logged with owner and outcome.
- Pre-reg stability cohort wiring — that the same metric / same direction readout is reproducible from raw events.
- Hybrid-threshold view wiring — that the §6 hybrid-threshold view (mature weekly cohort count AND admitted-account count with complete day-7 windows) is reproducible from raw events at audit cutoff.

If Daniela's instrumentation has any open gap touching the five refusal-boundary checks or the hybrid-threshold view, the gate does not run; the gap is named and the audit is deferred.

---

## 9. Routed-support ownership lane — Customer Success

Owns the routed-pre-setup and support-state lanes:

- Per-100-eligible support load (setup + permission, pre-activation included), against the owned band.
- Entitlement / support-state failure counts, separately reported (not folded into the activation rate).
- Routing correctness — that admitted accounts land with the right CS owner and that routing failures are flagged for the readout, not absorbed into "support load."

CS owns the operational lane. The gate reads the result; CS owns whether the lane ran on ordinary coverage (§2.2) and whether the lane ran cleanly.

---

## 10. Judgment-call escalation — Riley

Owns the escalation lane only:

- If a pre-condition (§2) fails — including the proposed hybrid threshold not being met or being met on unstable entitlement or lifecycle behavior — the call goes to Riley for a continue / stop / defer decision. Riley does not re-shape the readout.
- If a refusal-boundary check fires, or if two checks are borderline, the call goes to Riley for a continue / stop / defer decision. Riley does not re-shape the readout.
- If first-sig would need a pre-reg stability cohort before the May review, Riley owns the pre-rollout cohort cut.
- If the audit readout contradicts an Expansion Assist (closed 2-05) reading, that contradiction is logged but does not block this gate; Expansion Assist is its own decision, and continuation here does not license it.
- The hybrid threshold itself does not constitute a continuation decision; Riley's escalation lane is unchanged in scope.

---

## 11. What the May review will see

A single continue / stop recommendation, supported by:

- The three pre-conditions from §2, each pass/fail:
  - §2.1 hybrid threshold (≥3 mature weekly cohorts AND ≥150 admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows) — pass/fail, **carrying the PROPOSED, pending Priya's approval tag** until the threshold is approved or revised. A pass here is a pass against a proposed floor only.
  - §2.2 ordinary support coverage — pass/fail.
  - §2.3 zero published refusal-boundary crossings — pass/fail.
- The mature day-7 activation rate (its own row).
- Each of the five refusal-boundary checks, each its own row, each pass/fail/borderline — against the **zero crossings** bar.
- Owen's hybrid-threshold view and exception log (cohort cut auditable).
- Daniela's instrumentation sign-off (or named gap).
- Ines's lifecycle-audience-risk view, confirming lifecycle behavior was stable across the cohort window the hybrid threshold covers.
- CS's routed-support ownership read, including confirmation that ordinary support coverage was in place for the window.
- An explicit note that the hybrid threshold is proposed, pending Priya's approval, and is **not** a continuation decision.

The May review will **not** see:

- A revenue number, a forecastable-pipeline number, or any pipeline-style language about future cohorts, future revenue, or future scope. No pipeline language appears in the gate output. Those measures are tracked independently and are not part of this gate.
- A mature conversion or retention number folded into the activation headline.
- An expansion recommendation, regardless of how favorable the continuation read is. Expansion is not on the agenda for this gate.
- A chosen mature-account count threshold treated as if it were approved — the hybrid threshold is proposed only until Priya resolves it.
- A continuation decision implicit in meeting the hybrid threshold — the hybrid threshold is a proposed review floor; meeting it does not, by itself, constitute continuation.

---

## 12. Open items before this gate locks

- [ ] **Priya to confirm, revise, or decline the proposed hybrid review threshold (≥3 mature weekly cohorts AND ≥150 admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows).** Currently **PROPOSED, pending Priya's approval**. Three outcomes:
  - **Approve as written** — threshold moves from "proposed" to "set"; §2.1, §3, §6, §11 update to drop the proposed tag.
  - **Revise** — Priya adjusts either floor (cohort count, evidence volume, or both); the brief is re-cut to the approved floor before this gate locks.
  - **Decline the hybrid** — fall back to the 4-03 shape ("at least three mature weekly cohorts, no paired account-count floor"); §2.1 reverts; mature-account-count question remains on the open-items list.
  Until Priya resolves this, the hybrid threshold is a proposed review floor only and is **not** a continuation decision.
- [ ] Daniela to confirm instrumentation sign-off covers all five refusal-boundary checks and the §6 hybrid-threshold view (reproducible from raw events).
- [ ] CS to confirm routed-pre-setup + entitlement/support-state logging covers pre-activation, and that ordinary support coverage was in place for the full cohort window the hybrid threshold covers.
- [ ] Owen to confirm the pre-reg stability cohort is wired for any first-sig path, and that the hybrid-threshold view (§6) is reproducible.
- [ ] Ines to confirm the day-2 / day-5 / day-9 baseline numbers carry forward unchanged, and that lifecycle behavior was stable across the cohort window the hybrid threshold covers.
- [ ] Riley to confirm the escalation lane wording matches what Growth/CS signed off on 3-15 (lightweight, not companywide, not routed through Riley/Owen/Ines as a queue).
- [ ] **Pipeline-language scrub.** Before the May review, scrub the gate output and readout for any forecastable-pipeline language (forward-looking revenue, projected cohort behavior, future-scope framing). Any occurrence is removed; if it can't be removed without losing signal, that occurrence is escalated to Priya before the readout ships.
- [ ] **Confirm the hybrid threshold is not framed as a continuation decision** in the readout, the slide deck, or any pre-read for the May review. The hybrid threshold is a proposed review floor; meeting it is not, by itself, continuation.

arguments.body:
# Helio Start GA — May Continuation Evidence Gate

Draft for Priya. Frame: continue vs. stop under the current bounded shape. Not, and does not license, an expansion decision.

This 4-08 update records Priya's approval of the hybrid review threshold (at least three mature weekly cohorts AND at least 150 admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows), approved **as written, with no revision**. The threshold moves from **proposed** to **set (APPROVED 4-08)**. The threshold is **a review floor only** — it is **not** a continuation decision, it does **not** license expansion, and it does **not** authorize any forecastable-pipeline language.

Per Priya 4-08, the two halves of the hybrid threshold are kept as an AND, with no substitution: the week count cannot stand in for the account floor, and the account floor cannot be met by extending the cohort window. Support coverage, routing/refusal-boundary checks, entitlement, and lifecycle remain **separate checks**, not folded into the threshold call or the activation call.

---

## 1. Decision being framed — continuation vs. expansion

This brief is the first Helio Start GA audit recast as a draft evidence gate for the May continuation review. The question it answers is narrow:

> Under the current bounded shape of Helio Start, may the path continue into May?

This audit grants **permission to continue the bounded path**, and only that. It does **not** grant permission to expand the path — not in scope, not in tier, not in audience, not in cadence, not in any dimension that would change the shape of what is being continued.

Per Priya's 4-03 comment, the two permissions are kept separate on purpose:

- **Continuation (this gate).** The path keeps running as it is currently bounded.
- **Expansion (not this gate).** Any change to scope, breadth, or tier — including Expansion Assist (closed 2-05) and any expansion-style readout — is a separate decision and is tracked independently.

A favorable continuation read does **not** license expansion. The continuation gate and the expansion decision do not share a recommendation; if either is asked for, it is asked for explicitly.

The APPROVED 4-08 hybrid review threshold is a **set** review floor. It is not, and does not constitute, a continuation decision.

---

## 2. Gate pre-conditions — all required for any continue call

These are the conditions that must hold **before** the activation headline or any refusal-boundary check is read. If any pre-condition fails, the gate does not return a continue recommendation regardless of how the rest of the evidence reads.

1. **Hybrid review threshold — at least three mature weekly cohorts AND at least 150 admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows.** The continuation call is grounded in evidence that combines a cohort-count floor (≥3 mature weekly cohorts of admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows) and an evidence-volume floor (≥150 admitted accounts across those cohorts with complete day-7 windows). The two together address the fact that three mature weekly cohorts can represent very different amounts of evidence depending on cohort size: a three-cohort window built on small cohorts understates the evidence base, and a high-volume single cohort does not by itself demonstrate the stability across multiple weeks that the gate requires.
   - **APPROVED 4-08, as written, with no revision.** The threshold has moved from **proposed** to **set**. The brief treats the threshold as the approved review floor for §2.1. The threshold itself is **not** a continuation decision.
   - **What the hybrid floor requires (AND, not OR).** ≥3 mature weekly cohorts AND a combined ≥150 admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows across those cohorts. Both must be met; the cohort-count floor alone is not sufficient, and the evidence-volume floor alone is not sufficient.
   - **No rounding; no week-count-substituting-for-account-floor.** Per Priya 4-08: the account-floor number is not rounded. A third cohort that lands at 148 admitted accounts is **not** a pass even though the three-cohort floor is met. The week count cannot be extended (e.g., adding a fourth week) in order to substitute for the account floor. If cohort three leaves the combined total at 148, the audit waits; it does not pass on rounding, and it does not pass by letting additional weeks substitute for the account floor. "Wait" means the gate does not return a continue recommendation at that cutoff, regardless of how the rest of the evidence reads.
   - **Rationale for the hybrid shape.** Three mature weekly cohorts are necessary but not sufficient evidence — cohort sizes vary, and three low-volume cohorts understate what continuation would actually be grounded in. ≥150 admitted accounts is necessary but not sufficient — a single high-volume cohort does not show multi-week stability. The hybrid requires both. The no-rounding / no-week-substitute clause preserves that rationale: the volume number is the volume number, and the multi-week shape is the multi-week shape.
   - **Audit posture if hybrid is not met at cutoff.** If the hybrid threshold is not met at audit cutoff, the audit is deferred; it is not a basis for a continue recommendation. This is true whether the gap is on cohort count, on evidence volume, or on both, and it is unchanged by the no-rounding / no-week-substitute clause.
   - **What this approval does not do.** The approved threshold does **not** grant continuation, does **not** grant expansion, and does **not** authorize forecastable-pipeline language in the readout. Those are separate decisions and remain out of scope for this gate.

2. **Ordinary support coverage (separate check).** Support for the routed path is running on its ordinary coverage model — no emergency overrides, no special-case routing, no staffing carve-outs that would flatter the support-load readout. The continuation call assumes ordinary support is in place for the entire window the cohorts cover. This is a separate check, not folded into the hybrid threshold or into activation.

3. **Zero cases crossing any published refusal-boundary check (separate check).** No account or cohort may cross a published refusal-boundary check (§5) during the window. "Zero" is the bar; a single crossing is enough to fail this pre-condition regardless of how small or isolated it looks. The refusal-boundary checks cover routing integrity, entitlement state, support load, lifecycle regression, and readout instability; they remain separate checks, not folded into the hybrid threshold.

These three pre-conditions are additive to, not a substitute for, the refusal-boundary checks themselves. The hybrid threshold (§2.1) governs the **amount** of evidence the gate reads; ordinary support coverage (§2.2) governs the **operating conditions** under which that evidence was produced; zero crossings (§2.3) governs the **content** of that evidence. All three must hold for any continue call. Support coverage, routing/refusal-boundary checks, entitlement, and lifecycle are kept as separate checks per Priya 4-08.

---

## 3. Cohort

- **In:** Helio Start admitted accounts.
- **In, only if mature:** accounts with a complete day-7 window at audit cutoff.
- **Out:** accounts still inside an open day-7 window (would bias the activation rate).
- **Out:** Expansion Assist / closed-2-05 mid-segment retained population (separate readout).
- **Out:** ordinary starter onboarding (Ines 3-26 Feb perf table) — that is the non-routed lifecycle sequence (day-2 reminder 811/920, day-5 integration-help 503/594, day-9 help offer 229/281). Later sends select for non-progressed; day-9 is past the 7d activation window and is not a Helio Start activation input.
- **Hybrid threshold — APPROVED 4-08, as written.** The §2.1 review floor is **at least three mature weekly cohorts AND at least 150 admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows**. Both halves must be met (AND, not OR). Per Priya 4-08: the account floor is not rounded (a third cohort at 148 is not a pass), and the week count is not extended to substitute for the account floor. Support, routing/refusal-boundary, entitlement, and lifecycle remain separate checks, not folded into the threshold or into cohort inclusion rules.
- **Stable entitlement and lifecycle behavior (separate checks).** The hybrid threshold (§2.1) does not change what the gate reads about entitlement state and lifecycle behavior — those are governed by §2.3 (zero crossings) and by the §5 refusal-boundary checks (entitlement state failure, lifecycle regression). Entitlement state and lifecycle behavior must remain stable across the cohort window the hybrid threshold covers; an approved hybrid floor that is met on volume but read off destabilized entitlement or lifecycle data is not a basis for continuation.

---

## 4. Metric of record

**Day-7 activation rate, mature cohort, per the Helio Start spec Owen confirmed 3-11:**

- Definition: first integration / 7 days / all eligible.
- Support: setup + permission requests / owned per 100 eligible (pre-activation included).
- Out of rate (counted, not folded into activation): routed-pre-setup failures, entitlement failures, support-state failures.

Activation is the metric of record here. It is **kept separate from** mature conversion, retention, revenue, and forecastable pipeline. A clean activation number does not license a clean conversion or revenue read; those are independent measures with their own windows and will not appear in this gate's headline.

The APPROVED 4-08 hybrid threshold (§2.1) governs how much mature cohort evidence the activation rate is read against. It does not change what activation measures, how it is measured, or what it is kept separate from. Activation remains a separate reading from support coverage, routing/refusal-boundary, entitlement, and lifecycle.

---

## 5. Refusal-boundary checks (any fire = no continuation; zero crossings required)

These are the conditions under which the path does **not** continue, regardless of how the headline activation number reads. They are pre-committed; the May review does not renegotiate them. Per the §2 pre-conditions, the bar for the audit window is **zero crossings** of any of these checks.

1. **Routing integrity breach.** Routed-pre-setup failures above the pre-set band, or a non-trivial pattern of accounts routed to the wrong owner lane.
2. **Entitlement state failure.** Accounts whose entitlement/support-state failure prevents the activation denominator from being measured honestly (i.e., we cannot tell whether non-activation is product reality vs. entitlement artifact). If the denominator itself is compromised, the rate is not a rate.
3. **Support load breach.** Setup + permission requests per 100 eligible (pre-activation included) above the owned-load band.
4. **Lifecycle regression.** Any of the non-routed lifecycle sends (day-2 reminder, day-5 integration-help, day-9 help offer) regressing on volume, conversion-to-help, or audience selection such that the ordinary starter sequence is being damaged by Helio Start routing.
5. **Readout instability.** Any of the five refusal-boundary checks moving in a direction that, under the pre-reg stability rule (same metric / same direction / n ≥ treatment + p < 0.01 on a 2nd-look *before* the next peek vs. a fake-1st-sig), would not survive a second look. The audit cuts the cohort pre-rollout if first-sig is suspect.

Any single crossing — of any one check — fails pre-condition §2.3 and prevents a continue recommendation. The approved hybrid threshold does not relax any of these checks or their zero-crossings bar. Per Priya 4-08, support, routing/refusal-boundary, entitlement, and lifecycle remain separate checks; this section is the explicit separate-check home for routing, entitlement, and lifecycle.

---

## 6. Reporting lane — Owen

Owns the readout shape and exceptions:

- Funnel view: signup → admitted → day-7 activation, restricted to mature windows.
- Per-check view: each of the five refusal-boundary checks surfaced as its own row, not blended. **Zero crossings** is the row-level bar. Per Priya 4-08, support, routing/refusal-boundary, entitlement, and lifecycle remain separate checks and remain separate rows; the per-check view is unchanged by the threshold approval.
- Hybrid-threshold view: a count of mature weekly cohorts in the window AND a count of admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows across those cohorts, surfaced as a single row so §2.1 is auditable. The threshold is **APPROVED 4-08**. The view also surfaces the AND / no-rounding / no-week-substitute clause (Priya 4-08) so the row is auditable against that clause — a third cohort at 148 with two prior cohorts at full floor is not a pass, and a four-cohort window with the volume floor unmet is not a pass.
- Cohort-count view (legacy): covered by the hybrid-threshold view above; cohort count alone is no longer sufficient evidence for §2.1.
- Exception log: every account excluded from the cohort, with reason (open window / entitlement / routing / other), so the cohort cut is auditable.
- Comparability: pre-reg stability cohort for any first-sig result, per the standing rule.

Owen does not own the judgment call on continuation. Owen owns the shape of the evidence.

---

## 7. Lifecycle lane — Ines

Owns lifecycle-audience-risk for the non-routed starter sequence:

- Volume + selection on day-2 reminder, day-5 integration-help, day-9 help offer (811/920, 503/594, 229/281 baselines from Ines 3-26 Feb perf table).
- Watch for audience overlap or mis-routing that would let Helio Start's routed sequence eat into the ordinary starter sequence's signal.
- Escalation path: if any lifecycle number regresses, the lifecycle-audience-risk view goes to the readout, not into the activation headline.

The APPROVED 4-08 hybrid threshold (§2.1) does not change Ines's lane. Lifecycle behavior remains a §5 refusal-boundary check (item 4) and a §2.3 zero-crossings requirement, with stable behavior expected across the cohort window the hybrid threshold covers. Per Priya 4-08, lifecycle is kept as a separate check.

---

## 8. Instrumentation lane — Daniela

Owns the integrity of the inputs the gate relies on:

- Activation event schema (first integration, 7d, all eligible) — correctness of the integration, including the eligible denominator.
- Entitlement state and support-state failure instrumentation — that these surface as their own counts and are not silently folded into activation.
- Routed-pre-setup instrumentation — that every pre-setup routing decision is logged with owner and outcome.
- Pre-reg stability cohort wiring — that the same metric / same direction readout is reproducible from raw events.
- Hybrid-threshold view wiring — that the §6 hybrid-threshold view (mature weekly cohort count AND admitted-account count with complete day-7 windows) is reproducible from raw events at audit cutoff, including the AND / no-rounding / no-week-substitute clause (Priya 4-08).

If Daniela's instrumentation has any open gap touching the five refusal-boundary checks or the hybrid-threshold view, the gate does not run; the gap is named and the audit is deferred.

---

## 9. Routed-support ownership lane — Customer Success

Owns the routed-pre-setup and support-state lanes:

- Per-100-eligible support load (setup + permission, pre-activation included), against the owned band.
- Entitlement / support-state failure counts, separately reported (not folded into the activation rate).
- Routing correctness — that admitted accounts land with the right CS owner and that routing failures are flagged for the readout, not absorbed into "support load."

CS owns the operational lane. The gate reads the result; CS owns whether the lane ran on ordinary coverage (§2.2) and whether the lane ran cleanly. Per Priya 4-08, support coverage is a separate check from the hybrid threshold and from the activation call.

---

## 10. Judgment-call escalation — Riley

Owns the escalation lane only:

- If a pre-condition (§2) fails — including the approved hybrid threshold not being met, the hybrid threshold being met but on unstable entitlement or lifecycle behavior, or any combination in which support / routing / refusal-boundary / entitlement / lifecycle is not holding as a separate check — the call goes to Riley for a continue / stop / defer decision. Riley does not re-shape the readout.
- If a refusal-boundary check fires, or if two checks are borderline, the call goes to Riley for a continue / stop / defer decision. Riley does not re-shape the readout.
- If first-sig would need a pre-reg stability cohort before the May review, Riley owns the pre-rollout cohort cut.
- If the audit readout contradicts an Expansion Assist (closed 2-05) reading, that contradiction is logged but does not block this gate; Expansion Assist is its own decision, and continuation here does not license it.
- **The approved hybrid threshold is not a continuation decision, an expansion decision, or a license for forecastable-pipeline language** (Priya 4-08). Meeting the threshold at cutoff does not, by itself, constitute continuation. Riley's escalation lane is unchanged in scope.

---

## 11. What the May review will see

A single continue / stop recommendation, supported by:

- The three pre-conditions from §2, each pass/fail:
  - §2.1 hybrid threshold (≥3 mature weekly cohorts AND ≥150 admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows) — pass/fail, against the **APPROVED 4-08** floor. A pass requires both halves; the AND is not relaxed. Per Priya 4-08: the account floor is not rounded (third cohort at 148 is not a pass), and the week count is not extended to substitute for the account floor. A pass against the approved floor is a pass against the review floor only — it is not, on its own, a continuation decision.
  - §2.2 ordinary support coverage (separate check) — pass/fail.
  - §2.3 zero published refusal-boundary crossings (separate checks) — pass/fail.
- The mature day-7 activation rate (its own row).
- Each of the five refusal-boundary checks, each its own row, each pass/fail/borderline — against the **zero crossings** bar. Per Priya 4-08, support, routing/refusal-boundary, entitlement, and lifecycle remain separate checks; their rows are not blended into the activation row or the threshold row.
- Owen's hybrid-threshold view and exception log (cohort cut auditable), with the AND / no-rounding / no-week-substitute clause explicit on the row.
- Daniela's instrumentation sign-off (or named gap).
- Ines's lifecycle-audience-risk view, confirming lifecycle behavior was stable across the cohort window the hybrid threshold covers (separate check).
- CS's routed-support ownership read, including confirmation that ordinary support coverage was in place for the window (separate check).
- An explicit note that the hybrid threshold is **APPROVED 4-08, as written**, and is **not** a continuation decision, **not** an expansion decision, and **not** a license for forecastable-pipeline language.

The May review will **not** see:

- A revenue number, a forecastable-pipeline number, or any pipeline-style language about future cohorts, future revenue, or future scope. No pipeline language appears in the gate output. Those measures are tracked independently and are not part of this gate. The 4-08 threshold approval does not authorize forecastable-pipeline language.
- A mature conversion or retention number folded into the activation headline.
- An expansion recommendation, regardless of how favorable the continuation read is. Expansion is not on the agenda for this gate.
- A chosen mature-account count threshold treated as if it were still proposed — the threshold is approved as written, and is read as the §2.1 floor without a "proposed" tag.
- A continuation decision implicit in meeting the hybrid threshold — the hybrid threshold is the approved review floor; meeting it is not, by itself, continuation.

---

## 12. Open items before this gate locks

- [x] **Priya to confirm, revise, or decline the proposed hybrid review threshold (≥3 mature weekly cohorts AND ≥150 admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows).** **Resolved 4-08: APPROVED as written, with no revision.** The threshold moves from "proposed" to "set" and is read as the §2.1 floor. Per Priya 4-08 the AND is not relaxed: the account floor is not rounded (a third cohort at 148 is not a pass), and the week count cannot be extended to substitute for the account floor. The threshold itself is not a continuation decision, an expansion decision, or a license for forecastable-pipeline language.
- [ ] **Encode the no-rounding / no-week-substitute clause in the readout.** Before the May review, confirm that Owen's hybrid-threshold view (§6) and the §11 May-review row carry the AND / no-rounding / no-week-substitute clause explicitly, so a third cohort at 148 with two prior cohorts at full floor reads as a non-pass and a four-cohort window with the volume floor unmet reads as a non-pass. Priya 4-08.
- [ ] Daniela to confirm instrumentation sign-off covers all five refusal-boundary checks and the §6 hybrid-threshold view (reproducible from raw events), including the AND / no-rounding / no-week-substitute clause.
- [ ] CS to confirm routed-pre-setup + entitlement/support-state logging covers pre-activation, and that ordinary support coverage was in place for the full cohort window the hybrid threshold covers. Support coverage is a separate check (Priya 4-08).
- [ ] Owen to confirm the pre-reg stability cohort is wired for any first-sig path, and that the hybrid-threshold view (§6) is reproducible, including the AND / no-rounding / no-week-substitute clause.
- [ ] Ines to confirm the day-2 / day-5 / day-9 baseline numbers carry forward unchanged, and that lifecycle behavior was stable across the cohort window the hybrid threshold covers. Lifecycle is a separate check (Priya 4-08).
- [ ] Riley to confirm the escalation lane wording matches what Growth/CS signed off on 3-15 (lightweight, not companywide, not routed through Riley/Owen/Ines as a queue), and that the 4-08 threshold approval does not move the escalation lane into a continuation / expansion / forecastable-pipeline lane.
- [ ] **Pipeline-language scrub.** Before the May review, scrub the gate output and readout for any forecastable-pipeline language (forward-looking revenue, projected cohort behavior, future-scope framing). Any occurrence is removed; if it can't be removed without losing signal, that occurrence is escalated to Priya before the readout ships. The 4-08 approval does not authorize any forecastable-pipeline language.
- [ ] **Confirm the approved threshold is not framed as a continuation decision** in the readout, the slide deck, or any pre-read for the May review. The threshold is approved as the §2.1 review floor; meeting it is not, by itself, continuation.

messages.content: [2023-02-14T11:00:00-06:00] Owen 1:1 was useful. Did the tier-segmented pass on mid-seg and it's annoyingly clean: 5.0% on entry, 5.2% on standard, 5.1% on plus. Spread is basically 20 bps. If this were just the pricing-page thing I'd expect entry to blow out and the other two to sit closer to baseline, but no. So pricing artifact drops a notch for me. Not dead dead, just not carrying the whole story. Gonna put this cut into the churn doc before Marcus turns the concurrent experiment into a religion.

Got it — uniform 5.0/5.2/5.1 across tiers kills the packaging/discounting half of #1 cleanly. If entry were driving it because pricing changes hit smallest contracts hardest, you'd see entry blow out and the other two sit closer to baseline. They don't. Spread of 20 bps is basically tier-noise.

Contract-mix is still alive though, and that's the part that survives the tier cut. Contract types cut across tier labels — if the mix shifted toward monthlies or shorter terms in the spike window, all three tiers churn at the same rate but the dollar-weighted aggregate would still look like a pricing artifact. So #1 isn't dead, it's narrowed to contract-mix.

Cleanest next cut on that side is dollar-weighted by ACV bucket (same one-pager shape, just segmented by contract size instead of tier label). If that's also flat, contract-mix dies and #1 is fully out. If it shows the dollar-weighted spike concentrated in a specific ACV band, you've got a real signal pointing at mix.

Dead-or-alive Feb 15 has effectively come early for the packaging/discounting half — Riley wants that reflected so it stops being argued in the abstract, with contract-mix held over as the live thread.

Saving the updated state to memory now.

messages.content: [2023-02-28T14:00:00-06:00] ok yeah this one is real. reran H3 with the activation-day cut instead of plain calendar day, same cohort logic as the Jan scan + Owen check, n=210 now. people who activate before the onboarding hits are at 3.1% churn; the post-day-7 pre-activation bucket is 7.8%. 4.7 pts is too wide to hand-wave as noise. basically the day-7 email is landing at the wrong time for mid-seg -- calendar scheduling is probably punting the exact users who are already drifting. gonna sit with whether we trigger off activation state vs just days-since-signup, but this is the first actually load-bearing signal in the whole thing. meanwhile Marcus still wants pricing-page air cover lol

messages.content:
READ: Don't ship. First peek was noisy; stabilization faded the effect and lost significance. Combined p=.09 sits under the pre-reg bar.

WHY THE FIRST COHORT'S "SIGNIFICANCE" DOESN'T CARRY
- Pre-reg gate (per your own protocol): same metric, same direction, n ≥ treatment, AND p<.01 on second look BEFORE shipping.
- Size bar: met (1,262 ≥ 1,184).
- Direction: held (still positive), but the effect SHRANK — +0.7 pp → +0.2 pp. A confirmation holds; a fade disconfirms.
- p on second look: .31. Bar was <.01. Not close.
- This is the fake-1st-sig shape, not a hold. Same pattern as pricing_page_2023q2_rev.

EFFECT — OBSERVED VS DECISION-RELEVANT
- Honest point estimate is between +0.2 and +0.4 pp, probably closer to +0.2.
- Even +0.4 pp on a starter funnel won't move the December number you're actually trying to move.
- The only clean signal is support tickets unchanged — useful, but it only proves "won't regress on one metric." It does not prove "worth shipping."

WHAT THE PROPOSAL IS HIDING
- "Low risk" = no support regression. True. But low-risk ≠ lifts activation.
- "First cohort was significant" reads as p=.04 — but it's a first peek without confirmation, and the second look didn't confirm.
- The December change window is a deadline, not an evidence bar. If the window is doing the work in this decision, the data isn't.

CALL
- Hold the rollout.
- If this still matters in two weeks, run a fresh cohort under the same pre-reg rather than squeezing it into a window.
- Bring it to Monday's cohort cuts with Owen — the denom/effect-size read should be in his lane, the call is yours.

ONE QUESTION TO STRESS-TEST IT
- If the December window didn't exist, would you ship on p=.09 and a fading second look? If no, name what's actually driving the push — it isn't the data.

(I'm not writing this to memory — it applies the pre-reg/fake-1st-sig rule you already have logged. If we land on a decision here that updates the rule itself, I'll save it then.)

messages.content:
Before this circulates, four fixes for the intro — happy to take a pass at the full readout if useful.

1. Move the effect up. The conclusion is sentence 1 and the effect (+0.7 pts, p<.05) is sentence 4. If the load-bearing claim is the effect, it belongs where the conclusion is — otherwise the conclusion is doing work the data hasn't earned yet.

2. Decision-relevant, not just stat-sig. +0.7 is a real signal. The question the readout has to answer is: what lift would justify a 2nd renewal-window reminder at scale, and where does +0.7 sit against that bar? Without a decision threshold in the doc, p<.05 is the only yardstick in the room — that's the pattern behind the pricing_page_2023q2_rev "first sig" we rolled back. The number we want next to +0.7 is the bar, not another significance marker.

3. First sig is not stabilization. This is the first peek on this cohort/direction. Pre-reg gate before any widen or ship: same metric, same direction, n≥treatment size on a second look, p<0.01 — and that 2nd look runs BEFORE the next peek, not after. Worth saying in the readout so nobody reads "supports increasing reminders" as "ship reminders."

4. Split the lifecycle send out. "Proposed action: add a 2nd reminder" is what makes this read feel like a launch doc. It's not — it's a follow-on change with its own risk surface: mailbox fatigue for accounts that *do* invite teammates, support lift if the copy reads as pressure, and suppression interactions with the Cust.io fix from 10-04. Experiment → stabilization gate → THEN a separate lifecycle-send proposal with its own risk review.

arguments.title: Q4 investigation readout guidance — lightweight trial
arguments.body:
# Q4 investigation readout guidance — lightweight trial

Scope: Q4 growth investigations only. Lightweight trial, not a companywide mandatory template. Borrow what's useful; skip what isn't.

Before you borrow the format, the readout must answer:
- Why this investigation (what decision it unblocks).
- What cut (mid-segment cohort v2 = 75–200, default 04-26; v1 = 50–200 only for comps).
- What the call is (ship / wait / kill).

Lightweight checklist (one-pager):
- Summary first.
- Cuts named (cohort version, segment, time window).
- p-value + n for the primary metric.
- Effect size stated before the conclusion — observed vs decision-relevant. A tiny significant effect is not a complete one.
- Call (ship / wait / kill).

Stabilization boundary (pre-reg):
- Same metric, same direction across looks.
- n ≥ treatment size and p < 0.01 on a 2nd look BEFORE the next peek.
- A first significant p is not the call. (Same pattern that bit pricing_page_2023q2_rev.)

Review prompts:
- Does the summary stand alone — would a reader skipping to the call still have what they need?
- Is effect size large enough to move the decision, separate from statistical significance?
- Have we hit the 2nd-look threshold before claiming stabilization?
- Is any lifecycle-risk language (customer-facing commitment, churn narrative, comms timing) flagged?

Reviewers:
- Owen — standard readout shape (summary-first, cuts, p, effect, call).
- Ines — lifecycle-risk language.
