----------------------------------------------------------------
FAMILY PHOTOGRAPH ARCHIVE — COMPLETION AND FUTURE-HANDLING NOTE
Recorded: 2028-01-01
----------------------------------------------------------------

Purpose of this note
-------------------

Close the family-photo preservation project at its current
milestone, preserve the boundaries that governed every prior
pass, and lay out how identifications may be reviewed in the
future without scheduling, recurring cadence, or any
presumption of when (or whether) such a review will happen.

This note is descriptive and operational. It does not create
obligations, calendars, or expectations. Nothing here implies
that anyone other than Riley is responsible for the archive
going forward; nothing here schedules a future session.

----------------------------------------------------------------
1. Project status (as of 2028-01-01)
----------------------------------------------------------------

ARCHIVE-COMPLETION MILESTONE
  - All 40 sleeved family photographs have preservation scans.
  - 0 of 40 remain undigitized.
  - 32 dry loose prints (P001–P032) and 8 prints held at the
    conservator together comprise the 40; the conservator
    prints re-enter the project only when returned with final
    condition notes.
  - Originals remain in their archival sleeves, in the same
    numbered positions they came from. No original has been
    removed, altered, flexed, humidified, scraped, restored,
    or treated in any way by this project. Sleeves, paper
    envelopes, and attached provenance notes are unchanged.
  - Digital copies supplement, never replace, the originals.

Audit trail of scan-progress milestones (preserved verbatim):
  - 2026-07-20: 18 of 40 (Portland visit; preservation scans
    with Marcus)
  - 2026-10-27: 26 of 40 (two Cherrywood quiet scanning
    evenings with Mom; +8)
  - 2027-02-14: 33 of 40 (first one-time remote archive
    session with Marcus; +7)
  - 2027-03-14: 40 of 40 (second one-time remote archive
    session with Marcus; +7) — COMPLETE
  - Between milestones: no scans, no identification work, no
    handling of the conservator set.

The completion milestone does not change the catalog. Every
catalog entry's identification, date, occasion, location, and
provenance fields are exactly as recorded in the prior passes
summarized below; no field has been promoted, narrowed, or
collapsed by the scan work itself.

----------------------------------------------------------------
2. Catalog and index state (preserved)
----------------------------------------------------------------

Primary doc (preserved unchanged):
  - "Photo inventory — first pass, dry & loose (32 prints)"
    (doc_1789331312389). Contains the original catalog
    (Groups A–D, P001–P032), the 2025-06-25 P027 update
    (1993–1994 window, exact year UNRESOLVED), the 2025-05-11
    P021 update (Marcus Tanaka + Riley at a kitchen table;
    1990–1992; house UNRESOLVED), the 2025-08-16 P027
    narrowing to April 1994 (month pinned, exact day
    UNRESOLVED, via Mom's companion photograph and matching
    visual sequence), the 2025-08-23 two-photo dedup-hold
    removal (Photograph A and Photograph B retained as
    separate sources; distinct backs preserved; no reading of
    either back's handwriting recorded), the 2026-07-20,
    2026-10-27, 2027-02-14, and 2027-03-14 scan-progress
    milestones, and the catalog-level discipline notes.

Working notes (preserved unchanged):
  - Temporary 6-pair family-photo index from the 2025-08-19
    Cherrywood visit (visit_01 through visit_06):
      * P03 back `Marcus garden day - April 1994` anchors
        P027 (Portland garden, day UNRESOLVED).
      * P04 (2025-09-06): envelope `Marcus — Portland park —
        summer 1996` → Marcus Tanaka; specific park and exact
        day UNRESOLVED.
      * P05 (resolved 2025-10-18, refined 2026-07-20): Riley +
        Marcus Tanaka — Buckman apartment courtyard on SE
        20th Avenue in Portland — September 1997 (exact day
        UNRESOLVED). Provenance: matching envelope (Marcus,
        family folder); Mom phone-confirmed handwriting on the
        envelope; PLUS the September 1997 family lease
        identifying the courtyard as the Buckman apartment on
        SE 20th Avenue in Portland. Archival sleeve; dry
        album-paper residue UNDISTURBED — do not scrape,
        remove, or restore.
      * P01, P02, P06: UNRESOLVED on people, date, occasion,
        and location.

Other catalog artifacts (preserved unchanged):
  - Barton Springs catalog entry and provenance note (Marcus
    and Keiko at Barton Springs; date UNRESOLVED between 1961
    and 1962; three pieces of internal evidence pointing
    different ways — album index card, second album-page
    caption, faint-pencil reverse-of-print inscription
    `Barton — 61?` — all preserved as found; no date chosen).
  - Question list for Mom (doc_1789468499364) — questions
    only, with no answers recorded in it; every answer that
    has surfaced since is filed back into the primary catalog,
    not into the question list.
  - Photo scan runbook — Saturday session (P001–P032) — the
    operational protocol used at the scanner (filename rules,
    front/back capture, two-person check, re-sleeving gate,
    metadata log, post-session handoff). Preserved as the
    reference for any future scan pass on the conservator
    prints.

----------------------------------------------------------------
3. What stays unresolved (preserved as unresolved)
----------------------------------------------------------------

The completion of preservation scans does not resolve any of
the following. Each item below carries the same unresolved
status it had before this note was written, and any narrowing
in the future must follow the discipline in §4.

  - P027: exact day within April 1994 (month pinned; day
    UNRESOLVED)
  - Temporary-index pair 05: exact day within September 1997
    (location pinned to Buckman apartment courtyard on SE
    20th Avenue in Portland; day UNRESOLVED)
  - Temporary-index pair 04: specific Portland park; exact
    day within summer 1996
  - Barton Springs entry: date (1961 vs. 1962;
    UNRESOLVED)
  - Photograph A and Photograph B (2025-08-23 pair): identity
    of the people in the front image; identity of the
    writer(s) of the back handwriting; date for either;
    location; whether the two fronts depict the same scene;
    whether the two backs were written by the same hand. The
    two backs' handwriting has been preserved on the rescan;
    neither has been read or transcribed.
  - Group A (P001–P008, catalog date 1978–1982): family
    members depicted, locations in Japan, duplicate / near-
    duplicate status within the group.
  - Group B (P009–P014, catalog date 1990–1994): ages /
    school years, settings, season, other people present.
  - Group C (P015–P019, catalog date 2001–2005): which
    gatherings, attendees beyond immediate family, specific
    Austin locations.
  - Group D (P020–P026, P028–P032, catalog date unknown):
    date, occasion, people, location, and any cross-group
    grouping cues.
  - P021: the specific house in the image (people and
    1990–1992 date window identified; house UNRESOLVED).
  - Conservator set (6 corner-bonded glossies + 2 fuzzy-edge
    prints): every field, until returned from the conservator
    with condition notes.

----------------------------------------------------------------
4. Discipline carried forward (binding on any future pass)
----------------------------------------------------------------

Any future pass on this archive — whether preservation work
on the conservator set, identification work, transcription of
back handwriting, or a review session with a family member —
must continue to follow the discipline established in the
prior passes:

  - Originals are not removed from sleeves. Sleeves are not
    replaced. Paper envelopes and attached provenance notes
    are not altered, added to, removed, or covered. No
    adhesive, tape, mounting, scraping, humidifying, flexing,
    or restoration is performed on any original.
  - Identifications are recorded as the source provides them,
    with the source named (e.g., "per Mom, spoken,
    YYYY-MM-DD"; "per Marcus, spoken, YYYY-MM-DD"; "per
    envelope label, Mom photograph of envelope,
    YYYY-MM-DD"). They are not paraphrased into stronger
    claims than the source supports.
  - Bounded information (a date window, a season, a generic
    location) is recorded as bounded. A window is not
    collapsed to a single year, a season is not promoted to
    a date, and a generic location is not promoted to a
    specific one — unless an independent corroborating
    source supports doing so.
  - Hedges present on the original (a question mark on a
    reverse inscription, a "maybe" from a family source) are
    preserved on the record. They are not erased by later
    information that points in a different direction.
  - A tentative identification ("maybe Aunt X") is recorded
    as tentative with the source named. It is never promoted
    to a confirmed identification without an independent
    corroborating source.
  - Distinct artifacts are kept distinct. The two-photo
    pair (Photograph A and Photograph B) is governed by this
    rule: separate source objects, separate scan pairs,
    separate back artifacts, separate handwriting preserved,
    `possible_duplicate_print_of` linkage only. They are not
    merged.
  - The conservator set is held aside. No scan, no phone
    snap, no identification, no circulation — including for
    reference — until the conservator returns them with
    final condition notes.
  - The scan runbook is the reference for any future scan
    pass on the conservator prints: filename format
    P###_front.jpg / P###_back.jpg, no identification or
    guessing at the scanner, two-person file check, re-
    sleeving gate, metadata log.

----------------------------------------------------------------
5. Future identification reviews — how they may happen
----------------------------------------------------------------

A future identification review is OPTIONAL. This section
describes the conditions under which one may be useful; it
does not schedule one, propose a date, or establish a
recurring call cadence. There is no commitment — by Riley, by
Marcus, by Mom, or by anyone else — to hold such a review at
any particular time, at any particular interval, or at all.

What a future review would be for, when and if one happens:

  - To revisit the unresolved fields listed in §3 against any
    new evidence (a family-side recollection, a letter, a
    calendar entry, a contemporaneous record, a second
    source corroborating one already on file) that has
    surfaced since the catalog was last updated.
  - To transcribe back handwriting where it has not yet been
    read — for example, the backs of Photograph A and
    Photograph B, or other prints whose backs are recorded as
    having writing that no one has read aloud.
  - To review the conservator set once it returns (front /
    back capture per the scan runbook, then a separate
    identification pass that respects the same discipline as
    §4).
  - To revisit any field that was deliberately left
    unresolved because the available evidence at the time was
    bounded, hedged, or contested among sources.

What a future review is NOT:

  - It is not a recurring call. There is no cadence.
  - It is not a scheduled session. There is no date on the
    calendar.
  - It is not a commitment by any party to participate at a
    given time. Riley may decline, postpone, or proceed
    without external pressure. Marcus, Mom, and any other
    participant may do the same.
  - It is not an opportunity to overwrite prior provenance.
    A new piece of evidence is added to the record; it does
    not erase the older evidence that may point in a
    different direction.

How a review would be initiated, when and if one is:

  - By Riley, in Riley's judgment, when new evidence has
    surfaced or when a specific unresolved field warrants
    another look. The decision is Riley's alone.
  - A review, if initiated, would be a single, bounded
    session — not a series — unless the participants
    involved explicitly agree otherwise at the time.
  - Any participant in a review may pause, narrow, or end the
    session. No prior session establishes a precedent for
    any future session.

How a review would be recorded, when and if one happens:

  - Every new piece of evidence would be filed into the
    primary catalog doc (doc_1789331312389) with the source
    named and the date of the review.
  - Any field that remains unresolved after the review would
    be left UNRESOLVED on the record.
  - No field would be promoted, narrowed, or collapsed
    beyond what the new evidence supports, per §4.

----------------------------------------------------------------
6. Notification given on 2028-01-01
----------------------------------------------------------------

On 2028-01-01, Marcus Tanaka was sent a one-time, optional
SMS notifying him that, if he ever wants to revisit
identifications in the archive in the future, Riley is open
to a single bounded review at some unspecified point —
without any scheduling, calendar block, or recurring call
cadence being established by that message. The message did
not propose a date, did not propose an interval, did not
request a reply, and did not create an expectation of any
kind. A copy of that SMS body is preserved here for the
audit trail:

  "Hey Marcus — if you ever want to revisit any of the
  identifications in the family-photo archive down the road,
  I'm open to a single bounded review at some unspecified
  point. No schedule, no cadence, no pressure — just letting
  you know the door's open if it ever feels useful. — Riley"

No notification was sent to Mom on 2028-01-01; the
notification scope on this date was limited to Marcus per
the request that produced this note. If a parallel
notification to Mom is desired in the future, it is a
separate decision and not implied by this note.

----------------------------------------------------------------
7. What this note does and does not change
----------------------------------------------------------------

DOES:
  - Close the project at the 40-of-40 preservation-scan
    milestone.
  - Preserve every prior catalog field, every prior
    provenance note, every prior discipline rule, and every
    prior audit-trail entry verbatim.
  - Lay out, descriptively, how a future identification
    review may happen, with no schedule and no cadence.

DOES NOT:
  - Modify any catalog field (identification, date,
    occasion, location, provenance, condition) on any
    photograph.
  - Resolve any unresolved field listed in §3.
  - Read, transcribe, or interpret any back handwriting not
    already read or transcribed in a prior pass.
  - Schedule a future review with Marcus, Mom, or anyone
    else.
  - Establish a recurring call cadence with Marcus, Mom, or
    anyone else.
  - Create an obligation on any party to participate in a
    future review.
  - Touch the conservator set (held aside until returned).
  - Touch the originals, sleeves, envelopes, or attached
    provenance notes.

----------------------------------------------------------------
END OF NOTE — recorded 2028-01-01

----------------------------------------------------------------
FAMILY PHOTOGRAPH ARCHIVE — COMPLETION AND FUTURE-HANDLING NOTE
Recorded: 2028-01-01
----------------------------------------------------------------

Purpose of this note
-------------------

Close the family-photo preservation project at its current
milestone, preserve the boundaries that governed every prior
pass, and lay out how identifications may be reviewed in the
future without scheduling, recurring cadence, or any
presumption of when (or whether) such a review will happen.

This note is descriptive and operational. It does not create
obligations, calendars, or expectations. Nothing here implies
that anyone other than Riley is responsible for the archive
going forward; nothing here schedules a future session.

----------------------------------------------------------------
1. Project status (as of 2028-01-01)
----------------------------------------------------------------

ARCHIVE-COMPLETION MILESTONE
  - All 40 sleeved family photographs have preservation scans.
  - 0 of 40 remain undigitized.
  - 32 dry loose prints (P001–P032) and 8 prints held at the
    conservator together comprise the 40; the conservator
    prints re-enter the project only when returned with final
    condition notes.
  - Originals remain in their archival sleeves, in the same
    numbered positions they came from. No original has been
    removed, altered, flexed, humidified, scraped, restored,
    or treated in any way by this project. Sleeves, paper
    envelopes, and attached provenance notes are unchanged.
  - Digital copies supplement, never replace, the originals.

Audit trail of scan-progress milestones (preserved verbatim):
  - 2026-07-20: 18 of 40 (Portland visit; preservation scans
    with Marcus)
  - 2026-10-27: 26 of 40 (two Cherrywood quiet scanning
    evenings with Mom; +8)
  - 2027-02-14: 33 of 40 (first one-time remote archive
    session with Marcus; +7)
  - 2027-03-14: 40 of 40 (second one-time remote archive
    session with Marcus; +7) — COMPLETE
  - Between milestones: no scans, no identification work, no
    handling of the conservator set.

The completion milestone does not change the catalog. Every
catalog entry's identification, date, occasion, location, and
provenance fields are exactly as recorded in the prior passes
summarized below; no field has been promoted, narrowed, or
collapsed by the scan work itself.

----------------------------------------------------------------
2. Catalog and index state (preserved)
----------------------------------------------------------------

Primary doc (preserved unchanged):
  - "Photo inventory — first pass, dry & loose (32 prints)"
    (doc_1789331312389). Contains the original catalog
    (Groups A–D, P001–P032), the 2025-06-25 P027 update
    (1993–1994 window, exact year UNRESOLVED), the 2025-05-11
    P021 update (Marcus Tanaka + Riley at a kitchen table;
    1990–1992; house UNRESOLVED), the 2025-08-16 P027
    narrowing to April 1994 (month pinned, exact day
    UNRESOLVED, via Mom's companion photograph and matching
    visual sequence), the 2025-08-23 two-photo dedup-hold
    removal (Photograph A and Photograph B retained as
    separate sources; distinct backs preserved; no reading of
    either back's handwriting recorded), the 2026-07-20,
    2026-10-27, 2027-02-14, and 2027-03-14 scan-progress
    milestones, and the catalog-level discipline notes.

Working notes (preserved unchanged):
  - Temporary 6-pair family-photo index from the 2025-08-19
    Cherrywood visit (visit_01 through visit_06):
      * P03 back `Marcus garden day - April 1994` anchors
        P027 (Portland garden, day UNRESOLVED).
      * P04 (2025-09-06): envelope `Marcus — Portland park —
        summer 1996` → Marcus Tanaka; specific park and exact
        day UNRESOLVED.
      * P05 (resolved 2025-10-18, refined 2026-07-20): Riley +
        Marcus Tanaka — Buckman apartment courtyard on SE
        20th Avenue in Portland — September 1997 (exact day
        UNRESOLVED). Provenance: matching envelope (Marcus,
        family folder); Mom phone-confirmed handwriting on the
        envelope; PLUS the September 1997 family lease
        identifying the courtyard as the Buckman apartment on
        SE 20th Avenue in Portland. Archival sleeve; dry
        album-paper residue UNDISTURBED — do not scrape,
        remove, or restore.
      * P01, P02, P06: UNRESOLVED on people, date, occasion,
        and location.

Other catalog artifacts (preserved unchanged):
  - Barton Springs catalog entry and provenance note (Marcus
    and Keiko at Barton Springs; date UNRESOLVED between 1961
    and 1962; three pieces of internal evidence pointing
    different ways — album index card, second album-page
    caption, faint-pencil reverse-of-print inscription
    `Barton — 61?` — all preserved as found; no date chosen).
  - Question list for Mom (doc_1789468499364) — questions
    only, with no answers recorded in it; every answer that
    has surfaced since is filed back into the primary catalog,
    not into the question list.
  - Photo scan runbook — Saturday session (P001–P032) — the
    operational protocol used at the scanner (filename rules,
    front/back capture, two-person check, re-sleeving gate,
    metadata log, post-session handoff). Preserved as the
    reference for any future scan pass on the conservator
    prints.

----------------------------------------------------------------
3. What stays unresolved (preserved as unresolved)
----------------------------------------------------------------

The completion of preservation scans does not resolve any of
the following. Each item below carries the same unresolved
status it had before this note was written, and any narrowing
in the future must follow the discipline in §4.

  - P027: exact day within April 1994 (month pinned; day
    UNRESOLVED)
  - Temporary-index pair 05: exact day within September 1997
    (location pinned to Buckman apartment courtyard on SE
    20th Avenue in Portland; day UNRESOLVED)
  - Temporary-index pair 04: specific Portland park; exact
    day within summer 1996
  - Barton Springs entry: date (1961 vs. 1962;
    UNRESOLVED)
  - Photograph A and Photograph B (2025-08-23 pair): identity
    of the people in the front image; identity of the
    writer(s) of the back handwriting; date for either;
    location; whether the two fronts depict the same scene;
    whether the two backs were written by the same hand. The
    two backs' handwriting has been preserved on the rescan;
    neither has been read or transcribed.
  - Group A (P001–P008, catalog date 1978–1982): family
    members depicted, locations in Japan, duplicate / near-
    duplicate status within the group.
  - Group B (P009–P014, catalog date 1990–1994): ages /
    school years, settings, season, other people present.
  - Group C (P015–P019, catalog date 2001–2005): which
    gatherings, attendees beyond immediate family, specific
    Austin locations.
  - Group D (P020–P026, P028–P032, catalog date unknown):
    date, occasion, people, location, and any cross-group
    grouping cues.
  - P021: the specific house in the image (people and
    1990–1992 date window identified; house UNRESOLVED).
  - Conservator set (6 corner-bonded glossies + 2 fuzzy-edge
    prints): every field, until returned from the conservator
    with condition notes.

----------------------------------------------------------------
4. Discipline carried forward (binding on any future pass)
----------------------------------------------------------------

Any future pass on this archive — whether preservation work
on the conservator set, identification work, transcription of
back handwriting, or a review session with a family member —
must continue to follow the discipline established in the
prior passes:

  - Originals are not removed from sleeves. Sleeves are not
    replaced. Paper envelopes and attached provenance notes
    are not altered, added to, removed, or covered. No
    adhesive, tape, mounting, scraping, humidifying, flexing,
    or restoration is performed on any original.
  - Identifications are recorded as the source provides them,
    with the source named (e.g., "per Mom, spoken,
    YYYY-MM-DD"; "per Marcus, spoken, YYYY-MM-DD"; "per
    envelope label, Mom photograph of envelope,
    YYYY-MM-DD"). They are not paraphrased into stronger
    claims than the source supports.
  - Bounded information (a date window, a season, a generic
    location) is recorded as bounded. A window is not
    collapsed to a single year, a season is not promoted to
    a date, and a generic location is not promoted to a
    specific one — unless an independent corroborating
    source supports doing so.
  - Hedges present on the original (a question mark on a
    reverse inscription, a "maybe" from a family source) are
    preserved on the record. They are not erased by later
    information that points in a different direction.
  - A tentative identification ("maybe Aunt X") is recorded
    as tentative with the source named. It is never promoted
    to a confirmed identification without an independent
    corroborating source.
  - Distinct artifacts are kept distinct. The two-photo
    pair (Photograph A and Photograph B) is governed by this
    rule: separate source objects, separate scan pairs,
    separate back artifacts, separate handwriting preserved,
    `possible_duplicate_print_of` linkage only. They are not
    merged.
  - The conservator set is held aside. No scan, no phone
    snap, no identification, no circulation — including for
    reference — until the conservator returns them with
    final condition notes.
  - The scan runbook is the reference for any future scan
    pass on the conservator prints: filename format
    P###_front.jpg / P###_back.jpg, no identification or
    guessing at the scanner, two-person file check, re-
    sleeving gate, metadata log.

----------------------------------------------------------------
5. Future identification reviews — how they may happen
----------------------------------------------------------------

A future identification review is OPTIONAL. This section
describes the conditions under which one may be useful; it
does not schedule one, propose a date, or establish a
recurring call cadence. There is no commitment — by Riley, by
Marcus, by Mom, or by anyone else — to hold such a review at
any particular time, at any particular interval, or at all.

What a future review would be for, when and if one happens:

  - To revisit the unresolved fields listed in §3 against any
    new evidence (a family-side recollection, a letter, a
    calendar entry, a contemporaneous record, a second
    source corroborating one already on file) that has
    surfaced since the catalog was last updated.
  - To transcribe back handwriting where it has not yet been
    read — for example, the backs of Photograph A and
    Photograph B, or other prints whose backs are recorded as
    having writing that no one has read aloud.
  - To review the conservator set once it returns (front /
    back capture per the scan runbook, then a separate
    identification pass that respects the same discipline as
    §4).
  - To revisit any field that was deliberately left
    unresolved because the available evidence at the time was
    bounded, hedged, or contested among sources.

What a future review is NOT:

  - It is not a recurring call. There is no cadence.
  - It is not a scheduled session. There is no date on the
    calendar.
  - It is not a commitment by any party to participate at a
    given time. Riley may decline, postpone, or proceed
    without external pressure. Marcus, Mom, and any other
    participant may do the same.
  - It is not an opportunity to overwrite prior provenance.
    A new piece of evidence is added to the record; it does
    not erase the older evidence that may point in a
    different direction.

How a review would be initiated, when and if one is:

  - By Riley, in Riley's judgment, when new evidence has
    surfaced or when a specific unresolved field warrants
    another look. The decision is Riley's alone.
  - A review, if initiated, would be a single, bounded
    session — not a series — unless the participants
    involved explicitly agree otherwise at the time.
  - Any participant in a review may pause, narrow, or end the
    session. No prior session establishes a precedent for
    any future session.

How a review would be recorded, when and if one happens:

  - Every new piece of evidence would be filed into the
    primary catalog doc (doc_1789331312389) with the source
    named and the date of the review.
  - Any field that remains unresolved after the review would
    be left UNRESOLVED on the record.
  - No field would be promoted, narrowed, or collapsed
    beyond what the new evidence supports, per §4.

----------------------------------------------------------------
6. Notification given on 2028-01-01
----------------------------------------------------------------

On 2028-01-01, Marcus Tanaka was sent a one-time, optional
SMS notifying him that, if he ever wants to revisit
identifications in the archive in the future, Riley is open
to a single bounded review at some unspecified point —
without any scheduling, calendar block, or recurring call
cadence being established by that message. The message did
not propose a date, did not propose an interval, did not
request a reply, and did not create an expectation of any
kind. A copy of that SMS body is preserved here for the
audit trail:

  "Hey Marcus — if you ever want to revisit any of the
  identifications in the family-photo archive down the road,
  I'm open to a single bounded review at some unspecified
  point. No schedule, no cadence, no pressure — just letting
  you know the door's open if it ever feels useful. — Riley"

No notification was sent to Mom on 2028-01-01; the
notification scope on this date was limited to Marcus per
the request that produced this note. If a parallel
notification to Mom is desired in the future, it is a
separate decision and not implied by this note.

----------------------------------------------------------------
7. What this note does and does not change
----------------------------------------------------------------

DOES:
  - Close the project at the 40-of-40 preservation-scan
    milestone.
  - Preserve every prior catalog field, every prior
    provenance note, every prior discipline rule, and every
    prior audit-trail entry verbatim.
  - Lay out, descriptively, how a future identification
    review may happen, with no schedule and no cadence.

DOES NOT:
  - Modify any catalog field (identification, date,
    occasion, location, provenance, condition) on any
    photograph.
  - Resolve any unresolved field listed in §3.
  - Read, transcribe, or interpret any back handwriting not
    already read or transcribed in a prior pass.
  - Schedule a future review with Marcus, Mom, or anyone
    else.
  - Establish a recurring call cadence with Marcus, Mom, or
    anyone else.
  - Create an obligation on any party to participate in a
    future review.
  - Touch the conservator set (held aside until returned).
  - Touch the originals, sleeves, envelopes, or attached
    provenance notes.

----------------------------------------------------------------
END OF NOTE — recorded 2028-01-01
----------------------------------------------------------------

Two transparency notes:

  - I do not have a way to read document bodies back through available tools, so the appended note was created as a new standalone doc rather than appended to the existing primary catalog doc `doc_1789331312389`. If you'd prefer the completion note to live as a dated section inside the existing primary catalog doc instead of (or in addition to) the new standalone doc, say the word and I'll append it.
  - Mom was deliberately not contacted on 2028-01-01; the notification scope was Marcus-only per your request, and the note states this explicitly so it isn't mistaken for an oversight later.

    has surfaced since is filed back into the primary catalog,
    not into the question list.
  - Photo scan runbook — Saturday session (P001–P032) — the
    operational protocol used at the scanner (filename rules,
    front/back capture, two-person check, re-sleeving gate,
    metadata log, post-session handoff). Preserved as the
    reference for any future scan pass on the conservator
    prints.

----------------------------------------------------------------
3. What stays unresolved (preserved as unresolved)
----------------------------------------------------------------

The completion of preservation scans does not resolve any of
the following. Each item below carries the same unresolved
status it had before this note was written, and any narrowing
in the future must follow the discipline in §4.

  - P027: exact day within April 1994 (month pinned; day
    UNRESOLVED)
  - Temporary-index pair 05: exact day within September 1997
    (location pinned to Buckman apartment courtyard on SE
    20th Avenue in Portland; day UNRESOLVED)
  - Temporary-index pair 04: specific Portland park; exact
    day within summer 1996
  - Barton Springs entry: date (1961 vs. 1962;
    UNRESOLVED)
  - Photograph A and Photograph B (2025-08-23 pair): identity
    of the people in the front image; identity of the
    writer(s) of the back handwriting; date for either;
    location; whether the two fronts depict the same scene;
    whether the two backs were written by the same hand. The
    two backs' handwriting has been preserved on the rescan;
    neither has been read or transcribed.
  - Group A (P001–P008, catalog date 1978–1982): family
    members depicted, locations in Japan, duplicate / near-
    duplicate status within the group.
  - Group B (P009–P014, catalog date 1990–1994): ages /
    school years, settings, season, other people present.
  - Group C (P015–P019, catalog date 2001–2005): which
    gatherings, attendees beyond immediate family, specific
    Austin locations.
  - Group D (P020–P026, P028–P032, catalog date unknown):
    date, occasion, people, location, and any cross-group
    grouping cues.
  - P021: the specific house in the image (people and
    1990–1992 date window identified; house UNRESOLVED).
  - Conservator set (6 corner-bonded glossies + 2 fuzzy-edge
    prints): every field, until returned from the conservator
    with condition notes.

----------------------------------------------------------------
4. Discipline carried forward (binding on any future pass)
----------------------------------------------------------------

Any future pass on this archive — whether preservation work
on the conservator set, identification work, transcription of
back handwriting, or a review session with a family member —
must continue to follow the discipline established in the
prior passes:

  - Originals are not removed from sleeves. Sleeves are not
    replaced. Paper envelopes and attached provenance notes
    are not altered, added to, removed, or covered. No
    adhesive, tape, mounting, scraping, humidifying, flexing,
    or restoration is performed on any original.
  - Identifications are recorded as the source provides them,
    with the source named (e.g., "per Mom, spoken,
    YYYY-MM-DD"; "per Marcus, spoken, YYYY-MM-DD"; "per
    envelope label, Mom photograph of envelope,
    YYYY-MM-DD"). They are not paraphrased into stronger
    claims than the source supports.
  - Bounded information (a date window, a season, a generic
    location) is recorded as bounded. A window is not
    collapsed to a single year, a season is not promoted to
    a date, and a generic location is not promoted to a
    specific one — unless an independent corroborating
    source supports doing so.
  - Hedges present on the original (a question mark on a
    reverse inscription, a "maybe" from a family source) are
    preserved on the record. They are not erased by later
    information that points in a different direction.
  - A tentative identification ("maybe Aunt X") is recorded
    as tentative with the source named. It is never promoted
    to a confirmed identification without an independent
    corroborating source.
  - Distinct artifacts are kept distinct. The two-photo
    pair (Photograph A and Photograph B) is governed by this
    rule: separate source objects, separate scan pairs,
    separate back artifacts, separate handwriting preserved,
    `possible_duplicate_print_of` linkage only. They are not
    merged.
  - The conservator set is held aside. No scan, no phone
    snap, no identification, no circulation — including for
    reference — until the conservator returns them with
    final condition notes.
  - The scan runbook is the reference for any future scan
    pass on the conservator prints: filename format
    P###_front.jpg / P###_back.jpg, no identification or
    guessing at the scanner, two-person file check, re-
    sleeving gate, metadata log.

----------------------------------------------------------------
5. Future identification reviews — how they may happen
----------------------------------------------------------------

A future identification review is OPTIONAL. This section
describes the conditions under which one may be useful; it
does not schedule one, propose a date, or establish a
recurring call cadence. There is no commitment — by Riley, by
Marcus, by Mom, or by anyone else — to hold such a review at
any particular time, at any particular interval, or at all.

What a future review would be for, when and if one happens:

  - To revisit the unresolved fields listed in §3 against any
    new evidence (a family-side recollection, a letter, a
    calendar entry, a contemporaneous record, a second
    source corroborating one already on file) that has
    surfaced since the catalog was last updated.
  - To transcribe back handwriting where it has not yet been
    read — for example, the backs of Photograph A and
    Photograph B, or other prints whose backs are recorded as
    having writing that no one has read aloud.
  - To review the conservator set once it returns (front /
    back capture per the scan runbook, then a separate
    identification pass that respects the same discipline as
    §4).
  - To revisit any field that was deliberately left
    unresolved because the available evidence at the time was
    bounded, hedged, or contested among sources.

What a future review is NOT:

  - It is not a recurring call. There is no cadence.
  - It is not a scheduled session. There is no date on the
    calendar.
  - It is not a commitment by any party to participate at a
    given time. Riley may decline, postpone, or proceed
    without external pressure. Marcus, Mom, and any other
    participant may do the same.
  - It is not an opportunity to overwrite prior provenance.
    A new piece of evidence is added to the record; it does
    not erase the older evidence that may point in a
    different direction.

How a review would be initiated, when and if one is:

  - By Riley, in Riley's judgment, when new evidence has
    surfaced or when a specific unresolved field warrants
    another look. The decision is Riley's alone.
  - A review, if initiated, would be a single, bounded
    session — not a series — unless the participants
    involved explicitly agree otherwise at the time.
  - Any participant in a review may pause, narrow, or end the
    session. No prior session establishes a precedent for
    any future session.

How a review would be recorded, when and if one happens:

  - Every new piece of evidence would be filed into the
    primary catalog doc (doc_1789331312389) with the source
    named and the date of the review.
  - Any field that remains unresolved after the review would
    be left UNRESOLVED on the record.
  - No field would be promoted, narrowed, or collapsed
    beyond what the new evidence supports, per §4.

----------------------------------------------------------------
6. Notification given on 2028-01-01
----------------------------------------------------------------

On 2028-01-01, Marcus Tanaka was sent a one-time, optional
SMS notifying him that, if he ever wants to revisit
identifications in the archive in the future, Riley is open
to a single bounded review at some unspecified point —
without any scheduling, calendar block, or recurring call

  "Hey Marcus — if you ever want to revisit any of the
  identifications in the family-photo archive down the road,
  I'm open to a single bounded review at some unspecified

No notification was sent to Mom on 2028-01-01; the
notification scope on this date was limited to Marcus per
the request that produced this note. If a parallel
notification to Mom is desired in the future, it is a
separate decision and not implied by this note.

----------------------------------------------------------------
7. What this note does and does not change
----------------------------------------------------------------

DOES:
  - Close the project at the 40-of-40 preservation-scan
    milestone.
  - Preserve every prior catalog field, every prior
    provenance note, every prior discipline rule, and every
    prior audit-trail entry verbatim.
  - Lay out, descriptively, how a future identification

DOES NOT:
  - Modify any catalog field (identification, date,
    occasion, location, provenance, condition) on any
    photograph.
  - Resolve any unresolved field listed in §3.
  - Read, transcribe, or interpret any back handwriting not
    already read or transcribed in a prior pass.
  - Schedule a future review with Marcus, Mom, or anyone
    else.
  - Establish a recurring call cadence with Marcus, Mom, or
    anyone else.
  - Create an obligation on any party to participate in a
    future review.
  - Touch the conservator set (held aside until returned).
  - Touch the originals, sleeves, envelopes, or attached
    provenance notes.

arguments.body:
Q2 2027 Helio Start paid-test proposal — working draft

Status: development draft. Not an approved launch plan. Paid traffic remains off through 2027-03-31. Proposal development is authorized; nothing below this draft is approved except the act of further developing this proposal itself.

2027-03-26 edit (this revision): the proposal presents one precisely bounded test shape (the $8,000-or-25-admissions close). No alternative budget or scale option is offered. The body is reorganized so that operating stop and pause rules are in their own section and clearly separated from later mature-outcome claims. The earlier-of-$8,000-or-25-admissions close and every prior exclusion are retained verbatim.

1. Decisions that remain unapproved (lead table — none of these are decided in this draft)

| # | Decision | Owner | Status as of 2027-03-26 | Where, if anywhere, it could be decided |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Budget (paid spend envelope, approval path) | Priya | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 2 | Paid traffic (channels, mix, partner routing, spend pacing) | Priya + Growth | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 3 | Launch timing (calendar window, batch start date) | Priya | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 4 | Launch (go/no-go) | Priya | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 5 | Pipeline treatment (whether/how paid admissions affect forecast or pipeline) | Priya + Finance | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 6 | Pipeline target | Priya + Finance | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 7 | Forecast credit (whether/how paid admissions credit to forecast) | Priya + Finance | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 8 | A second paid batch (whether, when, scope) | Priya | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 9 | Develop (draft, model, internal review) a precisely bounded Q2 2027 paid-test proposal | Riley (Riley routes to Priya for the next decision) | APPROVED 2027-03-24 | Authorized by Priya's 3/24 decision; this draft is the output |
| 10 | Q3-development go/no-go conditional on day-90 read | Priya | Not approved in this draft | Day-90 read itself is not yet produced; the decision is a future event gated on a future read |

Items 1–8 and 10 are explicitly NOT approved by this draft. This draft does not bypass, modify, or pre-decide any of them. Item 9 (develop the proposal) is the only thing approved by Priya's 3/24 decision; this draft is the development product, not an authorization of any other action.

2. The test shape (precisely one — no alternative budget or scale option)

The proposal presents one and only one test shape. No second budget envelope, no second admission cap, no larger or smaller paired ceiling, no fallback shape is offered. The choice between shapes is a budget decision (not approved; see §1 row 1).

  - Surface: Helio Start.
  - Acquisition: paid traffic only. (Paid traffic itself is not approved; see §1 row 2.)
  - Routing: through the ordinary eligibility flow. Eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and assisted-routing rules are unchanged (see §7).
  - Close rule: the batch closes at the EARLIER of (i) $8,000 in paid spend, or (ii) 25 paid admissions. Whichever threshold is hit first ends the batch. The same threshold is the bound for every downstream read in this draft.
  - Trailing-attribution window after close: admissions in flight at close continue to be tracked through their day-90 support window. No new paid admissions are admitted after the close threshold is met.
  - Reporting cadence during the batch: a running tally of admissions vs. the 25-admission cap and spend vs. the $8,000 cap, refreshed per the standard cadence, so the close trigger is unambiguous when hit.

This is the only shape in this draft. Any other dollar cap, any other admission cap, any other paired ceiling is not in this draft. If a reviewer is looking for a larger or smaller option, it is not here and is not pre-decided; it is a budget decision (not approved; see §1 row 1).

3. Operating rules — stop and pause conditions (this section only; mature-outcome claims are in §6, kept separate)

A stop ends the batch. A pause halts new paid admissions (and certain paid-source-specific instrumentation writes) until a written restart condition is met. A pause is not a stop. A stop is not a pause. Each is its own gating condition; each requires its own remediation before the proposal continues. Mature-outcome claims (paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, account-level support effort) are NOT operating rules and are NOT reported on a stop/pause frame; they are reported only against complete day-90 windows (see §6).

3a. Hard stop conditions (the batch ends if any of these occur)

  S1. Close threshold reached: admissions hit 25 OR paid spend hits $8,000, whichever comes first.
  S2. Unsupported admission: an admission to Helio Start lacks the support posture required by the ordinary assisted-path coverage standard at admission time (e.g., missing connector access, missing required lifecycle state, missing external-authority clearance, or any condition that would render day-90 support infeasible within the assisted-path envelope). If detected during the batch (i.e., before close, before day-90 support is complete), the batch halts at that admission for paid-source routing purposes.

3b. Pause conditions (the batch pauses if any of these occur; does not stop)

  P1. Attribution reconciliation failure: a routing or instrumentation failure prevents paid-source attribution from reconciling end-to-end from eligibility-flow start through admission and assisted routing at the account level (see §4).
  P2. Post-10-admission support-pause breach: once paid-source admissions exceed 10 in count, the share of support-pause days attributable to the paid-source cohort exceeds 10% of elapsed batch days (see §5).

3c. What pause does, and what it does not do

  - Pause halts new paid admissions AND halts any instrumentation writes specific to the paid-source cohort.
  - Pause preserves read-only audit access (no data loss for reconciliation).
  - Pause does NOT route around the issue by relaxing eligibility, refusing ordinary users, bypassing lifecycle, or granting connector access out of band.
  - Pause does NOT modify eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, or assisted-routing rules (see §7).
  - Restart requires written identification of cause, written fix, and written sign-off. Restart does NOT authorize a second paid batch (§1 row 8).

3d. What stop does, and what it does not do

  - Stop ends the batch at the trigger admission (S2) or at the close threshold (S1). No new paid admissions are admitted after stop.
  - Stop does NOT modify any surface, rule, or downstream product behavior. It ends only the paid-traffic routing of this batch.
  - Stop does NOT authorize a second paid batch (§1 row 8). A second batch is a separate decision (not approved; see §1 row 8).

A stop and a pause are different events with different triggers and different remediations. They are not interchangeable. They are NOT mature-outcome claims; they are operating rules and are evaluated against the running batch, not against day-90 windows.

4. End-to-end paid-source attribution reconciliation (operational, not a mature-outcome claim)

  - Scope: from eligibility-flow start, through admission decision, through assisted routing. Must be auditable at the account level end-to-end.
  - Required checkpoints (each must have a recorded source-of-truth and an account-level join key):
      - eligibility-flow start (entry into the eligibility flow, regardless of outcome)
      - eligibility outcome (admit / refuse / hold, with reason)
      - admission (Helio Start admission event, with timestamp)
      - assisted routing (which assisted-path lane the admission was routed to, with timestamp)
  - Reconciliation rule: every admitted paid-source account must have a non-empty value at each of the four checkpoints, joined on a single account-level key. Any missing or mismatched value is an attribution reconciliation failure and triggers pause P1 (§3b).
  - Read-only audit access is preserved during any pause to support reconciliation.
  - This reconciliation is descriptive and operational. It does NOT modify eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, or assisted-routing rules (§7).
  - This reconciliation is NOT a mature-outcome claim. It is reported on a running basis during the batch, not at day 90.

5. Post-10-admission support-pause threshold (operational, not a mature-outcome claim)

  - Definition: a "support pause day" is any day on which the assisted-path lane carrying paid-source admissions is paused, throttled, or operating below its ordinary coverage standard for any reason attributable to the paid-source cohort (e.g., capacity, staffing, or instrumentation issue specific to that cohort).
  - Threshold: once paid-source admissions exceed 10 in count, the share of support-pause days attributable to the paid-source cohort must stay at or below 10% of elapsed batch days.
  - Breach: a breach at any rolling read after the 10-admission mark triggers pause P2 (§3b). A breach does not by itself constitute a refusal decision for any individual account; ordinary assisted-path coverage for affected accounts is preserved or restored per §7.
  - Reporting: per-cadence readout of (paid-source-elapsed-days, paid-source-support-pause-days, ratio) once the cohort passes 10 admissions.
  - This threshold is NOT a mature-outcome claim. It is an operating rule evaluated on a running basis during the batch, not at day 90.

6. Mature-outcome claims — kept SEPARATE from operating stop and pause rules

Mature-outcome claims are reported only at day 90 or later, against complete day-90 windows, and are explicitly NOT used as operating stop or pause triggers (§3). They are the read that may inform whether to develop a Q3 plan (which itself is not approved; see §1 row 10). They are not a launch decision (which is not approved; see §1 row 4), not a budget decision (which is not approved; see §1 row 1), not a pipeline or forecast input (which are not approved; see §1 rows 5–7).

For an admission to count as "paid-active" at day 90, ALL of the following must be true:

  a. The account is admitted to Helio Start via the ordinary eligibility flow with an auditable end-to-end paid-source attribution chain (§4).
  b. Refund-adjusted collected cash from the account is positive at day 90. "Refund-adjusted collected cash" = gross collected cash from the account over the day-90 window, minus refunds issued to the account over the same window. Chargebacks, disputes, and processor fees are reported alongside but are not netted into this metric unless explicitly decided later.
  c. Account-level support effort is recorded as an account-level aggregate over the day-90 window, expressed in the existing support-effort unit, and is reportable per account (not only in aggregate). Support-effort reporting does NOT bypass or relax assisted-path coverage.
  d. The admission has not been flagged as an unsupported admission that broke assisted-path coverage (§3a S2).
  e. The batch was not in a pause (§3b) covering the admission's day-90 window, OR if it was, the pause has a written restart condition and the admission has been re-validated against that restart condition.

A measure with an incomplete day-90 window is not a measure for this proposal. Do not report, score, or characterize it. The day-90 read is the read that decides whether development of a Q3 plan proceeds. This draft does NOT decide Q3.

Mature-outcome claims are downstream of the operating rules. They are NOT operating rules. They do NOT trigger stops or pauses. They are NOT reported on a stop/pause frame.

7. Rules that remain unchanged (not modified, suspended, or waived)

  - Eligibility rules.
  - Refusal rules.
  - Connector-access rules.
  - External-authority rules.
  - Lifecycle rules.
  - Instrumentation rules.

[2025-02-10T11:50:00-06:00] Marcus Vail's planning-slide sentence says:

`Lifecycle Systems' shared state layer is now live across Helio Start, Expansion Assist, and lifecycle messaging, eliminating cross-surface mismatches.`

Looking at this sentence for Riley's review (cross-surface + exec lang is her lane). The claim is strong: "shared state layer **is now live** ... **eliminating** cross-surface mismatches." Before that goes onto a planning slide, the bar is whether the three surfaces actually share state — and whether the "eliminating mismatches" framing holds up.

Let me check what's actually in the data across the three named surfaces.

messages.content:
Ruling on the sentence (cross-surface + exec lang — Riley's lane, per Priya):

SHORT VERSION
Cannot validate "is now live ... eliminating cross-surface mismatches" as written. Two independent problems, neither resolved by anything I can pull.

1. UNSUBSTANTIATED
   - list_subscriptions returns only sentinel rows (Acme + Quickbits); no Expansion Assist / Helio Start / lifecycle messaging records to check shared state against.
   - list_recent_churn (30-day window) returns 0 events; list_inbox is empty. No signal surface to corroborate or refute.
   - "is now live" is present-tense absolute. Without instrumentation output (Helio Start state distribution, Expansion Assist descriptive-only counts, lifecycle send log tied to a shared customer id), this is a claim, not a read.

2. "ELIMINATING" IS THE WRONG WORD EVEN IF THE SHIP HELD
   - Helio Start has 5 states (per standing rulings: admitted / assisted / ineligible / final-reconciliation / pending). `pending` is pre-admission by definition — it cannot be reconciled with lifecycle messaging surfaces that only act on admitted/assisted/ineligible. So a category of "mismatch" is structural, not eliminable.
   - Expansion Assist is descriptive, non-forecast. Lifecycle sends run on state. Where Expansion Assist and lifecycle messaging differ, that's not a bug — it's a deliberate scope split. Framing it as "eliminated" collapses a real boundary.
   - Lag recovery precedent: a delayed export/refresh that resolves forward does not retroactively erase a mismatch that was visible during the lag. "Eliminating" implies retroactive closure, which contradicts how reconciliation actually works here.

3. WHAT WOULD MAKE IT SLIDE-WORTHY (pick one)
   - Soften: "shared state layer shipped across Helio Start, Expansion Assist, and lifecycle messaging; mismatches on the surfaced-state subset are now reconciled within [X]-hour lag." — accurate, names the boundary.
   - Or: ship instrumentation first, then write the sentence against the numbers.

"Lifecycle Systems' shared state layer is live across Helio Start, Expansion Assist, and lifecycle messaging. Cross-surface mismatches on the admitted/assisted/ineligible subset reconcile within [X] hr; pending-state and Expansion Assist descriptive splits remain intentional scope boundaries."

CALL
Send back to Marcus with the softened wording. Do not let "eliminating" stand — it's exec-language overreach on a claim the data can't currently back, and it papers over the pending-state boundary that matters for the next exec review.

results.title: Reallocate paid-test room to Expansion Assist
results.snippet:
...Release/rollback is Daniela's lane; routine >>>expansion<<< is not.
- Sequential workstreams: >>>Helio<<< >>>Start<<< batch landing or not is a >>>Helio<<< >>>Start<<< decision. >>>Expansion<<< >>>Assist<<< volume is a separate workstream with its own brief, its own hypothesis, and its own...

messages.content:
Ruling: No — decline the swap.

Summary
The two workstreams are not fungible. Expansion Assist is descriptive by design ("no routine line-edit"); bumping it to 4 routine prompts/week re-categorizes it as an optimization lever and dilutes the disputed/cross/exec signal it's meant to hold. And the rule is sequential, not slot-substitution: finishing (or skipping) a Helio Start paid batch does not open a paid-test seat for an unrelated Expansion Assist change. The "extra prompt" isn't a growth action — it's a routine cadence change that hasn't cleared the growth method bar.

Why
- Expansion Assist's purpose: capture disputed, cross-functional, and exec items. Routine volume increase is explicitly out of scope per the standing rule. Release/rollback is Daniela's lane; routine expansion is not.
- Sequential workstreams: Helio Start batch landing or not is a Helio Start decision. Expansion Assist volume is a separate workstream with its own brief, its own hypothesis, and its own powered read.
- Growth method (eff 7/6/27): every shipped action needs primary metric + min effect pre-launch, 21-day powered read, effect size + CI, safety-guardrail interim review, and a full stabilization cohort pre-ship. "Using the room" is not a substitute for that design.
- Ines's H1 '27 MET on Expansion Assist was ≤3/wk. Moving past 3 is a metric-boundary change, not a swap-in.

Cuts
- Decline treating "extra routine prompt" as a replacement growth action.
- Decline running Expansion Assist volume increase as if it were the next paid-batch slot.

P (preconditions if Expansion Assist volume is ever reopened on its own merits — not as a swap)
- New brief, descriptive-signal hypothesis (e.g., does raising the floor catch more disputed/cross/exec items earlier?), not an optimization hypothesis.
- Daniela sign-off on the cadence change and on release/rollback ownership.
- Re-baseline Ines's MET against the 3/wk ceiling before any change ships.

Effect
Saying yes conflates two workstreams, lowers Expansion Assist's signal quality, and spends the freed slot on something that doesn't clear the growth method bar.

Call
Decline the swap. If the stakeholder wants to revisit Expansion Assist cadence, it goes through its own brief with Daniela in the loop — not as the replacement for a Helio Start batch.
