arguments.body:
# 2027 Lifecycle Systems leadership model — December 4 decision draft

Author: Riley Tanaka
Status: PROPOSAL — decision draft, not approved. No role change is in effect. Riley's current routine monthly preparation and routine source-closure attendance are unchanged through end of FY26 and until a December 4 decision is recorded. Nothing in this draft takes effect early.

Update log
- 2026-11-18: Initial draft.
- 2026-11-24: Updated after today's 11:00am 1:1 with Owen. Added (a) four preserved-cadence properties in §2 (second-business-day snapshot preparation; named-owner certification before closure; explicit incomplete status when any required field or owner certification is missing; one closure-and-exception summary instead of informal follow-up fragments); (b) audit-evidence sequencing rule in §4; (c) audit-versus-closure implementation risk R9 in §6; (d) consolidated decision question Q9 in §7.
- 2026-11-25: Updated after today's conversation with Ines and separate clarification from Daniela. Added (a) §1a "Four functions and their holders" to draw clean boundaries between source closure, owner certification, hands-on audit, and final claim authority — with explicit Ines and Daniela constraints baked in so the audit cannot drift into a request for Riley's routine approval of Ines' certification, and cannot drift into release/suppress/restore/rollback authority (engineering controls remain Daniela's lane); (b) R10 "Audit-role boundary drift" in §6; (c) Q10 in §7 about which monthly audit shape gives Riley the most direct system contact with the least duplicate work. Ines' certification remains Ines'; the audit inspects evidence↔messaging-state agreement and may surface findings, but it does not convert her cert into something that requires Riley's routine sign-off. Daniela's lane (engineering release/suppress/restore/rollback controls) is not in the audit's authority; the audit inspects reliability evidence only.

## 1. Purpose & decision posture

Priya is requesting a 2027 role design that removes Riley from routine monthly Lifecycle Systems preparation and from source-closure attendance, while preserving a concrete monthly hands-on audit so Riley can still test the evidence system directly. Escalation rights on a defined trigger set must be retained. Authority over causal, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, and final-claim decisions must not be narrowed.

No role change is approved today. This document is the working draft for the December 4 decision meeting. Riley continues attending routine reviews through end of FY26. Nothing in this draft takes effect early.

Input the model is built from:
- Owen's November 6 independent source closure (independent prep + source-completeness closure inside the unchanged definition + named-owner certification).
- Riley's November 13 bounded claims decision (bounded instructional wording, precise extension-authority language).
- The November 17 manager calibration was working notes only — not delivered feedback, no authority expansion, no company calibration closure. It is not part of the input set for this role design.
- 2026-11-24 1:1 with Owen: four cadence-preservation properties (see §2) and the audit-evidence sequencing rule (see §4); see also R9 in §6.
- 2026-11-25: Ines' constraint that the hands-on audit may inspect whether evidence and messaging-state treatment agree, but must not turn her owner certification into a request for Riley's routine approval. Daniela's separate clarification that the audit may inspect reliability evidence, but cannot release, suppress, restore, or roll back anything; engineering controls remain in her lane. See §1a, R10, Q10.

## 1a. Four functions and their holders (drawn as separate roles)

These four functions are distinct. The model must not collapse them, and the audit must not silently take on authority that belongs to a different function.

1. Source closure (Lane A). Owner: Owen. Owen prepares the routine packet, performs source-completeness closure against the unchanged definition, and records named-owner certification. Riley does not co-sign, co-attest, or co-close routine source closure. The cert is Owen's. Riley's signature is not on the routine closure.
2. Owner certification (Lane B — and the lifecycle-governance cert inside it). Owner: Ines. Ines certifies routine message-state governance, extension-authority language precision, bounded instructional wording, and the lifecycle-governance pack. Ines' cert is Ines'. The audit may inspect whether evidence and messaging-state treatment agree, and may surface a finding when they do not, but it must not convert Ines' certification into something that requires Riley's routine approval or sign-off. Riley's role at the cert is to escalate on a trigger (see §3) or to take it up as a finding under §4, not to re-approve.
3. Hands-on audit (Lane D's testing channel). Owner: Riley. The audit is Riley's concrete monthly test of the evidence system. It pulls source-of-record, re-derives the claim, checks the closure cert (signed by Owen or Ines, as applicable), checks message-state and instructional wording against the cert, and surfaces cross-surface discrepancies. It inspects evidence only. It cannot release, suppress, restore, or roll back any system state, message, claim surface, or release. Those are engineering controls and remain in Daniela's lane; the audit does not acquire them.
4. Final claim authority (Lane D's decision right). Owner: Riley. Riley retains decision rights on causal, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, and final-claim domains (see §5). These are decision rights, not operating controls. The audit (§4) and escalation (§3) feed into this authority; they do not replace it.

Why the four are kept separate
- Collapsing source closure and owner certification into one role would let source-side judgments masquerade as lifecycle-governance certs, or vice versa.
- Collapsing owner certification and the audit would convert the audit into a routine co-approval of Ines' cert — exactly what Ines flagged as off the table today.
- Collapsing the audit and engineering controls would let the audit acquire release/suppress/restore/rollback authority — exactly what Daniela flagged as off the table.
- Final claim authority must remain distinct from all three so Riley can decide without being the operator.

## 2. Delegated monthly cadence

The four lanes and their owners are unchanged from FY26. What changes is *who carries routine prep and routine source-closure attendance*. Riley steps out of those two specific activities; everything else stays.

Lane A — Preparation and source-closure ownership: Owen
- Routine monthly preparation (data pulls, cycle definitions, source-completeness check, named-owner certification on the standard pack).
- Routine source-closure attendance: Owen owns the close on routine packets.
- Source of authority: unchanged from FY26 definition.

Lane B — Lifecycle governance and message-state discipline: Ines
- Routine message-state governance (sending/suppressed/queued state correctness).
- Precise extension-authority language on outbound claims.
- Bounded instructional wording (no expansion of claim scope beyond the approved surface).
- Lifecycle-governance certification.
- Note: per §1a item 2 and per Ines' 2026-11-25 input, Ines' cert is Ines'. The audit (§4) inspects evidence↔messaging-state agreement and may surface findings; it does not convert her cert into a request for Riley's routine approval.

Lane C — Cross-cycle/strategic: Priya
- Owns the cross-cycle narrative, the broader Lifecycle Systems roadmap, and the December 4 decision package.

Lane D — Final authority: Riley
- Retains decision rights (see §5).
- Stands out of routine prep and routine source-closure attendance.
- Stands in via the monthly hands-on audit (§4) and via escalation (§3).
- Per §1a item 3 and per Daniela's 2026-11-25 clarification, the audit inspects reliability evidence only; it cannot release, suppress, restore, or roll back any system state, message, or claim surface. Engineering controls remain in Daniela's lane.

What the delegated cadence preserves (Owen's 11/24 1:1 input)
The delegation transfers *who carries* routine prep and source-closure attendance to Owen and Ines. It does not change the form of the cadence. The following four properties must continue to hold under the delegation; they are part of the proposal's definition of the cadence, not implementation details.

1. Second-business-day snapshot preparation. The monthly snapshot is prepared by the second business day of the cycle, not later, and not on a rolling "when ready" basis. This is a hard date against the calendar, not against completion of any other step.
2. Named-owner certification before closure. Every routine closure carries a named-owner certification — Owen for source completeness, Ines for lifecycle-governance — recorded before the closure is treated as final. No silent closures.
3. Explicit incomplete status when any required field or owner certification is missing. If a required field is missing or a named-owner certification is not in place, the packet's status is recorded as explicitly incomplete. Not "ready with caveats." Not "closed with notes." Incomplete is incomplete. The closure cannot proceed in that state.
4. One closure-and-exception summary, not informal follow-up fragments. Closure is a single, written closure-and-exception summary per cycle. Disputes, exceptions, and follow-ups are folded into that summary, not carried as informal Slack threads, ad-hoc DMs, or email fragments that drift from the closure record.

Amending or dropping any of these four properties is a December 4 decision question (see §7 Q9), not an implementation detail.

## 3. Escalation triggers retained (not narrowed)

Riley is escalated into on any of the following six triggers. The set is closed. Adding a trigger is a December 4 decision question; removing one is not on the table.

1. Missing fields in a routine packet.
2. Disputed semantics on a defined term or claim surface.
3. Cross-surface discrepancies (e.g., a number that reconciles in one surface but not another).
4. Customer corrections (a customer has flagged an inaccuracy that affects a routine claim).
5. Incident stops (anything that pauses, rolls back, or quarantines a routine cycle).
6. Executive-language decisions (any claim headed to exec, board, investor, or external comms surfaces).

Escalation is *into Riley's queue*, not a request for re-prep. Owen/Ines remain the named owners; Riley arbitrates and decides.

Note: escalation on trigger 5 (incident stops) routes to Riley for decision; the actual release/suppress/restore/rollback action is an engineering control and remains in Daniela's lane (§1a item 3, §4 boundary).

## 4. Hands-on audit design (the concrete monthly test)

The audit exists so Riley can test the evidence system directly without redoing routine prep. It is not a second prep pass.

Sampling rule
- One named claim per month, picked by Riley.
- Drawn from a defined stratum: one of {a routine closing claim, a lifecycle-gov claim, a source-completeness close, a certified packet item}.
- Riley names the claim by the 5th business day of the cycle.

Walkthrough checklist (fixed, every month)
1. Pull the source-of-record artifact for the claim. Confirm it exists and is the named source.
2. Re-derive the claim from the source. Confirm the derivation is reproducible.
3. Check the closure cert for that item. Confirm the named owner and the certification date.
4. Check message-state (Lane B) for any related outbound. Confirm state matches the claim. (Per Ines' 2026-11-25 input, this is the spot where the audit may inspect evidence↔messaging-state agreement.)
5. Check instructional wording for any related artifact. Confirm it does not exceed the approved claim surface.
6. Note any cross-surface discrepancy, even one that "reconciles under a convention." Surface it.

Audit artifact
- A one-page audit note per month, posted in the Lifecycle Systems folder by the second business day of the following week.
- Format: claim picked, source used, derivation result, cert check, msg-state check (evidence↔messaging-state agreement), instructional-wording check, cross-surface note, sign-off.

Failure modes the audit is designed to catch
- Source-completeness closure that was performed but not actually complete.
- Cert signed against a stale source.
- Instructional wording that quietly expanded scope.
- Cross-surface numbers that reconcile by convention but not by derivation.
- Evidence and messaging-state treatment disagreeing (per Ines' 2026-11-25 input — inspection only; no operating authority over either side).

Time budget
- One audit per month. Half-day at most. Not a substitute for routine prep.

Audit-evidence sequencing rule (Owen's 11/24 1:1 input)
Riley declares the audit's evidence scope (the named claim, the source of record, the time window) only after Owen's routine source-completeness decision for that month is recorded. The audit cannot shape the routine sample, and the audit cannot quietly become a second closure review. Concretely:
- Owen records the routine source-completeness decision by the second business day of the cycle (per §2 item 1).
- Riley names the audit claim no earlier than that same day, and only after reading the recorded decision.
- The audit note (§4 artifact) cites Owen's recorded decision and is filed in the Lifecycle Systems folder, not in the routine closure packet.
- If the audit surfaces a finding, it is filed as a separate escalation under §3 or as an input to the next cycle's source-completeness decision — not as an amendment to the current cycle's closure.

Audit boundaries (Ines' and Daniela's 2026-11-25 input)
- Ines-boundary: the audit may inspect whether evidence and messaging-state treatment agree (checklist step 4; audit artifact format line "msg-state check"). It may surface a finding when they do not. It must not turn Ines' owner certification into a request for Riley's routine approval or sign-off. Ines' cert stands as Ines'. If the audit finding is significant enough to warrant Riley's involvement, it flows through escalation (§3) or as input to the next cycle — not as a co-approval of the current cert.
- Daniela-boundary: the audit may inspect reliability evidence only. It cannot release, suppress, restore, or roll back any system state, message, claim surface, or release. Engineering controls — the levers that actually move system state — remain in Daniela's lane. If the audit surfaces a finding about a release, suppression, restore, or rollback in progress, the finding routes to Daniela for action; the audit does not act.
- These two boundaries are part of the proposal's definition of the audit. Amending them is a December 4 decision question (see §7 Q10), not an implementation detail.

## 5. Decision rights retained (not narrowed)

Riley retains final decision authority on the following five domains. The model must not narrow any of these.

- Causal: any claim of the form "X caused Y" or "because of X" in a routine or strategic surface.
- Revenue: ARR/MRR/expansion/contraction claims, including cohort cuts and segment reads.
- Forecast: forward-looking revenue, retention, or growth projections.
- Board-readiness: anything headed to the board pack or the board pre-read.
- Final-claim: any claim whose authority is the Lifecycle Systems function rather than a named owner.

Note on generalization: the Nov 13 decision was on a *bounded* surface. It is one data point. The model must not assume all routine claims will close the way Nov 13 did. This is why the audit (§4) exists.

These five domains are decision rights (§1a item 4), not operating controls. Decision rights produce a call; operating controls (Lane A prep, Lane B cert, Lane D engineering controls in Daniela's lane) produce the underlying state. The audit inspects reliability of the state; it does not acquire decision rights.

## 6. Implementation risks

R1 — False confidence from two clean closes. Nov 6 and Nov 13 are two data points. The model assumes a stable success rate that may not hold. Mitigation: audit (§4) and the closed escalation set (§3).

R2 — Audit becomes performative. If the audit is predictable, it stops testing the system. Mitigation: Riley picks the claim; checklist is fixed but the stratum is wide.

R3 — Escalation under-triggering. Owen/Ines may resolve a trigger informally rather than escalating. Mitigation: the six triggers are closed and escalation is *into Riley's queue*, not a request to skip Riley.

R4 — Scope creep into causal/revenue/forecast language. Ines owns instructional wording but must not narrow or expand claim scope. Owen owns source closure but must not move into causal/revenue/forecast interpretation. Mitigation: §5 decision rights are explicit; the audit checks instructional-wording scope.

R5 — Cadence drift vs. cross-cycle obligations. Routine monthly cadence must not desynchronize from quarterly board-readiness, customer-correction cycles, or incident response. Mitigation: Priya owns the cross-cycle calendar; audit samples can land on a cross-cycle month.

R6 — Cert completeness decoupling. A named-owner cert can be signed while the underlying source-completeness is not actually complete (the failure mode Owen's Nov 6 close was built to prevent). Mitigation: audit step 3 (§4) explicitly checks the cert against the source.

R7 — Key-person risk. The model depends on Owen and Ines continuing in their roles. Mitigation: if either role is vacant or transitioning, default to *no delegation* — Riley re-attends routine prep and source closure until the role is filled.

R8 — Confusion with the manager-calibration channel. The Nov 17 working notes were not delivered feedback and did not expand authority. The audit is *not* a calibration instrument. Mitigation: the audit note is filed in the Lifecycle Systems folder, not the calibration folder.

R9 — Audit versus closure (added 2026-11-24). Even with the sequencing rule in §4, the audit can drift into a parallel closure review: Riley could pick claims that effectively re-litigate Owen's source-completeness decision; Owen could shape the source-completeness decision in anticipation of Riley's audit; or the audit note could quietly become a second closure artifact the routine packet links to. The risk is not that any single audit does this once — it's that over months the audit becomes a structural duplicate of the closure review rather than a system test of it. Mitigation: the audit-evidence sequencing rule in §4 (declare only after Owen's recorded decision; cite the decision; file the audit note separately); the closed escalation set in §3 (audit findings flow through escalation, not back into the routine packet); and a quarterly audit-vs-closure check (see §7 Q9) at the end of Q1 FY27 and again at the re-decision point, on whether the audit is functioning as a system test or as a second closure review. If the latter, the model is failing and the default is to re-attend routine prep and source closure until the audit design is reset.

R10 — Audit-role boundary drift (added 2026-11-25). Two specific drift modes, each named by the function it would collapse:
  (a) Cert drift — the audit starts acting as if Ines' owner certification requires Riley's routine approval. Symptom: Riley is asked to "co-sign" or "acknowledge" the cert; audit notes begin referencing "approval status" of Ines' cert; the audit note is filed against the routine packet rather than as a separate artifact. Drift source: well-meaning alignment pressure when evidence↔messaging-state findings surface. Per Ines' 2026-11-25 input, this is off the table — Ines' cert is Ines'. Mitigation: the Ines-boundary in §4 (audit inspects evidence↔messaging-state agreement and may surface a finding, but does not convert her cert into a request for Riley's routine approval); escalation (§3) as the only path for Riley to act on a cert finding; the audit artifact is filed separately, not against the routine packet.
  (b) Engineering-control drift — the audit starts acting as if it can release, suppress, restore, or roll back system state. Symptom: audit notes begin recommending or recording releases/suppressions/restores/rollbacks; Riley is asked to "authorize" a release from the audit; the audit is treated as a gate on engineering action. Drift source: scope creep when a finding touches live system state. Per Daniela's 2026-11-25 clarification, this is off the table — engineering controls remain in Daniela's lane. Mitigation: the Daniela-boundary in §4 (audit inspects reliability evidence only; cannot release/suppress/restore/roll back); audit findings about live system state route to Daniela for action, not to the audit for action; escalation (§3 trigger 5) covers Riley's involvement in incident decisions as a decision right, not as an operating lever.
  Both drift modes are detectable at the quarterly audit-vs-closure check (R9) and at the new audit-shape check (Q10). If either drift mode is detected, the default is to re-attend routine prep and source closure until the audit design is reset, the same fallback as R9.

## 7. December 4 decision questions

The December 4 meeting should produce a recorded decision on each of the following.

Q1. Approve the model as drafted (delegation in §2, escalation in §3, audit in §4, rights retained in §5)?
- Options: approve / approve with amendments / defer / decline.

Q2. If approving: any amendments to the escalation trigger set (§3)? Adding a trigger requires Riley's sign-off; removing one is off the table.

Q3. If approving: any amendments to the audit (§4)? Specifically: sampling cadence (default monthly), sampling rule (Riley picks, defined stratum), checklist (fixed), artifact (one-page note, Lifecycle Systems folder).

Q4. If approving: any amendments to the decision rights (§5)? The five domains are fixed; the question is whether any are under-articulated and need sharper definition.

Q5. Effective date. Default = first Lifecycle Systems cycle of FY27, with a written handoff and a one-cycle overlap where Riley co-attends. Alternative = a later date. Earliest possible date is the first FY27 cycle, not before.

Q6. Re-decision cadence. Default = re-decide at end of Q2 FY27 (end of June 2027) based on audit notes and escalation volume. Alternative = earlier or later.

Q7. Vacancy / transition rule (R7). Confirm: if Owen or Ines role is vacant or in transition, default is *no delegation* and Riley re-attends until filled.

Q8. Cross-cycle synchronization (R5). Confirm Priya owns the cross-cycle calendar and that audit samples may land on cross-cycle months.

Q9. Cadence-preservation rules and audit-versus-closure sequencing (added 2026-11-24). Confirm each of the following as part of the proposal — not as implementation details:
  (a) The four preserved-cadence properties in §2 hold under the delegation: second-business-day snapshot preparation; named-owner certification before closure; explicit incomplete status when any required field or owner certification is missing; one closure-and-exception summary instead of informal follow-up fragments. Any amendment to one of these properties requires an explicit decision.
  (b) The audit-evidence sequencing rule in §4: Riley declares the audit's evidence scope only after Owen's routine source-completeness decision for that month is recorded. The audit cannot shape the routine sample, and the audit cannot quietly become a second closure review.
  (c) Audit findings flow through the escalation set in §3 and are filed as a separate artifact in the Lifecycle Systems folder, not as an amendment to the routine closure packet.
  (d) A quarterly audit-vs-closure check (R9) at the end of Q1 FY27 and again at the re-decision point, on whether the audit is functioning as a system test or as a second closure review. If it is functioning as a second closure review, the default is to re-attend routine prep and source closure until the audit design is reset.

Q10. Audit shape: most direct system contact, least duplicate work (added 2026-11-25). Confirm the shape of the monthly audit, with three properties already baked in from the §1a role boundaries: (i) inspects evidence↔messaging-state agreement but does not require Ines' cert to be re-approved by Riley; (ii) inspects reliability evidence only and cannot release/suppress/restore/roll back (engineering controls stay with Daniela); (iii) does not become a parallel closure review (§4 sequencing, R9).
  Open question for December 4: which audit shape gives Riley the most direct contact with the evidence system while doing the least duplicate work relative to Owen's source-completeness decision and Ines' lifecycle-governance certification? Options to compare:
    - Shape A — current draft (§4 as written): one named claim per month, six-step checklist, separate one-page note. Direct contact: claim, source, derivation, cert, message-state, instructional wording. Duplicate work risk: medium if Riley picks claims that overlap the routine sample; sequencing rule mitigates but does not eliminate.
    - Shape B — claim-pull + countercheck: Riley pulls the named claim and runs only the derivation + cert checks (steps 1–3 of the checklist) on a quarterly cadence, with a monthly light-touch message-state check on a different item. Direct contact: source and cert. Duplicate work risk: low; loses monthly cadence on derivation check.
    - Shape C — evidence-system walk: Riley picks a named system (e.g., the message-state ledger, the source-completeness register, the cert log) and walks a single artifact end-to-end, instead of picking a claim. Direct contact: the system itself, not a claim derived from it. Duplicate work risk: low; pivots the audit from "is this claim right" to "is this system reliable."
    - Shape D — hybrid: Shape A's monthly claim pick + Shape C's quarterly system walk. Direct contact: high (both claim and system); duplicate work risk: medium; needs an explicit rule that the system walk cannot revisit a claim the routine packet just closed.
  Each shape must be evaluated against the §1a boundaries (cert drift, engineering-control drift), the §4 sequencing rule, and the R9/R10 checks. The December 4 decision is to pick a shape, amend a shape, or defer the question. Default if discussion runs long: Shape A as drafted, with the option to revisit toward Shape D at the end of Q1 FY27 quarterly check.

---
End of draft. This document is the working input for the December 4 decision. It is not the decision.

arguments.body:
# 2027 Lifecycle Systems leadership model — December 4 decision draft

Author: Riley Tanaka
Date: 2026-11-18
Status: Decision draft. Not approved. Riley continues attending routine Lifecycle Systems reviews through end of FY26 and until a December 4 decision is recorded.

## 1. Purpose & decision posture

Priya is requesting a 2027 role design that removes Riley from routine monthly Lifecycle Systems preparation and from source-closure attendance, while preserving a concrete monthly hands-on audit so Riley can still test the evidence system directly. Escalation rights on a defined trigger set must be retained. Authority over causal, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, and final-claim decisions must not be narrowed.

No role change is approved today. This document is the working draft for the December 4 decision meeting. Riley continues attending routine reviews through end of FY26. Nothing in this draft takes effect early.

Input the model is built from:
- Owen's November 6 independent source closure (independent prep + source-completeness closure inside the unchanged definition + named-owner certification).
- Riley's November 13 bounded claims decision (bounded instructional wording, precise extension-authority language).
- The November 17 manager calibration was working notes only — not delivered feedback, no authority expansion, no company calibration closure. It is not part of the input set for this role design.

## 2. Delegated monthly cadence

The four lanes and their owners are unchanged from FY26. What changes is *who carries routine prep and routine source-closure attendance*. Riley steps out of those two specific activities; everything else stays.

Lane A — Preparation and source-closure ownership: Owen
- Routine monthly preparation (data pulls, cycle definitions, source-completeness check, named-owner certification on the standard pack).
- Routine source-closure attendance: Owen owns the close on routine packets.
- Source of authority: unchanged from FY26 definition.

Lane B — Lifecycle governance and message-state discipline: Ines
- Routine message-state governance (sending/suppressed/queued state correctness).
- Precise extension-authority language on outbound claims.
- Bounded instructional wording (no expansion of claim scope beyond the approved surface).
- Lifecycle-governance certification.

Lane C — Cross-cycle/strategic: Priya
- Owns the cross-cycle narrative, the broader Lifecycle Systems roadmap, and the December 4 decision package.

Lane D — Final authority: Riley
- Retains decision rights (see §5).
- Stands out of routine prep and routine source-closure attendance.
- Stands in via the monthly hands-on audit (§4) and via escalation (§3).

## 3. Escalation triggers retained (not narrowed)

Riley is escalated into on any of the following six triggers. The set is closed. Adding a trigger is a December 4 decision question; removing one is not on the table.

1. Missing fields in a routine packet.
2. Disputed semantics on a defined term or claim surface.
3. Cross-surface discrepancies (e.g., a number that reconciles in one surface but not another).
4. Customer corrections (a customer has flagged an inaccuracy that affects a routine claim).
5. Incident stops (anything that pauses, rolls back, or quarantines a routine cycle).
6. Executive-language decisions (any claim headed to exec, board, investor, or external comms surfaces).

Escalation is *into Riley's queue*, not a request for re-prep. Owen/Ines remain the named owners; Riley arbitrates and decides.

## 4. Hands-on audit design (the concrete monthly test)

The audit exists so Riley can test the evidence system directly without redoing routine prep. It is not a second prep pass.

Sampling rule
- One named claim per month, picked by Riley.
- Drawn from a defined stratum: one of {a routine closing claim, a lifecycle-gov claim, a source-completeness close, a certified packet item}.
- Riley names the claim by the 5th business day of the cycle.

Walkthrough checklist (fixed, every month)
1. Pull the source-of-record artifact for the claim. Confirm it exists and is the named source.
2. Re-derive the claim from the source. Confirm the derivation is reproducible.
3. Check the closure cert for that item. Confirm the named owner and the certification date.
4. Check message-state (Lane B) for any related outbound. Confirm state matches the claim.
5. Check instructional wording for any related artifact. Confirm it does not exceed the approved claim surface.
6. Note any cross-surface discrepancy, even one that "reconciles under a convention." Surface it.

Audit artifact
- A one-page audit note per month, posted in the Lifecycle Systems folder by the second business day of the following week.
- Format: claim picked, source used, derivation result, cert check, msg-state check, instructional-wording check, cross-surface note, sign-off.

Failure modes the audit is designed to catch
- Source-completeness closure that was performed but not actually complete.
- Cert signed against a stale source.
- Instructional wording that quietly expanded scope.
- Cross-surface numbers that reconcile by convention but not by derivation.

Time budget
- One audit per month. Half-day at most. Not a substitute for routine prep.

## 5. Decision rights retained (not narrowed)

Riley retains final decision authority on the following five domains. The model must not narrow any of these.

- Causal: any claim of the form "X caused Y" or "because of X" in a routine or strategic surface.
- Revenue: ARR/MRR/expansion/contraction claims, including cohort cuts and segment reads.
- Forecast: forward-looking revenue, retention, or growth projections.
- Board-readiness: anything headed to the board pack or the board pre-read.
- Final-claim: any claim whose authority is the Lifecycle Systems function rather than a named owner.

Note on generalization: the Nov 13 decision was on a *bounded* surface. It is one data point. The model must not assume all routine claims will close the way Nov 13 did. This is why the audit (§4) exists.

## 6. Implementation risks

R1 — False confidence from two clean closes. Nov 6 and Nov 13 are two data points. The model assumes a stable success rate that may not hold. Mitigation: audit (§4) and the closed escalation set (§3).

R2 — Audit becomes performative. If the audit is predictable, it stops testing the system. Mitigation: Riley picks the claim; checklist is fixed but the stratum is wide.

R3 — Escalation under-triggering. Owen/Ines may resolve a trigger informally rather than escalating. Mitigation: the six triggers are closed and escalation is *into Riley's queue*, not a request to skip Riley.

R4 — Scope creep into causal/revenue/forecast language. Ines owns instructional wording but must not narrow or expand claim scope. Owen owns source closure but must not move into causal/revenue/forecast interpretation. Mitigation: §5 decision rights are explicit; the audit checks instructional-wording scope.

R5 — Cadence drift vs. cross-cycle obligations. Routine monthly cadence must not desynchronize from quarterly board-readiness, customer-correction cycles, or incident response. Mitigation: Priya owns the cross-cycle calendar; audit samples can land on a cross-cycle month.

R6 — Cert completeness decoupling. A named-owner cert can be signed while the underlying source-completeness is not actually complete (the failure mode Owen's Nov 6 close was built to prevent). Mitigation: audit step 3 (§4) explicitly checks the cert against the source.

R7 — Key-person risk. The model depends on Owen and Ines continuing in their roles. Mitigation: if either role is vacant or transitioning, default to *no delegation* — Riley re-attends routine prep and source closure until the role is filled.

R8 — Confusion with the manager-calibration channel. The Nov 17 working notes were not delivered feedback and did not expand authority. The audit is *not* a calibration instrument. Mitigation: the audit note is filed in the Lifecycle Systems folder, not the calibration folder.

## 7. December 4 decision questions

The December 4 meeting should produce a recorded decision on each of the following.

Q1. Approve the model as drafted (delegation in §2, escalation in §3, audit in §4, rights retained in §5)?
- Options: approve / approve with amendments / defer / decline.

Q2. If approving: any amendments to the escalation trigger set (§3)? Adding a trigger requires Riley's sign-off; removing one is off the table.

Q3. If approving: any amendments to the audit (§4)? Specifically: sampling cadence (default monthly), sampling rule (Riley picks, defined stratum), checklist (fixed), artifact (one-page note, Lifecycle Systems folder).

Q4. If approving: any amendments to the decision rights (§5)? The five domains are fixed; the question is whether any are under-articulated and need sharper definition.

# Helio Start capped paid-acquisition proposal — Q2 2026 working draft

**Status (post 2026-04-02 budget review): PROPOSAL — RECOMMENDATION BUDGET-APPROVED, PREFLIGHT PENDING. NOT LAUNCH AUTHORIZATION.**

This document is a proposal artifact for the capped Q2 Helio Start paid-acquisition test. As of the 2026-04-02 budget review (chair: Riley; scheduling: Priya), the recommended six-week high-intent paid-search shape has been approved by Priya with a budget of no more than $15,000, closing at the earlier of $15,000 in spend or 50 admitted workspaces. **Preflight is pending.** Paid traffic remains blocked. Paid traffic stays blocked until paid-source attribution reconciles from eligibility-flow start through admission and through assisted routing. No launch authorization is implied or granted by this document.

- **Author:** Riley Tanaka
- **Prepared:** 2026-03-04
- **Last revised (in-place, no scope expansion):** 2026-03-09 — §4.4 success measure, §4.5 support-load and unsupported-admission guardrails, and §4.6 monitoring and stop rules updated with owner inputs from Owen (Growth), Customer Success, and Ines (Lifecycle). All other sections unchanged at that revision.
- **Revised 2026-04-02 (in-place, post budget review):** Status banner updated to budget-approved / preflight-pending. §4.1 traffic cap, §4.2 budget request, §4.3 audience and channel, §4.5 support-load and unsupported-admission guardrails, §4.6 monitoring and stop rules, and §4.9 decision owners updated to reflect the 2026-04-02 budget-review outcome. Recommendation ($15,000 / 50 admitted workspaces / 6-week high-intent paid search) is recorded as approved by Priya with the documented stop / pause conditions. Fallback ($8,000 / 25 admitted workspaces / 6-week high-intent paid search) remains unapproved. §4.4 success measure, §4.7 refund-adjusted cash treatment, and the cadence / escalation-path sub-items remain OPEN. Organic-only boundary through 2026-03-31 has now lapsed by date; the live boundary is "paid traffic stays blocked until preflight passes." All preserved rules in §3 are unchanged. No new artifact, no pipeline target, no forecast credit.
- **Reviewer / approver (recommendation + budget envelope):** Priya, 2026-04-02.
- **Authority invoked:** Priya's 2026-03-03 confirmation that the published evidence condition is satisfied, authorizing Riley to PREPARE a Q2 capped proposal, plus Priya's 2026-04-02 approval of the recommended six-week high-intent paid-search shape with a $15,000 budget ceiling closing at the earlier of $15,000 spend or 50 admitted workspaces. Proposal + budget-envelope authority only. Preflight + launch authorization still pending.

---

## 0. 2026-04-02 budget-review outcome (decision record)

A 30-minute budget review was chaired by Riley on Thursday, 2026-04-02, 13:30–14:00 CT (calendar event `evt_1789617541495`). Frame: review, not approval — but the review resulted in a budget approval of the recommended shape. The decisions recorded here are the ones the review was empowered to make; everything else is documented as out of scope or as still pending.

**In the review (decided):**

1. **Recommended shape approved.** Six-week high-intent paid-search test. Channel: paid search only, against a curated high-intent keyword set (decision-stage, mid-segment-fit terms). No broad / display / social expansion in this shape. The recommended shape is recorded as approved by Priya on 2026-04-02.
2. **Budget envelope approved.** No more than **$15,000** total spend on the test, closing at the **earlier of $15,000 in spend or 50 admitted workspaces**. Time cap is 6 weeks from launch. Whichever ceiling binds first stops new spend on the recommendation. Approved by Priya on 2026-04-02.
3. **Fallback shape: NOT approved.** The smaller fallback ($8,000 / 25 admitted workspaces / 6-week high-intent paid search, same shape otherwise) remains unapproved. It is documented as the smaller-shape alternative the review was empowered to choose instead of the recommendation; the review chose the recommendation, so the fallback stays on file as the documented fallback and is not active.
4. **Stop / pause conditions binding on the approved recommendation:**
   - **Stop immediately if an unsupported applicant enters the admitted path.** This is unchanged from the published evidence condition (Jan 27 and Feb 24 packets both confirmed zero unsupported cases admitted) and from §4.5 of this draft. Detection = halt, not warning.
   - **Pause if a routing or instrumentation failure prevents paid-source reconciliation.** Reconciliation means paid-source attribution is visible from eligibility-flow start through admission, and is preserved through assisted routing. A reconciliation failure pauses the test until it is resolved; it is not a warning to investigate.
   - **After at least 20 admissions, pause if more than 10% exceed 90 support minutes.** Account-level support minutes, captured per account from first assisted contact through the published mature window (Customer Success input, §4.5), are the unit the pause reads on; aggregated averages are not acceptable. The pause is a stop-rule input, not a stop on its own.
5. **Success-measure frame confirmed:** Day-7 first integration is a leading operating read only. Paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort all need complete outcome windows before any mature claim. Partial-window reads may trigger a halt or continue the test but cannot support a mature claim. Mature-claim gating is unchanged from §4.4 / §4.6.

**Pending preflight (NOT decided in the review — blocks launch):**

- Paid-source attribution reconciliation, from eligibility-flow start through admission and through assisted routing. Until preflight confirms reconciliation, paid traffic stays blocked.
- Implementation checks (traffic-cap mechanics, ad-ops setup, lifecycle-instrumentation verification, support-routing confirmation) happen after the preflight passes, not before.
- Final go/no-go on launch is a separate decision owned by Priya and is not granted by the budget approval.

**Out of scope for the review (unchanged):**

- Pipeline or forecast credit — excluded by §4.8. Not in scope of this draft at any stage.
- Mature outcome claims — out of scope until complete outcome windows exist.
- Q1 board-lane readiness — still not board-ready because the two certified mature cohorts (Jan 27 and Feb 24 packets) still lack exact start and end dates. This is a separate Q1-readiness item and is not changed by the budget review.
- Final launch go/no-go — Priya only, separate from the budget approval.

**Continuing boundary (post review):**

- Paid traffic stays blocked until preflight passes. The organic-only-through-2026-03-31 boundary has lapsed by date; its successor boundary is the preflight gate.
- Existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and support-routing rules are unchanged.
- No pipeline target. No forecast credit.

---

## 1. Standing boundary — do not change

- Helio Start was **organic-only through 2026-03-31**. That boundary has now lapsed by date.
- The **live boundary** as of 2026-04-02 is: **paid traffic stays blocked until preflight passes**, where preflight is the paid-source attribution reconciliation from eligibility-flow start through admission and through assisted routing.
- Through the preflight-pending period: no paid traffic, no pipeline or forecast attribution, no launch.
- This draft does not authorize launch. It records the budget approval of the recommendation; it does not flip the preflight gate.
- Organic-only status through 2026-03-31, and the no-paid-traffic-before-April-1 rule, are both preserved as historical boundary conditions. They are not in force as live gates today; the preflight gate replaces them.

## 2. The two qualifying mature cohorts (summary)

The published condition for reopening capped paid acquisition is:

- Two mature cohorts, each with **fewer than 5%** of cases crossing the **>90 supplementary-minute** threshold, AND
- **Zero unsupported cases** in the admitted path.

Per Priya's 2026-03-03 review, the evidence condition is satisfied based on two mature cohort packets:

- **Jan 27 mature cohort packet** — condition met on the published thresholds. (Per the Q1 source-lock read on `Quarterly board operating evidence intake — Q1 2026`, `doc_1789577240164`: 86 admitted workspaces with a complete day-90 window; 4 of 86 (4.7%) over 90 support minutes; 0 unsupported case admitted.)
- **Feb 24 mature cohort packet** — condition met on the published thresholds. (Per the same source-lock read: 91 admitted workspaces with a complete day-90 window; 3 of 91 (3.3%) over 90 support minutes; 0 unsupported case admitted.)

**Open gap carried forward:** the source packets for both cohorts still lack cohort dates. Because of that gap, the Q1 board lane remains not board-ready. This draft is structured for Q2; the missing cohort dates are a separate Q1-readiness item and are not fixed here. The 2026-04-02 budget approval does not change this — Q1 readiness is a separate track, and the budget approval is a Q2 proposal-review decision.

(Per-cohort numbers, exact percentages, and cohort identifiers are not restated in this draft because they are not in this working session's source materials; Priya has the source packets.)

## 3. Rules that must be preserved by any test this draft proposes

Any Q2 test, including the 2026-04-02 budget-approved recommendation, must preserve all of the following exactly as they operate today. None of these are open for renegotiation inside the capped paid-acquisition test. If a proposed test would require changing any of them, that change is out of scope for this draft and must be raised separately.

- **Eligibility rules** — current Helio Start eligibility logic, unchanged.
- **Refusal rules** — current refusal logic and refusal messaging, unchanged.
- **Connector-access rules** — current connector gating, unchanged.
- **External-authority rules** — current rules on what requires external sign-off, unchanged.
- **Lifecycle rules** — current lifecycle stages and transitions, unchanged. No new lifecycle branch is created for paid-acquired Helio Start cases. Paid-acquired cases flow through the same lifecycle stages and transitions as organic cases, with the existing branch logic determining next-touch, suppression, and reactivation behaviour.
- **Instrumentation rules** — current event taxonomy and properties, unchanged. Paid-source attribution must remain visible from eligibility-flow start through admission, and must be preserved through assisted routing; this is an instrumentation requirement, not a downstream reporting nicety.
- **Support-routing rules** — current routing of Helio Start cases in support, unchanged. Assisted-route reasons and account-level support minutes are captured from first contact, not reconstructed later. Per-account minutes — not aggregated averages — are the unit any guardrail reads on.

## 4. Open decisions

Each subsection below is an explicit decision. The 2026-04-02 budget review resolved the items marked RESOLVED. Items still marked OPEN are either deferred to preflight, deferred to launch gate, or deferred to mature-window completion. No choice is presented as settled beyond what the budget review actually settled.

### 4.1 Traffic cap — RESOLVED 2026-04-02 (recommendation)

- **Question:** what is the maximum paid-traffic exposure for the test?
- **Decision (post budget review):** the recommendation is approved with the following caps (whichever hits first stops new spend):
  - Spend cap: **$15,000 total**.
  - Volume cap: **50 admitted workspaces**.
  - Time cap: **6 weeks from launch**.
- **Constraint respected:** capped (not open-ended); small enough that an adverse outcome cannot move cohort-level metrics; sized to produce a readable signal inside Q2.
- **Status:** RESOLVED on the recommendation by Priya on 2026-04-02. The fallback's $8,000 / 25 admitted workspaces cap remains documented but is not active.
- **Launch gate:** time cap and any per-day pacing are set at launch gate, not here.

### 4.2 Budget request — RESOLVED 2026-04-02 (recommendation)

- **Question:** what dollar budget is requested for the test, and against which budget line?
- **Decision (post budget review):** Priya approved a budget envelope of **no more than $15,000** for the recommended six-week high-intent paid-search test, closing at the **earlier of $15,000 in spend or 50 admitted workspaces**. The budget approval is for the recommendation only; the fallback's $8,000 envelope is not approved.
- **Constraint respected:** the budget approval is for the capped test, not for open-ended paid acquisition; no separate pipeline or forecast credit is implied.
- **Status:** RESOLVED on the recommendation by Priya on 2026-04-02.
- **What the budget approval does NOT do:** the budget approval is not launch authorization, not preflight authorization, not acquisition authorization, not a pipeline target, and not forecast credit. Preflight must still pass before any spend occurs.

### 4.3 Audience and channel — RESOLVED 2026-04-02 (recommendation)

- **Question:** which audience, and through which channel(s)?
- **Decision (post budget review):** paid search only, against a curated high-intent keyword set (decision-stage, mid-segment-fit terms). **No broad / display / social expansion in this shape.** Audience scope is bounded to the curated keyword set; expansion beyond paid search is out of scope for this draft.
- **Constraint respected:** must not bypass any preserved rule in §3 (eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, support-routing). The paid-search scope must run through the same lifecycle branches and current-state suppression behaviour as the organic flow (per Ines, §4.6); no paid-source bypass.
- **Status:** RESOLVED on the recommendation by Priya on 2026-04-02.

### 4.4 Success measure — OPEN (owner input received 2026-03-09 from Owen, Growth; reaffirmed at the 2026-04-02 budget review)

- **Question:** what is the primary read on whether the capped test succeeded?
- **Constraints to respect:** must be measurable inside the cap; must not be redefined post-hoc; must not be conflated with pipeline or forecast credit (see §4.8). Per Owen (2026-03-09), and reaffirmed at the 2026-04-02 budget review, the success-measure frame is:
  - **Keep paid-source attribution visible from eligibility-flow start through admission, and through assisted routing.** Attribution cannot be dropped at any step between the first eligibility touch and admission, and must be preserved through assisted routing; if it is, the resulting cohort cannot support a mature claim. This is an instrumentation requirement, not a downstream reporting nicety — it is what makes any later paid-vs-organic comparison defensible.
  - **Treat Day-7 first integration as a leading operating indicator only.** It is an early read on activation momentum, not an outcome. It may inform monitoring and stop-rule judgement but cannot by itself support a mature claim.
  - **Require complete outcome windows before supporting a mature claim.** The mature outcome measures are:
    - paid-active status at the published mature window,
    - refund-adjusted collected cash at the published mature window,
    - account-level support effort at the published mature window (per Customer Success in §4.5).
    No mature claim may be made on any of these before its full outcome window has closed. Reporting on a partial window is acceptable only as a leading read and must be labelled as such.
- **Decision:** OPEN — no specific metric threshold or window length is proposed in this draft. The frame is locked; the thresholds and window length are deferred to preflight.

### 4.5 Support-load and unsupported-admission guardrails — RESOLVED 2026-04-02 (stop / pause thresholds); frame locked 2026-03-09 (Customer Success)

- **Question:** what thresholds trigger a halt on support load or on any unsupported case appearing in the admitted path?
- **Constraints to respect:** the published evidence condition — zero unsupported cases in the admitted path — must remain in force throughout the test. Any unsupported case in the admitted path is, by definition, a **halt signal**, not a warning.
- **Per Customer Success (2026-03-09), the support-load capture frame is:**
  - **Capture assisted-route reasons from the first contact.** The reason a case enters the assisted route (e.g., self-serve stall, eligibility question, refusal appeal, integration blocker, billing) is recorded at first contact, not reconstructed later. This is what makes account-level support effort attributable rather than approximate.
  - **Capture account-level support minutes from the first contact.** Minutes are tracked per account from first assisted contact through the published mature window, not summarised after the fact. Per-account minutes — not aggregated averages — are the unit the guardrail reads on.
  - **Treat any unsupported case in the admitted path as an immediate stop condition.** "Immediate stop" means the test halts on detection; it is not a warning to investigate. This is unchanged from the published evidence condition.
- **Stop / pause thresholds binding on the recommendation (resolved 2026-04-02 budget review):**
  - **Stop immediately if an unsupported applicant enters the admitted path.**
  - **After at least 20 admissions, pause if more than 10% exceed 90 support minutes.** Account-level minutes captured per account from first assisted contact.
- **Decision:** frame RESOLVED on 2026-03-09; stop / pause thresholds RESOLVED on 2026-04-02. No additional per-account-minute threshold or assisted-route taxonomy is being introduced in this draft beyond what is recorded above.

### 4.6 Monitoring and stop rules — RESOLVED 2026-04-02 (binding stop / pause conditions); spine locked 2026-03-09 (Owen + Ines); cadence OPEN

- **Question:** what monitoring cadence and what stop rules apply during the test?
- **Constraints to respect:** monitoring must be live, not retrospective; stop rules must be pre-committed, not discretionary; halt triggers include, at minimum:
  - any breach of the support-load guardrail in §4.5,
  - any breach of the unsupported-admission guardrail in §4.5 (i.e., any unsupported case in the admitted path),
  - any breach of the >90 supplementary-minute threshold on a paid-acquired cohort,
  - any change that would require modifying a preserved rule in §3.
- **Per Owen (2026-03-09), and reaffirmed at the 2026-04-02 budget review, the monitoring and stop-rule frame is:**
  - **Require complete outcome windows before supporting a mature claim.** Same point as §4.4, restated here because it is a stop-rule input: a stop rule cannot be "lifted on a mature read" because the read was partial. Partial-window reads may trigger a halt or continue the test, but they cannot clear a stop.
  - **Use paid-source attribution as the spine of monitoring.** Because §4.4 requires paid-source attribution to remain visible from eligibility-flow start through admission (and through assisted routing), every monitoring cut relevant to a stop decision (paid-active, refund-adjusted collected cash, account-level support effort, Day-7 first integration, unsupported-admission events) must be reproducible on the attributed paid cohort. Monitoring that loses attribution at any step is not acceptable.
  - **Pause if a routing or instrumentation failure prevents paid-source reconciliation.** Resolved 2026-04-02. Reconciliation must be verified end-to-end (eligibility-flow start → admission → assisted routing) before spend resumes after any pause.
- **Per Ines (2026-03-09), the lifecycle-instrumentation frame is:**
  - **Reuse the existing lifecycle branches as-is.** No new lifecycle branch is created for paid-acquired Helio Start cases. Paid-acquired cases flow through the same lifecycle stages and transitions as organic cases (per §3), with the existing branch logic determining next-touch, suppression, and reactivation behaviour.
  - **Reuse the current-state suppression behavior as-is.** No paid-source bypass of current-state suppression is introduced. If a case is suppressed under current-state logic (e.g., already converted, in an active onboarding sequence, in a cooldown window), it stays suppressed for the paid-acquired cohort exactly as it would for the organic cohort. A paid-source bypass is explicitly out of scope and is one of the changes that would require modifying a preserved rule in §3 (lifecycle, instrumentation).
- **Decision:** spine RESOLVED on 2026-03-09; binding stop / pause conditions RESOLVED on 2026-04-02 (unsupported-admission stop, reconciliation pause, >90-minute pause after ≥20 admissions). Monitoring cadence and escalation path remain OPEN and are deferred to preflight / launch gate.

### 4.7 Refund-adjusted cash treatment — OPEN

- **Question:** how is refund-adjusted cash from paid-acquired Helio Start cases treated for the purposes of this test?
- **Constraint to respect:** cash treatment is a test-level accounting choice only; it must not flow into MRR pipeline or forecast (see §4.8). Refund-adjusted collected cash is one of the mature outcome measures in §4.4 that requires a complete outcome window before any mature claim; the per-test treatment (gross vs. refund-adjusted, when in the window) is separate from that mature-read frame.
- **Decision:** OPEN — no treatment proposed in this draft.

### 4.8 Pipeline and forecast credit — EXCLUDED

- This draft **excludes** any pipeline or forecast credit for the proposed test.
- No MRR pipeline number, no forecast adjustment, and no modeled contribution to Q2 or later periods is implied or requested by this document.
- Cash treatment in §4.7 is a test-level accounting choice only; it does not authorize any forecast or pipeline attribution.
- The 2026-04-02 budget approval does not introduce any pipeline or forecast credit; the budget envelope is a spending ceiling, not a revenue or pipeline number.

### 4.9 Decision owners — RESOLVED 2026-04-02 (where the budget review resolved ownership); otherwise OPEN

- **Proposal owner (this draft):** Riley Tanaka.
- **Decision owner for traffic cap (§4.1):** RESOLVED 2026-04-02 — Priya, on the recommendation; fallback unapproved.
- **Decision owner for budget (§4.2):** RESOLVED 2026-04-02 — Priya, on the recommendation ($15,000 ceiling); fallback unapproved.
- **Decision owner for audience and channel (§4.3):** RESOLVED 2026-04-02 — Priya, on the recommendation (high-intent paid-search only); fallback unapproved.
- **Decision owner for success measure (§4.4):** Owen (Growth). Frame locked 2026-03-09; thresholds / window length OPEN.
- **Decision owner for support-load and unsupported-admission guardrails (§4.5):** Customer Success, with Priya on stop / pause thresholds as resolved 2026-04-02.
- **Decision owner for monitoring and stop rules (§4.6):** Owen (Growth) on the spine, Ines (Lifecycle) on lifecycle / suppression, with Priya on binding stop / pause conditions as resolved 2026-04-02. Cadence and escalation path: OPEN.
- **Decision owner for refund-adjusted cash treatment (§4.7):** OPEN.
- **Final go/no-go on launch:** Priya — separate from the budget approval. The 2026-04-02 budget approval is not launch authorization.

## 5. What this draft does not do

- It does not authorize launch. The 2026-04-02 budget approval authorizes the budget envelope and the recommendation shape; it does not flip the preflight gate or authorize paid traffic.
- It does not authorize pipeline or forecast attribution.
- It does not modify any preserved rule in §3.
- It does not lift the missing cohort dates on the Jan 27 and Feb 24 packets (separate Q1-readiness item); the Q1 board lane remains not board-ready on that input.
- It does not create a paid-source lifecycle branch or a paid-source suppression bypass (per Ines, §4.6).
- It does not relax the requirement that paid-source attribution remain visible from eligibility-flow start through admission and through assisted routing (per Owen, §4.4 and §4.6; reaffirmed 2026-04-02).
- It does not approve the smaller fallback shape; the fallback is documented but unapproved.
- It does not introduce any mature outcome claim. Day-7 first integration remains a leading read only; paid-active, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort remain deferred to complete outcome windows.

## 6. Next steps (proposal + preflight + launch gate, in order)

1. **Preflight — pending.** Confirm paid-source attribution reconciliation from eligibility-flow start through admission and through assisted routing. Until preflight passes, paid traffic stays blocked.
2. **Implementation checks — after preflight.** Traffic-cap mechanics, ad-ops setup, lifecycle-instrumentation verification against current taxonomy, support-routing confirmation. None of these are in scope of this draft and none are decided here.
3. **Launch gate.** Final go/no-go on launch is Priya's decision, separate from the 2026-04-02 budget approval. Launch gate is not authorized by this draft.
4. **Monitoring during the test.** Per the §4.6 frame: paid-source attribution as the spine of monitoring; complete outcome windows required for any mature claim; immediate stop on any unsupported case in the admitted path; pause on any reconciliation failure; pause after ≥20 admissions if >10% exceed 90 support minutes.
5. **Mature outcome claims — deferred.** No mature claim on paid-active, refund-adjusted collected cash, or account-level support effort until each measure's full outcome window has closed. Partial-window reads are leading indicators only.
6. **Q1 board-lane readiness — separate track.** The missing cohort dates on the Jan 27 and Feb 24 packets remain a separate Q1-readiness item and are not changed by the 2026-04-02 budget approval.

Helio Start was excluded in both Q1 and Q2 2026, but the two exclusions are not the same kind of exclusion. Q1 was a gate/input exclusion that produced a forecast-credit decision. Q1 2026 (final claims review 2026-03-24)

Two certified mature Helio Start cohorts (Jan 27, 2026: 86/66/10/6/4, $100,840 gross / $94,760 refund-adjusted, 4.7% over 90 support min, 0 unsupported case admitted; Feb 24, 2026: 91/71/10/6/4, $108,230 gross / $102,410 refund-adjusted, 3.3% over 90 support min, 0 unsupported case admitted). The Jan 6, 2026 readiness gate (Owen) requires exact cohort start and end dates for any cohort admitted to a board-ready claim. The source packets for both certified cohorts did not contain those dates. The lane stayed `not board-ready`. The gate was not weakened to admit the lane.

Resolved NO at the 2026-03-24 final claims review. Marcus Vail's question — whether the two qualifying mature cohorts create Q2 forecast credit — was answered NO. No Helio Start figure entered the Q1 board package as forecast credit. Organic-only-through-2026-03-31 boundary remained in force; the cleared proposal gate did not authorize paid traffic, budget, acquisition claims, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit.

The other three lanes (approved Q1 section, bounded as ratified)

No causal lift, no revenue credit, no forecast credit. Eng release/rollback routing stayed with Daniela.

Coverage Nov 26, 2025 → Feb 28, 2026; 9,604 organic pricing-page sessions; 143 of 1,981 Helio Start eligibility-flow starts (7.2%) later routed out for an existing unsupported condition; 44.0% eligible-workspace admission completion; p90 75-min account-level support time. Framed as post-rollout continuity (control retired Nov 26, 2025); explicitly NOT a second causal test; NOT a transfer of Helio Start methodology.
- System controls (CS auto-nudge) — board-ready, system-control performance only. Coverage Jan 1, 2026 → Feb 28, 2026; 2,146 CS auto-nudge decisions (83 visible field-specific holds + 2,063 proceeded/suppressed using current state); no governed-field disagreement, customer correction, or rollback; two source-age alerts fired before breach, both refreshed before their limits. Tomás Vega approved the Q1 operating-evidence section containing those three lanes WITHOUT adding a Helio Start forecast claim.

Q2 2026 (final claims review 2026-07-10)
What was on the table
A fixed 50-workspace paid Helio Start cohort with a 39-of-50 day-7 first-integration read. Complete day-90 paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort were not yet available. The cohort remained bounded by the same stop / pause conditions approved on 2026-04-02 (immediate stop on unsupported applicant in admitted path; pause on routing/instrumentation failure that breaks paid-source reconciliation from eligibility-flow start through admission through assisted routing; pause after ≥20 admissions if more than 10% exceed 90 account-level support minutes).

Why Helio Start was excluded
The 50-workspace cohort still lacked complete mature outcomes. The lane was excluded from the Q2 operating-evidence section until its mature window closes. No acquisition claim was added. No forecast claim was added.

What the day-7 result did and did not establish
What it DID establish: the 39-of-50 day-7 first-integration read is a leading operating indicator on the paid cohort — a real activation-momentum signal inside the capped test, useful for monitoring and for stop-rule judgement. It is recorded against the cohort.
What it DID NOT establish: by itself, the day-7 read does not support a growth or forecast claim. Marcus Vail asked at the 2026-07-10 review whether it could; it could not, because the mature outcomes (day-90 paid-active, refund-adjusted collected cash, account-level support effort) were not yet observable. Marcus's question was therefore kept out of the Q2 section.
The paid-pilot day-90 outcome matter remains open separately and is not closed by the Q2 final-claims review.

The other three lanes (approved Q2 section, bounded as ratified)
- Expansion Assist — descriptive, no causal / revenue / pipeline / forecast treatment. Locked coverage Feb 1, 2026 → Apr 14, 2026; 14 actual exposures with complete 45-day windows; 5 help-or-options requests, 3 expansions; every exposure met standing eligibility; no account had active CS adoption or renewal work at exposure; no randomized control.
- Pricing-page path quality — post-rollout continuity evidence only, NOT a new causal result. Locked coverage Mar 1, 2026 → May 24, 2026; 8,972 organic pricing-page sessions; 132 of 1,844 Helio Start eligibility-flow starts (7.2%) later routed out for an existing unsupported condition; 44.2% eligible-workspace admission completion; p90 76-min account-level support time. Both quarters excluded Helio Start, and both exclusions rest on the same board-discipline rule — no claim enters a board package until its required inputs and required outcome windows are complete, and the gate is not weakened to admit the lane. But the operative failure mode was different in each quarter. messages.content:
CALL
Hold the 4 extra chicken portions as a private-event service cushion — not as inventory, not as menu surplus, not as a refill offering. Pre-stage per Sam's tested sequence; do not place on the pass or the table; do not announce. Retire whatever is left at event close — no carry into a sale batch, weekly menu, family meal, or future event plan.

TREATMENT (during service)
- Stage the 4 through the same pre-staging sequence as the 32 confirmed portions. Same mise, same holding protocol, same doneness check.
- Keep them off the pass until a trigger fires. No refill bowl, no "seconds" board, no family-style overflow.
- Default service line if a guest asks "is there more?": "we have what we brought." True, and not a refill invitation.
- Do not pre-offer — not to regulars, not to the host, not to anyone who cleaned the first plate enthusiastically.

TRIGGERS (when to deploy)
- A portion is dropped, damaged, or fails the doneness check during service.
- A guest flags a quality issue that warrants a replacement. Sam's call, not a guest demand.
- An unannounced additional diner shows up who would otherwise go without (forgotten +1, late-arriving partner, host miscount).
- A guest finishes and explicitly asks for more. Mid-service discretionary — Sam or Riley decides whether to draw from cushion. Never a table-wide offer.
- A late-course timing pivot that would otherwise leave someone short.

NOT TRIGGERS
- Anticipated appetite ("they'll probably want seconds").
- "Help yourself" framing.
- A proactive offer by Sam or you.
- A second plate brought alongside the first "just in case."

BOUNDARIES (keeps this from becoming a weekly batch)
- Cushion is labeled by event — "Sept 13 private dinner" — not by service line. No "this is the cushion we always keep."
- Unused portions at event close: compost, staff meal, or family — same as any one-off surplus. Not a sale line, not a next-day menu item, not rolled into the next event's plan.
- Do not log the 4 into any recurring inventory count or par level. They are a procurement outcome (case yield > confirmed count), not a planned buffer.
- If a future private event has the same shape, re-decide per event. Do not let "we usually hold 4" become the rule.

WHY THIS FITS SAM'S ASK
Sam's concern was the cushion recreating an open-ended weekly sale batch. An event-scoped contingency — pre-staged but off-pass, triggered by specific failure modes, retired at event close — gives operational safety without seeding a refill expectation or a recurring menu line. The cushion exists for service failures, not for appetite upside.

ONE ASSUMPTION FLAGGED
I'm reading "+svc ≠ debt/catch-up" as fully covering this — adding cushion to a private event is not an obligation to scale it into a weekly pattern. If Sam reads it differently (e.g., he wants zero cushion and would rather run 32 portions exact with a trim-loss plan), tell him the recommendation is conditional on wanting the buffer at all. The above only applies if the cushion is being held.

DECISION-EVIDENCE SHEET
Roasted-chicken sale runs — Jun 28 / Jul 26 / Aug 16, 2024
Scope: run evidence only. The chef-owner's Aug 19, 2024 ruling
(advance-count private-dinner option, not a standing weekly
special) is settled and is NOT being reopened here.

================================================================
SUM-FIRST
================================================================
Production (the side Sam controls):
- All three runs stayed inside the pre-registered chef-owner
  thresholds — labor ≤ 60 min AND complete 7-oz portions ≥ 44
  (source: chef-owner's Aug 19, 2024 review covering all three
  runs; Jun 28 figures verified directly in the run sheet).
- The tested pre-staging + tray sequence held on every run; no
  deviation recorded.
- Verdict: production method is repeatable. Three controlled
  trials, same case size, same sequence, all clear.

Demand (the side the kitchen does not control):
- Sell-through varied enough across the three runs that the
  chef-owner judged a standing weekly special was not warranted
  (chef-owner, Aug 19, 2024).
- This is a verdict about VARIANCE, not about a single run's
  performance. June 28 alone was strong (43/45 = 95.6% sold).
  The variance came from the other two runs; magnitudes are not
  recorded in any session on file.
- Verdict: open-menu demand is too inconsistent to justify a
  fixed slot. Known-count demand (private dinners) is the lane
  that fits the evidence.

Bottom line (evidence-based, menu-neutral):
- Repeatable production, inconsistent open-menu demand.
- The advance-count private-dinner lane is the one the evidence
  supports; the standing-weekly lane is the one the evidence
  does not. That is the chef-owner's standing call and is not
  re-litigated in this sheet.

EVIDENCE — RUN BY RUN
================================================================

----------------
JUN 28, 2024 — baseline (single approved sale run)
----------------

- Raw case: 30 lb (same case as test #2)
- Incremental labor: 57 min              (cap 60)  PASS
- Cooked yield: 19 lb 12 oz (316 oz)
- Yield % (cooked / raw): 65.83%
- Complete 7-oz portions: 45             (floor 44) PASS
- Leftover oz: 1
- Sequence deviations: none — pre-staging and tray sequence
  run as tested

SERVICE / DEMAND
- Plates prepared: 45
- Plates sold: 43  (95.6% sell-through)
- Unsold: 2 portions (14 oz), chilled per the restaurant's
  food-handling procedure and used for staff meal — no waste,
  no revenue beyond the 2 unsold plates

ECONOMICS
- Menu price: $18 / plate
- Menu revenue: 43 × $18 = $774.00
- Food cost: $146.00
- Incremental labor cost: 57 min × $24/hr = $22.80
- Contribution after food + incremental labor: $605.20

THRESHOLD CALL (pre-registered, not adjusted)
- Labor ≤ 60 min: PASS (3 min headroom)
- Complete 7-oz portions ≥ 44: PASS (1 portion headroom)
- Both thresholds cleared.

----------------
JUL 26, 2024 — Run 1 of 2 controlled repeats
----------------
PRODUCTION (from chef-owner review, Aug 19, 2024)
- Labor and yield thresholds: CLEARED
- Sequence deviations: none recorded (consistent with the
  trial design — same pre-staging + tray sequence on the same
  30 lb case)

SERVICE / DEMAND
- Plates prepared / sold / unsold disposition: NOT ON FILE
  in any session on record, and the repeat-trial document
  (doc_1789332028679) is not readable from this environment.
  Direction of sell-through is known only in aggregate
  ("varied enough" — chef-owner, Aug 19, 2024).

ECONOMICS
- Revenue / food cost / labor cost / contribution: NOT ON FILE.
  Cannot be reconstructed without plates-sold and minutes.

GAP (flagged, not papered over)
- Per-run sell-through and per-run contribution for Jul 26 are
  not in the searchable record. The aggregate chef-owner verdict
  is the only demand signal on file.

----------------
AUG 16, 2024 — Run 2 of 2 controlled repeats
----------------
PRODUCTION (from chef-owner review, Aug 19, 2024)
- Labor and yield thresholds: CLEARED
- Sequence deviations: none recorded

SERVICE / DEMAND
- Plates prepared / sold / unsold disposition: NOT ON FILE.
  Same gap as Jul 26.

ECONOMICS
- Revenue / food cost / labor cost / contribution: NOT ON FILE.

GAP (flagged, not papered over)
- Same as Jul 26: per-run demand and contribution figures are
  not in the searchable record. The chef-owner's verdict is
  the only signal on file, and it speaks to variance across
  the three runs, not to the August run alone.

================================================================
WHAT THE EVIDENCE DOES AND DOES NOT SAY
================================================================

- Production is repeatable on the tested pre-staging sequence
  with the 30 lb case (3 of 3 runs cleared both thresholds;
  Jun 28 verified directly, Jul 26 and Aug 16 per chef-owner
  review).

  enough that a standing weekly slot was not justified.

  approved after reviewing all three runs.

- The exact plates-sold figure for Jul 26 or Aug 16.
- The unsold disposition on either repeat.
- The contribution figure on either repeat.

  Jun 28 posted, or whether both repeats underperformed. The
  chef-owner's "varied enough" phrasing is consistent with both
  one-and-one or two-underperforming outcomes; the record does
  not distinguish.

================================================================
NOTE ON THE REPEAT-TRIAL DOCUMENT
================================================================
The comparative repeat-trial doc (doc_1789332028679, folder
"Kitchen", created Jul 3, 2024) carries the Jun 28 baseline in
full and the Jul 26 / Aug 16 sections as blank templates with
the same field set. If those blanks were filled in later, the

so the per-run demand and economics above are flagged as gaps
rather than reconstructed.

================================================================
- Repeatable production: yes — three controlled trials cleared

  per the chef-owner's Aug 19, 2024 review.

  supports and the chef-owner approved.

  are not on file in this environment; if they are needed for

messages.content:
Compact sequence — fits in the gap between watercolor end and departure (~3 min if the painting is dry):

1. Dryness check (right before you pack)
   - Touch a clean back corner to the inside of your wrist. Room-temp = dry. Cool = still damp; leave it.
   - Press a corner of interleaving paper to the painted face for 10 sec. No pigment transfer = dry.

2. Sandwich — bottom board → painting → interleaving → top board
   - Bottom board flat on a table.
   - Painting face-up on the board (board touches only the back of the paper).
   - Interleaving sheet over the painted face.
   - Top board on top — never touches paint.

3. Secure — tape on boards only; never crosses the painting
   - Four short strips, one across each edge seam, joining the boards.
   - Or one strip wrapped around the full perimeter.
   - Removable paper tape → no residue on boards, never reaches the painting.

4. Pack
   - Slide the sandwich flat into the tote, painting-side up. Jostle pushes the bottom board into the back of the paper, not the painted face.
   - Two rigid boards prevent warping from cabin pressure / humidity swing; interleaving prevents offset onto the top board.
   - Tote in carry-on, not checked.

5. Airport
   - Keep sandwich flat in the tote until the security belt.
   - At X-ray: lift it flat out, lay face-up in its own bin, tote in another bin. Reassemble after.

Block fit: ~3 minutes end-of-watercolor → leaving for the airport. No change to either block. If the check fails, leave it and ship / carry on a later flight.
