- The reference frame used for the routine-vs-state-changing call was the 2027-12-01 precedent: op-wording clarifications are routine + non-state-changing; incomplete-setup (non-admin) is state-changing and must be escalated, not released.

Basis for marking the development goal complete: Priya recorded Ines's Q4 development focus as met on 2027-12-08. The independent lifecycle-risk explanations across all three cycles were the observable artifact; each explanation correctly placed its item on the routine or state-changing side using the 12/1 reference frame; state-changing items were escalated, not released; routine items stayed within her release lane. The classification-only posture was held — Ines did not act as the release gate, did not redefine the 12/1 precedent, and did not stretch her lane into engineering control.

# Helio Start — decision spine (working draft for Wed)

What Tomás and Marcus are approving: a guarded operating model for moving the
sub-50-seat band from pre-discovery into discovery — defined as a four-gate
readiness contract, not a launch plan. The motion becomes launchable only when
the four gates clear in writing; until then, every output is internal and every
artifact lives inside this brief. This is the structure that turns the four
risks Priya, Owen, Daniela, and Ines surfaced into a single decision the room
can take Wednesday without re-litigating each gate separately.

## The decision on the table (one sentence)

Approve the operating model and the four readiness gates below as the path from
pre-discovery to discovery for the sub-50-seat band; do not approve pricing-page
motion, public naming, or Q3 launch — those remain conditional and ungoverned
by this decision.

## The four gates, named

Each gate has an owner, a written artifact the gate produces, and a clear
exclusion that keeps the gate from drifting into adjacent workstreams.

1. Instrumentation gate (Daniela)
   Owner: Daniela's team, with Riley as cross-workstream constraint-check.
   Artifact: written event taxonomy + entitlement-state instrumentation plan
   covering admin complexity, import/migration help, support handoff, and
   entitlement state — the four properties flagged in the engineering scoping.
   Exit: end-to-end verification against a known cohort (Owen's baseline cut),
   not "events fire." This gate is hard before any pricing-page experiment or
   public launch.

2. Measurement spine (Owen)
   Owner: Owen, weekly cadence, 1-pager format (why / cuts / p-value /
   effect-size / call) at the top with raw attached.
   Artifact: the under-50 baseline cut, band-separated from the 75-200 v2
   mid-seg cohort and the 50-75 starter band per the 2023-04-26 taxonomy.
   Exit: a cut the room can read as an anchor, not a treatment effect. The
   number fills in from Monday's cohort-cuts recurring; the spine here is the
   structure the number sits inside.
   Frame to repeat in the readout: this is a baseline. It tells us where we
   start, not what changed it.

3. Eligibility + refusal rules (Riley, with Daniela)
   Owner: Riley (business rules), Daniela (eng scoping).
   Artifact: written boundary conditions for sub-50 self-serve eligibility and
   refusal/guardrail logic that routes accounts back to sales-assisted when
   they don't fit. Testable, not vibes. Includes the billing-exception /
   manual-import / migration-help refusal risks for June.
   Exit: rules signed off by Priya before any external motion.

4. Pricing-page coordination rule (Marcus Vail, with Riley as constraint-check)
   Owner: Marcus Vail owns formalizing the rule; Riley owns confirming the
   sub-50 workstream respects it. This was flagged as the one sentence not yet
   anchored to a writing owner — fixing that here.
   Artifact: one short note from Marcus to the room naming the rule and the
   owner. Rule: no concurrent pricing-page layout/UI change runs adjacent to
   any sub-50 motion. Sub-50 only lands on the pricing page when (a) operating
   logic above is settled and (b) sequencing respects this rule.
   Exit: confirmation in writing before any motion.

## Why this lands as "guarded operating model," not "we're scared"

Each gate is named with an owner and an artifact. The decision Wednesday is
whether to commit to those four artifacts on the cadence below — it is not a
decision to ship anything externally. That is the difference between a
guarded operating model and a list of reasons to do nothing:

- The decision commits four owners to four written artifacts on a 12-week
  envelope — measurable, defensible, and reviewable at the next readout.
- Each gate explicitly names what is NOT in scope (pricing-page launch, public
  naming, Q3 launch) so the room cannot accidentally read the decision as a
  launch promise.
- The Q3 ship → 65% activation target remains conditional on the four outputs
  landing and Marcus Vail's instrumentation sign-off. One sentence, said out
  loud: "Q3 is still conditional, gated on instrumentation finishing." That
  pre-empts the re-litigation question.

## What Ines's lifecycle fork becomes inside this spine

Ines's risk map stays open as a working state inside the eligibility /
lifecycle track — not as a fourth standalone gate. The rule that closes the
risk without expanding the gate: lifecycle copy and support routing can be
mapped and QA'd against assumptions now (light tier per 2023-06-23), but no
state-changing lifecycle touch ships until entitlement + support-handoff state
exists. Branches in Customer.io are marked as assumptions and left
un-configured; when instrumentation lands, assumptions reconcile against real
properties, validate on a small cohort, then turn on.

This is the fork-risk surface named, not the fork opened. It keeps Priya's
"nothing Helio Start-shaped ships until eligibility, instrumentation, and
support boundaries are all real" line intact.

## What the expansion-nudge read becomes inside this spine

It doesn't. expansion_nudge_60d_v1 is a separate retained-mid (75-200 v2)
behavior-based motion on its own pre-reg gate (standing rule, 2023-03-26:
first sig doesn't ship, wait one stab cohort, stab def + p<0.01 second-look
bar before next peek). The 2023-06-22 read closed inconclusive; rollout stays
at 25% and eligibility does not widen to the high-depth slice from this read.
Saying that on the record once — "expansion-nudge is a separate retained-mid
behavior-based learning, not a Helio Start proof point" — closes the
conflation door Marcus is most likely to push on.

## Decisions for the room Wednesday

1. Approve the four-gate operating model above as the path from pre-discovery
   to discovery for the sub-50-seat band.
2. Accept instrumentation as the hard gate before any pricing-page experiment
   or launch.
3. Confirm the no-concurrent pricing-page layout/UI-change rule, with Marcus
   Vail owning formalization.
4. Hold Q3 launch as conditional on the four gates clearing and Marcus Vail's
   instrumentation sign-off.

## Not decisions this week

- No public pricing-page copy change.
- No Q3 launch commitment (still conditional).
- No change to retained-mid expansion-nudge eligibility or rollout (still 25%,
   pre-reg gate held).
- No Helio Start external motion until the four artifacts above exist.

## Open questions for the readout (kept tight)

- Engineering: event taxonomy freeze date; capacity split between activation-
  event instrumentation and tier-eligibility instrumentation (these compete
  for the same eng weeks — confirm they are priced separately, not bundled).
- Lifecycle: which onboarding paths must fork to support the sub-50 shape
  without creating support promises Ines can't back.
- Support: which handoffs are allowed for the first self-serve shape and
  which remain assisted (this is the smallest paragraph in the doc and the
  one most likely to bite us in week 3 if left open).
- Measurement: the >15-point lag figure for complex sub-50 deployments needs
  a one-line source attribution ("from under-50 cohort cuts, [date]") before
  it lands in the readout.

## Three sentences the readout must hit in the first 90 seconds

1. "Helio Start is in pre-discovery — this is a scope and instrumentation
   conversation, not a ship-date conversation." Closes: are we launching?
2. "Owen's under-50 numbers are a baseline. They tell us where we start, not
   what changed it." Closes: is this causal?
3. "Expansion-nudge is a separate retained-mid behavior-based learning — it
   isn't a Helio Start proof point." Closes: does this prove Helio Start
   works?

results.snippet:

messages.content:
Call: Exclude all 14 from the latency analysis for now. Don't impute. Run latency on the unaffected rows, note the exclusion, and track the 9 pending as a forward reconciliation — not a blocker for the rest of the read.

Why this is the right move:

  - The Oct 31 2:00am stamp is a warehouse artifact, not a product event. Substituting it would manufacture an artificial spike in the latency distribution (all 14 clustered at one timestamp) and corrupt the median and tail reads. You're already ruling that out.
  - Activation v3 stays fixed. The independent evidence supporting the classifications is intact, and per how you've handled prior exception reviews, accepted point-in-time tables don't get rewritten by later reconciliation findings — the timestamp issue is a forward event, not a reclassification.
  - N=14 out of a Q3 activation-v3 cohort is small. Excluding them won't materially shift the latency read, especially since the cohort count is what stakeholders actually care about and you've already separated that from this secondary cut.

Cuts to run:

  1. Primary latency cut — exclude all 14, run on the remaining cohort. State N explicitly and call out the exclusion reason in the methods note so it's not invisible to whoever picks this up next.
  2. Sensitivity cut — for the 5 rows where immutable connector logs give you an original, swap those in and report that subset separately with a clear provenance label (connector-log original, not warehouse event). Don't merge into the primary cut; the methodology has to stay clean.
  3. Pending register — track the 9 remaining rows with owner, ETA, and source-log location. When they land, run the reconciliation as an update to the sensitivity cut, not a revision to the primary.

Effect:

  - Cohort count: unchanged, as you noted.
  - Latency metric: based on real product events only. The 14 show up as an honest N reduction with a documented reason, not as a fabricated distribution.
  - Reproducibility: anyone re-running gets the same answer until the 9 logs land. No silent moves.

Two judgment calls worth flagging before you lock it:

  - Scope check for Owen: his QA found 14 because he was looking. Worth asking whether backfilled warehouse timestamps could be hiding elsewhere in the cohort under a different shape. If yes, the latency methodology note needs to acknowledge that as a residual risk, not just a one-off N=14.
  - Naming the 9: do you want them visible somewhere (working doc, thread with Owen) so reconciliation doesn't get quietly dropped, or kept internal until they land? I'd make them visible — silent-pending is how these stay pending.

Question back to you: do you want the 5 connector-log originals folded in as a sensitivity cut now, or held entirely aside until the 9 land and the full 14 are reconciled together in one pass? I lean sensitivity cut now — partial recovery beats no recovery, and provenance is labeled so it can't bleed into the primary read. Your call.

arguments.body:
# Riley Tanaka — H1 2027 self-review working notes

For: Priya. Draft due June 4. Center: outcomes, operating leverage, one development edge. Style: summary first; why / cuts / p / effect / call.

One-line summary: H1 was the half I stopped doing the work and started ruling on it — operating model reset in January, exception-only hands-on through Q1, bounded Q2 paid test, and one deliberate growth edge.

## 1. January operating-model transition

What changed: briefs became descriptive, not prescriptive. I rule on disputed / cross-surface / exec asks only; routine line-edits stay with the owner. Release and rollback authority moved to Daniela. Kickoff and certification flow through Priya. The point was to push variance out of the routine path and concentrate my judgment where it's actually load-bearing.

Effect: fewer rewrites mid-flight, cleaner signal in #growth-investigations and #lifecycle-systems, and I regained hours I'd been losing to second-opinion reviews.

Call: the model held. Don't relitigate it this half.

## 2. Exception-only involvement + quarterly hands-on audit

Day-to-day, I'm out of the routine path — I read locks before recurring meetings and I weigh in on the cohort cuts Owen and I walk through Mondays. Once per quarter I run a hands-on audit anyway, to keep my eye calibrated and to catch what the dashboards miss.

[TBD — fill: which audit (e.g. mid-segment churn cohort), dates, the one finding that changed a decision.]

The audit is leverage, not a deliverable: it lets me stay credible in exceptions without re-entering the queue.

## 3. Q2 Helio Start paid test — bounded execution

Closed 5/17 (Owen '27 cohort, CS-led paid-source lane):
- 25-admin enrollment cap; $7.6K committed; 61 screened → 25 active / 18 assistant / 18 ineligible.
- Attribution reconciles end-to-end (no double-count vs. organic).
- Support load: 2 of 25 = 8% exceeded 90-min support. No pause triggered. No unsupported admin.
- Day-90 window still open as of 5/20 — retention and downstream ARR impact are NOT yet established by this test.

What this test establishes:
- Paid-source mechanics work: enrollment gating, eligibility filter, attribution, support-cost baseline.
- The 25-admin cap is operationally safe at this support ratio.

What this test does NOT establish (read these out loud if asked):
- Day-90 retention, expansion, or net revenue — window incomplete.
- Generalizability to organic-source cohorts or other tiers.
- Authority for an eligibility or lifecycle change.
- That paid is preferable to organic at scale — that's a different experiment.

Decision lane: I signed off on the bounded scope and the NOs. Source mechanics, screening rules, and day-to-day enrollment are Owen's routine ownership. Lifecycle and certification governance are Ines's lane. Engineering controls on release/rollback are Daniela's. I did not, and should not, edit those layers mid-test.

## 4. Team development

[Fill in 2–3 concrete moments. Suggested frame: who grew into what, what I stopped doing so they could do it, what I unblocked. Avoid generic "supportive manager" language — Priya wants the moves.]

Working frame I'd use: Owen took full source ownership on Helio Start with me only on exceptions — that's the development, not a status update. Ines ran lifecycle kickoff and certification end-to-end without escalation. Daniela held release authority and I stayed out of it. [Add one moment where I explicitly got out of the way and it landed.]

## 5. One growth edge

The edge I want to name: learning to stop reading every brief end-to-end and only reading the locks + exceptions. Half 1 was the operational version of this (the model transition). Half 2 is the personal version — pushing my own floor on what I'll touch, and trusting the lanes.

Why it matters: if I keep drifting into the routine path under load, the model erodes quietly. The edge is keeping the model intact when it's inconvenient, not when it's easy.

## Boundaries to keep clean in the draft

- My decisions: scope of Helio Start paid test, the NOs (no lifecycle bypass, no 5th shared-state, no eligibility change), quarterly audit calls, disputed/cross-surface/exec rulings.
- Owen: routine source ownership — mechanics, screening, enrollment ops.
- Ines: lifecycle governance — kickoff, certification, journey rules.
- Daniela: engineering controls — release, rollback, feature-flag gating.

Don't let the draft blur these. If a sentence could be read as me owning Owen's, Ines's, or Daniela's lane, rewrite it as my ruling on a question they brought me.

---

[For the final pass: tighten section 2 (audit specifics) and section 4 (2–3 concrete moments). Sections 1, 3, 5, and the boundaries block are draft-ready.]

# Cohort-cut template — historical operating pattern

**Status:** Archived reference. Documents the operating pattern used while two experiments were cut concurrently on the same weekly pass. **Not a current-work assignment.** No lanes are running today under this template; lane ownership and any active cuts live in current docs.

---

## Context this template was built from

During the Mar–Apr 2023 window, two experiments were live concurrently and being read on the same weekly cohort cut:

1. **Pricing-page weekly cohort cut** — `pricing_page_2026q2_rev` (EXP-2023-02-pricing-page, shipped 2023-03-07).
2. **Onboarding-trigger weekly cohort cut** — `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2` (EXP-2023-04-onboarding-trigger, shipped 2023-04-10).

Both ran in the same weekly pass on Mondays. The cut shape, owner, and packaging below were the operating pattern for that concurrent window.

---

## Template — copy this block when a future cut needs it

```
[Experiment name] — weekly cohort cut — [date]
Flag key: [flag_key]
Cohort: [segment / seat-band / cut-def]
Metric of record: [e.g. activation v3, day-7 retention, conversion-by-day]

=== 1-PAGER (summary up top; Riley scans this first) ===

Why this cut exists: [one sentence — the question it's answering]
Cuts run:
  - [cut 1 — what was sliced, why]
  - [cut 2 — what was sliced, why]
  - [optional: cut 3 — planning view, direction-only]
p-value: [value or "n/a — monitor read"]
Effect size: [value + unit, vs. baseline]
Call: [ship / hold / cut-again / roll-back / inconclusive]
Guardrails: [what held; what was NOT tested]

=== RAW DATA (attached below) ===
- [CSV / table / query export — one row per observation, full N]
- [Provenance: source table, query timestamp, owner]
- [Exclusions: rows dropped and reason]
```

---

## Operating pattern this documents (historical, not assigned)

- **Owner of the cut:** Owen (read-only / sign-off: Riley; cuts in the Mon protected block).
- **Cadence:** Weekly, Mondays. 08:30–10:00 CT protected block. Both lanes cut in the same pass when more than one was live.
- **Packaging rule (locked 2023-02-13):** every ruling in/out → 1-pager with why / cuts / p-value / effect-size / call. Summary up top, raw data attached. Riley scans the summary first and only opens the raw cuts for the metrics in scope.
- **Pre-registration discipline:** stabilization def + second-look bar pinned before each new cohort (same metric, same direction, n ≥ treatment, p<0.01 second-look) — no peeking between cuts.
- **Scope discipline:** lanes are kept scope-disjoint for attribution. Pricing-page cuts and onboarding-trigger cuts were not co-mingled, even when cut in the same weekly pass.

---

## How to use this template

1. Copy the block above.
2. Fill in the 1-pager section first (summary up top is the contract).
3. Attach the raw data — full N, provenance, exclusions called out.
4. Route: Riley scans summary; raw cuts opened only on the metrics in scope.
5. Treat any cross-lane signal (e.g. a metric that touches both lanes) as a separate investigation, not as a co-mingled cut.

---

## What this template deliberately does not do

- Does not assign ownership of any current cut.
- Does not authorize re-opening any closed lane.
- Does not substitute for current-work docs (those live in the working folders, not the archive).
- Does not change the standing pre-registration or scope-disjoint rules.

---

## Provenance

Sourced from session history covering the Mar 14, 2023 concurrent-cut Monday and the locked cadence rule from 2023-02-13. Lane names and flag keys preserved as they appeared at the time.

• Ines Kovac — lifecycle governance and message-state controls. Owns cadence, change control, audit posture, and the controls that gate when a message may fire or a state transition is permitted.
• Daniela's team — engineering partner for event and state reliability. • CS case ownership stays with CS; Lifecycle Systems defines the lifecycle-state inputs CS reads.

1. The shared state contract is not live in production. Approval authorizes the function and the remit; any production rollout of a shared-state implementation requires a separate go decision (Ines on governance, Daniela's org on reliability).

3. Helio Start five-state model (admitted / assisted / ineligible / final-reconciliation / pending) and the intake-rule-additive / refusal-non-softening rule are unchanged.

Agenda (45 min):
1. Decision record walk-through (§9) and the §8 boundary clarification — confirm shared read on scope.
2. Each lane lead (Owen, Ines, Daniela's team, Riley) gives a 5-minute read on what "ready to operate" looks like for their lane by EOD Friday, January 31, and what would block it.

arguments.body:
# 2027 Lifecycle Systems leadership model — approved decision record (effective January 5, 2027)

Author: Riley Tanaka
Status: APPROVED. Effective date: January 5, 2027. Nothing in this decision takes effect before January 5, 2027. Through January 4, 2027, Riley continues current routine monthly preparation and routine source-closure attendance unchanged.

Source of approval
- 2026-12-04 morning decision meeting (Priya presiding). Recorded in this entry per Riley's 2026-12-04T11:18-06:00 message.

Update log
- 2026-11-18: Initial draft.
- 2026-11-24: Updated after 11:00am 1:1 with Owen. Added the four preserved-cadence properties in §2, the audit-evidence sequencing rule in §4, R9 in §6, and consolidated Q9 in §7.
- 2026-11-25: Updated after Ines and Daniela input. Added §1a (four functions and their holders); audit-role boundaries in §4; R10 audit-role boundary drift; Q10 on audit shape.
- 2026-12-01: Recommendation finalized. Replaced §4 with quarterly rotating recheck of one evidence lane. Five inspection dimensions, four safeguards, lane-selection sequencing rule, half-day budget. Implementation date left for Priya's decision.
- 2026-12-04: APPROVED by Priya in this morning's decision meeting. Effective date set to January 5, 2027. This entry converts the document from a decision draft to the approved decision record. Status header updated from PROPOSAL to APPROVED. Implementation date locked to January 5, 2027. Business-day cadence for Owen/Ines/Daniela and the late-month closure rule for Owen added as §2a. Riley's attendance change and recheck cadence retained from the approved recommendation. Nothing in this record takes effect before January 5, 2027.

## 1. Purpose & decision posture

Approved operating model for the Lifecycle Systems function from January 5, 2027. Riley stands out of routine monthly preparation and routine source-closure attendance; Owen, Ines, and Daniela carry the routine cycle under the boundaries below. Riley stands in via the closed escalation set (§3) and the quarterly rotating recheck (§4). Final decision authority on the five domains in §5 is retained without narrowing.

Effective date: January 5, 2027. Through January 4, 2027, Riley continues current routine monthly preparation and routine source-closure attendance; nothing in this decision takes effect early.

## 1a. Four functions and their holders

Unchanged from the approved recommendation. The four functions are kept separate; the holders do not exchange their function.

- Source closure. Owen. Routine monthly preparation, source-completeness check, source-completeness closure, named-owner certification on the standard pack.
- Owner certification (lifecycle governance). Ines. Routine message-state governance, precise extension-authority language, bounded instructional wording, lifecycle-governance certification.
- Independent verification (the recheck). Riley. The quarterly rotating recheck of one evidence lane as defined in §4. Inspects evidence; does not collapse into source closure, owner certification, or engineering controls.
- Final claim authority. Riley. Retained decision rights (§5). The recheck is not a route for second approval of routine claims.

## 2. Delegated monthly cadence

Four lanes and their owners unchanged from FY26. What changes effective January 5, 2027: who carries routine prep and routine source-closure attendance. Riley steps out of those two specific activities; everything else stays.

Lane A — Preparation and source-closure ownership: Owen
- Routine monthly preparation: data pulls, cycle definitions, source-completeness check.
- Named-owner certification on the standard pack.
- Routine source-closure attendance: Owen owns the close on routine packets.
- Source of authority: unchanged from FY26 definition.

Lane B — Lifecycle governance and message-state discipline: Ines
- Routine message-state governance (sending/suppressed/queued state correctness).
- Precise extension-authority language on outbound claims.
- Bounded instructional wording (no expansion of claim scope beyond the approved surface).
- Lifecycle-governance certification.

Lane C — Cross-cycle/strategic: Priya
- Owns the cross-cycle narrative, the broader Lifecycle Systems roadmap, and the cross-cycle calendar.

Lane D — Final authority: Riley
- Retains decision rights (§5).
- Stands out of routine prep and routine source-closure attendance effective January 5, 2027.
- Stands in via the quarterly rotating recheck (§4) and via escalation (§3).

What the delegated cadence preserves
The delegation transfers *who carries* routine prep and source-closure attendance to Owen and Ines. It does not change the form of the cadence. The following four properties must continue to hold under the delegation; they are part of the approved record, not implementation details.

1. Second-business-day snapshot preparation. The monthly snapshot is prepared by the second business day of the cycle.
2. Named-owner certification before closure. Owen for source completeness; Ines for lifecycle governance. No silent closures.
3. Explicit incomplete status when any required field or owner certification is missing. The closure cannot proceed in that state.
4. One closure-and-exception summary per cycle, not informal follow-up fragments.

Amending or dropping any of these four properties requires an explicit decision, not implementation drift.

## 2a. Routine monthly cadence — business-day deadlines (effective January 5, 2027)

The following business-day deadlines are part of the approved record. They govern the routine monthly cycle once the new model is in effect. They do not take effect before January 5, 2027.

- By the second business day of the cycle: Owen's monthly sanitized campaign snapshot is due. This is the routine handoff artifact for the cycle.
- By the fourth business day of the cycle:
  - Ines's lifecycle-governance and owner-state certification is due.
  - Daniela's source-reliability and release certification is due.
- By the fifth business day of the cycle: Owen must either close the routine four-lane source review or explicitly leave it incomplete, and send one closure-and-exception summary. If incomplete, the closure cannot proceed in that state (per §2 property 3).

These deadlines are hard dates against the calendar of the cycle, not against completion of any other step. They are part of the cadence, not implementation details.

## 3. Escalation triggers retained (not narrowed)

Riley is escalated into on any of the following six triggers. The set is closed. Adding a trigger requires Riley's sign-off; removing one is not on the table.

1. Missing fields in a routine packet.
2. Disputed semantics on a defined term or claim surface.
3. Cross-surface discrepancies (e.g., a number that reconciles in one surface but not another).
4. Customer corrections (a customer has flagged an inaccuracy that affects a routine claim).
5. Incident stops (anything that pauses, rolls back, or quarantines a routine cycle).
6. Causal, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, or executive-language decisions.

Escalation is *into Riley's queue*. Owen, Ines, and Daniela remain the named owners; Riley arbitrates and decides.

## 4. Quarterly rotating recheck of one evidence lane (approved)

Approved as the concrete independent verification activity replacing the prior monthly hands-on audit shape. Effective January 5, 2027.

Recommendation summary (now approved)
- Cadence: quarterly. One recheck per quarter.
- Subject: one evidence lane per quarter.
- Lane selection: only after Owen's routine packet closure for the relevant cycle is recorded. The recheck does not select or shape the routine sample.
- Five inspection dimensions (each recheck walks all five):
  1. Denominator or coverage dates. Inspect, do not modify.
  2. Outcome window. Inspect, do not redefine.
  3. Exclusions. Inspect, do not authorize or remove.
  4. Reliability evidence. Inspect; per Daniela's constraint, the recheck inspects reliability evidence only and does not release, suppress, restore, or roll back anything. Engineering controls remain in Daniela's lane.
  5. Revenue and forecast treatment. Inspect; per §5, causal/revenue/forecast decision rights remain with Riley.
- Four safeguards (each must hold for every recheck):
  1. Does not reopen source closure. The recheck does not revisit Owen's source-completeness decision or modify it.
  2. Does not approve Ines's owner certification. The recheck does not convert Ines's lifecycle-governance certification into a request for Riley's approval.
  3. Does not exercise Daniela's release or rollback controls. The recheck does not release, suppress, restore, or roll back anything.
  4. Does not create a second approval queue. The recheck produces an inspection artifact, not a separate approval. Findings, if any, flow through the existing escalation set (§3) or as input to the next cycle's source-completeness decision — never as an amendment to the current cycle's closure.
- Lane rotation: default rotates by quarter. Repeated selection of the same lane requires an explicit decision and a written reason.
- Time budget: one recheck per quarter; half-day at most.
- Artifact: a one-page recheck note per quarter, posted in the Lifecycle Systems folder by the second business day of the week following the quarter close. Format: lane selected, source of record, dimension-by-dimension result, safeguard confirmation, findings (if any), sign-off. The note cites Owen's recorded source-completeness decision for the relevant cycle and is filed in the Lifecycle Systems folder, not in the routine closure packet.

Quarterly recheck does not: reopen source closure; approve Ines's certification; exercise Daniela's release or rollback controls.

## 5. Decision rights retained (not narrowed)

Riley retains final decision authority on the following five domains. The model must not narrow any of these.

- Causal: any claim of the form "X caused Y" or "because of X" in a routine or strategic surface.
- Revenue: ARR/MRR/expansion/contraction claims, including cohort cuts and segment reads.
- Forecast: forward-looking revenue, retention, or growth projections.
- Board-readiness: anything headed to the board pack or the board pre-read.
- Final-claim: any claim whose authority is the Lifecycle Systems function rather than a named owner.

Note on generalization: the Nov 13 decision was on a bounded surface. It is one data point. The model must not assume all routine claims will close the way Nov 13 did. This is why the recheck (§4) exists.

## 6. Implementation risks (retained)

R1 — False confidence from two clean closes. Mitigation: recheck (§4) and closed escalation set (§3).
R2 — Recheck becomes performative. Mitigation: Riley picks the lane from a defined set; lanes rotate by quarter; same-lane repetition requires an explicit decision.
R3 — Escalation under-triggering. Mitigation: the six triggers are closed and escalation is *into Riley's queue*.
R4 — Scope creep into causal/revenue/forecast language. Mitigation: §5 decision rights are explicit; the recheck's revenue and forecast dimension inspects treatment but does not decide it.
R5 — Cadence drift vs. cross-cycle obligations. Mitigation: Priya owns the cross-cycle calendar; recheck lanes may land on a cross-cycle quarter.
R6 — Cert completeness decoupling. Mitigation: recheck dimensions 1 and 3 explicitly check that the lane's source supports the cert.
R7 — Key-person risk. Mitigation: if Owen or Ines is vacant or transitioning, default to *no delegation* — Riley re-attends routine prep and source closure until the role is filled.
R8 — Confusion with the manager-calibration channel. Mitigation: the recheck note is filed in the Lifecycle Systems folder, not the calibration folder.
R9 — Recheck versus closure. Mitigation: lane-selection sequencing rule in §4; closed escalation set in §3; semi-annual recheck-vs-closure check at the end of Q2 FY27 and at the re-decision point. If the recheck is functioning as a second closure review, the default is to re-attend routine prep and source closure until the recheck design is reset.
R10 — Audit-role boundary drift (cert drift, engineering-control drift). Mitigation: §1a explicitly names the four functions as separate; the four safeguards in §4 prohibit both drift modes. If either drift mode is observed, the default is to re-attend routine prep and source closure until the recheck design is reset.
R11 — Quarterly cadence too sparse. Mitigation: the closed escalation set (§3) catches acute issues mid-quarter; the recheck is a system test, not real-time monitoring.
R12 — Lane set too narrow. Mitigation: lane set defined as part of the approved record; expand or amend at the re-decision point if coverage is too thin.

## 7. Decision questions — closed by approval

Closed by Priya's approval on December 4, 2026, with effective date January 5, 2027:

Q1. Approved as drafted.
Q2. No amendments to the escalation trigger set (§3).
Q3. No amendments to the recheck (§4) shape.
Q4. No amendments to decision rights (§5).
Q5. Implementation date: January 5, 2027. Through January 4, 2027, Riley continues current routine monthly preparation and routine source-closure attendance; nothing takes effect early.
Q6. Re-decision cadence: re-decide at end of Q2 FY27 (end of June 2027) based on recheck notes and escalation volume.
Q7. Vacancy / transition rule (R7): confirmed.
Q8. Cross-cycle synchronization (R5): confirmed. Priya owns the cross-cycle calendar; recheck lanes may land on cross-cycle quarters.
Q9. Cadence-preservation rules and recheck-vs-closure sequencing: confirmed. The four preserved-cadence properties in §2 hold under the delegation; the lane-selection sequencing rule in §4 holds; recheck findings flow through §3 and are filed as a separate artifact; a semi-annual recheck-vs-closure check at the end of Q2 FY27 and again at the re-decision point.
Q10. Quarterly recheck recommendation: approved. Cadence = quarterly; subject = one evidence lane per quarter. Five inspection dimensions fixed; four safeguards fixed; lane-selection sequencing rule holds.

## 8. Pre-effective window (through January 4, 2027)

Until the effective date, nothing changes. Specifically:

- Riley continues current routine monthly preparation.
- Riley continues current routine source-closure attendance.
- Owen continues current second-business-day snapshot preparation cadence, but the formal sanitized campaign snapshot due on the second business day per §2a does not bind until January 5.
- Ines continues current lifecycle-governance and owner-state certification work; the fourth-business-day deadline per §2a does not bind until January 5.
- Daniela continues current source-reliability and release work; the fourth-business-day deadline per §2a does not bind until January 5.
- Owen continues current five-business-day closure / closure-and-exception summary work; the fifth-business-day deadline per §2a does not bind until January 5.

Effective January 5, 2027, the §2a deadlines govern.

---

End of approved decision record. Effective January 5, 2027.

- 2026-11-18: Initial draft.
- 2026-11-24: Updated after 11:00am 1:1 with Owen. Added the four preserved-cadence properties in §2, the audit-evidence sequencing rule in §4, R9 in §6, and consolidated Q9 in §7.
- 2026-11-25: Updated after Ines and Daniela input. Added §1a (four functions and their holders); audit-role boundaries in §4; R10 audit-role boundary drift; Q10 on audit shape.
- 2026-12-01: Recommendation finalized. Replaced §4 with quarterly rotating recheck of one evidence lane. Five inspection dimensions, four safeguards, lane-selection sequencing rule, half-day budget. Implementation date left for Priya's decision.
- 2026-12-04: APPROVED by Priya in this morning's decision meeting. Effective date set to January 5, 2027. This entry converts the document from a decision draft to the approved decision record. Status header updated from PROPOSAL to APPROVED. Implementation date locked to January 5, 2027. Business-day cadence for Owen/Ines/Daniela and the late-month closure rule for Owen added as §2a. Riley's attendance change and recheck cadence retained from the approved recommendation. Nothing in this record takes effect before January 5, 2027.

## 1. Purpose & decision posture

Approved operating model for the Lifecycle Systems function from January 5, 2027. Riley stands out of routine monthly preparation and routine source-closure attendance; Owen, Ines, and Daniela carry the routine cycle under the boundaries below. Riley stands in via the closed escalation set (§3) and the quarterly rotating recheck (§4). Final decision authority on the five domains in §5 is retained without narrowing.

Effective date: January 5, 2027. Through January 4, 2027, Riley continues current routine monthly preparation and routine source-closure attendance; nothing in this decision takes effect early.

## 1a. Four functions and their holders

Unchanged from the approved recommendation. The four functions are kept separate; the holders do not exchange their function.

- Source closure. Owen. Routine monthly preparation, source-completeness check, source-completeness closure, named-owner certification on the standard pack.
- Owner certification (lifecycle governance). Ines. Routine message-state governance, precise extension-authority language, bounded instructional wording, lifecycle-governance certification.
- Independent verification (the recheck). Riley. The quarterly rotating recheck of one evidence lane as defined in §4. Inspects evidence; does not collapse into source closure, owner certification, or engineering controls.
- Final claim authority. Riley. Retained decision rights (§5). The recheck is not a route for second approval of routine claims.

## 2. Delegated monthly cadence

Four lanes and their owners unchanged from FY26. What changes effective January 5, 2027: who carries routine prep and routine source-closure attendance. Riley steps out of those two specific activities; everything else stays.

Lane A — Preparation and source-closure ownership: Owen
- Routine monthly preparation: data pulls, cycle definitions, source-completeness check.
- Named-owner certification on the standard pack.
- Routine source-closure attendance: Owen owns the close on routine packets.
- Source of authority: unchanged from FY26 definition.

Lane B — Lifecycle governance and message-state discipline: Ines
- Routine message-state governance (sending/suppressed/queued state correctness).
- Precise extension-authority language on outbound claims.
- Bounded instructional wording (no expansion of claim scope beyond the approved surface).
- Lifecycle-governance certification.

Lane C — Cross-cycle/strategic: Priya
- Owns the cross-cycle narrative, the broader Lifecycle Systems roadmap, and the cross-cycle calendar.

Lane D — Final authority: Riley
- Retains decision rights (§5).
- Stands out of routine prep and routine source-closure attendance effective January 5, 2027.
- Stands in via the quarterly rotating recheck (§4) and via escalation (§3).

What the delegated cadence preserves
The delegation transfers *who carries* routine prep and source-closure attendance to Owen and Ines. It does not change the form of the cadence. The following four properties must continue to hold under the delegation; they are part of the approved record, not implementation details.

1. Second-business-day snapshot preparation. The monthly snapshot is prepared by the second business day of the cycle.
2. Named-owner certification before closure. Owen for source completeness; Ines for lifecycle governance. No silent closures.
3. Explicit incomplete status when any required field or owner certification is missing. The closure cannot proceed in that state.
4. One closure-and-exception summary per cycle, not informal follow-up fragments.

Amending or dropping any of these four properties requires an explicit decision, not implementation drift.

## 2a. Routine monthly cadence — business-day deadlines (effective January 5, 2027)

The following business-day deadlines are part of the approved record. They govern the routine monthly cycle once the new model is in effect. They do not take effect before January 5, 2027.

- By the second business day of the cycle: Owen's monthly sanitized campaign snapshot is due. This is the routine handoff artifact for the cycle.
- By the fourth business day of the cycle:
  - Ines's lifecycle-governance and owner-state certification is due.
  - Daniela's source-reliability and release certification is due.
- By the fifth business day of the cycle: Owen must either close the routine four-lane source review or explicitly leave it incomplete, and send one closure-and-exception summary. If incomplete, the closure cannot proceed in that state (per §2 property 3).

These deadlines are hard dates against the calendar of the cycle, not against completion of any other step. They are part of the cadence, not implementation details.

## 3. Escalation triggers retained (not narrowed)

Riley is escalated into on any of the following six triggers. The set is closed. Adding a trigger requires Riley's sign-off; removing one is not on the table.

1. Missing fields in a routine packet.
2. Disputed semantics on a defined term or claim surface.
3. Cross-surface discrepancies (e.g., a number that reconciles in one surface but not another).
4. Customer corrections (a customer has flagged an inaccuracy that affects a routine claim).
5. Incident stops (anything that pauses, rolls back, or quarantines a routine cycle).
6. Causal, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, or executive-language decisions.

Escalation is *into Riley's queue*. Owen, Ines, and Daniela remain the named owners; Riley arbitrates and decides.

## 4. Quarterly rotating recheck of one evidence lane (approved)

Approved as the concrete independent verification activity replacing the prior monthly hands-on audit shape. Effective January 5, 2027.

Recommendation summary (now approved)
- Cadence: quarterly. One recheck per quarter.
- Subject: one evidence lane per quarter.
- Lane selection: only after Owen's routine packet closure for the relevant cycle is recorded. The recheck does not select or shape the routine sample.
- Five inspection dimensions (each recheck walks all five):
  1. Denominator or coverage dates. Inspect, do not modify.
  2. Outcome window. Inspect, do not redefine.
  3. Exclusions. Inspect, do not authorize or remove.
  4. Reliability evidence. Inspect; per Daniela's constraint, the recheck inspects reliability evidence only and does not release, suppress, restore, or roll back anything. Engineering controls remain in Daniela's lane.
  5. Revenue and forecast treatment. Inspect; per §5, causal/revenue/forecast decision rights remain with Riley.
- Four safeguards (each must hold for every recheck):
  1. Does not reopen source closure. The recheck does not revisit Owen's source-completeness decision or modify it.
  2. Does not approve Ines's owner certification. The recheck does not convert Ines's lifecycle-governance certification into a request for Riley's approval.
  3. Does not exercise Daniela's release or rollback controls. The recheck does not release, suppress, restore, or roll back anything.
  4. Does not create a second approval queue. The recheck produces an inspection artifact, not a separate approval. Findings, if any, flow through the existing escalation set (§3) or as input to the next cycle's source-completeness decision — never as an amendment to the current cycle's closure.
- Lane rotation: default rotates by quarter. Repeated selection of the same lane requires an explicit decision and a written reason.
- Time budget: one recheck per quarter; half-day at most.
- Artifact: a one-page recheck note per quarter, posted in the Lifecycle Systems folder by the second business day of the week following the quarter close. Format: lane selected, source of record, dimension-by-dimension result, safeguard confirmation, findings (if any), sign-off. The note cites Owen's recorded source-completeness decision for the relevant cycle and is filed in the Lifecycle Systems folder, not in the routine closure packet.

Quarterly recheck does not: reopen source closure; approve Ines's certification; exercise Daniela's release or rollback controls.

## 5. Decision rights retained (not narrowed)

Riley retains final decision authority on the following five domains. The model must not narrow any of these.

- Causal: any claim of the form "X caused Y" or "because of X" in a routine or strategic surface.
- Revenue: ARR/MRR/expansion/contraction claims, including cohort cuts and segment reads.
- Forecast: forward-looking revenue, retention, or growth projections.
- Board-readiness: anything headed to the board pack or the board pre-read.
- Final-claim: any claim whose authority is the Lifecycle Systems function rather than a named owner.

Note on generalization: the Nov 13 decision was on a bounded surface. It is one data point. The model must not assume all routine claims will close the way Nov 13 did. This is why the recheck (§4) exists.

## 6. Implementation risks (retained)

R1 — False confidence from two clean closes. Mitigation: recheck (§4) and closed escalation set (§3).
R2 — Recheck becomes performative. Mitigation: Riley picks the lane from a defined set; lanes rotate by quarter; same-lane repetition requires an explicit decision.
R3 — Escalation under-triggering. Mitigation: the six triggers are closed and escalation is *into Riley's queue*.
R4 — Scope creep into causal/revenue/forecast language. Mitigation: §5 decision rights are explicit; the recheck's revenue and forecast dimension inspects treatment but does not decide it.
R5 — Cadence drift vs. cross-cycle obligations. Mitigation: Priya owns the cross-cycle calendar; recheck lanes may land on a cross-cycle quarter.
R6 — Cert completeness decoupling. Mitigation: recheck dimensions 1 and 3 explicitly check that the lane's source supports the cert.
R7 — Key-person risk. Mitigation: if Owen or Ines is vacant or transitioning, default to *no delegation* — Riley re-attends routine prep and source closure until the role is filled.
R8 — Confusion with the manager-calibration channel. Mitigation: the recheck note is filed in the Lifecycle Systems folder, not the calibration folder.
R9 — Recheck versus closure. Mitigation: lane-selection sequencing rule in §4; closed escalation set in §3; semi-annual recheck-vs-closure check at the end of Q2 FY27 and at the re-decision point. If the recheck is functioning as a second closure review, the default is to re-attend routine prep and source closure until the recheck design is reset.
R10 — Audit-role boundary drift (cert drift, engineering-control drift). Mitigation: §1a explicitly names the four functions as separate; the four safeguards in §4 prohibit both drift modes. If either drift mode is observed, the default is to re-attend routine prep and source closure until the recheck design is reset.
R11 — Quarterly cadence too sparse. Mitigation: the closed escalation set (§3) catches acute issues mid-quarter; the recheck is a system test, not real-time monitoring.
R12 — Lane set too narrow. Mitigation: lane set defined as part of the approved record; expand or amend at the re-decision point if coverage is too thin.

## 7. Decision questions — closed by approval

Closed by Priya's approval on December 4, 2026, with effective date January 5, 2027:

Q1. Approved as drafted.
Q2. No amendments to the escalation trigger set (§3).
Q3. No amendments to the recheck (§4) shape.
Q4. No amendments to decision rights (§5).
Q5. Implementation date: January 5, 2027. Through January 4, 2027, Riley continues current routine monthly preparation and routine source-closure attendance; nothing takes effect early.
Q6. Re-decision cadence: re-decide at end of Q2 FY27 (end of June 2027) based on recheck notes and escalation volume.
Q7. Vacancy / transition rule (R7): confirmed.
Q8. Cross-cycle synchronization (R5): confirmed. Priya owns the cross-cycle calendar; recheck lanes may land on cross-cycle quarters.
Q9. Cadence-preservation rules and recheck-vs-closure sequencing: confirmed. The four preserved-cadence properties in §2 hold under the delegation; the lane-selection sequencing rule in §4 holds; recheck findings flow through §3 and are filed as a separate artifact; a semi-annual recheck-vs-closure check at the end of Q2 FY27 and again at the re-decision point.
Q10. Quarterly recheck recommendation: approved. Cadence = quarterly; subject = one evidence lane per quarter. Five inspection dimensions fixed; four safeguards fixed; lane-selection sequencing rule holds.

## 8. Pre-effective window (through January 4, 2027)

Until the effective date, nothing changes. Specifically:

- Riley continues current routine monthly preparation.
- Riley continues current routine source-closure attendance.
- Owen continues current second-business-day snapshot preparation cadence, but the formal sanitized campaign snapshot due on the second business day per §2a does not bind until January 5.
- Ines continues current lifecycle-governance and owner-state certification work; the fourth-business-day deadline per §2a does not bind until January 5.
- Daniela continues current source-reliability and release work; the fourth-business-day deadline per §2a does not bind until January 5.
- Owen continues current five-business-day closure / closure-and-exception summary work; the fifth-business-day deadline per §2a does not bind until January 5.

Effective January 5, 2027, the §2a deadlines govern.

---

End of approved decision record. Effective January 5, 2027.

Maya Shah engagement review — March 20 decision brief
Prepared: 2026-03-18 | Updated: 2026-03-20 (post-review) | For: Priya | Review meeting: 2026-03-20

Summary
Maya's 11:00am engagement review is complete. Evidence supports a separately approved bounded extension; Path A (orderly close on March 27) was rejected on evidence. Priya and Maya signed the bounded extension (Path B) covering March 30 through June 26, 2026 at $72/hr, capped at 12 hrs/week and $12,000 total, with no automatic renewal. No extension hours or deliverables may begin before March 30. All owner lanes are preserved; Maya's authority boundary is unchanged — prep only, no production access or decision authority of any kind.

Current terms (in force through March 27, 2026; unchanged)
- End date: through March 27, 2026
- Rate: $72 / hour
- Weekly ceiling: no more than 20 hours / week
- Total cap: no more than $36,000 cumulative
- Renewal: none automatic

Signed extension (Path B; takes effect March 30, 2026)
- Dates: March 30, 2026 through June 26, 2026 (no automatic renewal)
- Rate: $72 / hour (unchanged)
- Weekly ceiling: no more than 12 hours / week (reduced from 20)
- Total cap: no more than $12,000 cumulative (reduced from $36,000)
- Start condition: no extension hours or deliverables may begin before March 30, 2026
- New preparation deliverables under the extension:
  1. Monthly sanitized campaign snapshot, delivered by the second business day of each month
  2. Q2 board-evidence source-completeness packet, delivered by June 12, 2026
- Any spend, scope, or production-access change beyond the above requires a separately approved amendment

Evidence confirmed in the March 20 review
1. Completed preparation work
   - Maya delivered the monthly sanitized campaign snapshot and supporting prep work on the agreed cadence through the March cycle.

2. Monthly sanitized-inventory completeness
   - March sanitized inventory: 129 unique campaigns
   - All 129 carry a current-or-archived status and an assigned owner

## 1. Why a test, not a launch

Pricing-page path clarity has been floated as a launch lever, but the eligible-workspace admission path and the message-state guide for the connector-adjacent product area already moved earlier in Q3. We do not want to stack another surface change into the same quarter without a controlled read on whether the clarity gain is real and whether it hurts conversion or support load. This brief frames the change as a **bounded organic-only test** with explicit thresholds so we get a clean signal before any rollout decision.

## 2. Hypothesis

If we give the bounded under-50, simple-deployment Helio Start path and the assisted path separate entry points on the pricing page, then users with an existing unsupported condition self-route to the assisted path more often before starting Helio Start, reducing wasted eligibility-flow starts that later route out — without hurting eligible-workspace admission completion or support load.

## 3. Population & split

- **Population:** all pricing-page sessions in the test window.
- **Split:** 50/50, deterministic at the session level (specifics locked with Ines before 10/20).
- **Exclusions:** paid traffic (out of scope by design); internal/staff sessions.

## 4. Treatment (control vs. variant)

- **Control:** current single pricing-page entry to the Helio Start / assisted paths.
- **Variant:** two separate entry points —
  1. **Helio Start** — clearly labeled for the bounded under-50, simple-deployment profile.
  2. **Assisted path** — clearly labeled for everything else.

No eligibility logic changes. No refusal-message changes. No connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, or support-routing rule changes. **All existing rules remain unchanged.**

## 5. What is explicitly NOT changing

- Eligibility / refusal rules (Ines Q3 message-state guide, state #1 owner-permission/allowlist logic, state #2 connector auth, state #3 entitlement, state #4 qualifying-human-admin, state #5 active CS adoption/renewal).
- Connector access and external-system authority.
- Lifecycle / nurture messaging, including the routine CS auto-nudge pathway Ines has authority over.
- Instrumentation schema, event names, funnel definitions.
- Support routing and the 5-state dispute/correction channel (which still routes to Riley).

## 6. Primary metric

**≥25% relative reduction** in *Helio Start eligibility-flow starts that later route out for an existing unsupported condition*, treatment vs. control.

Defined as: starts of the Helio Start eligibility flow from pricing-page sessions, where the session ends in an existing-condition route-out (per the current refusal-message taxonomy). Denominator = Helio Start eligibility-flow starts, not pricing-page sessions, so the metric is robust to overall traffic mix.

## 7. Guardrails

1. **Eligible-workspace admission completion** — absolute change, treatment vs. control: **no more than a 1.5 percentage-point decline** over the full window. Read against the same-week control baseline; compared against pre-test 4-week baseline for context.
2. **Account-level support time at p90** — **no more than a 10-minute increase** vs. control p90 over the full window.

Either guardrail breach = stop and investigate; no auto-roll-forward.

# Quarterly board operating evidence intake — Q1 2026

Working pre-read for the January 6, 2026 prep review (1:00–2:00pm Central).
Attendees: Riley Tanaka, Priya (lead), Owen, Ines, Daniela.

## Ownership (locked, applies to all sections below)

- Riley Tanaka — recurring operating-evidence ownership begins January 1, 2026.
- Marcus Vail — retains forecast ownership. None of the four sections below feed his forecast.
- Tomás Vega — retains the final board narrative. Final claim owner on each section below.

## How to use this pre-read

Per the 12/10/25 deck rule, Helio Start, retained-mid Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and system controls stay SEPARATE — do not combine, do not cross-reference fields between sections.

The 11-field intake order, applied in this exact sequence within each section:

  1. Evidence lane
  2. Proposed claim
  3. Denominator
  4. Cohort or coverage dates
  5. Predeclared outcome window and completion status
  6. Measurement limits
  7. Exclusions
  8. Source owner
  9. Source or release-reliability evidence
 10. Revenue and forecast treatment
 11. Final claim owner

---

## 1. Helio Start

1. **Evidence lane:** Organic activation signals within Helio Start's bounded window.
2. **Proposed claim:** Helio Start delivers organic activation uplift within its declared bounded scope.
3. **Denominator:** Organic-start signups in the coverage window (paid acquisition explicitly out of denominator).
4. **Cohort or coverage dates:** [TBD at Jan 6 review — bounded organic window runs through 2026-03-31.]
5. **Predeclared outcome window and completion status:** [TBD at Jan 6 review — window not yet elapsed; completion status to be set at review.]
6. **Measurement limits:** Bounded organic scope only. No paid-acq interpretation. No pipeline reading.
7. **Exclusions:** Paid acquisition, pipeline metrics, forecast inputs, any non-organic attribution.
8. **Source owner:** [Product/release lead — Daniela or designee, to be confirmed at Jan 6 review.]
9. **Source or release-reliability evidence:** Bounded organic scope confirmed through 2026-03-31; no paid-acq path open.
10. **Revenue and forecast treatment:** Does NOT feed Marcus Vail's forecast. Excluded from revenue modeling.
11. **Final claim owner:** Tomás Vega.

---

## 2. Expansion Assist (retained-mid)

1. **Evidence lane:** Descriptive evidence for retained-mid Expansion Assist across the two bounded first pilots. Routine vs. disputed/cross-surface/exec split is preserved. Evidence is descriptive and noncausal — it reports what customers "selected," "showed," and "were observed" doing inside the bounded pilots. No randomized control. No implied counterfactual.

2. **Proposed claim:** Expansion Assist operates descriptively on routine cases; disputed, cross-surface, and exec cases retain line-level treatment. The lane is descriptive-only across both pilots — it does not claim to have driven, caused, or prevented retention, expansion, or revenue, and it is NOT a revenue, pipeline, forecast, or paid-acquisition input.

3. **Denominator (per cohort AND combined — kept separate):**
   - **Bounded first pilot (cohort 1) denominator:** 30 actual exposures. Entry condition used in cohort 1: older ceiling event allowed (no 14-day recency rule). 18 of the 30 cohort-1 exposures had an older ceiling event at entry.
   - **Bounded second pilot (cohort 2) denominator:** 13 actual exposures. Entry condition used in cohort 2: 14-day "ceiling newly crossed" recency rule applied.
   - **Combined two-pilot denominator:** 43 actual exposures across both bounded first pilots' closed, complete 45-day windows.
   - **Keep these three denominators separate in any read-out.** The aggregate 43 mixes two distinct entry conditions; that mix is recorded, not normalized away.

4. **Cohort or coverage dates:** [TBD at Jan 6 review — bounded pilots' 45-day windows are closed and complete at the time of certification (2025-12-01), with no partial-window extrapolation.]

5. **Predeclared outcome window and completion status:** Closed, complete 45-day windows per bounded pilot. The 45-day window is the observation unit; the bounded pilot is the boundedness unit. Help-or-options requests and expansions are counted inside the closed 45-day windows, as defined, with no partial-window extrapolation. No late-admitted or post-window exposure enters the read.

6. **Measurement limits (methodology difference made visible):**
   - **First-pilot methodology:** descriptive selection-and-observation framing only. Help-or-options = in-product engagement, NOT purchase intent. Expansions = bookings in-window, NOT incremental ARR vs. a counterfactual.
   - **Methodology difference vs. Helio Start:** the Helio Start methodology (mature status + refund-adjusted cash + account-level support effort read as three, against a day-90 mature cohort) is NOT transferred onto Expansion Assist. Expansion Assist is not a day-90 mature-cohort read; there is no refund-adjusted cash number paired against a support-effort tail in this lane.
   - **Population-mix caveat (carried plainly):** the 14-day recency-of-ceiling rule applied to cohort 2 only. The 43/13/9 figure mixes the two entry conditions; that mix is recorded, not normalized away.
   - **Small sample, descriptive only:** no significance, no effect size, no generalization beyond the two bounded first pilots.
   - **Routine vs. disputed/cross-surface/exec split:** descriptive scope on routine cases; line-level treatment limited to disputed, cross-surface, and exec cases. Routine customer-success line-edits stay descriptive.

7. **Exclusions:**
   - **Causal language** ("drove," "caused," "prevented") — evidence is descriptive only.
   - **Revenue implication, acquisition implication, pipeline implication, forecast / forward statement, eligibility implication** — none of these are claimed for the Expansion Assist lane.
   - **Generalization beyond the two bounded first pilots** — 43/13/9 is bounded to those two pilots.
   - **Claim that the 14-day ceiling-recency rule applied across both cohorts** — it applied to cohort 2 only.
   - **Treating help-or-options as purchase intent or expansions as incremental ARR vs. a counterfactual.**
   - **Transfer of the Helio Start methodology onto Expansion Assist** — methodology stays distinct.
   - **Combined-growth-number claim across the four lanes** — deck rule 12/10/25; this lane does not roll into Helio Start, pricing-page path quality, or system controls.
   - **Eng release/rollback authority** — unchanged and not in scope here (Daniela retains eng release/rollback control).

8. **Source owner:** Owen (extract owner) and Ines (CS adoption/renewal suppression confirmation). CS messaging-state owner per the Ines Q3 message-state guide (5 states: ext-sys authority / connector auth / entitlement / qualifying-human-admin / active CS adoption & renewal), OK'd 2025-07-25. Product-side / eng-side owners out of scope for this section (eng release/rollback authority unchanged).

9. **Source or release-reliability evidence:** Expansion Assist governance memo; 2025-12-01 certified extract (Owen + Ines, board-pre-read extract); two bounded first pilots' closed complete 45-day windows; routine-vs-disputed split record. The 45-day windows are closed and complete at the time of certification; help-or-options and expansions are counted inside those windows as defined, with no partial-window extrapolation.

10. **Revenue and forecast treatment:** Descriptive only — no revenue impact attributed; no pipeline number carried; no forecast credit. Expansion Assist remains outside pipeline, revenue commitments, and forecast credit. Does NOT feed Marcus Vail's forecast. Excluded from revenue modeling.

11. **Final claim owner:** Tomás Vega.

### Standing operating limits established by the historical decision (carried into this pre-read)

These limits are the standing operating limits on the Expansion Assist lane, established by the prior decision and preserved verbatim here. They are not renegotiated by this pre-read.

- **Lane posture:** narrow, behavior-based, state-specific. Active Customer Success adoption or renewal work suppresses a commercial prompt — that suppression behavior is part of the lane's design and is not optional.
- **Descriptive and noncausal:** evidence is descriptive only. No randomized control. No implied counterfactual. No causal claim that Expansion Assist drove, caused, or prevented retention, expansion, or revenue.
- **Outside pipeline, revenue commitments, and forecast credit:** Expansion Assist does not carry a pipeline number, does not carry a revenue commitment, and does not carry forecast credit. Marcus Vail's forecast is unchanged.
- **No Helio Start methodology transfer:** the mature status + refund-adjusted cash + account-level support-effort three-part read (Helio Start's day-90 mature-cohort methodology) is not applied to Expansion Assist. The two pilots are not day-90 mature-cohort reads; there is no refund-adjusted cash number paired against a support-effort tail in this lane.
- **Bounded pilot as boundedness unit:** the bounded pilot is the boundedness unit, not a launch frame. Two bounded first pilots only; no expansion of the boundedness beyond those two.
- **Eng release/rollback authority unchanged:** Daniela retains eng release/rollback control on this surface and others. Engineering authority is not absorbed by the Expansion Assist lane or by this pre-read.
- **Routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews are NOT in scope here:** those run through Ines's separate auto-nudge process and are excluded from Expansion Assist, Helio Start reporting, and lifecycle preflight (deck rule 12/10/25).
- **Cross-section blocklist (binding):** no combined growth number across the four lanes; no revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast implication from this lane; no transfer of the Helio Start methodology onto Expansion Assist; no causal language; no generalization of 43/13/9 beyond the two bounded first pilots; no normalization away of the population-mix caveat (14-day recency in cohort 2 only; 18 of 30 cohort-1 exposures with older ceiling events).

---

## 3. Pricing-page path quality

1. **Evidence lane:** Organic path-separation on the pricing page, post control retirement.
2. **Proposed claim:** Pricing-page delivers 100% organic path-separation; control retired; no taxonomy change.
3. **Denominator:** Pricing-page sessions in the coverage window.
4. **Cohort or coverage dates:** [TBD at Jan 6 review — coverage begins after 2025-11-26 control retirement.]
5. **Predeclared outcome window and completion status:** [TBD at Jan 6 review.]
6. **Measurement limits:** Organic path-separation only. Control is retired (Daniela). No taxonomy changes in scope.
7. **Exclusions:** Control-period data (retired, not applicable). Non-pricing-page sessions. Any taxonomy-change claims.
8. **Source owner:** Daniela (control owner — retired).
9. **Source or release-reliability evidence:** 2025-11-26 control retirement record; 100% organic path-separation observed.
10. **Revenue and forecast treatment:** Path quality is descriptive; no direct revenue attribution; excluded from forecast.
11. **Final claim owner:** Tomás Vega.

---

## 4. System controls

1. **Evidence lane:** System-level controls governing the surfaces above — CS messaging-state authority, retired pricing-page control, release/rollback controls.
2. **Proposed claim:** System controls remain governed per established rules; no combined or co-mingled claims between surfaces.
3. **Denominator:** Control population in the coverage window (per control, not aggregated).
4. **Cohort or coverage dates:** [TBD at Jan 6 review — per control.]
5. **Predeclared outcome window and completion status:** [TBD at Jan 6 review — per control.]
6. **Measurement limits:** Control-level evidence only. Do not combine with surface-level outcomes; do not aggregate across controls.
7. **Exclusions:** Combined or co-mingled claims across surfaces (deck rule 12/10/25). Cross-surface mixing. Routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews are NOT in scope here — that runs through Ines's separate auto-nudge process and is excluded from Expansion Assist, Helio Start reporting, and lifecycle preflight.
8. **Source owner:** Per control — Ines (CS messaging-state, 5-state guide OK'd 2025-07-25); Daniela (pricing-page retired control, eng release/rollback).
9. **Source or release-reliability evidence:** Ines Q3 message-state guide (5 states: ext-sys authority / connector auth / entitlement / qualifying-human-admin / active CS adoption & renewal). Pricing-page control retirement record 2025-11-26.
10. **Revenue and forecast treatment:** System controls do not directly drive revenue; descriptive only; excluded from forecast.
11. **Final claim owner:** Tomás Vega.

---

## Open items for the Jan 6 review

- [ ] Confirm cohort/coverage dates per section.
- [ ] Confirm predeclared outcome windows and completion status per section.
- [ ] Confirm source owner assignments (especially Helio Start product/release lead).
- [ ] Confirm no section accidentally feeds Marcus Vail's forecast (none should).
- [ ] Confirm Tomás Vega's final-claim-owner status for each section before board narrative is drafted.
- [ ] Expansion Assist (retained-mid): confirm the three-denominator split (cohort 1 = 30, cohort 2 = 13, combined = 43) is read as three numbers, not collapsed; confirm the 14-day recency-of-ceiling rule is read as cohort-2-only; confirm the standing operating limits block above is the carried-forward baseline, not a renegotiation.

# 2028 self-serve operating model — annual review agenda

Prepared: 2028-01-01 | Author: Riley Tanaka | Frame: operating-review kickoff (not an org change, not a reporting-line change)

## Sum-first

Annual review of the self-serve operating model. Same accountability frame as the approved 2027 model, same measurement balance. Goal: read whether the model is working across the five surfaces and the full year, and reset the closed escalation set and quarterly recheck cadence for 2028. No structural changes on the table; no reporting-line moves; no new metrics. This is the operating review.

## Why this review, this year

- The 2027 model has now run a full year under the approved delegation (Owen = source closure, Ines = lifecycle governance, Daniela = engineering release/rollback, Riley = retained decision rights and quarterly recheck).
- The first semi-annual recheck-vs-closure check (end of Q2 FY27) has been logged; the year-end recheck closes the second half.
- The lifecycle-function cadence has now produced a full annual cycle of monthly closures under the §2a business-day deadlines.

## Cuts (the agenda — one page)

1. **Year-end read on the self-serve model.** Did the five-surface judgment boundary hold under a full annual cycle? Where did the model bend (any escalation into Riley's queue, and from which trigger)? Did the four preserved-cadence properties stay intact? Did the closed escalation set trigger, and how was each closed?

2. **2027 quarterly recheck roll-up.** Walk the four quarterly recheck notes filed in the Lifecycle Systems folder. Any findings, any safeguard hold violations, any drift toward a second approval queue? Quarter-by-quarter lane selection: did rotation hold? Any same-lane repetition (which requires a written reason)?

3. **Closed escalation set review.** Six triggers retained from the approved record: missing fields, disputed semantics, cross-surface discrepancies, customer corrections, incident stops, causal/revenue/forecast/board-readiness/exec-language decisions. Trigger count by category for the year. Confirm the set is still the right set going into 2028; no additions, no removals.

4. **Measurement balance — the standing Growth/CS readout.** Confirm the readout stays lightweight. The three-signal read: self-serve operating model (Riley's accountability read), source-completeness and exception reporting (Owen), lifecycle governance and message-state controls (Ines). Support-load signal stays beside activation reporting; it does not roll in.

5. **Five retained decision-rights domains — confirmation.** Causal, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, final-claim. Confirm no narrowing during 2027 and that each domain's authority line held where claims were routed.

6. **Owner-lane health.** Owen, Ines, Daniela — any key-person or transition risk entering 2028? The R7 rule (vacancy/transition: default to *no delegation* until the role is filled) is in place; we confirm whether any lane needs it.

7. **2028 cadence refresh.** Confirm §2a business-day deadlines carry into 2028 unchanged. Quarterly recheck cadence continues. Semi-annual recheck-vs-closure check at end of Q2 FY28 and at the year-end re-decision point.

8. **Re-decision posture.** End of Q2 FY28 is the standing re-decision point per the approved record. The year-end review does not pre-empt it; it sets up the inputs (recheck notes, escalation volume, owner-lane health) the Q2 FY28 re-decision will read against.

## Scope guardrails (re-stated for the kickoff)

- **No org change.** The 2027 approved model is the model under review. No new lanes, no reporting-line moves, no team restructures on the table.
- **No new metrics.** The standing Growth/CS readout's three-signal frame is the frame. Expansion Assist stays descriptive, not forecast. Helio Start five-state model and the intake-rule-additive / refusal-non-softening rule are unchanged.
- **No narrowing of retained decision rights.** Causal, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, final-claim — all five retained.
- **The shared-state contract remains not-live-in-production.** Any production rollout of a shared-state implementation is a separate go decision (Ines on governance, Daniela's org on reliability). This review does not take that decision.

## Decisions on the table at the review

- Confirm 2027 escalation volume and trigger distribution; confirm the set is closed.
- Confirm 2027 quarterly recheck notes are filed and the four safeguards held each quarter.
- Confirm 2028 cadence carries forward under the same business-day deadlines.
- Confirm the Q2 FY28 re-decision point stands.

## Call to action

Read-ahead: the four 2027 quarterly recheck notes (Lifecycle Systems folder) and the year-end closure-and-exception summary. No pre-work on the agenda items above — they walk from the standing readout.

Format: 60 minutes, walk-the-record. Decision outputs are confirmations, not amendments.
