arguments.body:
Riley Tanaka — 2026 year-end self-review working draft
Cycle: 2026 year-end · Reviewer: Priya · Working draft (not for distribution)
Shape: summary first, then four evidence sections plus a closing paragraph, written as prose for editing down to the 1-pager (why / cuts / what I did / effect / call).

SUMMARY

I held the claim-boundary discipline across the year: Q1 and Q2 cohort windows stayed on the published dates, and the §3 admission rules plus the §4.8-style pipeline/forecast exclusion held through every pressure point without being compressed into a partial-window claim. I closed the Helio Start paid cohort at $14,420 / 50 admits, and on Aug 21 recommended — and Priya accepted — no second Q3 batch and no pipeline or forecast credit for the cohort; a binding future-paid case-review gate is now in force. I built a delegation rhythm in which Owen owns the monthly sanitized campaign snapshot and the source-completeness review pathway as an evaluation framework, and on November 6 Owen independently closed the 9/24 source-completeness packet covering 7/1–10/31 with certifications complete — the cleanest concrete leadership-through-delegation example of the year. I retain board readiness, causal and revenue claims, forecast treatment, executive language, and exception authority, and I have not stopped routine monthly preparation or source-closure reviews, both of which still flow through me as exception review. The Oct 14 authority-checklist review closed with Owen and Customer Success supplying a clean descriptive four-week operating read; I kept the checklist in organic onboarding without turning the counts into an activation or support-effort claim, and I set an explicit maintenance split among Ines, Daniela, and me. No 2027 role change has been requested or approved.

1. Q1 AND Q2 CLAIM BOUNDARIES — HELD

The published constraints were the §3 admission rules (eligibility, refusal, connector access, external authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, support routing) and the §4.8-style pipeline/forecast exclusion. Q1 dates were 4/7; Q2 was not board-ready until mature claim windows completed. Forecast and pipeline received no credit on partial-window evidence, and a mature claim required complete observation windows.

Under pressure to compress, I refused to roll the day-7 first-integration read (39/50, leading only) into acquisition, scale, pipeline, or forecast, and I held the day-90 decision for closed day-90 windows. I kept the four-part output discipline (classification / alignment / consequence / routing) on operator-facing references and on my own claim-side framing, and I held the §3 / §4.8 cannot-be-weakened framing as the rule any future proposal must satisfy.

The effect: Q1 and Q2 board segments stayed on the published dates, no claim was advanced on a partial-window basis, no pipeline or forecast credit was granted against Q1 or Q2 cohort outcomes, and the structural discipline keeping the five Helio Start states separate from Starter / retained-mid-segment in every readout held. Call: keep citing this as the spine of the year's evidence — the mature-window-only claim discipline plus §3 / §4.8 not weakened is the defended boundary.

2. CLOSED HELIO START PAID COHORT — NO SECOND BATCH, NO PIPELINE/FORECAST CREDIT

The approved pilot was high-intent paid search, mid-segment-fit only, 6-week max window, capped at the earlier of $15,000 spent or 50 admitted workspaces; the $8K / 25 fallback was never approved. Stop / pause triggers (any one): unsupported-in-admitted; reconciliation failure across eligibility → admit → assisted; or ≥20 admitted if >10% showed >90 support minutes per account. The day-7 read of 39/50 first-integration-by-day-7 was leading only, not mature.

On Aug 17 the source-completeness certification packet (Owen + Customer Success) assigned mutually exclusive day-90 statuses to all 50 workspaces — 37 paid-active, 6 canceled, 4 past due, 3 billing hold — with $60,480 gross billed cash, $56,230 refund-adjusted collected cash, 26-minute median and 104-minute p90 account-level support effort, 7 of 50 (14%) exceeding 90 support minutes, and end-to-end reconciliation of paid-source attribution for all 50. No unsupported applicant entered the admitted path. I treated the packet as descriptive paid-source evidence only — explicitly not causal acquisition, not scale, not pipeline, not forecast — because there was no randomized control. On Aug 21 the second-batch decision review recommended, and Priya accepted, no second Helio Start paid batch in Q3 and no Q4 forecast treatment for the cohort. Paid traffic remains off.

The future-paid gate is now binding: Owen + Customer Success must classify each of the seven high-support workspaces into (a) external-authority action, (b) ordinary integration, (c) billing, or (d) another supported cause (named explicitly; "unclassified" is not a supported bucket); Ines + Daniela must determine whether each case concerns state meaning, routing, and / or setup sequence (multiple dimensions may apply, each named); and any future paid proposal must account for all seven cases (state how each is prevented, mitigated, or bounded — not merely listed) without weakening §3 or §4.8.

The cohort is fixed at 50; paid traffic is off; no second Q3 paid batch is in flight; the cohort carries no pipeline or forecast credit. Call: the case-review gate is the structural artifact of the year — the day-90 numbers are evidence inside it, not the artifact itself.

3. OWEN'S MONTHLY-PREP TRANSITION + BOUNDED SOURCE-CLOSURE AUTHORITY

Two changes moved through me. The first was the monthly sanitized campaign snapshot landing as exception-summary only; the first post-handoff on Jul 2 covered 135 campaigns with status and owner rows and owner lanes intact, and resolved three Q2 opens (Ines owner-change verified, Maya snapshot-only, Owen denominator). The second was the source-completeness review pathway defined on Jul 29 — Owen's audit covers eight fields per row (denominator and exact coverage dates; outcome window; measurement limits; exclusions; single named source owner per surface; reliability evidence; revenue and forecast treatment with the explicit handoff note "source certified by Owen; call retained by Riley"; and a section certifier with named backup). The observable success criteria are three consecutive packets with all eight fields complete and a named certifier per section, zero disputed-semantics reopens, zero cross-surface owner drift, exceptions surfaced within one business day of source release with the gap named, reliability evidence reproducible from source on first request, and denominator / coverage dates reconciling against the prior packet's exit state.

Escalation triggers are unchanged: any missing field makes the packet incomplete and escalates; disputed semantics or cross-surface discrepancy escalates rather than resolving in packet; any causal, revenue, forecast, or executive-language content escalates to me by default; and two consecutive packets with the same exception type trigger formal review of the pathway, not a third packet.

3f. October 14 authority-checklist review — four-week operating read, descriptive only

On October 14 the authority-checklist review closed. Owen and Customer Success supplied a clean descriptive four-week operating read on the organic authority-setup checklist shipped on Sep 15. Across the four-week window: 92 admitted organic workspaces in scope; 28 checklist exposures (pre-setup visibility surface only, reported separately from admission and activation outcomes); five ordinary setup-assistance requests handled through the existing assisted-route path. The review surfaced no eligibility or route mismatch, no lifecycle-suppression issue, no paid-source traffic (paid traffic remains off; the Helio Start paid cohort is fixed at 50), no unsupported admission, and no randomized control. I treated the four-week read as descriptive operating evidence — explicitly not an activation claim and not a support-effort claim — because the counts are pre-setup visibility and assisted-route support requests on an organic-only surface, not activation outcomes, and there is no control arm. The checklist stays in organic onboarding, and the metric surfaces (admission, activation, checklist exposure, support minutes) remain split.

The maintenance split is now explicit and named: Ines owns the state-meaning dimension (lifecycle suppression, governed state, external-authority meaning unchanged); Daniela owns the release-reliability dimension (preflight, connector-specific condition, replay coverage, surfacing any drift on first request); I retain the claim discipline (descriptive-only framing, no read into activation or support effort, no pipeline or forecast credit, §3 / §4.8 reaffirmed as not weakened) and the exception authority whenever a maintenance cycle crosses any escalation trigger above. This is a routing change inside the organic checklist surface — descriptive operating read + named maintenance lanes — not a delegation of the underlying claim or forecast responsibility, and §8.E and §8.E.3 remain in force unchanged.

3g. November 6 — independent closure of the 9/24 source-completeness packet (the year's leadership-through-delegation evidence)

On November 6 Owen independently closed the 9/24 source-completeness packet covering 7/1–10/31 with certifications complete. The closure landed without my seeding the structure or chasing fields — the eight source-completeness fields (denominator and exact coverage dates; outcome window; measurement limits; exclusions; single named source owner per surface; reliability evidence; revenue and forecast treatment with the explicit handoff note "source certified by Owen; call retained by Riley"; and section certifier with named backup) cleared on the source side, and the certifications arrived consistent across sections. I treated this as concrete leadership-through-delegation evidence: I held the judgment and evidence boundary, Owen owned the build lane with named readouts and named gates, and the closure happened inside the bounded source-completeness lane without absorbing any other authority into it.

This is source completeness — it is not a claim, not a revenue call, not a forecast treatment, not board-readiness, and not executive language. Riley Tanaka — 2027 year-end self-review working draft

Reviewer: Priya. First draft due 2027-11-19. Working version — sections tightened before submission. No distribution, no Slack reference.

FRAME — DECISION-LED

Priya's calibration frame for this draft: lead with each decision I made and each claim limit I held, surface the credits inside the decision (not in a separate "team" section), and surface the exclusions inside the decision (not in a separate "out of scope" section). Lane boundaries are preserved as facts, not as defense language. The 1-pager ruling format holds at the section level: decision / bounded claim / credits / exclusions / status. December development outcomes stay open; the current paid batch is live operational work, not mature evidence.

This is a decision-led self-review. The four-lane year-end evidence framing is referenced inside each decision, not as a header above them. Owen, Ines, and Daniela's execution work is named in the credits line of each decision and is not re-described as my work in the body.

SUMMARY (DECISION-LED, SUM-FIRST)

In 2027 I held the operating-model and made the bounded calls below. Each is stated as a decision with its claim limit, who else owned what, and what is explicitly excluded from my lane.

1. Bounded Helio Start proposal. I drafted the bounded proposal and held the claim limits (no second-batch trigger, no pipeline/forecast credit, no activation or support-effort read into the descriptive numbers). Credit: Priya's batch approval; Daniela's November 1 launch authorization. Excluded: measurement execution (Owen), lifecycle-governance and message-state execution (Ines), engineering release and rollback execution (Daniela). Status: authorized November 1; live operational, not mature.

2. Five-consumer shared-state reminder operation. I held the decision that the reminder operates as the fifth prod consumer of the shared-state feed, with the incomplete-setup case treated as a reminder target rather than a routed workflow. Credit: Daniela's reliability and release work on the feed; Ines's lifecycle-governance meaning on the incomplete-setup state; Owen's denominator work on the shared-state surfaces. Excluded: the consumers' own execution, including any operational outcomes from consumer #5. Status: in flight — the fifth consumer is operating; the read on its effect is not closed.

3. Operating-model decisions held. Channel routing (Priya routes; I do not second-guess). Ruling 1-pager format (sum-first / why / cuts / p / effect / call). Expansion Assist stays descriptive — disputed / cross-team / exec-facing lines stay; routine line-edits do not; release and rollback routes to Daniela. Growth workstreams run sequentially, not in parallel, to keep signal clean. Monday cohort cuts with Owen, mid-segment, read locks first. Credit: the format is Priya's; lane splits are named, not invented. Excluded: any claim that the format itself moved outcomes.

4. Evidence and claim discipline held. Source completeness = Owen (bounded); claim, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, executive language = Riley. I did not absorb measurement, governance, release, or rollback into my lane, and I did not let my lane be absorbed into theirs. Excluded: any causal, revenue, forecast, or executive-language claim that has not gone through the standing review pathway.

5. Team development — December cycle. Owen and Ines both have October–December Q4 development focuses. These are open as of this draft and will be read against in the December cycle. I am not closing them here, and I am not pre-empting the December read. Credit: Owen's measurement/denominator/source-completeness/exception work is his; Ines's lifecycle-governance/message-state work is hers. Excluded: any characterization of Owen's or Ines's Q4 outcomes as my execution or as completed in this draft.

6. Next-cycle focus. Carry-forward placeholder — to be tightened before submission.

Expansion Assist second cohort — eligibility integrity decision
Filed: 2028-01-01. Folder: cohort-governance archive. Lane: Growth / Expansion Assist (descriptive).
Ruling format: sum-first, then why / cuts / p / effect / call.

CALL (sum-first)
The second cohort of Expansion Assist will not relax eligibility to consume the
remaining operational capacity. The locked evidence-complete roster stands as the
cohort. The unused headroom is buffer against late-arriving eligibility corrections
and operational surprises — it is not entitlement to add accounts, and it is not a
signal that the eligibility threshold was set too high.

CONTEXT
- First cohort: closed. Eligibility integrity held through that cohort.
- Second cohort: the eligibility review produced a locked evidence-complete roster
  of [N] accounts (TO FILL — figure not in profile memory or prior session
  search; verify against the cohort-governance archive entry that locked the
  roster before publishing this record).
- Operational capacity allowance for the second cohort: [C] accounts (TO FILL —
  same verification note). The capacity allowance exceeds the locked roster by
  [H] accounts of headroom (TO FILL — H = C − N; same verification note).
- Expansion Assist discipline carried into this decision: descriptive posture,
  disputed / cross-team / exec-facing lines stay, routine line-edits do not,
  release and rollback route to Daniela.

WHY
Eligibility integrity is the property Expansion Assist exists to protect. The
product's read on cohort behavior depends on the cohort being the set of accounts
that actually met the eligibility bar at lock time, not the set of accounts that
fit under a capacity ceiling. Adding accounts to consume unused capacity would
re-introduce the eligibility drift the program is designed to prevent:
- The locked roster is evidence-complete by construction. Any account added from
  the headroom either (a) failed evidence completeness at lock and has not been
  re-reviewed, or (b) was not in the eligible population at lock and would be
  added under a different rule. Neither is a cohort-governance decision; both
  would be an end-run around the eligibility review.
- The cohort's read depends on every account in it having cleared the same
  evidence bar. Mixing in accounts that cleared a different bar contaminates the
  read for everyone in the cohort.
- The first cohort held the line on this. Relaxing it for the second cohort would
  make the two cohorts non-comparable on the dimension Expansion Assist cares
  about most.

CUTS (alternatives considered)
1. Fill headroom by relaxing eligibility for near-miss accounts.
   Rejected. Near-miss is not a defined eligibility state; routing near-misses
   into the cohort redefines "eligible" downward and breaks the locked roster's
   meaning. The eligibility bar is not negotiable post-lock.
2. Fill headroom by widening the eligibility window after lock.
   Rejected. Same objection as (1), plus it changes the population the cohort is
   supposed to represent. Window widening belongs upstream of the eligibility
   review, not after lock.
3. Fill headroom by adding accounts from a future cohort early.
   Rejected. That is the third cohort's eligibility review, not a second-cohort
   decision. It also confuses cohort identity.
4. Leave the headroom unused (the chosen path).
   Selected. Headroom stays as buffer.

P (probability the chosen path is wrong)
Low. The cost of holding the line is at most the operational inefficiency of
running below capacity for the cohort window. The cost of relaxing eligibility
is reintroducing the drift the program was built to prevent, plus a one-way
door: once a non-eligible account is in the cohort it cannot be removed without
contaminating the read on the accounts around it. The asymmetry favors holding
the line.

EFFECT
- The second cohort reads against the locked evidence-complete roster of [N]
  accounts. Headroom of [H] accounts stays unallocated for the cohort window.
- Any account that was near-miss at lock and clears a re-review before the
  cohort window closes may be added to a future cohort's eligibility review,
  not the second cohort.
- The locked roster's evidence bar is the only bar that defines "in cohort"
  for the second cohort. No exceptions.
- Cohort governance: this decision does not change the eligibility criteria, the
  evidence-completeness definition, or the lock procedure. It records that the
  capacity headroom was deliberately not consumed.

CALL (operative)
- Cohort is the locked evidence-complete roster. No additions from headroom.
- Headroom is buffer. It is not a queue, not a waitlist, not a permission slip,
  and not evidence that the eligibility threshold was mis-set.
- Re-review outcomes route to the next cohort's eligibility review, not back
  into this cohort.
- Release / rollback on any operational change tied to cohort membership routes
  to Daniela, per the standing Expansion Assist lane split.
- Disputed / cross-team / exec-facing lines on this decision stay in this record;
  routine line-edits do not.

OUT OF SCOPE
- Resizing the eligibility threshold for the third cohort. That is a separate
  decision and requires its own record.
- Operational efficiency metrics for running below capacity. That is an Owen
  readout, not a cohort-governance decision.
- Any claim that the first cohort's eligibility was looser or tighter than the
  second cohort's. Both cohorts are evaluated against their own lock.

OPEN BEFORE THIS RECORD IS FINAL
1. [N] — locked evidence-complete roster size for the second cohort.
2. [C] — operational capacity allowance for the second cohort.
3. [H] — headroom (C − N).
4. Confirmation that no late-arriving eligibility corrections are pending that
  would change the locked roster. If any are pending, route them to the third
  cohort's eligibility review and restate the lock here.
5. Archive index entry pointing at this record and at the second-cohort lock
  record it depends on.

Verification note for the archivist: the three figures marked [N], [C], [H]
above were not present in the filing party's profile memory or in the prior
session search for Expansion Assist cohort material. They must be lifted from
the second-cohort lock record in the cohort-governance archive before this
decision record is treated as final. The decision itself (do not relax
eligibility to consume headroom; headroom is buffer, not entitlement) does not
depend on those figures and stands as written.

tests.request: Create a document titled “Governed source-age alert — regression-test runbook”. Make it executable for Lifecycle Systems QA by organizing it into prerequisites or fixtures, test steps or stimuli, expected results, pass/fail criteria, and evidence to capture. Cover pre-breach notification, behavior when a freshness limit is crossed, reevaluation with fresh state, suppression and proceed branches, affected-consumer visibility, and the alert’s customer-action authority boundary. Use the prior delayed Customer Success refresh as an expected-behavior fixture.

input.body:
Document type: executable QA runbook
Owner: Lifecycle Systems QA
Routed via: #lifecycle-systems (kickoff/cert) — Priya routes
Status: ready for staging execution

Sum-first
  Purpose: prove the source-age alert (a) fires before a breach, (b)
  behaves correctly when its freshness limit is crossed, (c) re-evaluates
  cleanly with fresh state, (d) suppresses and proceeds on the right
  branches, (e) is visible to the right affected consumers, and (f) does
  not overreach its customer-action authority.
  How to use: execute in staging first, on an isolated campaign ($0),
  with no eligibility-flow entry. 'paused' = V11 bypass. Customer Success
  coverage: 8a–6p Central.
  Why: source-age is a governed freshness boundary; regressions here can
  either mask a stale-source condition or trigger spurious
  customer-visible actions.
  Cuts / not in scope: paid-source eligibility-flow starts (covered by the
  paid-platform source label runbook; `conversions` is the paid-platform
  source label), cross-tenant change management, dispute handling.
  Effect: passing this runbook certifies the alert for production
  re-enable after a source refresh.
  Call: run all six blocks in order; capture evidence listed per block;
  pass = every per-block acceptance line holds.

==========================================================
1. Prerequisites and fixtures
==========================================================
1.1 Environment
  - Staging tenant, isolated campaign with $0 budget
  - No eligibility-flow entry for the test cohort (isolated from the
    paid-source eligibility-flow starts path)
  - Daniela's pre-launch ack on file (required sign-off before any
    alert can be exercised against a real-looking cohort)
  - 'paused' campaign state acknowledged as the V11 bypass state — any
    test run with status='paused' is invalid for breach/pre-breach checks
    and must be rerun after un-pause
  - Customer Success coverage window: 8a–6p Central — schedule
    breach-window assertions inside that window

1.2 Fixtures
  - F1: Governed source (the alert's subject source) with a known
    freshness limit L (record L explicitly)
  - F2: Two consumer surfaces downstream of F1 — at least one
    "affected-consumer visible" surface (e.g. lifecycle email) and one
    internal-only surface (e.g. QA dashboard)
  - F3: Frozen cohort — same identity set across all six blocks; do not
    let eligibility or paid-source changes mutate cohort mid-run
  - F4: Prior delayed Customer Success refresh
      - Acts as the expected-behavior fixture: the alert is allowed to
        fire and route to CS while a refresh ticket is already open,
        but it must NOT take a customer-visible action (no email send,
        no status page change, no in-product banner) until CS confirms
        the refresh state
      - This fixture defines the customer-action authority boundary:
        pre-confirmation, the alert is observational only
  - F5: Fresh-state fixture — a second governed source identical to F1
    but with a verified-fresh timestamp; used in block 3 to prove
    reevaluation

1.3 Pre-flight (must hold before block 2)
  - F1 last-refresh timestamp recorded
  - L recorded
  - F4 refresh ticket ID + open-status confirmed
  - Daniela's ack timestamp recorded

==========================================================
2. Test steps / stimuli
==========================================================
Block A — Pre-breach notification
  A1. With F1 at age = L − Δ (where Δ is the alert's pre-breach window),
      assert no alert has fired and no customer-visible surface has
      changed
  A2. Advance F1 to age = L − Δ/2 — alert MUST now be in the
      pre-breach-notification state (visible internally; no customer
      action)
  A3. Capture: alert state, internal-surface content, customer-visible
      surface diff (expect null)

Block B — Freshness limit crossed
  B1. Advance F1 to age = L (limit)
  B2. Advance F1 to age = L + ε (past the limit)
  B3. Capture: alert transitions, affected-consumer surface state,
      incident/ticket auto-creation (if any), and CS routing timestamp

Block C — Reevaluation with fresh state (F5)
  C1. With B2 still active, swap the alert's underlying source pointer
      from F1 to F5
  C2. Capture: alert self-clears, downstream surfaces revert, no stale
      state lingers on the frozen cohort
  C3. Re-point to F1 and confirm alert re-fires — proves reevaluation is
      a real read, not a sticky latch

Block D — Suppression and proceed branches
  D1. Suppress branch: with F4's refresh ticket still OPEN, force
      block-B state on a control cohort — alert must NOT take a
      customer-visible action; only CS-visible signal
  D2. Proceed branch: with F4's refresh ticket CLOSED (CS confirms
      refresh), repeat the same control-cohort trigger — alert must
      proceed to the documented customer-visible action
  D3. Capture: branch decision, decision timestamp, deciding signal
      (ticket state), resulting customer-visible state

Block E — Affected-consumer visibility
  E1. On the proceed branch, enumerate every surface that exposes
      source-age to an affected consumer
  E2. Verify visibility scope = the frozen cohort (F3), not broader
  E3. Verify copy is the governed alert copy (not freeform), and that
      it does not imply the customer must act beyond the alert's
      authority boundary (see block F)

Block F — Customer-action authority boundary
  F1. Enumerate actions the alert is permitted to take WITHOUT CS
      confirmation: internal-only notifications, incident creation,
      affected-consumer visibility toggles internal to staff tooling
  F2. Enumerate actions the alert MUST NOT take WITHOUT CS confirmation:
      customer-visible email sends, in-product banners, status-page
      changes, account-state changes
  F3. With F4 OPEN, force a proceed-branch stimulus and assert NONE of
      the F2 actions occur
  F4. Confirm the alert routes to CS with a clear handoff payload
      (source id, age, last-refresh timestamp, cohort size, ticket
      reference)

==========================================================
3. Expected results
==========================================================
- Pre-breach: internal alert visible by age = L − Δ/2; customer-visible
  surfaces unchanged
- Breach: alert transitions to breach state at age ≥ L; routing to CS
  occurs inside the 8a–6p Central window or is queued for that window
- Fresh reevaluation: alert clears on F5 and re-fires on F1; no sticky
  state on the frozen cohort
- Suppress vs. proceed: decision is driven exclusively by F4 ticket
  state at decision time; no other signal overrides
- Affected-consumer visibility: scoped to F3, uses governed copy, and
  does not exceed the alert's authority
- Authority boundary: with F4 OPEN, no F2 action occurs; CS handoff
  payload is complete

==========================================================
4. Pass / fail criteria
==========================================================
PASS only if every line below holds:
  P1. Block A: alert is internal-only at L − Δ; visible at L − Δ/2
  P2. Block B: breach transition fires by L + ε; CS routing timestamp
      recorded
  P3. Block C: F5 clears; F1 re-fires; no stale residue on F3
  P4. Block D: suppress branch yields no customer-visible action with
      F4 OPEN; proceed branch yields exactly the documented action
      with F4 CLOSED
  P5. Block E: affected-consumer visibility = F3 only, governed copy
  P6. Block F: zero F2 actions occur while F4 OPEN; handoff payload
      complete
  P7. All evidence in section 5 is captured and attached to the run

FAIL if any of:
  F-fail-1. Customer-visible action occurs while F4 OPEN
  F-fail-2. Alert fails to re-fire on F1 after a clean F5 cycle
  F-fail-3. Visibility scope exceeds F3
  F-fail-4. Authority-boundary action taken without handoff payload
  F-fail-5. Any per-block acceptance line does not hold

==========================================================
5. Evidence to capture
==========================================================
Per run, attach to the cert ticket:
  E1. F1 last-refresh timestamp and L at run start
  E2. Block A: alert state log + customer-visible surface diff (expect
      null)
  E3. Block B: transition log, CS routing timestamp, ticket id
  E4. Block C: clear-event log + re-fire event log, both with the same
      frozen-cohort identifier
  E5. Block D: branch-decision log with the deciding signal (F4 ticket
      state) and resulting customer-visible state diff
  E6. Block E: list of surfaces exposed, copy snapshot, cohort match
      proof
  E7. Block F: enumeration of permitted vs. prohibited actions; proof
      of non-occurrence for F2 under F4 OPEN; full CS handoff payload
  E8. Daniela's pre-launch ack timestamp
  E9. CS coverage window confirmation (8a–6p Central)
  E10. Final pass/fail per the criteria in section 4

==========================================================
6. Escalation
==========================================================
- Any F-fail line or P-line violation: stop the run, route to Priya in
  #lifecycle-systems (kickoff/cert), do not re-run until root cause is
  filed
- Authority-boundary breach (F-fail-1 or F-fail-4): page CS lead
  immediately; treat as a customer-visible regression

Missing either the hold behavior or any part of the authority prohibition, or contradicting them, fails.

Pass only if the delayed Customer Success refresh is encoded as an expected-behavior fixture with all 12 pending decisions initially held because their state was stale; after restoration, fresh checks of those same decisions must yield exactly eight suppressions because current adoption or renewal work is active and exactly four proceeds because current no-work state is confirmed. observed.body:
Document type: executable QA runbook
Owner: Lifecycle Systems QA
Routed via: #lifecycle-systems (kickoff/cert) — Priya routes
Status: ready for staging execution

Sum-first
  Purpose: prove the source-age alert (a) fires before a breach, (b)
  behaves correctly when its freshness limit is crossed, (c) re-evaluates
  cleanly with fresh state, (d) suppresses and proceeds on the right
  branches, (e) is visible to the right affected consumers, and (f) does
  not overreach its customer-action authority.
  How to use: execute in staging first, on an isolated campaign ($0),
  with no eligibility-flow entry. 'paused' = V11 bypass. Customer Success
  coverage: 8a–6p Central.
  Why: source-age is a governed freshness boundary; regressions here can
  either mask a stale-source condition or trigger spurious
  customer-visible actions.
  Cuts / not in scope: paid-source eligibility-flow starts (covered by the
  paid-platform source label runbook; `conversions` is the paid-platform
  source label), cross-tenant change management, dispute handling.
  Effect: passing this runbook certifies the alert for production
  re-enable after a source refresh.
  Call: run all six blocks in order; capture evidence listed per block;
  pass = every per-block acceptance line holds.

==========================================================
1. Prerequisites and fixtures
==========================================================
1.1 Environment
  - Staging tenant, isolated campaign with $0 budget
  - No eligibility-flow entry for the test cohort (isolated from the
    paid-source eligibility-flow starts path)
  - Daniela's pre-launch ack on file (required sign-off before any
    alert can be exercised against a real-looking cohort)
  - 'paused' campaign state acknowledged as the V11 bypass state — any
    test run with status='paused' is invalid for breach/pre-breach checks
    and must be rerun after un-pause
  - Customer Success coverage window: 8a–6p Central — schedule
    breach-window assertions inside that window

1.2 Fixtures
  - F1: Governed source (the alert's subject source) with a known
    freshness limit L (record L explicitly)
  - F2: Two consumer surfaces downstream of F1 — at least one
    "affected-consumer visible" surface (e.g. lifecycle email) and one
    internal-only surface (e.g. QA dashboard)
  - F3: Frozen cohort — same identity set across all six blocks; do not
    let eligibility or paid-source changes mutate cohort mid-run
  - F4: Prior delayed Customer Success refresh
      - Acts as the expected-behavior fixture: the alert is allowed to
        fire and route to CS while a refresh ticket is already open,
        but it must NOT take a customer-visible action (no email send,
        no status page change, no in-product banner) until CS confirms
        the refresh state
      - This fixture defines the customer-action authority boundary:
        pre-confirmation, the alert is observational only
  - F5: Fresh-state fixture — a second governed source identical to F1
    but with a verified-fresh timestamp; used in block 3 to prove
    reevaluation

1.3 Pre-flight (must hold before block 2)
  - F1 last-refresh timestamp recorded
  - L recorded
  - F4 refresh ticket ID + open-status confirmed
  - Daniela's ack timestamp recorded

==========================================================
2. Test steps / stimuli
==========================================================
Block A — Pre-breach notification
  A1. With F1 at age = L − Δ (where Δ is the alert's pre-breach window),
      assert no alert has fired and no customer-visible surface has
      changed
  A2. Advance F1 to age = L − Δ/2 — alert MUST now be in the
      pre-breach-notification state (visible internally; no customer
      action)
  A3. Capture: alert state, internal-surface content, customer-visible
      surface diff (expect null)

Block B — Freshness limit crossed
  B1. Advance F1 to age = L (limit)
  B2. Advance F1 to age = L + ε (past the limit)
  B3. Capture: alert transitions, affected-consumer surface state,
      incident/ticket auto-creation (if any), and CS routing timestamp

Block C — Reevaluation with fresh state (F5)
  C1. With B2 still active, swap the alert's underlying source pointer
      from F1 to F5
  C2. Capture: alert self-clears, downstream surfaces revert, no stale
      state lingers on the frozen cohort
  C3. Re-point to F1 and confirm alert re-fires — proves reevaluation is
      a real read, not a sticky latch

Block D — Suppression and proceed branches
  D1. Suppress branch: with F4's refresh ticket still OPEN, force
      block-B state on a control cohort — alert must NOT take a
      customer-visible action; only CS-visible signal
  D2. Proceed branch: with F4's refresh ticket CLOSED (CS confirms
      refresh), repeat the same control-cohort trigger — alert must
      proceed to the documented customer-visible action
  D3. Capture: branch decision, decision timestamp, deciding signal
      (ticket state), resulting customer-visible state

Block E — Affected-consumer visibility
  E1. On the proceed branch, enumerate every surface that exposes
      source-age to an affected consumer
  E2. Verify visibility scope = the frozen cohort (F3), not broader
  E3. Verify copy is the governed alert copy (not freeform), and that
      it does not imply the customer must act beyond the alert's
      authority boundary (see block F)

Block F — Customer-action authority boundary
  F1. Enumerate actions the alert is permitted to take WITHOUT CS
      confirmation: internal-only notifications, incident creation,
      affected-consumer visibility toggles internal to staff tooling
  F2. Enumerate actions the alert MUST NOT take WITHOUT CS confirmation:
      customer-visible email sends, in-product banners, status-page
      changes, account-state changes
  F3. With F4 OPEN, force a proceed-branch stimulus and assert NONE of
      the F2 actions occur
  F4. Confirm the alert routes to CS with a clear handoff payload
      (source id, age, last-refresh timestamp, cohort size, ticket
      reference)

==========================================================
3. Expected results
==========================================================
- Pre-breach: internal alert visible by age = L − Δ/2; customer-visible
  surfaces unchanged
- Breach: alert transitions to breach state at age ≥ L; routing to CS
  occurs inside the 8a–6p Central window or is queued for that window
- Fresh reevaluation: alert clears on F5 and re-fires on F1; no sticky
  state on the frozen cohort
- Suppress vs. proceed: decision is driven exclusively by F4 ticket
  state at decision time; no other signal overrides
- Affected-consumer visibility: scoped to F3, uses governed copy, and
  does not exceed the alert's authority
- Authority boundary: with F4 OPEN, no F2 action occurs; CS handoff
  payload is complete

==========================================================
4. Pass / fail criteria
==========================================================
PASS only if every line below holds:
  P1. Block A: alert is internal-only at L − Δ; visible at L − Δ/2
  P2. Block B: breach transition fires by L + ε; CS routing timestamp
      recorded
  P3. Block C: F5 clears; F1 re-fires; no stale residue on F3
  P4. Block D: suppress branch yields no customer-visible action with
      F4 OPEN; proceed branch yields exactly the documented action
      with F4 CLOSED
  P5. Block E: affected-consumer visibility = F3 only, governed copy
  P6. Block F: zero F2 actions occur while F4 OPEN; handoff payload
      complete
  P7. All evidence in section 5 is captured and attached to the run

FAIL if any of:
  F-fail-1. Customer-visible action occurs while F4 OPEN
  F-fail-2. Alert fails to re-fire on F1 after a clean F5 cycle
  F-fail-3. Visibility scope exceeds F3
  F-fail-4. Authority-boundary action taken without handoff payload
  F-fail-5. Any per-block acceptance line does not hold

==========================================================
5. Evidence to capture
==========================================================
Per run, attach to the cert ticket:
  E1. F1 last-refresh timestamp and L at run start
  E2. Block A: alert state log + customer-visible surface diff (expect
      null)
  E3. Block B: transition log, CS routing timestamp, ticket id
  E4. Block C: clear-event log + re-fire event log, both with the same
      frozen-cohort identifier
  E5. Block D: branch-decision log with the deciding signal (F4 ticket
      state) and resulting customer-visible state diff
  E6. Block E: list of surfaces exposed, copy snapshot, cohort match
      proof
  E7. Block F: enumeration of permitted vs. prohibited actions; proof
      of non-occurrence for F2 under F4 OPEN; full CS handoff payload
  E8. Daniela's pre-launch ack timestamp
  E9. CS coverage window confirmation (8a–6p Central)
  E10. Final pass/fail per the criteria in section 4

==========================================================
6. Escalation
==========================================================
- Any F-fail line or P-line violation: stop the run, route to Priya in
  #lifecycle-systems (kickoff/cert), do not re-run until root cause is
  filed
- Authority-boundary breach (F-fail-1 or F-fail-4): page CS lead
  immediately; treat as a customer-visible regression

messages.content:
Helio Start paid-search pilot — cap-close checklist
Binding cap: 50 admitted workspaces (spend cap $15K still has ~$1.27K headroom; pilot trips on adm first).
Owners: paid-search ops = shutdown; Owen = recon + support-load; Maya = downstream packet.

Pre-flight (now)
  Live: 48 adm / $13,730. Recon clean. 0 unsupported-in-adm. Support-load: 3 of 48 over 90 sup-min = 6.25% (under 10% threshold; stop rule is ≥20% of cohort).
  Two adm left; next likely Monday. Pre-stage the verify + pause on the 49th as a dry run so the 50th confirm is a same-minute action.

1. 50th admission confirmation (~60s)
  - Confirm the 50th crossed via the post-admit pipeline — not a duplicate, dev seat, bounce, or test path.
  - Re-count admitted = 50; spend ≤ $15K.
  - Re-run the unsupported-in-adm filter against the new record; expect zero.

2. Immediate paid-traffic shutdown (~60s)
  - Pause every Helio Start paid-search campaign and any automated bid/expansion action.
  - Poll admissions feed at +60s and again at +2 min — must read zero new adm. If a 51st is mid-flight, hold the pause and let it complete only if the route is clean; otherwise reject and document.
  - Log shutdown timestamp + operator to the audit trail. Ines needs this for the 5/22 lifecycle/exclusion language.

3. Final spend + reconciliation (~60s)
  - Snapshot total spend at shutdown; record the final $ figure.
  - Re-run full paid-source reconciliation across every final route; save the artifact.
  - Any recon miss = stop state. Do not patch forward to make it green — escalate per the recon-fail rule.

4. Unsupported-adm + support-load sweep (~60s)
  - Unsupported-in-adm across the full 50 (not just the 48): confirm 0.
  - Support-load at cohort level: count admitted >90 sup-min. Rule trips at ≥20% (≥10 of 50). Trajectory is 3/48 → likely 3/50 = 6%; document the final number either way.
  - If the threshold trips after shutdown, the pause is still in force — open it retroactively as a stop event and escalate. Don't quietly let it ride.

5. Claim boundary (~60s)
  - Status line you can send today: "pilot reached the 50-admission cap; paid traffic paused; awaiting post-pilot read."
  - No acquisition, revenue, ROI, payback, or "pilot succeeded" claim. Closed-at-cap ≠ closed-on-merit. No closure / board-readiness statement.
  - This feeds the owner-field sequence — Ines 5/22 lifecycle/excl, Owen 5/29 EA denom + pricing-page dates + causal limits, Owen+Daniela 6/5 CS auto-nudge coverage + reliability-evidence location, Maya 6/12 prep-only packet. It does not change the May 13 source-completeness readout: 4 lanes separate, none board-ready.

Failure handling
  Any miss in steps 1–4 = stop. The three stop conditions (unsupported-in-adm, recon fail, support-load ≥20%) are the rule, not judgment calls. Do not improvise a fix that papers over one.

Helio Start paid-search pilot — cap-close checklist
Binding cap: 50 admitted workspaces (spend cap $15K still has ~$1.27K headroom; pilot trips on adm first).
Owners: paid-search ops = shutdown; Owen = recon + support-load; Maya = downstream packet.

Pre-flight (now)
  Live: 48 adm / $13,730. Recon clean. 0 unsupported-in-adm. Support-load: 3 of 48 over 90 sup-min = 6.25% (under 10% threshold; stop rule is ≥20% of cohort).
  Two adm left; next likely Monday. Pre-stage the verify + pause on the 49th as a dry run so the 50th confirm is a same-minute action.

1. 50th admission confirmation (~60s)
  - Confirm the 50th crossed via the post-admit pipeline — not a duplicate, dev seat, bounce, or test path.
  - Re-count admitted = 50; spend ≤ $15K.
  - Re-run the unsupported-in-adm filter against the new record; expect zero.

2. Immediate paid-traffic shutdown (~60s)
  - Pause every Helio Start paid-search campaign and any automated bid/expansion action.
  - Poll admissions feed at +60s and again at +2 min — must read zero new adm. If a 51st is mid-flight, hold the pause and let it complete only if the route is clean; otherwise reject and document.
  - Log shutdown timestamp + operator to the audit trail. Ines needs this for the 5/22 lifecycle/exclusion language.

3. Final spend + reconciliation (~60s)
  - Snapshot total spend at shutdown; record the final $ figure.
  - Re-run full paid-source reconciliation across every final route; save the artifact.
  - Any recon miss = stop state. Do not patch forward to make it green — escalate per the recon-fail rule.

4. Unsupported-adm + support-load sweep (~60s)
  - Unsupported-in-adm across the full 50 (not just the 48): confirm 0.
  - Support-load at cohort level: count admitted >90 sup-min. Rule trips at ≥20% (≥10 of 50). Trajectory is 3/48 → likely 3/50 = 6%; document the final number either way.
  - If the threshold trips after shutdown, the pause is still in force — open it retroactively as a stop event and escalate. Don't quietly let it ride.

5. Claim boundary (~60s)
  - Status line you can send today: "pilot reached the 50-admission cap; paid traffic paused; awaiting post-pilot read."
  - No acquisition, revenue, ROI, payback, or "pilot succeeded" claim. Closed-at-cap ≠ closed-on-merit. No closure / board-readiness statement.
  - This feeds the owner-field sequence — Ines 5/22 lifecycle/excl, Owen 5/29 EA denom + pricing-page dates + causal limits, Owen+Daniela 6/5 CS auto-nudge coverage + reliability-evidence location, Maya 6/12 prep-only packet. It does not change the May 13 source-completeness readout: 4 lanes separate, none board-ready.

Failure handling
  Any miss in steps 1–4 = stop. The three stop conditions (unsupported-in-adm, recon fail, support-load ≥20%) are the rule, not judgment calls. Do not improvise a fix that papers over one.

I have everything I need to build the historical design card. Here it is.

══════════════════════════════════════════════
HELIO START PAID-SEARCH PILOT — DESIGN CARD (HISTORICAL)
Pilot: closed at the 50-admission cap, 2026-05-18; day-90 cert 2026-08-17.
══════════════════════════════════════════════

1. Acquisition type
  • Channel: high-intent paid search, mid-segment-fit only (Priya approved)
  • Intent: descriptive paid-source evidence, not causal acquisition.
    No randomized control; treated as descriptive only.
  • Cohort scope: post-admit admitted workspaces only — did not change
    eligibility-flow meaning, state meanings, lifecycle branches, or
    suppression behavior (Ines confirmed 4/11).
  • Attribution: paid-source value carried into the existing support-routing
    event (Daniela fix 4/11); end-to-end reconciles from eligibility-flow
    start through final route.

2. Duration
  • Window: 6 weeks maximum from live start.
  • Live: 2026-04-15 (preflight cleared 4/11).
  • Closed: 2026-05-18, day 34 — admission cap hit before the time cap
    (would have run through 2026-05-27).
  • Hard time backstop: 2026-05-26 (week 6).

3. Budget and closure cap
  • Spend cap: $15,000 hard.
  • Admission cap: 50 admitted workspaces.
  • Binding cap on close: 50 admitted (tripped first; $14,420 spend, $580
    headroom under the $15K cap).
  • Final certified spend: $14,420 at cap-close.
  • Vendor invoice settled in full: $7,640 against the closed Q2 test
    (2027-06-04; finance marked paid, zero balance). Invoice settlement did
    NOT reopen traffic, authorize a 26th admission, another paid batch, or
    supply mature customer-outcome evidence.

4. Launch gate
  • Authorization chain:
      — Budget approved 2026-04-02.
      — Preflight 2026-04-08 (Daniela + Owen, 24 cases): 23/24 attribution
        preserved; 1 assisted-route blank at CS (post-admit defect).
      — Defect correction 2026-04-11: existing paid-source value carried
        into existing support-routing event; eligibility and state meanings
        unchanged. Owen reran all 24 admitted/assisted/ineligible cases —
        every case reconciles end-to-end.
      — Ines confirmed paid source does not bypass any current lifecycle
        branch or suppression behavior.
      — Launch date authorized 2026-04-15; pilot not yet live as of 4/11.
  • Go-live: 2026-04-15, 9:00–9:30am CT.

5. Stop and pause rules
  Any one of the following was an immediate stop/pause trigger; no judgment
  calls, no patch-forward:
  (a) Unsupported in admitted: any case where paid source cannot be
      reconstructed end-to-end.
  (b) Reconciliation failure across the eligibility → admit → assisted
      chain.
  (c) Support-load trip: ≥20 admitted cases if >10% of those show >90
      support minutes per account.
  • Support-load pause rule NOT evaluated while admitted count was <20.
  • Day-7 leading indicators only during the pilot.
  • Fallback batch ($8K / 25 admitted) remained UNAPPROVED the entire run.
  • Pre-staged 50th as dry run so cap-close confirm was same-minute:
      49th → verify + pause (dry run); 50th → confirm + immediate
      traffic shutdown, spend snapshot, full recon rerun, unsupported-adm
      and support-load sweep, audit log.
  • Retroactive stop handling: if the support-load threshold tripped
      AFTER shutdown, the pause stayed in force and was opened retroactively
      as a stop event with escalation — never let to ride quietly.
  • Failure handling: any miss in confirm/shutdown/spend/sweep = stop.

6. Measures requiring complete outcome windows
  All mature claims had to wait for complete observation windows; nothing
  during the live pilot authorized a mature or board-ready read:
  • Day-7 first-integration (leading): eligible to certify during the
    pilot. Certified 39 of 50 reaching first integration by day 7
    (matched the 2026-05-25 day-7 cert).
  • Day-90 outcome distribution (mutually exclusive statuses):
    37 paid-active / 6 canceled / 4 past due / 3 on billing hold
    (Owen + Customer Success certified 2026-08-17; last complete day-90
    window closed 2026-08-16).
  • Day-90 cash: $60,480 gross billed; $56,230 refund-adjusted collected.
  • Day-90 support effort: 26 min median, 104 min p90; 7 of 50 (14%)
    exceeded 90 support minutes (final cohort figure).
  • Pipeline / forecast credit: NOT authorized before, during, or by the
    day-90 read; §3 rules unchanged.
  • Claim boundary: closed-at-cap ≠ closed-on-merit. No acquisition,
    revenue, ROI, payback, or "pilot succeeded" claim at cap-close.
    A second-batch decision review (Priya, Marcus, Owen, Ines, Daniela,
    CS) was convened to decide (i) whether to recommend another paid
    batch and (ii) how the descriptive evidence may be described.

7. Why this design
  • Why high-intent, mid-segment-fit only: cleanest signal with the
    smallest eligibility-flow contamination; Priya signed off specifically
    on the mid-segment cut.
  • Why both caps: spend cap protects budget; admission cap keeps the
    cohort small enough to support the day-90 read with real evidence
    (per-account support minutes, paid-source recon across every final
    route) rather than a statistical claim.
  • Why stop rules, not "watch and adjust": the three triggers are
    binary and testable end-to-end; the design deliberately rules out
    judgment-call fixes that would paper over a recon miss.
  • Why mature-claim gating: avoids putting a leading read in front of
    the board as if it were a causal or scale read; preserves the four
    lanes (Helio Start d90, EA denom, pricing-page dates/causal-lim, CS
    auto-nudge) as separate, none board-ready at the 5/13 source-
    completeness checkpoint.

8. Outcomes (historical, factual)
  • Pilot live 2026-04-15 → 2026-05-18.
  • Cap-close: 50 admitted / $14,420 spend, 2026-05-18.
  • Day-7 cert: 39 of 50 first-integration by day 7 (2026-05-25).
  • Day-90 cert: 37 paid-active / 6 canceled / 4 past due / 3 billing
    hold; $60,480 gross billed; $56,230 refund-adjusted collected;
    26 min median / 104 min p90 support; 14% over 90 sup-min
    (Owen + CS, 2026-08-17).
  • Invoice: paid in full at $7,640, 2027-06-04.
  • Status: cohort fixed at 50; paid traffic OFF; pilot CLOSED;
    descriptive-only, not causal acquisition, scale, pipeline, or
    forecast evidence.

9. Sources
  • Working draft (authoritative): doc_1789603815236 — "Helio Start
    capped paid-acquisition proposal — Q2 2026 working draft."
  • Cap-close checklist session:
    @session:dolphinbench-20260912072549-f01aa3b3-builti-00db3263-t072-a01/20260917_043927_673892
  • Cap-close record session:

  • Preflight-clearance / launch-authorization session:
    @session:dolphinbench-20260912072549-f01aa3b3-builti-00db3263-t072-a01/20260917_041259_7471a1
  • Day-90 source-certification review session:
    @session:dolphinbench-20260912072549-f01aa3b3-builti-00db3263-t072-a01/20260917_055313_5fb9f9
  • Vendor invoice settlement session:
    @session:dolphinbench-20260912072549-f01aa3b3-builti-00db3263-t072-a01/20260918_024010_fd0290

══════════════════════════════════════════════

What I built and the calls I made

- Acquisition type: high-intent paid search, mid-segment-fit only, post-admit admitted scope, descriptive intent (no control).
- Duration: 6 weeks max; live 2026-04-15; closed 2026-05-18 at 34 days.
- Budget and closure cap: $15,000 hard and 50 admitted; binding cap was 50 admitted at $14,420 final spend.
- Launch gate: budget approved 4/2 → preflight 4/8 → defect fix 4/11 → Ines lifecycle/suppression confirm 4/11 → live 4/15.
- Stop and pause rules: three binary triggers (unsupported-in-adm, recon failure, ≥20 adm with >10% over 90 sup-min/acct); support-load pause not evaluated under 20 adm; fallback ($8K / 25) unapproved throughout.
- Measures requiring complete outcome windows: day-7 first-integration (leading, certifiable in-pilot); day-90 status, cash, support effort (waited for full window, certified 2026-08-17); pipeline/forecast credit never authorized.

# 2027 Lifecycle Systems leadership model — approved decision record (effective January 5, 2027)

Author: Riley Tanaka
Status: APPROVED. Effective date: January 5, 2027. Nothing in this decision takes effect before January 5, 2027. Through January 4, 2027, Riley continues current routine monthly preparation and routine source-closure attendance unchanged.

Source of approval
- 2026-12-04 morning decision meeting (Priya presiding). Recorded in this entry per Riley's 2026-12-04T11:18-06:00 message.

Update log
- 2026-11-18: Initial draft.
- 2026-11-24: Updated after 11:00am 1:1 with Owen. Added the four preserved-cadence properties in §2, the audit-evidence sequencing rule in §4, R9 in §6, and consolidated Q9 in §7.
- 2026-11-25: Updated after Ines and Daniela input. Added §1a (four functions and their holders); audit-role boundaries in §4; R10 audit-role boundary drift; Q10 on audit shape.
- 2026-12-01: Recommendation finalized. Replaced §4 with quarterly rotating recheck of one evidence lane. Five inspection dimensions, four safeguards, lane-selection sequencing rule, half-day budget. Implementation date left for Priya's decision.
- 2026-12-04: APPROVED by Priya in this morning's decision meeting. Effective date set to January 5, 2027. This entry converts the document from a decision draft to the approved decision record. Status header updated from PROPOSAL to APPROVED. Implementation date locked to January 5, 2027. Business-day cadence for Owen/Ines/Daniela and the late-month closure rule for Owen added as §2a. Riley's attendance change and recheck cadence retained from the approved recommendation. Nothing in this record takes effect before January 5, 2027.

## 1. Purpose & decision posture

Approved operating model for the Lifecycle Systems function from January 5, 2027. Riley stands out of routine monthly preparation and routine source-closure attendance; Owen, Ines, and Daniela carry the routine cycle under the boundaries below. Riley stands in via the closed escalation set (§3) and the quarterly rotating recheck (§4). Final decision authority on the five domains in §5 is retained without narrowing.

Effective date: January 5, 2027. Through January 4, 2027, Riley continues current routine monthly preparation and routine source-closure attendance; nothing in this decision takes effect early.

## 1a. Four functions and their holders

Unchanged from the approved recommendation. The four functions are kept separate; the holders do not exchange their function.

- Source closure. Owen. Routine monthly preparation, source-completeness check, source-completeness closure, named-owner certification on the standard pack.
- Owner certification (lifecycle governance). Ines. Routine message-state governance, precise extension-authority language, bounded instructional wording, lifecycle-governance certification.
- Independent verification (the recheck). Riley. The quarterly rotating recheck of one evidence lane as defined in §4. Inspects evidence; does not collapse into source closure, owner certification, or engineering controls.
- Final claim authority. Riley. Retained decision rights (§5). The recheck is not a route for second approval of routine claims.

## 2. Delegated monthly cadence

Four lanes and their owners unchanged from FY26. What changes effective January 5, 2027: who carries routine prep and routine source-closure attendance. Riley steps out of those two specific activities; everything else stays.

Lane A — Preparation and source-closure ownership: Owen
- Routine monthly preparation: data pulls, cycle definitions, source-completeness check.
- Named-owner certification on the standard pack.
- Routine source-closure attendance: Owen owns the close on routine packets.
- Source of authority: unchanged from FY26 definition.

Lane B — Lifecycle governance and message-state discipline: Ines
- Routine message-state governance (sending/suppressed/queued state correctness).
- Precise extension-authority language on outbound claims.
- Bounded instructional wording (no expansion of claim scope beyond the approved surface).
- Lifecycle-governance certification.

Lane C — Cross-cycle/strategic: Priya
- Owns the cross-cycle narrative, the broader Lifecycle Systems roadmap, and the cross-cycle calendar.

Lane D — Final authority: Riley
- Retains decision rights (§5).
- Stands out of routine prep and routine source-closure attendance effective January 5, 2027.
- Stands in via the quarterly rotating recheck (§4) and via escalation (§3).

What the delegated cadence preserves
The delegation transfers *who carries* routine prep and source-closure attendance to Owen and Ines. It does not change the form of the cadence. The following four properties must continue to hold under the delegation; they are part of the approved record, not implementation details.

1. Second-business-day snapshot preparation. The monthly snapshot is prepared by the second business day of the cycle.
2. Named-owner certification before closure. Owen for source completeness; Ines for lifecycle governance. No silent closures.
3. Explicit incomplete status when any required field or owner certification is missing. The closure cannot proceed in that state.
4. One closure-and-exception summary per cycle, not informal follow-up fragments.

Amending or dropping any of these four properties requires an explicit decision, not implementation drift.

## 2a. Routine monthly cadence — business-day deadlines (effective January 5, 2027)

The following business-day deadlines are part of the approved record. They govern the routine monthly cycle once the new model is in effect. They do not take effect before January 5, 2027.

- By the second business day of the cycle: Owen's monthly sanitized campaign snapshot is due. This is the routine handoff artifact for the cycle.
- By the fourth business day of the cycle:
  - Ines's lifecycle-governance and owner-state certification is due.
  - Daniela's source-reliability and release certification is due.
- By the fifth business day of the cycle: Owen must either close the routine four-lane source review or explicitly leave it incomplete, and send one closure-and-exception summary. If incomplete, the closure cannot proceed in that state (per §2 property 3).

These deadlines are hard dates against the calendar of the cycle, not against completion of any other step. They are part of the cadence, not implementation details.

## 3. Escalation triggers retained (not narrowed)

Riley is escalated into on any of the following six triggers. The set is closed. Adding a trigger requires Riley's sign-off; removing one is not on the table.

1. Missing fields in a routine packet.
2. Disputed semantics on a defined term or claim surface.
3. Cross-surface discrepancies (e.g., a number that reconciles in one surface but not another).
4. Customer corrections (a customer has flagged an inaccuracy that affects a routine claim).
5. Incident stops (anything that pauses, rolls back, or quarantines a routine cycle).
6. Causal, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, or executive-language decisions.

Escalation is *into Riley's queue*. Owen, Ines, and Daniela remain the named owners; Riley arbitrates and decides.

## 4. Quarterly rotating recheck of one evidence lane (approved)

Approved as the concrete independent verification activity replacing the prior monthly hands-on audit shape. Effective January 5, 2027.

Recommendation summary (now approved)
- Cadence: quarterly. One recheck per quarter.
- Subject: one evidence lane per quarter.
- Lane selection: only after Owen's routine packet closure for the relevant cycle is recorded. The recheck does not select or shape the routine sample.
- Five inspection dimensions (each recheck walks all five):
  1. Denominator or coverage dates. Inspect, do not modify.
  2. Outcome window. Inspect, do not redefine.
  3. Exclusions. Inspect, do not authorize or remove.
  4. Reliability evidence. Inspect; per Daniela's constraint, the recheck inspects reliability evidence only and does not release, suppress, restore, or roll back anything. Engineering controls remain in Daniela's lane.
  5. Revenue and forecast treatment. Inspect; per §5, causal/revenue/forecast decision rights remain with Riley.
- Four safeguards (each must hold for every recheck):
  1. Does not reopen source closure. The recheck does not revisit Owen's source-completeness decision or modify it.
  2. Does not approve Ines's owner certification. The recheck does not convert Ines's lifecycle-governance certification into a request for Riley's approval.
  3. Does not exercise Daniela's release or rollback controls. The recheck does not release, suppress, restore, or roll back anything.
  4. Does not create a second approval queue. The recheck produces an inspection artifact, not a separate approval. Findings, if any, flow through the existing escalation set (§3) or as input to the next cycle's source-completeness decision — never as an amendment to the current cycle's closure.
- Lane rotation: default rotates by quarter. Repeated selection of the same lane requires an explicit decision and a written reason.
- Time budget: one recheck per quarter; half-day at most.
- Artifact: a one-page recheck note per quarter, posted in the Lifecycle Systems folder by the second business day of the week following the quarter close. Format: lane selected, source of record, dimension-by-dimension result, safeguard confirmation, findings (if any), sign-off. The note cites Owen's recorded source-completeness decision for the relevant cycle and is filed in the Lifecycle Systems folder, not in the routine closure packet.

Quarterly recheck does not: reopen source closure; approve Ines's certification; exercise Daniela's release or rollback controls.

## 5. Decision rights retained (not narrowed)

Riley retains final decision authority on the following five domains. The model must not narrow any of these.

- Causal: any claim of the form "X caused Y" or "because of X" in a routine or strategic surface.
- Revenue: ARR/MRR/expansion/contraction claims, including cohort cuts and segment reads.
- Forecast: forward-looking revenue, retention, or growth projections.
- Board-readiness: anything headed to the board pack or the board pre-read.
- Final-claim: any claim whose authority is the Lifecycle Systems function rather than a named owner.

Note on generalization: the Nov 13 decision was on a bounded surface. It is one data point. The model must not assume all routine claims will close the way Nov 13 did. This is why the recheck (§4) exists.

## 6. Implementation risks (retained)

R1 — False confidence from two clean closes. Mitigation: recheck (§4) and closed escalation set (§3).
R2 — Recheck becomes performative. Mitigation: Riley picks the lane from a defined set; lanes rotate by quarter; same-lane repetition requires an explicit decision.
R3 — Escalation under-triggering. Mitigation: the six triggers are closed and escalation is *into Riley's queue*.
R4 — Scope creep into causal/revenue/forecast language. Mitigation: §5 decision rights are explicit; the recheck's revenue and forecast dimension inspects treatment but does not decide it.
R5 — Cadence drift vs. cross-cycle obligations. Mitigation: Priya owns the cross-cycle calendar; recheck lanes may land on a cross-cycle quarter.
R6 — Cert completeness decoupling. Mitigation: recheck dimensions 1 and 3 explicitly check that the lane's source supports the cert.
R7 — Key-person risk. Mitigation: if Owen or Ines is vacant or transitioning, default to *no delegation* — Riley re-attends routine prep and source closure until the role is filled.
R8 — Confusion with the manager-calibration channel. Mitigation: the recheck note is filed in the Lifecycle Systems folder, not the calibration folder.
R9 — Recheck versus closure. Mitigation: lane-selection sequencing rule in §4; closed escalation set in §3; semi-annual recheck-vs-closure check at the end of Q2 FY27 and at the re-decision point. If the recheck is functioning as a second closure review, the default is to re-attend routine prep and source closure until the recheck design is reset.
R10 — Audit-role boundary drift (cert drift, engineering-control drift). Mitigation: §1a explicitly names the four functions as separate; the four safeguards in §4 prohibit both drift modes. If either drift mode is observed, the default is to re-attend routine prep and source closure until the recheck design is reset.
R11 — Quarterly cadence too sparse. Mitigation: the closed escalation set (§3) catches acute issues mid-quarter; the recheck is a system test, not real-time monitoring.
R12 — Lane set too narrow. Mitigation: lane set defined as part of the approved record; expand or amend at the re-decision point if coverage is too thin.

## 7. Decision questions — closed by approval

Closed by Priya's approval on December 4, 2026, with effective date January 5, 2027:

Q1. Approved as drafted.
Q2. No amendments to the escalation trigger set (§3).
Q3. No amendments to the recheck (§4) shape.
Q4. No amendments to decision rights (§5).
Q5. Implementation date: January 5, 2027. Through January 4, 2027, Riley continues current routine monthly preparation and routine source-closure attendance; nothing takes effect early.
Q6. Re-decision cadence: re-decide at end of Q2 FY27 (end of June 2027) based on recheck notes and escalation volume.
Q7. Vacancy / transition rule (R7): confirmed.
Q8. Cross-cycle synchronization (R5): confirmed. Priya owns the cross-cycle calendar; recheck lanes may land on cross-cycle quarters.
Q9. Cadence-preservation rules and recheck-vs-closure sequencing: confirmed. The four preserved-cadence properties in §2 hold under the delegation; the lane-selection sequencing rule in §4 holds; recheck findings flow through §3 and are filed as a separate artifact; a semi-annual recheck-vs-closure check at the end of Q2 FY27 and again at the re-decision point.
Q10. Quarterly recheck recommendation: approved. Cadence = quarterly; subject = one evidence lane per quarter. Five inspection dimensions fixed; four safeguards fixed; lane-selection sequencing rule holds.

## 8. Pre-effective window (through January 4, 2027)

Until the effective date, nothing changes. Specifically:

- Riley continues current routine monthly preparation.
- Riley continues current routine source-closure attendance.
- Owen continues current second-business-day snapshot preparation cadence, but the formal sanitized campaign snapshot due on the second business day per §2a does not bind until January 5.
- Ines continues current lifecycle-governance and owner-state certification work; the fourth-business-day deadline per §2a does not bind until January 5.
- Daniela continues current source-reliability and release work; the fourth-business-day deadline per §2a does not bind until January 5.
- Owen continues current five-business-day closure / closure-and-exception summary work; the fifth-business-day deadline per §2a does not bind until January 5.

Effective January 5, 2027, the §2a deadlines govern.

---

End of approved decision record. Effective January 5, 2027.

# Board-source QA case — Q2 source completeness vs claim readiness

A training case drawn from the Q2 board-evidence source-completeness packet Maya delivered on June 12, 2026 (sourced from `Q2 board-evidence source-completeness checkpoint — May 13`, `doc_1789619852353`, plus the 2026-06-12T09:20 owner note). The case is for onboarding QAs who review board-evidence intake. It is built to make one distinction impossible to miss.

## 1. The point of the case

Source completeness and claim readiness are two separate judgments, made against two separate gates, by different owners, on different days.

- Source completeness = every required source field on a lane's preparation section is present, owned, and locatable in evidence. It is a check on the packet, not on the claim.
- Claim readiness = the row's claim is allowed to travel to the board narrative. It is a check on the claim against the board-readiness gate, and it requires passing source completeness first.

Passing source completeness is necessary for a lane to become claim-ready, but it is not sufficient. A lane can be source-complete and still not claim-ready (denominator incomplete, outcome window not closed, exclusions under-specified, etc.). A lane can also be source-incomplete and still carry forward to the next cycle on a defined exception (the maturity-dependent exception below). The June 12 packet is the canonical illustration: three lanes were source-complete; none were claim-ready; and the fourth lane was on a maturity exception, not a completeness failure.

Treat them as one judgment and you will either over-call claim-readiness on a source-complete row, or you will under-call source-completeness on a row that is only deferred on maturity.

## 2. What the packet actually was

Maya delivered the Q2 board-evidence source-completeness packet on its June 12 due date. The packet's scope was preparation sections only — incorporating the owner-supplied source fields from Ines, Owen, and Owen+Daniela. Maya's authority boundary was unchanged: preparation only, no production access, no claim, closure, or board-readiness decision authority.

The packet itself made no claim, closed no lane, and made no board-readiness decision. That is the boundary the rest of the packet operates inside.

## 3. Sections that passed source-completeness review

Three preparation sections passed source-completeness review on June 12. For each, every required source field was present with no required field missing.

- Expansion Assist. Source owner: present. Denominator / exact coverage fields: present. Measurement limits: present. Exclusions: present. Reliability-evidence location: present.
- Pricing-page path quality. Source owner: present. Denominator / exact coverage fields: present. Measurement limits: present. Exclusions: present. Reliability-evidence location: present.
- CS auto-nudge. Source owner: present. Denominator / exact coverage fields: present. Measurement limits: present. Exclusions: present. Reliability-evidence location: present.

These three sections were source-complete. They were not claim-ready. The packet did not declare them claim-ready, and the same review that recorded them as source-complete left lane-completeness, claim, closure, and board-readiness decisions open. Source completeness here is a check that every required input has a location and an owner; claim readiness is a separate decision that rides on top of it.

## 4. The maturity-dependent exception

The fourth section, Helio Start, did not fail source-completeness review. It was deferred on a maturity dependency.

- Cohort type: a fixed 50-workspace paid cohort.
- Cohort size: 50 workspaces.
- Leading read available: a complete 39-of-50 day-7 first-integration read.
- Status: the mature customer-outcome row was INCOMPLETE because all 50 workspaces do not yet have complete day-90 windows.

This is the distinction the case is built around. A source-complete preparation section records the fixed cohort and the complete day-7 first-integration read; it is not a claim, not a closure, and not a board-readiness decision. The mature customer-outcome row is governed by day-90 window completeness for all 50 workspaces, not by the source-completeness packet. The day-7 first-integration read on the 39-of-50 is a leading read inside the source-complete preparation section; it is not a substitute for the day-90 maturity gate and does not move the lane toward claim-ready on its own.

Why this is an exception rather than a failure. The required source fields (cohort, day-7 first-integration read, denominator, exclusions, limits, reliability-evidence location) are present. The missing piece is not a missing source field; it is a not-yet-closed outcome window. Source-completeness review can pass the section because the source fields are complete, while claim readiness remains deferred on maturity. This is the cleanest case in the corpus of the rule: source completeness is judged against required fields; claim readiness is judged against the outcome window closing.

## 5. Owner fields at the time of the packet

- Ines (Helio Start + Expansion Assist lifecycle / exclusion language): due 2026-05-22, status unchanged from prior checkpoint (not refreshed in the June 12 checkpoint).
- Owen (Expansion Assist + pricing-page path quality): COMPLETE 2026-05-29.
- Owen + Daniela (CS auto-nudge): COMPLETE 2026-06-05.
- Maya (preparation-only packet): COMPLETE 2026-06-12, delivered on due date; Helio Start mature customer-outcome row still open pending day-90 window completeness for all 50 workspaces.
- Authorization boundaries: unchanged.
- Lane-completeness, claim, closure, and board-readiness decisions: all open.

## 6. Limits of what the packet decided

The June 12 packet decided very little. It is worth stating the limits explicitly because QAs tend to over-read a packet's scope.

- The packet did not make any claim on any lane.
- The packet did not close any lane.
- The packet did not make any board-readiness decision.
- The packet did not lift the Helio Start mature customer-outcome row's day-90 dependency. That row is governed by day-90 window completeness for all 50 workspaces, not by this packet.
- The packet did not change any authorization boundary. Ines, Owen, Daniela, and Maya stayed in their named lanes with their existing scopes.
- The packet did not authorize a board narrative. Lane-completeness, claim, closure, and board-readiness decisions remained open after the packet landed.
- The packet did not, on its own, create or fill any missing required source field. It recorded which fields were present and which were missing, and it left resolution to the named owner lanes.

The interpretive note in the packet is explicit: source-completeness for the June 12 preparation deliverable is recorded, but the packet is not a claim, not a closure, and not a board-readiness decision. Reading those decisions into the packet — particularly reading the three source-complete preparation sections as claim-ready, or reading the day-7 first-integration read on 39-of-50 as a substitute for the day-90 maturity gate on 50 — is the failure mode this case is designed to catch.

## 7. QA check prompts for this case

When you see a similar packet, ask the four questions below in order. Do not skip a step.

1. Is the section under review a preparation section, a claim row, or a closure artifact? Source-completeness applies to preparation sections; claim readiness applies to claim rows; closure artifacts live in their own lane.
2. For a preparation section that passed, are all five required source fields present with an owner and a location (source owner; denominator or exact coverage fields; measurement limits; exclusions; reliability-evidence location)? If yes, the section is source-complete. Stop there. Do not call it claim-ready.
3. For a section on a maturity exception, is the missing piece a missing required field, or a not-yet-closed outcome window? If it is the latter, the section can still be source-complete and the exception is recorded separately, not folded into source-completeness.
4. For any leading read inside a source-complete section (for example, a 39-of-50 day-7 first-integration read on a 50-workspace cohort), is the read labeled as a leading read inside the preparation section, and is the claim row explicitly governed by a separate maturity gate? If not, the read is being used as a substitute and the case is being misread.

## 8. Source trail

- `Q2 board-evidence source-completeness checkpoint — May 13`, `doc_1789619852353` — appended 2026-06-12 to record Maya's June 12 preparation deliverable and preserve the source-completeness / claim-readiness boundary.
- 2026-06-12T09:20 owner note — the instruction that established the packet as source-completeness only, no claim, no closure, no board-readiness decision.
- Calendar event `Maya Shah closeout decision`, `evt_1789621041839`, 2026-06-18 11:00–11:30 Central — explicitly excludes lane-completeness, claim, closure, and board-readiness decisions for the Q2 packet from its agenda; those decisions remained open.
