arguments.body:
# Helio Start capped paid-acquisition proposal — Q2 2026 working draft

**Status (post 2026-04-02 budget review): PROPOSAL — RECOMMENDATION BUDGET-APPROVED, PREFLIGHT PENDING. NOT LAUNCH AUTHORIZATION.**

This document is a proposal artifact for the capped Q2 Helio Start paid-acquisition test. As of the 2026-04-02 budget review (chair: Riley; scheduling: Priya), the recommended six-week high-intent paid-search shape has been approved by Priya with a budget of no more than $15,000, closing at the earlier of $15,000 in spend or 50 admitted workspaces. **Preflight is pending.** Paid traffic remains blocked. Paid traffic stays blocked until paid-source attribution reconciles from eligibility-flow start through admission and through assisted routing. No launch authorization is implied or granted by this document.

- **Author:** Riley Tanaka
- **Prepared:** 2026-03-04
- **Last revised (in-place, no scope expansion):** 2026-03-09 — §4.4 success measure, §4.5 support-load and unsupported-admission guardrails, and §4.6 monitoring and stop rules updated with owner inputs from Owen (Growth), Customer Success, and Ines (Lifecycle). All other sections unchanged at that revision.
- **Revised 2026-04-02 (in-place, post budget review):** Status banner updated to budget-approved / preflight-pending. §4.1 traffic cap, §4.2 budget request, §4.3 audience and channel, §4.5 support-load and unsupported-admission guardrails, §4.6 monitoring and stop rules, and §4.9 decision owners updated to reflect the 2026-04-02 budget-review outcome. Recommendation ($15,000 / 50 admitted workspaces / 6-week high-intent paid search) is recorded as approved by Priya with the documented stop / pause conditions. Fallback ($8,000 / 25 admitted workspaces / 6-week high-intent paid search) remains unapproved. §4.4 success measure, §4.7 refund-adjusted cash treatment, and the cadence / escalation-path sub-items remain OPEN. Organic-only boundary through 2026-03-31 has now lapsed by date; the live boundary is "paid traffic stays blocked until preflight passes." All preserved rules in §3 are unchanged. No new artifact, no pipeline target, no forecast credit.
- **Reviewer / approver (recommendation + budget envelope):** Priya, 2026-04-02.
- **Authority invoked:** Priya's 2026-03-03 confirmation that the published evidence condition is satisfied, authorizing Riley to PREPARE a Q2 capped proposal, plus Priya's 2026-04-02 approval of the recommended six-week high-intent paid-search shape with a $15,000 budget ceiling closing at the earlier of $15,000 spend or 50 admitted workspaces. Proposal + budget-envelope authority only. Preflight + launch authorization still pending.

---

## 0. 2026-04-02 budget-review outcome (decision record)

A 30-minute budget review was chaired by Riley on Thursday, 2026-04-02, 13:30–14:00 CT (calendar event `evt_1789617541495`). Frame: review, not approval — but the review resulted in a budget approval of the recommended shape. The decisions recorded here are the ones the review was empowered to make; everything else is documented as out of scope or as still pending.

**In the review (decided):**

1. **Recommended shape approved.** Six-week high-intent paid-search test. Channel: paid search only, against a curated high-intent keyword set (decision-stage, mid-segment-fit terms). No broad / display / social expansion in this shape. The recommended shape is recorded as approved by Priya on 2026-04-02.
2. **Budget envelope approved.** No more than **$15,000** total spend on the test, closing at the **earlier of $15,000 in spend or 50 admitted workspaces**. Time cap is 6 weeks from launch. Whichever ceiling binds first stops new spend on the recommendation. Approved by Priya on 2026-04-02.
3. **Fallback shape: NOT approved.** The smaller fallback ($8,000 / 25 admitted workspaces / 6-week high-intent paid search, same shape otherwise) remains unapproved. It is documented as the smaller-shape alternative the review was empowered to choose instead of the recommendation; the review chose the recommendation, so the fallback stays on file as the documented fallback and is not active.
4. **Stop / pause conditions binding on the approved recommendation:**
   - **Stop immediately if an unsupported applicant enters the admitted path.** This is unchanged from the published evidence condition (Jan 27 and Feb 24 packets both confirmed zero unsupported cases admitted) and from §4.5 of this draft. Detection = halt, not warning.
   - **Pause if a routing or instrumentation failure prevents paid-source reconciliation.** Reconciliation means paid-source attribution is visible from eligibility-flow start through admission, and is preserved through assisted routing. A reconciliation failure pauses the test until it is resolved; it is not a warning to investigate.
   - **After at least 20 admissions, pause if more than 10% exceed 90 support minutes.** Account-level support minutes, captured per account from first assisted contact through the published mature window (Customer Success input, §4.5), are the unit the pause reads on; aggregated averages are not acceptable. The pause is a stop-rule input, not a stop on its own.
5. **Success-measure frame confirmed:** Day-7 first integration is a leading operating read only. Paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort all need complete outcome windows before any mature claim. Partial-window reads may trigger a halt or continue the test but cannot support a mature claim. Mature-claim gating is unchanged from §4.4 / §4.6.

**Pending preflight (NOT decided in the review — blocks launch):**

- Paid-source attribution reconciliation, from eligibility-flow start through admission and through assisted routing. Until preflight confirms reconciliation, paid traffic stays blocked.
- Implementation checks (traffic-cap mechanics, ad-ops setup, lifecycle-instrumentation verification, support-routing confirmation) happen after the preflight passes, not before.
- Final go/no-go on launch is a separate decision owned by Priya and is not granted by the budget approval.

**Out of scope for the review (unchanged):**

- Pipeline or forecast credit — excluded by §4.8. Not in scope of this draft at any stage.
- Mature outcome claims — out of scope until complete outcome windows exist.
- Q1 board-lane readiness — still not board-ready because the two certified mature cohorts (Jan 27 and Feb 24 packets) still lack exact start and end dates. This is a separate Q1-readiness item and is not changed by the budget review.
- Final launch go/no-go — Priya only, separate from the budget approval.

**Continuing boundary (post review):**

- Paid traffic stays blocked until preflight passes. The organic-only-through-2026-03-31 boundary has lapsed by date; its successor boundary is the preflight gate.
- Existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and support-routing rules are unchanged.
- No pipeline target. No forecast credit.

---

## 1. Standing boundary — do not change

- Helio Start was **organic-only through 2026-03-31**. That boundary has now lapsed by date.
- The **live boundary** as of 2026-04-02 is: **paid traffic stays blocked until preflight passes**, where preflight is the paid-source attribution reconciliation from eligibility-flow start through admission and through assisted routing.
- Through the preflight-pending period: no paid traffic, no pipeline or forecast attribution, no launch.
- This draft does not authorize launch. It records the budget approval of the recommendation; it does not flip the preflight gate.
- Organic-only status through 2026-03-31, and the no-paid-traffic-before-April-1 rule, are both preserved as historical boundary conditions. They are not in force as live gates today; the preflight gate replaces them.

## 2. The two qualifying mature cohorts (summary)

The published condition for reopening capped paid acquisition is:

- Two mature cohorts, each with **fewer than 5%** of cases crossing the **>90 supplementary-minute** threshold, AND
- **Zero unsupported cases** in the admitted path.

Per Priya's 2026-03-03 review, the evidence condition is satisfied based on two mature cohort packets:

- **Jan 27 mature cohort packet** — condition met on the published thresholds. (Per the Q1 source-lock read on `Quarterly board operating evidence intake — Q1 2026`, `doc_1789577240164`: 86 admitted workspaces with a complete day-90 window; 4 of 86 (4.7%) over 90 support minutes; 0 unsupported case admitted.)
- **Feb 24 mature cohort packet** — condition met on the published thresholds. (Per the same source-lock read: 91 admitted workspaces with a complete day-90 window; 3 of 91 (3.3%) over 90 support minutes; 0 unsupported case admitted.)

**Open gap carried forward:** the source packets for both cohorts still lack cohort dates. Because of that gap, the Q1 board lane remains not board-ready. This draft is structured for Q2; the missing cohort dates are a separate Q1-readiness item and are not fixed here. The 2026-04-02 budget approval does not change this — Q1 readiness is a separate track, and the budget approval is a Q2 proposal-review decision.

(Per-cohort numbers, exact percentages, and cohort identifiers are not restated in this draft because they are not in this working session's source materials; Priya has the source packets.)

## 3. Rules that must be preserved by any test this draft proposes

Any Q2 test, including the 2026-04-02 budget-approved recommendation, must preserve all of the following exactly as they operate today. None of these are open for renegotiation inside the capped paid-acquisition test. If a proposed test would require changing any of them, that change is out of scope for this draft and must be raised separately.

- **Eligibility rules** — current Helio Start eligibility logic, unchanged.
- **Refusal rules** — current refusal logic and refusal messaging, unchanged.
- **Connector-access rules** — current connector gating, unchanged.
- **External-authority rules** — current rules on what requires external sign-off, unchanged.
- **Lifecycle rules** — current lifecycle stages and transitions, unchanged. No new lifecycle branch is created for paid-acquired Helio Start cases. Paid-acquired cases flow through the same lifecycle stages and transitions as organic cases, with the existing branch logic determining next-touch, suppression, and reactivation behaviour.
- **Instrumentation rules** — current event taxonomy and properties, unchanged. Paid-source attribution must remain visible from eligibility-flow start through admission, and must be preserved through assisted routing; this is an instrumentation requirement, not a downstream reporting nicety.
- **Support-routing rules** — current routing of Helio Start cases in support, unchanged. Assisted-route reasons and account-level support minutes are captured from first contact, not reconstructed later. Per-account minutes — not aggregated averages — are the unit any guardrail reads on.

## 4. Open decisions

Each subsection below is an explicit decision. The 2026-04-02 budget review resolved the items marked RESOLVED. Items still marked OPEN are either deferred to preflight, deferred to launch gate, or deferred to mature-window completion. No choice is presented as settled beyond what the budget review actually settled.

### 4.1 Traffic cap — RESOLVED 2026-04-02 (recommendation)

- **Question:** what is the maximum paid-traffic exposure for the test?
- **Decision (post budget review):** the recommendation is approved with the following caps (whichever hits first stops new spend):
  - Spend cap: **$15,000 total**.
  - Volume cap: **50 admitted workspaces**.
  - Time cap: **6 weeks from launch**.
- **Constraint respected:** capped (not open-ended); small enough that an adverse outcome cannot move cohort-level metrics; sized to produce a readable signal inside Q2.
- **Status:** RESOLVED on the recommendation by Priya on 2026-04-02. The fallback's $8,000 / 25 admitted workspaces cap remains documented but is not active.
- **Launch gate:** time cap and any per-day pacing are set at launch gate, not here.

### 4.2 Budget request — RESOLVED 2026-04-02 (recommendation)

- **Question:** what dollar budget is requested for the test, and against which budget line?
- **Decision (post budget review):** Priya approved a budget envelope of **no more than $15,000** for the recommended six-week high-intent paid-search test, closing at the **earlier of $15,000 in spend or 50 admitted workspaces**. The budget approval is for the recommendation only; the fallback's $8,000 envelope is not approved.
- **Constraint respected:** the budget approval is for the capped test, not for open-ended paid acquisition; no separate pipeline or forecast credit is implied.
- **Status:** RESOLVED on the recommendation by Priya on 2026-04-02.
- **What the budget approval does NOT do:** the budget approval is not launch authorization, not preflight authorization, not acquisition authorization, not a pipeline target, and not forecast credit. Preflight must still pass before any spend occurs.

### 4.3 Audience and channel — RESOLVED 2026-04-02 (recommendation)

- **Question:** which audience, and through which channel(s)?
- **Decision (post budget review):** paid search only, against a curated high-intent keyword set (decision-stage, mid-segment-fit terms). **No broad / display / social expansion in this shape.** Audience scope is bounded to the curated keyword set; expansion beyond paid search is out of scope for this draft.
- **Constraint respected:** must not bypass any preserved rule in §3 (eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, support-routing). The paid-search scope must run through the same lifecycle branches and current-state suppression behaviour as the organic flow (per Ines, §4.6); no paid-source bypass.
- **Status:** RESOLVED on the recommendation by Priya on 2026-04-02.

### 4.4 Success measure — OPEN (owner input received 2026-03-09 from Owen, Growth; reaffirmed at the 2026-04-02 budget review)

- **Question:** what is the primary read on whether the capped test succeeded?
- **Constraints to respect:** must be measurable inside the cap; must not be redefined post-hoc; must not be conflated with pipeline or forecast credit (see §4.8). Per Owen (2026-03-09), and reaffirmed at the 2026-04-02 budget review, the success-measure frame is:
  - **Keep paid-source attribution visible from eligibility-flow start through admission, and through assisted routing.** Attribution cannot be dropped at any step between the first eligibility touch and admission, and must be preserved through assisted routing; if it is, the resulting cohort cannot support a mature claim. This is an instrumentation requirement, not a downstream reporting nicety — it is what makes any later paid-vs-organic comparison defensible.
  - **Treat Day-7 first integration as a leading operating indicator only.** It is an early read on activation momentum, not an outcome. It may inform monitoring and stop-rule judgement but cannot by itself support a mature claim.
  - **Require complete outcome windows before supporting a mature claim.** The mature outcome measures are:
    - paid-active status at the published mature window,
    - refund-adjusted collected cash at the published mature window,
    - account-level support effort at the published mature window (per Customer Success in §4.5).
    No mature claim may be made on any of these before its full outcome window has closed. Reporting on a partial window is acceptable only as a leading read and must be labelled as such.
- **Decision:** OPEN — no specific metric threshold or window length is proposed in this draft. The frame is locked; the thresholds and window length are deferred to preflight.

### 4.5 Support-load and unsupported-admission guardrails — RESOLVED 2026-04-02 (stop / pause thresholds); frame locked 2026-03-09 (Customer Success)

- **Question:** what thresholds trigger a halt on support load or on any unsupported case appearing in the admitted path?
- **Constraints to respect:** the published evidence condition — zero unsupported cases in the admitted path — must remain in force throughout the test. Any unsupported case in the admitted path is, by definition, a **halt signal**, not a warning.
- **Per Customer Success (2026-03-09), the support-load capture frame is:**
  - **Capture assisted-route reasons from the first contact.** The reason a case enters the assisted route (e.g., self-serve stall, eligibility question, refusal appeal, integration blocker, billing) is recorded at first contact, not reconstructed later. This is what makes account-level support effort attributable rather than approximate.
  - **Capture account-level support minutes from the first contact.** Minutes are tracked per account from first assisted contact through the published mature window, not summarised after the fact. Per-account minutes — not aggregated averages — are the unit the guardrail reads on.
  - **Treat any unsupported case in the admitted path as an immediate stop condition.** "Immediate stop" means the test halts on detection; it is not a warning to investigate. This is unchanged from the published evidence condition.
- **Stop / pause thresholds binding on the recommendation (resolved 2026-04-02 budget review):**
  - **Stop immediately if an unsupported applicant enters the admitted path.**
  - **After at least 20 admissions, pause if more than 10% exceed 90 support minutes.** Account-level minutes captured per account from first assisted contact.
- **Decision:** frame RESOLVED on 2026-03-09; stop / pause thresholds RESOLVED on 2026-04-02. No additional per-account-minute threshold or assisted-route taxonomy is being introduced in this draft beyond what is recorded above.

### 4.6 Monitoring and stop rules — RESOLVED 2026-04-02 (binding stop / pause conditions); spine locked 2026-03-09 (Owen + Ines); cadence OPEN

- **Question:** what monitoring cadence and what stop rules apply during the test?
- **Constraints to respect:** monitoring must be live, not retrospective; stop rules must be pre-committed, not discretionary; halt triggers include, at minimum:
  - any breach of the support-load guardrail in §4.5,
  - any breach of the unsupported-admission guardrail in §4.5 (i.e., any unsupported case in the admitted path),
  - any breach of the >90 supplementary-minute threshold on a paid-acquired cohort,
  - any change that would require modifying a preserved rule in §3.
- **Per Owen (2026-03-09), and reaffirmed at the 2026-04-02 budget review, the monitoring and stop-rule frame is:**
  - **Require complete outcome windows before supporting a mature claim.** Same point as §4.4, restated here because it is a stop-rule input: a stop rule cannot be "lifted on a mature read" because the read was partial. Partial-window reads may trigger a halt or continue the test, but they cannot clear a stop.
  - **Use paid-source attribution as the spine of monitoring.** Because §4.4 requires paid-source attribution to remain visible from eligibility-flow start through admission (and through assisted routing), every monitoring cut relevant to a stop decision (paid-active, refund-adjusted collected cash, account-level support effort, Day-7 first integration, unsupported-admission events) must be reproducible on the attributed paid cohort. Monitoring that loses attribution at any step is not acceptable.
  - **Pause if a routing or instrumentation failure prevents paid-source reconciliation.** Resolved 2026-04-02. Reconciliation must be verified end-to-end (eligibility-flow start → admission → assisted routing) before spend resumes after any pause.
- **Per Ines (2026-03-09), the lifecycle-instrumentation frame is:**
  - **Reuse the existing lifecycle branches as-is.** No new lifecycle branch is created for paid-acquired Helio Start cases. Paid-acquired cases flow through the same lifecycle stages and transitions as organic cases (per §3), with the existing branch logic determining next-touch, suppression, and reactivation behaviour.
  - **Reuse the current-state suppression behavior as-is.** No paid-source bypass of current-state suppression is introduced. If a case is suppressed under current-state logic (e.g., already converted, in an active onboarding sequence, in a cooldown window), it stays suppressed for the paid-acquired cohort exactly as it would for the organic cohort. A paid-source bypass is explicitly out of scope and is one of the changes that would require modifying a preserved rule in §3 (lifecycle, instrumentation).
- **Decision:** spine RESOLVED on 2026-03-09; binding stop / pause conditions RESOLVED on 2026-04-02 (unsupported-admission stop, reconciliation pause, >90-minute pause after ≥20 admissions). Monitoring cadence and escalation path remain OPEN and are deferred to preflight / launch gate.

### 4.7 Refund-adjusted cash treatment — OPEN

- **Question:** how is refund-adjusted cash from paid-acquired Helio Start cases treated for the purposes of this test?
- **Constraint to respect:** cash treatment is a test-level accounting choice only; it must not flow into MRR pipeline or forecast (see §4.8). Refund-adjusted collected cash is one of the mature outcome measures in §4.4 that requires a complete outcome window before any mature claim; the per-test treatment (gross vs. refund-adjusted, when in the window) is separate from that mature-read frame.
- **Decision:** OPEN — no treatment proposed in this draft.

### 4.8 Pipeline and forecast credit — EXCLUDED

- This draft **excludes** any pipeline or forecast credit for the proposed test.
- No MRR pipeline number, no forecast adjustment, and no modeled contribution to Q2 or later periods is implied or requested by this document.
- Cash treatment in §4.7 is a test-level accounting choice only; it does not authorize any forecast or pipeline attribution.
- The 2026-04-02 budget approval does not introduce any pipeline or forecast credit; the budget envelope is a spending ceiling, not a revenue or pipeline number.

### 4.9 Decision owners — RESOLVED 2026-04-02 (where the budget review resolved ownership); otherwise OPEN

- **Proposal owner (this draft):** Riley Tanaka.
- **Decision owner for traffic cap (§4.1):** RESOLVED 2026-04-02 — Priya, on the recommendation; fallback unapproved.
- **Decision owner for budget (§4.2):** RESOLVED 2026-04-02 — Priya, on the recommendation ($15,000 ceiling); fallback unapproved.
- **Decision owner for audience and channel (§4.3):** RESOLVED 2026-04-02 — Priya, on the recommendation (high-intent paid-search only); fallback unapproved.
- **Decision owner for success measure (§4.4):** Owen (Growth). Frame locked 2026-03-09; thresholds / window length OPEN.
- **Decision owner for support-load and unsupported-admission guardrails (§4.5):** Customer Success, with Priya on stop / pause thresholds as resolved 2026-04-02.
- **Decision owner for monitoring and stop rules (§4.6):** Owen (Growth) on the spine, Ines (Lifecycle) on lifecycle / suppression, with Priya on binding stop / pause conditions as resolved 2026-04-02. Cadence and escalation path: OPEN.
- **Decision owner for refund-adjusted cash treatment (§4.7):** OPEN.
- **Final go/no-go on launch:** Priya — separate from the budget approval. The 2026-04-02 budget approval is not launch authorization.

## 5. What this draft does not do

- It does not authorize launch. The 2026-04-02 budget approval authorizes the budget envelope and the recommendation shape; it does not flip the preflight gate or authorize paid traffic.
- It does not authorize pipeline or forecast attribution.
- It does not modify any preserved rule in §3.
- It does not lift the missing cohort dates on the Jan 27 and Feb 24 packets (separate Q1-readiness item); the Q1 board lane remains not board-ready on that input.
- It does not create a paid-source lifecycle branch or a paid-source suppression bypass (per Ines, §4.6).

tool_call(name="mcp__dolphinbench_apps__update_doc", arguments={body: ..., doc_id: ..., mode: "replace"})

arguments.body:
Q2 2027 Helio Start paid-test proposal — working draft

Status: development draft. Not an approved launch plan. Paid traffic remains off through 2027-03-31. Proposal development is authorized; nothing below this draft is approved except the act of further developing this proposal itself.

2027-03-26 edit (carried forward): the proposal presents one precisely bounded test shape (the $8,000-or-25-admissions close). No alternative budget or scale option is offered. The body is organized so that operating stop and pause rules are in their own section and clearly separated from later mature-outcome claims. The earlier-of-$8,000-or-25-admissions close and every prior exclusion are retained verbatim.

2027-03-29 edit (carried forward): Owen supplied the proposal's measurement-operating shape. The running view is rebuilt around four separate counts (paid-source eligibility-flow starts, assisted routes, admissions, attribution failures); once paid-source admissions exceed 10, the post-10 read shows both the number and the share of admitted workspaces exceeding 90 account-level support minutes; day-7 first integration is included only as a leading indicator; the fixed admitted cohort is preserved after batch closure; and the existing rule that paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort require complete day-90 windows is reaffirmed. Nothing in this revision turns the reporting design into acquisition, pipeline, revenue, or forecast evidence. All prior exclusions, decisions that remain unapproved, stop and pause rules, mature-outcome framing, and carried-in posture are retained verbatim.

2027-03-31 edit (this revision): Ines (lifecycle), Daniela (engineering attribution), and Customer Success supplied the remaining operating inputs as preflight controls that gate traffic BEFORE it begins. A new §2a is inserted between §2 and §3 with three preflight controls: (i) Ines's lifecycle preflight evidence that paid source does not bypass any existing lifecycle branch, hold, or suppression; (ii) Daniela's end-to-end attribution preflight requiring every preflight case to reconcile paid source from eligibility-flow start through assisted routing or admission before traffic begins, with any later reconciliation failure pausing the run via P1; (iii) CS's confirmation that the 25-admission ceiling is a hard staffing cap and that support minutes and assisted-route reasons are recorded from first contact. Preflight controls do not modify any rule in §7, do not redefine any state meaning, and do not change eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, or assisted-routing rules. The runtime rules in §3 (stop/pause), §4 (running view), §5 (post-10 read), §6 (mature outcomes), and §7 (unchanged rules) are retained verbatim, with cross-references added where §2a is now the entry gate. Owner inputs in §8 are updated to record Ines's, Daniela's, and CS's contributions. New open items in §10 are added for the §2a controls. All prior exclusions, decisions that remain unapproved, mature-outcome framing, and carried-in posture are retained verbatim.

1. Decisions that remain unapproved (lead table — none of these are decided in this draft)

| # | Decision | Owner | Status as of 2027-03-29 | Where, if anywhere, it could be decided |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Budget (paid spend envelope, approval path) | Priya | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 2 | Paid traffic (channels, mix, partner routing, spend pacing) | Priya + Growth | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 3 | Launch timing (calendar window, batch start date) | Priya | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 4 | Launch (go/no-go) | Priya | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 5 | Pipeline treatment (whether/how paid admissions affect forecast or pipeline) | Priya + Finance | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 6 | Pipeline target | Priya + Finance | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 7 | Forecast credit (whether/how paid admissions credit to forecast) | Priya + Finance | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 8 | A second paid batch (whether, when, scope) | Priya | Not approved | Separate, future decision path; not in this draft |
| 9 | Develop (draft, model, internal review) a precisely bounded Q2 2027 paid-test proposal | Riley (Riley routes to Priya for the next decision) | APPROVED 2027-03-24 | Authorized by Priya's 3/24 decision; this draft is the development product |
| 10 | Q3-development go/no-go conditional on day-90 read | Priya | Not approved in this draft | Day-90 read itself is not yet produced; the decision is a future event gated on a future read |

Items 1–8 and 10 are explicitly NOT approved by this draft. This draft does not bypass, modify, or pre-decide any of them. Item 9 (develop the proposal) is the only thing approved by Priya's 3/24 decision; this draft is the development product, not an authorization of any other action.

2. The test shape (precisely one — no alternative budget or scale option)

The proposal presents one and only one test shape. No second budget envelope, no second admission cap, no larger or smaller paired ceiling, no fallback shape is offered. The choice between shapes is a budget decision (not approved; see §1 row 1).

  - Surface: Helio Start.
  - Acquisition: paid traffic only. (Paid traffic itself is not approved; see §1 row 2.)
  - Routing: through the ordinary eligibility flow. Eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and assisted-routing rules are unchanged (see §7).
  - Close rule: the batch closes at the EARLIER of (i) $8,000 in paid spend, or (ii) 25 paid admissions. Whichever threshold is hit first ends the batch. The same threshold is the bound for every downstream read in this draft.
  - Trailing-attribution window after close: admissions in flight at close continue to be tracked through their day-90 support window. No new paid admissions are admitted after the close threshold is met.
  - Fixed admitted cohort after closure: once the close threshold is met (or a stop is triggered per §3a), the set of admitted workspaces in the batch is FROZEN. The same set of admitted accounts is the cohort for every read in this draft — running tally, post-10 support-pause read, day-90 mature-outcome read, and any post-closure audit. New eligibility-flow starts that would otherwise route through paid source are NOT admitted into this batch after closure; they do not enter the cohort retroactively and do not change any count in the running view.
  - Reporting cadence during the batch: a running tally of admissions vs. the 25-admission cap and spend vs. the $8,000 cap, refreshed per the standard cadence, so the close trigger is unambiguous when hit.

This is the only shape in this draft. Any other dollar cap, any other admission cap, any other paired ceiling is not in this draft. If a reviewer is looking for a larger or smaller option, it is not here and is not pre-decided; it is a budget decision (not approved; see §1 row 1).

2a. Preflight controls (before traffic begins)

These controls operate as gates BEFORE traffic begins. They do not modify any rule in §7, do not redefine any state meaning, and do not change eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, or assisted-routing rules. They are recorded and evidenced before the batch starts and remain auditable for the life of the cohort.

Preflight is descriptive evidence + recording gates. It is not a launch decision (not approved; see §1 row 4), not a budget decision (not approved; see §1 row 1), and not a pipeline or forecast input (not approved; see §1 rows 5–7). Preflight passing does not authorize traffic to begin; traffic remains off until a separate launch decision (§1 row 4) is made.

2a.1 Lifecycle preflight evidence — Ines

Before traffic begins, written preflight evidence must show that paid-source routing does NOT bypass any existing lifecycle branch, hold, or suppression. Specifically:

  - Each existing lifecycle branch, hold, and suppression that could apply to a paid-source account is enumerated (the universe). The universe is owned by Ines (lifecycle) and is the standing reference; it is not redefined by this draft.
  - For each entry in the universe, the evidence shows whether paid-source routing changes the branch / hold / suppression outcome vs. organic routing. The expected answer for every entry is: no change.
  - Any branch, hold, or suppression where paid-source routing would change the outcome is a preflight FAILURE. On preflight failure, traffic does not begin.
  - The evidence is owned by Ines, archived with the cohort record, and preserved for audit. It does not expire when the batch closes; it is preserved alongside the fixed admitted cohort (§4e).

Preflight lifecycle evidence does NOT modify lifecycle rules (§7). It does NOT add, remove, or relax any branch, hold, or suppression. It does NOT grant connector access out of band. If the evidence shows paid source would bypass any lifecycle state, that is an unsupported-posture condition (consistent with §3a S2 — no admission proceeds; traffic does not begin); it is not a waiver and not a temporary override.

2a.2 End-to-end attribution preflight — Daniela

Before traffic begins, every preflight case must reconcile paid source from eligibility-flow start through assisted routing or admission, on the same account-level join key as the runtime reconciliation in §4c. Specifically:

  - The preflight universe is a documented set of test accounts (or replayed historical events) covering each branch that will be encountered: organic-equivalent entry, refuse, hold, admit-then-route, admit-then-abandon, and the assisted-routing paths that will carry paid-source admissions.
  - For each preflight case, all four §4c checkpoints (eligibility-flow start, eligibility outcome, admission, assisted routing) must be present, non-empty, and joined on a single account-level key.
  - Any preflight case with a missing or mismatched checkpoint is a preflight FAILURE. On preflight failure, traffic does not begin.
  - Once traffic begins, §4c and P1 continue to apply: ANY later reconciliation failure on a paid-source account (not only preflight cases) increments C4 and triggers pause P1 (§3b). Preflight is the entry gate; P1 is the continuing gate. Preflight passing does not exempt the runtime from P1.
  - Preflight evidence is owned by Daniela (engineering), archived with the cohort record, and preserved for audit alongside the fixed admitted cohort (§4e).

Preflight attribution reconciliation does NOT modify attribution, instrumentation, eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, or assisted-routing rules (§7). It is descriptive evidence that the runtime reconciliation in §4c can be expected to succeed end-to-end; it is not a relaxation of P1.

2a.3 Hard staffing cap and from-first-contact recording — Customer Success

Two CS-confirmed controls gate traffic:

  a. The 25-admission ceiling in §2 is a HARD STAFFING CAP. CS confirms this. The cap is not a soft target, not a discretionary ceiling, and not a stretch number; reaching 25 admissions ends the batch per §3a S1 regardless of any other read. This control does not modify the §2 close rule; it reaffirms the cap as a staffing constraint with no override from the running view, the post-10 read (§5), or any mature-outcome read (§6).

  b. SUPPORT MINUTES and ASSISTED-ROUTE REASONS are RECORDED FROM FIRST CONTACT. Specifically:
       - "First contact" = the first assisted-path interaction with a paid-source-eligible account, regardless of whether that account is later admitted, refused, held, or abandoned. First contact is a recording boundary, not a state transition; it does not redefine admission, refusal, hold, or abandonment.
       - Support minutes are recorded at the account level starting at first contact, using the existing support-effort unit (per §6c). Recording begins at first contact and continues through the day-90 window for any account that is admitted.
       - Assisted-route reasons are recorded at every assisted-routing decision starting at first contact, with reason text and timestamp. The reason field does NOT change eligibility, refusal, or assisted-routing rules; it records why a routing decision was made under existing rules. Assisted-route reasons feed §4c (assisted-routing checkpoint) and the assisted-path audit; they do not feed pipeline, revenue, or forecast reads.
       - Recording from first contact is descriptive and operational. It is not a mature-outcome claim and does not enter any pipeline, revenue, or forecast read. Account-level support effort as a mature-outcome claim remains gated by complete day-90 windows (§6c) and is UNAVAILABLE before that window closes.
       - The 25-admission ceiling is preserved (§2, §3a S1). Recording from first contact does not change the cap, the close rule, or the cohort definition.

Preflight CS controls do NOT modify assisted-routing rules or assisted-path coverage (§7). The CS cert posture (closed 2027-03-17: 45/45 day-90 support windows complete; median 24m, p90 86m, 3 >90m; no unsupported case entered admitted path; future capped run of ≤25 admitted wkspcs w/o displacing ordinary assisted-path coverage; descriptive — no randomized control) is the standing reference and is not modified by this draft.

3. Operating rules — stop and pause conditions (this section only; mature-outcome claims are in §6, kept separate)

A stop ends the batch. A pause halts new paid admissions (and certain paid-source-specific instrumentation writes) until a written restart condition is met. A pause is not a stop. A stop is not a pause. Each is its own gating condition; each requires its own remediation before the proposal continues. Mature-outcome claims (paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, account-level support effort) are NOT operating rules and are NOT reported on a stop/pause frame; they are reported only against complete day-90 windows (see §6).

Preflight controls in §2a are the entry gate before any of §3, §4, §5, or §6 begins evaluating. §3 does not authorize traffic to begin; traffic is governed by the launch decision (§1 row 4), which remains unapproved.

3a. Hard stop conditions (the batch ends if any of these occur)

  S1. Close threshold reached: admissions hit 25 OR paid spend hits $8,000, whichever comes first. The admitted cohort is then frozen per §2. The 25-admission ceiling is a hard staffing cap per §2a.3(a); reaching 25 admissions ends the batch regardless of any other read.
  S2. Unsupported admission: an admission to Helio Start lacks the support posture required by the ordinary assisted-path coverage standard at admission time (e.g., missing connector access, missing required lifecycle state, missing external-authority clearance, or any condition that would render day-90 support infeasible within the assisted-path envelope). If detected during the batch (i.e., before close, before day-90 support is complete), the batch halts at that admission for paid-source routing purposes.

3b. Pause conditions (the batch pauses if any of these occur; does not stop)

  P1. Attribution reconciliation failure: a routing or instrumentation failure prevents paid-source attribution from reconciling end-to-end from eligibility-flow start through admission and assisted routing at the account level (see §4). Preflight cases per §2a.2 must have reconciled before traffic began; P1 applies to any LATER reconciliation failure on a paid-source account, whether or not that account was covered by a preflight case.
  P2. Post-10-admission support-pause breach: once paid-source admissions exceed 10 in count, the share of support-pause days attributable to the paid-source cohort exceeds 10% of elapsed batch days (see §5).

3c. What pause does, and what it does not do

  - Pause halts new paid admissions AND halts any instrumentation writes specific to the paid-source cohort.
  - Pause preserves read-only audit access (no data loss for reconciliation).
  - Pause does NOT route around the issue by relaxing eligibility, refusing ordinary users, bypassing lifecycle, or granting connector access out of band.
  - Pause does NOT modify eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, or assisted-routing rules (see §7).
  - Restart requires written identification of cause, written fix, and written sign-off. Restart does NOT authorize a second paid batch (§1 row 8).

3d. What stop does, and what it does not do

  - Stop ends the batch at the trigger admission (S2) or at the close threshold (S1). No new paid admissions are admitted after stop.
  - Stop does NOT modify any surface, rule, or downstream product behavior. It ends only the paid-traffic routing of this batch.
  - Stop does NOT authorize a second paid batch (§1 row 8). A second batch is a separate decision (not approved; see §1 row 8).

A stop and a pause are different events with different triggers and different remediations. They are not interchangeable. They are NOT mature-outcome claims; they are operating rules and are evaluated against the running batch, not against day-90 windows.

4. Running measurement view — separate counts, leading indicators only (operational, not mature-outcome)

The running view reports four separate counts. They are NOT a funnel, NOT a conversion rate, NOT a yield, and NOT a CAC, ROAS, payback, LTV, pipeline, or forecast input. They are operational counts used to evaluate the operating rules in §3 and to support end-to-end attribution reconciliation. None of these counts is or becomes acquisition, pipeline, revenue, or forecast evidence under this proposal.

4a. The four separate counts

The running view, refreshed per the standard cadence, displays exactly these four counts as separate numbers:

  C1. Paid-source eligibility-flow starts — every entry into the eligibility flow attributable to paid source, regardless of outcome (admit / refuse / hold / abandon / error). Counted at eligibility-flow start, joined on the attribution source.
  C2. Assisted routes — every eligibility-flow outcome that resulted in a routing decision into the assisted-path lane carrying paid-source admissions. Counted at assisted-routing decision, joined to C1 by account.
  C3. Admissions — every admission to Helio Start via the ordinary eligibility flow with an auditable end-to-end paid-source attribution chain (per §4c). Counted at the admission event, joined to C1 and C2 by account.
  C4. Attribution failures — every account in the paid-source cohort for which one or more of the four attribution checkpoints in §4c is missing, mismatched, or not joined on a single account-level key. Counted at reconciliation time, regardless of when the underlying gap occurred.

Each count is its own row. They are not summed, not divided into a rate, not compared as numerator and denominator against each other in this proposal. They are reported as four separate numbers with their own cadence and own source-of-truth field.

4b. What the running view is, and is not

  - The running view is the operating instrument for §3 and §4c. It informs stop and pause decisions during the batch.
  - The running view is NOT acquisition evidence. C1 (eligibility-flow starts) is not a reach, impression, click, or channel-performance number; it is an entry count into the eligibility flow for a single paid-source cohort in a single batch.
  - The running view is NOT pipeline evidence. C1–C4 do not enter any pipeline, do not produce a pipeline number, and do not adjust a pipeline target. Pipeline treatment and pipeline target remain decisions that are not approved (§1 rows 5 and 6).
  - The running view is NOT revenue or cash evidence. None of C1–C4 is, or is used to produce, paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, collected ARR/MRR, gross cash, or net cash. Mature revenue/cash reads require complete day-90 windows and are reported only in §6.
  - The running view is NOT forecast evidence. C1–C4 do not enter any forecast, do not produce a forecast number, and do not adjust a forecast credit. Forecast credit remains a decision that is not approved (§1 row 7).

If anyone reuses any of C1–C4 outside this proposal to claim acquisition, pipeline, revenue, or forecast credit, that reuse is outside this draft and is not authorized by it.

4c. End-to-end paid-source attribution reconciliation (operational, not a mature-outcome claim)

  - Scope: from eligibility-flow start, through admission decision, through assisted routing. Must be auditable at the account level end-to-end.
  - Required checkpoints (each must have a recorded source-of-truth and an account-level join key):
      - eligibility-flow start (entry into the eligibility flow, regardless of outcome) — feeds C1.
      - eligibility outcome (admit / refuse / hold, with reason) — feeds the join to C2 / C3.
      - admission (Helio Start admission event, with timestamp) — feeds C3.
      - assisted routing (which assisted-path lane the admission was routed to, with timestamp and reason) — feeds C2. The reason field per §2a.3(b) is recorded from first contact and does not change assisted-routing rules.
  - Preflight gate (per §2a.2): every preflight case must reconcile end-to-end on the same join key before traffic begins. Preflight passing is the entry gate; P1 (§3b) is the continuing gate for any later failure.
  - Reconciliation rule: every admitted paid-source account must have a non-empty value at each of the four checkpoints, joined on a single account-level key. Any missing or mismatched value is an attribution reconciliation failure, increments C4, and triggers pause P1 (§3b).
  - C4 is reported as a running count alongside C1, C2, C3. C4 alone does not trigger stop; it triggers pause P1.
  - Read-only audit access is preserved during any pause to support reconciliation.
  - This reconciliation is descriptive and operational. It does NOT modify eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, or assisted-routing rules (§7).
  - This reconciliation is NOT a mature-outcome claim. It is reported on a running basis during the batch, not at day 90.

4d. Day-7 first integration — leading indicator only

  - Day-7 first integration is reported as a leading indicator only on the running view. It is a directional read on whether admitted accounts are reaching first integration within seven days of admission.
  - Day-7 first integration is NOT a mature-outcome claim. It is NOT a substitute for paid-active status. It is NOT a substitute for refund-adjusted collected cash. It is NOT a substitute for account-level support effort. It does NOT enter any pipeline, revenue, or forecast read.
  - Day-7 first integration does NOT trigger any stop or pause condition in §3. It is observed, recorded, and reported; it does not gate the batch.
  - If day-7 first integration is reported alongside other numbers, it must be labeled as a leading indicator and must not be combined with mature-outcome reads in a single statement.

4e. Cohort preservation after closure

  - Once the close threshold is met (per §2 or §3a S1), the admitted cohort is fixed. The same set of admitted accounts is the cohort for every subsequent read in this draft — running tally, post-10 support-pause read (§5), day-7 leading indicator (§4d), and mature-outcome read (§6).
  - No new account enters the cohort after closure. Eligibility-flow starts that would otherwise route through paid source after closure are not admitted into this batch and are not added to C1, C2, C3, or C4 retroactively.
  - C4 (attribution failures) may still be reconciled post-closure for accounts already in the cohort; reconciliation does not admit a new account.
  - The fixed cohort is preserved for audit. It is not modified, expanded, or pruned by any read in this proposal.

5. Post-10-admission support-pause threshold and >90-account-level-support-minutes read (operational, not mature-outcome)

5a. Post-10-admission support-pause threshold

  - Definition: a "support pause day" is any day on which the assisted-path lane carrying paid-source admissions is paused, throttled, or operating below its ordinary coverage standard for any reason attributable to the paid-source cohort (e.g., capacity, staffing, or instrumentation issue specific to that cohort).
  - Threshold: once paid-source admissions exceed 10 in count, the share of support-pause days attributable to the paid-source cohort must stay at or below 10% of elapsed batch days.
  - Breach: a breach at any rolling read after the 10-admission mark triggers pause P2 (§3b). A breach does not by itself constitute a refusal decision for any individual account; ordinary assisted-path coverage for affected accounts is preserved or restored per §7.
  - Reporting: per-cadence readout of (paid-source-elapsed-days, paid-source-support-pause-days, ratio) once the cohort passes 10 admissions.
  - This threshold is NOT a mature-outcome claim. It is an operating rule evaluated on a running basis during the batch, not at day 90.

5b. >90 account-level support minutes — number AND share, post-10

  - Once paid-source admissions exceed 10 in count, the running view reports two additional separate numbers alongside C1–C4:
      - M1. Number of admitted workspaces whose account-level support minutes over the elapsed batch window exceed 90 minutes. Counted at the running read, joined to C3 by account.
      - M2. Share of admitted workspaces (from C3) whose account-level support minutes exceed 90 minutes. Computed as M1 divided by the admitted count at the running read, expressed as a fraction and as a percentage.
  - Both M1 (number) and M2 (share) are reported. Reporting only the share, or only the number, is insufficient.
  - M1 and M2 are operational reads. They inform §5a's pause rule but are not themselves triggers independent of §5a.
  - M1 and M2 are NOT mature-outcome claims. They are reported on a running basis during the batch, not at day 90. Account-level support effort as a mature-outcome claim is in §6.
  - M1 and M2 are NOT acquisition, pipeline, revenue, or forecast evidence. They do not enter any of those reads.

6. Mature-outcome claims — kept SEPARATE from operating stop and pause rules, and from the running view

Mature-outcome claims are reported only at day 90 or later, against complete day-90 windows. They are explicitly NOT used as operating stop or pause triggers (§3). They are explicitly NOT part of the running view in §4 — the running view is operational; mature-outcome claims are not. The day-7 first integration read in §4d is a leading indicator and is NOT a mature-outcome claim. The >90-support-minutes read in §5b is operational and is NOT a mature-outcome claim. The from-first-contact recording in §2a.3(b) is descriptive and operational and is NOT a mature-outcome claim. Mature-outcome claims may inform whether to develop a Q3 plan (which itself is not approved; see §1 row 10). They are not a launch decision (which is not approved; see §1 row 4), not a budget decision (which is not approved; see §1 row 1), not a pipeline or forecast input (which are not approved; see §1 rows 5–7).

For an admission to count as "paid-active" at day 90, ALL of the following must be true:

  a. The account is admitted to Helio Start via the ordinary eligibility flow with an auditable end-to-end paid-source attribution chain (§4c), and is in the fixed admitted cohort per §2 / §4e.
  b. Refund-adjusted collected cash from the account is positive at day 90. "Refund-adjusted collected cash" = gross collected cash from the account over the day-90 window, minus refunds issued to the account over the same window. Chargebacks, disputes, and processor fees are reported alongside but are not netted into this metric unless explicitly decided later.
  c. Account-level support effort is recorded as an account-level aggregate over the day-90 window, expressed in the existing support-effort unit, and is reportable per account (not only in aggregate). Support-effort reporting does NOT bypass or relax assisted-path coverage. Recording of account-level support minutes begins at first contact per §2a.3(b), but the day-90 aggregate remains a mature-outcome claim gated by complete day-90 windows.
  d. The admission has not been flagged as an unsupported admission that broke assisted-path coverage (§3a S2).
  e. The batch was not in a pause (§3b) covering the admission's day-90 window, OR if it was, the pause has a written restart condition and the admission has been re-validated against that restart condition.

A measure with an incomplete day-90 window is not a measure for this proposal. Do not report, score, or characterize it. Paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort are UNAVAILABLE for any admission whose day-90 window is not yet complete; this is true at any read taken before that window closes. The day-90 read is the read that decides whether development of a Q3 plan proceeds. This draft does NOT decide Q3.

Mature-outcome claims are downstream of the operating rules and downstream of the running view. They are NOT operating rules. They do NOT trigger stops or pauses. They are NOT reported on a stop/pause frame. They are NOT reported on the running-view frame. They are reported only at day 90 or later, against complete day-90 windows, against the fixed admitted cohort.

7. Rules that remain unchanged (not modified, suspended, or waived)

  - Eligibility rules.
  - Refusal rules.
  - Connector-access rules.
  - External-authority rules.
  - Lifecycle rules.
  - Instrumentation rules.
  - Assisted-routing rules.

This draft (including the 2027-03-31 preflight controls in §2a) does not modify, suspend, or waive any of them. The CS cert posture (closed 2027-03-17: 45/45 day-90 support windows complete; median 24m, p90 86m, 3 >90m; no unsupported case entered admitted path; future capped run of ≤25 admitted wkspcs w/o displacing ordinary assisted-path coverage; descriptive — no randomized control) is the standing reference for assisted-path coverage and is not modified by this draft. The Expansion Assist descriptive posture (descriptive; keep disputed/cross-surface/exec; don't line-edit routine; eng release/rollback → Daniela) applies to any instrumentation or routing write described here and is not modified by this draft.

8. Inputs from owners (solicited, not yet committed in this draft)

  - Priya: launch-timing decision, budget decision, traffic allocation decision, pipeline treatment/target decision, forecast credit decision, launch go/no-go, second-paid-batch decision, Q3-development go/no-go on day-90 read. None of these are in this draft (§1).
  - Ines (lifecycle): preflight lifecycle evidence per §2a.1 — written evidence that paid-source routing does not bypass any existing lifecycle branch, hold, or suppression. Descriptive evidence; does not modify lifecycle rules. Owner authority unchanged.
  - Daniela (engineering attribution): preflight attribution reconciliation per §2a.2 (entry gate before traffic begins); engineering release/rollback posture for any instrumentation touching paid-source routing; runtime attribution reconciliation per §4c with P1 (§3b) as the continuing gate. Preflight is descriptive evidence; P1 is the runtime rule. Owner authority unchanged.
  - Owen: cohort cuts on the paid-source cohort at the post-10-admission gate and at day 90. Methodology consistent with existing cohort work; the running view in §4 and the >90-support-minutes read in §5b follow Owen's 2027-03-29 measurement-operating shape. No new methodology in this draft.
  - Customer Success: hard staffing cap confirmation per §2a.3(a) (25-admission ceiling reaffirmed as a hard staffing cap, no override); from-first-contact recording of support minutes and assisted-route reasons per §2a.3(b); capacity and staffing read for the assisted-path lane carrying paid-source admissions (arithmetic + tradeoff input, not a coverage-adequacy judgment). Owner authority unchanged.

This draft does not solicit approval for any of §1 from these owners; it records the inputs that will be required when those decisions are made.

9. Carried-in posture (preserved verbatim)

  - Paid traffic remains off through 2027-03-31.
  - This is a development draft, not an approved launch plan. Only proposal development is authorized (§1 row 9).
  - Helio Start remains organic through 2027-03-31.
  - Later commercial or launch decisions require separate approval and are outside this draft.
  - Batch start date, gate cadence, and go/no-go review date are specified in the (separate, future, not-yet-approved) launch plan, not in this draft.

10. Open items for the next iteration (not decisions; just unresolved items)

  - Lifecycle preflight universe (§2a.1): exact enumeration of lifecycle branches / holds / suppressions to be evidenced before traffic. Owner: Ines. Confirmation needed before launch plan.
  - Preflight case set (§2a.2): exact list of preflight cases (test accounts or replayed historical events) and the branch-coverage target (organic-equivalent / refuse / hold / admit-then-route / admit-then-abandon / assisted-routing paths). Owner: Daniela. Confirmation needed before launch plan.
  - Assisted-route reason taxonomy (§2a.3(b)): exact reason categories to be recorded at every assisted-routing decision from first contact. Must not change assisted-routing rules. Owner: CS with Daniela. Confirmation needed before launch plan.
  - First-contact definition edge cases (§2a.3(b)): any out-of-band contact channels (e.g., direct outreach, partner-driven inquiries) and whether they count as first contact. Owner: CS. To be specified before launch plan.
  - Preflight archive retention (§2a.1, §2a.2, §2a.3): retention period for preflight evidence alongside the fixed admitted cohort (§4e). Default candidate: cohort lifetime. Confirmation needed before launch plan.
  - Preflight sign-off format (§2a): the form of written sign-off required before traffic begins (e.g., per-owner written sign-off vs. single consolidated sign-off). Owner: Riley to coordinate with Ines, Daniela, CS. To be specified before launch plan.
  - Exact attribution join key for end-to-end reconciliation (§4c). Candidate: existing account-level key. Confirmation needed before launch plan.
  - Reporting cadence for §2 close-trigger tally, §4 four-count running view, §4d day-7 leading indicator, §5a support-pause readout, and §5b M1/M2 number-and-share readout. Default candidate: standard cadence; confirmation needed before launch plan.
  - Definition of "support pause day" for §5a (which throttling states count). To be specified before launch plan; not in this draft.
  - Whether the >90 account-level-support-minute threshold in §5b uses the existing support-effort unit (per §6c) on the same per-account basis. To be confirmed before launch plan; not in this draft.
  - Whether day-7 first integration in §4d is sourced from the same instrumentation as the day-90 mature-outcome reads, or from a separate leading-indicator pipeline. To be confirmed before launch plan; not in this draft.
  - Confirmation of the §1 owner column for each row before any pre-launch review.

Scope: every input on the approved public-path admission checklist as of 2024-04-23, plus the connector-access input that was added to the checklist later. The connector-access input is recorded separately here because it joined the checklist after the original approval.

- Refusal input
- External-authority input
- Lifecycle input
- Instrumentation input
- Support-routing input
- Connector-access input (added to the checklist later; see lineage note below)

- The original approved public-path admission checklist (as of 2024-04-23) did not include connector-access as a separate input.
- Connector-access was added to the checklist after 2024-04-23 as its own distinct input, alongside the six original inputs.
- An admitted case on or after the connector-access addition must have all seven inputs present.

- Case A1 (admitted). Eligibility: present. Refusal: present. External-authority: present. Lifecycle: present. Instrumentation: present. Support-routing: present. Connector-access: present. Outcome: admitted.

Non-admitted cases (one per individual missing input; inputs are not combined into a single case):
- Case N1 (non-admitted, eligibility input missing). Eligibility: missing. Refusal: present. External-authority: present. Lifecycle: present. Instrumentation: present. Support-routing: present. Connector-access: present. Outcome: not admitted — missing eligibility input.
- Case N2 (non-admitted, refusal input missing). Eligibility: present. Refusal: missing. External-authority: present. Lifecycle: present. Instrumentation: present. Support-routing: present. Connector-access: present. Outcome: not admitted — missing refusal input.
- Case N3 (non-admitted, external-authority input missing). Eligibility: present. Refusal: present. External-authority: missing. Lifecycle: present. Instrumentation: present. Support-routing: present. Connector-access: present. Outcome: not admitted — missing external-authority input.
- Case N4 (non-admitted, lifecycle input missing). Eligibility: present. Refusal: present. External-authority: present. Lifecycle: missing. Instrumentation: present. Support-routing: present. Connector-access: present. Outcome: not admitted — missing lifecycle input.
- Case N5 (non-admitted, instrumentation input missing). Eligibility: present. Refusal: present. External-authority: present. Lifecycle: present. Instrumentation: missing. Support-routing: present. Connector-access: present. Outcome: not admitted — missing instrumentation input.
- Case N6 (non-admitted, support-routing input missing). Eligibility: present. Refusal: present. External-authority: present. Lifecycle: present. Instrumentation: present. Support-routing: missing. Connector-access: present. Outcome: not admitted — missing support-routing input.
- Case N7 (non-admitted, connector-access input missing). Eligibility: present. Refusal: present. External-authority: present. Lifecycle: present. Instrumentation: present. Support-routing: present. Connector-access: missing. Outcome: not admitted — missing connector-access input.

Card boundaries:
- This card is a historical baseline only. It does not authorize, modify, or waive any current Helio Start admission rule.
- The seven inputs above are recorded as the inputs present on the approved public-path admission checklist plus the later connector-access addition; do not read this card as a current rule set.
- Each non-admitted case isolates exactly one missing input. Two missing inputs are not combined into a single case in this card.

arguments.body:
# Quarterly board operating evidence intake — Q1 2026

Working pre-read for the January 6, 2026 prep review (1:00–2:00pm Central) and the downstream Q1 source-lock / final-claims-review sequence.
Attendees (Jan 6 review): Riley Tanaka, Priya (lead), Owen, Ines, Daniela.

## Ownership (locked, applies to all sections below)

- Riley Tanaka — recurring operating-evidence ownership begins January 1, 2026.
- Marcus Vail — retains forecast ownership. None of the four sections below feed his forecast.
- Tomás Vega — retains the final board narrative. Final claim owner on each section below.

## How to use this pre-read

Per the 12/10/25 deck rule, Helio Start, retained-mid Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and system controls stay SEPARATE — do not combine, do not cross-reference fields between sections.

After the Jan 6 prep review, the Q1 board operating-evidence sequence is locked in two stages:
- **Q1 board operating-evidence source lock** — March 16, 2026, 10:00–11:00am Central. Locks the inputs that downstream claims are allowed to cite.
- **Q1 board operating-evidence final claims review** — March 24, 2026, 1:00–2:00pm Central. Final pass before Tomás takes the board narrative.

## Row-shape decision (locked at the Jan 6 prep review)

Every row below carries the 11-field intake order plus an explicit row-level **readiness status**. There are two row shapes:

**Customer-outcome rows** — Helio Start, Expansion Assist (retained-mid), Pricing-page path quality. Must name:
- a denominator,
- cohort dates,
- a complete predeclared outcome window (not partial, not extrapolated).

**Continuous-control rows** — System controls. Must name:
- exact coverage dates,
- outcome-window field set to `not applicable — continuous control coverage`.

**Required inputs on every row, regardless of shape:**
measurement limits, exclusions, source owner, source or release-reliability evidence, revenue and forecast treatment, and final claim owner. Lifecycle limits live INLINE on each row (per Ines at the Jan 6 prep review) — not in a shared note. Any row missing a required input remains `not board-ready`.

Per Daniela's ruling at the Jan 6 prep review: continuous system-control coverage cannot truthfully be labeled as a predeclared customer-outcome window, so System controls is always a continuous-control row. Per Owen's ruling at the Jan 6 prep review: customer-motion rows (Helio Start, Expansion Assist, pricing-page) require complete cohort windows — partial-window extrapolation is not permitted. Per Ines's ruling at the Jan 6 prep review: lifecycle limits stay attached to the individual claim they constrain rather than living in a shared note.

## Readiness status — per section

Each section has an independent readiness status. A status of `board-ready` requires every required input on every row in that section to be filled in.

- **Helio Start:** `not board-ready — first mature cohort (post-Dec packet) certified by Owen + CS on 2026-01-27 after Riley's Tue 1:1 with Owen; satisfies both paid-acq-reopen evidence conditions, but source packet does not state cohort dates and a second consecutive qualifying cohort plus a separate budget decision are still required. Continuing boundary: Helio Start remains organic-only through 2026-03-31; no paid traffic, pipeline target, or forecast credit authorized.`
- **Expansion Assist (retained-mid):** `[readiness status — confirm at source lock on March 16, 2026]`
- **Pricing-page path quality:** `[readiness status — confirm at source lock on March 16, 2026]`
- **System controls (CS auto-nudge system controls):** `[readiness status — confirm at source lock on March 16, 2026]`

The 11-field intake order, applied in this exact sequence within each section:

  1. Evidence lane
  2. Proposed claim
  3. Denominator
  4. Cohort or coverage dates
  5. Predeclared outcome window and completion status
  6. Measurement limits
  7. Exclusions
  8. Source owner
  9. Source or release-reliability evidence
 10. Revenue and forecast treatment
 11. Final claim owner

---

## 1. Helio Start (customer-outcome row)

### Certified first mature cohort — 2026-01-27 (post-Dec packet)

Certified by Owen and Customer Success after Riley's Tuesday 1:1 with Owen, on 2026-01-27. This is the first consecutive mature cohort since the December packet to satisfy both evidence conditions for potentially reopening the capped paid-acquisition proposal.

**Cohort composition (workspace-level, day-90 window complete):**
- Admitted workspaces with a complete day-90 window: **86**
- Paid-active: **66**
- Canceled: **10**
- Past due: **6**
- Billing hold: **4**

**Cash read:**
- Gross billed cash: **$100,840**
- Refund-adjusted collected cash: **$94,760**

**Account-level support effort:**
- Median: **19 minutes**
- 90th percentile: **84 minutes**
- Accounts exceeding 90 support minutes: **4 of 86 (4.7%)**

**Unsupported-case gate:**
- Unsupported case admitted into the admitted path: **0** (none).

**Paid-acq-reopen gate status — 1 of 2:**
- This cohort is the **first consecutive mature cohort** to satisfy both conditions of the capped paid-acq reopen rule (mature cohort + <5% of accounts over 90 support minutes + no unsupported case in the admitted path).
- A **second consecutive qualifying cohort** is still required.
- A **separate budget decision** is still required. The two-step gate (evidence × 2 consecutive cohorts + budget approval) is not yet met.
- No paid-acquisition, pipeline, or forecast action is authorized by this certification.

**Limitation carried into the row:**
- The source packet does **not** state cohort dates. Until cohort dates are supplied and locked, the Helio Start row remains `not board-ready` per Owen's Jan 6 ruling (customer-motion rows require complete cohort windows; partial-window extrapolation is not permitted).

**Continuing boundary (unchanged):**
- Helio Start remains **organic-only through 2026-03-31**. No paid traffic, no pipeline target, and no forecast credit are authorized. This boundary holds regardless of the 1-of-2 gate progress.

---

1. **Evidence lane:** Organic activation signals within Helio Start's bounded window. The Jan 27, 2026 certified first mature cohort (post-Dec packet) is recorded as the first consecutive mature cohort satisfying the capped paid-acq reopen evidence conditions; it does not by itself authorize paid acquisition, a pipeline target, or forecast credit.
2. **Proposed claim:** Helio Start delivers organic activation uplift within its declared bounded scope. The certified Jan 27, 2026 cohort is one of two consecutive qualifying cohorts required before a capped paid-acquisition proposal can potentially reopen, and only after a separate budget decision.
3. **Denominator:** Organic-start signups in the coverage window (paid acquisition explicitly out of denominator). For the Jan 27, 2026 certified cohort: 86 admitted workspaces with a complete day-90 window.
4. **Cohort dates:** `Not stated in the source packet — supplied at certification but not recorded in the packet. Row remains not board-ready on this input until cohort dates are locked at source lock on March 16, 2026. Per Owen's Jan 6 ruling, partial-window extrapolation is not permitted, so the window cannot be back-filled from the day-90 maturity alone.`
5. **Predeclared outcome window and completion status:** `Day-90 window is the predeclared outcome window for mature cohorts. The Jan 27, 2026 certified cohort's day-90 window is complete for all 86 admitted workspaces (66 paid-active, 10 canceled, 6 past due, 4 on billing hold). Window-completion status is established; cohort-dates input is still missing from the source packet and is the blocker on readiness, not window completion itself.`
6. **Measurement limits (lifecycle limits attached to this row, not shared):** Bounded organic scope only. No paid-acq interpretation. No pipeline reading. Lifecycle-touch scope on this row follows the conservative, non-state-changing fork (no state-changing sends into the Helio Start cohort) and the fork boundary from sub-50 to mid-seg stays a documented state — same event, same threshold, same QA tier per send. **Jan 27, 2026 certified-cohort gate:** (i) <5% of accounts over 90 support minutes — 4.7% satisfied; (ii) no unsupported case admitted into the admitted path — 0 satisfied. Both conditions met for the first consecutive mature cohort since the December packet; the second consecutive qualifying cohort is still required. The Jan 27, 2026 certification does not relax any prior limit on this row.
7. **Exclusions:** Paid acquisition, pipeline metrics, forecast inputs, any non-organic attribution. Combined/co-mingled claims across surfaces (deck rule 12/10/25). Lifecycle copy that would imply anything in the not-supported list (manual billing help, import help, pricing-page exposure, paid acquisition, GA/launch language). **Jan 27, 2026 certified cohort specifically excludes:** any inference that the 1-of-2 gate progress authorizes paid traffic, a pipeline target, or forecast credit; any read of the certified figures as a budget decision (the budget decision remains separate); any read that a single qualifying cohort is sufficient (the second consecutive qualifying cohort is still required).
8. **Source owner:** `[Product/release lead — Daniela or designee, to be confirmed at Jan 6 review.]` For the Jan 27, 2026 certified cohort: Owen (extract owner) and Customer Success (joint certification after Riley's Tue 1:1 with Owen).
9. **Source or release-reliability evidence:** Bounded organic scope confirmed through 2026-03-31; no paid-acq path open. **Jan 27, 2026 certified cohort evidence:** 86 admitted workspaces / 66 paid-active / 10 canceled / 6 past due / 4 billing hold; $100,840 gross billed / $94,760 refund-adjusted collected; 19-min median / 84-min p90 account-level support effort; 4 of 86 (4.7%) over 90 support minutes; 0 unsupported case admitted. Source packet does not state cohort dates — recorded as a limitation on this row.
10. **Revenue and forecast treatment:** Does NOT feed Marcus Vail's forecast. Excluded from revenue modeling. **Jan 27, 2026 certified cohort:** refund-adjusted collected cash ($94,760) is a Helio Start lane read and is NOT a revenue, pipeline, or forecast input. No forecast credit is authorized by the 1-of-2 gate progress.
11. **Final claim owner:** Tomás Vega.
**Row readiness:** `not board-ready — pending cohort-dates input (source packet does not state cohort dates) and pending the second consecutive qualifying cohort and a separate budget decision before any capped paid-acq reopen could be considered. Continuing boundary unchanged: Helio Start remains organic-only through 2026-03-31.`

---

## 2. Expansion Assist (retained-mid) (customer-outcome row)

1. **Evidence lane:** Descriptive evidence for retained-mid Expansion Assist across the two bounded first pilots. Routine vs. disputed/cross-surface/exec split is preserved. Evidence is descriptive and noncausal — it reports what customers "selected," "showed," and "were observed" doing inside the bounded pilots. No randomized control. No implied counterfactual.

2. **Proposed claim:** Expansion Assist operates descriptively on routine cases; disputed, cross-surface, and exec cases retain line-level treatment. The lane is descriptive-only across both pilots — it does not claim to have driven, caused, or prevented retention, expansion, or revenue, and it is NOT a revenue, pipeline, forecast, or paid-acquisition input.

3. **Denominator (per cohort AND combined — kept separate):**
   - **Bounded first pilot (cohort 1) denominator:** 30 actual exposures. Entry condition used in cohort 1: older ceiling event allowed (no 14-day recency rule). 18 of the 30 cohort-1 exposures had an older ceiling event at entry.
   - **Bounded second pilot (cohort 2) denominator:** 13 actual exposures. Entry condition used in cohort 2: 14-day "ceiling newly crossed" recency rule applied.

session_search.description: Recall past conversations: search or read old Hermes sessions (FTS5), or scroll inside one. Four shapes, picked by args: `query` = discovery (top-N matching sessions, top result fully hydrated); `session_id` + `around_message_id` = scroll (window of messages around an anchor); `session_id` alone = read a whole session — how you resolve an `@session:<profile>/<id>` link (split on '/' into profile + id); no args = browse recent sessions. Results are actual DB messages, no LLM. Searches conversation history ONLY — when the user gave a direct source (URL, file, contact, live system), inspect that first; never conclude 'not found' from history alone. Use for questions about past conversations: 'what did we do about X', 'where did we leave Y'. When referring the user to a session, write its `link` value verbatim inline (it renders as a titled link).

query.description: Search query (discovery shape). Keywords, phrases, or boolean expressions to find in past sessions. Omit to browse recent sessions. Ignored when session_id + around_message_id are set (scroll shape).

limit.description: Discovery shape only. Max sessions to return (default 3, max 10). Bump to 5–10 when the topic likely spans several sessions and you want to pick the right one to scroll into.

sort.description: Discovery shape only. Temporal bias on top of FTS5 ranking: omit for relevance-only (exploratory recall), 'newest' for "where did we leave X", 'oldest' for "how did X start".

detail.description: Discovery shape only. 'adaptive' (default) fully hydrates the top-ranked result and returns only the exact anchor message for lower-ranked results. 'full' returns bookends and the complete anchored window for every result.

session_id.description: Scroll shape. Session to read inside. Use the session_id returned from a prior discovery call. Must be paired with around_message_id.

around_message_id.description: Scroll shape. Message id to center the window on — use match_message_id from a discovery result, or any id from a prior window.

window.description: Scroll shape only. Messages to return on each side of the anchor (anchor itself always included). Clamped to [1, 20]. Default 5.

role_filter.description: Optional. Comma-separated roles to include. Discovery defaults to 'user,assistant' (tool output is usually noise). Pass 'user,assistant,tool' to include tool output (debugging tool behaviour) or 'tool' to search tool output only.

profile.description: Optional. Read sessions from another Hermes profile's database (read-only). Use when resolving an `@session:<profile>/<id>` link: pass the profile segment here with session_id as the id segment. Omit to use the current profile.
