tests.request: Create a reusable readiness checklist for any 2028 Helio Start paid-acquisition proposal. State the mature evidence required before budget or channel tactics can be discussed, how the evidence must be combined, and the approved responsibility for the package. Do not invent separate owners for individual evidence categories.

input.body:
2028 HELIO START — PAID-ACQUISITION PROPOSAL READINESS CHECKLIST
Reusable. Resets per proposal. Apply before any budget, channel, or audience tactic is discussed.

SUM
Mature evidence first. One owner per proposal. Evidence reconciles to the paid-source convention before budget or channel tactics enter the room.

SCOPE
Every 2028 Helio Start paid-acquisition proposal that proposes a budget, channel mix, or audience target. Not transferable between proposals.

MATURE EVIDENCE REQUIRED (all four, reconciled)

1. Cohort cuts, read-locked first.
   Mid-segment cuts with Owen; Monday cohort as the baseline. Admit, assist, and ineligible kept as separate counts — not collapsed into admissions or activations.

2. Paid-source convention applied.
   `conversions` is the paid-platform source label, not a funnel stage. 19 marks where the paid-source eligibility flow starts. Cohort cuts restated under this convention before they enter the proposal.

3. Pre-launch QA on file.
   Staging run first; isolated campaign at $0; no eligibility-flow entry; Daniela acknowledgement recorded. A `paused` state does not substitute — it is treated as a V11 bypass.

4. CS coverage matched to the live window.
   8a–6p Central is the baseline. Any off-hours exposure is stated inside the proposal, not deferred.

HOW THE EVIDENCE IS COMBINED
The four pieces land as one package, in this order: cohort cuts → convention reconciliation → QA sign-off → coverage confirmation. The package is treated as a single artifact. No piece is cited standalone. If the four contradict each other, the proposal returns to cohort cuts — it is not patched at the tactical layer.

APPROVED RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE PACKAGE
One owner of record per proposal, named at intake. That owner carries the package end-to-end: cohort cuts, convention reconciliation, QA sign-off, coverage confirmation, and the tactical proposal that follows. Per-evidence owners are not assigned. Priya routes the proposal into #growth-investigations; the named owner runs it.

GATE
Budget, channel, or audience tactics are not discussed until all four evidence pieces are mature and reconciled. The gate is the owner's call, not a committee.

ANTI-PATTERNS (do not do)
- Per-row ownership across the four evidence categories.
- Citing one evidence piece without the other three.
- Treating a `paused` campaign as QA sign-off.
- Collapsing admit/assist/ineligible into a single admissions or activations count.
- Starting tactical discussion before the package is reconciled.

arguments.body:
Riley Tanaka — 2026 year-end self-review working draft
Cycle: 2026 year-end · Reviewer: Priya · Working draft (not for distribution)
Shape: summary first, then four required evidence sections with transitions, plus a short closing. Compresses to the 1-pager (why / cuts / what I did / effect / call) without restructuring.

SUMMARY

The year's spine is claim-boundary discipline held under pressure. Q1 and Q2 cohort windows stayed on the published dates; §3 admission rules and the §4.8-style pipeline/forecast exclusion did not get compressed into a partial-window claim. The Helio Start paid cohort closed at $14,420 / 50 admits; on Aug 21 I recommended — and Priya accepted — no second Q3 batch and no pipeline or forecast credit, with a binding future-paid case-review gate now in force. A delegation rhythm took shape: Owen owns the monthly sanitized campaign snapshot and the source-completeness review pathway as an evaluation framework, while I retain board readiness, causal and revenue claims, forecast treatment, executive language, and exception authority. I have not stopped routine monthly preparation or source-closure reviews — both still flow through me as exception review. The Oct 14 authority-checklist review closed clean and descriptive; the metric surfaces (admission, activation, checklist exposure, support minutes) remain split.

1. Q1 AND Q2 CLAIM BOUNDARIES — HELD

This is the year's first defended boundary and the lens for everything that follows. The published constraints were the §3 admission rules and the §4.8-style pipeline/forecast exclusion; Q1 dates were 4/7, and Q2 was not board-ready until mature claim windows completed. Under pressure to compress, I refused to roll the day-7 first-integration read (39/50, leading only) into acquisition, scale, pipeline, or forecast, and held the day-90 decision for closed day-90 windows. The four-part output discipline (classification / alignment / consequence / routing) held on operator-facing references and on my own claim-side framing, and the §3 / §4.8 cannot-be-weakened framing stayed the rule any future proposal must satisfy. No claim was advanced on a partial-window basis; no pipeline or forecast credit was granted against Q1 or Q2 cohort outcomes; the five Helio Start states stayed separate from Starter / retained-mid-segment in every readout. Keep citing this as the spine.

2. CLOSED HELIO START PAID COHORT — NO SECOND BATCH, NO PIPELINE/FORECAST CREDIT

If §1 is the lens, this is the most pressured case it had to survive. The approved pilot was high-intent paid search, mid-segment-fit only, 6-week max window, capped at the earlier of $15,000 spent or 50 admitted workspaces. Stop/pause triggers (any one): unsupported-in-admitted, reconciliation failure across eligibility → admit → assisted, or ≥20 admitted if >10% showed >90 support minutes per account.

On Aug 17 the source-completeness certification packet (Owen + Customer Success) assigned mutually exclusive day-90 statuses to all 50 workspaces — 37 paid-active, 6 canceled, 4 past due, 3 billing hold — with $60,480 gross billed cash, $56,230 refund-adjusted collected cash, 26-minute median and 104-minute p90 account-level support effort, 7 of 50 (14%) over 90 support minutes, and end-to-end reconciliation of paid-source attribution for all 50. No unsupported applicant entered the admitted path. I treated the packet as descriptive paid-source evidence only — explicitly not causal acquisition, not scale, not pipeline, not forecast — because there was no randomized control. On Aug 21 the second-batch decision review recommended, and Priya accepted, no second Helio Start paid batch in Q3 and no Q4 forecast treatment for the cohort. Paid traffic remains off.

The future-paid gate is binding: Owen + Customer Success classify each of the seven high-support workspaces into (a) external-authority action, (b) ordinary integration, (c) billing, or (d) another named supported cause; Ines + Daniela determine whether each case concerns state meaning, routing, and/or setup sequence; any future paid proposal accounts for all seven (prevented, mitigated, or bounded — not merely listed) without weakening §3 or §4.8. The cohort is fixed at 50; no pipeline or forecast credit has been granted. The gate is the structural artifact; the day-90 numbers are evidence inside it.

3. OWEN'S MONTHLY-PREP TRANSITION + BOUNDED SOURCE-CLOSURE AUTHORITY (INCL. OCT 14 REVIEW)

The delegation rhythm is what let the boundary in §2 hold without my being on every line. First, the monthly sanitized campaign snapshot landed as exception-summary only; the first post-handoff on Jul 2 covered 135 campaigns with status and owner rows and owner lanes intact, and resolved three Q2 opens (Ines owner-change verified, Maya snapshot-only, Owen denominator). Second, the source-completeness review pathway defined on Jul 29 — Owen's audit covers eight fields per row (denominator and exact coverage dates; outcome window; measurement limits; exclusions; single named source owner per surface; reliability evidence; revenue and forecast treatment with the handoff note "source certified by Owen; call retained by Riley"; and a section certifier with named backup). The graduation criterion is three consecutive packets with all eight fields complete, a named certifier per section, zero disputed-semantics reopens, zero cross-surface owner drift, exceptions surfaced within one business day of source release with the gap named, reliability evidence reproducible from source on first request, and denominator/coverage dates reconciling against the prior packet's exit state. Escalation triggers remain: any missing field escalates; disputed semantics or cross-surface discrepancy escalates rather than resolving in packet; causal, revenue, forecast, or executive-language content escalates to me by default; two consecutive packets with the same exception type trigger formal review of the pathway, not a third packet.

On Oct 14 the authority-checklist review closed. Owen and Customer Success supplied a clean descriptive four-week operating read on the organic authority-setup checklist shipped on Sep 15. Across the four-week window: 92 admitted organic workspaces in scope, 28 checklist exposures (pre-setup visibility surface only, reported separately from admission and activation outcomes), five ordinary setup-assistance requests handled through the existing assisted-route path; no eligibility or route mismatch, no lifecycle-suppression issue, no paid-source traffic (paid traffic remains off; the cohort is fixed at 50), no unsupported admission, no randomized control. I treated the four-week read as descriptive operating evidence — explicitly not an activation claim and not a support-effort claim. The maintenance split is now explicit and named: Ines owns the state-meaning dimension (lifecycle suppression, governed state, external-authority meaning unchanged); Daniela owns the release-reliability dimension (preflight, connector-specific condition, replay coverage, surfacing any drift on first request); I retain the claim discipline (descriptive-only framing, no read into activation or support effort, no pipeline or forecast credit, §3 / §4.8 reaffirmed as not weakened) and the exception authority whenever a maintenance cycle crosses any escalation trigger above. §8.E and §8.E.3 remain in force unchanged.

What is delegated versus what is mine. Delegated preparation is Owen's monthly sanitized snapshot, the source-completeness review pathway as an evaluation framework, and on the checklist surface the four-week descriptive operating read and the maintenance cycles within the Ines/Daniela/Riley split. Routine source review still comes to me as exception review; I have not left that work, and no new review-closure authority has been granted. Routine monthly preparation still flows through me as exception review; I have not left that work either. What I retain are the claims (causal and revenue), the forecast treatment, the executive language, the descriptive-only discipline on the checklist read, and the exception authority whenever a packet or maintenance cycle crosses any escalation trigger. The transition is routing — line-by-line to exception-summary where clean, descriptive operating read + named maintenance lanes on the checklist — not a handoff of the underlying responsibility, and the underlying responsibility on those streams did not change.

4. ORGANIC AUTHORITY-SETUP CHECKLIST — RELEASED, ELIGIBILITY AND STATE MEANINGS PRESERVED

The same boundary, applied to a release. The approved release was a non-state-changing, connector-specific pre-setup checklist for admitted Helio Start workspaces whose selected connector requires an owner-level permission or a network-allowlist action; release target was the organic Helio Start onboarding path only; eligibility and state meanings had to be preserved; checklist exposure is reported separately from admission and activation outcomes. At the 10:30 release gate on Sep 15, Ines and Daniela completed the 24-case replay and lifecycle preflight. Condition for receiving the checklist: a selected connector requiring an owner-level permission or a network-allowlist action, AND current verified-yes external authority at the moment of replay. Eight of the 24 cases met the condition and received the connector-specific checklist; 16 did not and did not receive it. Every case preserved existing eligibility, route, lifecycle suppression, and governed state. Daniela released the checklist to the organic onboarding path, and Owen began reporting checklist exposure separately from admission and activation outcomes — the rationale being that checklist exposure is a pre-setup visibility surface, not an admission or activation event, and keeping the metric surfaces split preserves the integrity of the admission and activation numbers and prevents the checklist from being read into the §4.8-style pipeline/forecast framing. The §8.E future-paid case-review gate and §8.E.3 proposal precondition remain in force; the checklist release does not weaken, satisfy, or replace any element of §8.E. The checklist is live on the organic path with eligibility and state meanings intact — the cleanest example of the year of shipping a release with every surrounding lever reasserted and §3 + §4.8 reaffirmed as not weakened.

CLOSING

Two development priorities are in flight, and neither implies I have left routine monthly preparation or source-closure reviews. First, bring Owen's source-completeness review pathway to its three-packet graduation criterion — all eight fields, a named certifier per section, the named success criteria — while I remain the routine source-closure reviewer on the underlying stream and the exception reviewer on the pathway itself until the criterion clears; that responsibility is not in scope to delegate until it does. Second, hold the exception-summary monthly snapshot handoff without regression to line-by-line reconciliation, with the leverage goal of making every claim name its denominator and complete predeclared outcome window. To close the deliberate frame for the reviewer: I have not left routine monthly preparation or delegated source-closure reviews; I have not weakened §3 admission rules or the §4.8-style pipeline/forecast exclusion; I have not authorized a second Helio Start paid batch; and I have not turned the Oct 14 four-week descriptive checklist read into an activation or support-effort claim. The boundary held, the rhythm is repeatable, and the underlying responsibility on these streams did not change.

Routing: this doc stays in Growth until edited down to a 1-pager for Priya; until then, no distribution, no Slack reference.

SUMMARY

The spine of the year is claim-boundary discipline held under pressure. Q1 and Q2 cohort windows stayed on the published dates; §3 admission rules and the §4.8-style pipeline/forecast exclusion did not get compressed into a partial-window claim. The Helio Start paid cohort closed at $14,420 / 50 admits; on Aug 21 I recommended — and Priya accepted — no second Q3 batch and no pipeline or forecast credit, with a binding future-paid case-review gate now in force. A delegation rhythm took shape around that boundary: Owen owns the monthly sanitized campaign snapshot and the source-completeness review pathway as an evaluation framework, while I retain board readiness, causal and revenue claims, forecast treatment, executive language, and exception authority. I have not stopped routine monthly preparation or source-closure reviews — both still flow through me as exception review. The Oct 14 authority-checklist review closed clean and descriptive; metric surfaces (admission, activation, checklist exposure, support minutes) remain split.

1. Q1 AND Q2 CLAIM BOUNDARIES — HELD

This is the year's first defended boundary and the lens for everything that follows. The published constraints were the §3 admission rules and the §4.8-style pipeline/forecast exclusion; Q1 dates were 4/7, Q2 not board-ready until mature claim windows completed. Under pressure to compress, I refused to roll the day-7 first-integration read (39/50, leading only) into acquisition, scale, pipeline, or forecast, and held the day-90 decision for closed day-90 windows. The four-part output discipline (classification / alignment / consequence / routing) held on operator-facing references and on my own claim-side framing; the §3 / §4.8 cannot-be-weakened framing stayed the rule any future proposal must satisfy. No claim was advanced on a partial-window basis; no pipeline or forecast credit was granted against Q1 or Q2 cohort outcomes; the five Helio Start states stayed separate from Starter / retained-mid-segment in every readout. Keep citing this as the spine.

2. CLOSED HELIO START PAID COHORT — NO SECOND BATCH, NO PIPELINE/FORECAST CREDIT

If §1 is the lens, this is the most pressured case it had to survive. The approved pilot was high-intent paid search, mid-segment-fit only, 6-week max window, capped at the earlier of $15,000 spent or 50 admitted workspaces; stop/pause triggers (any one): unsupported-in-admitted, reconciliation failure across eligibility → admit → assisted, or ≥20 admitted if >10% showed >90 support minutes per account. On Aug 17 the source-completeness certification packet (Owen + Customer Success) assigned mutually exclusive day-90 statuses to all 50 workspaces — 37 paid-active, 6 canceled, 4 past due, 3 billing hold — with $60,480 gross billed cash, $56,230 refund-adjusted collected cash, 26-minute median and 104-minute p90 account-level support effort, 7 of 50 (14%) over 90 support minutes, and end-to-end reconciliation of paid-source attribution for all 50; no unsupported applicant entered the admitted path. I treated the packet as descriptive paid-source evidence only — explicitly not causal acquisition, not scale, not pipeline, not forecast — because there was no randomized control. On Aug 21 the second-batch decision review recommended, and Priya accepted, no second Helio Start paid batch in Q3 and no Q4 forecast treatment for the cohort; paid traffic remains off.

The future-paid gate is binding: Owen + Customer Success classify each of the seven high-support workspaces into (a) external-authority action, (b) ordinary integration, (c) billing, or (d) another named supported cause; Ines + Daniela determine whether each case concerns state meaning, routing, and/or setup sequence; any future paid proposal accounts for all seven (prevented, mitigated, or bounded — not merely listed) without weakening §3 or §4.8. The cohort is fixed at 50; no pipeline or forecast credit has been granted. The gate is the structural artifact; the day-90 numbers are evidence inside it.

3. OWEN'S MONTHLY-PREP TRANSITION + BOUNDED SOURCE-CLOSURE AUTHORITY (INCL. OCT 14 REVIEW)

The delegation rhythm is what let the boundary in §2 hold without my being on every line. Two changes moved through me. First, the monthly sanitized campaign snapshot landed as exception-summary only; the first post-handoff on Jul 2 covered 135 campaigns with status, owner rows, and owner lanes intact, resolving three Q2 opens (Ines owner-change verified, Maya snapshot-only, Owen denominator). Second, the source-completeness review pathway defined on Jul 29 has Owen's audit covering eight fields per row — denominator and exact coverage dates, outcome window, measurement limits, exclusions, single named source owner per surface, reliability evidence, revenue and forecast treatment with the handoff note "source certified by Owen; call retained by Riley," and a section certifier with named backup — and a graduation criterion of three consecutive packets with all eight fields complete, a named certifier per section, zero disputed-semantics reopens, zero cross-surface owner drift, exceptions surfaced within one business day of source release with the gap named, reliability evidence reproducible from source on first request, and denominator/coverage dates reconciling against the prior packet's exit state. On Oct 14 the authority-checklist review closed. I treated the four-week read as descriptive operating evidence — explicitly not an activation claim and not a support-effort claim. The maintenance split is now explicit and named: Ines owns the state-meaning dimension, Daniela owns the release-reliability dimension, and I retain the claim discipline (descriptive-only framing, no read into activation or support effort, no pipeline or forecast credit, §3 / §4.8 reaffirmed as not weakened) and the exception authority whenever a maintenance cycle crosses any escalation trigger above. §8.E and §8.E.3 remain in force unchanged.

What is delegated versus what is mine. Delegated preparation is Owen's monthly sanitized snapshot, the source-completeness review pathway as an evaluation framework, and on the checklist surface the four-week descriptive operating read and the maintenance cycles within the Ines/Daniela/Riley split. Routine source review still comes to me as exception review; routine monthly preparation still flows through me as exception review; I have not left either work, and no new review-closure authority has been granted. What I retain are the claims (causal and revenue), the forecast treatment, the executive language, the descriptive-only discipline on the checklist read, and the exception authority whenever a packet or maintenance cycle crosses any escalation trigger. The transition is routing, not handoff — the underlying responsibility on those streams did not change.

4. ORGANIC AUTHORITY-SETUP CHECKLIST — RELEASED, ELIGIBILITY AND STATE MEANINGS PRESERVED

The same boundary, applied to a release. The approved release was a non-state-changing, connector-specific pre-setup checklist for admitted Helio Start workspaces whose selected connector requires an owner-level permission or a network-allowlist action; release target was the organic Helio Start onboarding path only; eligibility and state meanings had to be preserved; checklist exposure is reported separately from admission and activation outcomes. At the 10:30 release gate on Sep 15, Ines and Daniela completed the 24-case replay and lifecycle preflight. Condition for receiving the checklist: a selected connector requiring an owner-level permission or a network-allowlist action, AND current verified-yes external authority at the moment of replay. Eight of the 24 cases met the condition and received the connector-specific checklist; 16 did not and did not receive it. Every case preserved existing eligibility, route, lifecycle suppression, and governed state. Daniela released the checklist to the organic onboarding path, and Owen began reporting checklist exposure separately from admission and activation outcomes — the rationale being that checklist exposure is a pre-setup visibility surface, not an admission or activation event, and keeping the metric surfaces split preserves the integrity of the admission and activation numbers and prevents the checklist from being read into the §4.8-style pipeline/forecast framing. The checklist is live on the organic path with eligibility and state meanings intact — the cleanest example of the year of shipping a release with every surrounding lever reasserted and §3 + §4.8 reaffirmed as not weakened.

CLOSING

Two development priorities are in flight, and neither implies I have left routine monthly preparation or source-closure reviews. First, bring Owen's source-completeness review pathway to its three-packet graduation criterion — all eight fields, a named certifier per section, the named success criteria — while I remain the routine source-closure reviewer on the underlying stream and the exception reviewer on the pathway itself until the criterion clears; that responsibility is not in scope to delegate until it does. Second, hold the exception-summary monthly snapshot handoff without regression to line-by-line reconciliation, with the leverage goal of making every claim name its denominator and complete predeclared outcome window. To close the deliberate frame for the reviewer: I have not left routine monthly preparation or delegated source-closure reviews; I have not weakened §3 admission rules or the §4.8-style pipeline/forecast exclusion; I have not authorized a second Helio Start paid batch; and I have not turned the Oct 14 four-week descriptive checklist read into an activation or support-effort claim. The boundary held, the rhythm is repeatable, and the underlying responsibility on these streams did not change.

Read: Priya, 10/11/27 11:40am CT — does the 10/4 source-certification-delay synthesis count as the first of Owen's three Q4 development-cycle examples.

The synthesis demonstrates four pieces of source-completeness lane discipline:

  - Correct exception classification (source-certification delay, not missing-data, not cross-surface, not disputed-semantics, not no-exception).
  - Snapshot visibly incomplete held — not papered over with a substitute status.
  - No stale data substituted.
  - Closure completed only after certification arrived 10/5 9am CT, with the delay preserved in the closure summary.

The key constraint: the closure summary preserves the delay. That means the closure is *not* an exception-free packet under the three-packet graduation criterion — the source-completeness review pathway defined 7/29 requires "zero disputed-semantics reopens... exceptions surfaced within one business day of source release with the gap named." A preserved-delay closure does not satisfy that bar.

So the answer depends on what bar Priya is using:

  - Under the three-packet graduation criterion (clean closures, all eight fields complete + named certifier per section + zero preserved exceptions): the October synthesis does **not** count as one of three. The delay is in the record. Owen's three under that bar have to come from exception-free closures elsewhere in Q4 — i.e., one was October, and if October itself doesn't count, then November and December plus whatever still lands in October is the only path. (And per the feedback working notes, "one packet is not the three-packet graduation criterion" is the standing framing — the prior 11/6 closure was inside the bounded source-completeness lane but not a graduation event for the same reason.)
  - Under "three demonstrations of source-completeness discipline in Q4": the October synthesis **does** count, and counts strongly. Correct classification, visibly-incomplete held, no stale substitution, delay preserved in closure — that is exactly the discipline the 9/24 ruling bounded Owen to. This is the strongest kind of evidence that the source-completeness lane is operating as designed.

The framing matters because if Priya is using the graduation-criterion bar, the answer to her is *no* and the October synthesis should be cited as a discipline example, not a graduation event. If she's using the discipline-demonstration bar, the answer is *yes* and the October synthesis is the cleanest of the three by virtue of having gone through an exception correctly.

My read: Priya's phrasing — "three Q4 development-cycle examples" rather than "three clean closures" or "three graduation packets" — leans toward the discipline-demonstration reading. But it's ambiguous enough that I would not commit either way without asking.

Three options for what to do next:

  1. Reply to Priya with the clarifying question: which bar — clean closures under the 7/29 graduation criterion, or demonstrations of source-completeness discipline — is the count she's running?
  2. Reply with both readings laid out and let her pick, while flagging that under the strict graduation-criterion bar the October synthesis does not count.

arguments.body:
Riley Tanaka — 2026 year-end self-review working draft
Cycle: 2026 year-end · Reviewer: Priya · Working draft (not for distribution)
Shape: summary first, then four evidence sections plus a closing paragraph, written as prose for editing down to the 1-pager (why / cuts / what I did / effect / call).

SUMMARY

I held the claim-boundary discipline across the year: Q1 and Q2 cohort windows stayed on the published dates, and the §3 admission rules plus the §4.8-style pipeline/forecast exclusion held through every pressure point without being compressed into a partial-window claim. I closed the Helio Start paid cohort at $14,420 / 50 admits, and on Aug 21 recommended — and Priya accepted — no second Q3 batch and no pipeline or forecast credit for the cohort; a binding future-paid case-review gate is now in force. I built a delegation rhythm in which Owen owns the monthly sanitized campaign snapshot and the source-completeness review pathway as an evaluation framework, and on November 6 Owen independently closed the 9/24 source-completeness packet covering 7/1–10/31 with certifications complete — the cleanest concrete leadership-through-delegation example of the year. I retain board readiness, causal and revenue claims, forecast treatment, executive language, and exception authority, and I have not stopped routine monthly preparation or source-closure reviews, both of which still flow through me as exception review. The Oct 14 authority-checklist review closed with Owen and Customer Success supplying a clean descriptive four-week operating read; I kept the checklist in organic onboarding without turning the counts into an activation or support-effort claim, and I set an explicit maintenance split among Ines, Daniela, and me. No 2027 role change has been requested or approved.

1. Q1 AND Q2 CLAIM BOUNDARIES — HELD

The published constraints were the §3 admission rules (eligibility, refusal, connector access, external authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, support routing) and the §4.8-style pipeline/forecast exclusion. Q1 dates were 4/7; Q2 was not board-ready until mature claim windows completed. Forecast and pipeline received no credit on partial-window evidence, and a mature claim required complete observation windows.

Under pressure to compress, I refused to roll the day-7 first-integration read (39/50, leading only) into acquisition, scale, pipeline, or forecast, and I held the day-90 decision for closed day-90 windows. I kept the four-part output discipline (classification / alignment / consequence / routing) on operator-facing references and on my own claim-side framing, and I held the §3 / §4.8 cannot-be-weakened framing as the rule any future proposal must satisfy.

The effect: Q1 and Q2 board segments stayed on the published dates, no claim was advanced on a partial-window basis, no pipeline or forecast credit was granted against Q1 or Q2 cohort outcomes, and the structural discipline keeping the five Helio Start states separate from Starter / retained-mid-segment in every readout held. Call: keep citing this as the spine of the year's evidence — the mature-window-only claim discipline plus §3 / §4.8 not weakened is the defended boundary.

2. CLOSED HELIO START PAID COHORT — NO SECOND BATCH, NO PIPELINE/FORECAST CREDIT

The approved pilot was high-intent paid search, mid-segment-fit only, 6-week max window, capped at the earlier of $15,000 spent or 50 admitted workspaces; the $8K / 25 fallback was never approved. Stop / pause triggers (any one): unsupported-in-admitted; reconciliation failure across eligibility → admit → assisted; or ≥20 admitted if >10% showed >90 support minutes per account. The day-7 read of 39/50 first-integration-by-day-7 was leading only, not mature.

On Aug 17 the source-completeness certification packet (Owen + Customer Success) assigned mutually exclusive day-90 statuses to all 50 workspaces — 37 paid-active, 6 canceled, 4 past due, 3 billing hold — with $60,480 gross billed cash, $56,230 refund-adjusted collected cash, 26-minute median and 104-minute p90 account-level support effort, 7 of 50 (14%) exceeding 90 support minutes, and end-to-end reconciliation of paid-source attribution for all 50. No unsupported applicant entered the admitted path. I treated the packet as descriptive paid-source evidence only — explicitly not causal acquisition, not scale, not pipeline, not forecast — because there was no randomized control. On Aug 21 the second-batch decision review recommended, and Priya accepted, no second Helio Start paid batch in Q3 and no Q4 forecast treatment for the cohort. Paid traffic remains off.

The future-paid gate is now binding: Owen + Customer Success must classify each of the seven high-support workspaces into (a) external-authority action, (b) ordinary integration, (c) billing, or (d) another supported cause (named explicitly; "unclassified" is not a supported bucket); Ines + Daniela must determine whether each case concerns state meaning, routing, and / or setup sequence (multiple dimensions may apply, each named); and any future paid proposal must account for all seven cases (state how each is prevented, mitigated, or bounded — not merely listed) without weakening §3 or §4.8.

The cohort is fixed at 50; paid traffic is off; no second Q3 paid batch is in flight; the cohort carries no pipeline or forecast credit. Call: the case-review gate is the structural artifact of the year — the day-90 numbers are evidence inside it, not the artifact itself.

3. OWEN'S MONTHLY-PREP TRANSITION + BOUNDED SOURCE-CLOSURE AUTHORITY

Two changes moved through me. The first was the monthly sanitized campaign snapshot landing as exception-summary only; the first post-handoff on Jul 2 covered 135 campaigns with status and owner rows and owner lanes intact, and resolved three Q2 opens (Ines owner-change verified, Maya snapshot-only, Owen denominator). The second was the source-completeness review pathway defined on Jul 29 — Owen's audit covers eight fields per row (denominator and exact coverage dates; outcome window; measurement limits; exclusions; single named source owner per surface; reliability evidence; revenue and forecast treatment with the explicit handoff note "source certified by Owen; call retained by Riley"; and a section certifier with named backup). The observable success criteria are three consecutive packets with all eight fields complete and a named certifier per section, zero disputed-semantics reopens, zero cross-surface owner drift, exceptions surfaced within one business day of source release with the gap named, reliability evidence reproducible from source on first request, and denominator / coverage dates reconciling against the prior packet's exit state.

Escalation triggers are unchanged: any missing field makes the packet incomplete and escalates; disputed semantics or cross-surface discrepancy escalates rather than resolving in packet; any causal, revenue, forecast, or executive-language content escalates to me by default; and two consecutive packets with the same exception type trigger formal review of the pathway, not a third packet.

3f. October 14 authority-checklist review — four-week operating read, descriptive only

On October 14 the authority-checklist review closed. Owen and Customer Success supplied a clean descriptive four-week operating read on the organic authority-setup checklist shipped on Sep 15. Across the four-week window: 92 admitted organic workspaces in scope; 28 checklist exposures (pre-setup visibility surface only, reported separately from admission and activation outcomes); five ordinary setup-assistance requests handled through the existing assisted-route path. The review surfaced no eligibility or route mismatch, no lifecycle-suppression issue, no paid-source traffic (paid traffic remains off; the Helio Start paid cohort is fixed at 50), no unsupported admission, and no randomized control. I treated the four-week read as descriptive operating evidence — explicitly not an activation claim and not a support-effort claim — because the counts are pre-setup visibility and assisted-route support requests on an organic-only surface, not activation outcomes, and there is no control arm. The checklist stays in organic onboarding, and the metric surfaces (admission, activation, checklist exposure, support minutes) remain split.

The maintenance split is now explicit and named: Ines owns the state-meaning dimension (lifecycle suppression, governed state, external-authority meaning unchanged); Daniela owns the release-reliability dimension (preflight, connector-specific condition, replay coverage, surfacing any drift on first request); I retain the claim discipline (descriptive-only framing, no read into activation or support effort, no pipeline or forecast credit, §3 / §4.8 reaffirmed as not weakened) and the exception authority whenever a maintenance cycle crosses any escalation trigger above. This is a routing change inside the organic checklist surface — descriptive operating read + named maintenance lanes — not a delegation of the underlying claim or forecast responsibility, and §8.E and §8.E.3 remain in force unchanged.

3g. November 6 — independent closure of the 9/24 source-completeness packet (the year's leadership-through-delegation evidence)

On November 6 Owen independently closed the 9/24 source-completeness packet covering 7/1–10/31 with certifications complete. The closure landed without my seeding the structure or chasing fields — the eight source-completeness fields (denominator and exact coverage dates; outcome window; measurement limits; exclusions; single named source owner per surface; reliability evidence; revenue and forecast treatment with the explicit handoff note "source certified by Owen; call retained by Riley"; and section certifier with named backup) cleared on the source side, and the certifications arrived consistent across sections. I treated this as concrete leadership-through-delegation evidence: I held the judgment and evidence boundary, Owen owned the build lane with named readouts and named gates, and the closure happened inside the bounded source-completeness lane without absorbing any other authority into it.

This is source completeness — it is not a claim, not a revenue call, not a forecast treatment, not board-readiness, and not executive language. The 11/6 brief explicitly split Owen's closed source row from the open causal, revenue, pipeline, forecast, board-readiness, and executive-language rows, and those open rows stayed with me. Source-completeness closure is the lane that Owen was bounded to; the broader authorities stayed where they were on 9/24 and are unchanged today. I continue to participate in routine monthly preparation and source-closure reviews as exception review — the 11/6 closure did not remove me from that work, and no new review-closure authority has been granted.

What is delegated versus what is mine. Delegated preparation is Owen's monthly sanitized campaign snapshot and the source-completeness review pathway as an evaluation framework — the line-by-line build work moves to him, with named readouts and named gates — and, on the checklist surface, the four-week descriptive operating read and the maintenance cycles within the Ines / Daniela / Riley split; the 11/6 independent closure of the 9/24 packet is the cleanest instance of that build-lane ownership completing on the source side. Routine source review still comes to me as exception review; I have not left that work, and no new review-closure authority has been granted. Routine monthly preparation still flows through me as exception review; I have not left that work either. What I retain are the claims (causal and revenue), the forecast treatment, the executive language, the descriptive-only discipline on the checklist read, the source completeness boundary itself (the lane Owen operates inside, not the closure authority), and the exception authority whenever a packet or maintenance cycle crosses any escalation trigger above. The transition is a routing change — line-by-line to exception-summary where clean, and descriptive operating read + named maintenance lanes on the checklist — not a handoff of the underlying responsibility, and the underlying responsibility on those streams did not change.

Effect: the 7/2 handoff held (135 campaigns, status + owner + lanes intact, no Q2 board redo); the 7/29 pathway is a written evaluation framework with explicit trigger conditions for re-review, not a delegation; the 10/14 checklist review closed with 92 admitted / 28 exposures / 5 ordinary setup-assistance requests, no eligibility or route mismatch, no lifecycle-suppression issue, no paid-source traffic, no unsupported admission, and no randomized control; the 11/6 independent closure of the 9/24 packet (7/1–10/31, certs complete) landed on the source side with the open causal / revenue / pipeline / forecast / board / executive-language rows staying with me. Call: this is the year's leadership-through-delegation example — I held the judgment and evidence boundary, Owen owned the build lane with named readouts and named gates, and the 11/6 closure is the concrete artifact of the year, with source completeness remaining bounded and the broader authorities unchanged.

4. ORGANIC AUTHORITY-SETUP CHECKLIST — RELEASED, ELIGIBILITY AND STATE MEANINGS PRESERVED

The approved release was a non-state-changing, connector-specific pre-setup checklist for admitted Helio Start workspaces whose selected connector requires an owner-level permission or a network-allowlist action. The release target was the organic Helio Start onboarding path only, and eligibility and state meanings had to be preserved; checklist exposure is reported separately from admission and activation outcomes.

At the 10:30 release gate on Sep 15, Ines and Daniela completed the 24-case replay and lifecycle preflight. The condition for receiving the checklist was a selected connector requiring an owner-level permission or a network-allowlist action, AND current verified-yes external authority at the moment of replay. Eight of the 24 cases met the condition and received the connector-specific checklist; 16 did not meet the condition and did not receive it. Every case preserved existing eligibility, route, lifecycle suppression, and governed state. Daniela released the checklist to the organic onboarding path, and Owen began reporting checklist exposure separately from admission and activation outcomes — the rationale being that checklist exposure is a pre-setup visibility surface, not an admission or activation event, and keeping the metric surfaces split preserves the integrity of the admission and activation numbers and prevents the checklist from being read into the §4.8-style pipeline / forecast framing.

The surrounding levers are all unchanged at Sep 15: §3 admission rules remain in force; external-authority meaning (field definition, current-and-verified-yes semantics, and the missing / stale / conflicting / pending / no / not-sure state set) is unchanged; assisted routing (assisted-route reason capture from first contact and per-account support-minute capture from first contact) is unchanged; fail-closed handling (immediate-stop on any unsupported case in the admitted path, reconciliation-failure pause, >10% over-90-sup-min pause for n ≥ 20) is unchanged; and paid-acquisition status is unchanged (cap closed at $14,420 / 50 admits, paid traffic off, no second Q3 paid batch authorized). The §8.E future-paid case-review gate and the §8.E.3 proposal precondition remain in force; the checklist release does not weaken, satisfy, or replace any element of §8.E.

Effect: the checklist is live on the organic Helio Start onboarding path with eligibility and state meanings intact. The Sep 15 release introduced no new admission, routing, lifecycle, or fail-closed rule; it did not alter external-authority meaning; it did not open a second paid batch. Call: this is the cleanest example of the year of shipping a release with every surrounding lever reasserted and §3 + §4.8 reaffirmed as not weakened.

CLOSING

Two priorities remain in flight, and neither implies I have left routine monthly preparation or source-closure reviews. Priority 1 is to bring Owen's source-completeness review pathway to its graduation criterion: three consecutive packets with all eight fields complete, a named certifier per section, zero disputed-semantics reopens, zero cross-surface owner drift, exceptions surfaced within one business day of source release with the gap named, reliability evidence reproducible from source on first request, and denominator / coverage dates reconciling against the prior packet's exit state. The 11/6 independent closure of the 9/24 packet is concrete progress on that lane, but it is one packet, not the three-packet criterion — I remain the routine source-closure reviewer on the underlying stream and the exception reviewer on the pathway itself until the criterion is met, and that responsibility is not in scope to delegate. Priority 2 is to hold the exception-summary monthly snapshot handoff without regression to line-by-line reconciliation; the 7/2 routing change stays in force, routine monthly preparation still flows through me as exception review, and my current responsibilities on that stream did not change. Source completeness stays separate from the claim, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, and executive-language authorities — the 11/6 closure operated inside that boundary, and no 2027 role change has been requested or approved.

I have not left routine monthly preparation; the 7/2 handoff was a routing change, and the underlying responsibility still flows through me as exception review. I have not delegated source-closure reviews; the 7/29 pathway is an evaluation framework with explicit three-packet success criteria and escalation triggers, the 11/6 closure is one packet inside that frame, and no new review-closure authority has been granted. I have not weakened §3 admission rules or the §4.8-style pipeline / forecast exclusion; both are reaffirmed as not weakened in the §8.E future-paid gate, the §11 organic-checklist release addendum, and the 8/21 second-batch decision record. I have not authorized a second Helio Start paid batch; paid traffic is off, the cohort is fixed at 50, and no pipeline or forecast credit has been granted against the cohort. I have not introduced a new admission, routing, lifecycle, or fail-closed rule; the 9/15 organic authority-setup checklist is non-state-changing and shipped to the organic path only. I have not turned the Oct 14 four-week descriptive checklist read into an activation or support-effort claim; the read is descriptive operating evidence on a pre-setup visibility surface, with the metric surfaces (admission, activation, checklist exposure, support minutes) kept split and §3 / §4.8 reaffirmed as not weakened. The 11/6 closure is source-completeness, not claim, not revenue, not forecast, not board-readiness, and not executive language; the open rows on those authorities stayed with me on 11/6 and continue to stay with me. No 2027 role change has been requested or approved.

# Owen Pham — 2026 year-end feedback working notes

_Owner: Riley. Status: working manager document — preliminary observations, not final feedback, and not an expansion of Owen's authority._

## Frame

These are my working notes to inform Owen's year-end conversation. They are preliminary and may shift before the final feedback is delivered. They do **not** modify Owen's authority. Per the 9/24 ruling, Owen remains bounded to source-completeness; Priya's Q4 Lifecycle System frame (4 evidence lanes, owner splits unchanged) is still in force. The 11/6 independent closure of the 9/24 source-completeness packet (7/1–10/31 coverage, certifications complete) confirms the source-completeness lane is operating as designed — and confirms only that. The standing split is unchanged: source completeness = Owen (bounded); claim, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, and executive-language authority = Riley. The 11/6 brief explicitly split Owen's closed source row from the open causal, revenue, pipeline, forecast, board-readiness, and executive-language rows, and those open rows stayed with me. Riley retains monthly prep + source-closure + exception review. No 2027 role change has been requested or approved, and nothing in these notes implies one.

## What this document is NOT

- Not final feedback. It is the working set of observations that will feed the final conversation.
- Not an expansion of Owen's authority. The 9/24 source-completeness ruling holds; the 11/6 closure is source-completeness only and does not absorb claim, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, or executive-language authority; Q4 lanes and owner splits are unchanged.
- Not an evaluation of work outside Owen's lane (e.g., Eng release/rollback stays with Daniela; owner-change vs. lifecycle stays with Ines).
- Not an implication of a 2027 role change. No 2027 role change has been requested or approved.

## Demonstrated in 2026

- **June preparation transition.** Handed the prep work for the Q2 evidence cycle over cleanly — no dropped threads, no noise downstream. Made the next phase easier to start.
- **Independent July and October sanitized campaign snapshots.** Both monthly snapshots (2nd biz day cadence) landed complete without me seeding structure or chasing fields. Status + owner + sanitized form held in both.
- **Complete first-pass Q2 and August evidence structures.** Q2 evidence and the 8/17 Day-90 CERT prep both arrived in usable first-pass form. Downstream review did not have to rebuild the skeleton.
- **Disciplined use of the September 24 source-completeness authority.** Stayed inside the bounded lane. Did not absorb revenue, forecast, claim, board-readiness, or executive-language authority — those stayed with me.
- **Held the October packet incomplete when exact coverage and owner certification did not match.** Did not paper over the gap on 10/7. Correctly stopped rather than weaken §3 or §4.8, and let the gate hold. This is the right call.
- **November 6 independent closure of the 9/24 source-completeness packet.** Closed the 9/24 packet covering 7/1–10/31 with certifications complete, inside the source-completeness lane only. The eight source-completeness fields cleared, the certifications arrived consistent across sections, and the closure landed without my seeding the structure or chasing fields. This is the year's cleanest concrete example of leadership-through-delegation operating as designed: build lane owned by Owen, judgment and evidence boundary held by me, and the closure event stayed inside source completeness without claiming, forecasting, or reframing any other authority.

## Next-cycle expectations

- **Obtain owner certification earlier.** The 10/7 packet stalled because certification arrived late in the cycle, and earlier certification is the development area carried forward from that. Pushing owner sign-off to the front of the window prevents end-of-window collapses and keeps the gate from being the bottleneck. The 11/6 closure did not retire this expectation — one packet is not the three-packet graduation criterion, and earlier certification is what protects the next packet from repeating the 10/7 stall.
- **State exact through-dates before requesting closure review.** Closure should be declared with a specific date (e.g., "through 10/16" or "through 10/31") rather than as a general "ready" — that keeps source-completeness reviewable and avoids a closure conversation about scope. The 11/6 closure was declared with the exact through-date of 10/31; making that the standing pattern across packets is the carry-forward expectation.
- **Continue to distinguish source completeness from my authorities.** The line is: source completeness = Owen (bounded); claim, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, and executive-language authority = Riley. Do not soften that boundary by letting source-completeness absorb the other authorities back into it. The 11/6 closure operated inside the bounded lane — and continuing to hold that lane, rather than letting a clean closure pull the boundary outward, is the carry-forward expectation. The 8/21 Priya ruling (no 2nd-batch / pipeline / forecast credit) reinforces this — Owen held the line then too.

## Open threads to revisit before final feedback

- Reference the 8/21 Priya ruling in the final conversation as evidence Owen held the line when asked to extend past source-completeness.
- The 7 high-suppression classifications (Owen + CS, per the 10/7 gate) — quality and provenance worth surfacing as a strength.
- The 11/6 independent closure of the 9/24 packet (7/1–10/31, certs complete) — surface as concrete leadership-through-delegation evidence, framed as one packet inside the source-completeness lane, not as a graduation or authority expansion.
- Confirm whether a December snapshot lands before the year-end conversation; if so, incorporate.

arguments.body:
Riley Tanaka — 2026 year-end self-review working draft
Cycle: 2026 year-end · Reviewer: Priya · Working draft (not for distribution)
Shape: summary first, then five evidence sections plus a closing "have NOT done" block, written as prose for editing down to the 1-pager (why / cuts / what I did / effect / call).

SUMMARY

I held the claim-boundary discipline across the year: Q1 and Q2 cohort windows stayed on the published dates, and the §3 admission rules plus the §4.8-style pipeline/forecast exclusion held through every pressure point without being compressed into a partial-window claim. I closed the Helio Start paid cohort at $14,420 / 50 admits, and on Aug 21 recommended — and Priya accepted — no second Q3 batch and no pipeline or forecast credit for the cohort; a binding future-paid case-review gate is now in force. I built a delegation rhythm in which Owen owns the monthly sanitized campaign snapshot and the source-completeness review pathway as an evaluation framework, while I retain board readiness, causal and revenue claims, forecast treatment, executive language, and exception authority — and I have not stopped routine monthly preparation or source-closure reviews, both of which still flow through me as exception review. The Oct 14 authority-checklist review closed with Owen and Customer Success supplying a clean descriptive four-week operating read; I kept the checklist in organic onboarding without turning the counts into an activation or support-effort claim, and I set an explicit maintenance split among Ines, Daniela, and me.


1. Q1 AND Q2 CLAIM BOUNDARIES — HELD

The published constraints were the §3 admission rules (eligibility, refusal, connector access, external authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, support routing) and the §4.8-style pipeline/forecast exclusion. Q1 dates were 4/7; Q2 was not board-ready until mature claim windows completed. Forecast and pipeline received no credit on partial-window evidence, and a mature claim required complete observation windows.

Under pressure to compress, I refused to roll the day-7 first-integration read (39/50, leading only) into acquisition, scale, pipeline, or forecast, and I held the day-90 decision for closed day-90 windows. I kept the four-part output discipline (classification / alignment / consequence / routing) on operator-facing references and on my own claim-side framing, and I held the §3 / §4.8 cannot-be-weakened framing as the rule any future proposal must satisfy.

The effect: Q1 and Q2 board segments stayed on the published dates, no claim was advanced on a partial-window basis, no pipeline or forecast credit was granted against Q1 or Q2 cohort outcomes, and the structural discipline keeping the five Helio Start states separate from Starter / retained-mid-segment in every readout held. Call: keep citing this as the spine of the year's evidence — the mature-window-only claim discipline plus §3 / §4.8 not weakened is the defended boundary.


2. CLOSED HELIO START PAID COHORT — NO SECOND BATCH, NO PIPELINE/FORECAST CREDIT

The approved pilot was high-intent paid search, mid-segment-fit only, 6-week max window, capped at the earlier of $15,000 spent or 50 admitted workspaces; the $8K / 25 fallback was never approved. Stop / pause triggers (any one): unsupported-in-admitted; reconciliation failure across eligibility → admit → assisted; or ≥20 admitted if >10% showed >90 support minutes per account. The day-7 read of 39/50 first-integration-by-day-7 was leading only, not mature.

On Aug 17 the source-completeness certification packet (Owen + Customer Success) assigned mutually exclusive day-90 statuses to all 50 workspaces — 37 paid-active, 6 canceled, 4 past due, 3 billing hold — with $60,480 gross billed cash, $56,230 refund-adjusted collected cash, 26-minute median and 104-minute p90 account-level support effort, 7 of 50 (14%) exceeding 90 support minutes, and end-to-end reconciliation of paid-source attribution for all 50. No unsupported applicant entered the admitted path. I treated the packet as descriptive paid-source evidence only — explicitly not causal acquisition, not scale, not pipeline, not forecast — because there was no randomized control. On Aug 21 the second-batch decision review recommended, and Priya accepted, no second Helio Start paid batch in Q3 and no Q4 forecast treatment for the cohort. Paid traffic remains off.

The future-paid gate is now binding: Owen + Customer Success must classify each of the seven high-support workspaces into (a) external-authority action, (b) ordinary integration, (c) billing, or (d) another supported cause (named explicitly; "unclassified" is not a supported bucket); Ines + Daniela must determine whether each case concerns state meaning, routing, and / or setup sequence (multiple dimensions may apply, each named); and any future paid proposal must account for all seven cases (state how each is prevented, mitigated, or bounded — not merely listed) without weakening §3 or §4.8.

The cohort is fixed at 50; paid traffic is off; no second Q3 paid batch is in flight; the cohort carries no pipeline or forecast credit. Call: the case-review gate is the structural artifact of the year — the day-90 numbers are evidence inside it, not the artifact itself.


3. OWEN'S MONTHLY-PREP TRANSITION + BOUNDED SOURCE-CLOSURE AUTHORITY

Two changes moved through me. The first was the monthly sanitized campaign snapshot landing as exception-summary only; the first post-handoff on Jul 2 covered 135 campaigns with status and owner rows and owner lanes intact, and resolved three Q2 opens (Ines owner-change verified, Maya snapshot-only, Owen denominator). The second was the source-completeness review pathway defined on Jul 29 — Owen's audit covers eight fields per row (denominator and exact coverage dates; outcome window; measurement limits; exclusions; single named source owner per surface; reliability evidence; revenue and forecast treatment with the explicit handoff note "source certified by Owen; call retained by Riley"; and a section certifier with named backup). The observable success criteria are three consecutive packets with all eight fields complete and a named certifier per section, zero disputed-semantics reopens, zero cross-surface owner drift, exceptions surfaced within one business day of source release with the gap named, reliability evidence reproducible from source on first request, and denominator / coverage dates reconciling against the prior packet's exit state.

Escalation triggers are unchanged: any missing field makes the packet incomplete and escalates; disputed semantics or cross-surface discrepancy escalates rather than resolving in packet; any causal, revenue, forecast, or executive-language content escalates to me by default; and two consecutive packets with the same exception type trigger formal review of the pathway, not a third packet.

3f. October 14 authority-checklist review — four-week operating read, descriptive only

On October 14 the authority-checklist review closed. Owen and Customer Success supplied a clean descriptive four-week operating read on the organic authority-setup checklist shipped on Sep 15. Across the four-week window: 92 admitted organic workspaces in scope; 28 checklist exposures (pre-setup visibility surface only, reported separately from admission and activation outcomes); five ordinary setup-assistance requests handled through the existing assisted-route path. The review surfaced no eligibility or route mismatch, no lifecycle-suppression issue, no paid-source traffic (paid traffic remains off; the Helio Start paid cohort is fixed at 50), no unsupported admission, and no randomized control. I treated the four-week read as descriptive operating evidence — explicitly not an activation claim and not a support-effort claim — because the counts are pre-setup visibility and assisted-route support requests on an organic-only surface, not activation outcomes, and there is no control arm. The checklist stays in organic onboarding, and the metric surfaces (admission, activation, checklist exposure, support minutes) remain split.

The maintenance split is now explicit and named: Ines owns the state-meaning dimension (lifecycle suppression, governed state, external-authority meaning unchanged); Daniela owns the release-reliability dimension (preflight, connector-specific condition, replay coverage, surfacing any drift on first request); I retain the claim discipline (descriptive-only framing, no read into activation or support effort, no pipeline or forecast credit, §3 / §4.8 reaffirmed as not weakened) and the exception authority whenever a maintenance cycle crosses any escalation trigger above. This is a routing change inside the organic checklist surface — descriptive operating read + named maintenance lanes — not a delegation of the underlying claim or forecast responsibility, and §8.E and §8.E.3 remain in force unchanged.

What is delegated versus what is mine. Delegated preparation is Owen's monthly sanitized campaign snapshot and the source-completeness review pathway as an evaluation framework — the line-by-line build work moves to him, with named readouts and named gates — and, on the checklist surface, the four-week descriptive operating read and the maintenance cycles within the Ines / Daniela / Riley split. Routine source review still comes to me as exception review; I have not left that work, and no new review-closure authority has been granted. Routine monthly preparation still flows through me as exception review; I have not left that work either. What I retain are the claims (causal and revenue), the forecast treatment, the executive language, the descriptive-only discipline on the checklist read, and the exception authority whenever a packet or maintenance cycle crosses any escalation trigger above. The transition is a routing change — line-by-line to exception-summary where clean, and descriptive operating read + named maintenance lanes on the checklist — not a handoff of the underlying responsibility, and the underlying responsibility on those streams did not change.

Effect: the 7/2 handoff held (135 campaigns, status + owner + lanes intact, no Q2 board redo); the 7/29 pathway is a written evaluation framework with explicit trigger conditions for re-review, not a delegation; the 10/14 checklist review closed with 92 admitted / 28 exposures / 5 ordinary setup-assistance requests, no eligibility or route mismatch, no lifecycle-suppression issue, no paid-source traffic, no unsupported admission, and no randomized control. Call: this is the year's leadership-through-delegation example — I held the judgment and evidence boundary while Owen owned the build lane with named readouts and named gates, and the organic checklist read carries the same shape with Ines and Daniela on named maintenance lanes and the descriptive-only discipline held.


4. ORGANIC AUTHORITY-SETUP CHECKLIST — RELEASED, ELIGIBILITY AND STATE MEANINGS PRESERVED

The approved release was a non-state-changing, connector-specific pre-setup checklist for admitted Helio Start workspaces whose selected connector requires an owner-level permission or a network-allowlist action. The release target was the organic Helio Start onboarding path only, and eligibility and state meanings had to be preserved; checklist exposure is reported separately from admission and activation outcomes.

At the 10:30 release gate on Sep 15, Ines and Daniela completed the 24-case replay and lifecycle preflight. The condition for receiving the checklist was a selected connector requiring an owner-level permission or a network-allowlist action, AND current verified-yes external authority at the moment of replay. Eight of the 24 cases met the condition and received the connector-specific checklist; 16 did not meet the condition and did not receive it. Every case preserved existing eligibility, route, lifecycle suppression, and governed state. Daniela released the checklist to the organic onboarding path, and Owen began reporting checklist exposure separately from admission and activation outcomes — the rationale being that checklist exposure is a pre-setup visibility surface, not an admission or activation event, and keeping the metric surfaces split preserves the integrity of the admission and activation numbers and prevents the checklist from being read into the §4.8-style pipeline / forecast framing.

The surrounding levers are all unchanged at Sep 15: §3 admission rules remain in force; external-authority meaning (field definition, current-and-verified-yes semantics, and the missing / stale / conflicting / pending / no / not-sure state set) is unchanged; assisted routing (assisted-route reason capture from first contact and per-account support-minute capture from first contact) is unchanged; fail-closed handling (immediate-stop on any unsupported case in the admitted path, reconciliation-failure pause, >10% over-90-sup-min pause for n ≥ 20) is unchanged; and paid-acquisition status is unchanged (cap closed at $14,420 / 50 admits, paid traffic off, no second Q3 paid batch authorized). The §8.E future-paid case-review gate and the §8.E.3 proposal precondition remain in force; the checklist release does not weaken, satisfy, or replace any element of §8.E.

Effect: the checklist is live on the organic Helio Start onboarding path with eligibility and state meanings intact. The Sep 15 release introduced no new admission, routing, lifecycle, or fail-closed rule; it did not alter external-authority meaning; it did not open a second paid batch. Call: this is the cleanest example of the year of shipping a release with every surrounding lever reasserted and §3 + §4.8 reaffirmed as not weakened.


5. DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES — TWO, CONCRETE

Two priorities are in flight, and neither implies I have left routine monthly preparation or source-closure reviews.

Priority 1 is to bring Owen's source-completeness review pathway to its graduation criterion: three consecutive packets with all eight fields complete, a named certifier per section, zero disputed-semantics reopens, zero cross-surface owner drift, exceptions surfaced within one business day of source release with the gap named, reliability evidence reproducible from source on first request, and denominator / coverage dates reconciling against the prior packet's exit state. Until those three packets clear, I remain the routine source-closure reviewer on the underlying stream and the exception reviewer on the pathway itself — that responsibility is not in scope to delegate until the criterion is met.

Priority 2 is to hold the exception-summary monthly snapshot handoff without regression to line-by-line reconciliation. The 7/2 routing change (line-by-line to exception-summary where clean) stays in force, and routine monthly preparation still flows through me as exception review. My current responsibilities on that stream did not change. The leverage goal for the year is to make the input and review path repeatable on this rhythm — every claim naming its denominator and complete predeclared outcome window — without my returning to line-by-line reconciliation.


6. WHAT I HAVE NOT DONE — DELIBERATE, FOR THE REVIEWER

I have not left routine monthly preparation; the 7/2 handoff was a routing change, and the underlying responsibility still flows through me as exception review. I have not delegated source-closure reviews; the 7/29 pathway is an evaluation framework with explicit three-packet success criteria and escalation triggers, and no new review-closure authority has been granted. I have not weakened §3 admission rules or the §4.8-style pipeline / forecast exclusion; both are reaffirmed as not weakened in the §8.E future-paid gate, the §11 organic-checklist release addendum, and the 8/21 second-batch decision record. I have not authorized a second Helio Start paid batch; paid traffic is off, the cohort is fixed at 50, and no pipeline or forecast credit has been granted against the cohort. I have not introduced a new admission, routing, lifecycle, or fail-closed rule; the 9/15 organic authority-setup checklist is non-state-changing and shipped to the organic path only. I have not turned the Oct 14 four-week descriptive checklist read into an activation or support-effort claim; the read is descriptive operating evidence on a pre-setup visibility surface, with the metric surfaces (admission, activation, checklist exposure, support minutes) kept split and §3 / §4.8 reaffirmed as not weakened.
