arguments.body:
REHEARSAL ONLY. NOT A LIVE SEND. NO CUSTOMER CONTACT. PROPOSAL INACTIVE.
Owner of the candidate proposal (Sept 27): Riley. Rehearsal is mechanical only;
it does not authorize rollout, does not transfer ownership, and does not
substitute for the trial-approval gates in force (non-incident-affected +
≥48h post-prod-release). Final go/no-go remains with Riley.

Reference: Priya 2024-09-25 09:05 CT — both timing boundaries met; rehearsal
authorized on 10 historical rows only. The live-send proposal stays inactive.
Surface for rehearsal: [ flag_id / candidate_id / experiment_key — to be
filled in by Ines before run ]  Target rehearsal window: 2026-09-27
(calendar currently empty — confirmed via list_calendar_events 2026-09-27).

================================================================
1. HARD GUARDRAILS — confirm before any row is touched
================================================================
[ ] This run is a REHEARSAL on HISTORICAL rows. No live channel emits.
[ ] Customer.io / sending connector state is set to DRY-RUN / sandbox.
    Connector state must be a single coherent value; conflicting values
    on (env, channel) fail closed (see §5).
[ ] Release metadata for the Sept 27 candidate is present in the registry:
    owner, status, rollout_pct, created_at, audience, audit_window.
    Missing or stale release metadata → fail closed (§5).
[ ] Customer contact is prohibited. The connector must not be able to
    resolve a recipient address from any rehearsal row. Verify by
    inspecting 1 sampled row end-to-end before continuing.
[ ] Owner representation preserved: candidate flag owner field remains
    "riley". Do not edit owner, status, or rollout_pct during rehearsal.
[ ] Audit roles for this rehearsal:
    - Ines (lifecycle-aud-risk): row evidence, fail-closed decisions,
      rehearsal log. Correction-triggered stop routes to Riley (not to
      Ines) for this rehearsal per Priya 2024-09-25.
    - Daniela (entitlement / support-state): entitlement validity on
      each row, connector-state QA, dry-run sanity.
    - Riley (judgment-escalation / proposal owner): receives any stop,
      owns proposal, has not transferred ownership.

================================================================
2. PRE-FLIGHT — must pass before row 1
================================================================
[ ] Candidate ID / flag key recorded: ____________________________
[ ] Release metadata fields captured (snapshot, not edit):
    - owner: riley
    - status: __________________
    - rollout_pct: ____________
    - audience: ________________
    - created_at: ______________
    - audit_window: ____________
[ ] Connector dry-run flag set; resolver disabled on the channel used
    by the Sept 27 candidate. Evidence: connector config hash + a
    test resolve attempt that returns null.
[ ] 10 historical rows pre-selected by Ines; rows are NOT in the live
    cohort window for the candidate. Each row carries:
    row_id, as_of_date, account_id (anonymized if needed), segment,
    evidence_sources (list).
[ ] Hypothetical audit assignment per §4 ready (one auditor, ≤24h
    window per row).
[ ] Stop-route contact = Riley. Channel confirmed (DM/email) and
    monitored during rehearsal window.

================================================================
3. PER-ROW EVIDENCE TABLE — fill for each of 10 rows
================================================================
Format: one block per row. Disposition is SEND-EQUIV or HOLD-EQUIV;
supporting evidence is the actual signals that would have driven the
decision on the row's as_of_date. No live data is touched.

Row ___ of 10
  row_id:           ________________
  as_of_date:       ________________
  account_id:       ________________
  segment:          ________________
  evidence_sources: ________________ (e.g. activation event, lifecycle
                     state, suppression status, prior hold reason)
  disposition:      [ ] SEND-EQUIV   [ ] HOLD-EQUIV
  rationale:        ________________ (1-2 sentences, plain Qs)
  entitlement check (Daniela): PASS / FAIL — notes _______________
  fail-closed triggered? [ ] no  [ ] yes — reason _______________
  audit assignment:  auditor __________  due_by __________ (≤24h)

(repeat the block 10 times)

================================================================
4. HYPOTHETICAL AUDIT ASSIGNMENT — within 24h per row
================================================================
[ ] Auditor assigned per row (may be the same person across rows).
    Auditor name: ________________   role: ________________
[ ] Audit deliverable per row: disposition matches evidence on file;
    no live-channel artifact produced; release metadata consistent;
    fail-closed triggers respected.
[ ] Audit due ≤24h from row evaluation timestamp. Due-by logged in
    the rehearsal log alongside timestamp of evaluation.
[ ] Audit outcomes aggregated by Ines into a single rehearsal
    summary for Riley (not a proposal update).

================================================================
5. FAIL-CLOSED RULES
================================================================
Trigger a stop and route to Riley (§6) if ANY of the following is true
at any point in the rehearsal, including pre-flight:

  a) Release metadata missing or stale for the Sept 27 candidate
     (owner, status, rollout_pct, audience, created_at, audit_window
     not all present and consistent).
  b) Connector state is conflicting — e.g. dry-run=true on channel A
     but dry-run=false on channel B for the same (env, channel class);
     or resolver disabled on one channel but enabled on another.
  c) A historical row resolves to a live recipient address through
     any code path.
  d) The connector emits anything outside the rehearsal sandbox.
  e) Entitlement check (Daniela) returns FAIL on any row.
  f) Any row's evidence trail cannot be reconstructed from on-file
     sources within the 24h audit window.

Fail-closed action: stop, log the trigger, route to Riley, do not
retry the row. Do not "fix forward" inside the rehearsal.

================================================================
6. CORRECTION-TRIGGERED STOP ROUTE
================================================================
Channel:        [ Slack DM to Riley / email to riley — fill ]
Opened by:      Ines (rehearsal owner of the moment)
Trigger:        any §5 condition; additionally any post-evaluation
                correction that would change a row's disposition.
Payload:        row_id (or "pre-flight" / "row N"), trigger class
                (a-f), release-metadata snapshot, connector-state
                snapshot, evidence trail pointer, recommended hold
                duration.
Riley ack SLA:  next business hour. Rehearsal stays paused until ack.
Re-open rule:   only after Riley ack AND the §5 condition is cleared
                AND the connector state is re-validated by Daniela.
                Do NOT auto-resume.

================================================================
7. OWNERSHIP & APPROVAL — preserved as-is
================================================================
[ ] Candidate flag owner field: riley (unchanged).
[ ] Candidate flag status: unchanged through rehearsal.
[ ] Rollout eligibility: not widened. The rehearsal does not consume
    any of the trial gates (non-incident-affected, ≥48h post-prod).
[ ] Rehearsal does NOT count as a live rehearsal for ownership
    transfer. Non-live rehearsal ≠ trial approval ≠ ownership
    transfer.
[ ] Post-rehearsal: Ines produces a rehearsal summary only. Riley
    reviews before any subsequent live-rehearsal proposal.

================================================================
8. SIGN-OFF
================================================================
Pre-flight completed by:  Ines ____  Daniela ____  Riley ____
Rehearsal executed by:    Ines ____
Audit aggregated by:      Ines ____
Stop routes acknowledged: Riley ____ (count: ___)

Final state on close: candidate unchanged, proposal inactive, owner
still riley, no customer contacted, rehearsal summary filed.

arguments.body:
PRODUCTION SHADOW — MAY 2 CLOSE AND EVIDENCE
Added 2025-05-02 by Riley Tanaka. Source: scheduled production shadow
for the CS auto-nudge integration, closed May 2 (Fri). The shadow ran
April 25 through May 2 against the legacy production path. Both paths
were evaluated on the same 204 live decisions in the shadow window;
the released audience was not changed by the shadow. The legacy
production path remains the released production path at the close of
this section; the bounded May 8 production release authorized below
does not take effect until the May 8 switch.

Shadow scope (recap, carried forward)
  Window: April 25 (Fri) through May 2 (Fri).
  Lane: Daniela Schultz (engineering) — ran the shadow.
  Observers: Owen Pham (Lifecycle semantics readout), Ines Kovac
  (audit-risk review), Customer Success (consumer-lane sign-off).
  Intent: observational only. Shadow recorded what the shared-state
  contract would have done, against the legacy production path, on the
  same records and over the same window, without acting on the result.

Shadow result — total
  204 live decisions evaluated by both paths in the shadow window.
  191 records produced the same decision under both paths; the
  shared-state contract agreed with the legacy path's outcome.
  13 records the shared-state contract prevented from proceeding
  under the legacy eligibility result.
  Released audience was not changed by the shadow. No record reached
  a customer through the shared-state path; all shadow output was
  observational.

Operational category breakdown — of the 13 contract-blocked records
  Field-specific holds (9 of 13)
    - 7 records held for stale qualifying-human-admin state.
      Same root cause as the April 24 historical replay: the legacy
      eligibility result would have proceeded using the last-known
      qualifying-human-admin value; the contract holds because the
      field is past its freshness limit even though the feed-level
      timestamp on those records remains current. A current feed-level
      timestamp does not substitute for field freshness.
    - 2 records held for unresolved external-system authority.
      The legacy eligibility result would have proceeded treating the
      external-system-authority state as resolved; the contract holds
      because the authority state has not been confirmed within the
      freshness limit. Second governed field, fail-closed hold,
      applied to live shadow data.
  Suppressions (4 of 13)
    - 4 records suppressed because active Customer Success adoption
      or renewal work was in flight. The contract yields to active CS
      work rather than overriding it. Suppression is a deliberate
      yield to in-flight CS adoption or renewal activity, recorded
      here as a separate category from the field-specific holds above.

Verifications carried out in the shadow window
  - Hold and suppression reasons: Daniela Schultz verified each of
    the 9 holds and the 4 suppressions against the contract rules
    that produce them. Every hold and suppression was traceable to a
    specific contract rule and a specific field state on the record
    at the time of evaluation; no hold or suppression was generated
    without a contract-rule reason attached.
  - Production rollback behavior: Daniela exercised the production
    rollback path against the shadow cohort. Forward-only holds
    survived rollback; no eligibility or messaging state rewound;
    no record that had been held or suppressed acquired a release
    path through the rollback. The forward-only recheck protocol
    held under rollback, consistent with the Apr 14 engineering
    workback and the Apr 24 historical-replay boundary statement.
  - Lifecycle messaging adjacency (Ines Kovac, audit-risk review):
    Ines confirmed that no held or suppressed case in the shadow
    window received adjacent lifecycle messaging that assumed
    eligibility. The held and suppressed sets were not exposed to
    lifecycle sends that would have contradicted their state; the
    messaging surface respected the contract's hold and suppression
    semantics, including the suppression-as-yield semantics for
    active CS work.
  - Classification completeness: every observed difference between
    the shadow path and the legacy path fell under an established
    contract rule. No record appeared as a difference without a
    matching rule; no record was classified into a category that
    was not already a contract category. The set of contract
    categories observed in shadow (stale qualifying-human-admin
    hold; unresolved external-system authority hold; active CS
    adoption or renewal suppression) is a subset of the categories
    observed in the April 24 historical replay; no new category
    appeared in shadow that would have required a new fixture or a
    contract amendment.

Cross-walk to the April 24 historical replay
  - April 24 replay (412 records, observational): 386 matched; 26
    contract-blocked (19 holds [15 stale qualifying-human-admin + 4
    unresolved external-system authority] + 7 suppressions).
  - April 25–May 2 shadow (204 live decisions, observational): 191
    agreed; 13 contract-blocked (9 holds [7 stale qualifying-human-
    admin + 2 unresolved external-system authority] + 4 suppressions).
  - The category mix in shadow tracks the category mix in replay:
    stale qualifying-human-admin is the dominant hold category;
    unresolved external-system authority is the secondary hold
    category; active CS adoption or renewal work is the suppression
    category. The proportion of contract-blocked records in shadow
    (13/204 ≈ 6.4%) is in the same band as replay (26/412 ≈ 6.3%),
    so the shadow did not surface a higher-than-replay rate of
    contract-blocked outcomes against live traffic.

What the shadow did NOT produce
  - No production switch occurred during the shadow window.
  - No record reached a customer through the shared-state path.
  - No adjacent lifecycle send was issued to a held or suppressed
    record on the assumption of eligibility.
  - No eligibility decision changed between the legacy path and the
    shared-state contract on a record where all required state was
    current and supported.
  - No new contract category appeared that would require a new
    fixture, a contract amendment, or a re-scope of the replay
    cohort.

BOUNDED MAY 8 PRODUCTION RELEASE — AUTHORIZATION
Added 2025-05-02 by Riley Tanaka. Source: May 2 close of the production
shadow; the evidence above; the April 24 historical replay; the
agreed input mapping; the engineering workback; the rollback
validation record. Lane roles for this authorization follow the
3/24 audit-role ruling and the 4/15 operating retro:
  - Ines Kovac: lifecycle governance, message-state review, and
    audit-risk classification (authority on whether held or
    suppressed records were exposed to adjacent messaging).
  - Owen Pham: Lifecycle Systems semantics readout (authority on
    the meaning of the contract's categories and the operating
    consequence of the 13 contract-blocked records under the new
    messaging state).
  - Daniela Schultz: engineering reliability and release controls
    (deploy hygiene; production rollback exercised against the
    shadow cohort; prod-path verification).
  - Riley Tanaka: release boundary only. I joined the May 2 close
    for the release boundary, not for row-level review.

What is authorized
  I authorize a bounded production release for the CS auto-nudge
  integration on May 8 (Thu). The bounded release flips the
  shared-state path from observational to released for the CS
  auto-nudge surface, with the legacy production path continuing to
  operate as the safety backstop through the switch window. The
  bounded release is conditional on the release-review sign-off
  chain closing in standard form before May 8; the standard
  release-review gate is not waived by this authorization.

What is NOT authorized by this section
  - The shared-state path is not yet live. It is authorized for a
    bounded release on May 8. Until the May 8 switch executes, the
    legacy production path remains the released production path.
    This section does not describe the integration as live, and
    nothing in it should be read as a statement that the switch
    has already been made.
  - No scope expansion is authorized. The bounded release covers
    the CS auto-nudge surface only. Adjacent lifecycle surfaces,
    other cohorts, and other messaging channels are out of scope.
  - No forecast credit is established. The shadow record and the
    April 24 replay record are evidence of the contract's
    behavior, not forecasts of how the shared-state path will
    perform under sustained load.
  - No contract amendment is authorized. The contract categories
    observed in shadow are a subset of the categories observed in
    replay; no amendment, no new fixture, and no new category is
    authorized on the basis of the May 2 close.
  - No rollback is waived. The rollback path remains mandatory and
    must remain exercisable end-to-end against the live cohort
    after the May 8 switch, on the same terms as it was exercised
    against the shadow cohort.

Release boundary — applied to the May 8 switch
  - Switch date: May 8 (Thu), conditional on standard release-review
    sign-off closing in advance.
  - Until the switch executes: legacy production path remains the
    released production path. The shadow record is closed and
    frozen; the shared-state path remains observational.
  - At the switch: the shared-state path becomes the released path
    for the CS auto-nudge surface; the legacy path becomes the
    safety backstop for the duration of the switch window.
  - After the switch: forward-only behavior remains in force.
    Forward-only recheck protocol applies to any lag observed post-
    switch: if a delayed export or refresh resolves, recheck current
    state only; do NOT restore pre-switch eligibility or messaging
    state. Held rows stay held. Suppressed rows stay suppressed
    unless the in-flight CS adoption or renewal work that

CS AUTO-NUDGE — PRODUCTION-SHADOW EVIDENCE CARD (AUDIT)
Compiled 2028-01-01. Lane attribution per the 3/24 audit-role ruling and the 4/15 operating retro: Ines Kovac (governance / message-state review / audit-risk classification), Owen Pham (Lifecycle Systems semantics readout), Daniela Schultz (engineering reliability, rollback validation, hold- and suppression-reason verification), Riley Tanaka (release boundary only — not row-level review).

PURPOSE
This card is the audit-ready evidence record for the historical CS auto-nudge production shadow. It is read alongside (a) the April 24 historical-replay artifact and (b) the engineering workback and rollback-validation record. The card is descriptive, not an authorization. It does not describe a production switch.

1. SHADOW INTERVAL
  Window: April 25 (Fri) through May 2 (Fri), 2025.
  Mode: dual-evaluation, observational. Both the legacy production path and the shared-state contract evaluated every live CS auto-nudge decision in the window. The legacy path remained the released production path for the entire window. The shared-state path was observational only; no record reached a customer through it. The released audience was not changed by the shadow.
  Lane: Daniela Schultz ran the shadow. Owen Pham kept the cumulative decision ledger. Ines Kovac ran the adjacent-message alignment check. Customer Success attended the consumer-lane readout. Riley joined only for the release boundary.

2. RECONCILED OUTCOMES AND CAUSES
  Total live decisions evaluated by both paths in the window: 204.
  Agreed outcomes (legacy and shared-state contract returned the same decision): 191.
  Contract-blocked (the shared-state contract prevented the record from proceeding under the legacy eligibility result): 13.

  Operational category breakdown of the 13 contract-blocked records:
    Field-specific holds (9 of 13):
      - 7 holds, cause: stale qualifying-human-admin state.
        Plain reading: the legacy eligibility result would have proceeded using the last-known value of the qualifying-human-admin field. The contract held because that field's value was past its freshness limit, even though the feed-level timestamp on the record was still current. A current feed-level timestamp does not substitute for field freshness. Same root cause as the dominant category in the April 24 historical replay.
      - 2 holds, cause: unresolved external-system authority.
        Plain reading: the legacy eligibility result would have proceeded treating the external-system-authority state as resolved. The contract held because the authority had not been confirmed within the freshness limit. This is the second governed field and is a fail-closed hold. See section 6 for the plain-language explanation of external-system authority.
    Suppressions (4 of 13):
      - 4 suppressions, cause: active Customer Success adoption or renewal work in flight.
        Plain reading: the record was suppressed because real CS work was actively underway on it. The contract yields to active CS work rather than overriding it. Suppression is a deliberate yield to in-flight CS adoption or renewal activity, recorded as a separate category from the field-specific holds above.

  Classification completeness: every observed difference between the shadow path and the legacy path fell under an established contract rule. No record appeared as a difference without a matching rule. No record was classified into a category that was not already a contract category. No new category appeared in shadow that would have required a new fixture or a contract amendment.

3. SUPPRESSIONS — DISTINGUISHED FROM HOLDS
  Suppressions and field-specific holds are distinct categories and must not be merged.
  A field-specific hold is a fail-closed state driven by governed-field state (field freshness or authority freshness). It blocks the record on contract grounds and surfaces a specific field-level reason.
  A suppression is a yield to in-flight Customer Success adoption or renewal work. It is not a field-state failure. The record may have all governed fields current and supported; it is still suppressed because active CS work is in flight.
  During the shadow window, 4 records were suppressed because active CS work was in flight. Those records continued to be handled by the legacy production path during the shadow; the shadow was observational and did not change what they received.
  Both categories share one operational consequence under the messaging surface: no held or suppressed record received adjacent lifecycle messaging that assumed eligibility (see section 4).

4. REVIEWER VALIDATIONS
  Hold and suppression reason verification (Daniela Schultz, engineering reliability):
    Each of the 9 shadow holds and the 4 shadow suppressions was verified against the contract rule that produces it. Every hold and suppression was traceable to (a) a specific contract rule and (b) a specific field state on the record at the time of evaluation. No hold or suppression was generated without a contract-rule reason attached.

  Production rollback behavior (Daniela Schultz):
    Daniela exercised the production rollback path against the shadow cohort. Forward-only holds survived the rollback. No eligibility or messaging state rewound. No record that had been held or suppressed acquired a release path through the rollback. The forward-only recheck protocol held under rollback, consistent with the April 14 engineering workback and the April 24 historical-replay boundary statement.

  Adjacent-message alignment (Ines Kovac, audit-risk review):
    Ines confirmed that no held or suppressed case in the shadow window received adjacent lifecycle messaging that assumed eligibility. The messaging surface respected the contract's hold and suppression semantics, including suppression-as-yield for active CS work. The held and suppressed sets were not exposed to lifecycle sends that would have contradicted their state.

  Lifecycle Systems semantics readout (Owen Pham):
    Owen carried the cumulative decision ledger and the operational consequence of the 13 contract-blocked records under the new messaging state. Owen's readout is the source of the denominator (204) and the category breakdown (7 + 2 + 4).

5. RELEASE BOUNDARY
  As of the close of the shadow window (May 2, 2025):
    - The legacy production path was the released production path.
    - The shared-state path was observational only.
    - No production switch had occurred. No record reached a customer through the shared-state path.
    - The shadow record was closed and frozen.
    - The April 24 historical-replay artifact remained in force as the verification gate for shared-state reproducibility; the May 2 shadow record sat alongside it as observational evidence on live traffic.

  The May 2 close separately authorized a bounded production release for May 8, conditional on standard release-review sign-off closing in advance. That authorization was a release-boundary statement, not a switch. Until the May 8 switch executed, the legacy production path remained the released production path. The authorization did not waive the standard release-review gate, did not waive rollback, and did not expand scope beyond the CS auto-nudge surface.

  Forward-only recheck protocol: in force at and after any switch. Lag recovery is forward-only. Held rows stay held. Suppressed rows stay suppressed unless the in-flight CS adoption or renewal work that suppressed them has itself concluded under the standard suppression-yield rule.

  Rollback: remains mandatory and exercisable end-to-end against the live cohort at and after any switch, on the same terms as it was exercised against the shadow cohort.

6. EXTERNAL-SYSTEM AUTHORITY — PLAIN EXPLANATION
  What the field is:
    External-system authority is one of two governed fields on a CS auto-nudge record (the other being qualifying-human-admin state). It records whether an outside system that has decision rights over the record — for example, a downstream platform that can confirm or override the eligibility verdict — has actually weighed in within the freshness limit the contract requires.

  Why it matters:
    A record can look eligible on its own surface fields and on its qualifying-human-admin state and still be unsafe to act on, because something outside our system may have a say. The shared-state contract treats external-system authority as a governed field precisely so the contract does not silently proceed past an unresolved outside verdict.

  What "unresolved" means here:
    The outside system either has not responded within the freshness limit, or has responded in a way the contract cannot classify as a clean confirmation. The authority state has not been confirmed within the freshness limit the contract requires.

  How the contract treats it:
    Fail-closed hold. The legacy eligibility result would have proceeded treating the authority as resolved; the contract instead holds the record. The contract is explicit that a current feed-level timestamp on the record does not substitute for the authority being confirmed — the outside system's confirmation is what counts, and its freshness limit is what governs. This is the second governed field, distinct from qualifying-human-admin freshness, and the two must not be collapsed.

  Why it shows up as a hold and not a suppression:
    A hold is a field-state outcome — the field is not in a contract-acceptable state, so the contract blocks the record. A suppression is a yield to active CS work. Unresolved external-system authority is the former: the field has not been confirmed within the freshness limit, so the contract holds. There is no active CS work in flight on these records in the shadow cohort; the holds are not suppressions.

  Plain-language summary:
    "Until the outside system with decision rights on this record has confirmed its verdict within the time window the contract requires, the contract holds the record. We will not act on the legacy path's view of eligibility until that outside verdict is in."

7. SHADOW EVALUATION vs PRODUCTION SWITCH — DISTINCTION
  Shadow evaluation (what the May 2 close actually was):
    - Observational only. Both paths evaluated each live decision; the shadow path did not act on the result.
    - The released audience was not changed by the shadow.
    - The legacy production path remained the released production path for the entire shadow window.
    - No record reached a customer through the shared-state path.
    - The output of the shadow is a reconciled record: how many decisions the two paths agreed on, how many the contract blocked, and the contract-rule reason attached to each block.
    - The shadow did not, by itself, change what any customer received.

  Production switch (what the shadow was NOT):
    - A production switch would flip the shared-state path from observational to released for the CS auto-nudge surface, with the legacy path becoming the safety backstop through the switch window.
    - A production switch would require the standard release-review gate to close in advance; that gate was not waived by the shadow record.
    - A production switch would not be implied by the shadow record. The shadow record is evidence of contract behavior on live traffic; it is not an authorization to switch, and it does not constitute a switch.
    - A production switch, when it occurs, must be a separate explicit decision recorded against the release boundary; it is not the May 2 close.

  Audit-relevant consequence:
    Anything in the shadow record should be read as observational evidence, not as a release. The May 8 bounded-release authorization referenced in section 5 is a separate decision resting on this evidence, on the April 24 replay, and on the engineering workback and rollback-validation record; the May 8 authorization itself is not a switch, and the switch itself (when and if it executes) is not the shadow.

8. EVIDENCE THE CARD RESTS ON
  1. April 24 historical replay (412 records, observational): 386 matched legacy; 26 contract-blocked — 19 field-specific holds (15 stale qualifying-human-admin + 4 unresolved external-system authority) + 7 active CS adoption or renewal suppressions. No record with all required state current and supported changed outcome.
  2. April 25 – May 2, 2025 production shadow (204 live decisions, observational): 191 agreed with legacy; 13 contract-blocked — 9 field-specific holds (7 stale qualifying-human-admin + 2 unresolved external-system authority) + 4 active CS adoption or renewal suppressions. Released audience not changed by the shadow. No record reached a customer through the shared-state path.
  3. Hold and suppression reason verification: Daniela verified each of the 9 shadow holds and the 4 shadow suppressions against the contract rules that produce them. Every difference classified under an established contract rule; no unmatched or unclassified case.
  4. Production rollback validation: forward-only holds survived rollback; no eligibility or messaging state rewound; no held or suppressed record acquired a release path through the rollback.
  5. Adjacent-message alignment: Ines confirmed no held or suppressed case received adjacent lifecycle messaging that assumed eligibility; the messaging surface respected the contract's hold and suppression semantics, including suppression-as-yield for active CS work.
  6. Category stability: contract categories observed in shadow are a subset of the categories observed in the April 24 replay. No new fixture, no contract amendment.
  7. Proportion check: contract-blocked rate in shadow (13/204 ≈ 6.4%) is in the same band as replay (26/412 ≈ 6.3%); the shadow did not surface a higher-than-replay rate of contract-blocked outcomes against live traffic.

9. WHAT THIS CARD DOES NOT CONTAIN
  - No production switch. The shadow was observational; the legacy production path remained released.
  - No forecast credit. The replay and shadow records are evidence of contract behavior, not forecasts of sustained-load performance.
  - No contract amendment. No new category, no new fixture.
  - No row-level release review. Riley joined only for the release boundary, not for row-level review; row-level evidence is Daniela's, Owen's, and Ines'.
  - No waiver of the standard release-review gate. That gate is not waived by this card.
  - No waiver of rollback. Rollback remains mandatory and exercisable end-to-end against the live cohort.
  - No scope expansion beyond the CS auto-nudge surface.

10. CARRY-FORWARD (DESCRIPTIVE, NOT AN AUTHORIZATION)
  - The April 24 historical-replay artifact and the May 2, 2025 production-shadow record together constitute the observational evidence base for the CS auto-nudge shared-state contract on the historical cohort.
  - The shared-state path is not live as of this card.
  - Any production switch is a separate explicit decision recorded against the release boundary.
  - Forward-only recheck protocol and mandatory rollback remain in force at and after any switch.

SUMMARY

arguments.body:
# Q3 Evidence Lock — Sep 19, 2025 (working template)

Purpose: assemble this lock continuously rather than reconstruct at the deadline. One primary row per scheduled decision; holds, fresh checks, warnings, and reevaluations attach as linked history. Boundaries unchanged: higher-risk, stop, release, rollback.

Decision scope (Sep 24, 2025): as defined. Out of scope: Ines's independent routine-review authority — NOT implied as approved here. That authority remains a separate question and is not advanced by anything in this lock.

---

## Unique-decision + warning-history rule (added 2025-08-04)

The denominator is unique scheduled decisions, not events. Each scheduled decision contributes exactly one primary row in its owner lane. Anything else that happens around that decision — a fresh check, a warning, a reevaluation, an alert — links to that row as history; it does not create a new primary row, a new hold, or a new decision.

Explicit guard — no double-counting:
A single scheduled decision is never counted twice. In particular, a scheduled decision that triggers a source-age (or any other) alert must not also be recorded as an additional hold, an additional decision, or an additional entry in any other lane's denominator. The alert attaches as linked warning history to the same primary row; the underlying decision remains one unique row.

Warning history behaves the same way: warnings, fresh checks, and reevaluations are linked time-stamped history on the primary row. They are not parallel rows, not parallel holds, and not parallel decisions.

Measurement rule only:
This is a measurement / counting rule for the evidence lock. It governs how rows are counted, how alerts and warnings are linked, and how the denominator is constructed. It does not assume that any specific alert — including the source-age alert referenced in prior context — is live, firing, or effective at lock time. Live status of the source-age alert is a separate question, tracked in Lane C (Daniela source-reliability) and the Aug 6 alert plan, and is not implied by anything in this lock. A single live fire does not promote the alert to mature reliability evidence — that promotion requires repeated live fires under the standing-lane cadence rules and remains a separate question.

---

## Lane A — Owen: unique-decision denominator + hold dispositions

Evidence-limit prompts (per row):
- Denominator construction: which decisions count as unique? Apply the same rule to all rows in the window. Apply the unique-decision + warning-history rule above — one primary row per scheduled decision; alerts/warnings/fresh checks/reevaluations link, never replace or duplicate.
- Hold reason code: stop | release-prep | rollback-prep | awaiting-fresh-check | higher-risk-review.
- Hold exit condition: what unblocks the row, in Owen's terms.
- Fresh-check cadence: ≤3 neutral reviews/week standing; stale fails closed.
- No-double-count guard: a scheduled decision that surfaces an alert or warning attaches that history to the existing primary row; do not create an additional hold row or additional decision row for the same scheduled decision.

Schema (one primary row per scheduled decision):
| Decision ID | Denominator rule | Hold? | Hold reason | Exit condition | Linked: fresh check / warning / reeval |

Controls:
- If a row shows two competing denominator rules, route to Owen before lock.
- Holds never delete the primary row — they link to it.
- Stale (no fresh check within cadence) fails closed, does not auto-resolve.

---

## Lane B — Ines: operator-guidance interventions

Evidence-limit prompts (per row):
- Intervention type: lifecycle-aud-risk operator guidance only. (Independent routine-review authority = out of scope; do not record as approved.)
- Recipient surface: CS / Growth / Lifecycle Systems.
- Change scope: additive only; no silent expansion of authority.
- Escalation trigger: anything resembling routine-review reclassification → boundary call to Riley.
- No-double-count guard: an operator-guidance intervention tied to a scheduled decision in Lane A links to Lane A's primary row; it does not create a parallel Lane B row that would double-count the same decision.

Schema:
| Intervention ID | Type (operator guidance) | Surface | Additive? | Escalation flag | Linked: warning / reeval |

Controls:
- Rows labelled "routine review reclassification" or independent authority go to Riley for boundary check, not into this lane as approved.
- Standing-lane ≤3 neutral/week rule still applies.
- `routine education` = HIGHER-RISK; Ines reclassifies; boundary remains Riley's.

---

## Lane C — Daniela: source-reliability + rollback evidence

Evidence-limit prompts (per row):
- Source reliability: connector auth, entitlement, qualifying-human-admin, active CS adoption/renewal — per the 5-state guide Ines OK'd 2025-07-25.
- Release vs rollback: which path, which artifact, which owner.
- Lag handling: forward-only — delayed export/refresh that has resolved → recheck current state; do NOT restore pre-lag eligibility.
- Rollback authority: eng release/rollback routes to Daniela; state-meaning disputes route to Riley.
- Alert/warning linkage: source-age (or any) alerts attached to a scheduled decision are linked warning history on that decision's primary row; they do not generate a parallel Lane C decision row. Live/effective status of any specific alert is tracked here and is NOT implied by its inclusion as linked history in any other lane.
- No-double-count guard: a source-reliability event tied to a scheduled decision links to the primary row; do not record the same event as both an alert and an additional hold/decision.

Schema:
| Source/Event ID | State(s) affected | Reliability evidence | Release path | Rollback path | Linked: warning / reeval |

Controls:
- Every release row must carry a rollback path or be flagged as not-yet-eligible-for-release.
- Lag-recovery actions never restore pre-lag eligibility — flag if proposed.
- INPUT ≠ RELEASE; neither substitutes. Both required where the 2025-03-28 lifecycle audit applies.

### Lane C — Source-age alert: first live operational result (2025-08-14)

Status change for the alert: as of the July 23 chair's-review close, the Aug 6 source-age alert plan (Daniela, fixes the learn-after-hold gap) was APPROVED, NOT LIVE — review gating. Today's entry is the first live fire on record.

Facts (single fire; no extrapolation):
- Event time: 2025-08-14 08:50 CT.
- Trigger: qualifying-human-admin source refresh stalled with 17 pending CS auto-nudge decisions on the source side.
- Source-age alert fired: 43 minutes before the freshness limit would have been reached.
- Restoration: Daniela restored the refresh with 18 minutes remaining before the freshness limit.
- Verification: Owen verified the fresh reevaluation against the post-restoration source.
- Outcome: 13 of 17 proceeded on the fresh reevaluation.
- Suppression: 4 of 17 were suppressed because current Customer Success adoption or renewal work was active on the account (governed-state component #5 per the 2025-07-25 reference #2; suppression is multi-causal, and active CS work is one cause, not the definition).
- None entered stale state. No manual release of any decision. No customer correction required. No rollback executed. No eng release executed.

Evidence-limit framing (preserved verbatim from the user's bound):
This is the alert's first live operational result, not mature reliability evidence. A single live fire demonstrates that the alert can detect, alert within the freshness window, allow a restoration inside the window, and produce a verified fresh reevaluation. It does NOT establish:
- That the alert is reliable across cohorts, surfaces, or repeat firings.
- That 13/17 (or any single split) is a stable outcome distribution.
- That the 18-minute cushion is sufficient under load.
- That suppression reasons will continue to map cleanly to the 5-state governed meanings in every case.
- That the alert qualifies for release-promotion or maturity promotion.
Maturity promotion remains a separate question, gated on repeated live fires under the standing-lane cadence rules and on Owen's reporting lane, and is not implied by this entry.

Lane attribution:
- Lane C (Daniela): the source-reliability event itself — stalled refresh, alert fire, restoration inside the freshness window, no rollback needed.
- Lane A (Owen): verification of the fresh reevaluation against the post-restoration source. Owen's verification is linked history on the underlying scheduled decisions, not a parallel Lane A decision row.
- Lane B (Ines): the suppression reason (active CS adoption or renewal work) is an Ines-governed meaning (governed-state component #5). The 4 suppressed decisions are suppressed under the existing governed-state meaning, not under a new interpretation; no Lane B intervention is required and no escalation flag is raised.
- Lane D (Riley): no disputed semantics, no customer correction, no incident stop. No Lane D row is created.

No-double-count audit (per the Aug-4 rule):
- The 17 pending decisions map to 17 underlying scheduled decisions; each carries one primary row in its owner lane.

arguments.title: Holly → Cherrywood — Runbook
arguments.body:
Summary
One compact plan replacing scattered notes. Holly stays undisturbed until move day; nothing enters or moves into Cherrywood before the May 1 key release. Holly is photographed after final cleaning. Two people, one dog, one move.

Hard rules
- Nothing enters or moves into Cherrywood before May 1 (Wed).
- Keys + lease papers stay with Riley — never inside a packed box.
- Aerosol fixative and fuel canisters do NOT go on the truck.
- Mover access: per 4-18 confirmation — 42-ft ground-level street-load to front door; below 75-ft long-carry threshold; no stair/elev/alley/dock surcharge. Retain confirmation email + agent measurement on move day.

By date

Sat Apr 27 — Packing block (Riley + Sam)
- 9:00–11:30am: fixed packing block
- Pack remaining linens, bathroom items
- Stage one overnight bag each (not used until May 1 morning)

Tue Apr 30 — Pre-move walkthrough (Riley + Sam)
- 4:00–4:30pm: walk Holly end-to-end
- Verify nothing left behind that should go on the truck
- Do NOT surrender keys — keys stay with Riley until May 1 release
- After final cleaning: photograph Holly

Wed May 1 — Move day
All:
  - Hard rule: do not enter or move items into Cherrywood until key release is complete.
7:30am — Mom picks up Kibo at Holly (Riley hands off)
8:00am–12:00pm — Movers load at Holly (Sam on site)
  - Per 4-18 access confirmation (see Hard rules)
  - Truck must NOT carry: aerosol fixative, fuel canisters
  - Riley keeps keys + lease papers on person
After key release — only then — transport to Cherrywood and unload

By owner

Riley
- Custody of keys + lease papers, start to finish
- Coordinate Mom's 7:30am Kibo handoff at Holly on May 1
- Lead pre-move walkthrough (Apr 30, 4:00–4:30pm); do not surrender keys
- Photograph Holly after final cleaning

Sam
- Packing block (Apr 27, 9:00–11:30am): linens, bathroom, own overnight bag
- On site at Holly for movers (May 1, 8:00am–12:00pm)
- Co-walk the pre-move walkthrough on Apr 30

Mom
- May 1, 7:30am: pick up Kibo at Holly

Movers
- May 1, 8:00am–12:00pm: load at Holly
- Access: 42-ft ground-level street-load to front door (4-18 confirmation); no stair/elev/alley/dock surcharge

Items that must stay accessible (NOT packed into boxes)
- Keys — Holly and Cherrywood
- Lease papers
- 4-18 mover access confirmation email + agent measurement
- One overnight bag each (Riley, Sam) — used May 1 morning
- Phone, chargers, ID, meds, water

Items that do NOT go on the truck
- Aerosol fixative
- Fuel canisters

Takeaway
Runbook is the single source of truth from Apr 27 through May 1. If anything diverges from this doc, update here — not in a parallel note.

arguments.body:
## Context

Daniela completed the trace on both discrepancy groups. Both came from independently-timed downstream refreshes of state — not missing or corrupted source records. Source integrity holds. The fail-closed holds remain correct and are not in scope for relaxation. The problem is contract and freshness, not safety stance.

## Why a contract, not more reports

Two independently-owned surfaces reporting on the same underlying record will continue to surface "ambiguous" cases whenever their refresh cadences drift. Per-surface report fixes preserve the ambiguity; the only durable fix is one governed contract that all surfaces consume.

## Proposal — governance under the existing operating model

Establish one **state contract** and one **shared ownership-and-freshness model** across three surfaces:

- **Helio Start** — intake / admission lifecycle, including the five-state reporting model (admitted / assisted / ineligible / final-reconciliation / **external_authority=pending** as a non-final pre-admission state per the locked 12/16 op-instruction + 12/20 rewrite).
- **Expansion Assist** — eligibility, account-state, and forward-resolution semantics.
- **Lifecycle messaging** — enrollment, suppression, and prompt-hold eligibility keyed off the above states.

No new team. Roles under the existing model:

- **Owen** — shape + expansion review (state schema, surface exposure, ex-risks).
- **Ines** — lifecycle audit / risk (hold correctness, refusal boundary, prompt-hold compliance).
- **Riley** — judgment escrow / escalation owner (fail-closed holds, ambiguous forward-event interpretation).
- **Daniela** — data / trace evidence (refresh cadence, source-of-truth lineage).
- **Customer Success** — routing and operational surface for pending external_authority cases.

## What "contract" means here

- Single canonical state vocabulary across all three surfaces.
- Single freshness SLA per state, with one authoritative writer per state.
- Named read-paths — no silent downstream caches.
- Forward-event resolution only — point-in-time snapshots stay fixed; later state is a new forward event, never a rewrite of a historical snapshot (exception-review discipline holds).

## Decisions to make at the Jan 7 mapping session

1. Canonical state names and definitions across all three surfaces.
2. Authoritative writer per state (one owner).
3. Freshness SLA per state (max staleness allowed; refresh trigger).
4. Read-paths: which downstream surfaces consume which states, and how stale they may be.
5. Edge cases: pending external_authority routing; ambiguous forward-event interpretation; reconciliation timing across surfaces.
6. Single definition of "prompt-hold" across surfaces.

## Pre-work for Jan 7 attendees

- **Daniela** — refresh-cadence trace per surface (start time, frequency, lag distribution, observed drift).
- **Owen** — list of Expansion Assist states and which surfaces currently consume them.
- **Ines** — lifecycle suppression triggers that depend on Helio Start or Expansion Assist state.
- **CS** — current routing rules for pending external_authority cases.
- **Riley** — re-circulate the locked 12/16 op-instruction + 12/20 rewrite intake rule for shared reference.

## Non-goals (explicit)

- No new team and no org restructuring.
- No relaxation of fail-closed holds.
- No retroactive rewrite of accepted point-in-time tables.
- No change to the Helio Start refusal boundary or intake gate structure.
- Pending external_authority remains a non-final, non-rate-bearing state — the contract must preserve, not soften, that boundary.

## Timeline

- **Jan 7** — source-and-consumer mapping session (this brief's kickoff).
- **Jan 14** — contract v0.1 draft circulated.
- **Jan 21** — cross-functional review (Owen shape, Ines risk, Daniela data, CS routing).
- **Jan 31** — locked contract + freshness model.
- **Feb 14** — migration / rollout plan.

Five-minute staff demo — outline
"Shared lifecycle state feed: what changed" — Tomás, Tuesday 2025-03-25
Frame: operating safeguard, not product launch.

0. Opening — 30s
   - Bounded change to three surfaces, not a companywide system claim.
   - I'll show the three consumers, one fail-closed example, then the boundary — so no one walks out calling this "mature."

1. The three live consumers — 75s
   - Helio Start reporting. Drives the four admission states (admitted / assisted / ineligible / final-reconciliation). `pending` is separate, pre-admission, NOT in any rate or activation denominator, resolves forward only.
   - Expansion Assist selection. Descriptive, nonforecast. Not an activation driver. Reads from the same feed but does not feed activation commentary.
   - Lifecycle preflight. Gates lifecycle sends on non-`routine education` lanes. `routine education` stays on Ines's aud-risk lane under the lifecycle runbook.
   - Five governed fields per record: external authority, connector authentication, entitlement, qualifying-human-admin status, active CS adoption or renewal work. Feed-level timestamp is transport-only; field-level timestamps are the freshness authority.

2. One visible fail-closed example — 90s
   - Walk the 2025-03-17 incident (per @session:dolphinbench-20260912072549-f01aa3b3-builtin-riley-profile/20260915_005000_ef60dc): two preflight rows normalized to the same destination but lived under different workspaces with conflicting entitlement states.
   - Pre-feed: each consumer read its own legacy derivation; a row could have shipped under a contested entitlement.
   - Post-feed: the shared feed exposed the conflict. Preflight refused to ship on both rows. Visible field-specific hold reason, source + consumer as-of shown, no silent carry-forward.
   - Held stayed held. Lag recovery is forward-only. No record inherited a prior true value. Freshness alarm (2hr source / 4hr consumer) auto-clears on catch-up, retains the gap in audit, and is NON-eligibility-authority. Clearing the alarm does not restore pre-lag eligibility.

3. Current scope boundary — 75s
   - IN (the entire release): the three consumers above, against the five-field contract.
   - OUT (explicit, do not generalize): messaging copy, activation reporting cadence, CS-nudge logic, mid-segment rate commentary, any other consumer surface.
   - Unchanged on release: the five-state Helio Start model; `pending` pre-admission and forward-only; intake additive, refusal semantics unchanged; Expansion Assist descriptive not forecast; held rows remain held; forward-only lag recovery; `routine education` lifecycle on Ines's aud-risk lane.
   - Posture: this is a safeguard, not a metric, and not a feature. Don't cite the freshness alarm as eligibility authority.

4. Close — 30s
   - If anyone sees drift between reporting and messaging on these three surfaces, route to Ines (lifecycle-aud-risk) before quoting numbers. Numbers require a fresh preflight; otherwise we're re-citing a set we already know is clean.
   - Q&A. Cheat sheet on the back page if asked.

A fuller version of this demo as a staff-facing doc already exists at `doc_1789434478467` from the 2025-03-21 session if you want to lift speaker notes or the Q&A cheat sheet verbatim. ## Context

Daniela completed the trace on both discrepancy groups. Both came from independently-timed downstream refreshes of state — not missing or corrupted source records. Source integrity holds. The fail-closed holds remain correct and are not in scope for relaxation. The problem is contract and freshness, not safety stance.

## Why a contract, not more reports

Two independently-owned surfaces reporting on the same underlying record will continue to surface "ambiguous" cases whenever their refresh cadences drift. Per-surface report fixes preserve the ambiguity; the only durable fix is one governed contract that all surfaces consume.

## Proposal — governance under the existing operating model

Establish one **state contract** and one **shared ownership-and-freshness model** across three surfaces:

- **Helio Start** — intake / admission lifecycle, including the five-state reporting model (admitted / assisted / ineligible / final-reconciliation / **external_authority=pending** as a non-final pre-admission state per the locked 12/16 op-instruction + 12/20 rewrite).
- **Expansion Assist** — eligibility, account-state, and forward-resolution semantics.
- **Lifecycle messaging** — enrollment, suppression, and prompt-hold eligibility keyed off the above states.

No new team. Roles under the existing model:

- **Owen** — shape + expansion review (state schema, surface exposure, ex-risks).
- **Ines** — lifecycle audit / risk (hold correctness, refusal boundary, prompt-hold compliance).
- **Riley** — judgment escrow / escalation owner (fail-closed holds, ambiguous forward-event interpretation).
- **Daniela** — data / trace evidence (refresh cadence, source-of-truth lineage).
- **Customer Success** — routing and operational surface for pending external_authority cases.

## What "contract" means here

- Single canonical state vocabulary across all three surfaces.
- Single freshness SLA per state, with one authoritative writer per state.
- Named read-paths — no silent downstream caches.
- Forward-event resolution only — point-in-time snapshots stay fixed; later state is a new forward event, never a rewrite of a historical snapshot (exception-review discipline holds).

## Decisions to make at the Jan 7 mapping session

1. Canonical state names and definitions across all three surfaces.
2. Authoritative writer per state (one owner).
3. Freshness SLA per state (max staleness allowed; refresh trigger).
4. Read-paths: which downstream surfaces consume which states, and how stale they may be.
5. Edge cases: pending external_authority routing; ambiguous forward-event interpretation; reconciliation timing across surfaces.
6. Single definition of "prompt-hold" across surfaces.

## Pre-work for Jan 7 attendees

- **Daniela** — refresh-cadence trace per surface (start time, frequency, lag distribution, observed drift).
- **Owen** — list of Expansion Assist states and which surfaces currently consume them.
- **Ines** — lifecycle suppression triggers that depend on Helio Start or Expansion Assist state.
- **CS** — current routing rules for pending external_authority cases.
- **Riley** — re-circulate the locked 12/16 op-instruction + 12/20 rewrite intake rule for shared reference.

## Non-goals (explicit)

- No new team and no org restructuring.
- No relaxation of fail-closed holds.
- No retroactive rewrite of accepted point-in-time tables.
- No change to the Helio Start refusal boundary or intake gate structure.
- Pending external_authority remains a non-final, non-rate-bearing state — the contract must preserve, not soften, that boundary.

## Timeline

- **Jan 7** — source-and-consumer mapping session (this brief's kickoff).
- **Jan 14** — contract v0.1 draft circulated.
- **Jan 21** — cross-functional review (Owen shape, Ines risk, Daniela data, CS routing).
- **Jan 31** — locked contract + freshness model.
- **Feb 14** — migration / rollout plan.

|---|---|

| `external_authority=pending` is a **non-final pre-admission state**. It is not in any of the four final buckets, not in any rate or denominator, not folded into activation. | 12/16 op-instruction + 12/20 rewrite |
| `pending` ≠ refused / declined / partial-admit. Prompts are held while pending. | 12/16 op-instruction + 12/20 rewrite |
| `pending` resolves **forward only** — verify → `admitted`; assist → `assisted`; refuse → `ineligible`. Landing is a forward event, not retroactive backfill. | 12/16 op-instruction + 12/20 rewrite |
| `pending` row is reported on its own line. Intake rule unchanged: the pending row is additive; it does not soften refusals or move the refusal boundary. | 12/16 op-instruction + 12/20 rewrite |
| External-authority is a **separate gate** from `admin_proof` and `connector_authentication`. Pending external-authority is a distinct pre-admission state, not a final ineligible outcome. | 12/16 op-instruction + 12/20 rewrite |
| Fail-closed holds are correct as applied. Not in scope to relax. | Original proposal (this brief) + Daniela's trace |
| Exception-review discipline: accepted point-in-time tables stay fixed. Later state is a separate forward event, never a revision to a historical snapshot. | Exception-review doctrine |

### 2. What the Jan 7 session surfaced (evidence, not decisions)

The session produced concrete evidence, captured here as input to the still-open governance questions. **Not closed by the session; just recorded so it does not get re-discovered.**

- Refresh cadences across the three surfaces are timed independently. The observed discrepancy groups trace to drift between those cadences, not to source-record corruption (consistent with Daniela's pre-session trace).

Cross-functional review of those resolutions is scheduled for the "Jan 21 — cross-functional review" milestone.

### 4. What this addendum does NOT do

- Does **not** assign owners. Owner assignment is a v0.1-draft outcome, reviewed at the Jan 21 cross-functional review.
- Does **not** constitute a formal team or org change. Still governance under the existing operating model.

arguments.body:
Customer Success — Message-State Onboarding (Operator Handout, One Page)

Purpose: help new operators read the five governed message-state fields correctly on day one. Source of authority: Ines's approved Message-State Reference #2, accepted 2025-07-25 (Priya + Riley, no substantive edits). This handout does not redefine any field and does not change any authority boundary.

================================================================
FIVE GOVERNED FIELDS — KEEP THEM SEPARATE
================================================================

1. External-system authority
   What it means: the connector has the owner permission or network-allowlist clearance it needs to run its action on the external system. This is a READINESS signal on the connector.
   What it is NOT: it is NOT permission for automated contact on the customer. It does not authorize a send, a refresh, or a cross-system push.
   Plain rule: "Authority verified" = connector is ready. It never = "we may contact the customer."

2. Connector authentication
   What it means: the technical auth state of the connector itself — token validity, rotation, scope, replay-window freshness. Owner: Daniela.
   What it is NOT: it does NOT decide whether the connector may run against this customer. Authenticated does not mean authorized. Run-eligibility lives in field 1 plus the CS suppression state plus the dispute path.
   Plain rule: auth says the connector can talk; it does not say to whom or when.

3. Entitlement
   What it means: the customer's product-surface right — plan, tier, seats, add-ons, Expansion Assist scope. Source = the governed entitlement record.
   What it is NOT: it is not CS-work, not suppression, not authority. An entitled account can still be Held, Suppressed, or under disputed semantics.
   Plain rule: entitlement is the right to the surface. It is not the right to be contacted about the surface.

4. Qualifying-human-admin status
   What it means: whether the customer has a human administrator who meets the qualification criteria for the surface in question. One specific field, tracked separately.
   What it is NOT: it is NOT "account is healthy" or "in good standing." A qualifying-human-admin = true record can still be Held, Suppressed, or disputed.
   Plain rule: one field, one meaning. Not a composite health score.

5. Active Customer Success adoption or renewal work
   What it means: live, in-progress CS adoption or renewal work on the account — what work, what owner, what age.
   What it is NOT: it does NOT override Held / Suppressed / cross-surface dependency. It also does NOT speak to plan, seats, or authority.
   Plain rule: live CS work does not, by itself, authorize outreach. Suppression and Held stay in force unless explicitly released.

================================================================
THE KEY DISTINCTION ON DAY ONE
================================================================

External-system authority (field 1) is about connector readiness. Permission for automated contact (whether CS or another surface may send to this customer) is a SEPARATE question governed by the suppression lane plus the dispute path plus the held state. Conflating the two is the exact error the 2025-06-17 CS auto-nudge rule was written to prevent. "Authority verified" never translates to "may contact."

================================================================
FIELD-SPECIFIC HOLD AND SUPPRESSION BEHAVIOR
================================================================

- Held and Suppressed are routine operator-facing states (see Reference #1). They sit alongside the five governed fields above — they do not replace them and they are not bundled into any of them.
- A record can carry entitlement (field 3) and qualifying-human-admin = true (field 4) and still be Held or Suppressed. Each state is independent.
- Active CS work (field 5) does not lift Held or Suppressed. Only an explicit release does.
- Field 1 (external-system authority) is a connector-side readiness signal. The CS suppression lane can still block the action even when the connector is ready.
- Lag recovery is forward-only. A delayed export / refresh that resolves leads to a recheck of CURRENT state. Do NOT restore pre-lag eligibility.

================================================================
ESCALATION BOUNDARIES — WHO OWNS WHAT
================================================================

- Riley (judgment lane): state-meaning changes, disputed interpretations, customer corrections, incident stops. This handout does NOT widen that lane.
- Daniela (engineering lane): engineering release and rollback controls — replay, fallback, accessibility-copy, held-queue release. Auth (field 2) is hers.
- Owen (reporting lane): single-path CS auto-nudge readout. Standing-lane neutral readouts ≤3 per week; stale readouts fail closed.
- Ines (governance lane): lifecycle governance and how messaging consumes the governed fields. Routine-education reclassification (HIGHER-RISK) lives here, boundary owned by Riley.
- Priya: shared state between Growth and CS for lifecycle is mandatory.

If you are unsure whether something is a state-meaning change, a customer correction, or an incident stop — it goes to Riley. If you are unsure whether something is a release or rollback — it goes to Daniela. Do not act on the unsure case.

================================================================
ENGINEERING-CONTROL BOUNDARIES (UNCHANGED)
================================================================

- Engineering release and rollback control remain with Daniela. This handout does not move that.
- Lifecycle audit = INPUT (snapshot, rules, reclassification) versus RELEASE (replay, fallback, a11y, held-queue release). Neither substitutes for the other.
- Expansion Assist is descriptive-only. It does not commit a promotional-state change. Starter / retained mid-segment promotion is a separate decision path.
- Helio Start intake is additive: new records enter "pending" and do not displace existing records. "Pending" is pre-admission, forward-only, and is excluded from rate and activation denominators.

================================================================
SCOPE NOTE
================================================================

This handout is derived from the approved reference. It does not expand review-closure or release authority. Any field-meaning change, dispute, customer correction, or incident stop still routes to Riley. Any release or rollback still routes to Daniela. The five fields above remain the five fields. If a case you are looking at does not fit any of them, that is a routing question, not a definition question.

2025-07-28 — Customer Success onboarding handout created from this reference

A one-page operator handout titled "Message-State Onboarding — Customer Success Operator Handout" has been created in the Lifecycle folder, derived directly from this approved reference (Reference #2, accepted 2025-07-25).

The handout is an onboarding aid only. It does not redefine any of the five governed fields, does not bundle any pair together, does not widen the review-closure authority, and does not move any release or rollback control. It carries forward:

- The five-field separation: external-system authority, connector authentication, entitlement, qualifying-human-admin status, active Customer Success adoption or renewal work.
- The external-system-authority ≠ automated-contact-permission distinction (the 2025-06-17 rule, restated for day-one operators).
- Field-specific hold and suppression behavior (Held / Suppressed are independent of and not bundled into any of the five governed fields).
- Escalation boundaries unchanged: state-meaning, disputes, customer corrections, incident stops → Riley; engineering release and rollback → Daniela; single-path CS auto-nudge readout → Owen; lifecycle governance and routine-education reclassification → Ines (HIGHER-RISK boundary owned by Riley).
- Engineering-control boundaries unchanged: lifecycle audit INPUT vs RELEASE, Expansion Assist descriptive-only, Helio Start intake additive with "pending" excluded from rate and activation denominators.

Request originated from Customer Success (2025-07-28 09:15 CT). Reference doc itself is not modified.

Helio Start pending external-authority quick reference
New-operator field card — what this state is, what it is not, who owns what

================================================================
WHAT THIS STATE IS
================================================================

external_authority = pending on a Helio Start record means the
external-system authority check has not yet landed. The record is
in a non-final, pre-admission state — separate from the four final
admission outcomes. It is the fifth state in Helio Start reporting.

Locked intake rule (12/16 op-instruction + 12/20 rewrite):

  - Five states, not four.
  - Four final, mutually exclusive on final route-out:
    admitted | assisted | ineligible | final-reconciliation.
  - Fifth = external_authority = pending.
    Routed to CS before admission.

================================================================
WHAT IT IS NOT — DO NOT CONFLATE
================================================================

  pending is NOT:
  - refused, declined, or a partial-admit
  - one of the four final admission states
  - in any rate or denominator
  - folded into activation
  - admin_proof or connector_authentication (separate gate)

  pending DOES NOT:
  - soften a refusal or move the refusal boundary
  - replace a final-state decision later
  - retroactively rewrite an earlier snapshot
  - count toward pre-launch QA eligibility-flow entries

================================================================
RECORDING — WHO WRITES THE STATE
================================================================

  Helio Start (intake / five-state reporting) — Riley, judgment
    escrow / escalation lane. State-meaning, disputed
    interpretation, and forward-event resolution live here.
    Field-meaning questions route to Riley, not to the operator.

  The pending row itself — CS is the operational owner while the
    record sits in pending. CS receives the row, runs CS-side
    verification, and routes the outcome forward.

  Source-of-truth trace / refresh evidence — Daniela. If you see
    a discrepancy between what the record shows and what CS sees,
    the trace is Daniela's lane; do not patch locally.

================================================================
DEPENDENT SETUP MESSAGING — WHO HANDLES IT
================================================================

  Prompts are HELD while pending. Lifecycle messaging stays off
  the record for the duration of the pending state. No setup
  message, no reminder, no nudge goes out.

  - Lifecycle suppression triggers keyed off the pending state —
    Ines (lifecycle audit / risk lane). Trigger definitions and
    suppression behavior live here.
  - Messaging copy, send timing, suppression release — Ines, with
    Priya as the shared Growth↔CS coordination point while the
    record is in pending.
  - Held state is independent of the five governed fields; do not
    infer suppression from entitlement or qualifying-human-admin.

  Forward-only rule (do not backfill): when the record resolves,
  it resolves to a forward event — verify → admitted, assist →
  assisted, refuse → ineligible. Landing is a new forward event,
  never a retroactive backfill of a prior snapshot.

================================================================
REPORTING — WHO READS, WHO PUBLISHES, WHO NUMBERS
================================================================

  - Pending row is reported on its own line. It is additive. It
    does not roll into any of the four final rows and it does not
    enter any rate, denominator, or activation commentary.
  - Readout lane: Owen (shape + expansion review). Standing-lane
    neutral readouts; pending stays visible, not folded.
  - Reporting cadence and segment cuts — Owen, mid-segment.
  - Cross-surface consistency across Helio Start, Expansion
    Assist, and lifecycle messaging — sourced from the locked
    12/16 + 12/20 rule. If two readouts disagree, the rule wins;
    Daniela's trace settles which read is fresh.
  - External commentary on activation or mid-segment rate must
    not include pending as a denominator component.

================================================================
PRE-LAUNCH QA POSTURE (for new operators seeing pending on
campaign traffic)
================================================================

  - Staging first, then isolated campaign at $0 spend.
  - No eligibility-flow entry for the pending row.
  - Daniela's acknowledgment required before any pending record
    touches a live eligibility-flow lane.
  - "paused" in the campaign UI is the V11 bypass. Do not treat
    a paused campaign as live eligibility authority.
  - CS coverage for routing pending rows: 8a–6p Central.
  - If a pending record surfaces on a live eligibility path,
    stop the path and route to Daniela. Do not advance the row
    under any campaign setting.

================================================================
ESCALATION CHEAT-SHEET
================================================================

  State-meaning, dispute, customer correction, or ambiguous
    forward-event interpretation  → Riley
  Engineering release, rollback, replay, held-queue release,
    auth-side issue, refresh-cadence trace                  → Daniela
  Lifecycle suppression / reclassification, prompt-hold
    definition, routine-education boundary                  → Ines
  Readout shape, segment cuts, mid-segment rate readouts    → Owen
  Routing for pending external_authority, daily CS-side
    verification, forward routing to admitted / assisted /
    ineligible                                              → CS
  Cross-team coordination while a record is in pending      → Priya

  If you are unsure whether something is a state-meaning
  change, a customer correction, or an incident stop — it
  goes to Riley. If you are unsure whether something is a
  release or rollback — it goes to Daniela. Do not act on
  the unsure case.

================================================================
SCOPE OF THIS CARD
================================================================

  This is a new-operator field card. It does not redefine the
  five-state model, does not change the intake rule, does not
  widen any escalation lane, and does not move release or
  rollback control. Source of authority remains the 12/16
  op-instruction + 12/20 rewrite, restated here for quick use.

  If a case you are looking at does not fit any of the five
  states above, that is a routing question, not a definition
  question. Send it to Riley.

  it resolves to a forward event — verify → admitted, assist →
  assisted, refuse → ineligible. Landing is a new forward event,
  never a retroactive backfill of a prior snapshot.

================================================================

    does not roll into any of the four final rows and it does not

    12/16 + 12/20 rule. If two readouts disagree, the rule wins;

    not include pending as a denominator component.

campaign traffic)
================================================================

    stop the path and route to Daniela. Do not advance the row
    under any campaign setting.

================================================================

    forward-event interpretation  → Riley
  Engineering release, rollback, replay, held-queue release,
    auth-side issue, refresh-cadence trace                  → Daniela

  change, a customer correction, or an incident stop — it
  goes to Riley. If you are unsure whether something is a
  release or rollback — it goes to Daniela. Do not act on
  the unsure case.

================================================================
SCOPE OF THIS CARD
================================================================

  This is a new-operator field card. It does not redefine the
  five-state model, does not change the intake rule, does not
  widen any escalation lane, and does not move release or
  rollback control. Source of authority remains the 12/16
  op-instruction + 12/20 rewrite, restated here for quick use.

  question. Send it to Riley.

tests.request: Create a document in the `Growth archive` folder titled `Expansion Assist — first-pilot cohort integrity note`. State the exact operational exposure maximum separately from the locked primary reporting denominator. Also document the rule for prompts during outcome maturation and how reserve exposures must be handled, so analysts can safely reuse the mature-window reporting population.

input.body:
Operational exposure maximum (separate from reporting denominator)

The operational exposure maximum is the highest number of accounts that could ever be counted as Expansion Assist exposures under any reasonable reading of the cohort definition. It is a ceiling, not the cohort. For the first pilot it is the total population that entered the eligibility-flow window (the paid-source eligibility-flow starts that began on 11/19), before any of the maturation cuts below are applied. The number in this row is allowed to move up only; it must never decrease, and it is not used as a denominator in any locked reporting view.

Locked primary reporting denominator

The primary reporting denominator for the first pilot is the mature-window reporting population described in the next section. It is locked at the moment the maturation window closes for the cohort and does not change afterward except for explicit, documented corrections. Any analyst reusing the mature-window population must treat this denominator as fixed.

Rule for prompts during outcome maturation

While outcome maturation is still in progress for a cohort, no analyst may issue ad hoc queries against the in-flight cohort that would re-define, re-cut, or otherwise disturb the reporting population. Routine line-edits and descriptive cuts are not permitted against the maturing cohort; only the locked cuts and the disputed / cross-cohort / exec-scope queries that are already on file are allowed. Once the maturation window closes and the denominator is locked, normal descriptive analysis resumes against the fixed population.

Reserve exposures

Reserve exposures — accounts that are part of the operational exposure maximum but not part of the locked primary reporting denominator — must be held aside and reported separately. They are not folded into the primary denominator, not netted against it, and not used to recompute it. If a reserve exposure later becomes eligible for the primary population under the documented cohort rules, it is added via an explicit, dated correction to the denominator; it is never silently merged in. Analysts reusing the mature-window reporting population may do so only against the locked denominator, with reserve exposures tracked alongside.
