arguments.title: Helio Start pre-discovery readout — measurement spine
arguments.body:
Pre-read for Monday. Builds on the baseline summary Priya already read. Goal of this doc: lock the measurement spine before we go further on naming, lifecycle, or pricing mechanics.

Sections:
1. Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
2. Measurement method
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
5. Open questions (lifecycle, instrumentation, support, eng sizing)

—
1. Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
—

"Helio Start" is the working name for the sub-50-seat tier we are pre-discovering. It is internal shorthand only.

Priya's gate (2023-06-14): the name implies nothing customer-facing until all of the following are ready — eligibility rules, refusal rules, instrumentation, lifecycle paths, and support boundaries. Nothing in this doc, in the baseline summary, or in any Slack thread should be read as a launch commitment, a launch date, or a marketing promise.

If this tier ships, the working name may change. Anything written here should hold under that.

—
2. Measurement method
—

Cohort definitions (locked):
- Mid-seg v2 = 75–200 seats (default since 2023-04-26). 50–75 = starter band. v1 (50–200) stays in the warehouse for back-compat comps only — we do not roll v1 forward.
- Under-50 / sub-50 = the band this tier work is actually about. We report it separately from mid-seg v2 in every cut going forward.

Activation (locked):
- Activation definition v3: `+ ≥1 in-product event in 14d` (locked 2023-03-16). Target: 60% for mid-seg+ in 14d; the conditional 65% target is tied to sub-50 tier ship in Q3 and is not in scope of this doc.
- Activation KPI is owned by me.

What we measure for the sub-50 work (per the 2023-06-01 small-biz tier scoping):
- Activation deltas (vs. control, vs. mid-seg v2 baseline)
- Support load (tickets / contact rate per activated account, by seat band)
- Gross retention by seat band (we are NOT using ACV as a metric for this tier)

What we explicitly do NOT do in this readout:
- We do not pool 50–75 into mid-seg v2. The 50–75 band is reported on its own line.
- We do not mix sub-50 cuts with the mid-seg v2 cohort for significance. They are separate populations with different effect-size expectations.
- We do not use first-significance-only as evidence. Standing rule from 2023-03-26: first sig on a growth exp does not ship — wait one stab cohort. Pre-registered stab def (same metric, same direction, n ≥ treatment) plus p<0.01 on the second-look cohort must clear before the next peek.

Cuts (per Owen's cadence, locked 2023-02-13): every ruling — in or out — gets a 1-pager with why, cuts, p-value, effect-size, and call. Summary up top, raw attached.

—
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
—

Headline: simple under-50 deployments where the customer lands a first integration inside week 1 are already behaving near the target range. The gap is not in the happy path — the gap is in the friction modes around it.

Specifically:
- Near target: first-week first integration on simple under-50 deployments. Activation v3 sits in the band we would expect a healthy sub-50 segment to reach if the deployment stayed simple.
- Lagging by more than 15 points: permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity. Each of these on its own pulls activation v3 down by ≥15 points relative to the simple-deployment baseline.

Read: the activation ceiling for sub-50 is not gated by acquisition quality or by the product's ability to deliver value on a clean install. It is gated by the four friction modes above. Any tier design that does not address those four modes will not move the activation KPI regardless of pricing, naming, or lifecycle cadence.

Implication for scoping: the four friction modes are the spine of what "Helio Start" needs to actually solve. Anything we add on top (lifecycle nudges, expansion plays, pricing-page mechanics) is downstream of these four.

We are NOT yet calling this finding "shippable." It is a baseline read, not a treatment effect. It needs the second-look cohort before we promote it.

—
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
—

Pending decisions — to be locked before any customer-facing naming:

Eligibility (open):
- Which seat bands qualify. Band 20–75 is pending as the working envelope; we need a clean ruling on whether 20–50, 50–75, or 20–75 is the in-scope band for the tier.
- Self-serve vs. sales-assisted boundary for sub-50. Affects refusal-rule design.
- Trial vs. freemium vs. paid-only entry. Affects refusal rules and instrumentation scope.

Refusal rules (open):
- When do we say "this customer is not a Helio Start fit" — at signup, at first-integration miss, at billing-failure, or at migration-complexity flag?
- What is the escalation path for refused accounts (sales handoff, hold queue, manual review)? Affects support load metric.

Pre-read for Monday. Builds on the baseline summary Priya already read. Goal of this doc: lock the measurement spine before we go further on naming, lifecycle, or pricing mechanics.

How to read this doc: the refusal rules, eligibility checks, and tier design we are pre-discovering exist to protect customers from a self-serve setup that won't deliver value for them. If a setup will fail for an account — whether because of permissions, import, billing, or migration complexity, or because the account's needs exceed what self-serve carries — the right move is to route that account to a path where they can succeed, not to push them through a plan they will churn out of. Every refusal rule below should be readable as a customer safeguard first.

Sections:
1. Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
2. Measurement method
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
5. Open questions (lifecycle, instrumentation, support, eng sizing)

—
1. Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
—

"Helio Start" is the working name for the sub-50-seat tier we are pre-discovering. It is internal shorthand only.

Priya's gate (2023-06-14): the name implies nothing customer-facing until all of the following are ready — eligibility rules, refusal rules, instrumentation, lifecycle paths, and support boundaries. Nothing in this doc, in the baseline summary, or in any Slack thread should be read as a launch commitment, a launch date, or a marketing promise.

The framing is protective, not exclusionary: we are pre-discovering whether the tier can be designed so that customers who enter it have a realistic path to activation, and so that customers the tier won't serve are routed to a path that does. If the design can't meet that bar, the right answer is to not ship the tier, not to ship it with weaker rules.

If this tier ships, the working name may change. Anything written here should hold under that.

—
2. Measurement method
—

Cohort definitions (locked):
- Mid-seg v2 = 75–200 seats (default since 2023-04-26). 50–75 = starter band. v1 (50–200) stays in the warehouse for back-compat comps only — we do not roll v1 forward.
- Under-50 / sub-50 = the band this tier work is actually about. We report it separately from mid-seg v2 in every cut going forward.

Activation (locked):
- Activation definition v3: `+ ≥1 in-product event in 14d` (locked 2023-03-16). Target: 60% for mid-seg+ in 14d; the conditional 65% target is tied to sub-50 tier ship in Q3 and is not in scope of this doc.
- Activation KPI is owned by me.

What we measure for the sub-50 work (per the 2023-06-01 small-biz tier scoping):
- Activation deltas (vs. control, vs. mid-seg v2 baseline)
- Support load (tickets / contact rate per activated account, by seat band)
- Gross retention by seat band (we are NOT using ACV as a metric for this tier)

What we explicitly do NOT do in this readout:
- We do not pool 50–75 into mid-seg v2. The 50–75 band is reported on its own line.
- We do not mix sub-50 cuts with the mid-seg v2 cohort for significance. They are separate populations with different effect-size expectations.
- We do not use first-significance-only as evidence. Standing rule from 2023-03-26: first sig on a growth exp does not ship — wait one stab cohort. Pre-registered stab def (same metric, same direction, n ≥ treatment) plus p<0.01 on the second-look cohort must clear before the next peek.

Cuts (per Owen's cadence, locked 2023-02-13): every ruling — in or out — gets a 1-pager with why, cuts, p-value, effect-size, and call. Summary up top, raw attached.

—
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
—

Caveat on what this section shows (Owen, 2023-06-17): the baseline below is descriptive, not causal. It describes what we observe in the data, not what produces activation. In particular, first-week first integration is observed alongside activation in simple deployments — it is not, by itself, established as the cause of activation. We will not promote any framing that treats first-week integration as the lever that "creates" activation until we have a treatment effect in a controlled cut.

Headline: simple under-50 deployments where the customer lands a first integration inside week 1 are already behaving near the target range. The gap is not in the happy path — the gap is in the friction modes around it.

Specifically:
- Near target: first-week first integration on simple under-50 deployments. Activation v3 sits in the band we would expect a healthy sub-50 segment to reach if the deployment stayed simple.
- Lagging by more than 15 points: permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity. Each of these on its own pulls activation v3 down by ≥15 points relative to the simple-deployment baseline.

Read (descriptive): across the sub-50 population we have today, activation v3 is high in the simple-deployment, first-week-first-integration subset and lower in the four friction modes. The descriptive pattern is consistent with — but does not prove — those friction modes being the binding constraint on the segment's activation ceiling. A treatment-effect read (does fixing each mode move activation in a controlled cut?) is the next step.

Implication for scoping: if a future controlled cut confirms the friction-mode pattern as causal, the activation ceiling for sub-50 is gated by those four modes, not by acquisition quality or by the product's ability to deliver value on a clean install. Anything we add on top (lifecycle nudges, expansion plays, pricing-page mechanics) would be downstream of these four. Until that controlled cut lands, we treat the friction modes as the leading candidate spine for what "Helio Start" would need to actually solve — not as a confirmed one.

We are NOT yet calling this finding "shippable." It is a baseline read, not a treatment effect. It needs the second-look cohort and a controlled cut before we promote it.

—
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
—

Framing (Priya, 2023-06-17): the labels below are written so the tier reads as protective for the customer, not as a screen that sorts accounts into a lower tier. We don't say "this account isn't a fit for us." We say "this self-serve setup won't carry this account" — and route them to a path where the setup does carry them. The same framing applies to entry-mechanic choices: trial vs. freemium vs. paid-only entry is about making sure the customer has enough runway and context to succeed, not about offering a cheaper plan.

Pending decisions — to be locked before any customer-facing naming:

Eligibility (open):
- Which seat bands qualify. Band 20–75 is pending as the working envelope; we need a clean ruling on whether 20–50, 50–75, or 20–75 is the in-scope band for the tier. Bands describe what the self-serve setup can carry, not what tier of customer we're willing to take.
- Self-serve vs. sales-assisted boundary for sub-50. Affects refusal-rule design — the question is at what point an account needs a human to succeed, not at what point we choose not to sell to them.
- Trial vs. freemium vs. paid-only entry. The choice is governed by what gives the customer a fair chance to land a first integration and learn whether the product carries their use case — not by offering a lower-priced path.

Refusal rules (open):
- When do we route an account off the self-serve path — at signup, at first-integration miss, at billing-failure, or at migration-complexity flag? Each trigger is a moment where the self-serve setup has stopped carrying the account, and the right response is to move them to a path that does.

- How refusal interacts with the four friction modes: if a customer hits permissions or migration friction, do we route, hold, or sequence? The principle is the same — the self-serve path has stopped carrying the account, so we don't keep them on it.

—
5. Open questions
—

Lifecycle:
- What is the in-product nudge cadence for the four friction modes? Standing rule (2023-03-26) applies — first sig does not ship, wait one stab cohort.
- Email vs. in-product vs. PostHog-flagged-only routing for sub-50 expansion plays — must stay disambiguated from email-lift attribution per the expansion_nudge_60d_v1 precedent (launched 2023-05-23, mid-seg v2 only).
- How does the lifecycle path branch when a customer hits a refusal rule? The branch should be a hand-off to a setup that will carry them, not a stop sign.

Instrumentation:
- Are permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity each individually evented in PostHog with sufficient coverage to support the activation v3 cut? Need an audit before we can run the 1-pagers.
- Seat-band tagging at signup — do we have a reliable band-at-signup field, or do we reconstruct it post-hoc? Affects whether eligibility can be measured cleanly.
- Refusal-rule eventing — what fires when a refusal rule trips, and where does it land in the warehouse? Need the same eventing for the routing hand-off, not just the refusal moment.

Support:
- Support load model for the four friction modes — what is the expected ticket volume per activated sub-50 account under each mode? Marcus Vail (CRO) alignment requires this to be explicit before any instrumentation commitments land.
- Support boundary: what does Helio support cover for the tier vs. what falls to self-serve docs / community? The boundary should make it clear to the customer where the hand-off is.
- How refusal escalations hit support load — do they count against the support-load metric for this tier? Need this pinned before we read the load number.

Engineering sizing:
- Daniela (eng) capacity is the binding constraint. Need a clean read on the eng ask for the four friction-mode fixes before we can promise anything to Marcus Vail on a ship window.
- Which of the four friction modes are quick wins vs. multi-quarter work? Determines whether we scope to a v0 of the tier or wait for a fuller build.
- Instrumentation work above — eng sizing depends on what the audit surfaces.

—
End of pre-read. Next step: walk this with Priya Monday, then lock the band decision and start the instrumentation audit.

   - Event taxonomy locked, baseline cuts delivered

   - Lifecycle/support fork map delivered
   - Ship-readiness revisited end of June with the four outputs in hand

This is internal pre-discovery, not a Q3 promise. No external motion until the June gate lands.

arguments.title: Helio Start pre-discovery readout — measurement spine
arguments.body:
Pre-read for Monday. Builds on the baseline summary Priya already read. Goal of this doc: lock the measurement spine before we go further on naming, lifecycle, or pricing mechanics.

Sections:
1. Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
2. Measurement method
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
5. Open questions (lifecycle, instrumentation, support, eng sizing)

—
1. Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
—

"Helio Start" is the working name for the sub-50-seat tier we are pre-discovering. It is internal shorthand only.

Priya's gate (2023-06-14): the name implies nothing customer-facing until all of the following are ready — eligibility rules, refusal rules, instrumentation, lifecycle paths, and support boundaries. Nothing in this doc, in the baseline summary, or in any Slack thread should be read as a launch commitment, a launch date, or a marketing promise.

If this tier ships, the working name may change. Anything written here should hold under that.

—
2. Measurement method
—

Cohort definitions (locked):
- Mid-seg v2 = 75–200 seats (default since 2023-04-26). 50–75 = starter band. v1 (50–200) stays in the warehouse for back-compat comps only — we do not roll v1 forward.
- Under-50 / sub-50 = the band this tier work is actually about. We report it separately from mid-seg v2 in every cut going forward.

Activation (locked):
- Activation definition v3: `+ ≥1 in-product event in 14d` (locked 2023-03-16). Target: 60% for mid-seg+ in 14d; the conditional 65% target is tied to sub-50 tier ship in Q3 and is not in scope of this doc.
- Activation KPI is owned by me.

What we measure for the sub-50 work (per the 2023-06-01 small-biz tier scoping):
- Activation deltas (vs. control, vs. mid-seg v2 baseline)
- Support load (tickets / contact rate per activated account, by seat band)
- Gross retention by seat band (we are NOT using ACV as a metric for this tier)

What we explicitly do NOT do in this readout:
- We do not pool 50–75 into mid-seg v2. The 50–75 band is reported on its own line.
- We do not mix sub-50 cuts with the mid-seg v2 cohort for significance. They are separate populations with different effect-size expectations.
- We do not use first-significance-only as evidence. Standing rule from 2023-03-26: first sig on a growth exp does not ship — wait one stab cohort. Pre-registered stab def (same metric, same direction, n ≥ treatment) plus p<0.01 on the second-look cohort must clear before the next peek.

Cuts (per Owen's cadence, locked 2023-02-13): every ruling — in or out — gets a 1-pager with why, cuts, p-value, effect-size, and call. Summary up top, raw attached.

—
3. Baseline finding (under-50 deployments)
—

Headline: simple under-50 deployments where the customer lands a first integration inside week 1 are already behaving near the target range. The gap is not in the happy path — the gap is in the friction modes around it.

Specifically:
- Near target: first-week first integration on simple under-50 deployments. Activation v3 sits in the band we would expect a healthy sub-50 segment to reach if the deployment stayed simple.
- Lagging by more than 15 points: permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity. Each of these on its own pulls activation v3 down by ≥15 points relative to the simple-deployment baseline.

Read: the activation ceiling for sub-50 is not gated by acquisition quality or by the product's ability to deliver value on a clean install. It is gated by the four friction modes above. Any tier design that does not address those four modes will not move the activation KPI regardless of pricing, naming, or lifecycle cadence.

Implication for scoping: the four friction modes are the spine of what "Helio Start" needs to actually solve. Anything we add on top (lifecycle nudges, expansion plays, pricing-page mechanics) is downstream of these four.

We are NOT yet calling this finding "shippable." It is a baseline read, not a treatment effect. It needs the second-look cohort before we promote it.

—
4. Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
—

Pending decisions — to be locked before any customer-facing naming:

Eligibility (open):
- Which seat bands qualify. Band 20–75 is pending as the working envelope; we need a clean ruling on whether 20–50, 50–75, or 20–75 is the in-scope band for the tier.
- Self-serve vs. sales-assisted boundary for sub-50. Affects refusal-rule design.
- Trial vs. freemium vs. paid-only entry. Affects refusal rules and instrumentation scope.

Refusal rules (open):
- When do we say "this customer is not a Helio Start fit" — at signup, at first-integration miss, at billing-failure, or at migration-complexity flag?
- What is the escalation path for refused accounts (sales handoff, hold queue, manual review)? Affects support load metric.
- How refusal interacts with the four friction modes: if a customer hits permissions or migration friction, do we refuse, route, or sequence?

Implication of the baseline: refusal rules need to be at least as good at catching the four friction modes as they are at catching fit-mismatches. A tier that refuses on fit but admits on permissions complexity will still miss the activation target.

Naming implication: until eligibility and refusal rules are locked, "Helio Start" stays internal. We will not surface the name in lifecycle copy, pricing, or sales conversations.

—
5. Open questions
—

Lifecycle:
- What is the in-product nudge cadence for the four friction modes? Standing rule (2023-03-26) applies — first sig does not ship, wait one stab cohort.
- Email vs. in-product vs. PostHog-flagged-only routing for sub-50 expansion plays — must stay disambiguated from email-lift attribution per the expansion_nudge_60d_v1 precedent (launched 2023-05-23, mid-seg v2 only).
- How does the lifecycle path branch when a customer hits a refusal rule?

Instrumentation:
- Are permissions, import, billing, and migration complexity each individually evented in PostHog with sufficient coverage to support the activation v3 cut? Need an audit before we can run the 1-pagers.
- Seat-band tagging at signup — do we have a reliable band-at-signup field, or do we reconstruct it post-hoc? Affects whether eligibility can be measured cleanly.
- Refusal-rule eventing — what fires when a refusal rule trips, and where does it land in the warehouse?

Support:
- Support load model for the four friction modes — what is the expected ticket volume per activated sub-50 account under each mode? Marcus Vail (CRO) alignment requires this to be explicit before any instrumentation commitments land.
- Support boundary: what does Helio support cover for the tier vs. what falls to self-serve docs / community?
- How refusal escalations hit support load — do they count against the support-load metric for this tier?

Engineering sizing:
- Daniela (eng) capacity is the binding constraint. Need a clean read on the eng ask for the four friction-mode fixes before we can promise anything to Marcus Vail on a ship window.
- Which of the four friction modes are quick wins vs. multi-quarter work? Determines whether we scope to a v0 of the tier or wait for a fuller build.
- Instrumentation work above — eng sizing depends on what the audit surfaces.

—
End of pre-read. Next step: walk this with Priya Monday, then lock the band decision and start the instrumentation audit.

# Lifecycle Systems — Operating Review
**Mar 4, 3:00–4:00pm CT** · Riley, Priya, Owen, Ines, Daniela
**Purpose:** Separate what is already operating from what remains gated. One page. No re-litigation of settled calls.

---

## Operating today (in production, governed)

### 1. Owen — reporting & exception lane
- **Reporting shape:** cohort + segment cuts, mid-segment focused (Riley's standing read for the Monday w/ Owen). Measurement definitions, denominators, and routine exception carve-outs live here.
- **Exception lane:** standing lane holds ≤3 neutral exceptions/week; anything beyond stale-fails-closed. Exceptions are descriptive only — never forecasts or eligibility calls.
- **Ruling format:** 1-pager per exception — *why / cuts / p / effect / call*; summary first, plain questions.

### 2. Ines — lifecycle-governance lane
- **Audit-risk ownership** across the lifecycle send surface (lifecycle emails, lifecycle state transitions, the held-release queue).
- **Account-status `routine education`** is treated as a HIGHER-RISK lifecycle send; Ines reclassifies, runs a fresh preflight, contractor docs only. Boundary = Riley for judgment escalations.
- **Expansion Assist** sits in this lane as **descriptive, non-forecast only** — no rate math, no activation denominator moves.
- **Lag recovery** is **forward-only**: when a delayed export/refresh resolves, recheck current state — do NOT restore pre-lag eligibility. Held rows stay held.
- **Misuse/disposal** charges require visit-specific lease basis + evidence of resident-attributable damage; absent both, charge is removed (precedent: Disposal $165, 2025-01-18).

### 3. Daniela — transport & source-reliability lane
- **Source-of-truth transport** for lifecycle state to consumers (analytics, lifecycle sends, finance reconciliation).
- **Source-reliability signals** (freshness, catch-up, consumer lag) are her responsibility to surface, not to adjudicate. Fulfillment ≠ verification.
- **Not-yet-live shared-state feed** (separate from the live freshness alarm below) is owned here — Daniela raises when a consumer drifts from src; Riley/Ines rule.

### 4. Export freshness alarm (LIVE since 2025-02-20, owned by Daniela)
- **Thresholds:** 2hr warn / 4hr crit, measured against src + consumer as-of timestamps.
- **Auto-clears** on verified catch-up. Audit retains the interval window; no eligibility authority — held rows stay held, forward-only holds survive rollback.
- **Drill validated 2025-02-21:** 3 consumers preserved selectors through a delay, no eligibility rewind.

---

## Gated (accepted but not yet shipped)

### 5. Lifecycle-preflight *operator view* — accepted, not yet implemented
- **What it is:** a read-only operator surface showing the preflight state (held rows, classifier confidence, source-freshness, exception counters) per cohort / per send.
- **Why gated:** the underlying preflight logic is operating (Ines's lane uses it manually), but the operator UI hasn't been scoped, prioritized, or staffed. No review meeting has signed off on the read-only surface.
- **Open to decide:** scope (single cohort vs. cross-cohort), access (Riley + Ines only, or broader read?), freshness contract (does it consume the same alarm feed, or its own derived view?).

### 6. Shared-state production replay & release — still unapproved
- **What it is:** the production replay path that would let us reproduce a shared-state lifecycle event end-to-end (src → transport → consumer) for any historical window, plus the release process that gates changes to that shared-state surface.
- **Why gated:** shared-state changes cut across all three lanes and the freshness alarm. The replay path needs Owen (measurement reproducibility), Ines (audit trail + held-row fidelity), and Daniela (transport semantics) to align on a contract before approval. Fulfillment ≠ verification — replay is a verification tool, not a fulfillment substitute.
- **Open to decide:** replay scope (full vs. sampled), retention window, who can trigger, whether release requires Ines sign-off in addition to engineering sign-off.

---

## What I want out of the hour
1. Confirm the operating-vs-gated split is accurate — anyone see a lane or item in the wrong bucket?
2. Preflight operator view: pick a scope for v1 (single cohort? access model?).
3. Shared-state replay/release: name the blockers (Riley: held-row fidelity / forward-only; Ines: audit trail; Daniela: transport contract; Owen: measurement reproducibility). Who owns each before next review.
4. Reconfirm standing-lane cadence and escalation path between this review and the Monday cohort read.

---

## Apr 15 operating retro — outcome (2025-04-15, 3:00–3:45pm CT)

The Apr 15 retro (Priya, Owen, Ines, Daniela, Riley) reviewed whether the four lanes that grew out of the 3/24 audit-role ruling are actually working under first live load, and whether the CS auto-nudge integration fits inside that lane mix or forces a rebalance. This retro is **not a release decision** and remains non-prescriptive.

**Conclusion.** The current division of work is functioning. No capacity reassignment is made.

**Lane ownership — unchanged:**
- **Owen** continues to own routine measurement and exception explanation (shape + ex integrity; std Helio Start report circulated independently; standing-lane cap ≤3 neutral/wk; stale fail-closed handling). Q2 lane addition of Lifecycle exec explanation + decision framing is absorbed at current load.
- **Ines** continues to own lifecycle governance and message-state work (audit-risk classification; `routine education` = HIGHER-RISK per 3/24 ruling, Ines reclassifies, Riley is boundary; routine-vs-disputed-semantics handoff and lag-recovery forward-only behavior under audit hold).
- **Daniela** retains engineering reliability and release controls (deploy hygiene; prod-path verification on shared-state changes; a11y copy discipline; replay / fallback / held-queue behavior on shared-state surfaces).
- **Riley** stays out of row-level review. The high-stakes decision lane remains — judgment escalations, disputed semantics, cross-surface rulings, exec language — and is entered only when a high-stakes decision or disputed meaning arises.

**CS auto-nudge integration.** The CS auto-nudge workback is kept **unchanged rather than turned into a release promise.** Auto-nudge exceptions continue to flow through the existing lane mix at its current load; no lane's standing-lane budget or boundary moves.

**Evidence gates (still gated, not flipped to operating):**

The following remain evidence gates that must close before any shared-state switch moves from gated to operating. None of them has closed yet, and none of them is being waved through:

- **Adapter completion** — the transport adapter that puts CS-side traffic onto shared Lifecycle Systems state.
- **Field-specific operator view** — the v1 lifecycle-preflight operator surface (Item 5 above), with field-specific scope, access, and freshness contract agreed.
- **Internal dry run** — Ines + Owen + Daniela rehearsal of the full held-queue / replay / fallback flow against current shared-state data.
- **April 24 historical replay** — the first historical-window replay through the production replay path, used as the verification gate for shared-state reproducibility, not as a fulfillment substitute.
- **Rollback validation** — confirmation that forward-only holds survive a rollback of any shared-state change, and that no eligibility or messaging state rewinds.
- **Any production shadow** — if shadow traffic is run, it is observational only; it is not used as causal evidence, not forecast credit, and does not authorize scope expansion.
- **Release review** — the gate that combines Owen's measurement reproducibility, Ines's audit-trail + held-row fidelity sign-off, and Daniela's transport-contract sign-off, with the trigger authority and sign-off chain agreed in advance.

**State of the production path.** The **legacy production path remains live**. **No shared-state switch has been made.** Lifecycle Systems state on the production surface continues to be the pre-shared-state implementation; the items above (operator view, replay/release, CS auto-nudge adapter) are not in production. Any read of shared-state lifecycle behavior against live data still goes through the existing lane mix against the legacy path, not against the gated shared-state path.

**Why no movement now.** The first live evidence (3/28 readout, 638 records; 4/3 personalization migration; CW-2025-218 close 4/4) is established and the lanes are absorbing it within their standing budgets. Expansion Assist remains descriptive, not prescriptive. Helio Start `pending` remains pre-admission and forward-only. Where shared state would matter — and where it would drift if lanes crossed — is still monitored through the existing readouts. The lane mix is holding. The retro keeps the gate where it is.

**Next review.** No follow-up operating retro is scheduled. Evidence-gate progress (adapter completion, operator-view v1 scope, internal dry run, Apr 24 replay, rollback validation, production shadow, release review) will be tracked in the standing lane readouts, not in a new operating record, until any one of those gates closes.

arguments.title: Q1 2027 Lifecycle Systems operating priorities — staff-review draft
arguments.body:
# Q1 2027 Lifecycle Systems operating priorities — staff-review draft

Author: Riley Tanaka
For: December 18 staff review (owner-lane input)
Status: DRAFT. Restates the December 4, 2026 decision already approved by Priya (Lifecycle Systems operating model, effective January 5, 2027). It is a Q1 restatement for staff review, not a new authority decision. Nothing in this draft takes effect early. Anything that conflicts with the Dec 4 decision record is overridden by that record; this draft surfaces the Q1 shape, not a re-decision.

---

## Summary (one page)

What changes on January 5, 2027 — and what does not:
- On January 5, Riley stops attending routine monthly Lifecycle Systems preparation and source-closure reviews. Through January 4, nothing changes — Riley continues current routine preparation and source-closure attendance as today.
- The four evidence lanes stay separate. No combined growth number. No cross-lane revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast credit.
- Owner lanes are unchanged. What changes is who carries the routine cadence and what Riley attends.
- The quarterly rotating recheck of one evidence lane is the concrete independent verification activity replacing prior hands-on attendance. It does not reopen source closure, approve any other lane owner's certification, or exercise any engineering control. It is an inspection, not a second approval queue.
- Future paid Helio Start is a separate question. Nothing in this draft approves traffic, budget, or scope for paid Helio Start.

## Q1 priorities — by lane (unchanged)

The four lanes are the established board-evidence lanes. They are kept separate. They are read independently. None of them is a revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast input.

- Helio Start. Lane owner: Owen (measurement) + Riley (final claims). Status through Q1: bounded-organic as it already is. Reporting inside the existing four-lane scope. Five-state model unchanged (admitted / assisted / ineligible / final-reconciliation + `pending` forward-only). `pending` stays pre-admission, NOT in the rate or activation denominator, intake additive. No Q1 launch, beta, pricing-page approval, or new consumer.
- Expansion Assist (retained-mid). Lane owner: Owen (eligibility cuts) + Ines (lifecycle governance) + Riley (final claims). Descriptive only. Causal language (drove / caused / prevented) deferred to a controlled read-out. No forecast or rollout.
- Pricing-page path quality. Lane owner: Owen (measurement) + Daniela (transport + rollout) + Riley (final claims). Lane supports only "fewer unsupported-path starts" — funnel-quality evidence, not revenue, paid-acquisition, pipeline, forecast, or eligibility.
- CS auto-nudge / system controls. Lane owner: Owen (reporting + exception explanation) + Ines (messaging-state governance) + Daniela (transport + source reliability + rollback). Lane is system-control performance, not a customer-behavior read.

## The four production consumers and their current field meanings

The four board-evidence lanes are the four production consumers of the operating state. Each lane carries the same seven required fields; "current field meanings" are what each field has meant in the deck-format operating evidence since FY26.

The seven required fields per lane (current meanings):
1. Denominator or coverage dates. What population and time window the lane covers. Read as the count plus the window, not the count alone.
2. Outcome window. The complete predeclared window the source supports. Read only inside the window; not truncated, not extended.
3. Measurement limits. What the source can and cannot say. Stated explicitly. Limits are part of the claim, not a footnote.
4. Exclusions. What is excluded from the lane's read and why. Documented. Consistent with how routine claims treat them.
5. Source owner. The named owner who certifies the lane's source completeness.
6. Reliability evidence. The evidence the source is intact (Daniela's lane inspects this; the recheck inspects it; engineering release controls stay with Daniela).
7. Revenue and forecast treatment. How the lane treats revenue and forecast. Descriptive lanes name it as descriptive. Causal/revenue/forecast decision rights are Riley's; the field records the treatment, not the decision.

These seven fields are what each lane carries today. The Jan 5 model preserves them; it changes who closes them.

## Current through January 4, 2027 — explicit

- Riley attends routine monthly Lifecycle Systems preparation and routine source-closure reviews as today.
- The four-lane cadence runs exactly as it does today. No new owner, no new role, no new authority.
- Nothing about the Dec 4 decision is in effect. It is approved; it is not yet effective.

## Effective January 5, 2027 — first January cycle

The first cycle under the new model opens Tuesday, January 5, 2027. (January 4 is a Monday and the last day of the prior routine; January 5 is the first effective day.) The cadence is unchanged in form; what changes is who carries it and how incomplete status is handled.

Cadence (effective January 5, 2027):
- Second business day. Owen's monthly sanitized campaign snapshot is due. Hard date against the calendar, not against completion of any other step.
- Fourth business day. Ines's lifecycle-governance and owner-state certification is due. Daniela's source-reliability and release certification is due.
- Fifth business day. Owen must either close the routine four-lane source review OR explicitly leave it incomplete. Either way, Owen sends one closure-and-exception summary — not informal follow-up fragments.

Incomplete handling (explicit, not "closed with notes"):
- If any required field on any lane is missing, the lane's status is recorded as explicitly incomplete. Not "ready with caveats." Not "closed with notes." Incomplete is incomplete. The closure cannot proceed in that state.
- If a named-owner certification (Owen for source completeness, Ines for lifecycle governance, Daniela's source-reliability and release certification) is not in place, the packet is incomplete. Closure cannot proceed.
- If Owen closes the packet incomplete, the closure-and-exception summary names the missing fields, the missing certifications, and the owner-attributed reason for each. The summary is the single written record for the cycle. Disputes, exceptions, and follow-ups fold into the summary, not into Slack threads, DMs, or email fragments.

The first January cycle is therefore a clean test of the new cadence under incomplete-handling rules. If a required field is missing on day 2, 4, or 5, the cycle closes incomplete and the exception summary names it. That is the intended operating behavior, not a failure.

## The quarterly rotating recheck (one lane per quarter)

Effective January 5, 2027, Riley enters the routine cadence only via the quarterly rotating recheck of one evidence lane. The recheck is independent verification, not a second approval queue.

Shape:
- Cadence. One recheck per quarter.
- Subject. One evidence lane per quarter, picked by Riley.
- Lane selection. Only after Owen's routine packet closure for the relevant cycle is recorded. The recheck cannot shape the routine sample and cannot quietly become a second closure review.
- Inspection dimensions (fixed, five). Denominator or coverage dates; outcome window; exclusions; reliability evidence; revenue and forecast treatment.
- Safeguards (fixed, four). Does not reopen source closure; does not approve Ines's owner certification; does not exercise Daniela's release or rollback controls; does not create a second approval queue.
- Artifact. One-page recheck note per quarter, filed in the Lifecycle Systems folder by the second business day of the week following the quarter close. The note cites Owen's recorded source-completeness decision for the cycle the lane belongs to and is filed separately from the routine closure packet.
- Time budget. Half-day at most. Not a substitute for routine prep, source closure, owner certification, or engineering controls.

What the recheck is NOT:
- Not a request for Riley to approve or reject any other lane owner's certification.
- Not a release / suppress / restore / rollback action.
- Not a route for second approval of routine claims.
- Not a calibration instrument (the November 17 working notes were not delivered feedback and did not expand authority).

If the recheck's findings need action, they flow through the existing escalation set (see below) or as input to the next cycle's source-completeness decision — never as an amendment to the current cycle's closure.

## Escalation triggers retained (Riley enters on these)

The escalation set is closed. Six triggers. Adding a trigger requires Riley's sign-off; removing one is not on the table.

1. Missing fields in a routine packet.
2. Disputed semantics on a defined term or claim surface.
3. Cross-surface discrepancies (a number that reconciles in one surface but not another).
4. Customer corrections (a customer has flagged an inaccuracy affecting a routine claim).
5. Incident stops (anything that pauses, rolls back, or quarantines a routine cycle).
6. Executive-language decisions (any claim headed to exec, board, investor, or external comms surfaces).

Escalation is into Riley's queue, not a request to skip Riley. Owen / Ines remain the named owners; Riley arbitrates and decides.

## Decision-owner boundaries (established, unchanged)

- Owen Pham. Routine single-path operating explanation + exception explanation. Source-completeness closure on routine packets. Within scope: monthly sanitized campaign snapshot by second business day; routine exception readouts on the four-lane scope (≤3 neutral readouts per week; stale fail-closed); Helio Start reporting as one of the existing shared-state consumers; the day-5 closure or explicit incomplete recording + closure-and-exception summary. Outside scope: causal / revenue / forecast / board-readiness / exec-language decisions; approval of Ines's certification; engineering release / suppress / restore / rollback controls.
- Ines Kovac. Lifecycle governance and message-state controls. Within scope: lifecycle-governance certification by fourth business day; owner-state certification; messaging consumption tied to shared-state; Expansion Assist descriptive posture; `routine education` reclassification authority (HIGHER-RISK); boundary to Riley on disputed semantics and exec language. Outside scope: source-completeness closure; engineering release controls; causal / revenue / forecast interpretation.
- Daniela Schultz. Transport, source reliability, and engineering release / rollback controls. Within scope: source-reliability and release certification by fourth business day; the rollback path as one of the two approved restore conditions (the other is Riley-led customer correction / incident stop); reliability evidence for the recheck's fourth dimension. Outside scope: lifecycle governance; source-completeness closure; causal / revenue / forecast treatment decisions.
- Riley Tanaka. Final claim authority + the recheck + escalation. Within scope: causal / revenue / forecast / board-readiness / exec-language decisions; the quarterly rotating recheck; arbitration on the six escalation triggers; judgment-boundary ownership for cross-surface lifecycle decisions. Outside scope: routine prep; routine source-closure attendance (effective Jan 5); engineering release controls.

## Boundaries preserved at the Q1 frame (carried over from the Dec 4 decision)

- Engineering reliability and release controls remain with Daniela's organization.
- Customer Success case ownership does not transfer.
- Expansion Assist remains descriptive, not forecast.
- Helio Start intake rule remains additive; refusal semantics are unchanged; five-state model preserved.
- The shared state contract is not in production as a result of this draft or the Dec 4 decision. Any production rollout requires a separate go decision with its own change-control path (Ines on governance, Daniela's org on reliability).
- Existing domain authority for each surface owner is preserved.

## Cuts (what this draft does NOT do)

- Does not change lane ownership. Owen / Ines / Daniela / Riley lanes are the same.
- Does not change the four-lane scope or count.
- Does not change the seven required fields per lane or their meanings.
- Does not authorize any Q1 production rollout of a shared-state implementation.
- Does not reopen Expansion Assist's descriptive posture or convert it into a forecast input.
- Does not authorize a fifth consumer.
- Does not delegate disputed semantics, cross-surface consequences, customer-correction / incident-stop, or exec-language carry away from Riley.
- Does not imply a re-decision. The Dec 4 decision is the decision; this draft surfaces its Q1 shape for staff review.

## Future paid Helio Start — held separately

The future paid Helio Start question is held separately. This draft does not:
- approve or imply approved traffic for paid Helio Start;
- approve or imply approved budget for paid Helio Start;
- change Helio Start's product or pricing status;
- change the existing reopen conditions (the 5/18 paid-acq cap and 8/21 denials of second-batch / pipeline / forecast credit carry forward until a separate go decision).

The paid-Helio-Start question has its own review path and its own decision owner. It is not part of the Q1 Lifecycle Systems operating priorities and is not addressed by them.

## Calls for staff review (December 18)

1. Confirm the Q1 shape matches the Dec 4 decision record. Any amendment to a lane boundary, the recheck shape, or the escalation set is a re-decision, not a staff-review edit.
2. Confirm the four lanes stay separate through Q1. No combined growth number; no cross-lane revenue / forecast credit.
3. Confirm the seven required fields per lane and their current meanings are preserved under the Jan 5 cadence.
4. Confirm the first January cycle (Jan 5 open; second / fourth / fifth business-day cadence; explicit incomplete handling) is the intended operating behavior.
5. Flag any conflict between this draft and the wider Q1 plan so we reconcile before Q1 starts.

---

End of draft. Status: DRAFT for December 18 staff review. Owner-lane input invited. The Dec 4 decision is the decision; this is its Q1 restatement.

messages.content:
Ruling: No — decline the swap.

Summary
The two workstreams are not fungible. Expansion Assist is descriptive by design ("no routine line-edit"); bumping it to 4 routine prompts/week re-categorizes it as an optimization lever and dilutes the disputed/cross/exec signal it's meant to hold. And the rule is sequential, not slot-substitution: finishing (or skipping) a Helio Start paid batch does not open a paid-test seat for an unrelated Expansion Assist change. The "extra prompt" isn't a growth action — it's a routine cadence change that hasn't cleared the growth method bar.

Why
- Expansion Assist's purpose: capture disputed, cross-functional, and exec items. Routine volume increase is explicitly out of scope per the standing rule. Release/rollback is Daniela's lane; routine expansion is not.
- Sequential workstreams: Helio Start batch landing or not is a Helio Start decision. Expansion Assist volume is a separate workstream with its own brief, its own hypothesis, and its own powered read.
- Growth method (eff 7/6/27): every shipped action needs primary metric + min effect pre-launch, 21-day powered read, effect size + CI, safety-guardrail interim review, and a full stabilization cohort pre-ship. "Using the room" is not a substitute for that design.
- Ines's H1 '27 MET on Expansion Assist was ≤3/wk. Moving past 3 is a metric-boundary change, not a swap-in.

Cuts
- Decline treating "extra routine prompt" as a replacement growth action.
- Decline running Expansion Assist volume increase as if it were the next paid-batch slot.

P (preconditions if Expansion Assist volume is ever reopened on its own merits — not as a swap)
- New brief, descriptive-signal hypothesis (e.g., does raising the floor catch more disputed/cross/exec items earlier?), not an optimization hypothesis.
- Daniela sign-off on the cadence change and on release/rollback ownership.
- Re-baseline Ines's MET against the 3/wk ceiling before any change ships.

Effect
Saying yes conflates two workstreams, lowers Expansion Assist's signal quality, and spends the freed slot on something that doesn't clear the growth method bar.

Call
Decline the swap. If the stakeholder wants to revisit Expansion Assist cadence, it goes through its own brief with Daniela in the loop — not as the replacement for a Helio Start batch.

Saving the study sheet to your home dir so you can pull it up at the easel.

Writing the protocol to a file:

arguments.command:
cat > /home/ubuntu/watercolor-study-35deg.md << 'EOF'
# Watercolor Study — 35° Tilt, Lower-Bead Wicking Frequency

Date: 2024-10-26
Instructor diagnosis: at 35°, lower bead gets too heavy and feeds back into the
drying wash, producing two cauliflower edges. Cure = wick more often, do NOT
change brush moisture.

## Question
How does the interval between lower-bead removals affect cauliflower edges at
35°, holding brush moisture, contact time, and pass count constant?

## Hypothesis (H1)
Shorter wick interval -> fewer cauliflower edges. The 40s condition is included
as a built-in validation of the instructor's diagnosis (it should reproduce the
problem).

## Held constant (every wash)
- Brush condition: one firm blot after loading
- 20-second touch window after laying the wash
- One-touch rule: single pass, no re-entry
- Tilt: 35 degrees (prop board, check angle)
- Paper: same sheet/batch, pre-cut 12 strips of equal size
- Pigment, dilution, brush, load amount: identical
- Lighting + phone angle for photos: identical

## Variable: wick interval
  Level   Interval   Wicks within 20s window
  A       40 s       0   (validation: expect cauliflower)
  B       20 s       1   (current practice)
  C       10 s       2
  D        5 s       3

## Reps & order
- 3 reps per level = 12 washes, one session (~25-35 min painting)
- Randomize the order of all 12 before starting; label each strip with its
  condition (A1..D3) before painting so scoring is blind to where you are in
  the sequence

## Per-wash procedure
1. Load brush, one firm blot -- done.
2. One-touch lay the wash on the strip.
3. Tilt board to 35 deg, start timer.
4. At the prescribed wick interval, touch tissue to lower bead ~1 s to wick.
   (Level A: do NOT wick during the window -- this is the failure case.)
5. At t = 20 s, lower the board, photograph the strip under fixed lighting.
6. Score on the rubric below.

## Scoring (per strip)
- Cauliflower edges: count (0 / 1 / 2+)
- Lower bead weight at t=20s: none / light / medium / heavy
- Feed-back into drying wash: yes / no
- Edge evenness: 1-5  (1 = broken/cauliflowered, 5 = clean)
- One-line note

## Reading the results
- Level A should reproduce the two cauliflower edges. If it doesn't, wick
  interval alone is not the driver.
- Expect edge count and evenness to improve as interval shortens.
- Diminishing returns: if 10s and 5s look the same, your working interval is
  <=10s; pick the longer of the two that still looks clean.
- If even 5s still cauliflowers, the next variable to isolate is brush
  moisture (load amount or blot count) at the best wick interval found here.

## Next study (if needed)
Isolate brush moisture at the winning wick interval.
EOF
echo "wrote $(wc -l < /home/ubuntu/watercolor-study-35deg.md) lines to /home/ubuntu/watercolor-study-35deg.md"

session_search.description: Recall past conversations: search or read old Hermes sessions (FTS5), or scroll inside one. Four shapes, picked by args: `query` = discovery (top-N matching sessions, top result fully hydrated); `session_id` + `around_message_id` = scroll (window of messages around an anchor); `session_id` alone = read a whole session — how you resolve an `@session:<profile>/<id>` link (split on '/' into profile + id); no args = browse recent sessions. Results are actual DB messages, no LLM. Searches conversation history ONLY — when the user gave a direct source (URL, file, contact, live system), inspect that first; never conclude 'not found' from history alone. Use for questions about past conversations: 'what did we do about X', 'where did we leave Y'. When referring the user to a session, write its `link` value verbatim inline (it renders as a titled link).

query.description: Search query (discovery shape). Keywords, phrases, or boolean expressions to find in past sessions. Omit to browse recent sessions. Ignored when session_id + around_message_id are set (scroll shape).

limit.description: Discovery shape only. Max sessions to return (default 3, max 10). Bump to 5–10 when the topic likely spans several sessions and you want to pick the right one to scroll into.

sort.description: Discovery shape only. Temporal bias on top of FTS5 ranking: omit for relevance-only (exploratory recall), 'newest' for "where did we leave X", 'oldest' for "how did X start".

detail.description: Discovery shape only. 'adaptive' (default) fully hydrates the top-ranked result and returns only the exact anchor message for lower-ranked results. 'full' returns bookends and the complete anchored window for every result.

session_id.description: Scroll shape. Session to read inside. Use the session_id returned from a prior discovery call. Must be paired with around_message_id.

around_message_id.description: Scroll shape. Message id to center the window on — use match_message_id from a discovery result, or any id from a prior window.

window.description: Scroll shape only. Messages to return on each side of the anchor (anchor itself always included). Clamped to [1, 20]. Default 5.

role_filter.description: Optional. Comma-separated roles to include. Discovery defaults to 'user,assistant' (tool output is usually noise). Pass 'user,assistant,tool' to include tool output (debugging tool behaviour) or 'tool' to search tool output only.

profile.description: Optional. Read sessions from another Hermes profile's database (read-only). Use when resolving an `@session:<profile>/<id>` link: pass the profile segment here with session_id as the id segment. Omit to use the current profile.

- Meaning: pricing artifact hypothesis for the mid-segment churn spike. It held two sub-mechanisms together at lockup — packaging/discounting on our side, and contract-mix shift on the customer side. On 2023-02-14, after Owen's tier-segmented cut (mid-seg entry 5.0% / standard 5.2% / plus 5.1%, ~20 bps spread), the packaging/discounting half was killed; H1 was narrowed to contract-mix only ahead of the Feb 15 close.
- Ruling date: February 15, 2023. This was the "dead-or-alive Feb 15" date set in the 2023-02-12 lockup. Owen closed the loop on H1 the morning of Feb 15, 2023 (per the Feb 15, 14:00 CT sync); the ruling was recorded that afternoon.
- Ruling status: provisional, not final. Verbatim from Feb 15: "pricing artifact is out for now." Tier cut alone was treated as sufficient ("ACV-bucket dollar-weighted cut isn't needed to finish the ruling — tier alone is enough") and Owen's 1-pager was directed to say so explicitly so the ruling wouldn't be re-litigated through a different cut later. - Owen's one-page ruling record status at that time: in flight, not yet filed. messages.content: [2023-06-08T09:27:00-05:00] Owen's next cut on EXP-2023-05-expansion-nudge is finally more informative than the n=92 snapshot, but I'm still trying to keep everyone from getting ahead of the data. Treatment is still ahead, around +$5 expansion MRR per account versus control, but the sample is still modest and it's below the original +$8 bar. The lift also isn't broad — it's mostly in accounts with deeper integration usage and more than one active admin. Marcus is already tempted to call it a retained-mid expansion win. I want a measured readout I can use with Marcus, Owen, and Ines: the experiment stays narrow, no copy change, the next cut needs to split integration depth and active-admin count explicitly, and the working hypothesis is usage-readiness rather than a generic day-60 prompt win. Can you draft that?

Here's a draft you can paste into the 1-pager or post in-thread. Top-of-page summary up front, raw attached at the bottom per your cadence with Owen.

---

EXP-2023-05-expansion-nudge — readout after next cut

Summary
  - Treatment still ahead, ~+$5 expansion MRR / account vs control
  - Below the +$8 pre-reg bar; sample still modest
  - Lift is concentrated, not broad: deeper integration usage + >1 active admin
  - Working hypothesis: usage-readiness, not a generic day-60 prompt win
  - Call: HOLD narrow. No copy change. Next cut must split on
    integration depth × active-admin count before any peek

What the cut shows
  - Direction consistent with the n=92 snapshot; magnitude is the question,
    not the sign
  - Lift concentrated in accounts that have already wired Helio into their
    stack AND have distributed admin ownership
  - Pattern reads as the nudge surfacing accounts that were already primed
    for expansion — the day-60 prompt itself isn't the lever; audience-
    readiness is

Why this is not yet a retained-mid expansion win
  - Pre-reg bar was +$8; we're at +$5
  - Standing rule (2023-03-26): first sig does not ship — wait one stab
    cohort under the pre-reg def (same metric/direction, n≥treatment),
    p<0.01 on the 2nd-look bar BEFORE the next decision peek
  - "Retained-mid expansion win" implies breadth across the 75-200 cohort.
    We're seeing a subgroup, not breadth. Calling it a win now overstates
    the result and locks in copy we haven't earned

What I want from the next cut
  - Pre-register sub-cohort definitions BEFORE the data lands:
      (a) integration depth — shallow vs deep (Owen to define + tag)
      (b) active-admin count — 1 vs >1
      (c) the interaction — depth AND admin is where I expect the lift
  - Keep experiment narrow: 25% hold on retained mid-seg (75-200 v2).
    No copy variant. No timing change. No audience expansion until the
    subgroup story is clean

Asks
  - Marcus: please hold the "retained-mid expansion win" framing until we
    have a sub-cohort-clean second look. Lift is real but narrow; we
    shouldn't sell a narrow result as a broad one.
  - Owen: tee up the next cut with the integration-depth × active-admin
    split pre-registered before peeking.
  - Ines: no copy work this cycle. If the next cut holds, the right next
    experiment is holdout vs targeted-send on the primed slice — that's
    an audience question, not a copy question.

What would change my read
  - A second cohort look at +$5 or better on a sample that clears the
    pre-reg stab def, with p<0.01 on the 2nd-look bar
  - OR a clean subgroup story — lift X% in the primed slice, ~0 elsewhere
    — at which point the right next move is targeted-send to primed, not
    broad rollout

Attached: Owen's raw cut.

---

Two notes on what I assumed, flag if either is off:

  1. The pre-reg bar (+$8) and the standing 2nd-look bar (p<0.01, same
     metric/direction, n≥treatment) are still the operative gates for
     this experiment. If Owen has revised either since launch, the
     framing in "Why this is not yet a win" needs to track that.
  2. I held the audience tight (Marcus / Owen / Ines only) and didn't
     loop in Daniela or Tomas — matches the "stays narrow" constraint.
     Say the word if you want the small-biz tier doc owner looped in
     given the expansion-nudge signal intersects the 20-75 band question.

arguments.body:
Riley Tanaka — 2027 year-end self-review working draft

Reviewer: Priya. First draft due 2027-11-19. Working version — sections tightened before submission. No distribution, no Slack reference.

FRAME — DECISION-LED

Priya's calibration frame for this draft: lead with each decision I made and each claim limit I held, surface the credits inside the decision (not in a separate "team" section), and surface the exclusions inside the decision (not in a separate "out of scope" section). Lane boundaries are preserved as facts, not as defense language. The 1-pager ruling format holds at the section level: decision / bounded claim / credits / exclusions / status. December development outcomes stay open; the current paid batch is live operational work, not mature evidence.

This is a decision-led self-review. The four-lane year-end evidence framing is referenced inside each decision, not as a header above them. Owen, Ines, and Daniela's execution work is named in the credits line of each decision and is not re-described as my work in the body.

SUMMARY (DECISION-LED, SUM-FIRST)

In 2027 I held the operating-model and made the bounded calls below. Each is stated as a decision with its claim limit, who else owned what, and what is explicitly excluded from my lane.

1. Bounded Helio Start proposal. I drafted the bounded proposal and held the claim limits (no second-batch trigger, no pipeline/forecast credit, no activation or support-effort read into the descriptive numbers). Credit: Priya's batch approval; Daniela's November 1 launch authorization. Excluded: measurement execution (Owen), lifecycle-governance and message-state execution (Ines), engineering release and rollback execution (Daniela). Status: authorized November 1; live operational, not mature.

2. Five-consumer shared-state reminder operation. I held the decision that the reminder operates as the fifth prod consumer of the shared-state feed, with the incomplete-setup case treated as a reminder target rather than a routed workflow. Credit: Daniela's reliability and release work on the feed; Ines's lifecycle-governance meaning on the incomplete-setup state; Owen's denominator work on the shared-state surfaces. Excluded: the consumers' own execution, including any operational outcomes from consumer #5. Status: in flight — the fifth consumer is operating; the read on its effect is not closed.

3. Operating-model decisions held. Channel routing (Priya routes; I do not second-guess). Ruling 1-pager format (sum-first / why / cuts / p / effect / call). Expansion Assist stays descriptive — disputed / cross-team / exec-facing lines stay; routine line-edits do not; release and rollback routes to Daniela. Growth workstreams run sequentially, not in parallel, to keep signal clean. Monday cohort cuts with Owen, mid-segment, read locks first. Credit: the format is Priya's; lane splits are named, not invented. Excluded: any claim that the format itself moved outcomes.

4. Evidence and claim discipline held. Source completeness = Owen (bounded); claim, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, executive language = Riley. I did not absorb measurement, governance, release, or rollback into my lane, and I did not let my lane be absorbed into theirs. Excluded: any causal, revenue, forecast, or executive-language claim that has not gone through the standing review pathway.

5. Team development — December cycle. Owen and Ines both have October–December Q4 development focuses. These are open as of this draft and will be read against in the December cycle. I am not closing them here, and I am not pre-empting the December read. Credit: Owen's measurement/denominator/source-completeness/exception work is his; Ines's lifecycle-governance/message-state work is hers. Excluded: any characterization of Owen's or Ines's Q4 outcomes as my execution or as completed in this draft.

6. Next-cycle focus. Carry-forward placeholder — to be tightened before submission.

DECISIONS — DETAIL

Decision 1 — Bounded Helio Start proposal and claim limits.

What I decided. The proposal I drafted held three limits that I am not relaxing in this draft: (a) no automatic second-batch trigger from the day-7 leading read, (b) no pipeline or forecast credit against the cohort, (c) no read of the descriptive numbers into activation or support-effort claims. The launch posture I set was staged: staging first; isolated real-platform test campaign with no eligibility-flow entry; written Daniela ack; CS hours honored (M–F 8a–6p Central; after-hours route to the next opening); "paused" is not a bypass for V11.

Bounded claim. The launch is authorized and the gating rules are documented. The proposal does not prove acquisition, scale, pipeline, or forecast, and the bounded claim stays bounded.

Credits.
- Priya — batch approval.
- Daniela — November 1 launch authorization.
- Owen — measurement, denominator, source-completeness, and exception work on the proposal's numbers (his lane, not mine).
- Ines — lifecycle-governance and message-state meaning on the proposal's eligibility and routing (her lane, not mine).
- Daniela — engineering release and rollback on the launch itself (her lane, not mine).

Exclusions.
- The day-7 leading read, the cohort's mature-window read, and any support-effort classification — Owen's numbers, not mine.
- Lifecycle suppression, governed state meaning, and owner-state semantics — Ines's, not mine.
- Release preflight, connector-specific conditions, replay coverage, and rollback posture — Daniela's, not mine.
- Mature-outcome claims on the paid batch. The current paid batch is live operational work; the post-launch review runs after the batch clears.

Status. Authorized November 1. Live operational. Mature read pending the post-launch review; this draft does not claim mature outcomes.

Decision 2 — Five-consumer shared-state reminder operation (consumer #5 = incomplete-setup reminder).

What I decided. The shared-state feed has five prod consumers. Consumer #5 is the incomplete-setup reminder: a reminder targeted at the incomplete-setup case, operating off the shared-state feed without becoming a routed workflow. I held the decision that consumer #5 stays a reminder and does not absorb routing or governance responsibilities that belong to other lanes.

Bounded claim. The reminder operates as the fifth consumer. This draft does not claim operational outcomes from consumer #5; the read on its effect is in flight.

Credits.
- Daniela — reliability, release, and rollback on the shared-state feed (her lane).
- Ines — lifecycle-governance meaning on the incomplete-setup state (her lane).
- Owen — denominator and source-completeness on the shared-state surfaces (his lane).

Exclusions.
- Consumer #5's operational outcomes — not claimed here.
- The four prior consumers' execution — their lanes, not mine.
- Any causal or activation read off consumer #5's reminder traffic — out of scope for this draft.

Status. In flight. Consumer #5 is operating; the effect read is not closed.

Decision 3 — Operating-model decisions held.

What I decided.
- Channel routing: I own #growth-investigations (churn/cohort) and #lifecycle-systems (kickoff/certification). Priya routes cross-stream work; I do not second-guess that path.
- Ruling 1-pager format: sum-first, then why / cuts / p / effect / call.
- Expansion Assist: descriptive. Disputed, cross-team, exec-facing lines stay; routine line-edits do not; release and rollback routes to Daniela.
- Sequential growth workstreams: activation/retention, lifecycle email, feature-flag work do not all run hot at the same time. Workstreams run sequentially to keep signal clean.
- Monday cohort cuts with Owen, mid-segment. Read locks come first.

Bounded claim. The format and routing held through the year. This draft does not claim that the format itself moved outcomes.

Credits. Priya owns the format and the cross-stream routing. Lane splits are named; lane execution belongs to the named owners.

Exclusions. Any claim that format discipline alone drove a metric. Any claim about another owner's lane that is not explicitly credited above.

Status. Held through 2027. Continued into 2028 unless Priya redirects.

Decision 4 — Evidence and claim discipline held.

What I held. Source completeness = Owen (bounded). Claim, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, executive language = Riley. The split is preserved in every readout: I do not put a number on the page without naming the source-completeness lane it came from, and I do not put a causal or executive claim on the page without routing it through the standing review pathway.

Bounded claim. The discipline held under pressure through the year. This draft does not claim that the discipline by itself produced an outcome.

Credits. Owen — source-completeness review pathway and the bounded source lane. Ines — lifecycle-governance and message-state. Daniela — source-reliability, engineering-release, rollback.

Exclusions. Any read that conflates source completeness with claim, revenue, forecast, or executive language. Any read that lets my lane absorb theirs, or vice versa.

Status. Held through 2027. Carry-forward into 2028 unchanged unless Priya redirects.

Decision 5 — Team development: Owen and Ines Q4 focuses open through December.

What I held. Owen and Ines both have October–December Q4 development focuses. I am not closing them in this draft. The December cycle is where they get read against. I do not pre-empt that cycle here.

Bounded claim. This draft does not characterize Owen's or Ines's Q4 outcomes as complete. It does not characterize their execution as mine.

Credits. Owen's measurement/denominator/source-completeness/exception work is his; Ines's lifecycle-governance/message-state work is hers. Their Q4 development is theirs.

Exclusions.
- Any statement that Owen's Q4 focus is closed or on track — closed in the December cycle, not here.
- Any statement that Ines's Q4 focus is closed or on track — closed in the December cycle, not here.
- Any inflation of my role in Owen's, Ines's, or Daniela's execution.

Status. Owen Q4 focus — open through December cycle. Ines Q4 focus — open through December cycle.

Decision 6 — Next-cycle focus.

Placeholder. Two to three concrete 2028 focuses to be added before the 11/19 send. Carry-forward candidates: hold the claim-boundary discipline under next-cycle pressure; keep sequential workstream discipline; keep the December-cycle read intact for Owen and Ines; carry the bounded Helio Start posture into any 2028 paid-batch conversation.

EVIDENCE AND CLAIM DISCIPLINE — HELD

Source completeness = Owen (bounded). Claim, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, executive language = Riley. The split is preserved in every readout. I do not claim another owner's number, posture, or release as mine, and I do not let mine be absorbed into theirs. The standing review pathway is unchanged. Routine monthly preparation and source-closure reviews still flow through me as exception review; I have not left that work.

Where a system is still being set up, I say so. The five-consumer reminder operation is in flight, not mature. The current paid batch is live operational work, not mature evidence. The descriptive four-week reads on the authority-setup checklist are descriptive operating evidence, not activation or support-effort claims.

TEAM DEVELOPMENT — DECEMBER CYCLE

Owen Q4 focus — open. To be read in the December cycle. I will not pre-empt that read in this draft. Owen's lane is measurement, denominator, source-completeness, and exception reporting; his work is his.

Ines Q4 focus — open. To be read in the December cycle. I will not pre-empt that read in this draft. Ines's lane is lifecycle-governance and message-state; her work is hers.

Daniela's lane is source-reliability, engineering-release, and rollback. Her work is hers; I do not describe her release or rollback decisions as my execution.

I have not stopped routine monthly preparation or source-closure exception review. Both still flow through me.

SYSTEM RELIABILITY — BY LANE

This section names systems by decision authority. Other systems are reported by their owners.

- Shared-state feed — five-consumer reminder operation. Five prod consumers in production. Consumer #5 (incomplete-setup reminder) operates off the shared-state feed; the reminder operation is in flight, not mature. Reliability and release on the feed: Daniela. Lifecycle-governance meaning on the incomplete-setup state: Ines. Denominator on the shared-state surfaces: Owen. I hold the decision that consumer #5 stays a reminder and does not absorb routing or governance responsibilities.

- Controlled November paid-batch launch. Launch posture gated: staging first; isolated real-platform test campaign with no eligibility-flow entry; written Daniela ack; CS hours honored (M–F 8a–6p Central; after-hours route to the next opening); "paused" is not a V11 bypass. Launch authorized November 1 by Priya's batch approval and Daniela's launch authorization. The current paid batch is live operational work; mature outcomes are not claimed here. Measurement on the batch: Owen. Lifecycle-governance on the batch: Ines. Engineering release and rollback on the batch: Daniela.

- Bounded Helio Start posture. No second-batch trigger from the day-7 leading read. No pipeline or forecast credit against the cohort. No read of the descriptive numbers into activation or support-effort claims. Posture held.

NEXT-CYCLE FOCUS

Placeholder — to be tightened before 11/19.

OPEN BEFORE 11/19

1. Two to three concrete 2028 focuses (Next-cycle focus section).
2. Any 2027-specific decision you want anchored by name (one per lane is usually enough for a self-review of this shape).
3. Confirm whether the December cycle closes Owen's and Ines's Q4 focuses before or after the final feedback conversation; the draft assumes the cycle closes them after.

ROUTING

This doc stays in Growth until edited down to a 1-pager for Priya. No distribution, no Slack reference until then.
