arguments.body:
Riley Tanaka — 2026 year-end self-review working draft
Cycle: 2026 year-end · Reviewer: Priya · Working draft (not for distribution)
Shape: summary first, then four evidence sections plus a closing paragraph, written as prose for editing down to the 1-pager (why / cuts / what I did / effect / call).

SUMMARY

I held the claim-boundary discipline across the year: Q1 and Q2 cohort windows stayed on the published dates, and the §3 admission rules plus the §4.8-style pipeline/forecast exclusion held through every pressure point without being compressed into a partial-window claim. I closed the Helio Start paid cohort at $14,420 / 50 admits, and on Aug 21 recommended — and Priya accepted — no second Q3 batch and no pipeline or forecast credit for the cohort; a binding future-paid case-review gate is now in force. I built a delegation rhythm in which Owen owns the monthly sanitized campaign snapshot and the source-completeness review pathway as an evaluation framework, and on November 6 Owen independently closed the 9/24 source-completeness packet covering 7/1–10/31 with certifications complete — the cleanest concrete leadership-through-delegation example of the year. I retain board readiness, causal and revenue claims, forecast treatment, executive language, and exception authority, and I have not stopped routine monthly preparation or source-closure reviews, both of which still flow through me as exception review. The Oct 14 authority-checklist review closed with Owen and Customer Success supplying a clean descriptive four-week operating read; I kept the checklist in organic onboarding without turning the counts into an activation or support-effort claim, and I set an explicit maintenance split among Ines, Daniela, and me. No 2027 role change has been requested or approved.

1. Q1 AND Q2 CLAIM BOUNDARIES — HELD

The published constraints were the §3 admission rules (eligibility, refusal, connector access, external authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, support routing) and the §4.8-style pipeline/forecast exclusion. Q1 dates were 4/7; Q2 was not board-ready until mature claim windows completed. Forecast and pipeline received no credit on partial-window evidence, and a mature claim required complete observation windows.

Under pressure to compress, I refused to roll the day-7 first-integration read (39/50, leading only) into acquisition, scale, pipeline, or forecast, and I held the day-90 decision for closed day-90 windows. I kept the four-part output discipline (classification / alignment / consequence / routing) on operator-facing references and on my own claim-side framing, and I held the §3 / §4.8 cannot-be-weakened framing as the rule any future proposal must satisfy.

The effect: Q1 and Q2 board segments stayed on the published dates, no claim was advanced on a partial-window basis, no pipeline or forecast credit was granted against Q1 or Q2 cohort outcomes, and the structural discipline keeping the five Helio Start states separate from Starter / retained-mid-segment in every readout held. Call: keep citing this as the spine of the year's evidence — the mature-window-only claim discipline plus §3 / §4.8 not weakened is the defended boundary.

2. CLOSED HELIO START PAID COHORT — NO SECOND BATCH, NO PIPELINE/FORECAST CREDIT

The approved pilot was high-intent paid search, mid-segment-fit only, 6-week max window, capped at the earlier of $15,000 spent or 50 admitted workspaces; the $8K / 25 fallback was never approved. Stop / pause triggers (any one): unsupported-in-admitted; reconciliation failure across eligibility → admit → assisted; or ≥20 admitted if >10% showed >90 support minutes per account. The day-7 read of 39/50 first-integration-by-day-7 was leading only, not mature.

On Aug 17 the source-completeness certification packet (Owen + Customer Success) assigned mutually exclusive day-90 statuses to all 50 workspaces — 37 paid-active, 6 canceled, 4 past due, 3 billing hold — with $60,480 gross billed cash, $56,230 refund-adjusted collected cash, 26-minute median and 104-minute p90 account-level support effort, 7 of 50 (14%) exceeding 90 support minutes, and end-to-end reconciliation of paid-source attribution for all 50. No unsupported applicant entered the admitted path. I treated the packet as descriptive paid-source evidence only — explicitly not causal acquisition, not scale, not pipeline, not forecast — because there was no randomized control. On Aug 21 the second-batch decision review recommended, and Priya accepted, no second Helio Start paid batch in Q3 and no Q4 forecast treatment for the cohort. Paid traffic remains off.

The future-paid gate is now binding: Owen + Customer Success must classify each of the seven high-support workspaces into (a) external-authority action, (b) ordinary integration, (c) billing, or (d) another supported cause (named explicitly; "unclassified" is not a supported bucket); Ines + Daniela must determine whether each case concerns state meaning, routing, and / or setup sequence (multiple dimensions may apply, each named); and any future paid proposal must account for all seven cases (state how each is prevented, mitigated, or bounded — not merely listed) without weakening §3 or §4.8.

The cohort is fixed at 50; paid traffic is off; no second Q3 paid batch is in flight; the cohort carries no pipeline or forecast credit. Call: the case-review gate is the structural artifact of the year — the day-90 numbers are evidence inside it, not the artifact itself.

3. OWEN'S MONTHLY-PREP TRANSITION + BOUNDED SOURCE-CLOSURE AUTHORITY

Two changes moved through me. The first was the monthly sanitized campaign snapshot landing as exception-summary only; the first post-handoff on Jul 2 covered 135 campaigns with status and owner rows and owner lanes intact, and resolved three Q2 opens (Ines owner-change verified, Maya snapshot-only, Owen denominator). The second was the source-completeness review pathway defined on Jul 29 — Owen's audit covers eight fields per row (denominator and exact coverage dates; outcome window; measurement limits; exclusions; single named source owner per surface; reliability evidence; revenue and forecast treatment with the explicit handoff note "source certified by Owen; call retained by Riley"; and a section certifier with named backup). The observable success criteria are three consecutive packets with all eight fields complete and a named certifier per section, zero disputed-semantics reopens, zero cross-surface owner drift, exceptions surfaced within one business day of source release with the gap named, reliability evidence reproducible from source on first request, and denominator / coverage dates reconciling against the prior packet's exit state.

Escalation triggers are unchanged: any missing field makes the packet incomplete and escalates; disputed semantics or cross-surface discrepancy escalates rather than resolving in packet; any causal, revenue, forecast, or executive-language content escalates to me by default; and two consecutive packets with the same exception type trigger formal review of the pathway, not a third packet.

3f. October 14 authority-checklist review — four-week operating read, descriptive only

On October 14 the authority-checklist review closed. Owen and Customer Success supplied a clean descriptive four-week operating read on the organic authority-setup checklist shipped on Sep 15. Across the four-week window: 92 admitted organic workspaces in scope; 28 checklist exposures (pre-setup visibility surface only, reported separately from admission and activation outcomes); five ordinary setup-assistance requests handled through the existing assisted-route path. The review surfaced no eligibility or route mismatch, no lifecycle-suppression issue, no paid-source traffic (paid traffic remains off; the Helio Start paid cohort is fixed at 50), no unsupported admission, and no randomized control. I treated the four-week read as descriptive operating evidence — explicitly not an activation claim and not a support-effort claim — because the counts are pre-setup visibility and assisted-route support requests on an organic-only surface, not activation outcomes, and there is no control arm. The checklist stays in organic onboarding, and the metric surfaces (admission, activation, checklist exposure, support minutes) remain split.

The maintenance split is now explicit and named: Ines owns the state-meaning dimension (lifecycle suppression, governed state, external-authority meaning unchanged); Daniela owns the release-reliability dimension (preflight, connector-specific condition, replay coverage, surfacing any drift on first request); I retain the claim discipline (descriptive-only framing, no read into activation or support effort, no pipeline or forecast credit, §3 / §4.8 reaffirmed as not weakened) and the exception authority whenever a maintenance cycle crosses any escalation trigger above. This is a routing change inside the organic checklist surface — descriptive operating read + named maintenance lanes — not a delegation of the underlying claim or forecast responsibility, and §8.E and §8.E.3 remain in force unchanged.

3g. November 6 — independent closure of the 9/24 source-completeness packet (the year's leadership-through-delegation evidence)

On November 6 Owen independently closed the 9/24 source-completeness packet covering 7/1–10/31 with certifications complete. The closure landed without my seeding the structure or chasing fields — the eight source-completeness fields (denominator and exact coverage dates; outcome window; measurement limits; exclusions; single named source owner per surface; reliability evidence; revenue and forecast treatment with the explicit handoff note "source certified by Owen; call retained by Riley"; and section certifier with named backup) cleared on the source side, and the certifications arrived consistent across sections. I treated this as concrete leadership-through-delegation evidence: I held the judgment and evidence boundary, Owen owned the build lane with named readouts and named gates, and the closure happened inside the bounded source-completeness lane without absorbing any other authority into it.

This is source completeness — it is not a claim, not a revenue call, not a forecast treatment, not board-readiness, and not executive language. The 11/6 brief explicitly split Owen's closed source row from the open causal, revenue, pipeline, forecast, board-readiness, and executive-language rows, and those open rows stayed with me. Source-completeness closure is the lane that Owen was bounded to; the broader authorities stayed where they were on 9/24 and are unchanged today. I continue to participate in routine monthly preparation and source-closure reviews as exception review — the 11/6 closure did not remove me from that work, and no new review-closure authority has been granted.

What is delegated versus what is mine. Delegated preparation is Owen's monthly sanitized campaign snapshot and the source-completeness review pathway as an evaluation framework — the line-by-line build work moves to him, with named readouts and named gates — and, on the checklist surface, the four-week descriptive operating read and the maintenance cycles within the Ines / Daniela / Riley split; the 11/6 independent closure of the 9/24 packet is the cleanest instance of that build-lane ownership completing on the source side. Routine source review still comes to me as exception review; I have not left that work, and no new review-closure authority has been granted. Routine monthly preparation still flows through me as exception review; I have not left that work either. What I retain are the claims (causal and revenue), the forecast treatment, the executive language, the descriptive-only discipline on the checklist read, the source completeness boundary itself (the lane Owen operates inside, not the closure authority), and the exception authority whenever a packet or maintenance cycle crosses any escalation trigger above. The transition is a routing change — line-by-line to exception-summary where clean, and descriptive operating read + named maintenance lanes on the checklist — not a handoff of the underlying responsibility, and the underlying responsibility on those streams did not change.

Effect: the 7/2 handoff held (135 campaigns, status + owner + lanes intact, no Q2 board redo); the 7/29 pathway is a written evaluation framework with explicit trigger conditions for re-review, not a delegation; the 10/14 checklist review closed with 92 admitted / 28 exposures / 5 ordinary setup-assistance requests, no eligibility or route mismatch, no lifecycle-suppression issue, no paid-source traffic, no unsupported admission, and no randomized control; the 11/6 independent closure of the 9/24 packet (7/1–10/31, certs complete) landed on the source side with the open causal / revenue / pipeline / forecast / board / executive-language rows staying with me. Call: this is the year's leadership-through-delegation example — I held the judgment and evidence boundary, Owen owned the build lane with named readouts and named gates, and the 11/6 closure is the concrete artifact of the year, with source completeness remaining bounded and the broader authorities unchanged.

4. ORGANIC AUTHORITY-SETUP CHECKLIST — RELEASED, ELIGIBILITY AND STATE MEANINGS PRESERVED

The approved release was a non-state-changing, connector-specific pre-setup checklist for admitted Helio Start workspaces whose selected connector requires an owner-level permission or a network-allowlist action. The release target was the organic Helio Start onboarding path only, and eligibility and state meanings had to be preserved; checklist exposure is reported separately from admission and activation outcomes.

At the 10:30 release gate on Sep 15, Ines and Daniela completed the 24-case replay and lifecycle preflight. The condition for receiving the checklist was a selected connector requiring an owner-level permission or a network-allowlist action, AND current verified-yes external authority at the moment of replay. Eight of the 24 cases met the condition and received the connector-specific checklist; 16 did not meet the condition and did not receive it. Every case preserved existing eligibility, route, lifecycle suppression, and governed state. Daniela released the checklist to the organic onboarding path, and Owen began reporting checklist exposure separately from admission and activation outcomes — the rationale being that checklist exposure is a pre-setup visibility surface, not an admission or activation event, and keeping the metric surfaces split preserves the integrity of the admission and activation numbers and prevents the checklist from being read into the §4.8-style pipeline / forecast framing.

The surrounding levers are all unchanged at Sep 15: §3 admission rules remain in force; external-authority meaning (field definition, current-and-verified-yes semantics, and the missing / stale / conflicting / pending / no / not-sure state set) is unchanged; assisted routing (assisted-route reason capture from first contact and per-account support-minute capture from first contact) is unchanged; fail-closed handling (immediate-stop on any unsupported case in the admitted path, reconciliation-failure pause, >10% over-90-sup-min pause for n ≥ 20) is unchanged; and paid-acquisition status is unchanged (cap closed at $14,420 / 50 admits, paid traffic off, no second Q3 paid batch authorized). The §8.E future-paid case-review gate and the §8.E.3 proposal precondition remain in force; the checklist release does not weaken, satisfy, or replace any element of §8.E.

Effect: the checklist is live on the organic Helio Start onboarding path with eligibility and state meanings intact. The Sep 15 release introduced no new admission, routing, lifecycle, or fail-closed rule; it did not alter external-authority meaning; it did not open a second paid batch. Call: this is the cleanest example of the year of shipping a release with every surrounding lever reasserted and §3 + §4.8 reaffirmed as not weakened.

CLOSING

Two priorities remain in flight, and neither implies I have left routine monthly preparation or source-closure reviews. Priority 1 is to bring Owen's source-completeness review pathway to its graduation criterion: three consecutive packets with all eight fields complete, a named certifier per section, zero disputed-semantics reopens, zero cross-surface owner drift, exceptions surfaced within one business day of source release with the gap named, reliability evidence reproducible from source on first request, and denominator / coverage dates reconciling against the prior packet's exit state. The 11/6 independent closure of the 9/24 packet is concrete progress on that lane, but it is one packet, not the three-packet criterion — I remain the routine source-closure reviewer on the underlying stream and the exception reviewer on the pathway itself until the criterion is met, and that responsibility is not in scope to delegate. Priority 2 is to hold the exception-summary monthly snapshot handoff without regression to line-by-line reconciliation; the 7/2 routing change stays in force, routine monthly preparation still flows through me as exception review, and my current responsibilities on that stream did not change. Source completeness stays separate from the claim, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, and executive-language authorities — the 11/6 closure operated inside that boundary, and no 2027 role change has been requested or approved.

I have not left routine monthly preparation; the 7/2 handoff was a routing change, and the underlying responsibility still flows through me as exception review. I have not delegated source-closure reviews; the 7/29 pathway is an evaluation framework with explicit three-packet success criteria and escalation triggers, the 11/6 closure is one packet inside that frame, and no new review-closure authority has been granted. I have not weakened §3 admission rules or the §4.8-style pipeline / forecast exclusion; both are reaffirmed as not weakened in the §8.E future-paid gate, the §11 organic-checklist release addendum, and the 8/21 second-batch decision record. I have not authorized a second Helio Start paid batch; paid traffic is off, the cohort is fixed at 50, and no pipeline or forecast credit has been granted against the cohort. I have not introduced a new admission, routing, lifecycle, or fail-closed rule; the 9/15 organic authority-setup checklist is non-state-changing and shipped to the organic path only. I have not turned the Oct 14 four-week descriptive checklist read into an activation or support-effort claim; the read is descriptive operating evidence on a pre-setup visibility surface, with the metric surfaces (admission, activation, checklist exposure, support minutes) kept split and §3 / §4.8 reaffirmed as not weakened. The 11/6 closure is source-completeness, not claim, not revenue, not forecast, not board-readiness, and not executive language; the open rows on those authorities stayed with me on 11/6 and continue to stay with me. No 2027 role change has been requested or approved.

# Owen Pham — 2026 year-end feedback working notes

_Owner: Riley. Status: working manager document — preliminary observations, not final feedback, and not an expansion of Owen's authority._

## Frame

These are my working notes to inform Owen's year-end conversation. They are preliminary and may shift before the final feedback is delivered. They do **not** modify Owen's authority. Per the 9/24 ruling, Owen remains bounded to source-completeness; Priya's Q4 Lifecycle System frame (4 evidence lanes, owner splits unchanged) is still in force. The 11/6 independent closure of the 9/24 source-completeness packet (7/1–10/31 coverage, certifications complete) confirms the source-completeness lane is operating as designed — and confirms only that. The standing split is unchanged: source completeness = Owen (bounded); claim, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, and executive-language authority = Riley. The 11/6 brief explicitly split Owen's closed source row from the open causal, revenue, pipeline, forecast, board-readiness, and executive-language rows, and those open rows stayed with me. Riley retains monthly prep + source-closure + exception review. No 2027 role change has been requested or approved, and nothing in these notes implies one.

## What this document is NOT

- Not final feedback. It is the working set of observations that will feed the final conversation.
- Not an expansion of Owen's authority. The 9/24 source-completeness ruling holds; the 11/6 closure is source-completeness only and does not absorb claim, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, or executive-language authority; Q4 lanes and owner splits are unchanged.
- Not an evaluation of work outside Owen's lane (e.g., Eng release/rollback stays with Daniela; owner-change vs. lifecycle stays with Ines).
- Not an implication of a 2027 role change. No 2027 role change has been requested or approved.

## Demonstrated in 2026

- **June preparation transition.** Handed the prep work for the Q2 evidence cycle over cleanly — no dropped threads, no noise downstream. Made the next phase easier to start.
- **Independent July and October sanitized campaign snapshots.** Both monthly snapshots (2nd biz day cadence) landed complete without me seeding structure or chasing fields. Status + owner + sanitized form held in both.
- **Complete first-pass Q2 and August evidence structures.** Q2 evidence and the 8/17 Day-90 CERT prep both arrived in usable first-pass form. Downstream review did not have to rebuild the skeleton.
- **Disciplined use of the September 24 source-completeness authority.** Stayed inside the bounded lane. Did not absorb revenue, forecast, claim, board-readiness, or executive-language authority — those stayed with me.
- **Held the October packet incomplete when exact coverage and owner certification did not match.** Did not paper over the gap on 10/7. Correctly stopped rather than weaken §3 or §4.8, and let the gate hold. This is the right call.
- **November 6 independent closure of the 9/24 source-completeness packet.** Closed the 9/24 packet covering 7/1–10/31 with certifications complete, inside the source-completeness lane only. The eight source-completeness fields cleared, the certifications arrived consistent across sections, and the closure landed without my seeding the structure or chasing fields. This is the year's cleanest concrete example of leadership-through-delegation operating as designed: build lane owned by Owen, judgment and evidence boundary held by me, and the closure event stayed inside source completeness without claiming, forecasting, or reframing any other authority.

## Next-cycle expectations

- **Obtain owner certification earlier.** The 10/7 packet stalled because certification arrived late in the cycle, and earlier certification is the development area carried forward from that. Pushing owner sign-off to the front of the window prevents end-of-window collapses and keeps the gate from being the bottleneck. The 11/6 closure did not retire this expectation — one packet is not the three-packet graduation criterion, and earlier certification is what protects the next packet from repeating the 10/7 stall.
- **State exact through-dates before requesting closure review.** Closure should be declared with a specific date (e.g., "through 10/16" or "through 10/31") rather than as a general "ready" — that keeps source-completeness reviewable and avoids a closure conversation about scope. The 11/6 closure was declared with the exact through-date of 10/31; making that the standing pattern across packets is the carry-forward expectation.
- **Continue to distinguish source completeness from my authorities.** The line is: source completeness = Owen (bounded); claim, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, and executive-language authority = Riley. Do not soften that boundary by letting source-completeness absorb the other authorities back into it. The 11/6 closure operated inside the bounded lane — and continuing to hold that lane, rather than letting a clean closure pull the boundary outward, is the carry-forward expectation. The 8/21 Priya ruling (no 2nd-batch / pipeline / forecast credit) reinforces this — Owen held the line then too.

## Open threads to revisit before final feedback

- Reference the 8/21 Priya ruling in the final conversation as evidence Owen held the line when asked to extend past source-completeness.
- The 7 high-suppression classifications (Owen + CS, per the 10/7 gate) — quality and provenance worth surfacing as a strength.
- The 11/6 independent closure of the 9/24 packet (7/1–10/31, certs complete) — surface as concrete leadership-through-delegation evidence, framed as one packet inside the source-completeness lane, not as a graduation or authority expansion.
- Confirm whether a December snapshot lands before the year-end conversation; if so, incorporate.

arguments.body:
# Midyear Self-Review 2025 — Riley Tanaka

**For:** Priya. Midyear review held Mon 2025-08-04, 10:00–10:30 CT.
**Status:** Revised per Priya's comment (2025-07-23) and Priya's written follow-up (2025-08-05).
**Format:** 1-pager, summary first; why / cuts / effect / call. Under 300 words on the body sections.
**Folder:** Growth.

---

## Q3 management focus (Priya written follow-up, 2025-08-05)

Priya identified my strongest H1 progress as making Owen's operating readouts and Ines's governance work independent instead of becoming the reconciliation layer myself. The Q3 management focus is the directive that follows from that read:

1. **Stop line-editing routine work once the established checks pass.** When Owen's readouts or Ines's governance work clears the standing checks (shared-state parity, field-specific reasons, age/owner, four-part output), I leave it alone. No phrasing polish, no sentence rewrite, no second-pass copy edit. My role on routine work is the check, not the line.
2. **Keep disputed semantics, cross-surface consequences, and executive claims with me.** Those are not routine; they stay on my desk regardless of whose surface they're on. Routine governance sign-off routes through Ines; routine readout shape routes through Owen; I stay reserved for the lanes where one decision binds across surfaces or carries into the exec room.
3. **Do not write as though the September decision is already made.** The September review of Ines's CS auto-nudge review lane is open. I will not pre-write its outcome into Q3 language, deck language, exec updates, or readouts. Decision lands in September, with data, not now.
4. **Daniela's engineering release and rollback control does not change.** Replay / fallback / accessibility-copy / held-queue release paths remain with Daniela. The Q3 focus does not move that lane; it does not route any release decision through Owen, Ines, or me.

---

## Body (revised per Priya, 2025-07-23)

### 1. Decision I materially changed (high stakes)
Precedent call on misuse/disposal: required visit-lease plus resident-damage evidence, and walked back the cut absent both. Cost the deal $165; protected the precedent so future disposal writes stop being contested. Call I would repeat — easier to defend a small loss than a precedent you cannot enforce.

### 2. Leverage through my team
Lifecycle audit shipped because Owen owned the readouts and semantics and I owned the exception ledger. Ines keeps lifecycle-audit-risk and owns the routine-education reclassification pass; Daniela owns the engineering release and rollback for the 8/6 source-age fix — I do not pre-empt either boundary. The work that scales is the one where I write the boundary and someone else runs it. Owen and Ines are now running their own lanes; my work is the seam between them, not the lane itself.

### 3. Stop doing in H2 (observable)
Stop line-editing routine operating readouts once the established checks pass. Concrete: when Owen's or Ines's artifact clears the standing checks (shared-state parity, field-specific reasons, age/owner on held rows, four-part output on operator-facing language), I will not draft copy, propose phrasing, propose timing, or edit the artifact in any surface. If something in that lane lands on my desk, I route to the owner and stop. Observable test: by the next op review, no routine readout shows my redline on a routine section. Routine work that fails a check still comes to me; routine work that passes does not.

### 4. September decision (OPEN, not pre-decided)
The review of Ines's CS auto-nudge review lane is open. Open question for September: does her lane run without my line-by-line read, or do we keep shared sign-off? I will not write toward either outcome in Q3. Decision lands then, with data, not now.

### 5. Authority boundaries (unchanged)
- Ines = lifecycle-audit-risk; routine-education reclassification; boundary = Riley. No engineering-control access.
- Owen = shape + exception readouts + Helio Start report. Single-path CS auto-nudge readout (June 27 calibration). Escalates disputed semantics / cross-surface consequences to Riley.
- Daniela = engineering release and rollback. Replay / fallback / accessibility-copy / held-queue release paths. Lifecycle audit INPUT ≠ RELEASE; neither substitutes for the other.
- Riley = judgment escalations + disputed semantics + cross-surface calls + executive claims + routine-education reclassification boundary + customer-correction + incident-stop.

---

## What I am NOT claiming in this review
- Not claiming Helio Start is a mature system. Lifecycle audit CLOSED 2025-03-28 (Owen, 638 records, 22 stale fail-closed); ≠ mature.
- Not claiming the September decision is settled. It is open.
- Not claiming I broadened Ines's review-closure authority. Two approved references, no change to closure.
- Not claiming the connector-access check is a launch metric. It is an evidence boundary.

---

## Operating guardrails (carried forward)
- Shared state mandatory across Growth and CS for lifecycle (Priya).
- Lag recovery forward-only: delayed export / refresh that resolves leads to a recheck of current state, not restoration of pre-lag eligibility.
- Standing-lane neutral readouts ≤3 / week; stale readouts fail closed.
- Auth, admin, entitlement, CS-work representations identical across eligibility, reporting, and messaging surfaces.
- Expansion Assist descriptive-only; no promotional-state change delegated.
- `routine education` = HIGHER-RISK; Ines reclassifies; boundary owned by Riley.

---

## Open questions for Priya (plain)
1. The Q3 directive is "stop line-editing routine work once the established checks pass" — is the observable test ("no routine readout shows my redline on a routine section by next op review") the right marker, or do you want a different one?
2. On the September decision: should I bring the data set to the September review myself, or do you want to commission it?
3. Anything in the body sections above that should not survive into the September review packet?

arguments.title: Operator Message-State Language — Approved Reference (Suppressed / Held / Cross-surface dependency / Proceed)
arguments.body:
# Operator Message-State Language — Approved Reference

**Status:** Approved operator reference. Accepted 2025-07-11 without Riley rewrite.
**Source:** Ines, corrected operator-facing message-state guide.
**Tested against:** May 20 Customer Success source-delay scenario (12 held → 8 Suppressed + 4 Proceeded; 0 reclassification).
**Supersedes:** Any prior provisional operator-facing wording for these four terms.

This doc is the canonical operator-facing source for the four message-state terms below. It is built on the governed meanings and on the four-part output requirement (classification + alignment read + operator consequence + routing call). It does not change any authority boundary.

---

## 1. Suppressed

**Meaning.** The active Customer Success suppression is currently in effect on this record. Suppression is multi-causal — never read "Suppressed" as a single reason.

**What an operator sees.**
- The record is on a live suppression lane with an active cause attached (e.g. recent outreach, opt-out, dispute in progress, lifecycle hold).
- Suppression does not equal freshness. A Suppressed record is not stale and is not unresolved; it is intentionally paused.
- The Suppression cause field is required; bare "Suppressed" without cause is not acceptable.

**Routing call.** Do not send. Do not retry. If the suppression cause has changed or expired, route to the operator consequence path, not to a fresh send.

**Boundary reminder.** Routine education that is reclassified HIGHER-RISK is a separate boundary (Ines reclassifies; Riley owns the boundary). A Suppressed record carrying a HIGHER-RISK routine education tag is still Suppressed; the reclassification boundary is independent.

---

## 2. Held

**Meaning.** A field-specific hold is in effect: the record is not currently Suppressed, not currently Proceed-able, and is being held for one or more named field-specific reasons.

**What an operator sees.**
- The record carries a field-specific hold reason (the specific field, not a category label). "Held" without the field is not acceptable.
- Held ≠ Suppressed. A Suppressed record is paused by an active cause; a Held record is paused waiting on field-level resolution.
- Held ≠ stale. Stale is a separate readout condition; a Held record may be fresh or stale depending on age since the decision.

**Required fields on every Held row.**
1. The specific field driving the hold.
2. Age (days since the hold was set).
3. Owner of resolution (Owen for routine exception; Ines for lifecycle-audit-risk / reclass; Daniela for engineering / release; Riley for disputed semantics, cross-surface, customer-correction, incident-stop). "Unassigned" is not acceptable.
4. Drift check within the same readout cycle if any held record has aged beyond the routine band.

**Routing call.** Escalate to the named owner. Standing-lane ≤3 neutral readouts per week stays in force; stale Held readouts fail closed. Held queues beyond the routine band escalate to Riley as incident-stop.

---

## 3. Cross-surface dependency

**Meaning.** A cross-surface dependency exists when the same governed field (entitlement, plan display name source, integration summary population, renewal-reminder population, CS-work representation, Authority verified, etc.) drives a decision in more than one surface, and the surfaces must agree.

**What an operator sees.**
- The record is on a decision that has at least one cross-surface consequence. The decision cannot be finalized until the cross-surface read is consistent.
- Parity requirement: auth, admin, entitlement, and CS-work representations must remain identical across eligibility, reporting, and messaging surfaces. Any drift between surfaces is itself a cross-surface dependency, not a separate category.
- Authority verified means external connector readiness, NOT contact permission (2025-06-17 CS auto-nudge rule). Reading it as contact permission creates a cross-surface dependency by definition.

**Routing call.** Cross-surface dependency is not a routine case. Escalate to Riley before the decision circulates. Riley redlines or signs off; Ines re-authors only if the governed meaning itself has to move.

**Boundary reminder.** Engineering release and rollback controls (replay, fallback, accessibility-copy, held-queue release) remain with Daniela. A cross-surface dependency that requires a release path change routes through Daniela, not through this guide.

---

## 4. Proceed

**Meaning.** The record is currently eligible for the next routine operator action after a fresh check has been performed. Proceed is a state after verification, not a freshness proxy.

**What an operator sees.**
- The record's classification, alignment read, and operator consequence all checked out at the time of decision.
- Proceed does NOT mean "the record is fresh." A record can be Proceeded and still be old; freshness is a separate readout dimension.
- Proceed does NOT mean "no cross-surface dependency." If a cross-surface read was required, Proceed only attaches after the cross-surface check resolves.

**Routing call.** Execute the next routine operator action per the routing call in the four-part output. Lag recovery is forward-only — a delayed export / refresh that resolves leads to a recheck of current state, not restoration of pre-lag eligibility.

**Boundary reminder.** State-changing decisions (any write that moves a record between the 5 Helio Start states: admitted / assisted / ineligible / final-reconciliation / pending) are NOT Proceed. Pending is pre-admission, forward-only, and excluded from rate and activation denominators. A Proceed decision on a pending record is itself a state-changing error and routes to Riley.

---

## Five Helio Start states (governed meanings carried forward)

admitted / assisted / ineligible / final-reconciliation / pending. Pending is pre-admission, forward-only, excluded from rate and activation denominators. Intake additive. Deck reporting separates activation + support-load from Starter / retained mid-segment.

## Operating guardrails (unchanged)

- Shared state mandatory across Growth and CS for lifecycle (Priya).
- Lag recovery forward-only; do not restore pre-lag eligibility.
- Standing-lane neutral readouts ≤3 / week; stale readouts fail closed.
- Auth, admin, entitlement, and CS-work representations identical across eligibility, reporting, and messaging surfaces.
- Expansion Assist descriptive-only; no promotional-state change delegated.
- `routine education` = HIGHER-RISK; Ines reclassifies; boundary owned by Riley.
- Engineering release and rollback controls (replay / fallback / a11y / held-queue release) remain with Daniela. Lifecycle audit = INPUT (snapshot / rules / reclass) vs RELEASE (replay / fallback / a11y / held-queue); neither substitutes for the other.

## Four-part output requirement (carry-forward from the original midyear focus)

For every routine, non-state-changing decision, the operator-facing explanation must include: (1) classification against the governed meanings; (2) state alignment read including what would flip the classification; (3) operator consequence across message / held queue / audit row / downstream surface; (4) routing call in plain language. Pass criterion: all four present and internally consistent, with no Riley rewrite.

## Pass / fail at acceptance

- Acceptance on 2025-07-11 was on the basis of internal consistency against the governed meanings, the May 20 test result (12 held → 8 Suppressed + 4 Proceeded, 0 reclassification), and the four-part output requirement.
- Independence criterion: Riley did not rewrite the guide on first pass.
- Second guide (governed-state, routine non-state-changing) is due 2025-07-25 and does not modify this reference.

## Linked sources

- Brief: BRIEF-2025-04-ines-midyear-growth-focus (Ines midyear growth-focus note; June 27 calibration entry; June 19 acceptance note; this acceptance entry).
- June 27 calibration entry on the same brief: pins the two-guide schedule, routing rules, and reporting lines.
- CS auto-nudge rule (2025-06-17): shared-state = sole prod path; Authority verified = connector readiness, not contact permission.

arguments.title: Q3 Lifecycle Systems — Priorities Decision Memo
arguments.body:
Q3 LIFECYCLE SYSTEMS — PRIORITIES DECISION MEMO
For: Priya | From: Riley | Date: 2025-06-17

SUMMARY
- Q3 treats the CS auto-nudge migration as complete. The legacy nightly path is disabled; shared-state is the sole production path.
- Q3 emphasizes: routine single-path operating explanation (Owen), messaging consumption and lifecycle governance (Ines), transport and source reliability (Daniela), high-stakes decisions (Riley).
- Helio Start stays a bounded-GA self-serve product on the public pricing page. Its reporting is one of the existing shared-state consumers.
- No new beta, no launch, no pricing-page decision, and no fifth consumer is implied.

WHY — CONTEXT BEHIND THE CUT
- 2025-06-17: CS auto-nudge legacy nightly DISABLED. Shared-state is the sole production path.
- "Authority verified" means connector readiness, NOT contact permission.
- Approved restore conditions are unchanged: (a) Daniela incident rollback, OR (b) Riley customer-correction / incident-stop.
- 2025-03-28 lifecycle audit INPUT vs RELEASE: LIVE CLOSED by Owen (638 records, 22 stale fail-closed). Shared-state remains mandatory for Growth + CS lifecycle.
- Owen's 1:1 recommendation (2025-06-17): the migration is closed. Frame Q3 around operating the result, not gating on the migration.

Q3 PRIORITIES BY LANE
- Owen — routine single-path operating explanation. Owns the routine read-out of the single live path: shape, exceptions, semantics, and Helio Start reporting as one of the existing shared-state consumers. Standing-lane neutral readouts remain bounded (≤3/week); stale entries fail closed.
- Ines — messaging consumption and lifecycle governance. Owns how downstream surfaces consume the path and how lifecycle governance holds. Expansion Assist stays descriptive. `routine education` remains HIGHER-RISK and Ines reclassifies; boundary = Riley.
- Daniela — transport and source reliability. Owns transport health, source reliability, and the rollback path that is one of the two approved restore conditions.
- Riley — high-stakes decisions. Owns disputed semantics, cross-surface judgment, customer-correction / incident-stop, and exec-language carry. Standing-lane readouts remain bounded.

HELIO START — OPERATING STATE PRESERVED
- Status: bounded-GA, self-serve, on the public pricing page. No Q3 launch, beta, or pricing-page decision implied.
- Reporting: one of the existing shared-state consumers. No fifth consumer implied.
- States (5, unchanged): admitted, assisted, ineligible, final-reconciliation, plus `pending` (pre-admission, forward-only).
- Reporting math: `pending` is NOT in the rate/activation denominator; intake is additive.

EFFECT
- The CS auto-nudge migration drops out of Q3 gates. Q3 reads as operating-state, not delivery-state.
- Each lane owns its stated surface; no new shared work is introduced.
- Restore posture is unchanged: incident rollback (Daniela) or customer-correction / incident-stop (Riley) only.

CALLS (FOR PRIYA)
1. Confirm the migration is framed as complete in the Q3 outline — no gate language.
2. Confirm the lane cuts as written: Owen / Ines / Daniela / Riley, with the stated boundaries.
3. Confirm Helio Start stays bounded-GA self-serve with its existing shared-state consumer, and Q3 does not introduce a new consumer.
4. Flag any quarter where this framing conflicts with the wider Q3 plan so we reconcile before circulation.

arguments.body:
DECISION (DRAFT) — disputed-semantics: entitlement: active → "paid" / "billing-current"
Date: 2027-07-02 · Lane: disputed-semantics (Riley) · Status: DRAFT — for your review before send

SUMMARY (3 lines)
- "entitlement: active" is one of the five certified message-state fields. It cannot be relabeled as "paid" or "billing-current" in any operator-facing or customer-facing copy. Those two terms carry separate meanings (Stripe-side billing status) that are not part of the governed set.
- The send in question remains held. No manual release. Stale / unresolved / conflicting-required-state still fails closed at the field level.
- Routine review can resume only after revised copy uses only the five certified fields and their established meanings. Authority and engineering-control boundaries are unchanged.

WHY (the disputed-semantics case)
The disputed-semantics lane is mine by standing rule (June 27 calibration; preserved Sept 24, 2025; carried into the Oct 8 brief). Ines independently authors routine operator guidance; she routes — she does not resolve — disputed semantics. Disputed semantics = "the governed meaning itself is in question, or a field definition is being read inconsistently across surfaces." That is exactly what is on the table here.

What the five certified fields mean (canonical, established):
  1. External-system authority — verified readiness to perform the connector's required owner-level permission / network-allowlist action. NOT contact permission.
  2. Connector authentication — the connector between Lifecycle Systems and the external system is authenticated and within its validity window.
  3. Entitlement — the account holds the entitlement that licenses the surface being nudged. This is the "is the account licensed to receive this nudge" state.
  4. Qualifying-human-admin — a verified human admin exists who qualifies for outreach under contact rules.
  5. Active Customer Success adoption / renewal work — no active CS adoption or renewal motion is already running that this nudge would step on.

What "entitlement: active" is NOT:
  - It is not Stripe payment status ("paid").
  - It is not invoice / dunning state ("billing-current").
  - It is not a conjunction of any of the above. Entitlement is a single governed field with a single established meaning.
  - It does not authorize contact under consent, suppression, regulatory, or policy rules (those are separate).

Why relabeling breaks the contract:
  - "paid" and "billing-current" are Stripe-shaped fields with separate owners and separate freshness rules. Folding them into "entitlement: active" creates a new, undefined governed meaning that does not exist in the certified set.
  - It would force a cross-surface read where the same label is being used on two different surfaces with two different meanings — exactly the disputed-semantics failure pattern.
  - It collapses a conjunction (entitlement AND contact-permission AND billing-state) into one field, which is the silent-ship failure mode the contract is designed to prevent.
  - It would invite a future incident where "entitlement: active" is treated as blanket permission to send, the same failure mode we closed in the May 13, 2025 review.

THE CUTS
- CUT 1: "entitlement: active" stays "entitlement: active." No synonym, no relabel.
- CUT 2: "paid" and "billing-current" cannot appear in the operator-facing or customer-facing copy as substitutes for, or in place of, "entitlement: active." If the copy needs to convey Stripe billing state, that is a separate field with a separate owner — it routes to that owner, not into the message-state vocabulary.
- CUT 3: The send in question remains held. No manual release. No exception path. Field-specific hold stands.
- CUT 4: Routine review (Ines's lane) does NOT resume on this copy. Resume only after revised copy uses only the five certified fields with their established meanings.
- CUT 5: If a different copy is needed to communicate payment or billing state to the customer, that copy lives on a separate surface with its own owner and review — not inside the CS auto-nudge messaging-state vocabulary.

P (what changes)
- The proposed revised copy is not used. Send remains held.
- Ines is informed that the copy as written is a disputed-semantics case, with the specific reasoning above, and that revised copy using only the five certified fields can re-enter routine review.
- The four consumer scope (CS auto-nudge messaging-state, Helio Start reporting, Expansion Assist selection, lifecycle preflight) is unchanged. Lifecycle Systems stays at four consumers.
- Daniela retains engineering release and rollback control. Ines has no engineering-control access. These are unchanged.
- Owen's standing weekly CS auto-nudge ledger cadence is unchanged.

EFFECT (what this does and does not do)
- Does: holds the certified vocabulary intact; keeps the send from going out with a relabeled meaning; preserves the field-specific hold; routes the case back to Ines with a clear pass-criterion for revised copy.
- Does: keep routine review cold on this copy until the revised version uses only certified fields with established meanings.
- Does NOT: change any of the five fields' meanings.
- Does NOT: change Ines's authority scope, Owen's authority scope, Daniela's engineering-control scope, or my disputed-semantics lane.
- Does NOT: retire, weaken, or broaden the contract.
- Does NOT: assign growth, revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast credit to this decision.

CALL (the decision, in one sentence)
"entitlement: active" cannot be relabeled as "paid" or "billing-current" in any CS auto-nudge copy; the send remains held; revised copy can re-enter routine review only when it uses only the five certified fields with their established meanings; authority and engineering-control boundaries are unchanged.

WHAT I'D DO NEXT (your call before I send)
1. Send this decision to Ines via Slack DM with the WHY + CUTS + P + EFFECT + CALL structure above, plus the canonical five-field definitions.
2. Add a comment to the existing Q3 evidence-lock template (or current-cycle equivalent) noting the disputed-semantics entry: field = entitlement; proposed relabel = "paid" / "billing-current"; outcome = not used; send held; revised copy required to use only certified fields.
3. Keep the send held. No manual release. Stale / unresolved / conflicting-required-state fails closed.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR YOU (before I send)
- Is the disputed-semantics entry going on the same Q3 evidence-lock template (Lane D = Riley bounded interpretation) or on a new entry? Memory says Lane D rows cite underlying lane rows — never stand alone.
- Do you want this as a Slack DM to Ines only, or also a post to #lifecycle-systems (bounded, like the Aug 14 source-age alert post)?
- Do you want the canonical five-field wording restated verbatim in the message, or referenced ("see prior calibration, June 27 / Sept 24 / Oct 8 brief")?

EVIDENCE-LOCK NOTE — Calibration Appendix
Q3 2025 distinct contributions: Ines Kovac (Lane B) and Daniela Schultz (Lane C)
Prepared: 2028-01-01 · For: calibration appendix · Status: note for the record

PURPOSE
Record, at evidence-lock quality, what each of Ines and Daniela contributed to Q3 2025 that is distinguishable from the other's. The appendix is a calibration reference, not a re-litigation of the work. Two interventions, two lanes — kept separate so the lanes cannot be silently merged in future recall.

LANE MAP (per the 2025-09-18 owner-section reconciliation; package locked 2025-09-19, brief BRIEF-2025-09-19-Q3-evidence-lock)
- Lane B = Ines: operator-guidance interventions + messaging-governance evidence (set by Priya on 2025-08-25).
- Lane C = Daniela: source-alert + source-reliability + release + rollback evidence (set by Priya on 2025-08-25).
- Lane B ≠ Lane C. Ines owns how downstream surfaces consume governed state. Daniela owns transport, source reliability, and the rollback path. They are not interchangeable and neither substitutes for the other; the same held decision can require Lane B intervention (operator-guidance correction) without requiring a Lane C action, and vice versa.

[INLANES — MESSAGING-GOVERNANCE INTERVENTIONS (LANE B)]

Scope of Lane B in Q3 2025: operator-facing language, governed meanings, suppression / hold / cross-surface dependency / proceed language. Messaging-governance interventions are changes to how downstream messaging surfaces consume the governed state — they are not changes to the governed state itself, not changes to source structure, and not changes to release or rollback control.

Distinct contributions recorded in the Q3 evidence-lock package:

1. Operator Message-State Language — Approved Reference (2025-07-11, accepted without Riley rewrite)
   - Authored the corrected operator-facing guide covering Suppressed / Held / Cross-surface dependency / Proceed.
   - Test against the May 20 Customer Success source-delay scenario: 12 previously held records resolved to 8 Suppressed + 4 Proceeded under the corrected language; 0 record required Riley-side reclassification.
   - The four-part output requirement (classification + alignment read + operator consequence + routing call) was satisfied internally without rewrite.
   - Independence criterion met on first pass — no Riley line-edit on routine guidance.
   - This is a messaging-governance intervention because it changes how operators read state on messaging surfaces, without touching transport, source, or release.

2. Governed-state guide (2025-07-25) — Lane B, due under the two-guide schedule pinned at the June 27 calibration.
   - Covers routine, non-state-changing decisions against the governed state set.
   - Built on the same four-part output requirement; does not modify the 2025-07-11 reference.
   - Messaging-governance scope: defines how routine non-state-changing language consumes the governed meanings; does not change the meanings.

3. Two pre-operator corrections captured in the Lane B section of the 2025-09-18 owner-section reconciliation
   - Both preserved in the package with their original limits intact.
   - Scope: operator-facing language corrections routed through the routine-governance lane; routing call escalates state-changing, ambiguous, disputed-semantics, exception-heavy, customer-correction, and incident-stop decisions to Riley.
   - These interventions did not require a Lane C action. They are Lane B, full stop.

What was prevented before operator exposure (Lane B):
- Operators reading "Suppressed" as a single cause rather than multi-causal — the 2025-07-11 guide requires the suppression cause field; bare "Suppressed" without cause is not acceptable.
- Operators treating "Held" as a category label — required fields on every Held row are the specific field driving the hold, age, owner of resolution, and drift check; "Held" without the field is not acceptable.
- Operators using "Proceed" as a freshness proxy — Proceed is a state after verification, not freshness; the guide makes this explicit.
- Operators reading "Authority verified" as contact permission — the CS auto-nudge rule (2025-06-17) holds: Authority verified = connector readiness, NOT contact permission; reading it as contact permission creates a cross-surface dependency by definition. The 2025-07-11 reference restates this so it cannot be silently lost.
- Cross-surface dependency mishandling — escalation to Riley before the decision circulates is required when the same governed field drives more than one surface; bare silent close is not acceptable.

Rollback used (Lane B): No.
- Messaging-governance interventions are pre-send language corrections; the rollback path is Daniela's lane, not Ines's.
- No operator-facing copy that had already been released was rolled back as part of the Lane B interventions recorded in the Q3 evidence-lock package.

[ DANIELA — SOURCE-RELIABILITY INTERVENTION (LANE C) ]

Scope of Lane C in Q3 2025: transport health, source reliability, release audit, and the rollback path that is one of the two approved restore conditions (the other being Riley customer-correction / incident-stop). Source-reliability interventions are changes to how the transport and source layer behaves — they are not changes to governed meanings, not changes to operator-facing language, and not changes to the messaging-consumption layer.

Distinct contributions recorded in the Q3 evidence-lock package:

1. 2025-08-14 source-age alert — first live fire of the measurement rule

   - The alert was a measurement of source freshness against the established freshness limit, not a customer-facing incident and not a rollback trigger.

2. Source-age-alert and release audit (continuous through the July 21 – September 15 reporting window)
   - Two source-age alerts fired before breach during the Q2 board evidence source-completeness period (2026-03-01 → 2026-05-31); both affected sources refreshed before their freshness limits (recorded in the July 6 source lock for the Q2 board evidence and reaffirmed at the Q3 evidence lock).

Readiness review — CS auto-nudge continuous-control row

Status: NOT ready as currently written. Readiness is marked "tentatively ready" but seven required metadata fields are blank, so the row cannot honestly remain marked ready while any required input is incomplete.

Blank outcome-window field — how to handle:
The outcome window is the period over which the continuous-control outcome (CS auto-nudge) is observed and attributed to the coverage dates (10/1–12/31/27). Because the row is a continuous control, the outcome window should normally equal the coverage window so attribution is unambiguous. Three acceptable resolutions, in order of preference:
1. Set outcome window = coverage dates exactly (10/1/27–12/31/27). This is the default for a continuous control and is what the board packet should reflect unless there is a documented reason to diverge.
2. If the measurement cadence genuinely lags (e.g., nudge effect observed with a delay), define a follow-through window (e.g., 10/1/27–1/31/28 or 2/15/28) and explicitly state the lag and rationale. The window must be stated as a concrete date range, not a duration in weeks/months.
3. Do not leave it blank and do not default silently. A blank outcome window makes the row non-falsifiable — the reader cannot tell what period the claim is actually about — and is a board-packet disqualifier on its own.

Required metadata that must also be present before this row can be marked ready:
- Measurement limits: the operational bounds that define what counts as the nudge firing (e.g., eligible-population filter, send-time window, frequency cap, dedupe rule). Vague phrasing ("standard limits") is not sufficient.
- Exclusions: any cohorts, accounts, or time slices deliberately removed (held-out geos, QA-only segments, holiday freeze, etc.). If there are none, state "none" — silence is not the same as "no exclusions."
- Source owner: the team or named individual accountable for the underlying source table or pipeline.
- Source or release-reliability evidence: a pointer to the source itself (table/dashboard/query) plus a release-reliability note — e.g., "stable, no schema change in window" or "v3 cutover on 11/14/27, backfill reconciled." Per pre-launch QA standing, 'paused' state in V11 is a bypass and must be disclosed if applicable.
- Revenue and forecast treatment: explicit statement of whether (and how) the control's outcome feeds revenue/forecast figures in the packet, or "not used in revenue/forecast" if it does not.
- Final claim owner: the single named owner of the board claim (not the source owner). This is the person who can be held to the number in the room.

Can the row remain "tentatively ready" with these fields blank?
No. Readiness should reflect the state of the inputs, not the hope of filling them in. As long as any of the seven fields above is missing — and especially while outcome window is blank — the readiness marker should be downgraded (e.g., "draft — incomplete metadata" or "blocked"). Flipping it back to ready is a one-line edit once each field above is filled with a concrete value and source. Per the staging-first / Daniela-acknowledged pre-launch QA standard, an isolated or under-specified control row should not advance with a ready marker; the pre-launch QA isolation rule (separate $0 campaign, no eligibility-flow entry, CS 8a–6p Central window) applies to launches, but the underlying discipline — no ready signal without complete, sourced inputs — applies here as well.

Recommendation: downgrade readiness to "draft — incomplete metadata," route the blanks to the source owner for fill, and only restore ready status after outcome window, measurement limits, exclusions, source owner, release-reliability evidence, revenue/forecast treatment, and final claim owner are all present and concrete.

arguments.body:
Riley Tanaka — 2026 year-end self-review working draft
Cycle: 2026 year-end · Reviewer: Priya · Working draft (not for distribution)
Shape: summary first, then four evidence sections plus a closing paragraph, written as prose for editing down to the 1-pager (why / cuts / what I did / effect / call).

SUMMARY

I held the claim-boundary discipline across the year: Q1 and Q2 cohort windows stayed on the published dates, and the §3 admission rules plus the §4.8-style pipeline/forecast exclusion held through every pressure point without being compressed into a partial-window claim. I closed the Helio Start paid cohort at $14,420 / 50 admits, and on Aug 21 recommended — and Priya accepted — no second Q3 batch and no pipeline or forecast credit for the cohort; a binding future-paid case-review gate is now in force. I built a delegation rhythm in which Owen owns the monthly sanitized campaign snapshot and the source-completeness review pathway as an evaluation framework, and on November 6 Owen independently closed the 9/24 source-completeness packet covering 7/1–10/31 with certifications complete — the cleanest concrete leadership-through-delegation example of the year. I retain board readiness, causal and revenue claims, forecast treatment, executive language, and exception authority, and I have not stopped routine monthly preparation or source-closure reviews, both of which still flow through me as exception review. The Oct 14 authority-checklist review closed with Owen and Customer Success supplying a clean descriptive four-week operating read; I kept the checklist in organic onboarding without turning the counts into an activation or support-effort claim, and I set an explicit maintenance split among Ines, Daniela, and me. No 2027 role change has been requested or approved.

1. Q1 AND Q2 CLAIM BOUNDARIES — HELD

The published constraints were the §3 admission rules (eligibility, refusal, connector access, external authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, support routing) and the §4.8-style pipeline/forecast exclusion. Q1 dates were 4/7; Q2 was not board-ready until mature claim windows completed. Forecast and pipeline received no credit on partial-window evidence, and a mature claim required complete observation windows.

Under pressure to compress, I refused to roll the day-7 first-integration read (39/50, leading only) into acquisition, scale, pipeline, or forecast, and I held the day-90 decision for closed day-90 windows. I kept the four-part output discipline (classification / alignment / consequence / routing) on operator-facing references and on my own claim-side framing, and I held the §3 / §4.8 cannot-be-weakened framing as the rule any future proposal must satisfy.

The effect: Q1 and Q2 board segments stayed on the published dates, no claim was advanced on a partial-window basis, no pipeline or forecast credit was granted against Q1 or Q2 cohort outcomes, and the structural discipline keeping the five Helio Start states separate from Starter / retained-mid-segment in every readout held. Call: keep citing this as the spine of the year's evidence — the mature-window-only claim discipline plus §3 / §4.8 not weakened is the defended boundary.

2. CLOSED HELIO START PAID COHORT — NO SECOND BATCH, NO PIPELINE/FORECAST CREDIT

The approved pilot was high-intent paid search, mid-segment-fit only, 6-week max window, capped at the earlier of $15,000 spent or 50 admitted workspaces; the $8K / 25 fallback was never approved. Stop / pause triggers (any one): unsupported-in-admitted; reconciliation failure across eligibility → admit → assisted; or ≥20 admitted if >10% showed >90 support minutes per account. The day-7 read of 39/50 first-integration-by-day-7 was leading only, not mature.

On Aug 17 the source-completeness certification packet (Owen + Customer Success) assigned mutually exclusive day-90 statuses to all 50 workspaces — 37 paid-active, 6 canceled, 4 past due, 3 billing hold — with $60,480 gross billed cash, $56,230 refund-adjusted collected cash, 26-minute median and 104-minute p90 account-level support effort, 7 of 50 (14%) exceeding 90 support minutes, and end-to-end reconciliation of paid-source attribution for all 50. No unsupported applicant entered the admitted path. I treated the packet as descriptive paid-source evidence only — explicitly not causal acquisition, not scale, not pipeline, not forecast — because there was no randomized control. On Aug 21 the second-batch decision review recommended, and Priya accepted, no second Helio Start paid batch in Q3 and no Q4 forecast treatment for the cohort. Paid traffic remains off.

The future-paid gate is now binding: Owen + Customer Success must classify each of the seven high-support workspaces into (a) external-authority action, (b) ordinary integration, (c) billing, or (d) another supported cause (named explicitly; "unclassified" is not a supported bucket); Ines + Daniela must determine whether each case concerns state meaning, routing, and / or setup sequence (multiple dimensions may apply, each named); and any future paid proposal must account for all seven cases (state how each is prevented, mitigated, or bounded — not merely listed) without weakening §3 or §4.8.

The cohort is fixed at 50; paid traffic is off; no second Q3 paid batch is in flight; the cohort carries no pipeline or forecast credit. Call: the case-review gate is the structural artifact of the year — the day-90 numbers are evidence inside it, not the artifact itself.

3. OWEN'S MONTHLY-PREP TRANSITION + BOUNDED SOURCE-CLOSURE AUTHORITY

Two changes moved through me. The first was the monthly sanitized campaign snapshot landing as exception-summary only; the first post-handoff on Jul 2 covered 135 campaigns with status and owner rows and owner lanes intact, and resolved three Q2 opens (Ines owner-change verified, Maya snapshot-only, Owen denominator). The second was the source-completeness review pathway defined on Jul 29 — Owen's audit covers eight fields per row (denominator and exact coverage dates; outcome window; measurement limits; exclusions; single named source owner per surface; reliability evidence; revenue and forecast treatment with the explicit handoff note "source certified by Owen; call retained by Riley"; and a section certifier with named backup). The observable success criteria are three consecutive packets with all eight fields complete and a named certifier per section, zero disputed-semantics reopens, zero cross-surface owner drift, exceptions surfaced within one business day of source release with the gap named, reliability evidence reproducible from source on first request, and denominator / coverage dates reconciling against the prior packet's exit state.

Escalation triggers are unchanged: any missing field makes the packet incomplete and escalates; disputed semantics or cross-surface discrepancy escalates rather than resolving in packet; any causal, revenue, forecast, or executive-language content escalates to me by default; and two consecutive packets with the same exception type trigger formal review of the pathway, not a third packet.

3f. October 14 authority-checklist review — four-week operating read, descriptive only

On October 14 the authority-checklist review closed. Owen and Customer Success supplied a clean descriptive four-week operating read on the organic authority-setup checklist shipped on Sep 15. Across the four-week window: 92 admitted organic workspaces in scope; 28 checklist exposures (pre-setup visibility surface only, reported separately from admission and activation outcomes); five ordinary setup-assistance requests handled through the existing assisted-route path. The review surfaced no eligibility or route mismatch, no lifecycle-suppression issue, no paid-source traffic (paid traffic remains off; the Helio Start paid cohort is fixed at 50), no unsupported admission, and no randomized control. I treated the four-week read as descriptive operating evidence — explicitly not an activation claim and not a support-effort claim — because the counts are pre-setup visibility and assisted-route support requests on an organic-only surface, not activation outcomes, and there is no control arm. The checklist stays in organic onboarding, and the metric surfaces (admission, activation, checklist exposure, support minutes) remain split.

The maintenance split is now explicit and named: Ines owns the state-meaning dimension (lifecycle suppression, governed state, external-authority meaning unchanged); Daniela owns the release-reliability dimension (preflight, connector-specific condition, replay coverage, surfacing any drift on first request); I retain the claim discipline (descriptive-only framing, no read into activation or support effort, no pipeline or forecast credit, §3 / §4.8 reaffirmed as not weakened) and the exception authority whenever a maintenance cycle crosses any escalation trigger above. This is a routing change inside the organic checklist surface — descriptive operating read + named maintenance lanes — not a delegation of the underlying claim or forecast responsibility, and §8.E and §8.E.3 remain in force unchanged.

3g. November 6 — independent closure of the 9/24 source-completeness packet (the year's leadership-through-delegation evidence)

On November 6 Owen independently closed the 9/24 source-completeness packet covering 7/1–10/31 with certifications complete. The closure landed without my seeding the structure or chasing fields — the eight source-completeness fields (denominator and exact coverage dates; outcome window; measurement limits; exclusions; single named source owner per surface; reliability evidence; revenue and forecast treatment with the explicit handoff note "source certified by Owen; call retained by Riley"; and section certifier with named backup) cleared on the source side, and the certifications arrived consistent across sections. I treated this as concrete leadership-through-delegation evidence: I held the judgment and evidence boundary, Owen owned the build lane with named readouts and named gates, and the closure happened inside the bounded source-completeness lane without absorbing any other authority into it.

This is source completeness — it is not a claim, not a revenue call, not a forecast treatment, not board-readiness, and not executive language. The 11/6 brief explicitly split Owen's closed source row from the open causal, revenue, pipeline, forecast, board-readiness, and executive-language rows, and those open rows stayed with me. Source-completeness closure is the lane that Owen was bounded to; the broader authorities stayed where they were on 9/24 and are unchanged today. I continue to participate in routine monthly preparation and source-closure reviews as exception review — the 11/6 closure did not remove me from that work, and no new review-closure authority has been granted.

What is delegated versus what is mine. Delegated preparation is Owen's monthly sanitized campaign snapshot and the source-completeness review pathway as an evaluation framework — the line-by-line build work moves to him, with named readouts and named gates — and, on the checklist surface, the four-week descriptive operating read and the maintenance cycles within the Ines / Daniela / Riley split; the 11/6 independent closure of the 9/24 packet is the cleanest instance of that build-lane ownership completing on the source side. Routine source review still comes to me as exception review; I have not left that work, and no new review-closure authority has been granted. Routine monthly preparation still flows through me as exception review; I have not left that work either. What I retain are the claims (causal and revenue), the forecast treatment, the executive language, the descriptive-only discipline on the checklist read, the source completeness boundary itself (the lane Owen operates inside, not the closure authority), and the exception authority whenever a packet or maintenance cycle crosses any escalation trigger above. The transition is a routing change — line-by-line to exception-summary where clean, and descriptive operating read + named maintenance lanes on the checklist — not a handoff of the underlying responsibility, and the underlying responsibility on those streams did not change.

Effect: the 7/2 handoff held (135 campaigns, status + owner + lanes intact, no Q2 board redo); the 7/29 pathway is a written evaluation framework with explicit trigger conditions for re-review, not a delegation; the 10/14 checklist review closed with 92 admitted / 28 exposures / 5 ordinary setup-assistance requests, no eligibility or route mismatch, no lifecycle-suppression issue, no paid-source traffic, no unsupported admission, and no randomized control; the 11/6 independent closure of the 9/24 packet (7/1–10/31, certs complete) landed on the source side with the open causal / revenue / pipeline / forecast / board / executive-language rows staying with me. Call: this is the year's leadership-through-delegation example — I held the judgment and evidence boundary, Owen owned the build lane with named readouts and named gates, and the 11/6 closure is the concrete artifact of the year, with source completeness remaining bounded and the broader authorities unchanged.

4. ORGANIC AUTHORITY-SETUP CHECKLIST — RELEASED, ELIGIBILITY AND STATE MEANINGS PRESERVED

The approved release was a non-state-changing, connector-specific pre-setup checklist for admitted Helio Start workspaces whose selected connector requires an owner-level permission or a network-allowlist action. The release target was the organic Helio Start onboarding path only, and eligibility and state meanings had to be preserved; checklist exposure is reported separately from admission and activation outcomes.

At the 10:30 release gate on Sep 15, Ines and Daniela completed the 24-case replay and lifecycle preflight. The condition for receiving the checklist was a selected connector requiring an owner-level permission or a network-allowlist action, AND current verified-yes external authority at the moment of replay. Eight of the 24 cases met the condition and received the connector-specific checklist; 16 did not meet the condition and did not receive it. Every case preserved existing eligibility, route, lifecycle suppression, and governed state. Daniela released the checklist to the organic onboarding path, and Owen began reporting checklist exposure separately from admission and activation outcomes — the rationale being that checklist exposure is a pre-setup visibility surface, not an admission or activation event, and keeping the metric surfaces split preserves the integrity of the admission and activation numbers and prevents the checklist from being read into the §4.8-style pipeline / forecast framing.

The surrounding levers are all unchanged at Sep 15: §3 admission rules remain in force; external-authority meaning (field definition, current-and-verified-yes semantics, and the missing / stale / conflicting / pending / no / not-sure state set) is unchanged; assisted routing (assisted-route reason capture from first contact and per-account support-minute capture from first contact) is unchanged; fail-closed handling (immediate-stop on any unsupported case in the admitted path, reconciliation-failure pause, >10% over-90-sup-min pause for n ≥ 20) is unchanged; and paid-acquisition status is unchanged (cap closed at $14,420 / 50 admits, paid traffic off, no second Q3 paid batch authorized). The §8.E future-paid case-review gate and the §8.E.3 proposal precondition remain in force; the checklist release does not weaken, satisfy, or replace any element of §8.E.

Effect: the checklist is live on the organic Helio Start onboarding path with eligibility and state meanings intact. The Sep 15 release introduced no new admission, routing, lifecycle, or fail-closed rule; it did not alter external-authority meaning; it did not open a second paid batch. Call: this is the cleanest example of the year of shipping a release with every surrounding lever reasserted and §3 + §4.8 reaffirmed as not weakened.

CLOSING

Two priorities remain in flight, and neither implies I have left routine monthly preparation or source-closure reviews. Priority 1 is to bring Owen's source-completeness review pathway to its graduation criterion: three consecutive packets with all eight fields complete, a named certifier per section, zero disputed-semantics reopens, zero cross-surface owner drift, exceptions surfaced within one business day of source release with the gap named, reliability evidence reproducible from source on first request, and denominator / coverage dates reconciling against the prior packet's exit state. The 11/6 independent closure of the 9/24 packet is concrete progress on that lane, but it is one packet, not the three-packet criterion — I remain the routine source-closure reviewer on the underlying stream and the exception reviewer on the pathway itself until the criterion is met, and that responsibility is not in scope to delegate. Priority 2 is to hold the exception-summary monthly snapshot handoff without regression to line-by-line reconciliation; the 7/2 routing change stays in force, routine monthly preparation still flows through me as exception review, and my current responsibilities on that stream did not change. Source completeness stays separate from the claim, revenue, forecast, board-readiness, and executive-language authorities — the 11/6 closure operated inside that boundary, and no 2027 role change has been requested or approved.

I have not left routine monthly preparation; the 7/2 handoff was a routing change, and the underlying responsibility still flows through me as exception review. I have not delegated source-closure reviews; the 7/29 pathway is an evaluation framework with explicit three-packet success criteria and escalation triggers, the 11/6 closure is one packet inside that frame, and no new review-closure authority has been granted. I have not weakened §3 admission rules or the §4.8-style pipeline / forecast exclusion; both are reaffirmed as not weakened in the §8.E future-paid gate, the §11 organic-checklist release addendum, and the 8/21 second-batch decision record. I have not authorized a second Helio Start paid batch; paid traffic is off, the cohort is fixed at 50, and no pipeline or forecast credit has been granted against the cohort. I have not introduced a new admission, routing, lifecycle, or fail-closed rule; the 9/15 organic authority-setup checklist is non-state-changing and shipped to the organic path only. I have not turned the Oct 14 four-week descriptive checklist read into an activation or support-effort claim; the read is descriptive operating evidence on a pre-setup visibility surface, with the metric surfaces (admission, activation, checklist exposure, support minutes) kept split and §3 / §4.8 reaffirmed as not weakened. The 11/6 closure is source-completeness, not claim, not revenue, not forecast, not board-readiness, and not executive language; the open rows on those authorities stayed with me on 11/6 and continue to stay with me. No 2027 role change has been requested or approved.
